# Engineer handoff: Colorado eligibility rules for the programs served by PEAK and CBMS

Generated from `volumes/co/`. One line per item. `@assembly` items are implemented in the fact-assembly layer; `@engine` items in the determination engine. Types and scopes are those of the codex. `unknown` propagates: any derivation whose inputs are unknown is unknown unless an `otherwise` supplies a default, and an unknown outcome is reported as *cannot determine* with the list of unknown supplied facts.

Each derivation is given twice: in pattern English, and as the expression tree the ledger stores, which is the form to generate code from. Every operator in the tree is defined in `docs/operators.md` (arguments, unknown propagation, empty groups, numeric and date rules). The same items, trees and parameter versions are available as JSON (`npm run export` writes `conformance/<volume>/ledger.json`), and the conformance suite is `npm run conformance` (`docs/conformance.md`).

### CO-005 Has a military connection `@engine`

The person is on active duty (other than training) in the U.S. Armed Forces, or is an honorably discharged veteran, or is the spouse, surviving spouse, or unmarried dependent child of such a person, within the military-connection category.

Precision. An unmarried dependent child is read as an unmarried child of the veteran (the dependency the statute names, a child the veteran supports, is not separately stated). The spouse is the legal spouse.

Type yes/no, scope person, program All.
Uses: `has_qualifying_military_service`, `is_married`, `is_surviving_spouse_of_veteran`, `relationships`.

```
any of the following is true:
  - Has qualifying military service
  - (there is a person of whom this person is a spouse such that;   that person's Has qualifying military service), otherwise no
  - Surviving spouse of a veteran, otherwise no
  - all of the following are true:
    - it is not the case that Is married
    - (there is a person of whom this person is a child such that;   that person's Has qualifying military service), otherwise no
```

["any","has_qualifying_military_service",["otherwise",["exists_related",["spouse"],["of",["P"],"has_qualifying_military_service"]],false],["otherwise","is_surviving_spouse_of_veteran",false],["all",["not","is_married"],["otherwise",["exists_related",["child"],["of",["P"],"has_qualifying_military_service"]],false]]]
```

Examples: 3, all passing.

### CO-017 Is Medicare entitled or enrolled `@engine`

The person is entitled to or enrolled for Medicare benefits under Part A, or enrolled for benefits under Part B (42 CFR 435.553(a)(2)).

Type yes/no, scope person, program All.
Uses: `medicare_part_a_entitled`, `medicare_part_b_enrolled`.

```
any of the following is true:
  - Receives Medicare Part A
  - Enrolled in Medicare Part B
```

### CO-021 Is enrolled at least half-time in higher education `@engine`

The person is enrolled at least half time, as the institution defines it, in an institution of higher education (a college or university, or vocational or technical training after high school).

Type yes/no, scope person, program All.
Uses: `education_enrollment_intensity`, `education_program_type`.

```
all of the following are true:
  - Education program type is one of: postsecondary_career_and_technical, higher_education
  - Education enrollment intensity is one of: full_time, half_time

### CO-3151 Declared household income as a percentage of the poverty guideline `@engine`

The declared household income (declared_household_income_monthly, CO-092) as a decimal fraction of the monthly federal poverty guideline in force in the month for the declared household size (declared_household_size, CO-3150): the figure presumptive eligibility (10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.4.F.2, § 8.100.3.R.2; 10 CCR 2505-3 § 170.1) and Express Lane (§ 8.100.4.J.1.a.v, J.2.a.v) compare with their standards.

Precision. The annual guideline in force in the month for the declared size (on the month's first day, or on the determination date in the determination month), divided by 12, as ma_magi_monthly_household_income_pct_fpl (CO-6452) reads it; the table is read beyond its last row with federal_poverty_guideline_annual_each_additional (P51). Not rounded. MAGI close-out, MAGI-SW-1 (2026-11-24; docs/reviews/known-limits.md): per month. A person-scope item is one value per case, so the parameter was read on the determination date in every month that read it (docs/operators.md, Resolution step 2), and a retroactive or application month in another version period of the guideline (federal_poverty_guideline_annual_table, CO-181, and its each-additional figure, CO-182: a version from each January 1) took the determination date's figure. Eligibility in a month is judged on that month (10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.4.G.1, S3351: 'any person who is determined to be eligible for Medical Assistance based on MAGI at any time during a calendar month shall be eligible for benefits during the entire month'), and a retroactive month is one in which the person 'met all applicable eligibility requirements' (§ 8.100.3.E.1, S1503), so the figure of a month is the one in force in it: the version in force on the month's first day, or on the determination date in the determination month, as non-MAGI F7-2 made the personal needs allowance (CO-1987). Rules about the determination itself (presumptive eligibility, CO-2439, CO-3155, CO-708) read it in the determination month. Its month-scoped readers are the Express Lane tests (CO-3156, CO-4792) and the qualified-entity presumptive tests (CO-558, CO-559).

Type rate, scope person-month, program All.
Uses: `declared_household_income_monthly`, `declared_household_size`, `federal_poverty_guideline_annual_each_additional`, `federal_poverty_guideline_annual_table`.

Declared household income divided by ((HHS federal poverty guideline by household size, annual (48 states and D.C.) (table), for Declared household size, adding HHS federal poverty guideline, each additional household member, annual (48 states and D.C.) (5680) for each beyond its last row) divided by 12)
```

This item then still counted from qualified_status_date, the status held now, for its Colorado Works and Adult Financial readers (SNAP writes its own count for the month, CO-307), so a person who held an earlier qualified status restarted the five years at a later adjustment there (KL-CASH-2, docs/reviews/known-limits.md). KL-CASH-2 closed (2026-11-24): the five years are counted from the start of the waiting period (qualified_non_citizen_waiting_period_start_date, CO-7820: the first qualified status, or the status held now where the case shows it is the first), as 1613(a) runs them for Colorado Works, a federal means-tested benefit, as C.R.S. 26-2-706(1.5)(b) (S402: 'has been in a qualified alien status for a period of five years') and 9 CCR 2503-6 3.604.1.B.3 (S407) state them, and as C.R.S. 26-2-111.8(2)(b) (S1151: 'for a period of five years after the date of entry into the United States') states them for the Old Age Pension, Aid to the Needy Disabled and Aid to the Blind, after which (2)(c) (S5300) makes the qualified alien eligible. ### CO-7400 Most recent pregnancy end date, as the case records it `@engine`

The date the person's most recent pregnancy that has ended came to an end: the stated pregnancy_end_date (CO-089); where it is not stated, the date of birth of the child born last of the persons of the case she gave birth to (the gave_birth_to relationship), since a birth ends the pregnancy on the child's date of birth. Unknown where neither is stated.

Precision. Coverage pass 6, C6-03 (2026-11-24). The fact of a birth is recorded once, by the child's date_of_birth and the gave_birth_to relationship a newborn's case states (the product-owner rule that facts another record or edge can supply are read from it, not entered twice), so a mother applying with her newborn need not also state pregnancy_end_date. A stated pregnancy_end_date governs (a miscarriage or termination after the last birth is stated there). The latest birth is taken as the greatest number of days from the determination date to each such child's date of birth (P59 greatest; days_after back from the determination date), so a child born later counts over an older sibling; a child of the case whose date of birth is not stated leaves it unknown. Relationships not stated are read as none, as birth_mother_coverage_at_birth (CO-3322) reads them. Unknown where no end is stated and no child of the case was born to her: each reader says what that means for it (ma_is_pregnant_in_month CO-3601, chp_is_pregnant_in_month CO-7051: no ended pregnancy unless a pregnancy start is stated with no end, then the months from the start cannot be determined).

Type calendar date, scope person, program All.
Uses: `date_of_birth`, `pregnancy_end_date`, `relationships`.

```
if it is not the case that Pregnancy end date is unknown
  then Pregnancy end date
else if (the number of persons in all persons in every person in the case such that this person is a gave_birth_to of that person, otherwise no) is more than 0
  then the greatest of the number of days from the Determination Date to that person's Date of birth for each person in all persons in every person in the case such that this person is a gave_birth_to of that person, otherwise no days after the Determination Date
otherwise Pregnancy end date
```

### CO-7820 Start of the qualified non-citizen waiting period `@engine`

The date from which the five years of 8 U.S.C. 1613(a) are counted: the date the person first obtained a qualified non-citizen status or entered the United States in one, whatever status the person holds now. It is the date of the status held now (qualified_status_date, CO-003) where the person entered the United States in it (us_entry_date on or after qualified_status_date); otherwise the date of the first qualified status where the case states it (first_qualified_status_date, CO-7770); otherwise the date of the status held now where the case shows that status is the first: a lawful permanent resident admitted directly or adjusted from a status in which the person was not a qualified alien (status_before_lpr_adjustment none or non_qualified_status), or another qualified non-citizen who held no qualified status before the one held now (has_held_earlier_qualified_status false, CO-7890); otherwise the first date, which is then required.

Precision. KL-SNAP-2 and KL-CASH-2 (docs/reviews/known-limits.md; 2026-11-24): the reading Medicaid's five-year count took in coverage pass 7, C7-04 (ma_has_held_qualified_status_five_years_in_month, CO-7550), stated once for the other readers of the five years: SNAP (snap_meets_immigrant_additional_condition CO-307, snap_requires_verification_of_qualifying_quarters CO-3736, snap_requires_verification_of_military_connection CO-3738, and the 1931 arm of snap_is_exempt_from_waiting_period_other_than_military CO-3713) and the cash programs (has_held_qualified_status_five_years CO-508, read through meets_public_assistance_citizenship_requirement CO-905). 8 U.S.C. 1613(a) (S176) runs the five years 'beginning on the date of the alien's entry into the United States with a status within the meaning of the term "qualified alien"', 8 U.S.C. 1612(a)(2)(L) (S22) for SNAP 'beginning on the date of the alien's entry into the United States', and 10 CCR 2506-1 4.305.B.3.a (S12) 'on the date the non-citizen obtains status as a qualified non-citizen or enters the U.S. in a qualifying status': a later adjustment (a parolee of a year or more, a battered non-citizen or a conditional entrant who became a lawful permanent resident) does not restart them. No qualified status is held in the United States before entering it, so an entry on or after the status date shows the status held now is the first; an unstated entry date only leaves that shortcut unread. Required where read (decision 4 of 2026-11-23): where the case does not show the status held now is the first, first_qualified_status_date is read with no default, and so is status_before_lpr_adjustment for a lawful permanent resident who did not enter in the status and states no first date (C7-09's reading), and has_held_earlier_qualified_status for any other qualified non-citizen who did not enter in the status and states no first date (KL-SNAP-3); one not stated where read is cannot determine here. Its readers also count from qualified_status_date, so a person whose status held now has itself been held five years needs neither. Coverage verification 7 follow-up (V7-8; 2026-11-24): a lawful permanent resident whose earlier status is non_qualified_status (a nonimmigrant admission such as a work, student or fiance visa, or no lawful status: not a qualified alien under 8 U.S.C. 1641(b), S1900) first obtained a qualified status when granted permanent residence, so the five years start at qualified_status_date, as for none and as Medicaid's CO-7550 reads it; before, this item read none alone that way and asked first_qualified_status_date for non_qualified_status (stated equal to qualified_status_date, or cannot determine). Close-out verification F1, the arm left (KL-SNAP-3, docs/reviews/known-limits.md; 2026-11-24): a qualified non-citizen who is not a lawful permanent resident and whose only qualified status began after entry (a battered non-citizen found so in 2022 who entered in no status in 2018) had no fact saying the status held now is the first, so the start was cannot determine unless first_qualified_status_date was stated with the same date again; has_held_earlier_qualified_status (CO-7890) false now gives qualified_status_date (1613(a): the five years begin on the date the person first held a qualified status, which is then the status held now). A first_qualified_status_date the case states is the start wherever the entry does not settle it, before the shortcuts are read: it is the date the shortcuts stand in for, so a lawful permanent resident who states it and not the earlier status has a start (was cannot determine, CO-7820-T5). Medicaid's five-year count reads this item too (ma_has_held_qualified_status_five_years_in_month, CO-7550), in place of the same choice written inside it.

Type calendar date, scope person, program All.
Uses: `first_qualified_status_date`, `has_held_earlier_qualified_status`, `immigration_status`, `qualified_status_date`, `status_before_lpr_adjustment`, `us_entry_date`.

```
if Qualified status date is at most Date of entry into the United States, otherwise no
  then Qualified status date
else if it is not the case that First qualified status date is unknown
  then First qualified status date
else if Immigration status is equal to lawful_permanent_resident
  then (if Status before lawful permanent residence is one of: none, non_qualified_status;   then Qualified status date; otherwise First qualified status date)
else if it is not the case that Has held an earlier qualified status
  then Qualified status date
otherwise First qualified status date
```

```

### CO-800 SSI method: countable resources of the individual `@engine`

This person's own countable resources by the SSI method (20 CFR 416.1201, 416.1210; 10 CCR 2505-10 8.100.5.M.2), as an individual, not combined with a spouse's, on the determination date: the SSI method's holdings counted in the determination month (ma_ssi_holdings_countable_in_month, CO-5320), each kind of holding as the SSI method's holdings counting table (ma_ssi_holding_treatment_table, CO-5303) treats it: cash, accounts and securities, retirement accounts, real property other than the home, vehicles other than the one automobile used for transportation (416.1218(b)(1)), the cash surrender value of life insurance unless the face value is $1,500 or less (416.1230(a)), and revocable burial funds above the burial fund exclusion (§ 8.100.5.M.2.j); the unspent part of a retroactive SSI or Social Security payment is left out for the nine months following the month of receipt (§ 8.100.5.F.6.c), and the kinds the table excludes are not counted.

Precision. Resource records, Medicaid track H1 (docs/reviews/records-holdings-medicaid.md): read from the holdings records (CO-5300) by the SSI method's one counting table, Medicaid's (decision D6), which Adult Financial burial assistance adopts by its cited link through this item. The home (416.1212) is not counted here; Medicaid's home rules are ma_home_is_countable_resource (CO-4622). Medicaid's own findings (real property for sale or a co-owner's home, CO-4620; income-producing property above its exclusion, CO-4621; the value found available from a trust, an annuity or a life estate) are added by ma_ssi_countable_resources_individual (CO-4623), not here. Irrevocable burial funds (M.2.i), burial spaces (M.2.h), ABLE accounts (M.2.k) and household goods and personal effects (M.2.d-e) are not counted. The burial fund exclusion is the person's own, so each spouse has one (M.2.j). The determination month is stated as [det_month], in every month a determination evaluates: this item is per person, the SSI-method resources held on the determination date, and its readers (CO-801, CO-1405, CO-1225) are per person too; ma_ssi_holdings_countable_in_month reads the holdings valued in any month. Medicaid's own resource tests are per month (ma_ssi_countable_resources, CO-608, from ma_ssi_countable_resources_in_month, CO-5322; coverage pass 4, non-MAGI N4-7, OQ-952 resolved); this item serves the readers that determine at one date (Adult Financial burial assistance and the Colorado Works death reimbursement, by their cited links, and the verification of resources). A couple excludes one automobile (416.1218(b): "an individual (and spouse, if any)"): ssi_countable_resources_couple (CO-801) adds back the two spouses' own exclusions less the couple's one, a car they own together counted once (N4-6).

Type money, scope person, program All.
Uses: `ma_ssi_holdings_countable_in_month`.

```
Medicaid SSI method: the person's holdings counted in the month for the month containing the Determination Date
```

```

### CO-801 SSI method: countable resources of the couple `@engine`

The combined countable resources by the SSI method of this person and a spouse living together: each one's ssi_countable_resources_individual (20 CFR 416.1202(a), 10 CCR 2505-10 8.100.5.M.1's couple limit and § 8.100.7.O.1's ongoing test).

The person is a U.S. citizen or national, or a qualified non-citizen who entered the United States before August 22, 1996, who is in a federal exempt category under 8 U.S.C. 1613(b), or who has held qualified status for five years, or an Iraqi or Afghan special immigrant, adjusted or not, or an Afghan or Ukrainian humanitarian parolee within the term federal law sets, whom federal law gives refugee benefits to the same extent as refugees: the requirement C.R.S. 26-2-111.8(2) sets for Colorado Works, the Old Age Pension, Aid to the Needy Disabled and Aid to the Blind, and that 26-2-706(1.5)(b) and 9 CCR 2503-6 3.604.1.B restate for Colorado Works and 9 CCR 2503-5 3.520.61.C and 3.520.68.A for Aid to the Needy Disabled.

Precision. Vocabulary fix round (R-4, U-2, U-3): the 8 U.S.C. 1613(b) exemption is is_exempt_from_five_year_bar (CO-1725); Colorado Works had read SNAP's own waiting-period exemption, whose under-18 and pre-1931 prongs are not 1613(b) categories (so a lawful permanent resident child inside five years was found eligible and a refugee inside five years was not), and Aid to the Needy Disabled read no exemption at all (so a refugee inside five years failed). The pre-1996 entry test reads us_entry_date (CO-1726), not the date the qualified status was obtained. Once both programs read the same federal exemption, the Colorado Works item and meets_public_assistance_citizenship_requirement (CO-905) were the same rule, as 26-2-111.8(2) makes them; CO-943 is retired into this item, renamed from cw_meets_citizenship_requirement. Adult Financial reads it only for AND and AB (af_category, CO-953): 3.520.61.C and 3.520.68.A state the test 'for AND only', and OAP keeps its own test (af_meets_citizenship_requirement_oap, CO-929). Does not model 26-2-111(2)(c)(II)-(III)'s hardship and SSI-eligibility exceptions (OQ-119). Final cash review FC-13 (OQ-550): Pub. L. 111-8 div. F sec. 602(b)(8) and Pub. L. 110-181 sec. 1244(g), as amended by Pub. L. 111-118 sec. 8120 (S2627-S2630), give Afghan and Iraqi special immigrants refugee benefits "to the same extent, and for the same periods of time, as such refugees", so this item accepts them, adjusted or not, as it accepts a refugee, with no five-year bar. is_qualified_non_citizen (CO-506) and is_exempt_from_five_year_bar (CO-1725), which Medicaid reads with its own special-immigrant rule, are unchanged. Final cash review 2, N-3 and P2-1: Pub. L. 117-128 sec. 401(b)(1) (D-260, S2800) makes a Ukrainian humanitarian parolee whose parole has not been terminated eligible for "entitlement programs, and other benefits available to refugees ... to the same extent as such refugees", and Pub. L. 117-43 sec. 2502(b)(1) (D-261, S2801) does the same for an Afghan humanitarian parolee "until March 31, 2023, or the term of parole granted ..., whichever is later"; both are "Notwithstanding any other provision of law". The item accepts them as it accepts a special immigrant, by the same reading FC-13 took: a Ukrainian parolee while parole_end_date (CO-2703), where stated, has not passed, and an Afghan parolee through the later of afghan_humanitarian_parolee_refugee_benefits_end_date (CO-4006) and parole_end_date; the immigration status itself, as SAVE states it, stands for a parole not ended where no end date is stated. A trafficking victim is accepted for Colorado Works only (cw_meets_citizenship_and_immigration_requirement, CO-4005): 22 U.S.C. 7105(b)(1)(A) reaches programs funded or administered by HHS and the other agencies of (b)(1)(B), and Aid to the Needy Disabled, Aid to the Blind and the Old Age Pension are State and county programs, so for them a trafficking victim stays a qualified non-citizen under the five-year bar. KL-CASH-2 closed (2026-11-24; docs/reviews/known-limits.md): the five years (has_held_qualified_status_five_years, CO-508) are counted from the start of the waiting period, the first qualified status (qualified_non_citizen_waiting_period_start_date, CO-7820; first_qualified_status_date, CO-7770, required where read), not from the status held now, so a lawful permanent resident who was paroled into the United States more than five years before meets the requirement (LPR-EX-PAROLEE: stored households CO-1141, Colorado Works, and CO-1142, AND-SO). 9 CCR 2503-5 3.520.68.A dates the AND bar from the date of admission for permanent residence: OQ-1485.

Type yes/no, scope person, program All.
Uses: `afghan_humanitarian_parolee_refugee_benefits_end_date`, `has_held_qualified_status_five_years`, `immigration_status`, `is_exempt_from_five_year_bar`, `is_qualified_non_citizen`, `is_us_citizen_or_national`, `parole_end_date`, `qualified_non_citizen_entry_cutoff_date`, `status_before_lpr_adjustment`, `us_entry_date`.

```
any of the following is true:
  - Is a U.S. citizen or national
  - all of the following are true:
    - Is a qualified non-citizen
    - any of the following is true:
      - Date of entry into the United States is less than PRWORA qualified-alien entry date cutoff (1996-08-22)
      - Is exempt from the five-year bar (8 U.S.C. 1613(b))
      - Has held qualified status for the five-year waiting period
  - Immigration status is equal to iraqi_afghan_special_immigrant
  - all of the following are true:
    - Immigration status is equal to lawful_permanent_resident
    - (Status before lawful permanent residence, otherwise none) is equal to iraqi_afghan_special_immigrant
  - all of the following are true:
    - Immigration status is equal to ukrainian_humanitarian_parolee
    - the Determination Date is at most Parole end date, otherwise yes
  - all of the following are true:
    - Immigration status is equal to afghan_humanitarian_parolee
    - any of the following is true:
      - the Determination Date is at most Afghan humanitarian parolee: date through which refugee benefits run whatever the parole term (2023-03-31)
      - the Determination Date is at most Parole end date, otherwise yes

### CO-007 SNAP: resides in an institution that provides the majority of meals `@engine`

The person is a resident of an institution under 7 CFR 273.1(b)(7)(vi): the institution provides the person with the majority of meals (over 50 percent of three meals daily) as part of its normal services, and the person is not among the exceptions (A)-(E) - a resident of a drug or alcohol treatment and rehabilitation facility operated by a governmental unit or a private nonprofit organization and certified (B), a disabled or blind resident of a group living arrangement that is public or private nonprofit, serves no more than snap_group_living_max_residents (16) residents and is certified (C) (7 CFR 271.2; 10 CCR 2506-1 4.309.3.A-B, 4.309.4.A: "Individuals residing in a for-profit facility are considered residents of an institution"); residents of federally subsidized housing for the elderly (A) and of battered women's or homeless shelters (D, E) live in a private dwelling or shelter, not an institution, for residence_setting_type.

Precision. Read from residence_setting_type (CO-3330) and residence_setting_provides_majority_of_meals (CO-3334). Coverage review C-3: the (B) and (C) exceptions also read who operates the setting (residence_setting_operated_by_government, CO-3331; residence_setting_is_nonprofit, CO-4255, read as false when not stated), its size (residence_setting_bed_count, CO-3332, for (C)) and its certification (residence_setting_is_licensed_or_certified, CO-3335: the OBH approval of 4.309.3.B for a center, the 1616(e) certification of 4.309.4.A for a group living arrangement). The FNS retailer authorization of the center (4.309.3.B, 4.309.42) is the facility's standing and is not separately stated. The (B) exception's children of a treatment resident live in the same setting and are not residents of an institution either. Coverage pass 2 N2-4: a student whose meal plan bought through an institution of higher education provides more than half of the student's meals is a resident of an institution whatever the residence setting (has_higher_education_meal_plan_providing_majority_of_meals, CO-4686; 4.304.4.D.3, S3472), "unless the individual is otherwise exempt from the institution provisions as provided in Section 4.304.41": the treatment-center (B) and group-living (C) exceptions, and a shelter (D, E: nighttime_residence_type emergency_or_transitional_shelter). Federally subsidized housing for the elderly (A) has no fact apart from private_dwelling; a student with a college meal plan living there is read as a resident of an institution. Coverage pass 4 S4-14 (decision 4 of 2026-11-23): residence_setting_is_nonprofit is read with no default where this rule reads it (only for a resident of a treatment center or a group living arrangement not operated by a government; 4.309.3-4.309.4 and 7 CFR 271.2 name public and private nonprofit settings and give no reading for an operator not stated); before, it was read as false, so a treatment-center resident was read as in a for-profit institution and in no SNAP household when not stated. Three-pattern sweep D-2 (docs/reviews/pattern-sweep-snap-ce.md): for a student whose meal plan provides most meals, the shelter exception reads nighttime_residence_type (CO-2810) as stated, required where read (decision 4): no text on file reads an unstated nighttime residence as other than a shelter; before, it was read so, and the student was in no household.

### CO-037 SNAP: homeless individual `@engine`

Whether the person is a homeless individual for SNAP under 7 CFR 271.2 (S1950): lacks a fixed and regular nighttime residence, including one who will imminently lose it; or has as primary nighttime residence a supervised shelter giving temporary accommodations, a halfway house or similar institution for persons intended to be institutionalized, a temporary accommodation of not more than 90 days in the residence of another individual, or a public or private place not designed for, or ordinarily used as, a regular sleeping accommodation.

Precision. A motel or hotel, trailer park or campground stay for lack of alternative accommodations, and an abandonment in a hospital, are a lack of a fixed and regular nighttime residence (271.2 (1)). Substandard housing is fixed and regular, so it is not homelessness for SNAP. A stay in another's home, for any reason, is homeless for not more than snap_homeless_temporary_accommodation_max_days (90) days from temporary_residence_start_date; beyond that it is not (2)(iii). Three-pattern sweep T-4 (docs/reviews/pattern-sweep-snap-ce.md): per month, the days counted to the first day of the month evaluated, since prospective budgeting reads the circumstances of the issuance month (10 CCR 2506-1 4.402.1.A, S4734) and a status that gives the household a deduction is met for the month if it is met on any day of it (the day SNAP reads its ages and dated changes on, OQ-1262, OQ-1405). Before, the item was per person and counted to the determination date, so a household still within the ninety days in the determination month kept the homeless shelter deduction in every later month of the certification (probe CO-943). Coverage pass 7 for SNAP, C7-3 (docs/reviews/coverage7-snap.md): a stay in another person's home that began after the month's last day (temporary_residence_start_date on or after the first day of the next month) is not that month's "primary nighttime residence" (271.2), so the month is read from where the person slept before the stay began (nighttime_residence_type_before_stay, CO-7674), required there (decision 4): a homeless residence before the stay is homeless, a fixed home, substandard housing or an institution is not, and an earlier stay in another's home cannot be measured (its start is not stated), so the month cannot be determined; never homeless by default. A stay that began on the month's last day is homeless in that month (a status that gives a deduction is met on any day of it, OQ-1405). Before, the days counted to the month's first day were negative for a later stay, so the household read as homeless in a month before the stay began (probe STAY-LATE2: October $222 where the text gives $198). The other residence types are stated for the determination date and read for an earlier month as they are (OQ-1450).

Type yes/no, scope person-month, program SNAP.
Uses: `nighttime_residence_type`, `nighttime_residence_type_before_stay`, `snap_homeless_temporary_accommodation_max_days`, `temporary_residence_start_date`.

```
if Nighttime residence type is one of: imminently_losing_residence, motel_or_hotel_for_lack_of_alternative, trailer_park_for_lack_of_alternative, campground_for_lack_of_alternative, emergency_or_transitional_shelter, halfway_house, abandoned_in_hospital, place_not_designed_for_sleeping
  then yes
else if Nighttime residence type is one of: shared_housing_due_to_loss_or_hardship, shared_housing_other_temporary
  then (if Temporary residence start date is at least the first day of the month after the month;   then (if Nighttime residence before the temporary stay is one of: imminently_losing_residence, motel_or_hotel_for_lack_of_alternative, trailer_park_for_lack_of_alternative, campground_for_lack_of_alternative, emergency_or_transitional_shelter, halfway_house, abandoned_in_hospital, place_not_designed_for_sleeping;   then yes; else if Nighttime residence before the temporary stay is one of: fixed_regular_adequate, substandard_housing, institution;   then no); otherwise (the number of days from Temporary residence start date to the first day of the month) is at most SNAP homeless temporary accommodation, most days (90))
otherwise no
```

### CO-074 SNAP: countable non-liquid resources `@engine`

The person's own countable non-liquid resources in the month under 7 CFR 273.8 and 10 CCR 2506-1 4.409-4.410, before combining with other household members' resources: the person's countable real property (snap_countable_real_property, CO-5311: the equity not exempt, each holding returning more than $1,500), non-liquid personal property and installment contracts (snap_countable_other_nonliquid_resources, CO-6900), the equity of pre-purchased funeral agreements beyond the one per household member that 7 CFR 273.8(e)(2) excludes (snap_countable_funeral_agreements, CO-5312), and burial spaces beyond the one plot per household member the text excludes (snap_countable_burial_spaces, CO-5313). Colorado excludes every vehicle (4.410.A); the cash value of life insurance and household goods (273.8(e)(2)) and retirement accounts (273.8(e)(2)(i)) are excluded.

Precision. Coverage pass 4 for SNAP resources (docs/reviews/coverage4-snap-resources.md): per month (SR-9), each part read in the month evaluated; investment personal property and installment contracts not producing income consistent with their value are counted (SR-3, SR-5; CO-6900); one funeral agreement per member is excluded whatever its amount (SR-1, the statute override on CO-5312). Resource records, step H1 SNAP (docs/reviews/records-holdings-snap-af.md): each part is read from the person's holdings records (holdings, CO-5300) through snap_holding_treatment_table (CO-5301), each holding stated once, never from the scalar resource facts. A person whose holdings are not stated is cannot determine (decision 4 of 2026-11-23). Land used only to produce food for the household (produces_for_household_use) is counted as real property: 4.410.E.1 exempts property producing an annual income consistent with its value and D.1 livestock, and no paragraph exempts such land. Trusts and annuities are not read (OQ-1307); a life estate is not read (OQ-1202).

### CO-1239 SNAP: incurs heating or cooling cost `@engine`

The household incurs or anticipates heating or cooling costs separate and apart from its rent or mortgage (10 CCR 2506-1 4.407.31.A.1.a): it pays a heating vendor directly or its share of a shared heating bill (A.1.d), its landlord bills it on individual usage or charges a flat rate for heat separately from rent (A.1.c; a public-housing household responsible for excess heating costs, A.1.e), or it pays for cooling separately from its rent or mortgage.

Precision. Reads the neutral home facts once for the case. Heat included in rent with no separate charge, or no heating cost at all, does not qualify; a supplemental heating source is not the primary heating (A.3). Cooling unstated is read as none. Coverage pass 4 S4-14 (decision 4 checked): the home's utility costs not stated are read as not incurred, the rule giving that reading: a deduction is given only for an expense the household claims and shows, and an expense not shown is left out (10 CCR 2506-1 4.502.A.3, S818: "the household's eligibility and benefit level will be determined without providing a deduction or exclusion for the claimed but unverified expense"; 7 CFR 273.2(f)(3)(ii), S812), so a utility cost not claimed gives no utility allowance.

Type yes/no, scope case, program SNAP.
Uses: `home_heating_cost_arrangement`, `home_incurs_separate_cooling_cost`.

```
any of the following is true:
  - Home heating cost arrangement is one of: pays_vendor_directly, billed_by_landlord_on_usage, separate_charge_from_landlord
  - Home incurs separate cooling cost, otherwise no
```

```

### CO-1243 SNAP: entitled to the heating and cooling utility allowance `@engine`

Whether, in the month evaluated, the person's SNAP household is entitled to the Heating and Cooling Utility Allowance: it incurs or anticipates heating or cooling costs separate from rent or mortgage, or it received LEAP or E-EBT within the previous twelve months and contains an elderly or disabled member in the month (snap_household_has_elderly_or_disabled_member_in_month, CO-6603), per 10 CCR 2506-1 4.407.31.A.1 and Pub. L. 119-21 sec. 10103.

Precision. 10 CCR 2506-1 4.407.31.A.1.b as of 2026-10-01 (S743) still grants the HCUA on prior LEAP or E-EBT receipt alone; Pub. L. 119-21 sec. 10103 (S136) limits the energy-assistance route to households with an elderly or disabled member. This item follows the amended statute, as the volume does wherever the rule manual has not caught up (OQ-1, OQ-32); see OQ-251. Coverage pass 6 for SNAP, C6-3 (docs/reviews/coverage6-snap.md): per month, reading the month's elderly or disabled member (CO-6603), as S4-11 made every other reader that turns on the month's household (CO-344, CO-379): prospective budgeting reads "anticipated income and circumstances during the issuance month" (10 CCR 2506-1 4.402.1.A, S4734). Before, the item was per person and read the determination month's member (CO-314) in every month, so a household whose member turned 60 after the determination month was denied the allowance in that member's months (probe HCUA60, stored CO-863). Three-pattern sweep T-10 (docs/reviews/pattern-sweep-snap-ce.md): the energy assistance counts in a month only while that month is within the twelve months after the month of the most recent payment (energy_assistance_last_payment_month, CO-7451), since the federal rule the State's "within the previous twelve (12) month period" implements counts a payment received "in the current month or in the immediately preceding 12 months" (7 CFR 273.9(d)(6)(iii)(D)(3), S5090), a test of each issuance month. Before, a payment within the twelve months before the determination gave the allowance in every month of the certification (probe CO-950). Coverage pass 7 for SNAP, C7-2 (docs/reviews/coverage7-snap.md): the window has its lower bound as well: a payment counts for a month only if it was received in that month or before it (273.9(d)(6)(iii)(D)(3), S5090: "in the current month or in the immediately preceding 12 months"; (iii): the agency documents "the date and receipt of a payment ... to ensure the payment was received in the current month or the immediately preceding 12 months"). Where the most recent payment (CO-7451) came after the month evaluated (an application month before a payment made between the application and the determination), the month is entitled only through an earlier payment received in it or in the twelve months before it, read from energy_assistance_earlier_payment_months (CO-7673); not stated, the month's entitlement cannot be determined here, and the utility allowance (CO-1500) gives no heating and cooling allowance for it (4.502.A.3, S818, its declared reading; coverage verification 7, V7-6, CO-7673's precision). Before, a LEAP payment made in November gave an October application month the allowance (probe LIHEAP-LATE: October $312 where the text gives $280).

Type yes/no, scope person-month, program SNAP.
Uses: `energy_assistance_earlier_payment_months`, `energy_assistance_last_payment_month`, `received_energy_assistance_within_twelve_months`, `snap_household_has_elderly_or_disabled_member_in_month`, `snap_incurs_heating_cooling_cost`.

```
any of the following is true:
  - SNAP: incurs heating or cooling cost
  - all of the following are true:
    - Received energy assistance within twelve months
    - if Month of the most recent energy assistance payment is at most the month
      then the month is at most 12 months after Month of the most recent energy assistance payment
    otherwise (the sum of (if all of the following are true:;     - that month is at most the month;     - the month is at most 12 months after that month;   then 1; otherwise 0) for each month in Months of earlier energy assistance payments) is more than 0
    - SNAP: household has an elderly or disabled member in the month
```

### CO-1376 SNAP: requires verification of earned income `@engine`

Whether the person's earned income must be verified for SNAP: wages SNAP counts (net of the earnings 4.405 excludes, snap_excluded_earned_income, CO-2338) are always verified at application as gross nonexempt income; a self-employment statement, and an LLC or S-corporation owner's statement of the owner's income (4.403.F), are accepted unless questionable; a basic categorically eligible household is not asked again unless questionable; at recertification only income whose source has changed or whose amount has changed by more than $50, or that is questionable.

Precision. Verification is satisfied only by documents or a collateral contact: Department of Labor wage data is not verified upon receipt (4.504.61.B.3, S821). Coverage review snap-financial CF-10: verification of exempt income "is necessary only if the income is questionable" (4.405.J) and 4.506 verifies gross nonexempt income, so wages SNAP excludes in full (a child student's earnings, work-study, the other 4.405 exclusions) do not require verification; and 4.403.F (S3121) accepts an LLC or S-corporation owner's statement of that income unless questionable, as 4.506.C does for self-employment (OQ-760 records the federal text both stand against). Coverage pass 3 C3-1: the income always verified is the earned income SNAP counts other than self-employment, read from snap_person_earned_income_other_than_self_employment (CO-4930), the same item snap_person_earned_income (CO-330) adds up, so a training allowance other than WIOA (4.403.B.1) and VISTA payments counted as earned income (4.403.A.2, C) are verified as wages are. C3-7: payments from boarders are self-employment income (4.403.2, S2963), accepted on the statement unless questionable (4.506.C) as other self-employment is. Earned-income records, step E1 (SNAP; docs/reviews/records-earnings-snap.md): the owner's pay is the month's pay records marked paid_as_business_owner, the self-employment receipts the records whose row is counted_less_costs or counted_loss_offset, and the boarders' payments snap_room_and_board_payments (CO-5117), in place of wages_from_owned_llc_or_s_corporation, self_employment_gross_receipts and room_and_board_payments_received, each of which was read as 0 when not stated; earnings not stated: cannot determine. Coverage pass 4 S4-21: the owner's pay taken off the counted wages is converted as snap_person_wages (CO-4324) converts it, so a weekly owner wage leaves nothing to verify; the records are placed as the income items place them (S4-1 to S4-4).

### CO-1377 SNAP: requires verification of unearned income `@engine`

Whether the person's unearned income must be verified for SNAP: always when received at application, as gross nonexempt income, except that a basic categorically eligible household is not asked again unless questionable; at recertification only income whose source or amount (by more than $50) has changed, or that is questionable.

Type yes/no, scope person-month, program SNAP.
Uses: `snap_determination_is_recertification`, `snap_eligibility_category`, `snap_income_changed_since_last_certification`, `snap_income_information_is_outdated`, `snap_is_household_member`, `snap_person_unearned_income`, `unearned_income_attestation_is_questionable`.

```
all of the following are true:
  - SNAP: is a household member (not excluded as an institution resident)
  - SNAP: person unearned income is more than 0
  - any of the following is true:
    - it is not the case that SNAP: eligibility category is equal to basic_categorical
    - Unearned income attestation is questionable
  - any of the following is true:
    - it is not the case that SNAP determination is a recertification
    - SNAP: income changed since last certification
    - Unearned income attestation is questionable
    - SNAP: earned or unearned income information is outdated at recertification, otherwise no
```

### CO-1378 SNAP: requires verification of resources `@engine`

Whether the person's resources must be verified for SNAP: only when questionable, and only for a household subject to the resource test (not categorically eligible). A household whose declared resources are more than the resource limit that applies needs no verification of them: its written declaration is acceptable verification (10 CCR 2506-1 4.502.A.5).

Type yes/no, scope person-month, program SNAP.
Uses: `resources_attestation_is_questionable`, `snap_eligibility_category`, `snap_household_countable_resources`, `snap_household_has_elderly_or_disabled_member_in_month`, `snap_is_household_member`, `snap_resource_limit`, `snap_resource_limit_elderly_disabled`.

  - SNAP: is a household member (not excluded as an institution resident)
  - Resources attestation is questionable
  - SNAP: eligibility category is equal to standard
  - it is not the case that SNAP: household countable resources is more than (if SNAP: household has an elderly or disabled member in the month;   then SNAP resource limit, household with an elderly or disabled member (4750); otherwise SNAP resource limit (3000))

### CO-1379 SNAP: requires verification of shelter costs `@engine`

Whether the person's claimed shelter costs must be verified for SNAP: the household's declaration is accepted unless questionable, except that a household claiming costs for a home it is temporarily not occupying verifies the actual utility costs. Colorado's mandatory standard utility allowance leaves no claim of actual utility costs above the standard to verify.

Precision. An unverified expense does not deny the household; it is left out of the shelter deduction (273.2(f)(3)(ii), S812). Coverage pass 3 C3-3: the amount tested is the stated shelter costs SNAP counts (snap_person_stated_shelter_costs, CO-4931), the other continuing charges of 4.407.3.E (CO-4345) included, so questionable charges that are a household's only shelter cost are verified (4.507.B.1: "unless questionable"), and an unverified one is left out after the thirtieth day by CO-2300.

Type yes/no, scope person-month, program SNAP.
Uses: `claims_shelter_costs_for_unoccupied_home`, `shelter_costs_attestation_is_questionable`, `snap_is_household_member`, `snap_person_stated_shelter_costs`.

```
all of the following are true:
  - SNAP: is a household member (not excluded as an institution resident)
  - SNAP: person's stated shelter costs is more than 0
  - any of the following is true:
    - Shelter costs attestation is questionable
    - Claims shelter costs for an unoccupied home
```

all of the following are true:
  - SNAP: is a household member (not excluded as an institution resident)
  - SNAP: is elderly or disabled
  - SNAP: medical expenses is more than 0
  - any of the following is true:
    - it is not the case that SNAP determination is a recertification
    - SNAP allowable medical expenses source changed since last certification
    - (SNAP: medical expenses minus SNAP medical expenses at last certification) is more than SNAP recertification expense change threshold (25)
    - (SNAP medical expenses at last certification minus SNAP: medical expenses) is more than SNAP recertification expense change threshold (25)
    - SNAP: allowable medical expenses information is outdated at recertification, otherwise no

### CO-1393 SNAP: expedited postponement end date `@engine`

The last day of the period in which a household certified under expedited service may complete postponed verification: the application date plus snap_expedited_postponed_verification_days; for a migrant household needing out-of-state verification, which the thirtieth-day termination does not reach, the end of the month of participation snap_expedited_postponement_months_early (CO-3037) names for an application on or before the day of snap_expedited_late_application_day (CO-3036), or snap_expedited_postponement_months_late (CO-3038) for one after it.

Precision. Colorado elects thirty days for households applying before and after the fifteenth alike (4.205.11.B.2.b, S835); the federal second and third months of 7 CFR 273.2(i)(4)(iii)(A)-(B) (S1310) are permissive outer limits ("may be postponed"), so the thirty days stand (OQ-323). Case worker review (OQ-323): a migrant household needing out-of-state verification (CO-2570) is not terminated on the thirtieth day (4.205.11.B.2.b); its period is read as the federal outer limit of 7 CFR 273.2(i)(4)(iii)(A)-(B), through the last day of the second month of participation (application on or before the fifteenth) or the third (after it), the application month being the first. Vocabulary fix round (docs/reviews/vocabulary-reuse.md, R-13): reads snap_application_date (CO-1746), not the Medical Assistance application date.

Type calendar date, scope person, program SNAP.

if SNAP: is a migrant household needing out-of-state verification, otherwise no
  then -1 days after the first day of (if SNAP: application date is more than SNAP expedited service: day of the month after which an application is late in the month (15) minus 1 days after the first day of the month containing SNAP: application date;   then SNAP expedited service: month of participation verification may be postponed to, late-month application (3); otherwise SNAP expedited service: month of participation verification may be postponed to, early-month application (2)) months after the month containing SNAP: application date

### CO-1394 SNAP: verification status `@engine`

Where this person's SNAP household stands on verification: not applicable (the person is not a member of a SNAP household); no verification required; complete; complete except that a sponsored non-citizen's sponsor information is outstanding, or a non-citizen's status documents, forty quarters or military connection, or a questionable citizen's proof of citizenship (4.505.51.C; snap_is_ineligible_pending_citizenship_verification, CO-4251), are still outstanding after the documentation due date, so that member is ineligible until they are provided and the rest of the household is determined (members excluded, 4.505.7.B-C, 4.505.6.F, I; snap_is_ineligible_pending_non_citizen_verification, CO-4154); postponed under expedited service (identity verified, other verification outstanding, within the postponement period, and the verification postponed at the last expedited certification completed, 4.205.11.C; snap_prior_expedited_postponed_verification_incomplete, CO-4254); pending within the time allowed (ten days from the request, to the thirtieth day after application when only a non-citizen's status document is outstanding, and to the thirtieth day after application when only deductible expenses are); past that time with only deductible expenses unverified (the deductions are disallowed); or past the time allowed with an eligibility factor unverified.

Precision. past_due states only that the time allowed has run with a required factor unverified; when the agency denies (on the thirtieth day, or after a notice of pending status) is application processing and outside this item: 7 CFR 273.2(h)(1)(i)(C) (S813) makes the delay the household's once at least 10 days from the request have passed (OQ-309 resolved). The due date and the household's request date are the evaluated person's. Final verification pass 2 N-2 (F-18): an eligible alien status element still pending after the member's own documentation due date (snap_noncitizen_documentation_due_date, CO-1617) is counted with the sponsor element for members_excluded, since the member is then ineligible and the rest of the household is determined (4.505.6.I); before that date it is pending as before.

### CO-1500 SNAP: standard utility allowance `@engine`

The one standard utility allowance Colorado's four-tiered mandatory SUA gives the person's SNAP household - the Heating and Cooling Utility Allowance when the household is entitled to it; otherwise the Basic Utility Allowance for at least snap_bua_min_utility_cost_count (CO-3042) non-heating, non-cooling utility costs; otherwise the One Utility Allowance for one such cost other than a telephone; otherwise the telephone allowance when the telephone is the only utility cost; otherwise nothing - per 10 CCR 2506-1 4.407.31. A household receives only one of the four allowances and cannot claim actual utility expenses. Internet connection fees never enter it (4.407.3.E.5; Pub. L. 119-21 sec. 10104).

Precision. Household-level, once for the case: the utility facts are neutral facts about the home (CO-3300 to CO-3306, CO-1242, CO-1240), stated once in the case's case_facts, so every member of the household evaluates to the same figure, which snap_shelter_costs (CO-377) adds once. A heating arrangement or a utility the case does not state is read as not incurred (rule 12: unstated utility facts read as none, as before), so a case stating none gets no allowance. A case may still state this amount directly on a person, which the engine uses for that person in place of the rule. A household sharing utility costs with another SNAP household receives the full allowance (4.407.31.A.1.d, B.2, C.2, D.1), which needs no separate term. Time audit T-3: per month, so the figure is the one in force in the month evaluated (docs/operators.md, Resolution step 2); as a per-person item it gave the determination date's figure in every month. Coverage pass 4 S4-14 (decision 4 checked): the home's utility costs not stated are read as not incurred, the rule giving that reading: a deduction is given only for an expense the household claims and shows, and an expense not shown is left out (10 CCR 2506-1 4.502.A.3, S818: "the household's eligibility and benefit level will be determined without providing a deduction or exclusion for the claimed but unverified expense"; 7 CFR 273.2(f)(3)(ii), S812), so a utility cost not claimed gives no utility allowance.

Type money, scope person-month, program SNAP.
Uses: `home_incurs_telephone_cost`, `snap_bua_min_utility_cost_count`, `snap_entitled_to_heating_cooling_allowance`, `snap_non_heating_utility_cost_count`, `snap_sua_basic`, `snap_sua_heating_cooling`, `snap_sua_one_utility`, `snap_sua_telephone`.

```
if SNAP: entitled to the heating and cooling utility allowance, otherwise no
  then SNAP heating and cooling standard utility allowance (616)
else if SNAP: number of non-heating utility costs is at least SNAP Basic Utility Allowance: fewest non-heating utility costs (2)
  then SNAP basic utility allowance (390)
else if all of the following are true:
    - SNAP: number of non-heating utility costs is more than 0
    - it is not the case that (all of the following are true:;   - SNAP: number of non-heating utility costs is equal to 1;   - Home incurs telephone cost, otherwise no)
  then SNAP one utility allowance (73)
else if SNAP: number of non-heating utility costs is equal to 1
  then SNAP telephone allowance (100)
otherwise 0
```

### CO-1616 SNAP: requires verification of sponsor information `@engine`

Whether the income and resources of a sponsored non-citizen's sponsor (and the sponsor's spouse), the other non-citizens the sponsor supports, the sponsor's dependents and contact details must be verified for SNAP: for a sponsored household member, at application and recertification, except where a basic categorically eligible household's conferring program verified them.

Precision. Asked only where sponsor deeming applies (snap_sponsor_deeming_applies, CO-2337: none of the exemptions of 4.305.2.E, and not a child under 18). Unverified sponsor information makes only the sponsored member ineligible (4.505.7.B), which snap_is_ineligible_pending_non_citizen_verification (CO-4154) applies to eligibility (final verification pass 2 N-2); snap_verification_status (CO-1394) reports members_excluded when nothing else is pending (phase-10 sweep, OQ-380). The basic categorical exception reads snap_meets_bce_eligibility (CO-338), the category snap_eligibility_category (CO-341) tries first, except for a household returning after a substantial winnings disqualification, which is Standard Eligibility (CO-4153); reading the category itself would make this item, and CO-4154, depend on the household's income test, which counts the member as eligible or not. Coverage pass 3 N3-2: not asked for a member whose household has said documentation of the member's status cannot or will not be provided (declines_to_provide_immigration_documentation, CO-4687): 4.505.6.J (S902) classifies the member as an ineligible non-citizen and the office makes no further efforts, and no sponsor income or resources are deemed (CO-3701, CO-3702). ### CO-1702 SNAP: self-employment income `@engine`

The person's monthly net self-employment income for SNAP under 7 CFR 273.9(b)(1)(ii), 273.11(a)(2) and 10 CCR 2506-1 4.403.11: the gross receipts of the business (snap_self_employment_gross_receipts, CO-5114) less its allowable costs (snap_self_employment_costs, CO-1701), not below zero, plus the farm's gross receipts (snap_farm_gross_receipts, CO-5115) less the farm's costs (snap_farm_costs, CO-5116), not below zero; for self-employment that is the household's annual support (snap_self_employment_is_averaged, CO-4329), each net averaged over the averaging months (snap_self_employment_averaging_months, CO-4349) (10 CCR 2506-1 4.402.2.A.1, 4.403.11.A, 4.403.12).

Precision. Capital gains from the sale of business equipment are counted in full under 273.11(a)(3); state them in the gross receipts. A farm loss is offset against the household's other income by snap_farm_self_employment_loss (CO-3722), snap_farm_loss_offset_against_self_employment (CO-3724) and snap_farm_loss_remaining (CO-3725) (final verification F-8; 273.11(a)(2)(ii)). Coverage review snap-financial CF-3: an enterprise that is the household's annual support is averaged over its past twelve months, or the months since it began (4.403.12.A, C, D; S3114), each month's receipts and costs read for that month; an averaged net loss gives 0 here, and a farmer's averaged loss is offset by CO-3722. Self-employment that is part support is read month by month, as stated. Earned-income records, step E1 (SNAP; docs/reviews/records-earnings-snap.md): the business and the farm are each their own receipts and costs (before, one business per person, a farm by a person fact); a loss of the business other than a farm is not offset against the farm's net or other income (273.11(a)(2)(ii) offsets a farm's loss only). Earnings not stated: cannot determine. Coverage pass 4 S4-17: for averaged self-employment, the capital gains received in the past months averaged are taken out of them (snap_self_employment_capital_gains, CO-6605) and the capital gains anticipated in the twelve months beginning with the application month are added at a twelfth (snap_anticipated_capital_gains, CO-6606; 4.403.11.D, S4730); a business that is not averaged counts a capital gain in the month it is received (4.403.11.D, last paragraph).

Type money, scope person-month, program SNAP.
Uses: `snap_anticipated_capital_gains`, `snap_farm_costs`, `snap_farm_gross_receipts`, `snap_self_employment_averaging_months`, `snap_self_employment_capital_gains`, `snap_self_employment_costs`, `snap_self_employment_gross_receipts`, `snap_self_employment_is_averaged`.

otherwise (the greater of 0 and (SNAP: self-employment gross receipts minus SNAP: self-employment costs)) plus (the greater of 0 and (SNAP: farm gross receipts minus SNAP: farm costs))

The legally obligated child support the person pays that SNAP excludes from the person's gross income for the month: with a history of at least snap_child_support_averaging_months (CO-3039) months of payments, the average of the payments in that many months before the month; otherwise the month's anticipated payment, which is the estimate 4.407.5.E calls for.

### CO-2300 SNAP: counted shelter cost of a member `@engine`

The part of the shelter costs billed to or paid by this household member (shelter_cost_monthly) that counts as a shelter cost of the household: all of it for an eligible member and for a member disqualified for IPV or fraud, a work-requirement sanction (a voluntary quit included) or as a fleeing felon or probation or parole violator; for a member whose income is prorated (an ineligible non-citizen, an SSN refusal, an ABAWD at the time limit), the cost divided evenly among every household member, the ineligible members included, less the shares of the members whose income is prorated (7 CFR 273.11(c)(2)(iii); snap_prorated_member_share_counted_rate, CO-7250); nothing for an ineligible student, who is not a household member, or for any other ineligible member.

Precision. n is the count of snap_household_members, the disqualified members included, as in snap_counted_income_of_ineligible_member (CO-333). Each prorated member's cost loses the shares of every prorated member, the reading CO-333 gives the income of 4.411.1.B.2.b. The standard utility allowance is not prorated (4.411.1.B.2.c); snap_shelter_costs (CO-377) adds it once in full. A drug-felony disqualification counts nothing, matching CO-333, which counts none of that member's income. Unknown when this member's shelter_cost_monthly is unstated. Engineering follow-up 5: a prorated member with no household (snap_household_members empty, as for a person who is not a household member) has nothing counted to any household, so the share is 0 rather than a division by zero. Final verification F-10 (V-5): once the expense verification period has ended (snap_expense_verification_period_has_ended, CO-3739) with this member's shelter costs still required to be verified and unverified (snap_shelter_costs_verification_is_pending, CO-1612, required only when questionable or for an unoccupied home), nothing counts: 4.502.A.3 (S818) and 7 CFR 273.2(f)(3)(ii) (S812) determine eligibility and benefit "without providing a deduction ... for the unverified expense". The standard utility allowance is not an expense to verify (4.407.31) and stays. Final verification F-6: n counts the members other than an ineligible student (snap_household_members_other_than_ineligible_students, CO-3714), whom 4.411.2.C (S2508) treats as a non-household member not considered in the allotment. Coverage review snap-financial CF-15: the other continuing charges 4.407.3.E.1-3 allows (condominium and association fees, mobile home loans, second mortgages and home equity loans, reverse mortgage repayments, disaster repairs; S3126) are added to the member's rent or mortgage, taxes and insurance (shelter_other_continuing_charges, CO-4345, read as 0 when not stated). Coverage pass 3 C3-3: the stated costs are read from snap_person_stated_shelter_costs (CO-4931), the sum the shelter-cost verification (CO-1379) also reads. Coverage pass 6 for SNAP, C6-1 (docs/reviews/coverage6-snap.md): with two or more prorated members in the household, every prorated member's share is left out, not only this member's own: the fraction counted is snap_prorated_member_share_counted_rate (CO-7250), (n - k) / n with k the prorated members, as 7 CFR 273.11(c)(2)(ii)-(iii) (S4970) says ("All but the ineligible members' share is counted"). Before, (n - 1) / n was counted whatever k was.

Type money, scope person-month, program SNAP.
Uses: `snap_expense_verification_period_has_ended`, `snap_is_disqualified_member_counted_in_full`, `snap_is_ineligible_member`, `snap_is_ineligible_member_prorated`, `snap_person_stated_shelter_costs`, `snap_prorated_member_share_counted_rate`, `snap_shelter_costs_verification_is_pending`.

```
if all of the following are true:
    - SNAP: shelter costs verification is pending
    - SNAP: expense verification period has ended
  then 0
else if it is not the case that SNAP: is an ineligible member
  then SNAP: person's stated shelter costs
else if SNAP: is a disqualified member whose income and expenses count in full
  then SNAP: person's stated shelter costs
else if SNAP: is an ineligible member whose income is prorated
  then (if SNAP: share of a prorated member's income and expenses counted is equal to 0;   then 0; otherwise SNAP: person's stated shelter costs times SNAP: share of a prorated member's income and expenses counted)
otherwise 0

The person is a household member disqualified for an intentional program violation or fraud, for a work-requirement sanction (a voluntary quit included), as a fleeing felon or probation or parole violator, for a drug-related felony, or as a convicted felon under 7 CFR 273.11(s): the disqualifications of 10 CCR 2506-1 4.411.1.B.1 and 7 CFR 273.11(c)(1), whose income and resources count in their entirety and whose deductible expenses are allowed in their entirety.

Precision. CDHS review B-4: 4.411.1.B.1 names IPV, work sanctions and fleeing felons; 7 CFR 273.11(c)(1) (S1813) adds the felony drug conviction and the convicted felons of 273.11(s), which Colorado's list omits, so they count in full here as the federal rule requires (before this round a drug-felony member's income was not counted at all). Both read as false when not stated, as snap_is_ineligible_member (CO-311) already tests them. Coverage pass 2 N2-P2-2: the fleeing felon arm reads Colorado's four-part test (snap_is_fleeing_felon, CO-4683; 4.304.4.B, S3066) in place of the federal definition alone (is_fleeing_felon, CO-038). Coverage pass 4 for SNAP S4-11 (OQ-1263 resolved): per month, since prospective budgeting reads "anticipated income and circumstances during the issuance month" (10 CCR 2506-1 4.402.1.A, S4734): the voluntary quit (CO-2318) is the month's. Before, the item was per person and read on the determination date in every month.

Type yes/no, scope person-month, program SNAP.
Uses: `snap_is_disqualified_convicted_felon`, `snap_is_disqualified_drug_felony`, `snap_is_disqualified_for_voluntary_quit`, `snap_is_disqualified_for_work_requirement_noncompliance`, `snap_is_fleeing_felon`, `snap_is_probation_or_parole_violator`, `snap_is_serving_ipv_disqualification`.

any of the following is true:
  - SNAP: is serving an intentional program violation disqualification
  - Is disqualified for work-requirement noncompliance

  - SNAP: fleeing felon under the four-part test
  - SNAP: is a probation or parole violator
  - SNAP: is disqualified for a drug-related felony, otherwise no
  - SNAP: is disqualified as a convicted felon (conduct after February 7, 2014), otherwise no

### CO-2305 SNAP: is the initial month `@engine`

The month is the household's initial month of application: the month containing the date of application, or the later date benefits begin after a household-caused delay (snap_benefits_begin_date, CO-4269; 4.205.31, 4.205.4.A, 4.209.1.D), when the determination is not a recertification applied for before the certification period expired (10 CCR 2506-1 4.000.1 "Initial month of application") and the household is not a migrant or seasonal farmworker household in the job stream with a break in participation of thirty days or less (4.207.2.B).

### CO-2307 SNAP: full month allotment `@engine`

This person's SNAP household's allotment for a full month - the maximum allotment less the benefit reduction, rounded down to the nearest dollar (10 CCR 2506-1 4.207.3.A.3) and floored at $0, with a one- or two-person household that meets the net income test receiving at least the minimum allotment (4.207.3.C), and never more than it would receive with its disqualified members counted in its size (7 CFR 273.11(c)(1)(ii)) - the benefit for every month except an initial month, and the full month's benefit an initial month is prorated from. Nothing in a month the household fails an eligibility gate (snap_household_ineligibility_ground, CO-4680) - no eligible member, FDPIR participation, a refusal to cooperate, substantial lottery or gambling winnings, a transfer of resources, a striking member when it was not eligible the day before the strike, or the gross income, net income or resource test.

Precision. The minimum allotment floor applies only to a household of snap_minimum_allotment_household_size_limit (2) or fewer eligible members that passes every applicable eligibility test - the gross income test, the net income test, and the resource test - not the net income test alone; a household that fails any of those tests is not "eligible" within the meaning of S104's "all eligible one-person and two-person households" and gets $0, not the floor. A three-or-more-member household whose maximum-allotment-less-reduction is $0 (or negative, already floored at $0) simply receives $0; whether that household is denied depends on categorical eligibility (snap_eligibility_status, CO-387; OQ-26 resolved). Rounding down is written as the negated ceiling of the negated difference, the shape the volume uses for a floor. Final verification pass 2: a month disqualified for substantial winnings (snap_household_has_substantial_lottery_winnings, CO-4152; N-1) or for a knowing transfer of resources (snap_is_disqualified_for_resource_transfer, CO-4160; N-4) has no allotment; the result is capped at snap_allotment_cap_for_disqualified_members (CO-4182; N-7), which is the household's maximum allotment, and so never binds, when no member is left out of the size as disqualified. A household with no eligible member has no allotment (it was cannot determine, since the tables have no row for a size of 0): N-2 makes such households, every member awaiting non-citizen verification, a case the volume now meets. Coverage review snap-financial CF-9: 4.207.3.A determines the allotment "After eligibility has been established" (S3122); the striker condition of 7 CFR 273.1(e) (snap_household_meets_striker_condition, CO-3504; S1816), which snap_is_eligible (CO-386) and snap_eligibility_status (CO-387) test, was missing here, so a striker's ineligible household was issued its computed allotment. Coverage pass 2 N2-1: the eligibility gates are read from snap_household_ineligibility_ground (CO-4680), the one list that snap_is_eligible (CO-386), snap_eligibility_status (CO-387) and both allotment items share, so the FDPIR (4.303.B) and refusal-to-cooperate (7 U.S.C. 2015(c)) bars, added to the status alone in the coverage round, now give no allotment either, and a bar added later reaches all four.

Type money, scope person-month, program SNAP.
Uses: `snap_allotment_before_minimum_and_cap`, `snap_allotment_cap_for_disqualified_members`, `snap_eligible_household_size`, `snap_household_ineligibility_ground`, `snap_meets_net_income_test`, `snap_minimum_allotment`, `snap_minimum_allotment_household_size_limit`.

```
if it is not the case that SNAP: household ineligibility ground is equal to none
  then 0
else if all of the following are true:
    - SNAP: number of eligible household members is at most SNAP minimum allotment household size limit (2)
    - SNAP: meets the net income test
  then the lesser of SNAP: allotment cap for excluded disqualified members and (the greater of SNAP: allotment before the minimum and the cap and SNAP minimum allotment (25))
otherwise the lesser of SNAP: allotment cap for excluded disqualified members and SNAP: allotment before the minimum and the cap
```

### CO-2308 SNAP: prorated initial month allotment `@engine`

The household's benefit for its initial month before the test that issues nothing below snap_initial_month_minimum_issuance ($10; final verification F-1): the full month's benefit without the one- and two-person minimum (which applies "Except for an initial month", 4.207.3.C) and never more than the household would receive with its members disqualified under 7 CFR 273.11(c)(1) counted (snap_full_month_allotment_before_minimum, CO-6002), times the number of days from the date benefits begin (the date of application, or the later date a household-caused delay sets: snap_benefits_begin_date, CO-4269) through the end of the month, divided by the number of days in the month, rounded down to the lower whole dollar; $0 when the household fails the gross income, net income or resource test, or in a month it is disqualified for substantial winnings or a transfer of resources or has a striking member when it was not eligible the day before the strike.

Precision. Days from the application date to the first day of the next month equal 4.207.2.C's "Number of days in month plus one" less "the date of application". 4.207.2.C does not state the rounding; 7 CFR 273.10(a)(1)(iii)(C) rounds the product down, and the floor is written as the negated ceiling of the negated value. Final verification pass 2 N-2: a household with no eligible member has no allotment, as in the full month (CO-2307). Coverage review snap-financial CF-9: the full month (CO-2307) withheld the allotment for substantial winnings (N-1) and a transfer disqualification (N-4) but this item did not, so the initial month of a transfer disqualification (4.408.2.B: "The period of disqualification shall begin in the month of application", S2962) issued its prorated benefit; 4.207.3.A determines the allotment only "After eligibility has been established" (S3122). The striker condition (7 CFR 273.1(e), S1816) is gated here too. Coverage pass 2 N2-1: the eligibility gates are read from snap_household_ineligibility_ground (CO-4680), the one list that snap_is_eligible (CO-386), snap_eligibility_status (CO-387) and both allotment items share, so the FDPIR (4.303.B) and refusal-to-cooperate (7 U.S.C. 2015(c)) bars, added to the status alone in the coverage round, now give no allotment either, and a bar added later reaches all four.

Type money, scope person-month, program SNAP.
Uses: `snap_benefits_begin_date`, `snap_full_month_allotment_before_minimum`, `snap_household_ineligibility_ground`.

```
if it is not the case that SNAP: household ineligibility ground is equal to none
  then 0
otherwise 0 minus (0 minus ((SNAP: full month allotment before the minimum times (the number of days from SNAP: benefits begin date to the first day of the month after the month)) divided by (the number of days from the first day of the month to the first day of the month after the month)) rounded up to a whole number)
```

### CO-2318 SNAP: is disqualified for a voluntary quit `@engine`

The person is serving a SNAP disqualification for a voluntary quit in the month evaluated: the quit without good cause (snap_voluntary_quit_date) occurred within sixty days before the date of application or any time after it (4.308.B), and the month evaluated falls in the disqualification period, which begins in snap_voluntary_quit_disqualification_start_month and lasts one month the first time, three the second and six the third or a later time (4.310.8.A-B). The person is then a disqualified member (4.310.8.A). A person who becomes exempt from the work requirements during the period is eligible again (4.310.8.C-D; 7 CFR 273.7(j)(4)): the disqualification is not served while the person is exempt from work registration (snap_is_exempt_from_work_registration, CO-405).

Precision. False when no voluntary quit is stated. The sixty days count back from snap_application_date (CO-1746). Coverage pass 4 for SNAP S4-11 (OQ-1263 resolved): read for the month evaluated, since prospective budgeting reads "anticipated income and circumstances during the issuance month" (10 CCR 2506-1 4.402.1.A, S4734), so each month of the period is a month of disqualification and a month outside it is not; before, the determination month's answer was read in every month, since the disqualified-member items it feeds (snap_is_ineligible_member, CO-311) were stated per person. Coverage review C-8: the exemption is read as of the determination, not from "the date exemption information was provided to the local office" (4.310.8.D, S3058); a determination made after the member becomes exempt and reports it is the one that ends the disqualification. Coverage pass 3 N3-P2-2: a person 15 or younger or 60 or older is exempt from work registration (4.310.3.A, S126), so a disqualification is not served once the person turns 60 (4.310.8.C-D); the age range is read here (snap_work_registration_min_age, snap_work_registration_max_age, as CO-406 reads it), since snap_is_exempt_from_work_registration (CO-405) carries only the other exemptions and is also read by CO-414 and Medicaid. Coverage pass 4 S4-11: the age exemptions are read in the month and met on any day of it (OQ-1262; docs/operators.md, Ages in a month): younger than 16 on the first day (the age on the first day of the month), 60 or older on the last day (the age on the last day of the month); before, the age on the determination date. Three-pattern sweep D-4 (docs/reviews/pattern-sweep-snap-ce.md): the age exemption reads date_of_birth as stated, required where read (decision 4): before, an unstated date of birth was read as an age inside the work registration range, so a stated quit disqualified a person whose age could not be known.

Type yes/no, scope person-month, program SNAP.
Uses: `date_of_birth`, `snap_application_date`, `snap_is_exempt_from_work_registration`, `snap_level_sanction_first_months`, `snap_level_sanction_second_months`, `snap_level_sanction_third_months`, `snap_voluntary_quit_date`, `snap_voluntary_quit_disqualification_start_month`, `snap_voluntary_quit_lookback_days`, `snap_work_registration_max_age`, `snap_work_registration_min_age`, `snap_work_requirement_violation_number`.

### CO-2335 SNAP: battered non-citizen exemption from sponsor deeming applies `@engine`

This sponsored non-citizen is exempt from sponsor deeming under 10 CCR 2506-1 4.305.2.E.5: a child of a battered parent; or a battered non-citizen (spouse, parent of a battered child or child of a battered non-citizen, is_victim_of_battery_or_extreme_cruelty, CO-2363) who does not live with the batterer (lives_with_batterer, CO-2718), within snap_battered_non_citizen_exemption_months (CO-2720) of the county's finding that the battery is substantially connected to the need for benefits (battery_substantial_connection_finding_date, CO-2717), or later where a court or the immigration service has recognized it (CO-2719).

Precision. The twelve months are counted in calendar months from the month of the finding (snap_battered_non_citizen_exemption_months, CO-2720): the exemption runs through the eleventh month after it. A child of a battered parent is exempt whatever the twelve-month and living-arrangement conditions, as E.5's first sentence says. If the battery is not stated, SNAP reads it as false. Three-pattern sweep T-2 (docs/reviews/pattern-sweep-snap-ce.md): per month, reading the twelve months against the month evaluated, since prospective budgeting reads "anticipated income and circumstances during the issuance month" (10 CCR 2506-1 4.402.1.A, S4734) and the exemption of E.5 runs "during a twelve (12) month period after the local office determines" the connection. Before, the item was per person and compared the determination month, so the sponsor was not deemed in a certification month after the twelve months ended (probe CO-941). Coverage pass 7 for SNAP, C7-5 (docs/reviews/coverage7-snap.md): the twelve months begin with the month of the finding, not before it: 4.305.2.E.5 (S1619) exempts the sponsor's income "during a twelve (12) month period after the local office determines that the battering is substantially connected", so an application month before a finding made at the determination is not exempt by the finding (the court or immigration service recognition arm is unchanged). The finding's month itself is exempt (a status that makes a person eligible holds for the month if it holds on any day of it, OQ-1405). Before, a finding made in November exempted an October application month too.
