### CO-2337 SNAP: sponsor deeming applies `@engine`

The sponsor's (and sponsor's spouse's) income and resources are deemed to this person for SNAP: the person is a sponsored non-citizen (an affidavit of support executed on or after December 19, 1997, is_sponsored_non_citizen) who is not a member of the sponsor's SNAP household, is not sponsored by an organization, is not indigent, is not exempt as a battered non-citizen, whose sponsor has not died, and who has not worked or been credited with forty quarters under Title II (10 CCR 2506-1 4.305.2.A, E), and who is not under snap_sponsor_deeming_child_age_limit (18): the sponsor deeming provisions do not apply "to any alien who is under 18 years of age" (7 U.S.C. 2014(i)(2)(E); 8 U.S.C. 1631(d)(3)).

Precision. A non-citizen who needs no sponsor (a refugee, parolee, asylee or Cuban or Haitian entrant, E.3) or who has naturalized (E.6) has no affidavit of support in force and states is_sponsored_non_citizen false. The forty quarters are snap_creditable_qualifying_quarters (CO-4262): qualifying_quarters, which already includes quarters credited from a spouse or parent, less the post-1996 quarters in which a federal means-tested benefit was received (coverage review C-5), against federal_qualifying_quarters_threshold (CO-3033). Only an eligible sponsored non-citizen has the sponsor's income deemed (4.305.2.C); snap_requires_verification_of_sponsor (CO-1616) reads this item for a household member, so no sponsor verification is asked for a child under 18. The citizen child of 7 CFR 273.4(c)(3)(vii) is never sponsored; its share is taken out by the division (snap_sponsor_deeming_divisor, CO-3708), as is the share of a sponsored child exempt by age, who stays one of the sponsor's non-citizens in the divisor (273.4(c)(2)(v)). Final verification F-2 applied the narrower federal exemption of a sponsored child under 18 whose parent is also sponsored (273.4(c)(3)(vi), S2503); final verification pass 2 N-3: the statute exempts every child under 18 (S2958-S2960), so the parent test is dropped. Age is the age on the determination date, as for every person-scope item. Coverage pass 4 for SNAP S4-11 (OQ-1263 resolved): the age is read in the month evaluated, since prospective budgeting reads "anticipated income and circumstances during the issuance month" (10 CCR 2506-1 4.402.1.A, S4734); the exemption of "any alien who is under 18 years of age" is met when met on any day of the month (OQ-1262; docs/operators.md, Ages in a month), so deeming applies from the month after the 18th birthday, unless the birthday is the first day (the age on the first day of the month). Before, the age on the determination date in every month. Three-pattern sweep T-3 (docs/reviews/pattern-sweep-snap-ce.md): E.7 ("A person whose sponsor has died") is read in the month evaluated: every sponsor (sponsors, CO-2713) has died by the end of the month (is_deceased, CO-2200, per month), since prospective budgeting reads the circumstances of the issuance month (4.402.1.A, S4734). Before, the item read sponsor_has_died (CO-2336), the deaths as of the determination month, so a sponsor who died in a later month of the certification was still deemed.

### CO-2338 SNAP: excluded earned income `@engine`

The part of this person's earned income for the month that SNAP does not count: all the earnings of an elementary or secondary student under the age of parental control (snap_student_earnings_are_excluded, CO-2569; 4.405.C, 273.9(c)(7)), pay and self-employment alike; otherwise the pay snap_person_wages (CO-4324) holds that snap_person_counted_wages (CO-5113) does not count: work-study (4.403.A.1, 4.405.1), WIOA on-the-job training earnings of a member under 19 who lives with a parent or is under parental control (4.405.2.A.6, 4.403.B.2), summer youth employment and training wages (A.6), Senior Community Service Employment Program pay (A.9), combat pay (A.12), mandatory military education deductions (A.13), in-kind pay (7 CFR 273.9(c)(1)), infrequent or irregular pay when the quarter's infrequent or irregular income is no more than snap_irregular_income_quarterly_limit (4.405.A), and, in a destitute household's month of application, the pay received after the date of application (4.406.1.A).

Precision. Earned-income records, step E1 (SNAP; docs/reviews/records-earnings-snap.md): the excluded part is the whole pay less the counted pay, both summed record by record with the same conversion (CO-4324 and CO-5113 are registered siblings), so an exclusion is converted exactly as its pay is and is never subtracted from a figure that does not hold it. Irregular self-employment receipts within the quarter's limit are left out of the business's gross receipts (snap_self_employment_gross_receipts, CO-5114), not here. The Domestic Volunteer Service Act Title I (VISTA) payments and training allowances other than WIOA, which SNAP counts as earned income, are receipts (snap_receipt_treatment_table: counted_as_earned) that snap_person_earned_income_other_than_self_employment (CO-4930) adds (coverage review snap-financial CF-1). Earnings not stated: cannot determine; a stated empty list is 0.

Type money, scope person-month, program SNAP.
Uses: `snap_person_counted_wages`, `snap_person_wages`, `snap_self_employment_income`, `snap_student_earnings_are_excluded`.

if SNAP: earnings are excluded as a child student's
  then SNAP: person wages plus SNAP: self-employment income
otherwise SNAP: person wages minus SNAP: counted wages
```

This person is an ABAWD (able-bodied adult without dependents) who has used the three countable months of the thirty-six-month period and has neither regained eligibility nor entered the additional three months, so is ineligible to participate in SNAP while the household stays eligible (10 CCR 2506-1 4.304.4.A.5, 4.411.1.A; 7 CFR 273.11(c)(2)): snap_abawd_time_limit_status (CO-418) is limit_reached in the month evaluated.

### CO-2569 SNAP: earnings are excluded as a child student's `@engine`

This household member is an elementary or secondary school student at least half time who lives with a parent or is under the parental control of a household member other than a parent, and turned eighteen no earlier than in the month, so the person's earned income for the month is excluded from SNAP income (10 CCR 2506-1 4.405.C; 7 CFR 273.9(c)(7)).

Precision. A parent in the household is any parent this person has in the case (exists_related over the child role); 7 CFR 273.1(b)(1)(ii) makes a person under 22 living with a parent a member of the parent's household, so a parent in the case is a parent in the household. Reading snap_household_members instead made a dependency cycle (household -> elderly/disabled separate-household election -> gross income -> this item), fixed at the phase-12 merge; parental control by another member is snap_is_under_parental_control_of_household_member. Earnings that cannot be told apart from other members' (the proration in 273.9(c)(7)'s last sentence) are not modeled; a case states such a share in snap_excluded_earned_income. Same-word audit SW-1: a stepparent is read from the stepparent role ("natural, adoptive, or stepparent", S1817). Same-word audit SW-7 (convention rule 17): an edge joins persons who live together (lives_with, CO-1925, from dwelling_id); where a case states no dwelling_id the edge is read as living together, as before. Coverage review snap-financial CF-5: 4.405.C (S3101) excludes the income "until the month following the month in which the student turns eighteen (18)", in the month of application as in any month of the certification period, so the age is the age on the last day of the month before the month evaluated (under 18 then means the eighteenth birthday falls in the month or later), not the age on the determination date; the item is per month. Coverage pass 2 C2-3: 4.405.C and 7 CFR 273.9(c)(7) exclude the earnings of students "at least half-time" (S3101), so a child enrolled less_than_half_time (education_enrollment_intensity, CO-2881's fact) has the earnings counted; an elementary or secondary student whose intensity is not stated is read as at least half time, the ordinary school attendance. Coverage pass 4 S4-14 (decision 4 of 2026-11-23): education_enrollment_intensity is read with no default where this rule reads it (only for an elementary or secondary student; 4.405.C and 7 CFR 273.9(c)(7) exclude the earnings of students "at least half-time" and give no reading for an intensity not stated); before, it was read as at least half time when not stated. The intensity is read only for a student under 18 with pay or business receipts in the month: a student with no earnings has nothing to exclude (coverage pass 4 S4-14). Three-pattern sweep D-1 (docs/reviews/pattern-sweep-snap-ce.md): lives_with (CO-1925) is read as stated, required where read: no text on file says that persons related on the application live together unless it says otherwise (7 CFR 273.1(a): a household is individuals who live together and customarily purchase and prepare meals together, S1), so a stated relationship is no longer read as living together where no dwelling_id is stated (decision 4; docs/conventions.md rule 17, as MAGI's readers since coverage pass 6, C6-10); a case with persons related across the edge states dwelling_id for each of them. Coverage pass 7 for SNAP, C7-4 (docs/reviews/coverage7-snap.md): the exclusion is for a student "attending school" and continues through a break only "provided the child's enrollment will resume following the break" (7 CFR 273.9(c)(7), S3101; 10 CCR 2506-1 4.405.C, S1817; 4.306.C, S5092: enrollment is continuous "unless the student graduates"), so a month whose first day is after the student's expected_program_completion_date (CO-2882, graduation) has no exclusion, the test the three-pattern sweep's T-11 gave the ineligible-student rule and the work registration exemption (CO-405, CO-411); with no completion date stated the enrollment continues, as both texts deem it. Before, a 17-year-old who graduated in December kept her earnings excluded in January (probe GRAD17: January $725 where the text gives $509). Coverage pass 7, C7-1 (docs/reviews/coverage7-snap.md): living together is read for the month (snap_lives_with_in_month, CO-7672), not from the homes of the determination date in every month: a member who moved out after the application month lived in the home in the months that began before the date the two ceased to live together (CO-7352, CO-7506, CO-7670), and one who moved in after it did not live there before (CO-7671), since the application month is determined on "the household's circumstances for the entire month of application" (7 CFR 273.10(a)(1)(i), S5091).

The person meets one of the disability-based prongs of the 7 CFR 271.2 "elderly or disabled member" definition and 10 CCR 2506-1 4.000.1 "Person with disabilities" (SSI, disability or blindness payments under titles I, II, X, XIV or XVI or a disability-based state supplement, disability-based general assistance or interim assistance pending SSI, VA disability or a VA pension for a non-service-connected disability, a government disability retirement benefit for a permanent disability, a Railroad Retirement disability annuity with Medicare eligibility or a title XVI disability finding, or disability-based Medical Assistance), independent of age.

### CO-304 SNAP: is a household member (not excluded as an institution resident) `@engine`

The person is not excluded from every SNAP household as a resident of an institution that provides the majority of their meals (7 CFR 273.1(b)(7)(vi)) or as a boarder (273.1(c)(3)), and is not a child who already receives SNAP in another household and stays there because this household has not verified that it provides the majority of the child's meals (10 CCR 2506-1 4.505.4.C, 4.304.2.B.4). The other 273.1(b)(7) exclusions (disqualified for work-requirement noncompliance, intentional program violation, fleeing felon, drug felony) are folded into snap_is_ineligible_member instead, because those persons stay in the household for purposes of assembling the unit and counting income (273.11(c), S19) but are excluded only from the count of eligible members.

Precision. Three-pattern sweep T-6 (docs/reviews/pattern-sweep-snap-ce.md): per month, since prospective budgeting reads the circumstances anticipated during the issuance month (10 CCR 2506-1 4.402.1.A, S4734): a resident of an institution is out of the household in a month that begins on or after institution_entry_date, and is a member in the month of entry and the months before it, since a condition that takes a person out of the household holds for the month only if it holds on every day of it (OQ-1405, the day). Before, the item was per person: entry on or before the determination date excluded the person from every month the determination covers, the months before the entry included, and a later entry date excluded the person from none. Final verification pass 2 V-13: the duplicate child (receives_snap_in_another_household, CO-4178) joins this household once child_majority_of_meals_verified (CO-4179) is true; both are read as false when not stated, so the arm reads nothing more for any other person. Coverage pass 3 N3-1: the entry date is read only for a resident of a setting; a student whose college meal plan provides more than half of the student's meals (has_higher_education_meal_plan_providing_majority_of_meals, CO-4686, stated as of the determination date; 4.304.4.D.3, S3472) and who is a resident of an institution by that arm of CO-007 is excluded without it, since institution_entry_date (CO-008) is stated only for a setting other than a private dwelling.

### CO-305 SNAP: household members `@engine`

The persons who make up this person's SNAP purchase-and-prepare unit under 7 CFR 273.1(a)-(b)(1) and 10 CCR 2506-1 4.304 - everyone reachable from this person by a chain of buys_prepares_with, spouse, mandatory-member parent/child, or mandatory-member caretaker/dependent edges, minus anyone excluded as an institution resident. A buys_prepares_with edge is not crossed into or out of a household of an elderly person with a disability and that person's spouse granted separate household status under 7 CFR 273.1(b)(2) (snap_is_in_elderly_disabled_separate_household, CO-2304). Each member's value of this item is the same set (their own unit); a person who is not a household member (an institution resident) has no unit, so the value is empty for them.

Precision. A parent/child edge is only crossed into the household when the child member of that pair is under snap_mandatory_child_age in the month, matching the "person under 22 ... living with parent" mandatory-combination rule (7 CFR 273.1(b)(1)(ii); 10 CCR 2506-1 4.304.1.A.1). A caretaker/dependent edge is only crossed when the dependent is under snap_parental_control_age (18) and snap_is_under_parental_control_of_household_member is true for the dependent, matching the separate "child... under 18... under the parental control of a household member other than his or her parent" mandatory combination (7 CFR 273.1(b)(1)(iii); 10 CCR 2506-1 4.304.1.A.2). A spouse edge always crosses, matching 273.1(b)(1)(i); a buys_prepares_with edge crosses (273.1(a)(3)) unless either end is in a separate elderly and disabled household (273.1(b)(2), 4.304.3.A; phase-10 sweep, OQ-37). The mandatory parent/child and caretaker edges still cross, since 4.304.1 keeps mandatory members together. CDHS review C-2: a buys_prepares_with edge is not crossed into or out of a roomer or live-in attendant (snap_is_roomer_or_live_in_attendant, CO-2566; 7 CFR 273.1(c)(5)-(6)), who may be a separate household; the mandatory spouse, parent and child edges still cross, since 273.1(b)(1) persons are never roomers or attendants. A boarder is left out through snap_is_household_member (CO-304). A striking member stays in the household; 7 CFR 273.1(e) bars the household unless it was eligible the day before the strike (snap_household_meets_striker_condition, CO-3504) and counts the higher of the striker's pre-strike and current income (CO-3503; OQ-534, resolved). Same-word audit SW-1/SW-3/SW-8 (OQ-396): the parent edge is a legal parent or a stepparent ("natural or adoptive parent(s) or step-parent(s)", S2, S4); the parental-control edge is a household member with primary responsibility for the child or the child's legal guardian; a foster_parent edge is never crossed, since the combination is for "a child (other than a foster child)" (S2 iii). Same-word audit SW-7 (convention rule 17): an edge joins persons who live together (lives_with, CO-1925, from dwelling_id); where a case states no dwelling_id the edge is read as living together, as before. A SNAP household is persons who live together (7 CFR 273.1(a), S2), so no edge is crossed to a person who lives elsewhere. Coverage pass 4 for SNAP S4-11 (OQ-1263 resolved): the household is built for each month, and the ages of the mandatory combinations are taken in the month evaluated, since prospective budgeting reads "anticipated income and circumstances during the issuance month" (10 CCR 2506-1 4.402.1.A, S4734): a child is under 22 (or under 18 for parental control) when under it on the first day of the month (the age on the first day of the month), so a son who turns 22 during a month is a mandatory member for that month and not from the next (the day is OQ-1262's). The separate elderly and disabled household (CO-2304) is also read in the month. Before, the household was built once on the determination date's ages and every month read it. Three-pattern sweep T-7 (docs/reviews/pattern-sweep-snap-ce.md): a person of the case who died before the first day of the month (date_of_death, CO-2868), or who is not yet born on its last day (date_of_birth after it), is in no household that month, since a household is individuals who live together (7 CFR 273.1(a), S1) in the issuance month (4.402.1.A, S4734); the member who dies is counted in the month of death and the child born is counted in the month of birth, the day being OQ-1405's. A person whose date of death is not stated is living, and one whose date of birth is not stated is born (the persons a case names are persons; the test reads a stated date). Before, a stated death or a birth after the month changed no month's household (probes CO-945, CO-946). Three-pattern sweep D-1 (docs/reviews/pattern-sweep-snap-ce.md): lives_with (CO-1925) is read as stated, required where read: no text on file says that persons related on the application live together unless it says otherwise (7 CFR 273.1(a): a household is individuals who live together and customarily purchase and prepare meals together, S1), so a stated relationship is no longer read as living together where no dwelling_id is stated (decision 4; docs/conventions.md rule 17, as MAGI's readers since coverage pass 6, C6-10); a case with persons related across the edge states dwelling_id for each of them. Coverage pass 7, C7-1 (docs/reviews/coverage7-snap.md): living together is read for the month (snap_lives_with_in_month, CO-7672), not from the homes of the determination date in every month: a member who moved out after the application month lived in the home in the months that began before the date the two ceased to live together (CO-7352, CO-7506, CO-7670), and one who moved in after it did not live there before (CO-7671), since the application month is determined on "the household's circumstances for the entire month of application" (7 CFR 273.10(a)(1)(i), S5091).

Type group of persons, scope person-month, program SNAP.
Uses: `date_of_birth`, `date_of_death`, `relationships`, `snap_is_household_member`, `snap_is_in_elderly_disabled_separate_household`, `snap_is_roomer_or_live_in_attendant`, `snap_is_under_parental_control_of_household_member`, `snap_lives_with_in_month`, `snap_mandatory_child_age`, `snap_parental_control_age`.

### CO-306 SNAP: is exempt from the non-citizen waiting period `@engine`

A qualified non-citizen subject to the additional condition (10 CCR 2506-1 4.305,B,3) is exempt from the five-year/40-quarter waiting period because they have a military connection or meet one of the other exceptions of 8 U.S.C. 1612(a)(2) that snap_is_exempt_from_waiting_period_other_than_military (CO-3713) states: under 18; blind or a person with a disability receiving benefits or assistance for that condition (whatever their entry date); born on or before August 22, 1931 and in qualifying status on or before August 22, 1996; a former refugee, asylee, person whose deportation was withheld, Cuban or Haitian entrant or Amerasian immigrant; an American Indian born in Canada or tribal member; or a Hmong or Highland Lao veteran or the veteran's family.

Precision. The "born on or before August 22, 1931 and lawfully resided in the U.S. on August 22, 1996" test (S15) is modeled as date_of_birth on or before snap_elderly_non_citizen_birth_date_cutoff (CO-2601, 1931-08-22) and qualified_status_date on or before qualified_non_citizen_entry_cutoff_date (CO-279, 1996-08-22) (qualified_status_date stands in for lawful residence on that date, a fact this volume does not separately collect). The blind or disabled exception (4.305.B.3.d, S1305; 8 U.S.C. 1612(a)(2)(F)(ii), S1306) reads snap_is_disabled_member (CO-302): "receiving benefits or assistance for blindness or disability" within the meaning of 7 U.S.C. 2012 is the benefit-receipt list of the 7 CFR 271.2 elderly-or-disabled definition, and it has no August 22, 1996 condition (OQ-2 resolved: the brief had merged this exception with the elderly one). Coverage pass 4 for SNAP S4-11 (OQ-1263 resolved): per month, since prospective budgeting reads "anticipated income and circumstances during the issuance month" (10 CCR 2506-1 4.402.1.A, S4734): the exceptions (CO-3713, CO-4260) read the ages in the month. Before, the item was per person and read on the determination date in every month.

### CO-307 SNAP: meets the non-citizen additional condition `@engine`

A lawful permanent resident clears the five-year bar of 8 U.S.C. 1613(a) by having resided in the U.S. in a qualified status for five years (8 U.S.C. 1612(a)(2)(L)), counted from the date the person first obtained a qualified status or entered the United States in one (qualified_non_citizen_waiting_period_start_date, CO-7820) to the last day of the month, or by having held the lawful permanent residence itself (qualified_status_date) that long, by having federal_qualifying_quarters_threshold qualifying quarters (1612(a)(2)(B)), or by one of the exceptions in snap_is_exempt_from_immigrant_waiting_period. Colorado states the same tests at 10 CCR 2506-1 4.305,B,3.

Precision. Coverage pass 4 for SNAP S4-11 (OQ-1263 resolved): per month, since prospective budgeting reads "anticipated income and circumstances during the issuance month" (10 CCR 2506-1 4.402.1.A, S4734): the exceptions (CO-306) read the ages in the month. Before, the item was per person and read on the determination date in every month. Three-pattern sweep T-1 (docs/reviews/pattern-sweep-snap-ce.md): the five years are read in the month too (the five years counted to the last day of the month, written inline here and in CO-3736 and CO-3738; the separate item CO-7450 the sweep proposed was removed at its merge), not on the determination date (CO-508), so a non-citizen whose fifth anniversary falls in a later month of the certification meets the condition from that month. KL-SNAP-2 closed (2026-11-24; docs/reviews/known-limits.md): the five years were counted from qualified_status_date, the date of the status held now, so a lawful permanent resident who had been paroled, a battered non-citizen or a conditional entrant restarted them at the adjustment. 1612(a)(2)(L) (S22) counts residence 'with a status within the meaning of the term "qualified alien" for a period of 5 years or more beginning on the date of the alien's entry into the United States', and 4.305.B.3.a (S12) begins them 'on the date the non-citizen obtains status as a qualified non-citizen or enters the U.S. in a qualifying status': they are counted from the start of the waiting period (CO-7820; the first qualified status, first_qualified_status_date CO-7770, required where read: not needed where the person entered the United States in the status held now or is a lawful permanent resident admitted directly), the reading Medicaid took in coverage pass 7, C7-04 (CO-7550). The count from qualified_status_date stays as a second arm, so an LPR whose permanent residence alone has lasted five years needs no earlier date. LPR-EX-PAROLEE (paroled 2019-05-01, LPR 2023-03-01; stored household CO-1140): met from May 2024; before, from March 2028. CO-3736 and CO-3738 read the same two counts for the month.

### CO-309 SNAP: meets the citizenship requirement `@engine`

The person meets 7 U.S.C. 2015(f) - a resident of the United States who is a U.S. citizen or non-citizen national or an eligible non-citizen - and so may participate in SNAP as far as residence, citizenship and immigration status determine.

### CO-310 SNAP: is an ineligible non-citizen `@engine`

The person does not meet the citizenship requirement of 7 U.S.C. 2015(f), or is a non-citizen who meets it but is ineligible until the sponsor's information or the verification of eligible alien status is provided (snap_is_ineligible_pending_non_citizen_verification, CO-4154; 10 CCR 2506-1 4.505.7.B-C, 4.505.6.F, I; 7 CFR 273.4(c)(5)), so their own income and resources are counted toward the household under 7 CFR 273.11(c) but they are not counted as an eligible household member.

Precision. Final verification pass 2 N-2: the second arm. ### CO-330 SNAP: person earned income `@engine`

The person's earned income for the month for SNAP: wages as SNAP counts them (snap_person_wages, CO-4324: converted from the pay schedule or averaged under a contract) plus net self-employment income (gross receipts less the allowable costs of producing it, snap_self_employment_income, CO-1702) plus net income from boarders (snap_boarder_income, CO-4165), which 10 CCR 2506-1 4.403.2 treats as self-employment income, plus training allowances other than WIOA (4.403.B.1) and Domestic Volunteer Service Act Title I (VISTA) payments to a person who was not receiving SNAP or public assistance on joining (4.403.A.2, C), less the earned income 4.405 excludes (snap_excluded_earned_income, CO-2338).

Precision. Vocabulary fix round (R-1): reads gross wages (wages_gross, CO-023) and SNAP's own self-employment net (CO-1702). CDHS review C-2: the earnings of a child student (snap_student_earnings_are_excluded, CO-2569; 7 CFR 273.9(c)(7)) are excluded in full. For a striking member whose income before the strike was higher than the current income, the difference is added (snap_striker_income_above_current, CO-3503; 7 CFR 273.1(e)(2), S1816; OQ-534), so the member's counted income is the higher of the two. Final verification pass 2 N-5: boarder income net of the cost of doing business is added here, so the earned income deduction applies to it (4.403.2.C, S2963). N-6: in a destitute household's month of application (snap_is_destitute_application_month, CO-4168) the earned income received after the date of application (CO-4166) is left out (4.406.1.A, S2964). Coverage review snap-financial CF-1 and CF-3: the 4.405 exclusions of earned income are now derived from neutral receipt facts (CO-2338; OQ-390), the wages are SNAP's converted or averaged figure (CO-4324), and the training allowances and VISTA payments that the unearned income facts state but 4.403 counts as earned income are added here (they are left out of unearned income by CO-2339), so the earned income deduction applies to them. Coverage pass 3 C3-1: the wages, training allowances and VISTA payments, less the 4.405 exclusions and the destitute month's later receipts, are one item (snap_person_earned_income_other_than_self_employment, CO-4930) that the earned-income verification (CO-1376) also reads; the sum is unchanged.

### CO-331 SNAP: person unearned income `@engine`

The person's unearned income for the month for SNAP (7 CFR 273.9(b)(2)): the counted recurring receipts (snap_counted_recurring_receipts), plus substantial gambling winnings of the month (4.403.I), plus rental income net of its costs (4.404.D, snap_rental_income), less the excluded infrequent or irregular receipts (4.405.A) and need-based charitable cash within the quarterly limit (A.10), less, in a destitute household's month of application, the unearned income received after the application date (4.406.1.A); not below zero. Plus sick, vacation and bonus pay received in installments after the job ended (snap_leave_pay_after_termination, CO-6600; 4.404.F).

Precision. Receipt records, migration phase 1 (docs/reviews/receipts-migration-1.md): read from the receipts (CO-5000) through snap_receipt_treatment_table, replacing the sum of the unearned income facts and snap_excluded_unearned_income (CO-2339). The exclusions are rows of the table; a nonrecurring lump sum is a receipt paid once (4.405.E), so a payment stated once is excluded once (before receipt records a one-time payment of an excluded source stated both as its source and as a lump sum was subtracted twice, the SNAP twin of LEAP coverage-3 F3-2). Income deemed from a sponsor is added in snap_person_gross_income (CO-332; final verification F-2), not here. The destitute-household figure (CO-4167) is still its own fact, read as 0 when not stated. Coverage pass 4 S4-4: the installments of leave or bonus pay after termination are read from the earnings records, so a person whose earnings are not stated has unearned income that cannot be determined (decision 4 of 2026-11-23). Coverage pass 4 S4-14: in a destitute household's month of application the unearned income received after the date of application is left out record by record, by each receipt's date (4.406.1.A, S2964), as the earned income is (snap_person_counted_wages, CO-5113); a receipt of that month with no date cannot be placed, so the figure cannot be determined (decision 4). The separate fact snap_unearned_income_received_after_application_date (CO-4167), read as 0 when not stated, a second statement of the dated receipts, is retired.

### CO-333 SNAP: counted income of an ineligible member `@engine`

The amount of an ineligible household member's own gross income that is counted as income to the remaining, eligible household members - the full amount for an IPV, work-sanction, or fleeing-felon disqualification, and a pro rata share for a member whose income is prorated (an ineligible non-citizen, an SSN refusal, an ABAWD at the time limit): the income divided evenly among the household members, the ineligible members included, with all but the ineligible members' shares counted (7 CFR 273.11(c)(2)(ii); snap_prorated_member_share_counted_rate, CO-7250), so with two prorated members in a household of four, each one's income counts at two quarters. Zero for a member who is not an ineligible member.

Precision. The pro rata share divides the member's income evenly among every household member counted by snap_household_members (including the ineligible members), then counts all but the shares of the members whose income is prorated (CO-7250); n is the count of that person's whole purchase-and-prepare unit, not just the eligible members. Engineering follow-up 5: a prorated member with no household (snap_household_members empty, as for a person who is not a household member) has nothing counted to any household, so the share is 0 rather than a division by zero. Final verification F-6: n counts the members other than an ineligible student (snap_household_members_other_than_ineligible_students, CO-3714), whom 4.411.2.C (S2508) treats as a non-household member not considered in the allotment. Coverage pass 6 for SNAP, C6-1 (docs/reviews/coverage6-snap.md): with two or more prorated members in the household, every prorated member's share is left out, not only this member's own: the fraction counted is snap_prorated_member_share_counted_rate (CO-7250), (n - k) / n with k the prorated members, as 7 CFR 273.11(c)(2)(ii)-(iii) (S4970) says ("All but the ineligible members' share is counted"). Before, (n - 1) / n was counted whatever k was.

Type money, scope person-month, program SNAP.
Uses: `snap_is_disqualified_member_counted_in_full`, `snap_is_ineligible_member_prorated`, `snap_person_gross_income`, `snap_prorated_member_share_counted_rate`.

```
if SNAP: is a disqualified member whose income and expenses count in full
  then SNAP: person gross income
else if SNAP: is an ineligible member whose income is prorated
  then (if SNAP: share of a prorated member's income and expenses counted is equal to 0;   then 0; otherwise SNAP: person gross income times SNAP: share of a prorated member's income and expenses counted)
otherwise 0
```

```

This person's SNAP household's total countable resources in the month under 7 CFR 273.8 (liquid and non-liquid), the sum of every household member's own countable resources, including ineligible or disqualified members but not an ineligible student, and leaving out the resources of a member who receives SSI or public assistance (Colorado Works cash, or Old Age Pension, Aid to the Needy Disabled or Aid to the Blind), plus the resources deemed to a sponsored member from the member's sponsor (snap_sponsor_deemed_resources, CO-3702).

Precision. Sums each member's countable liquid and non-liquid resources (snap_countable_liquid_resources, CO-4176, and snap_countable_nonliquid_resources, CO-074) over the whole purchase-and-prepare unit, not snap_eligible_household_members, because 10 CCR 2506-1 4.411.1,B,1,a and B,2,a (S45, S46) count a disqualified or ineligible member's resources in full to the household whenever the household must meet a resource standard. Final verification F-6: an ineligible student is a non-household member whose resources are not available to the household (4.411.2.C, S2508), so the sum runs over snap_household_members_other_than_ineligible_students (CO-3714). F-2: each member's deemed sponsor resources are added (4.305.2.C, D.6, S2502). Final verification pass 2 N-8: each member's liquid resources are read net of the 4.409 and 4.410 exclusions held in liquid form (snap_countable_liquid_resources, CO-4176): tax refunds and earned income tax credits within twelve months, tax-deferred education accounts, and resources the member cannot reach. Resource records, step H1 SNAP (docs/reviews/records-holdings-snap-af.md): each member's resources are read from the member's holdings records through snap_countable_liquid_resources (CO-4176) and snap_countable_nonliquid_resources (CO-074), never from liquid_resources_value; a member whose holdings are not stated is cannot determine, as a member who did not state liquid_resources_value was. ### CO-348 SNAP: is entitled to expedited service `@engine`

This person's SNAP household is entitled to expedited service for the month - its gross income is under snap_expedited_income_ceiling and its liquid resources are at or below $100, or it is a destitute migrant or seasonal farmworker household with liquid resources at or below $100, or its combined gross income and liquid resources are less than its shelter costs (rent or mortgage plus the utility allowance).

Precision. Uses snap_shelter_costs (the household's summed rent or mortgage plus each member's derived standard utility allowance) for "monthly rent or mortgage, and utilities (including entitlement to a SUA)". Merge fix (phase 8/9): the rule first read the evaluated person's own shelter_cost_monthly and utility allowance, which is wrong for any member other than the one who states the costs; 273.2(i)(1)(iii) compares the household's income and resources with the household's shelter costs. Vocabulary fix round (docs/reviews/vocabulary-reuse.md, R-11): all three prongs read snap_household_liquid_resources (CO-1740), as 273.2(i)(1) states 'liquid resources'; a countable non-liquid resource no longer bars expedited service. Final verification F-23: liquid_resources_value (CO-3390) also holds stocks, bonds, mutual fund shares and cryptocurrency, which 273.2(i)(1)'s list ("cash on hand, checking or savings accounts, savings certificates, and lump sum payments") does not name, so the test is slightly stricter than the text for a household holding them; Colorado's 4.408.C reads "the value of liquid resources, as declared by the household" for expedited eligibility. Coverage pass 2 N2-P3-3: the household's entitlement here is the income and resource test of 4.205.1.A; a household that misses its first interview, or does not complete it within seven days, loses expedited service (4.204.C, 4.205.1.B.2), an application-processing condition this volume does not model (docs/design-colorado.md), so a worker reads this item as the entitlement before the interview conditions.

### CO-3701 SNAP: sponsor income deemed `@engine`

The unearned income SNAP counts to this person for the month from the person's sponsor (10 CCR 2506-1 4.305.2.C-D; 7 CFR 273.4(c)(2)): for an eligible non-citizen whose sponsor's income is deemed, this person's share of the sponsor's income after the deeming reductions (snap_sponsor_income_after_reductions divided by snap_sponsor_deeming_divisor), or the money the sponsor paid the person in the month if that is more (4.305.2.D.4); for anyone else, the money a sponsor paid the person, which is ordinary unearned income.

Precision. Deeming applies only to an eligible non-citizen (4.305.2.C, snap_is_eligible_non_citizen, CO-308) to whom no exemption applies (snap_sponsor_deeming_applies, CO-2337); an ineligible non-citizen's counted income excludes it (273.4(c)(5)). Money paid in excess of the deemed share is added, so the person's income from the sponsor is the greater of the two. The money is this person's own receipt and is not divided. A citizen is out at the first test, so nothing about a sponsor is read. Final verification pass 2 N-2: a member who is ineligible until the sponsor information or the status verification is provided (snap_is_ineligible_pending_non_citizen_verification, CO-4154) is an ineligible non-citizen, and 4.505.7.C (S2954) counts that member's income and resources "excluding the attributed income and resources of the non-citizen's sponsor". Coverage pass 3 N3-2: the test is [not, snap_is_ineligible_non_citizen] (CO-310), the one list of the grounds on which a non-citizen member is ineligible (status not verified by the due date, sponsor information outstanding, and a member the household declines to document, declines_to_provide_immigration_documentation, CO-4687; 4.505.6.J, S902), so a ground added to CO-310 stops deeming here too (4.305.2.C: "Only when a sponsored non-citizen is an eligible non-citizen"). Receipt records, migration phase 1: the money the sponsor paid is the month's receipts of the kind sponsor_payment (snap_receipt_treatment_table: sponsor_deeming). Receipts not stated: cannot determine, in both arms, since 4.305.2.D.4 and 7 CFR 273.4(c)(2)(iii) count the money the sponsor pays and give no reading for money not reported (decision 4 of 2026-11-23 (docs/plan-colorado.md): missing information is cannot determine unless the rule says otherwise; the phase-1 default of 0 is removed); a stated empty list is no money paid, 0. Three-pattern sweep T-5 (docs/reviews/pattern-sweep-snap-ce.md): money the sponsor pays as a stream (no month and no date) is counted only in the months from its start_date through its end_date (docs/conventions.md, "A record's time"), as every other SNAP receipt reader counts a stream (snap_counted_recurring_receipts, CO-5011); before, a stream that had ended was counted in every month.

Type money, scope person-month, program SNAP.
Uses: `receipts`, `snap_is_eligible_non_citizen`, `snap_is_ineligible_non_citizen`, `snap_receipt_treatment_table`, `snap_sponsor_deeming_applies`, `snap_sponsor_deeming_divisor`, `snap_sponsor_income_after_reductions`.

```
if all of the following are true:
    - SNAP: is an eligible non-citizen
    - it is not the case that SNAP: is an ineligible non-citizen
    - SNAP: sponsor deeming applies
  then the greater of (the sum of that receipt's amount for each receipt in Receipts where ((all of the following are true:;   - SNAP: how each kind of receipt is treated (table), for that receipt's kind is equal to sponsor_deeming;   - that receipt is received in the month;   - any of the following is true:;     - it is not the case that that receipt's month is unknown;     - all of the following are true:;       - any of the following is true:;         - that receipt's start date is unknown;         - the month containing that receipt's start date is at most the month;       - any of the following is true:;         - that receipt's end date is unknown;         - the month containing that receipt's end date is at least the month))) and (SNAP: sponsor income after the deeming reductions divided by SNAP: sponsor deeming divisor)
otherwise the sum of that receipt's amount for each receipt in Receipts where ((all of the following are true:;   - SNAP: how each kind of receipt is treated (table), for that receipt's kind is equal to sponsor_deeming;   - that receipt is received in the month;   - any of the following is true:;     - it is not the case that that receipt's month is unknown;     - all of the following are true:;       - any of the following is true:;         - that receipt's start date is unknown;         - the month containing that receipt's start date is at most the month;       - any of the following is true:;         - that receipt's end date is unknown;         - the month containing that receipt's end date is at least the month))

### CO-3702 SNAP: sponsor resources deemed `@engine`

The resources SNAP counts to this eligible sponsored non-citizen from the person's sponsors (10 CCR 2506-1 4.305.2.C, D.6; 7 CFR 273.4(c)(2)(iv)-(v)): the total countable resources of the sponsors and their spouses (8 U.S.C. 1631(a)(2)) less snap_sponsor_resource_reduction, never below zero, divided by snap_sponsor_deeming_divisor; zero when deeming does not apply.

Precision. Each sponsor's resources are read from the sponsor's own facts as SNAP counts them (snap_countable_liquid_resources, CO-4176, and snap_countable_nonliquid_resources, CO-074; 273.4(c)(2)(iv): "as determined in accordance with § 273.8"); the sponsors are those who signed the affidavit (CO-2713), with their spouses who did not (CO-2714), as for income (CO-3711; coverage review C-14, OQ-730 resolved). A citizen is out at the first test. Final verification pass 2 N-2: a member who is ineligible until the sponsor information or the status verification is provided (snap_is_ineligible_pending_non_citizen_verification, CO-4154) is an ineligible non-citizen, and 4.505.7.C (S2954) counts that member's resources "excluding the attributed income and resources of the non-citizen's sponsor". N-8: the sponsor's liquid resources are read net of the 4.410 exclusions (CO-4176), as the household's own are. Coverage pass 3 N3-2: the test is [not, snap_is_ineligible_non_citizen] (CO-310), the one list of the grounds on which a non-citizen member is ineligible (status not verified by the due date, sponsor information outstanding, and a member the household declines to document, declines_to_provide_immigration_documentation, CO-4687; 4.505.6.J, S902), so a ground added to CO-310 stops deeming here too (4.305.2.C: "Only when a sponsored non-citizen is an eligible non-citizen"). Resource records, step H1 SNAP (docs/reviews/records-holdings-snap-af.md): the sponsor's and the spouse's resources are read from their own holdings records, as the household's are. Coverage pass 4 for SNAP S4-11 (OQ-1263 resolved): per month, since prospective budgeting reads "anticipated income and circumstances during the issuance month" (10 CCR 2506-1 4.402.1.A, S4734): the deeming (CO-2337) and its divisor (CO-3708) read the ages in the month. Before, the item was per person and read on the determination date in every month. Coverage pass 4 for SNAP resources (docs/reviews/coverage4-snap-resources.md): per month (SR-9): the sponsors' resources are those of the month evaluated, valued on the month's day (CO-4176, CO-074).

Type money, scope person-month, program SNAP.
Uses: `snap_countable_liquid_resources`, `snap_countable_nonliquid_resources`, `snap_is_eligible_non_citizen`, `snap_is_ineligible_non_citizen`, `snap_sponsor_deeming_applies`, `snap_sponsor_deeming_divisor`, `snap_sponsor_resource_reduction`, `sponsor_spouses_not_cosigning`, `sponsors`.

    - SNAP: is an eligible non-citizen
    - it is not the case that SNAP: is an ineligible non-citizen
    - SNAP: sponsor deeming applies
  then (the greater of 0 and (((the sum of that person's SNAP: countable liquid resources plus that person's SNAP: countable non-liquid resources for each person in Sponsors) plus (the sum of that person's SNAP: countable liquid resources plus that person's SNAP: countable non-liquid resources for each person in Sponsors' spouses who did not sign)) minus SNAP sponsor deeming, resource reduction (1500))) divided by SNAP: sponsor deeming divisor

### CO-3708 SNAP: sponsor deeming divisor `@engine`

The number among whom the income and resources of this non-citizen's sponsors are divided before they are deemed (10 CCR 2506-1 4.305.2.D.2.c; 7 CFR 273.4(c)(2)(v)): the non-citizens the sponsors have sponsored - the number stated on the sponsors (non_citizens_sponsored_count), or, when that is not stated or smaller, this non-citizen and the persons of the case who share a sponsor with this non-citizen - plus each citizen child under snap_sponsor_deeming_child_age_limit of this non-citizen in this non-citizen's SNAP household, whose share is excluded as (c)(2)(v) directs for a child exempt under (c)(3)(vii).

Precision. A sponsored child under 18, exempt from deeming by 7 U.S.C. 2014(i)(2)(E) (final verification pass 2 N-3; formerly only under (c)(3)(vi)), is one of the sponsor's non-citizens and so already counted; its share is never deemed because deeming does not apply to it (CO-2337). Where a sponsor and a co-sponsor spouse both signed, the count is stated on one of them only, so the stated counts are added across the sponsors. Unknown when this person's relationships are unstated. Coverage pass 4 for SNAP S4-11 (OQ-1263 resolved): the household and the child's age are read in the month evaluated, since prospective budgeting reads "anticipated income and circumstances during the issuance month" (10 CCR 2506-1 4.402.1.A, S4734); a citizen child is under 18 when under it on the first day of the month (the age on the first day of the month; OQ-1262). Before, the age on the determination date in every month.

Type whole number, scope person-month, program SNAP.
Uses: `date_of_birth`, `immigration_status`, `non_citizens_sponsored_count`, `relationships`, `snap_household_members`, `snap_sponsor_deeming_child_age_limit`, `sponsors`.

```
(the greater of (1 plus (the number of persons in the persons who share a sponsor with this person)) and (the sum of that person's Non-citizens sponsored, otherwise 0 for each person in Sponsors)) plus (the number of persons in all persons in SNAP: household members such that (all of the following are true:;   - this person is a parent of that person;   - (the number of whole years between that person's Date of birth and the first day of the month) is less than SNAP sponsor deeming, child age limit (18);   - that person's Immigration status is one of: us_citizen, us_national))
```

### CO-371 SNAP: counted earned income of an ineligible member `@engine`

The portion of an ineligible household member's own earned income that is counted, for the earned income deduction, as earned income of the remaining household members - the full amount for an IPV, work-sanction, or fleeing-felon disqualification, and, for a member whose income is prorated, the same pro rata share snap_counted_income_of_ineligible_member (CO-333) uses for the member's total income: all but the ineligible members' shares (7 CFR 273.11(c)(2)(ii)-(iii); snap_prorated_member_share_counted_rate, CO-7250). Zero for a member who is not an ineligible member.

Precision. Mirrors snap_counted_income_of_ineligible_member's case structure and pro rata arithmetic exactly, but applied to snap_person_earned_income alone rather than snap_person_gross_income, so snap_household_earned_income_for_deduction can isolate the earned share for the 20% earned income deduction, separate from the unearned share that reaches the household only through snap_counted_income_of_ineligible_member and snap_household_gross_income. Engineering follow-up 5: a prorated member with no household (snap_household_members empty, as for a person who is not a household member) has nothing counted to any household, so the share is 0 rather than a division by zero. Final verification F-6: n counts the members other than an ineligible student (snap_household_members_other_than_ineligible_students, CO-3714), whom 4.411.2.C (S2508) treats as a non-household member not considered in the allotment. Coverage pass 6 for SNAP, C6-1 (docs/reviews/coverage6-snap.md): with two or more prorated members in the household, every prorated member's share is left out, not only this member's own: the fraction counted is snap_prorated_member_share_counted_rate (CO-7250), (n - k) / n with k the prorated members, as 7 CFR 273.11(c)(2)(ii)-(iii) (S4970) says ("All but the ineligible members' share is counted"). Before, (n - 1) / n was counted whatever k was.

Type money, scope person-month, program SNAP.
Uses: `snap_is_disqualified_member_counted_in_full`, `snap_is_ineligible_member_prorated`, `snap_person_earned_income`, `snap_prorated_member_share_counted_rate`.

```
if SNAP: is a disqualified member whose income and expenses count in full
  then SNAP: person earned income
else if SNAP: is an ineligible member whose income is prorated
  then (if SNAP: share of a prorated member's income and expenses counted is equal to 0;   then 0; otherwise SNAP: person earned income times SNAP: share of a prorated member's income and expenses counted)
otherwise 0
```

```

### CO-3713 SNAP: is exempt from the non-citizen waiting period other than by a military connection `@engine`

A lawful permanent resident is exempt from the five-year waiting period for a reason other than a military connection: under 18; blind or a person with a disability receiving benefits for it; born on or before August 22, 1931 and in qualified status on August 22, 1996; admitted for permanent residence after holding, or under, a status the five-year bar never reached - refugee, asylee, deportation withheld, Cuban or Haitian entrant, Amerasian immigrant (8 U.S.C. 1612(a)(2)(A), 1613(b)(1); 7 CFR 273.4(a)(6)(ii)(B)-(F), (iv)); an American Indian born in Canada or a member of an Indian tribe (1612(a)(2)(G); 273.4(a)(3)); or a Hmong or Highland Lao veteran, or the veteran's spouse, unremarried surviving spouse or dependent child (1612(a)(2)(K); 273.4(a)(4)).

Precision. The earlier status is status_before_lpr_adjustment (CO-2700), read as none when not stated. 1612(a)(2)(A) lifts the bar for seven years from admission or grant of the earlier status and (L) lifts it after five years in qualified status, which the earlier status counts toward, so the two together leave no gap: "Each category of eligible alien status stands alone ... Subsequent adjustment to a more limited status does not override eligibility based on an earlier less rigorous status" (273.4(a)(6)(iv)); no time limit is modeled. The Indian and Hmong facts (CO-2701, CO-2702, CO-3715) are read as false when not stated; a spouse in the case who is the veteran is read from the spouse edge, and the spouse arm is false when the person's relationships are not stated. "Lawfully residing" for the Hmong exception is met by the lawful permanent residence 7 U.S.C. 2015(f) already requires. The other arms are as snap_is_exempt_from_immigrant_waiting_period (CO-306) described them before this item took them over. Coverage pass 4 S4-14 (decision 4 of 2026-11-23): status_before_lpr_adjustment is read with no default where this rule reads it (only for a lawful permanent resident none of the earlier exemptions reaches; the exemption turns on the status held before adjustment, and no rule gives one); before, it was read as none when not stated. Coverage pass 4 for SNAP S4-11 (OQ-1263 resolved): the under-18 exception is read in the month evaluated, since prospective budgeting reads "anticipated income and circumstances during the issuance month" (10 CCR 2506-1 4.402.1.A, S4734), and met when the person is under 18 on the first day of the month (the age on the first day of the month; OQ-1262). Before, the age on the determination date in every month. KL-SNAP-2 (2026-11-24; docs/reviews/known-limits.md): the 1931 arm read qualified_status_date, the date of the status held now, so a person in a qualified status on August 22, 1996 who adjusted to permanent residence after it failed the arm. 8 U.S.C. 1612(a)(2)(I) (S24) asks whether the person 'on August 22, 1996 ... was lawfully residing in the United States', and 4.305.B.3.e (S1305) whether the person 'lawfully resided in the U.S. on August 22, 1996'; a qualified status first held on or before that day answers it, so the arm reads the start of the qualified status (qualified_non_citizen_waiting_period_start_date, CO-7820: the first qualified status, first_qualified_status_date CO-7770, where the case does not show the status held now is the first) as well as the status held now. Required where read: only for a person born on or before August 22, 1931 whose status held now began after August 22, 1996. Close-out verification F1, the arm left (KL-SNAP-3, docs/reviews/known-limits.md; 2026-11-24): the arm of a status held before permanent residence reads status_before_lpr_adjustment (CO-2700) for a lawful permanent resident only, as CO-2700 is stated ('Read only for a lawful permanent resident'); for a qualified non-citizen in another status (a battered non-citizen, a parolee) the arm is false. Before, the unstated earlier status of a person who is not a permanent resident left the exemption, and the five-year test (CO-307), cannot determine (probe A7).

The deduction for this person's SNAP household's out-of-pocket medical expenses incurred by its elderly or disabled members (summed across every elderly or disabled member) - nothing at snap_medical_deduction_threshold or less; above $35, Colorado's Standard Medical Expense Deduction of $165, or the actual expenses less snap_medical_deduction_threshold when that is more (10 CCR 2506-1 4.407.61.A).

### CO-405 SNAP: is exempt from work registration `@engine`

The person is exempt from general SNAP work registration because they are unfit for employment, complying with TANF work requirements, receiving or have applied for unemployment compensation, responsible for a dependent child under 6 or an incapacitated person, a regular participant in drug or alcohol treatment, meet the employment exemption, are enrolled at least half time in school or (as an eligible student) higher education, or are of the youth exemption's ages (snap_work_registration_min_age through snap_work_registration_youth_max_age) and either not the head of household or attending school or training at least half time.

Precision. The higher-education half-time arm requires the person not be an ineligible student (7 U.S.C. 2015(d)(2)(C) makes the exemption conditional on meeting subsection (e)). The youth arm runs from snap_work_registration_min_age through snap_work_registration_youth_max_age (CO-3040; a literal 17 before the hard-coded numbers audit H-10). Coverage pass 4 for SNAP S4-11 (OQ-1263 resolved): evaluated for the month, since prospective budgeting reads "anticipated income and circumstances during the issuance month" (10 CCR 2506-1 4.402.1.A, S4734). The youth arm's ages are taken in the month and met when met on any day of it (OQ-1262; docs/operators.md, Ages in a month): 16 or older on the last day (the age on the last day of the month) and 17 or younger on the first day (the age on the first day of the month). Before, the item was per person: the ages on the determination date and the compliance of the determination month, in every month. Three-pattern sweep T-11 (docs/reviews/pattern-sweep-snap-ce.md): the student exemption ends when "the student graduates" (7 CFR 273.7(b)(1)(viii), S125; 10 CCR 2506-1 4.306.C, S5092), so a person whose program is expected to be completed before the first day of the month evaluated (expected_program_completion_date, CO-2882) is not exempt as a student in that month; with no completion date stated the enrollment continues, as both texts deem it.

### CO-407 SNAP: meets the student employment exemption `@engine`

The student works at least snap_student_employment_hours_per_week hours a week on average, or at least snap_student_employment_hours_per_month (80) hours in the month (4.306.1.B, third paragraph), and is paid for that employment - a self-employed student also earning, after allowable business expenses, at least federal_minimum_wage times snap_student_employment_hours_per_week a week (10 CCR 2506-1 4.306.1.B; 7 CFR 273.5(b)(5)) - or is approved for a State or federally financed work-study program.

Precision. Final verification F-5: the earnings condition of 4.306.1.B's second paragraph (S135; 7 CFR 273.5(b)(5), S2507) applies to a self-employed student, read as one with self-employment receipts and no wages in the month evaluated; a student with wages is employed and paid, whatever self-employment the student also has. Weekly earnings are SNAP's net self-employment income (snap_self_employment_income, CO-1702) divided by snap_weeks_per_month, as snap_weekly_hours_worked divides hours. Coverage pass 2 N2-2: 4.306.1.B lets the weekly hours be averaged over the month "so long as the student is employed for eighty (80) hours per month" (S135), so the hours worked in the month evaluated (hours_worked) meet the test at snap_student_employment_hours_per_month (CO-4681) whatever their weekly average; dividing by snap_weeks_per_month alone required 86. Earned-income records, step E1 (SNAP; docs/reviews/records-earnings-snap.md): the self-employment receipts are the earnings records whose row is counted_less_costs or counted_loss_offset, and the wages snap_person_pay_received (CO-5119), in place of self_employment_gross_receipts and wages_gross. Coverage pass 4 for SNAP (docs/reviews/coverage4-snap.md, S4-1 to S4-4): a record is placed in the month of its regular_date when it states one, since pay or a benefit that came early or late because of a holiday, a weekend, a changed pay date, a mailing cycle or the employee's request is counted by its regular schedule (10 CCR 2506-1 4.402.B.1-3, S4720; 4.403.A.3, S4721), else in the month it came in; a stream (a record with no month and no date) recurs only from the month its job or source began through the month it ended (job_start_date and job_end_date; start_date and end_date on a receipt), since pay after a job ends or before it begins is not anticipated with reasonable certainty (4.402.1.B, S4722). Coverage pass 4 S4-13 (decision 4): the month's hours are snap_hours_worked_in_month (CO-6604), cannot determine when the earnings records state pay and the hours are not stated. Coverage pass 6 for SNAP, C6-6 (docs/reviews/coverage6-snap.md): per month, since prospective budgeting reads "anticipated income and circumstances during the issuance month" (10 CCR 2506-1 4.402.1.A, S4734) and the readers (the student's eligibility, CO-410 and CO-411; the work registration exemption, CO-405) are per month since S4-11: the month's hours and pay are read in each month evaluated. Before, the item was per person and read the determination month in every month, so a student who began a 20-hour job after the determination month stayed an ineligible student in that month.

### CO-411 SNAP: is an ineligible student `@engine`

The person is age snap_student_min_age through 49, enrolled at least half time in an institution of higher education, and not exempt under snap_is_student_exempt, and so may not participate in SNAP as a member of any household under 7 U.S.C. 2015(e).

Precision. Coverage pass 4 for SNAP S4-11 (OQ-1263 resolved): the ages are taken in the month evaluated (10 CCR 2506-1 4.402.1.A, S4734), on the day that makes the rule apply only when it applies on every day of the month (OQ-1262; docs/operators.md, Ages in a month): 18 or older on the first day (the age on the first day of the month) and 49 or younger on the last day (the age on the last day of the month). A student who turns 18 during a month is still "seventeen (17) or under" (4.306.B.1, S135) on its first day and is not an ineligible student that month; one who turns 50 during a month is "fifty (50) or over" (4.306.B.2) on its last day. These are the days snap_is_student_exempt (CO-410) reads for the same two exemptions, so the range and the exemptions agree. Before, the age on the determination date was read in every month: a student who turned 18 after the application month was ineligible in it. Three-pattern sweep T-11 (docs/reviews/pattern-sweep-snap-ce.md): enrollment "shall be deemed continuous ... unless the student graduates" (10 CCR 2506-1 4.306.C, S5092), so a student whose program is expected to be completed before the first day of the month evaluated (expected_program_completion_date, CO-2882) is not an enrolled student in that month, as prospective budgeting reads the circumstances anticipated during it (4.402.1.A, S4734). With no completion date stated the enrollment continues, as 4.306.C deems it. Before, a graduation in the certification left the person an ineligible student in every later month. The term's first day (4.306.C: enrollment "shall begin on the first day of the school term") has no field; a person stated as enrolled is enrolled from the months the case covers.

  - it is not the case that SNAP: is exempt from the ineligible-student rule
```

Precision. ### CO-4154 SNAP: is ineligible while non-citizen verification is outstanding `@engine`

This household member is an eligible non-citizen by the facts stated, but is ineligible until a verification of that eligibility is provided, while the eligibility of the remaining members is determined (10 CCR 2506-1 4.505.7.B-C, 4.505.6.F, I, 4.505.61; 7 CFR 273.4(c)(5), 273.2(f)(1)(ii)(B)): either the sponsor's information is outstanding, at any date (snap_sponsor_verification_is_pending, CO-1611), or the eligible alien status itself - the status document, the forty qualifying quarters or the military connection the eligibility rests on - is still unverified after the reasonable opportunity to the non-citizen's documentation due date (snap_immigration_status_verification_is_pending, CO-1601, past snap_noncitizen_documentation_due_date, CO-1617).

Precision. Read for the month containing the determination date, as household composition is. The status arm keeps the exceptions CO-1601 already applies: a document submitted to USCIS (4.505.6.F.1, immigration_status_is_verified_or_submitted) and the quarters while SSA reviews them (F.2). The sponsor arm keeps CO-1616's: deeming must apply (no child under 18 is asked), and a basic categorically eligible household's conferring program verified the sponsor. The member is an ineligible non-citizen (snap_is_ineligible_non_citizen, CO-310): income and resources count pro rata, as 273.4(c)(5) directs "in accordance with § 273.11(c)", and the sponsor's deemed income and resources are not attributed to the member (CO-3701, CO-3702; 4.505.7.C). Where one sponsor covers every member, every member is ineligible and so the household is (4.505.7.C last paragraph). A citizen or a non-citizen who is not eligible anyway is false here. Coverage pass 4 for SNAP S4-11 (OQ-1263 resolved): per month, since prospective budgeting reads "anticipated income and circumstances during the issuance month" (10 CCR 2506-1 4.402.1.A, S4734): the eligible non-citizen (CO-308) is the month's; the verifications stay those of the determination month. Before, the item was per person and read on the determination date in every month.

The length, in months, of this person's SNAP household's disqualification for knowingly transferring resources to qualify (10 CCR 2506-1 4.408.2.B-C): read from snap_resource_transfer_disqualification_months_table by the amount by which the value of the members' disqualifying transfers, added to the household's other countable resources, exceeds the household's resource limit; 0 when no member made a disqualifying transfer or the total does not exceed the limit (4.408.2.A.1).

Precision. Resource records, step H1 SNAP (docs/reviews/records-holdings-snap-af.md): the transferred value is, for each member for whom snap_resource_transfer_is_disqualifying (CO-4159), the value of the member's disqualifying transfers (snap_disqualifying_transfer_value, CO-5314): each transfer within the three months before the date of application or after it through the determination month, not returned in whole, at its uncompensated value, read from the member's holdings records in place of the month-scoped transfer facts. The members are those whose resources count to the household, ineligible non-citizens and disqualified members included (snap_household_members_other_than_ineligible_students, CO-3714). The other countable resources are snap_household_countable_resources (CO-343) on the determination date, and the limit is the one snap_meets_resource_limit (CO-344) applies: snap_resource_limit_elderly_disabled for a household with an elderly or disabled member, otherwise snap_resource_limit. Only a member's finding is read, so a household without one is 0 with nothing else read. Coverage pass 4 for SNAP S4-11 (OQ-1263 resolved): per month, since prospective budgeting reads "anticipated income and circumstances during the issuance month" (10 CCR 2506-1 4.402.1.A, S4734): the household, its countable resources and its elderly or disabled member (CO-6603) are those of the month evaluated, so the length is figured on the household of each month; before, on the determination date's household in every month. Coverage pass 4 for SNAP resources (docs/reviews/coverage4-snap-resources.md): per month (SR-9): the household's other countable resources (CO-343) and its elderly or disabled member (snap_household_has_elderly_or_disabled_member_in_month, CO-6603) are those of the month evaluated.

### CO-4160 SNAP: is disqualified for a transfer of resources `@engine`

This person's SNAP household is disqualified in the month for knowingly transferring resources to qualify (10 CCR 2506-1 4.408.2): it is not categorically eligible, and the month is within the disqualification period - snap_resource_transfer_disqualification_months months beginning with the month of application for a transfer before the application, or with snap_resource_transfer_disqualification_effective_month for a transfer made after the household was determined eligible.

Precision. 4.408.2 applies to "households not eligible under expanded or basic categorical eligibility rules" (snap_is_categorically_eligible, CO-342), which have no resource test. The period starts in the month of application where any member's disqualifying transfer was before the date of application (4.408.2.B, "shall begin in the month of application"): a member for whom snap_resource_transfer_is_disqualifying (CO-4159) has disqualifying transfers dated before the date of application (snap_disqualifying_transfer_value_before_application, CO-5315, more than 0). Otherwise it starts at the month the notice of adverse action makes it effective (CO-4156). ### CO-4165 SNAP: boarder income `@engine`

The net income SNAP counts to this person for the month from boarders and roomers, as self-employment income (10 CCR 2506-1 4.403.2; 7 CFR 273.9(b)(1)(ii)): the boarders' payments for room and meals or meals only (snap_room_and_board_payments, CO-5117) less the cost of doing business, which is the maximum allotment for a household the size of the number of boarders (snap_room_and_board_payers, CO-5118) or, if more, the documented separate costs of providing the room and meals (the cost records of kind business_cost_boarder_provision for room and board or meals only), never more than the payments; plus the roomers' payments for a room only less the documented costs of providing the room (the cost records for room only), never more than the payments; foster care payments are disregarded in full.

Precision. The maximum allotment is read from snap_maximum_allotment_table for the number of boarders, with snap_maximum_allotment_each_additional beyond the table's last row. The net is added to the person's earned income (snap_person_earned_income, CO-330), so the earned income deduction applies to it (4.403.2.C). The home's own shelter costs are deducted as usual, boarder contributions notwithstanding (4.403.2.D). A commercial boarding house's receipts are self-employment receipts and not read here. Coverage review snap-financial CF-21: for snap_maximum_allotment_large_household_size (18) boarders or more the single 18-or-more figure is read (snap_maximum_allotment_large_household, CO-3726), as snap_maximum_allotment (CO-383) reads it. Earned-income records, step E1 (SNAP; docs/reviews/records-earnings-snap.md): a boarder's payments are earnings records (boarder_payments, provides room_and_board), the foster care test is the record's own (foster_care); a meals-only payment is a boarder's and a room-only payment a roomer's (coverage pass 4 S4-9, below). Earnings not stated: cannot determine (before step E1 unstated payments were read as none); a stated list with no boarder is 0. Coverage pass 4 S4-9 (OQ-996 resolved by the text): a meals-only payer is a boarder (7 CFR 273.1(c)(3)(ii), S1815) and a roomer's payment is self-employment income (273.9(b)(1)(ii), S4728); 4.403.2.B's maximum-allotment cost is for boarders ("the number of boarders"), so a roomer's cost of doing business is the actual cost of providing the room (273.11(b)(1); 4.403.11.B, S4729). Before, both payments were unearned income read from the receipts (board_only_payment, room_only_payment), which SNAP now reads from these records only (read_from_earnings).

### CO-4168 SNAP: is a destitute household's month of application `@engine`

The month is the month of this household's SNAP application and the household is a migrant or seasonal farmworker household destitute of income, so its eligibility and benefit for the month count only the income received between the first of the month and the date of application (10 CCR 2506-1 4.406.1.A; 7 CFR 273.10(e)(3)).

Precision. The destitute finding is the case fact is_destitute_migrant_or_seasonal_farmworker (CO-055), which is considered only for the first month of a certification period (4.406), the month of application here; it is read as false when not stated, as the expedited service test reads it (CO-348). Income from a new source over $25 not received or anticipated within ten days (4.406.1.B) is income received after the date of application, so the after-the-date facts (CO-4166, CO-4167) already leave it out. Coverage review snap-financial CF-22: 4.406 also applies the destitute rule to the first month of a certification period at recertification; the volume states no certification period start, so a recertification reads the month of its own application date (snap_application_date), which is the month this item tests.

Type yes/no, scope person-month, program SNAP.
Uses: `is_destitute_migrant_or_seasonal_farmworker`, `snap_application_date`.

```
all of the following are true:
  - Is a destitute migrant or seasonal farmworker, otherwise no
  - the month is equal to the month containing SNAP: application date
```

Equal to snap_eligible_household_size when no member is so disqualified. ### CO-417 SNAP: countable ABAWD months in the current 36-month clock period `@engine`

The number of countable ABAWD (able-bodied adult without dependents) months accrued in Colorado's current fixed 36-month clock period before the month in context - from the most recent reset (July 2023, July 2026, July 2029, ...) through the month before - since the clock 'resets accrued countable months and ABAWD disqualifications, regardless of start date, for all ABAWDs every thirty-six (36) calendar months starting July 1, 2023' (10 CCR 2506-1 4.311.3.C.2).

Precision. Evaluated per month, not only as of the determination date. The period start is the clock start month plus snap_abawd_period_months times the whole number of 36-month periods elapsed (whole years between the first days of the two months, divided by three and rounded down; floor(x) is computed as -ceil(-x)). In the reset month itself nothing has accrued yet. A month before July 2023 keeps the rolling 36-month count 7 CFR 273.24(b)(3) also allows. Phase-8 fix round (K-6): the item counted a rolling snap_abawd_period_months months, which is not the clock Colorado chose.

otherwise the number of months in the months from SNAP ABAWD time limit period, months (36) times (-1 times (-1 times ((the number of whole years between the first day of SNAP ABAWD time limit clock start month (2023-07) and the first day of the month) divided by (SNAP ABAWD time limit period, months (36) divided by 12)) rounded up to the next whole dollar)) months after SNAP ABAWD time limit clock start month (2023-07) through the month before the month for which SNAP: is a countable ABAWD month for the month
```
