### CO-4176 SNAP: countable liquid resources `@engine`

The person's own liquid resources that SNAP counts in the month (7 CFR 273.8(c)(1); 10 CCR 2506-1 4.408.B, 4.408.1, 4.409.A, 4.410), from the person's holdings records (holdings, CO-5300) valued in the month and held on the month's day (the application filing date in the month of application, the first day of any other month), through snap_holding_treatment_table (CO-5301): cash, accounts, securities, business cash and the money still held from a retroactive benefit, a loan, insurance or a sale (rows counted and counted_no_rule_excludes); money set aside for burial that can be withdrawn (burial_fund, counted_unless_irrevocable: money in an account; an irrevocable fund is inaccessible, 4.410.F.1); a federal income tax refund only from twelve months after the date it was received (J.17); a state or local refund always, less the part of it that is an earned income tax credit (eitc_share) for twelve months from receipt when the person was participating in SNAP when it was received and since (J.12); a state or local earned income tax credit received apart from a refund only when J.12's twelve months do not exclude it; each at its value times the person's share, or all of it where it is owned with someone outside the case or with a person of the case who is not a member of the person's SNAP household, a separate household (4.409.C, 7 CFR 273.8(d)); never a holding the person cannot reach (accessible; 4.409.C, 4.410.F), nor one the table excludes (retirement and education accounts, ABLE accounts, excluded government payments, prorated income still counted as income). Securities and other resources are counted at their value less what is owed against them, not below 0 (4.408.1.A: "the current redemption rate less encumbrances"; rows counted_less_encumbrances); an account's or cash's encumbrance is a hold or lien that makes the part held inaccessible (4.410.F.1), stated as its own record with accessible false. A trust interest is counted unless SNAP's finding says the county has established its funds inaccessible under 4.410.F.3 (snap_trust_inaccessible; row counted_unless_found_inaccessible).

Precision. Coverage pass 4 for SNAP resources (docs/reviews/coverage4-snap-resources.md). Per month (SR-9): the resources of the month evaluated, valued on its day, the application filing date in the month of application (snap_application_date; 4.408.1, S4823: "The value of nonexempt household resources at the application filing date") and the first day of any other month (4.408.B: "as anticipated to be available in the issuance month"; the day is OQ-1310's): a record valued in the month (its month, or every month), and a holding disposed of (disposed_date) is held in a month whose day is before the disposal; the refund and credit windows are read against the same day. Before, one figure per case, on the determination date and the determination month's records, in every month, and a holding with any disposed_date in no month. SR-3: a burial fund the person can withdraw is money in an account (273.8(c)(1), S1958; (c)(2) and (e), S4820: only (e) excludes), not a funeral agreement (4.410.D.4); before, not counted (OQ-1202). SR-8: a holding owned with the person's spouse who is not a member of the person's SNAP household (a spouse in an institution that provides meals), or with another person of the case outside it (named by co_owner), is a separate household's joint resource and is counted in its entirety: the co-owners' part (1 - share) is added, read only when such a co-owner is outside the household (OQ-1252 resolved in part). SR-10: the Colorado earned income tax credit is paid in the state refund, so the refund record states the part of its value that is the credit (eitc_share, a fraction of the value, so a refund split into two records states the same credit); J.12 excludes it for twelve months from receipt for a participant. SR-19: a federal earned income tax credit is part of the federal refund it is paid with (held_income_tax_refund), which J.17 excludes for twelve months, longer than J.12's month of receipt and the next; held_eitc is a state or local credit received apart from a refund (its kind), so the branch that read a federal held_eitc is removed. Twelve months run from the date of receipt to the same day twelve months later (a day the later month lacks runs into the next month): a federal refund received on 2025-11-15 is excluded through 2026-11-14. A federal refund or a credit whose date of receipt is not stated is cannot determine (decision 4). The resources of a member who receives SSI or public assistance are left out by the household's figures (snap_household_countable_resources, CO-343; 273.8(e)(17)), not here. Commingled exempt money (4.409.D, 273.8(g)): OQ-1251. Before step H1 the old liquid facts were read; resource records, step H1 SNAP (docs/reviews/records-holdings-snap-af.md) moved this item onto the records. Field sweep fix round (FS-SNAP-4, FS-SNAP-5). FS-SNAP-5: 4.408.1.A (S4823): "The value of liquid resources is the current redemption rate less encumbrances." Before, every liquid holding was read at its value, so securities pledged for a loan counted in full; now securities and other resources are read at value less amount_owed (not below 0), then the share. amount_owed is required where read (decision 4): a securities record that does not state it cannot be determined. A bank account and cash are not read for amount_owed: money held against a debt is under a creditor's hold or lien, which 4.410.F.1 (S2968) makes inaccessible ("property prohibited from sale by a creditor holding a lien"), and the record schema's accessible names ("under a creditor's lien"); the part held is stated as its own record with accessible false (records are disjoint). FS-SNAP-4: 4.410.F.3 (S2968): funds in a trust "shall be considered inaccessible to the household if" its conditions hold; before, the row read no trust at all (not_counted_reading_open). The trust interest is now counted at its value times the share unless the county's finding (snap_trust_inaccessible, decision D9) says the funds are inaccessible; a trust with no finding cannot be determined (decision 4). Whether one of F.3's conditions suffices (its "or") or all are needed (7 CFR 273.8(e)(8)'s "and", S4824) stays OQ-1307, inside the finding.

### CO-418 SNAP: ABAWD (able-bodied adult without dependents) time limit status `@engine`

Not subject when the person is outside the ABAWD (able-bodied adult without dependents) age range or otherwise exempt from the time limit for the month; within limit when countable months in the current 36-month clock period are below the 3-month limit; regained when the person has reached the limit but regained eligibility (4.311.3.D.1) and meets the work requirement in the month (D.2); additional months when the person, having regained eligibility, is in the single three-month period after notifying the office of no longer meeting it (D.3); otherwise limit reached.

Precision. Regained eligibility and the additional months come from snap_abawd_eligibility_regained (CO-2309) and snap_abawd_is_in_additional_months (CO-2312), both read as false when not stated; a person who becomes exempt is not subject (D.1.d).

Type one of, scope person-month, program SNAP.
Uses: `snap_abawd_countable_month_limit`, `snap_abawd_countable_months_in_period`, `snap_abawd_eligibility_regained`, `snap_abawd_is_in_additional_months`, `snap_is_exempt_from_abawd_time_limit`, `snap_is_in_abawd_age_range`, `snap_meets_abawd_work_requirement`.

```
if it is not the case that SNAP: is in the ABAWD age range
  then not_subject
else if SNAP: is exempt from the ABAWD time limit
  then not_subject
else if SNAP: countable ABAWD months in the current 36-month clock period is less than SNAP ABAWD countable month limit (3)
  then within_limit
else if all of the following are true:
    - SNAP: ABAWD eligibility regained, otherwise no
    - SNAP: meets the ABAWD work requirement for the month
  then regained
else if SNAP: is in the ABAWD additional three months
  then additional_months
otherwise limit_reached
```

```json
["case",[["not","snap_is_in_abawd_age_range"],"not_subject"],["snap_is_exempt_from_abawd_time_limit","not_subject"],[["<","snap_abawd_countable_months_in_period","snap_abawd_countable_month_limit"],"within_limit"],[["all",["otherwise","snap_abawd_eligibility_regained",false],"snap_meets_abawd_work_requirement"],"regained"],["snap_abawd_is_in_additional_months","additional_months"],["else","limit_reached"]]
```

### CO-4180 SNAP: requires verification that the household provides the majority of a child's meals `@engine`

Whether this household must verify that it provides this child with the majority of the child's meals before it receives benefits for the child: the child already receives SNAP in another household (10 CCR 2506-1 4.505.4.C, 4.304.2.A). Required whether or not the household's statement is questionable.

Precision. 4.505.4.C refers to "Section 4.304.1.B"; the rule it describes, for children applied for by two households, is 4.304.2 (Children in Shared Custody Arrangements), which this item follows. The household's other composition statements are verified only when questionable (snap_requires_verification_of_household_composition, CO-1383). receives_snap_in_another_household (CO-4178) is read as false when not stated.

Type yes/no, scope person-month, program SNAP.
Uses: `receives_snap_in_another_household`.

```
Receives SNAP in another household, otherwise no
```

```json
["otherwise","receives_snap_in_another_household",false]
```

### CO-4181 SNAP: majority-of-meals verification for a child is pending `@engine`

Whether this household must verify that it provides this child, who already receives SNAP in another household, with the majority of the child's meals, and has not done so; until it does, the child stays in the household in which the child first began receiving SNAP and is not a member of this one (10 CCR 2506-1 4.505.4.C, 4.304.2.B.4).

Precision. Not gated by membership of this household, unlike the other pending items: the child is not a member while this is pending (snap_is_household_member, CO-304), and becomes one when the verification is received. Where the verification is required and child_majority_of_meals_verified (CO-4179) is not stated, this outcome cannot be determined and asks for it (membership, CO-304, reads it as not verified). Due by: snap_verification_due_date (CO-1392).

Type yes/no, scope person-month, program SNAP.
Uses: `child_majority_of_meals_verified`, `snap_requires_verification_of_child_majority_meals`.

```
all of the following are true:
  - SNAP: requires verification that the household provides the majority of a child's meals
  - it is not the case that Majority of the child's meals verified
```

```json
["all","snap_requires_verification_of_child_majority_meals",["not","child_majority_of_meals_verified"]]
```

### CO-4182 SNAP: allotment cap for excluded disqualified members `@engine`

The largest full-month allotment this person's SNAP household may receive so that leaving members disqualified under 7 CFR 273.11(c)(1) out of its size does not increase it (273.11(c)(1)(ii)): the allotment for the size with those members counted (snap_household_size_with_disqualified_members) - the maximum allotment for that size less snap_benefit_reduction_rate of snap_net_income_with_disqualified_members, rounded down and not below zero, raised to snap_minimum_allotment for a household of that size of snap_minimum_allotment_household_size_limit or fewer that meets the net income test. With no such member, the household's maximum allotment, which never binds.

Precision. The maximum allotment for the larger size is read as snap_maximum_allotment (CO-383) reads it for the household's size. The net income test is the household's own (snap_meets_net_income_test, CO-382). snap_full_month_allotment (CO-2307) takes the lesser of its own computation and this cap. Duplicate-paths audit D-S3 (docs/reviews/duplicate-paths-audit.md): the allotment for the larger size before the minimum is its own item (snap_allotment_cap_before_minimum, CO-6001), which the initial month reads too (CO-6002, CO-2308); this item raises it to the minimum for the full month.

Type money, scope person-month, program SNAP.
Uses: `snap_allotment_cap_before_minimum`, `snap_eligible_household_size`, `snap_household_size_with_disqualified_members`, `snap_maximum_allotment`, `snap_meets_net_income_test`, `snap_minimum_allotment`, `snap_minimum_allotment_household_size_limit`.

```
if SNAP: household size with disqualified members counted is equal to SNAP: number of eligible household members
  then SNAP: maximum allotment
else if all of the following are true:
    - SNAP: household size with disqualified members counted is at most SNAP minimum allotment household size limit (2)
    - SNAP: meets the net income test
  then the greater of SNAP: allotment cap for excluded disqualified members, before the minimum and SNAP minimum allotment (25)
otherwise SNAP: allotment cap for excluded disqualified members, before the minimum
```

```json
["case",[["=","snap_household_size_with_disqualified_members","snap_eligible_household_size"],"snap_maximum_allotment"],[["all",["<=","snap_household_size_with_disqualified_members","snap_minimum_allotment_household_size_limit"],"snap_meets_net_income_test"],["max","snap_allotment_cap_before_minimum","snap_minimum_allotment"]],["else","snap_allotment_cap_before_minimum"]]
```

### CO-419 SNAP: meets the elderly/disabled separate-household election `@engine`

An otherwise eligible member who is sixty or older and unable to purchase and prepare their own meals because of a permanent disability may elect, with their spouse, to be a SNAP household separate from the others they live with, unless the income of those others (excluding the elderly/disabled member and their spouse) exceeds 165 percent of the federal poverty line for the size of that "others" group.

Precision. The 'others' group is this person's physical residence-sharing group (everyone reachable by a chain of buys_prepares_with or spouse edges), minus this person and this person's spouse (if any); their combined own gross income for the month (snap_person_gross_income_before_sponsor_income, CO-3712: final verification F-2, without income deemed from a sponsor), compared against snap_elderly_disabled_separate_household_income_limit_table (CO-114) keyed by the others' count (floored at 1, since the table has no size-0 entry), with snap_elderly_disabled_separate_household_income_limit_each_additional (CO-3043) for each member beyond the table's last row (hard-coded numbers audit S-1). The person must ask for the separate household (snap_requests_elderly_disabled_separate_household, CO-2303, read as false when unstated) and be sixty or older (snap_is_elderly; 273.1(b)(2) and 4.304.3.A both say sixty or older). Phase-10 sweep (OQ-37): snap_household_members (CO-305) now reads this item through snap_is_in_elderly_disabled_separate_household (CO-2304); because the others are the physical residence group, not the composed household, there is no cycle. Colorado's 4.304.3.A.2 counts the spouse in the others' household when the spouse is the one purchasing and preparing meals; no fact says who purchases and prepares, so the spouse is always set aside, as 273.1(b)(2) states. Coverage pass 2 N2-P3-5 (first-pass P3-6): 4.304.1.C.2 and 4.304.3.A.2 set the spouse aside in the 165% test "unless the spouse is the person purchasing and preparing meals"; 7 CFR 273.1(b)(2) excludes "the income of the elderly and disabled individual and his or her spouse" (S20) without condition, and a State may not count income the federal test leaves out, so the spouse is always set aside here, as the federal text requires.

### CO-4250 SNAP: lives in the same home as a child under the ABAWD dependent-child age `@engine`

Someone who lives in the same home as the person (lives_with, CO-1925) is under snap_abawd_dependent_child_age (14) on the first day of the month, whether or not that child is a member of the person's SNAP household or is eligible: the ABAWD exception for an individual "Residing in the same physical household with an individual who is under the age of eighteen (18). The minor individual does not have to be included in the same SNAP household" (10 CCR 2506-1 4.311.A.4; 7 CFR 273.24(c)(4)), with the age the amended statute sets.

Precision. Read from lives_with (one home, from dwelling_id). Where a case states no dwelling_id the person's SNAP household (snap_household_members, CO-305) stands in, as CO-305 reads an edge as living together when no home is stated (convention rule 17). The person need not be the child's parent or caretaker: that is the separate (c)(3) parent exception, snap_has_responsibility_for_abawd_dependent_child (CO-413). Age is computed for the first day of the month in context, as CO-412 and CO-413 do. Coverage pass 2 N2-P2-1: the physical-household reading is Colorado's (4.311.A.4); the statute and 7 CFR 273.24(c)(4) speak of a member of the SNAP household. Which governs is OQ-835 (needs Legal); the assumption is Colorado's reading. Three-pattern sweep D-1 (docs/reviews/pattern-sweep-snap-ce.md): lives_with (CO-1925) is read as stated, required where read: no text on file says that persons related on the application live together unless it says otherwise (7 CFR 273.1(a): a household is individuals who live together and customarily purchase and prepare meals together, S1), so a stated relationship is no longer read as living together where no dwelling_id is stated (decision 4; docs/conventions.md rule 17, as MAGI's readers since coverage pass 6, C6-10); a case with persons related across the edge states dwelling_id for each of them. Before, an unstated home read the SNAP household (snap_household_members) in its place. The persons of the case are read child by child: a person under the age is tested for living with this person, so a case with no child under the age is false whatever the homes, and a child whose home or this person's home is not stated is cannot determine. Coverage pass 7, C7-1 (docs/reviews/coverage7-snap.md): living together is read for the month (snap_lives_with_in_month, CO-7672), not from the homes of the determination date in every month: a member who moved out after the application month lived in the home in the months that began before the date the two ceased to live together (CO-7352, CO-7506, CO-7670), and one who moved in after it did not live there before (CO-7671), since the application month is determined on "the household's circumstances for the entire month of application" (7 CFR 273.10(a)(1)(i), S5091).

### CO-4260 SNAP: has a military connection `@engine`

The person has a military connection for SNAP (7 CFR 273.4(a)(6)(ii)(G); 10 CCR 2506-1 4.305.B.3.f): the person is on active duty (other than training) or an honorably discharged veteran; the spouse or unremarried surviving spouse of such a person; or an unmarried dependent child of such a person, which is a child under snap_military_dependent_child_age_limit (18), a full-time student under snap_military_dependent_student_age_limit (22), or an adult child who was disabled and dependent on the parent before eighteen.

Precision. Read from the person's own service (has_qualifying_military_service, CO-2866), a spouse's or legal parent's service across the spouse and child edges, and surviving-spouse status (is_surviving_spouse_of_veteran, CO-2867), as has_military_connection (CO-005) reads them. "Child" is "the legally adopted or biological child" (S3054, S3055): the parent edge (natural or adoptive), never a stepparent. A child under 18, or a full-time student under 22, is read as dependent on the parent. A full-time student is one whose education_enrollment_intensity is full_time, read as not a student when not stated (that fact is not stated for a person in no program). The disabled adult child reads was_disabled_and_dependent_on_parent_before_eighteen (CO-4257), false when not stated. The child of a deceased veteran must have been dependent at the death (4.305.B.3.f.3.e); a deceased parent is read through the same edges, and that dependency is read as the age and student tests. Coverage pass 4 S4-14 (decision 4 of 2026-11-23): education_enrollment_intensity is read with no default where this rule reads it (only for an unmarried dependent child of a veteran or service member between the dependent child's and the student's age limits); before, it was read as not full time when not stated. Coverage pass 4 for SNAP S4-11 (OQ-1263 resolved): the dependent child's ages are read in the month evaluated, since prospective budgeting reads "anticipated income and circumstances during the issuance month" (10 CCR 2506-1 4.402.1.A, S4734), and met when the child is under 18 (or, a full-time student, under 22) on the first day of the month (the age on the first day of the month; OQ-1262). Before, the age on the determination date in every month. Coverage pass 7 for SNAP, C7-4 (docs/reviews/coverage7-snap.md): the full-time student under twenty-two is a student in the month evaluated, so a month whose first day is after the expected_program_completion_date (CO-2882) is not one in which the child is a full-time student, as the three-pattern sweep's T-11 reads the completion date for the ineligible-student rule and the work registration exemption (CO-405, CO-411; 10 CCR 2506-1 4.306.C, S5092: enrollment is continuous "unless the student graduates"); with no completion date stated the enrollment continues.

### CO-4322 SNAP: rental income `@engine`

The person's rental income for the month from property the person does not actively manage an average of at least twenty hours a week, as SNAP counts it (10 CCR 2506-1 4.404.D): the month's rental receipts (receipts of the kind snap_receipt_treatment_table counts net of costs) less the cost of doing business (rental_property_costs, CO-4321), not below zero.

Precision. The costs allowed are those of 4.403.11.B-C, the kinds the self-employment cost facts describe, stated for the rented property. A loss is not offset against other income; only a farmer's self-employment loss is (4.403.12.E). Receipt records, migration phase 1: the rent is a receipt of kind rental_income, which snap_counted_recurring_receipts does not count (its row is net_of_costs); snap_person_unearned_income adds this net figure. Coverage pass 4 for SNAP (docs/reviews/coverage4-snap.md, S4-1 to S4-4): a record is placed in the month of its regular_date when it states one, since pay or a benefit that came early or late because of a holiday, a weekend, a changed pay date, a mailing cycle or the employee's request is counted by its regular schedule (10 CCR 2506-1 4.402.B.1-3, S4720; 4.403.A.3, S4721), else in the month it came in; a stream (a record with no month and no date) recurs only from the month its job or source began through the month it ended (job_start_date and job_end_date; start_date and end_date on a receipt), since pay after a job ends or before it begins is not anticipated with reasonable certainty (4.402.1.B, S4722). Coverage pass 4 S4-18: the rent is converted as snap_counted_recurring_receipts (CO-5011) converts a receipt (4.402.A.2, S3112). Coverage pass 4 S4-14 (decision 4): the costs are read only in a month with rent, and with no default (4.404.D counts "total income, less the cost of doing business" and gives no reading for costs not stated); before, unstated costs were read as 0. In a destitute household's month of application a record dated after the date of application is not counted (4.406.1.A, S2964; coverage pass 4 S4-14). Field sweep fix round (FS-SNAP-2): 10 CCR 2506-1 4.405.E (S3476): "Money received in the form of non-recurring lump sum payments, includes ... retroactive lump-sum Social Security, SSI, public assistance, railroad retirement benefits or other payments". A receipt marked retroactive is such a lump sum whatever its frequency states, so it is read as a receipt paid once (frequency once) is: not recurring income (it is a resource from the month received, 4.405.E last paragraph, S4691). Before, only frequency once was tested, and a retroactive payment stated with its month and no frequency (an undated record's frequency is monthly) was counted as the month's income.

### CO-4324 SNAP: person wages `@engine`

The person's pay for work as an employee for the month as SNAP counts it before its exclusions (10 CCR 2506-1 4.402.A.2, 4.403.3; 7 CFR 273.9(b)(1)(i), 273.10(c)(2)(i)): each earnings record whose row in snap_earnings_treatment_table is a pay row (counted, counted_no_rule_excludes, excluded, excluded_in_combat_zone, excluded_under_19_with_parent) received in the month, each at its own amount: infrequent or irregular pay as received; pay under an annually renewable contract (annual_contract_pay) averaged over snap_annual_averaging_months (4.403.3), except for a destitute migrant or seasonal farmworker household (4.402.2.A.4, last paragraph); a pay made weekly, every two weeks, twice a month or less often converted by the 4.402.A.2 multiplier for its frequency (snap_income_conversion_rate_table), the stream's per-pay amount times the multiplier, or, for a dated weekly or biweekly pay, its amount times the multiplier divided by the number of paydays of its schedule in the month, when a full month's income is anticipated (the job neither begins nor ends in the month); every other pay as received.

Precision. Earned-income records, step E1 (SNAP; docs/reviews/records-earnings-snap.md): each pay is converted by its own frequency (design 2.5: per-record conversion), so two jobs on different schedules are each converted, and a part of a pay that SNAP excludes is its own record converted by its own frequency, which retires snap_regular_wages_conversion_factor (CO-4682). The exclusions are left to snap_person_counted_wages (CO-5113; registered siblings: the same conversion), and snap_excluded_earned_income (CO-2338) is this figure less that one. 4.402.A.2 converts "When a full month's income is anticipated" and 7 CFR 273.10(c)(2)(i) (S2050) "Whenever a full month's income is anticipated but is received on a weekly or biweekly basis": a pay whose job begins or ends in the month (job_start_date, job_end_date) is read as received; a record that states neither date began before and continues through the month (CO-5100). A stream (no date) converts its per_payment, which is then required (a weekly stream with no per-pay amount cannot be determined: decision 4 of 2026-11-23); a dated weekly or biweekly pay is one of the paydays its schedule has in the month (7 or 14 days apart from its date, counted within the month), so the month's dated pays of one job average to the same multiple of the pay as the stream (design 4.4, ME-5): four dated weekly pays of x in a four-payday month or five in a five-payday month give 4.3x. A dated pay of another frequency is read in its month as received. Monthly pay needs no conversion. Contract pay is averaged whatever the month's receipt under the contract (4.403.3, S3115), so a contract record states annual_contract_pay in every month it covers, a month with no pay included (amount 0). Coverage pass 3 C3-8: contract income is not averaged for a migrant or seasonal farmworker household that is destitute (4.402.2.A.4, last paragraph: "shall not be averaged or annualized for migrant households that are destitute of income", S3113). Earnings not stated: cannot determine; a stated empty list is 0. Coverage pass 4 for SNAP (docs/reviews/coverage4-snap.md, S4-1 to S4-4): a record is placed in the month of its regular_date when it states one, since pay or a benefit that came early or late because of a holiday, a weekend, a changed pay date, a mailing cycle or the employee's request is counted by its regular schedule (10 CCR 2506-1 4.402.B.1-3, S4720; 4.403.A.3, S4721), else in the month it came in; a stream (a record with no month and no date) recurs only from the month its job or source began through the month it ended (job_start_date and job_end_date; start_date and end_date on a receipt), since pay after a job ends or before it begins is not anticipated with reasonable certainty (4.402.1.B, S4722); a pay or receipt of a schedule paid less often than monthly (every other month, quarterly, twice a year, annually) that states its month or its date is one payment of the schedule, counted at its amount times the 4.402.A.2 multiplier in each month of its interval, from its (regular) month through the month before the next payment is due, so a quarterly payment is a third of itself in each of three months, not a third in one month (S4-1); a dated weekly or biweekly pay or receipt is its amount times the multiplier divided by the paydays its schedule has in the month, counted from its regular date. Sick, vacation and bonus pay (leave_or_bonus_pay) dated after its job_end_date is not wages: installments are unearned income (snap_leave_pay_after_termination, CO-6600; 4.404.F, S4723) and a lump sum is a resource (S4-4). The pay rows include subsidized employment that is not WIOA-funded and a difficulty of care payment (counted_unless_wioa_funded, counted_unless_foster_care_boarder), which snap_person_counted_wages (CO-5113) counts or excludes by the record's fields (S4-6, S4-8).

### CO-4329 SNAP: self-employment income is averaged `@engine`

SNAP averages this person's self-employment income over the months snap_self_employment_averaging_months (CO-4349) gives, instead of counting each month's receipts and costs (10 CCR 2506-1 4.402.2.A.1, 4.403.12.A, C, D): the person states business receipts (an earnings record whose row in snap_earnings_treatment_table is counted_less_costs or counted_loss_offset), and every such record states that the enterprise is the household's annual support (annual_support), that its business has not changed substantially (changed_substantially), and that it began before the month of application (job_start_date; a record that states none began before the months the case covers); the household is not a destitute migrant household.

Precision. An enterprise whose business has changed substantially is counted on anticipated earnings (4.403.12.A, C), and one that began in the month of application has no past months to average, so for both the month's figures, which are the anticipated amounts, are read. Self-employment that is only part of the year's support (4.403.12.B) is not averaged here; the case states each self-employment month already averaged over the season. Averaging does not apply to a migrant household destitute of income (4.402.2.A, last paragraph). Earned-income records, step E1 (SNAP; docs/reviews/records-earnings-snap.md): the business's own records say it: annual_support and changed_substantially are required where read (decision D3 of the earned-income design: no rule text gives them a value, CO-5100), so a business that does not say whether it is the household's annual support cannot be determined (before step E1 an unstated fact was read as no); changed_substantially is read only for a business that is annual support. A person with no business records is not averaged.

### CO-4333 SNAP: counted child support exclusion `@engine`

The part of this person's legally obligated child support exclusion (snap_child_support_exclusion, CO-2003) that comes off the SNAP household's total countable gross income (10 CCR 2506-1 4.407.5.A): all of it for an eligible member and for a member disqualified and counted in full (4.411.1.B.1.a); for a member whose income is prorated (an ineligible non-citizen, an SSN refusal, an ABAWD at the time limit), the same share snap_counted_income_of_ineligible_member (CO-333) counts of the member's income (all but the ineligible members' shares, 7 CFR 273.11(c)(2)(iii); snap_prorated_member_share_counted_rate, CO-7250), since the child support "is deducted before prorating income" (4.411.1.B.2.c); nothing for an ineligible student, who is not a household member.

Precision. The exclusion is taken from the household's total, not from the paying member's own income, so a member who pays more support than the member's own counted income (a spouse whose wages are the household's, or a minor whose earnings are exempt) still has the whole payment excluded, as 4.407.5.A says ("Legally obligated child support paid by a household member under the age of eighteen (18) shall be an allowable exclusion, even if the income of the child is considered exempt"). For a prorated member, deducting the support before prorating and taking the same share of the support from the household's total give the same figure, except that the household's total, not the member's, is floored at zero. n is the count of snap_household_members_other_than_ineligible_students, as in CO-333. Coverage pass 6 for SNAP, C6-1 (docs/reviews/coverage6-snap.md): with two or more prorated members in the household, every prorated member's share is left out, not only this member's own: the fraction counted is snap_prorated_member_share_counted_rate (CO-7250), (n - k) / n with k the prorated members, as 7 CFR 273.11(c)(2)(ii)-(iii) (S4970) says ("All but the ineligible members' share is counted"). Before, (n - 1) / n was counted whatever k was.

### CO-4683 SNAP: fleeing felon under the four-part test `@engine`

The person is a fleeing felon for SNAP under Colorado's four-part test (10 CCR 2506-1 4.304.4.B.1-4): there is an outstanding felony warrant for the person (has_outstanding_felony_warrant, CO-4684), the person, aware of the warrant or reasonably expecting it, has acted to avoid arrest or jail, which is what fleeing to avoid prosecution or custody means (is_fleeing_felon, CO-038), and law enforcement is actively seeking the person as 4.304.4.C.1 defines it (law_enforcement_is_actively_seeking_person, CO-4685).

Precision. is_fleeing_felon (CO-038) states parts 2 and 3 (awareness and an action to avoid arrest are what fleeing is); the warrant and the active search are law enforcement's statements, so a person's own admission is not enough, as 4.304.4.B requires the status to be verified. Each of the two read as false when not stated; is_fleeing_felon unstated with either of them false is false here. Colorado Works and Adult Financial keep reading is_fleeing_felon by its own meaning.

Type yes/no, scope person, program SNAP.
Uses: `has_outstanding_felony_warrant`, `is_fleeing_felon`, `law_enforcement_is_actively_seeking_person`.

```
all of the following are true:
  - Has an outstanding felony warrant, otherwise no
  - Law enforcement is actively seeking the person, otherwise no
  - Is a fleeing felon
```

### CO-4689 SNAP: household holds a foster child applying apart from the foster family `@engine`

A member of this person's SNAP household is a foster child under snap_parental_control_age (18) who lives with a foster parent who is not in this SNAP household: the foster parent chose not to include the child, and the foster child, with the child's own child or spouse, "may not apply for benefits separately from the foster family unless they are over eighteen (18) and no longer under the parental control of the foster parents" (10 CCR 2506-1 4.304.3.B.3), so every member of this household is an ineligible member.

Precision. The foster child is read from the foster_child role to a foster parent who lives with the child (lives_with, CO-1925; read as living together where no dwelling is stated). A foster child included by the foster parent is in the foster parent's SNAP household (CO-305) and is false here. Coverage pass 4 for SNAP S4-11 (OQ-1263 resolved): the age is read in the month evaluated, since prospective budgeting reads "anticipated income and circumstances during the issuance month" (10 CCR 2506-1 4.402.1.A, S4734); the bar holds for a month only when the child is under 18 on every day of it, so on the last day (the age on the last day of the month; OQ-1262): a foster child who turns 18 during a month may apply separately for that month, the text's "unless they are over eighteen (18)". Before, the age on the determination date in every month. A foster child of 18 or older is read as no longer under the foster parents' parental control, the age at which parental control ends for SNAP (snap_parental_control_age). The household so found is reported as disqualified members (snap_person_participation_status, CO-2571), since the rule bars it from applying rather than naming a status. Coverage pass 3 N3-P2-1: 18 or older stands for Colorado's "over eighteen (18) and no longer under the parental control of the foster parents"; 7 CFR 273.1(c)(4) (S3651) has no age exception, and the choice between the two texts is OQ-875 (needs Legal).

Type yes/no, scope person-month, program SNAP.

there is a person in SNAP: household members such that
  all of the following are true:
    - (the number of whole years between that person's Date of birth and -1 days after the first day of the month after the month) is less than SNAP parental control age (18)
    - that person's SNAP: foster child outside the foster parent's SNAP household
```

The person is a foster child (foster_child role) of someone who lives with the person and is not in the person's SNAP household: the foster parent chose not to include the child (10 CCR 2506-1 4.304.3.B.1).

### CO-4930 SNAP: earned income other than self-employment `@engine`

The part of the person's earned income for the month for SNAP that is not self-employment: the pay SNAP counts (snap_person_counted_wages, CO-5113: wages and the other pay the counting table counts, each converted by its frequency, less what 4.405 excludes and, in a destitute household's month of application, the pay received after the date of application, 4.406.1.A), training allowances other than WIOA (receipts of kind vocational_training_allowance, receipts CO-5000; 10 CCR 2506-1 4.403.B.1) and Domestic Volunteer Service Act Title I (VISTA) payments to a person who was not receiving SNAP or public assistance on joining (4.403.A.2, C). A child student's earnings are excluded in full (0).

Precision. Not floored at 0: snap_person_earned_income (CO-330) adds net self-employment income (CO-1702) and net boarder income (CO-4165) to it and floors the sum, as before. Coverage pass 3 C3-1: this is the one list of the receipts SNAP counts as earned income other than self-employment, read both by snap_person_earned_income and by snap_requires_verification_of_earned_income (CO-1376), so the income counted and the income verified cannot drift apart again (4.506: "Monthly, gross nonexempt income shall be verified prior to initial certification", S830). Receipt records, migration phase 1: the training allowances and Title I payments are the month's receipts of the kinds vocational_training_allowance and dvsa_title_i_volunteer_payment (snap_receipt_treatment_table: counted as earned). Receipts not stated: cannot determine, unless the student exclusion applies first, since 4.403.A.2, B.1 and C count the payments received and give no reading for payments not reported (decision 4 of 2026-11-23 (docs/plan-colorado.md): missing information is cannot determine unless the rule says otherwise; the phase-1 default of 0 is removed); a stated empty list is no such payment. Earned-income records, step E1 (SNAP; docs/reviews/records-earnings-snap.md): the pay is read from the earnings records, counted record by record (CO-5113), so the excluded part (snap_excluded_earned_income, CO-2338) and the pay after a destitute household's application date (snap_earned_income_received_after_application_date, CO-4166, read as 0 when not stated) are no longer subtracted here; in that month each pay states its date, or the figure cannot be determined. Coverage pass 4 for SNAP (docs/reviews/coverage4-snap.md, S4-1 to S4-4): a record is placed in the month of its regular_date when it states one, since pay or a benefit that came early or late because of a holiday, a weekend, a changed pay date, a mailing cycle or the employee's request is counted by its regular schedule (10 CCR 2506-1 4.402.B.1-3, S4720; 4.403.A.3, S4721), else in the month it came in; a stream (a record with no month and no date) recurs only from the month its job or source began through the month it ended (job_start_date and job_end_date; start_date and end_date on a receipt), since pay after a job ends or before it begins is not anticipated with reasonable certainty (4.402.1.B, S4722). Coverage pass 4 S4-18: the training allowances and Title I payments are converted as snap_counted_recurring_receipts (CO-5011) converts a receipt (4.402.A.2, S3112), not summed at their amount. Coverage pass 4 S4-14 (decision 4): whether the volunteer was receiving SNAP or public assistance on joining VISTA is read only for a person with Title I payments in the month, and with no default (4.403.A.2, S3106, excludes the payments "if the client was receiving SNAP benefits when they joined VISTA" and gives no reading for a status not stated); before, it was read as false. In a destitute household's month of application a record dated after the date of application is not counted (4.406.1.A, S2964; coverage pass 4 S4-14). Field sweep fix round (FS-SNAP-2): 10 CCR 2506-1 4.405.E (S3476): "Money received in the form of non-recurring lump sum payments, includes ... retroactive lump-sum Social Security, SSI, public assistance, railroad retirement benefits or other payments". A receipt marked retroactive is such a lump sum whatever its frequency states, so it is read as a receipt paid once (frequency once) is: not recurring income (it is a resource from the month received, 4.405.E last paragraph, S4691). Before, only frequency once was tested, and a retroactive payment stated with its month and no frequency (an undated record's frequency is monthly) was counted as the month's income.

Type money, scope person-month, program SNAP.

### CO-4931 SNAP: person's stated shelter costs `@engine`

The continuing shelter costs the person states for the month that SNAP allows (10 CCR 2506-1 4.407.3.E): rent or mortgage, property tax and home insurance (shelter_cost_monthly, CO-035) plus the other continuing charges for the dwelling - association fees, mobile-home loans, second mortgages and home-equity loans, reverse-mortgage repayments and disaster repairs (shelter_other_continuing_charges, CO-4345).

Precision. Coverage pass 3 C3-3: the one sum of the stated shelter costs, read both by snap_shelter_costs (CO-2300), which counts them, and by snap_requires_verification_of_shelter_costs (CO-1379), which asks for them when questionable, so a cost counted is a cost that can be verified.

Type money, scope person-month, program SNAP.
Uses: `shelter_cost_monthly`, `shelter_other_continuing_charges`.

```
Shelter cost, monthly plus (Other continuing shelter charges, otherwise 0)
```

### CO-5011 SNAP: a person's counted recurring receipts `@engine`

The person's recurring receipts of the month that SNAP's counting table counts (counted, counted because no rule excludes it, counted beyond the quarterly limit, a recurring Colorado Works diversion), each at its monthly amount: a receipt paid weekly, every two weeks, twice a month or less often than monthly converted by the 4.402.A.2 multiplier (snap_income_conversion_rate_table; 7 CFR 273.10(c)(2)(i)), any other at the amount received in the month; less the parts of it 4.405 leaves out: an overpayment recouped from the same source other than for an intentional failure to comply (D.1), child support turned over to the IV-D agency (D.2), a former spouse's share of military retirement (A.11), money received for a person who is not a household member (B: the part received for a person living elsewhere, and the part of a veterans benefit paid because of a dependent of the case who is not in the person's SNAP household in the month: one who lives elsewhere, or lives in the home but buys and prepares food apart and is no mandatory member) and income set aside under a PASS (A.22). Plus foster care payments when a foster individual placed with the person is a member of the household (snap_foster_care_payments_are_counted; 7 CFR 273.9(b)(2)(ii), (c)(15)), and a Colorado Works diversion paid once that covers more than snap_diversion_lump_sum_max_days (90) days of expenses or is expected again within twelve months, averaged over the months it covers (4.405.E, 4.402.2).

Precision. A receipt paid once is a nonrecurring lump sum, excluded (4.405.E), except a Colorado Works diversion that covers more than ninety days of expenses or is expected to occur again in a twelve-month period (4.405.E, second paragraph, S3476; coverage pass 2 C2-5, whose condition lived in the retired lump-sum fact CO-3367; coverage pass 4 S4-5): it is not a nonrecurring lump sum, and it is "income intended to cover a specific period of time ... divided by the number of months the income is intended to cover" (4.402.2, S4724), so its amount is divided by the months from the month of covers_from through the month of covers_through and counted in each of them. A diversion of ninety days or less not expected again is excluded; its period's dates and whether it recurs are required where read (decision 4 of 2026-11-23). Coverage pass 4 for SNAP (docs/reviews/coverage4-snap.md, S4-1 to S4-4): a record is placed in the month of its regular_date when it states one, since pay or a benefit that came early or late because of a holiday, a weekend, a changed pay date, a mailing cycle or the employee's request is counted by its regular schedule (10 CCR 2506-1 4.402.B.1-3, S4720; 4.403.A.3, S4721), else in the month it came in; a stream (a record with no month and no date) recurs only from the month its job or source began through the month it ended (job_start_date and job_end_date; start_date and end_date on a receipt), since pay after a job ends or before it begins is not anticipated with reasonable certainty (4.402.1.B, S4722); a pay or receipt of a schedule paid less often than monthly (every other month, quarterly, twice a year, annually) that states its month or its date is one payment of the schedule, counted at its amount times the 4.402.A.2 multiplier in each month of its interval, from its (regular) month through the month before the next payment is due, so a quarterly payment is a third of itself in each of three months, not a third in one month (S4-1); a dated weekly or biweekly pay or receipt is its amount times the multiplier divided by the paydays its schedule has in the month, counted from its regular date. Each receipt is converted as snap_person_wages (CO-4324) converts a pay (registered siblings). A receipt with no date that states its month is converted by its per_payment (coverage pass 3 C3-4, CF-3); a dated weekly or biweekly receipt needs no per_payment. A stream whose start_date or end_date falls in the month is read at its amount ("When a full month's income is anticipated", 4.402.A.2). Foster care payments (S4-6): 273.9(c)(15) (S4725) excludes "Governmental foster care payments received by households with foster care individuals who are considered to be boarders", and 273.9(b)(2)(ii) counts them for "children or adults who are considered members of the household"; the membership test is read only when the person states such a payment. Replaces the periodic-income facts (CO-4330 to CO-4332: one such income per person); a receipt's frequency and per_payment now state it for each receipt. In a destitute household's month of application a record dated after the date of application is not counted (4.406.1.A, S2964; coverage pass 4 S4-14). Field sweep fix round (FS-SNAP-2): 10 CCR 2506-1 4.405.E (S3476): "Money received in the form of non-recurring lump sum payments, includes ... retroactive lump-sum Social Security, SSI, public assistance, railroad retirement benefits or other payments". A receipt marked retroactive is such a lump sum whatever its frequency states, so it is read as a receipt paid once (frequency once) is: not recurring income (it is a resource from the month received, 4.405.E last paragraph, S4691). Before, only frequency once was tested, and a retroactive payment stated with its month and no frequency (an undated record's frequency is monthly) was counted as the month's income. Coverage verification 7, V7-2 (docs/reviews/verify-coverage7-fixes.md): 4.405.B (S3100) excludes "Monies received and used for the care and maintenance of a third-party beneficiary who is not a household member" and "any identifiable portion of the payment intended and used for the care and maintenance of the non-household member" (7 CFR 273.9(c)(6)). The receipts state that part once (CO-5000): for a beneficiary who is not a person of the case and lives elsewhere, for_person_living_elsewhere; for a veterans benefit's dependent who is a person of the case, for_dependent with for_person, wherever the dependent lives. The record's for_dependent is taken off where its for_person does not live with the person in the month (snap_lives_with_in_month, CO-7672), and is not read otherwise; a dependent who lives with the person is a household member (a spouse, or a child under 22 with a parent, 7 CFR 273.1(b)(1)), so the part is the household's income. Close-out verification F2 (KL-SNAP-4, docs/reviews/known-limits.md; 2026-11-24): the record's for_dependent is taken off where its for_person is not in the person's household of the month as SNAP builds it before any elderly and disabled separate household (snap_household_members_before_elderly_disabled_separation, CO-7892): CO-305's own membership, which reads income only through the 165 percent test of 273.1(b)(2) (CO-2304, CO-419), so CO-5011 cannot read it without a cycle, but whose every other part (the homes of the month, the spouse, mandatory parent and child and caretaker edges, purchase and prepare, institution, boarder) reads no income. A dependent outside that group is in no SNAP household with the person: one who lives elsewhere, or a parent or an adult child of 22 or older in the home who buys and prepares food apart (273.1(a)(2), S1). A dependent inside it whom only an elderly and disabled separate household would take out of the household is counted with it (OQ-1510). Before, a dependent of the case who lives in the home but buys and prepares meals apart was counted (probe H2: the veteran's mother of 76, $185 where the text gives $320). Before, SNAP never read for_dependent, so a dependent of the case who lives elsewhere, stated as the meaning asks, was counted as the veteran's income (S6-A: $185 where the text gives $320).

Type money, scope person-month, program SNAP.
Uses: `is_destitute_migrant_or_seasonal_farmworker`, `receipts`, `snap_application_date`, `snap_diversion_lump_sum_max_days`, `snap_foster_care_payments_are_counted`, `snap_household_members_before_elderly_disabled_separation`, `snap_income_conversion_rate_table`, `snap_receipt_treatment_table`.

### CO-5012 SNAP: a person's substantial gambling winnings `@engine`

The person's lottery or gambling winnings of the month, each a single game's prize, that are substantial: at least snap_resource_limit_elderly_disabled, before taxes or withholding (10 CCR 2506-1 4.000.1, 4.403.I; 7 CFR 273.11(r)): counted as unearned income in the month received.

Precision. One receipt per game (receipts, kind gambling_winnings). Other winnings are a nonrecurring lump sum, excluded as income and held as a resource (4.405.E). In a destitute household's month of application a record dated after the date of application is not counted (4.406.1.A, S2964; coverage pass 4 S4-14).

Type money, scope person-month, program SNAP.
Uses: `is_destitute_migrant_or_seasonal_farmworker`, `receipts`, `snap_application_date`, `snap_receipt_treatment_table`, `snap_resource_limit_elderly_disabled`.

```
the sum for each receipt in Receipts where
    all of the following are true:
      - SNAP: how each kind of receipt is treated (table), for that receipt's kind is equal to counted_if_substantial
      - that receipt is received in the month
      - that receipt's amount is at least SNAP resource limit, household with an elderly or disabled member (4750)
      - it is not the case that (all of the following are true:;   - Is a destitute migrant or seasonal farmworker, otherwise no;   - the month is equal to the month containing SNAP: application date;   - that receipt's date is more than SNAP: application date)
  of
    that receipt's amount
```

### CO-5013 SNAP: infrequent or irregular unearned receipts in the calendar quarter `@engine`

The person's receipts marked infrequent or irregular that SNAP counts as income (snap_receipt_treatment_table), not paid once, received in the months of the calendar quarter that contains the month (10 CCR 2506-1 4.405.A; 7 CFR 273.9(c)(2) "in a quarter").

Precision. The calendar quarter is also the federal fiscal quarter. Each earlier month's receipts are summed in that month ("in that month"), so a receipt is counted with the treatment table in force in the month it is received (docs/operators.md, Resolution step 2 and P57). Decision 4 of 2026-11-23 (docs/plan-colorado.md: missing information is cannot determine unless the rule says otherwise), applied as the reader-defaults round did (b49a7f2): receipts not stated are cannot determine (before, each month of the quarter was read as 0, as infrequent_or_irregular_income_in_quarter, CO-4077, read the month's fact); 4.405.A and 273.9(c)(2) exclude income "not in excess of $30 in a quarter" and give no reading for income not reported. A stated empty list is no irregular receipts. Its readers ask for the quarter only in a month that has irregular income of their own list (CO-5111, CO-5014). Coverage pass 4 S4-12: the $30 is a limit on income (4.405.A, S3100: "Any income ... not in excess of thirty dollars ($30) in three (3) months"), so only receipts SNAP's counting table counts as income (counted, counted because no rule excludes it, counted beyond the quarterly limit, counted as earned, net of costs, a diversion) and that are not paid once are summed; a reimbursement, a loan, educational assistance or a nonrecurring lump sum is not income (4.405.E, F, I, 4.405.1) and is not held against the limit. A record is placed by its regular date and its source's dates (S4-2, S4-3). Field sweep fix round (FS-SNAP-2): 10 CCR 2506-1 4.405.E (S3476): "Money received in the form of non-recurring lump sum payments, includes ... retroactive lump-sum Social Security, SSI, public assistance, railroad retirement benefits or other payments". A receipt marked retroactive is such a lump sum whatever its frequency states, so it is read as a receipt paid once (frequency once) is: not recurring income (it is a resource from the month received, 4.405.E last paragraph, S4691). Before, only frequency once was tested, and a retroactive payment stated with its month and no frequency (an undated record's frequency is monthly) was counted as the month's income.

Type money, scope person-month, program SNAP.
Uses: `receipts`, `snap_calendar_quarter_months`, `snap_receipt_treatment_table`.

```
the sum of the sum of that receipt's amount for each receipt in Receipts where ((all of the following are true:;   - that receipt's irregular;   - it is not the case that (any of the following is true:;   - that receipt's frequency is equal to once;   - that receipt's retroactive);   - if it is not the case that that receipt's regular date is unknown;     then the month containing that receipt's regular date is equal to the month;   otherwise (all of the following are true:;   - that receipt is received in the month;   - any of the following is true:;     - it is not the case that that receipt's month is unknown;     - all of the following are true:;       - any of the following is true:;         - that receipt's start date is unknown;         - the month containing that receipt's start date is at most the month;       - any of the following is true:;         - that receipt's end date is unknown;         - the month containing that receipt's end date is at least the month);   - SNAP: how each kind of receipt is treated (table), for that receipt's kind is one of: counted, counted_no_rule_excludes, counted_beyond_quarterly_limit, counted_as_earned, net_of_costs, counted_unless_short_lump_sum)) for that month for each month in SNAP: the months of the calendar quarter
```

### CO-5014 SNAP: excluded infrequent or irregular unearned receipts `@engine`

The month's recurring receipts marked infrequent or irregular that SNAP's counting table counts, when the calendar quarter's infrequent or irregular income, unearned and earned, is no more than snap_irregular_income_quarterly_limit (snap_irregular_income_is_within_quarterly_limit, CO-5110; 10 CCR 2506-1 4.405.A); otherwise 0, and 0 in a month with no such receipt.

Precision. Earned-income records, step E1 (SNAP; docs/reviews/records-earnings-snap.md): the quarter test is one item, read by this item and by snap_irregular_earnings_are_excluded (CO-5111) (duplicate-paths audit D-S4: it was written in both this item and snap_excluded_earned_income, CO-2338). A month with no irregular counted receipt has nothing to exclude, so the quarter is not read. Coverage pass 4 for SNAP (docs/reviews/coverage4-snap.md, S4-1 to S4-4): a record is placed in the month of its regular_date when it states one, since pay or a benefit that came early or late because of a holiday, a weekend, a changed pay date, a mailing cycle or the employee's request is counted by its regular schedule (10 CCR 2506-1 4.402.B.1-3, S4720; 4.403.A.3, S4721), else in the month it came in; a stream (a record with no month and no date) recurs only from the month its job or source began through the month it ended (job_start_date and job_end_date; start_date and end_date on a receipt), since pay after a job ends or before it begins is not anticipated with reasonable certainty (4.402.1.B, S4722). In a destitute household's month of application a record dated after the date of application is not counted (4.406.1.A, S2964; coverage pass 4 S4-14). Field sweep fix round (FS-SNAP-2): 10 CCR 2506-1 4.405.E (S3476): "Money received in the form of non-recurring lump sum payments, includes ... retroactive lump-sum Social Security, SSI, public assistance, railroad retirement benefits or other payments". A receipt marked retroactive is such a lump sum whatever its frequency states, so it is read as a receipt paid once (frequency once) is: not recurring income (it is a resource from the month received, 4.405.E last paragraph, S4691). Before, only frequency once was tested, and a retroactive payment stated with its month and no frequency (an undated record's frequency is monthly) was counted as the month's income.

### CO-5015 SNAP: excluded need-based charitable cash `@engine`

The month's need-based charitable cash receipts, up to what the earlier months of the calendar quarter left of snap_charitable_cash_quarterly_limit (10 CCR 2506-1 4.405.A.10).

Precision. The limit applies to the quarter's donations in the order received. Each earlier month's receipts are summed in that month ("in that month"), so a receipt is counted with the treatment table in force in the month it is received (docs/operators.md, Resolution step 2 and P57). Decision 4 of 2026-11-23 (docs/plan-colorado.md: missing information is cannot determine unless the rule says otherwise), applied as the reader-defaults round did (b49a7f2): receipts not stated are cannot determine (before, each earlier month was read as 0); 4.405.A.10 excludes donations "not exceeding three hundred dollars ($300) in the aggregate, per fiscal quarter" and gives no reading for donations not reported. The month's own sum already read the receipts with no default, so a person who states none was cannot determine before as well. Coverage pass 4 for SNAP (docs/reviews/coverage4-snap.md, S4-1 to S4-4): a record is placed in the month of its regular_date when it states one, since pay or a benefit that came early or late because of a holiday, a weekend, a changed pay date, a mailing cycle or the employee's request is counted by its regular schedule (10 CCR 2506-1 4.402.B.1-3, S4720; 4.403.A.3, S4721), else in the month it came in; a stream (a record with no month and no date) recurs only from the month its job or source began through the month it ended (job_start_date and job_end_date; start_date and end_date on a receipt), since pay after a job ends or before it begins is not anticipated with reasonable certainty (4.402.1.B, S4722). Coverage pass 4 S4-18: the donations are read at the amount snap_counted_recurring_receipts (CO-5011) counts them at (4.402.A.2, S3112), so what is excluded is what was counted. In a destitute household's month of application a record dated after the date of application is not counted (4.406.1.A, S2964; coverage pass 4 S4-14). Field sweep fix round (FS-SNAP-2): 10 CCR 2506-1 4.405.E (S3476): "Money received in the form of non-recurring lump sum payments, includes ... retroactive lump-sum Social Security, SSI, public assistance, railroad retirement benefits or other payments". A receipt marked retroactive is such a lump sum whatever its frequency states, so it is read as a receipt paid once (frequency once) is: not recurring income (it is a resource from the month received, 4.405.E last paragraph, S4691). Before, only frequency once was tested, and a retroactive payment stated with its month and no frequency (an undated record's frequency is monthly) was counted as the month's income.

Type money, scope person-month, program SNAP.
Uses: `is_destitute_migrant_or_seasonal_farmworker`, `receipts`, `snap_application_date`, `snap_calendar_quarter_months_before`, `snap_charitable_cash_quarterly_limit`, `snap_income_conversion_rate_table`, `snap_receipt_treatment_table`.

### CO-5110 SNAP: infrequent or irregular income of the quarter is within the limit `@engine`

The person's income received too infrequently or irregularly to be reasonably anticipated in the calendar quarter that contains the month, unearned (receipts marked irregular, snap_irregular_unearned_receipts_in_quarter, CO-5013) and earned (earnings records marked irregular, of every kind that is not a cost of doing business), is no more than snap_irregular_income_quarterly_limit, so the irregular income is excluded (10 CCR 2506-1 4.405.A, S3100: "$30 or less in three months"; 7 CFR 273.9(c)(2), S3128: "not in excess of $30 in a quarter").

Precision. One test for both readers (duplicate-paths audit D-S4: the test was written twice, in snap_excluded_earned_income, CO-2338, and snap_excluded_irregular_receipts, CO-5014): snap_irregular_earnings_are_excluded (CO-5111) and snap_excluded_irregular_receipts (CO-5014) read it, each only in a month that has irregular income of its own list. The calendar quarter is also the federal fiscal quarter (snap_calendar_quarter_months, CO-5021). Each month's earnings are summed in that month ("in that month"), so a record is read with the counting table in force in the month it was received. Earnings not stated: cannot determine (decision 4 of 2026-11-23); a stated empty list is no irregular earnings. Coverage pass 4 S4-12: only earnings SNAP counts are held against the limit (the pay and business rows, boarders other than foster care boarders, special pay outside a combat zone, subsidized employment not funded by WIOA, a difficulty of care payment not for foster care); work-study, summer youth employment, SCSEP pay, in-kind pay and costs are not income and are left out. Payments for meals only or a room only are boarder records SNAP reads (S4-9), so they are no longer left out.

### CO-5111 SNAP: irregular earnings of the month are excluded `@engine`

The person's earnings records received in the month include infrequent or irregular income (a record marked irregular, of a kind that is not a cost of doing business) and the quarter's infrequent or irregular income is within the limit (snap_irregular_income_is_within_quarterly_limit, CO-5110), so SNAP excludes the month's irregular earnings (10 CCR 2506-1 4.405.A; 7 CFR 273.9(c)(2)); false in a month with no irregular earnings.

Precision. A month with no irregular earnings has nothing to exclude, so the quarter is not read (the receipts of the quarter may then be unstated). The pay it excludes is read by snap_person_counted_wages (CO-5113), and the business receipts by snap_self_employment_gross_receipts (CO-5114) and snap_farm_gross_receipts (CO-5115). A meals-only or room-only boarder record is left out, as in CO-5110. Coverage pass 4 S4-12: the month's irregular earnings are those snap_irregular_income_is_within_quarterly_limit (CO-5110) holds against the limit.

### CO-5112 SNAP: WIOA on-the-job training earnings are excluded `@engine`

The person has earnings from WIOA on-the-job training in the month (a record whose row in snap_earnings_treatment_table is excluded_under_19_with_parent) and is a member under snap_wioa_ojt_exclusion_age_limit (19) on the first day of the month who lives with a parent or is under the parental control of an adult member, so those earnings are excluded (10 CCR 2506-1 4.405.2.A.6, 4.403.B.2, S3108: "On-the-job training payments for members under nineteen (19) years of age who are participating in WIOA Programs and are under the parental control of an adult member of the household shall be excluded as income"); false when the month has no such earnings.

Precision. The test of snap_excluded_earned_income (CO-2338) before step E1, unchanged: the age on the first day of the month, and the living-with-a-parent or parental-control test of snap_student_earnings_are_excluded (CO-2569). A person with no on-the-job training pay in the month is not tested, so the person's age and relationships are not read. Coverage pass 4 for SNAP (docs/reviews/coverage4-snap.md, S4-1 to S4-4): a record is placed in the month of its regular_date when it states one, since pay or a benefit that came early or late because of a holiday, a weekend, a changed pay date, a mailing cycle or the employee's request is counted by its regular schedule (10 CCR 2506-1 4.402.B.1-3, S4720; 4.403.A.3, S4721), else in the month it came in; a stream (a record with no month and no date) recurs only from the month its job or source began through the month it ended (job_start_date and job_end_date; start_date and end_date on a receipt), since pay after a job ends or before it begins is not anticipated with reasonable certainty (4.402.1.B, S4722). Three-pattern sweep D-1 (docs/reviews/pattern-sweep-snap-ce.md): lives_with (CO-1925) is read as stated, required where read: no text on file says that persons related on the application live together unless it says otherwise (7 CFR 273.1(a): a household is individuals who live together and customarily purchase and prepare meals together, S1), so a stated relationship is no longer read as living together where no dwelling_id is stated (decision 4; docs/conventions.md rule 17, as MAGI's readers since coverage pass 6, C6-10); a case with persons related across the edge states dwelling_id for each of them. Coverage pass 7, C7-1 (docs/reviews/coverage7-snap.md): living together is read for the month (snap_lives_with_in_month, CO-7672), not from the homes of the determination date in every month: a member who moved out after the application month lived in the home in the months that began before the date the two ceased to live together (CO-7352, CO-7506, CO-7670), and one who moved in after it did not live there before (CO-7671), since the application month is determined on "the household's circumstances for the entire month of application" (7 CFR 273.10(a)(1)(i), S5091).

### CO-5113 SNAP: counted wages `@engine`

The person's pay for work as an employee that SNAP counts for the month (10 CCR 2506-1 4.402.A.2, 4.403, 4.405; 7 CFR 273.9(b)(1)(i)): each earnings record SNAP's counting table counts as pay (snap_earnings_treatment_table: counted or counted_no_rule_excludes; uniformed_services_special_pay not received in a combat zone; WIOA on-the-job training unless snap_wioa_ojt_earnings_are_excluded), at the amount snap_person_wages (CO-4324) gives it, less its mandatory military education deduction (4.405.2.A.13), less the month's infrequent or irregular pay when snap_irregular_earnings_are_excluded (4.405.A), and, in a destitute household's month of application, without the pay received after the date of application (4.406.1.A). Less the part of a pay set aside under a Plan for Achieving Self-Support (4.405.2.A.22).

Precision. Each record's amount is converted as snap_person_wages converts it (registered siblings: a pay converted by 4.402.A.2 in one is converted the same way in the other, so the counted part of the pay and the whole of it cannot disagree). The rows SNAP excludes (work_study 4.405.1, summer_youth_employment and WIOA on-the-job training of a member under 19, 4.405.2.A.6, scsep_employment A.9, combat pay A.12, in_kind_pay 273.9(c)(1)) are left out. The education deduction is the month's amount withheld (the record's education_deduction), not converted. In a destitute household's month of application (is_destitute_migrant_or_seasonal_farmworker, the month of snap_application_date) each counted pay must state its date: one dated after the application date is not counted, and one with no date cannot be placed, so the figure cannot be determined (decision 4 of 2026-11-23; before step E1 the pay after the date was a separate fact read as 0 when not stated). Earnings not stated: cannot determine; a stated empty list is 0. Coverage pass 4 for SNAP (docs/reviews/coverage4-snap.md, S4-1 to S4-4): a record is placed in the month of its regular_date when it states one, since pay or a benefit that came early or late because of a holiday, a weekend, a changed pay date, a mailing cycle or the employee's request is counted by its regular schedule (10 CCR 2506-1 4.402.B.1-3, S4720; 4.403.A.3, S4721), else in the month it came in; a stream (a record with no month and no date) recurs only from the month its job or source began through the month it ended (job_start_date and job_end_date; start_date and end_date on a receipt), since pay after a job ends or before it begins is not anticipated with reasonable certainty (4.402.1.B, S4722); a pay or receipt of a schedule paid less often than monthly (every other month, quarterly, twice a year, annually) that states its month or its date is one payment of the schedule, counted at its amount times the 4.402.A.2 multiplier in each month of its interval, from its (regular) month through the month before the next payment is due, so a quarterly payment is a third of itself in each of three months, not a third in one month (S4-1); a dated weekly or biweekly pay or receipt is its amount times the multiplier divided by the paydays its schedule has in the month, counted from its regular date. Sick, vacation and bonus pay dated after the job ended is left out (4.404.F, S4723; snap_leave_pay_after_termination, CO-6600). Subsidized employment paid under a WIOA-funded program (wioa_funded) is excluded (10 CCR 2506-1 4.405.2.A.6, S3108: "Payments, allowances and earnings under the Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act (WIOA) are excluded as income"; 7 CFR 273.9(c)(10)(v), S4727; S4-8). A difficulty of care payment marked foster_care is counted only when a foster individual placed with the person is a member of the household (snap_foster_care_payments_are_counted, CO-6601; 7 CFR 273.9(b)(2)(ii), (c)(15), S4725; S4-6), read only when the person states one. Field sweep fix round (FS-SNAP-1): 10 CCR 2506-1 4.405.2.A.22 (S3110) excludes "Amounts necessary for the fulfillment of a Plan for Achieving Self-Support (PASS) under Title XVI of the Social Security Act", whatever income they come from; the part of a pay or a business's receipts set aside under a PASS (the earnings record's pass_set_aside, the month's amount set aside, not converted) is left out, as the receipts' set-aside is (snap_counted_recurring_receipts, CO-5011). Before, only the receipts' field was read and a set-aside of earnings was counted. Coverage pass 6 for SNAP, C6-4 (docs/reviews/coverage6-snap.md): the part of a pay its payer withheld to repay an advance on wages or an earlier overpayment (the earnings record's recouped, the month's amount, not converted) is left out, as the receipts' recouped is: 4.403.A.3 (S4721), "only the wages received is considered as income. The amount of repayment is disregarded", and 4.405.D.1 (S3102), "Only the net income received from these sources shall be considered countable income". The same part is left out of an irregular pay the quarter's limit excludes, so an excluded irregular pay takes off what was counted of it (amount less education deduction, PASS set-aside and repayment), never more. Before, no field stated the repayment and the gross was counted.

### CO-5114 SNAP: self-employment gross receipts `@engine`

The gross receipts of the person's self-employment other than a farm that SNAP counts for the month: the earnings records whose row in snap_earnings_treatment_table is counted_less_costs (self_employment_receipts) received in the month (10 CCR 2506-1 4.403.11; 7 CFR 273.9(b)(1)(ii)), less those marked irregular when snap_irregular_earnings_are_excluded (4.405.A), and, in a destitute household's month of application, without the receipts dated after the date of application (4.406.1.A). Each less the part set aside under a Plan for Achieving Self-Support (4.405.2.A.22).

Precision. The costs are snap_self_employment_costs (CO-1701); snap_self_employment_income (CO-1702) subtracts them. In a destitute household's month of application each receipt must state its date (decision 4 of 2026-11-23), as the pay does (snap_person_counted_wages, CO-5113). Earnings not stated: cannot determine. Coverage pass 4 for SNAP (docs/reviews/coverage4-snap.md, S4-1 to S4-4): a record is placed in the month of its regular_date when it states one, since pay or a benefit that came early or late because of a holiday, a weekend, a changed pay date, a mailing cycle or the employee's request is counted by its regular schedule (10 CCR 2506-1 4.402.B.1-3, S4720; 4.403.A.3, S4721), else in the month it came in; a stream (a record with no month and no date) recurs only from the month its job or source began through the month it ended (job_start_date and job_end_date; start_date and end_date on a receipt), since pay after a job ends or before it begins is not anticipated with reasonable certainty (4.402.1.B, S4722). Field sweep fix round (FS-SNAP-1): 10 CCR 2506-1 4.405.2.A.22 (S3110) excludes "Amounts necessary for the fulfillment of a Plan for Achieving Self-Support (PASS) under Title XVI of the Social Security Act", whatever income they come from; the part of a pay or a business's receipts set aside under a PASS (the earnings record's pass_set_aside, the month's amount set aside, not converted) is left out, as the receipts' set-aside is (snap_counted_recurring_receipts, CO-5011). Before, only the receipts' field was read and a set-aside of earnings was counted. Coverage pass 6 for SNAP, C6-4: a part of the receipts withheld by the payer to recover its earlier overpayment (the record's recouped) is left out (4.405.D.1, S3102: "Only the net income received from these sources shall be considered countable income"), in the counted receipts and in the irregular receipts the quarter's limit excludes alike; sibling of snap_person_counted_wages (CO-5113).

Type money, scope person-month, program SNAP.
Uses: `earnings`, `is_destitute_migrant_or_seasonal_farmworker`, `snap_application_date`, `snap_earnings_treatment_table`, `snap_irregular_earnings_are_excluded`.

```
(the sum of (that receipt's amount minus (that receipt's pass set aside plus that receipt's recouped)) for each receipt in Earnings where ((all of the following are true:;   - SNAP: how each kind of earnings is treated (table), for that receipt's kind is equal to counted_less_costs;   - if it is not the case that that receipt's regular date is unknown;     then the month containing that receipt's regular date is equal to the month;   otherwise (all of the following are true:;   - that receipt is received in the month;   - any of the following is true:;     - it is not the case that that receipt's month is unknown;     - all of the following are true:;       - any of the following is true:;         - that receipt's job start date is unknown;         - the month containing that receipt's job start date is at most the month;       - any of the following is true:;         - that receipt's job end date is unknown;         - the month containing that receipt's job end date is at least the month);   - it is not the case that (all of the following are true:;   - Is a destitute migrant or seasonal farmworker, otherwise no;   - the month is equal to the month containing SNAP: application date;   - that receipt's date is more than SNAP: application date)))) minus (if SNAP: irregular earnings of the month are excluded;   then the sum of (that receipt's amount minus (that receipt's pass set aside plus that receipt's recouped)) for each receipt in Earnings where ((all of the following are true:;   - SNAP: how each kind of earnings is treated (table), for that receipt's kind is equal to counted_less_costs;   - that receipt's irregular;   - if it is not the case that that receipt's regular date is unknown;     then the month containing that receipt's regular date is equal to the month;   otherwise (all of the following are true:;   - that receipt is received in the month;   - any of the following is true:;     - it is not the case that that receipt's month is unknown;     - all of the following are true:;       - any of the following is true:;         - that receipt's job start date is unknown;         - the month containing that receipt's job start date is at most the month;       - any of the following is true:;         - that receipt's job end date is unknown;         - the month containing that receipt's job end date is at least the month);   - it is not the case that (all of the following are true:;   - Is a destitute migrant or seasonal farmworker, otherwise no;   - the month is equal to the month containing SNAP: application date;   - that receipt's date is more than SNAP: application date))); otherwise 0)
