### CO-5115 SNAP: farm gross receipts `@engine`

The gross receipts of the person's farm that SNAP counts for the month: the earnings records whose row in snap_earnings_treatment_table is counted_loss_offset (farm_self_employment_receipts) received in the month (10 CCR 2506-1 4.403.12.E; 7 CFR 273.11(a)(2)), less those marked irregular when snap_irregular_earnings_are_excluded (4.405.A), and, in a destitute household's month of application, without the receipts dated after the date of application (4.406.1.A). Each less the part set aside under a Plan for Achieving Self-Support (4.405.2.A.22).

Precision. The farm's costs are snap_farm_costs (CO-5116); snap_self_employment_income (CO-1702) counts the farm's net and snap_farm_self_employment_loss (CO-3722) its loss. Earnings not stated: cannot determine. Coverage pass 4 for SNAP (docs/reviews/coverage4-snap.md, S4-1 to S4-4): a record is placed in the month of its regular_date when it states one, since pay or a benefit that came early or late because of a holiday, a weekend, a changed pay date, a mailing cycle or the employee's request is counted by its regular schedule (10 CCR 2506-1 4.402.B.1-3, S4720; 4.403.A.3, S4721), else in the month it came in; a stream (a record with no month and no date) recurs only from the month its job or source began through the month it ended (job_start_date and job_end_date; start_date and end_date on a receipt), since pay after a job ends or before it begins is not anticipated with reasonable certainty (4.402.1.B, S4722). Field sweep fix round (FS-SNAP-1): 10 CCR 2506-1 4.405.2.A.22 (S3110) excludes "Amounts necessary for the fulfillment of a Plan for Achieving Self-Support (PASS) under Title XVI of the Social Security Act", whatever income they come from; the part of a pay or a business's receipts set aside under a PASS (the earnings record's pass_set_aside, the month's amount set aside, not converted) is left out, as the receipts' set-aside is (snap_counted_recurring_receipts, CO-5011). Before, only the receipts' field was read and a set-aside of earnings was counted. Coverage pass 6 for SNAP, C6-4: a part of the receipts withheld by the payer to recover its earlier overpayment (the record's recouped) is left out (4.405.D.1, S3102), in the counted receipts and in the irregular receipts the quarter's limit excludes alike; sibling of snap_person_counted_wages (CO-5113).

### CO-5310 SNAP: real property not exempt `@engine`

The equity of the person's real property, of a former home that is no longer exempt, and of the mortgages and promissory notes the person holds, that SNAP does not exempt, in the month (7 CFR 273.8(c)(2), (e)(1), (e)(4)-(5); 10 CCR 2506-1 4.408.B, 4.408.1, 4.409.B-C, 4.410): every holdings record (holdings, CO-5300) valued in the month and held on the month's day whose row in snap_holding_treatment_table (CO-5301) is counted_less_real_property_exclusions (real_property), counted_with_real_property (loan_receivable), or excluded_while_home (home) when the person no longer lives in the home and is not away for a time for employment, training for future employment, illness, or because it is not habitable after a casualty or natural disaster with the intent to return (4.410.B: lives_in, temporary_absence), at its value less what is owed on it (4.409.B), times the person's share, or all of it where it is owned with someone outside the case or with a person of the case who is not a member of the person's SNAP household (4.409.C); leaving out a record the person cannot reach (accessible; 4.409.C, 4.410.F.1), and real property (or a former home) the person is making a good faith effort to sell (listed_for_sale; F.1), a lot on which a household with no home intends to build (lot_for_future_home; B), property producing income: property used in the person's own trade or business (used_in_trade_or_business; 273.8(e)(5)), or other income-producing property whose net return over the last twelve months is more than 0 and which the county has found produces an annual income consistent with its fair market value (net_annual_return, snap_return_consistent_with_value; E.1, 273.8(e)(4)), and property essential to farming within a year of the day the person stopped farming (farm_ended_date; E.4).

Precision. Coverage pass 4 for SNAP resources (docs/reviews/coverage4-snap-resources.md). Per month (SR-9): the resources of the month evaluated, valued on its day, the application filing date in the month of application (snap_application_date; 4.408.1, S4823: "The value of nonexempt household resources at the application filing date") and the first day of any other month (4.408.B: "as anticipated to be available in the issuance month"; the day is OQ-1310's): a record valued in the month (its month, or every month), and a holding disposed of (disposed_date) is held in a month whose day is before the disposal; the refund and credit windows are read against the same day. Before, one figure per case, on the determination date and the determination month's records, in every month, and a holding with any disposed_date in no month. SR-4: the home record (the dwelling the person owns and has lived in, lives_in saying whether the person lives there now) is exempt only while the person lives in it or it is temporarily unoccupied for one of 4.410.B's four reasons and the household intends to return (temporary_absence, a field of the record; intends_to_return is the long-term care test of other programs); a home left for good or for another reason is real property (273.8(e)(1), S4822 context; before, every home record was excluded). The home the person lives in reads nothing else. SR-5: 4.410.E.1 (S3477) exempts "Any property that is producing an annual income consistent with its fair market value", and 273.8(e)(5) (S4822) property "essential to the employment or self-employment of a household member" with no value test: income_producing property used in the person's trade or business is exempt; other income-producing property (a rental) is exempt only when its net return is more than 0 and the county has found it consistent with its value (the text sets no measure; the finding is SNAP's, decision D9; OQ-1308). A property that produced nothing is counted without reading the finding. Before, every income_producing record was exempt. SR-8: a co-owner of the case outside the person's SNAP household is a separate household (4.409.C): the co-owners' part is added. Decision 4: whether real property is for sale, a lot for a future home or producing income is required where read. A record with no farm_ended_date is not property essential to farming; the year is read against the month's day. A mortgage or note the person holds (loan_receivable) passes none of the real property exemptions (OQ-1202 resolved: 273.8(c)(1)-(2) count it). The $1,500 test is snap_countable_real_property's (CO-5311).

### CO-5311 SNAP: countable real property `@engine`

The person's real property SNAP counts in the month: each record snap_real_property_not_exempt (CO-5310) reads, at the person's part of it (the share, or all of it where owned with someone outside the case or with a person of the case outside the person's SNAP household, 4.409.C), unless the holding is an inaccessible resource because it would have a net return of snap_low_return_resource_maximum ($1,500) or less if sold (10 CCR 2506-1 4.410.F.2, its equity) or no significant return after the estimated costs of selling it (4.410.G, 7 CFR 273.8(e)(18): "after estimating costs of sale or disposition, and taking into account the ownership interest of the household"). The test is made on each holding at the household's interest, the whole holding: a part owned by another member of the household is the household's, and a part owned by a separate household is counted in its entirety (4.409.C). Neither test applies to a note the person holds that is a negotiable instrument (G; 273.8(e)(18)).

Precision. Coverage pass 4 for SNAP resources (docs/reviews/coverage4-snap-resources.md). Per month (SR-9): the resources of the month evaluated, valued on its day, the application filing date in the month of application (snap_application_date; 4.408.1, S4823: "The value of nonexempt household resources at the application filing date") and the first day of any other month (4.408.B: "as anticipated to be available in the issuance month"; the day is OQ-1310's): a record valued in the month (its month, or every month), and a holding disposed of (disposed_date) is held in a month whose day is before the disposal; the refund and credit windows are read against the same day. Before, one figure per case, on the determination date and the determination month's records, in every month, and a holding with any disposed_date in no month. SR-6: the test is made on each holding, not on the person's total, and at the household's interest: a record's whole equity (value less amount owed) and the costs of selling the whole holding (costs_of_sale, the same figure on each owner's record of a joint holding, as its value is). Two lots of $1,000 each return $1,000 each and are both inaccessible (before: $2,000 together, counted); a $2,400 lot owned half each by two members returns 2,400 - 100 = 2,300 for the household and is counted, $1,200 on each list (before: $1,200 on each list, each under $1,500, not counted). Because a holding owned by members only is the household's whole, and one owned with a separate household is counted in its entirety (4.409.C), the household's interest is the whole holding in every case the record can state (a holding owned by two members and a third person outside the household cannot be stated: co_owners names one kind of co-owner). The equity test reads only value and amount owed (1,500 or less: inaccessible, nothing else read); the exemptions of CO-5310 are read next; the costs of sale last (required where read: decision 4). OQ-1202 resolved for loan_receivable: 4.410.G "does not apply to negotiable financial instruments" (negotiable_instrument, a field of the record); a note that is not negotiable takes both tests. The integration review's sentence that CO-5311 tests each record's equity (docs/reviews/records-holdings-h1-integration.md, section 7) is corrected there.

### CO-5312 SNAP: countable funeral agreements `@engine`

The equity of the person's pre-purchased funeral agreements that SNAP counts in the month (7 CFR 273.8(e)(2); 10 CCR 2506-1 4.410.D.4): the equity (the paid-up amount, its value, times the person's share, or all of it where owned with someone outside the case) of the person's prepaid_burial_contract records (row counted_beyond_one_agreement_per_member) valued in the month and held on the month's day that the person can reach and that are not irrevocable (an irrevocable agreement is inaccessible, 4.410.F.1), less, for each member of the person's SNAP household (snap_household_members), the person's part of the one agreement excluded for that member (burial_for person_of_case, for_person naming the member): the value of one funeral agreement per household member is excluded, whatever its amount, once for the household: where the person alone holds one for the member, the largest of the person's; where other members hold one too, the one of the largest whole equity among the holders whose resources are counted (snap_funeral_agreement_excluded_for_member, CO-7201), the person's part of it divided among those tied (snap_funeral_agreement_tie_share_for_member, CO-7202).

Precision. Coverage pass 4 for SNAP resources (docs/reviews/coverage4-snap-resources.md). SR-1: (a) per member, not per holder: an agreement names the person it is for (burial_for, for_person, fields of the record), and one agreement per household member is excluded, so a parent who holds her own agreement and her child's has both excluded (FUN1); an agreement for someone who is not a member of the household (a relative elsewhere, a person of the case in another SNAP household) is counted; with two agreements for one member, the larger is excluded. Cross-list records round (docs/reviews/cross-list-records.md): the one funeral agreement per household member is chosen across the holders' lists, not on each holder's own: for a member for whom two or more members hold one (snap_funeral_agreement_holders_for_member, CO-7200), the one excluded is the one of the largest whole equity among the holders whose resources the household counts (snap_funeral_agreement_excluded_for_member, CO-7201; not an ineligible student, and not a member receiving SSI or public assistance, whose resources are excluded already, 7 CFR 273.8(e)(17)), and each holder of it excludes the part of it on its own list, divided among the agreements tied for the largest (snap_funeral_agreement_tie_share_for_member, CO-7202, at least 1), so the household excludes the value of one: two parents each holding a separate one for their child each exclude half of their own, and two holding one funeral agreement jointly each exclude their half whole. A holder who is the only one holding one for the member excludes its largest, as before, and no other member's facts are read for it. Before, each holder excluded its own largest for the member, so two members holding one each for the same third member had both excluded (CO-5312-T10: 0, by the text 1,500 for the household). The greatest over the holders is P59 (docs/operators.md); the holders' agreements for a member are read on the holders' lists with the member as this person (the reading of a record on another person's list that names the person evaluated). (b) The $1,500 cap: the statute override (273.8(e)(2) over 4.410.D.4; OQ-1305). SR-12: the equity of an agreement is its paid-up amount (the holding's value, by the record's meaning for a prepaid burial contract): what is still owed on an agreement paid in installments is not paid up and is not in the value, so it is not subtracted again (amount_owed is not read); an agreement owned with others is read at the person's share, or whole where owned with someone outside the case (4.409.C). SR-11: an agreement's irrevocable is read for every agreement the person can reach (one excluded or not), after whom it is for. A burial plot included in an agreement is stated as its own burial_space record (D.4: "the burial plot portion will be exempted prior to determining the equity value"; snap_countable_burial_spaces, CO-5313). Per month (SR-9): the resources of the month evaluated, valued on its day, the application filing date in the month of application (snap_application_date; 4.408.1, S4823: "The value of nonexempt household resources at the application filing date") and the first day of any other month (4.408.B: "as anticipated to be available in the issuance month"; the day is OQ-1310's): a record valued in the month (its month, or every month), and a holding disposed of (disposed_date) is held in a month whose day is before the disposal; the refund and credit windows are read against the same day. Before, one figure per case, on the determination date and the determination month's records, in every month, and a holding with any disposed_date in no month. No agreement held: 0, the household not read.

### CO-5313 SNAP: countable burial spaces `@engine`

The equity of the person's burial spaces that SNAP counts in the month (7 CFR 273.8(e)(2); 10 CCR 2506-1 4.410.D.1, F.2): the person's burial_space records (row counted_beyond_one_plot_per_member) valued in the month, held on the month's day and reachable, each at its equity times the person's share (all of it where owned with someone outside the case), leaving out a space whose value, or whose equity (value less what is owed on the whole space), is snap_low_return_resource_maximum ($1,500) or less (an inaccessible resource, F.2), less, for each member of the person's SNAP household (snap_household_members), the person's part of the one plot excluded for that member (burial_for person_of_case, for_person naming the member): one burial plot per household member is excluded, once for the household: where the person alone holds one for the member, the largest of the person's; where other members hold one too, the one of the largest whole equity among the holders whose resources are counted (snap_burial_space_excluded_for_member, CO-7204), the person's part of it divided among those tied (snap_burial_space_tie_share_for_member, CO-7205).

Precision. Coverage pass 4 for SNAP resources (docs/reviews/coverage4-snap-resources.md). SR-7: (a) the share: a space owned by two members is counted at each owner's share, so the household counts it once (before: at its whole equity on each list, twice); the $1,500 test reads the whole space's value and equity (the household's interest, as for real property, CO-5311). (b) A member's plot: the record names the person a space is for (burial_for, for_person), and the one plot excluded is a household member's, so a plot for a relative who is not a member (a parent in another state) is counted (OQ-1250 resolved by the text: "one burial plot per household member", 273.8(e)(2), 4.410.D.1); with two plots for one member the larger is excluded. for_immediate_family, the Adult Financial and SSI test, is not read. SR-11: a space of $1,500 or less is inaccessible without reading what is owed or whom it is for; one above it reads what is owed, then whom it is for. Per month (SR-9): the resources of the month evaluated, valued on its day, the application filing date in the month of application (snap_application_date; 4.408.1, S4823: "The value of nonexempt household resources at the application filing date") and the first day of any other month (4.408.B: "as anticipated to be available in the issuance month"; the day is OQ-1310's): a record valued in the month (its month, or every month), and a holding disposed of (disposed_date) is held in a month whose day is before the disposal; the refund and credit windows are read against the same day. Before, one figure per case, on the determination date and the determination month's records, in every month, and a holding with any disposed_date in no month. No space above $1,500 held: 0, the household not read. Cross-list records round (docs/reviews/cross-list-records.md): the one burial plot per household member is chosen across the holders' lists, not on each holder's own: for a member for whom two or more members hold one (snap_burial_space_holders_for_member, CO-7203), the one excluded is the one of the largest whole equity among the holders whose resources the household counts (snap_burial_space_excluded_for_member, CO-7204; not an ineligible student, and not a member receiving SSI or public assistance, whose resources are excluded already, 7 CFR 273.8(e)(17)), and each holder of it excludes the part of it on its own list, divided among the plots tied for the largest (snap_burial_space_tie_share_for_member, CO-7205, at least 1), so the household excludes the value of one: two parents each holding a separate one for their child each exclude half of their own, and two holding one burial plot jointly each exclude their half whole. A holder who is the only one holding one for the member excludes its largest, as before, and no other member's facts are read for it. Before, each holder excluded its own largest for the member, so two members holding one each for the same third member had both excluded (CO-5313-T10: 0, by the text 1,800 for the household). The greatest over the holders is P59 (docs/operators.md); the holders' plots for a member are read on the holders' lists with the member as this person (the reading of a record on another person's list that names the person evaluated).

### CO-5314 SNAP: value of the person's disqualifying transfers `@engine`

The uncompensated value of the resources this person transferred knowingly to qualify or attempt to qualify for SNAP within the three months immediately before the household's date of application (snap_application_date), or after it through the determination month (10 CCR 2506-1 4.408.2): the holdings records (holdings, CO-5300) with a disposed_date on or after the same day of the month three calendar months before the date of application and in the determination month or earlier, for which the county has established that the transfer was to qualify (snap_transfer_to_qualify), not returned in whole and not of a kind SNAP excludes.

Precision. The three months run back from the date of application to the same day of the month three calendar months earlier, that day included (a day the earlier month lacks runs into the next month: applied May 31, 2026, from March 3), as before step H1 (CO-4159); the day is OQ-1309's. A transfer after the date of application, through the determination month, is read as made after the household was determined eligible; one in a later month is not read. The county's finding (snap_transfer_to_qualify) not stated is read as no: 4.408.2.B applies "In the event the local office establishes that an applicant household knowingly transferred resources for the purpose of qualifying", so a transfer not established to be one does not disqualify (the rule's own reading, design decision D3; the person fact it replaces, CO-4155, was read the same way; a request to the integration owner to declare the default on the field). A transfer whose resource has been returned in whole (returned_date) is not read: the resource is again among the household's. Coverage pass 4 for SNAP resources SR-14: the transfers 4.408.2.A exempts (excluded property, a sale near fair market value, a transfer between members, one for another reason) are the county's finding (snap_transfer_to_qualify: "is not a transfer 10 CCR 2506-1 4.408.2.A exempts"), so no row of the table is read beside it (before, a holding of a row excluded outright was left out whatever the finding, a second, narrower statement of A.1). SR-11: the uncompensated value is the holding's value, less what was owed on it for a non-liquid holding (4.408.1.A values liquid resources at their redemption value and nothing is owed on cash or an account, so amount_owed is not read for a liquid kind), times the person's share, less what the person received for it (compensation_received), never below zero; 4.408.2.A.2 leaves a sale at or near fair market value unaffected, so a transfer that was fully compensated has no value to add. Field sweep defaults list (2026-11-23): snap_transfer_to_qualify is read as the holdings record states it, its default false declared once on the schema (CO-5300) with the rule that gives it (10 CCR 2506-1 4.408.2.B (S2962): disqualification "In the event the local office establishes that an applicant household knowingly transferred resources"); before, this reader gave the default itself (otherwise false), which conventions rule 12 and decision 4 do not allow a reader. No value changes.

```
the sum for each holding in Holdings where
    all of the following are true:

      - that holding's snap transfer to qualify
      - that holding's returned date is unknown
      - that holding's disposed date is at least the number of days from the first day of the month containing SNAP: application date to SNAP: application date days after the first day of 3 months before the month containing SNAP: application date
      - the month containing that holding's disposed date is at most the month containing the Determination Date
  of
    the greater of 0 and (((if that holding's kind is one of: cash, bank_account, securities, retirement_account, education_savings_account, able_account, business_cash_and_assets, held_income_tax_refund, held_eitc, held_retroactive_ssa_benefit, held_excluded_payment, held_loan_proceeds, held_replacement_proceeds, held_prorated_income;   then that holding's value; otherwise that holding's value minus that holding's amount owed) times (that holding's share, otherwise 1)) minus that holding's compensation received)
```

### CO-6000 SNAP: allotment before the minimum and the cap `@engine`

This person's SNAP household's allotment for a full month computed from its own size and income alone: the maximum allotment less the benefit reduction, rounded down to the nearest dollar (10 CCR 2506-1 4.207.3.A.3; 7 CFR 273.10(e)(2)(ii)(A)) and not below $0, before the one- and two-person minimum (4.207.3.C) and before the cap for members disqualified under 7 CFR 273.11(c)(1)(ii) (snap_allotment_cap_before_minimum, CO-6001).

Precision. Rounding down is written as the negated ceiling of the negated difference. Read by the full month (snap_full_month_allotment, CO-2307), which applies the minimum and the cap, and by the initial month's full-month figure (snap_full_month_allotment_before_minimum, CO-6002), which applies the cap only.

Type money, scope person-month, program SNAP.
Uses: `snap_benefit_reduction`, `snap_maximum_allotment`.

```
the greater of 0 and (0 minus (SNAP: benefit reduction minus SNAP: maximum allotment rounded up to the next whole dollar))
```

```json
["max",0,["-",0,["ceil",["-","snap_benefit_reduction","snap_maximum_allotment"]]]]
```

### CO-6001 SNAP: allotment cap for excluded disqualified members, before the minimum `@engine`

The allotment this person's SNAP household would receive for a full month with its members disqualified under 7 CFR 273.11(c)(1) counted in its size (snap_household_size_with_disqualified_members) and their income (snap_net_income_with_disqualified_members), before the one- and two-person minimum: the maximum allotment for that size less snap_benefit_reduction_rate of that net income, rounded down and not below zero (273.11(c)(1)(ii)); with no such member, the household's maximum allotment, which never binds.

### CO-6600 SNAP: leave or bonus pay received in installments after the job ended `@engine`

The person's sick pay, vacation pay and bonus pay received for the month in installments after the job it comes from ended, which 10 CCR 2506-1 4.404.F (S4723) counts as unearned income: "If vacation pay, sick pay, or bonus pay is received in installment payments after a person has terminated employment, it is considered unearned income." Each earnings record of a pay row of snap_earnings_treatment_table that is marked leave_or_bonus_pay, is dated after its job_end_date and is not paid once, at its monthly amount as snap_person_wages (CO-4324) converts a pay (4.402.A.2), placed in the month of its regular date. snap_person_unearned_income (CO-331) adds it, so the earned income deduction does not apply to it. Each less the part set aside under a Plan for Achieving Self-Support (4.405.2.A.22).

Precision. Coverage pass 4 for SNAP, S4-4. While the person is still employed, sick, vacation and bonus pay are earned income (4.403.A.4, S4721: "if the person was still employed while receiving the pay"), counted by snap_person_wages. Such pay received once after the job ended is a lump sum, "considered as a resource in the month received" (4.404.F): neither this item nor snap_person_wages counts it as income, and what is left of it is a holding (resources). A last paycheck for hours worked before the job ended is not leave or bonus pay (leave_or_bonus_pay false) and is wages in the month received. Earnings not stated: cannot determine; a stated empty list is 0. In a destitute household's month of application a record dated after the date of application is not counted (4.406.1.A, S2964; coverage pass 4 S4-14). Field sweep fix round (FS-SNAP-1): 10 CCR 2506-1 4.405.2.A.22 (S3110) excludes "Amounts necessary for the fulfillment of a Plan for Achieving Self-Support (PASS) under Title XVI of the Social Security Act", whatever income they come from; the part of a pay or a business's receipts set aside under a PASS (the earnings record's pass_set_aside, the month's amount set aside, not converted) is left out, as the receipts' set-aside is (snap_counted_recurring_receipts, CO-5011). Before, only the receipts' field was read and a set-aside of earnings was counted. Coverage pass 6 for SNAP, C6-4: a part of the leave pay withheld by the employer to repay an advance or an earlier overpayment (the record's recouped) is left out, as in snap_person_counted_wages (CO-5113; 4.403.A.3, 4.405.D.1, S3102).

### CO-6601 SNAP: foster care payments are counted `@engine`

A foster individual placed in this person's home (the foster_parent role toward a person who lives with this person) buys food and prepares meals with this person, so the household providing the foster care has asked that the individual be a member and the governmental foster care payments it receives are counted as unearned income (7 CFR 273.9(b)(2)(ii), S4725: "foster care payments for children or adults who are considered members of the household"; 273.1(c)(4), S3651: foster care individuals "may participate ... as members of the household providing the foster care services, only at the request of the household providing the foster care"). False when no foster individual placed with the person is such a member: a foster individual who is not is a boarder, and the payments are excluded (273.9(c)(15), S4725: "Governmental foster care payments received by households with foster care individuals who are considered to be boarders"; 10 CCR 2506-1 4.304.3.B.1, S3475: a foster child not included "will not have their income ... included").

Precision. Coverage pass 4 for SNAP, S4-6. Read only for a person who states a foster care payment (a receipt whose row in snap_receipt_treatment_table is counted_if_foster_individual_is_member) or a difficulty of care payment marked foster_care (snap_earnings_treatment_table: counted_unless_foster_care_boarder), so a person with no such payment is never asked for relationships. Membership is read from the buys_prepares_with role between the payee and the foster individual, the one edge by which a foster individual joins the foster household (snap_household_members, CO-305, never crosses a foster_parent edge); reading CO-305 itself would make a cycle (household, the separate elderly and disabled household's income test, gross income, this item). Living together is lives_with (CO-1925), read as true where no dwelling is stated (convention rule 17); a foster individual not declared in the case is not a member. A record does not say which foster individual a payment is for, so where one foster individual placed with the person is a member and another is not the payments are counted in full (OQ-1260). Relationships not stated: cannot determine. Three-pattern sweep D-1 (docs/reviews/pattern-sweep-snap-ce.md): lives_with (CO-1925) is read as stated, required where read: no text on file says that persons related on the application live together unless it says otherwise (7 CFR 273.1(a): a household is individuals who live together and customarily purchase and prepare meals together, S1), so a stated relationship is no longer read as living together where no dwelling_id is stated (decision 4; docs/conventions.md rule 17, as MAGI's readers since coverage pass 6, C6-10); a case with persons related across the edge states dwelling_id for each of them.

Type yes/no, scope person, program SNAP.
Uses: `lives_with`, `relationships`.

```
there is a person of whom this person is a foster_parent such that
  all of the following are true:
    - that person is in Lives with
    - this person is a buys_prepares_with of that person
```

```json
["exists_related",["foster_parent"],["all",["in_group",["P"],"lives_with"],["rel",["buys_prepares_with"],["P"]]]]
```

### CO-6603 SNAP: household has an elderly or disabled member in the month `@engine`

In the month evaluated, at least one member of this person's SNAP household (snap_household_members) is an elderly or disabled member under 7 CFR 271.2 and 7 U.S.C. 2012(j) (snap_is_elderly_or_disabled, read in the month).

Precision. Coverage pass 4 for SNAP (docs/reviews/coverage4-snap.md), S4-11: the income tests and deductions an elderly or disabled member changes (the gross income test, 4.401.A.1-3; the uncapped shelter deduction, 4.407.3.B; the net income with disqualified members) read the member's age in the month evaluated (4.402.1.A, S4734), so an application month before the month a member turns 60 is not budgeted as an elderly household, and the month he turns 60 is. Tests every member of the purchase-and-prepare unit, as snap_household_has_elderly_or_disabled_member (CO-314) did. CO-314 was retired by coverage pass 7, C7-8 (docs/reviews/coverage7-snap.md): once the heating and cooling allowance entitlement (CO-1243) read this item per month (coverage pass 6, C6-3), no item read it. Coverage pass 4 S4-11 (OQ-1263 resolved): the household (snap_household_members, CO-305) is now built for each month, and the resource test (CO-344) and the transfer disqualification (CO-4158) read this item.

Type yes/no, scope person-month, program SNAP.
Uses: `snap_household_members`, `snap_is_elderly_or_disabled`.

```
there is a person in SNAP: household members such that
  that person's SNAP: is elderly or disabled
```

### CO-6604 SNAP: hours worked for pay in the month `@engine`

The hours the person worked for pay, including self-employment, in the month as SNAP's work tests read them (the student's twenty hours, 10 CCR 2506-1 4.306.1.B; the work registration exemption, 4.310.3.E; the ABAWD work requirement, 4.311.B and its verification, 7 CFR 273.2(f)(1)(xiv)(A)): the hours stated (hours_worked, CO-022) when the person's earnings records state pay or business receipts in the month; 0 when they state none, since a person with no pay and no business receipts in the month worked no hours for pay in it.

Precision. Coverage pass 4 for SNAP (docs/reviews/coverage4-snap.md), S4-13, decision 4 of 2026-11-23 ("readers do not invent defaults"): before, every reader took unstated hours as 0 even when the person's own earnings records stated pay for the month, so a working student was an ineligible student (STU: CO-83's stepfather, a half-time student earning $1,500 with hours not stated, was out of the household, $362 in October) and an ABAWD with wages accrued a countable month, while the hours verification read the same fact with no default. No rule gives unstated hours a value, so where the records show pay or business receipts the hours are required and their absence is cannot determine, naming hours_worked. Where the records state no pay and no business receipts for the month (an empty list, or records of other months only) the hours worked for pay are 0 by the records' own statement, not by a default. The pay is snap_person_pay_received (CO-5119); the business receipts are the records whose row is counted_less_costs or counted_loss_offset, placed as the income items place them. Earnings not stated: cannot determine. One reading for every reader: snap_weekly_hours_worked (CO-402), snap_meets_student_employment_exemption (CO-407), snap_meets_abawd_work_requirement (CO-415) and snap_requires_verification_of_work_hours (CO-1386).

Type hours, scope person-month, program SNAP.
Uses: `earnings`, `hours_worked`, `snap_earnings_treatment_table`, `snap_person_pay_received`.

```
if all of the following are true:
    - SNAP: pay received in the month is equal to 0
    - (the sum of that receipt's amount for each receipt in Earnings where ((all of the following are true:;   - SNAP: how each kind of earnings is treated (table), for that receipt's kind is one of: counted_less_costs, counted_loss_offset;   - if it is not the case that that receipt's regular date is unknown;     then the month containing that receipt's regular date is equal to the month;   otherwise (all of the following are true:;   - that receipt is received in the month;   - any of the following is true:;     - it is not the case that that receipt's month is unknown;     - all of the following are true:;       - any of the following is true:;         - that receipt's job start date is unknown;         - the month containing that receipt's job start date is at most the month;       - any of the following is true:;         - that receipt's job end date is unknown;         - the month containing that receipt's job end date is at least the month)))) is equal to 0
  then Hours worked, otherwise 0
otherwise Hours worked
```

### CO-6606 SNAP: anticipated capital gains, monthly `@engine`

The capital gains of the person's self-employment that the household anticipates receiving in the twelve (snap_annual_averaging_months) months beginning with the month of the application, divided by twelve (10 CCR 2506-1 4.403.11.D, S4730: "any capital gains that the household anticipates receiving in the next twelve (12) months, beginning with the date the application is filed, are added, and divided by twelve (12)").

Precision. Coverage pass 4 for SNAP, S4-17: read by snap_self_employment_income (CO-1702) for self-employment that is averaged as the household's annual support (4.403.12), which adds it to the average of the past months' receipts less their capital gains (snap_self_employment_capital_gains, CO-6605). The twelve months are counted from the month of the application date, the month that contains the date the application is filed. A farm's receipts are averaged as stated, a capital gain included (the farm records state none apart). Earnings not stated: cannot determine.

### CO-6900 SNAP: countable non-liquid personal property and installment contracts `@engine`

The person's non-liquid personal property and installment contracts that SNAP counts in the month (7 CFR 273.8(c)(2); 10 CCR 2506-1 4.408.1.B, 4.410.E.2, F.2): every holdings record (holdings, CO-5300) valued in the month and held on the month's day whose row in snap_holding_treatment_table (CO-5301) is counted_at_equity (personal property held for its value or as an investment) or excluded_if_consistent_return (an installment contract for the sale of land or buildings) when the contract is not producing income consistent with its fair market value (a net return over the last twelve months of 0 or less, or one the county has not found consistent with its value: net_annual_return, snap_return_consistent_with_value; E.2, 273.8(e)(6)), at its equity (value less what is owed on it, 4.408.1.B) times the person's share, or all of it where owned with someone outside the case or with a person of the case outside the person's SNAP household (4.409.C); a holding whose equity is $1,500 or less is inaccessible (F.2) and the person cannot reach is left out (accessible).

Precision. Coverage pass 4 for SNAP resources (docs/reviews/coverage4-snap-resources.md). Per month (SR-9): the resources of the month evaluated, valued on its day, the application filing date in the month of application (snap_application_date; 4.408.1, S4823: "The value of nonexempt household resources at the application filing date") and the first day of any other month (4.408.B: "as anticipated to be available in the issuance month"; the day is OQ-1310's): a record valued in the month (its month, or every month), and a holding disposed of (disposed_date) is held in a month whose day is before the disposal; the refund and credit windows are read against the same day. Before, one figure per case, on the determination date and the determination month's records, in every month, and a holding with any disposed_date in no month. SR-3 (OQ-1202 resolved in part by the text): 273.8(c)(2) (S4820) includes "Nonliquid resources, personal property, ... and any other property, provided that these resources are not specifically excluded under paragraph (e)", and (e) excludes "only the following"; personal property held as an investment is not a household good or personal effect ((e)(2), 4.410.D.1), and 4.408.1.B (S4823) values "non-exempt non-liquid resources" other than real property "less verified encumbrances". Before, not counted. SR-5: an installment contract is exempt only while it produces income consistent with its fair market value (E.2, S3118); before, every contract was excluded. A contract that produced nothing is counted without reading the finding; one with a positive return needs the county's finding (decision 4; OQ-1308). The $1,500 test is F.2's, on the holding's whole equity (the household's interest, as for real property, CO-5311); G's costs of sale are not read for personal property (no field states them for it; F.2 alone decides the low-return test here). Trusts and annuities are not read (OQ-1307); a life estate is not read (OQ-1202).

### CO-7200 SNAP: the members who hold a funeral agreement for this person `@engine`

The members of this person's SNAP household (snap_household_members) on whose holdings list a funeral agreement is held in the month for this person (burial_for person_of_case, for_person naming this person) and read by snap_countable_funeral_agreements (CO-5312): the holders among whom 7 CFR 273.8(e)(2) (S2216: "the value of one funeral agreement per household member"; the statute override on snap_countable_funeral_agreements, CO-5312) and 10 CCR 2506-1 4.410.D.4 (S2967) is applied for this person.

Precision. Cross-list records round (docs/reviews/cross-list-records.md): one funeral agreement per household member is the household's, not each holder's, so the funeral agreement excluded for a member is chosen across the lists of every member who holds one for that member. The member is this person and the holder that person: a holder's funeral agreements for this person are read from that person's list ([of, [P], holdings]) and the record's for_person is compared with this person as the persons joined to this person by no edge ([reachable, [spouse], false], the person alone), the reading Adult Financial and Colorado Works use for a veterans benefit's dependent (CO-5017, CO-5651). A holder's list not stated: cannot determine (decision 4). Which holders' resources the household counts is read only where two or more hold one (snap_funeral_agreement_excluded_for_member). Read by snap_countable_funeral_agreements (CO-5312) only when the holder holds one for a member.

Type group of persons, scope person-month, program SNAP.
Uses: `holdings`, `relationships`, `snap_application_date`, `snap_holding_treatment_table`, `snap_household_members`.

```
all persons in SNAP: household members such that (the largest of that holding's value for each holding in that person's Holdings where ((all of the following are true:;   - all of the following are true:;     - all of the following are true:;       - that holding is valued in the month;       - any of the following is true:;         - that holding's disposed date is unknown;         - that holding's disposed date is more than (if the month is equal to the month containing SNAP: application date;   then SNAP: application date; otherwise the first day of the month);     - that holding's accessible;     - SNAP: how each kind of holding is treated (table), for that holding's kind is equal to counted_beyond_one_agreement_per_member;   - all of the following are true:;     - that holding's burial for is equal to person_of_case;     - that holding's for person is in the persons joined to this person by spouse, crossing an edge only where no;   - it is not the case that that holding's irrevocable))) is more than 0
```

### CO-7201 SNAP: the whole equity of the funeral agreement excluded for this person `@engine`

For a member of a SNAP household, the whole equity (its value (the paid-up amount)) of the largest funeral agreement held for this person in the month by a holder (snap_funeral_agreement_holders_for_member) whose resources the household counts: the one funeral agreement 7 CFR 273.8(e)(2) (S2216: "the value of one funeral agreement per household member"; the statute override on snap_countable_funeral_agreements, CO-5312) and 10 CCR 2506-1 4.410.D.4 (S2967) excludes for this person. A holder who is an ineligible student (not in snap_household_members_other_than_ineligible_students; 4.411.2.C) or who receives SSI or public assistance (Colorado Works cash, Old Age Pension, Aid to the Needy Disabled or Aid to the Blind; 7 CFR 273.8(e)(17)) is left out, since that member's resources are not the household's (snap_household_countable_resources, CO-343). 0 when no holder's counts.

Precision. Cross-list records round (docs/reviews/cross-list-records.md): one funeral agreement per household member is the household's, not each holder's, so the funeral agreement excluded for a member is chosen across the lists of every member who holds one for that member. The member is this person and the holder that person: a holder's funeral agreements for this person are read from that person's list ([of, [P], holdings]) and the record's for_person is compared with this person as the persons joined to this person by no edge ([reachable, [spouse], false], the person alone), the reading Adult Financial and Colorado Works use for a veterans benefit's dependent (CO-5017, CO-5651). The comparison is of whole equities, so a funeral agreement owned jointly by two members (on each list at its share, with one holding_id) is weighed once, at its whole equity, against one held by another member. With two of equal largest equity, which one is excluded does not change the household's total; snap_funeral_agreement_tie_share_for_member (CO-7202) shares the one exclusion among them. Whether a holder is an ineligible student or receives SSI or public assistance is read only here, where two or more members hold one for this person (a sole holder's is not asked for this). Not stated: cannot determine (decision 4).

### CO-7202 SNAP: how many funeral agreements tie for the one excluded for this person `@engine`

For a member of a SNAP household, the funeral agreements held for this person whose whole equity is the excluded one (snap_funeral_agreement_excluded_for_member), counted by the part of each the household counts: for each holder whose resources the household counts, the counted equity of the holder's funeral agreement of that whole equity for this person, divided by that whole equity (1 for one held alone, 0.5 for each half of one held by two members). snap_countable_funeral_agreements (CO-5312) divides the one exclusion among them by this number, at least 1.

Precision. Cross-list records round (docs/reviews/cross-list-records.md): one funeral agreement per household member is the household's, not each holder's, so the funeral agreement excluded for a member is chosen across the lists of every member who holds one for that member. The member is this person and the holder that person: a holder's funeral agreements for this person are read from that person's list ([of, [P], holdings]) and the record's for_person is compared with this person as the persons joined to this person by no edge ([reachable, [spouse], false], the person alone), the reading Adult Financial and Colorado Works use for a veterans benefit's dependent (CO-5017, CO-5651). Two members holding separate funeral agreements of equal largest equity for this person give 2, and each holder's figure excludes half of its own, so the household's total excludes the value of one; the two halves of one jointly owned funeral agreement give 1, each holder excluding its half whole; a funeral agreement owned with a member whose resources are left out (7 CFR 273.8(e)(17)) gives its counted part only, and the divisor is never below 1, so that holder excludes only its own part. Where every funeral agreement tied for the largest is owned partly by a member whose resources are left out and no fully counted one ties with them, the counted parts are added (two such halves exclude the value of one whole); no stored or generated household states such a case, and the operators cannot group a holding's records by holding_id to tell it apart.

```
  if any of the following is true:

  else if (the largest of that holding's value for each holding in that person's Holdings where ((all of the following are true:;   - all of the following are true:;     - all of the following are true:;       - that holding is valued in the month;       - any of the following is true:;         - that holding's disposed date is unknown;         - that holding's disposed date is more than (if the month is equal to the month containing SNAP: application date;   then SNAP: application date; otherwise the first day of the month);     - that holding's accessible;     - SNAP: how each kind of holding is treated (table), for that holding's kind is equal to counted_beyond_one_agreement_per_member;   - all of the following are true:;     - that holding's burial for is equal to person_of_case;     - that holding's for person is in the persons joined to this person by spouse, crossing an edge only where no;   - it is not the case that that holding's irrevocable))) is equal to SNAP: the whole equity of the funeral agreement excluded for this person
```

### CO-7205 SNAP: how many burial spaces tie for the one excluded for this person `@engine`

For a member of a SNAP household, the burial spaces held for this person whose whole equity is the excluded one (snap_burial_space_excluded_for_member), counted by the part of each the household counts: for each holder whose resources the household counts, the counted equity of the holder's burial space of that whole equity for this person, divided by that whole equity (1 for one held alone, 0.5 for each half of one held by two members). snap_countable_burial_spaces (CO-5313) divides the one exclusion among them by this number, at least 1.

Precision. Cross-list records round (docs/reviews/cross-list-records.md): one burial plot per household member is the household's, not each holder's, so the burial space excluded for a member is chosen across the lists of every member who holds one for that member. The member is this person and the holder that person: a holder's burial spaces for this person are read from that person's list ([of, [P], holdings]) and the record's for_person is compared with this person as the persons joined to this person by no edge ([reachable, [spouse], false], the person alone), the reading Adult Financial and Colorado Works use for a veterans benefit's dependent (CO-5017, CO-5651). Two members holding separate burial spaces of equal largest equity for this person give 2, and each holder's figure excludes half of its own, so the household's total excludes the value of one; the two halves of one jointly owned burial space give 1, each holder excluding its half whole; a burial space owned with a member whose resources are left out (7 CFR 273.8(e)(17)) gives its counted part only, and the divisor is never below 1, so that holder excludes only its own part. Where every burial space tied for the largest is owned partly by a member whose resources are left out and no fully counted one ties with them, the counted parts are added (two such halves exclude the value of one whole); no stored or generated household states such a case, and the operators cannot group a holding's records by holding_id to tell it apart.

### CO-7250 SNAP: share of a prorated member's income and expenses counted `@engine`

The fraction of a prorated member's income, and of the child support, shelter and dependent care expenses paid by or billed to that member, that is counted for the remaining household members: the income or expense is divided evenly among the members of this person's household other than ineligible students (snap_household_members_other_than_ineligible_students, CO-3714), the ineligible members included, and all but the ineligible members' shares are counted (7 CFR 273.11(c)(2)(ii)-(iii), S4970, applied to an ineligible non-citizen by (c)(3)(i), S4971; 10 CCR 2506-1 4.411.1.B.2.b-c, S46, S107). With n members and k of them members whose income is prorated (snap_is_ineligible_member_prorated, CO-2565), the fraction is (n - k) / n. Zero when this person has no such household.

Precision. Coverage pass 6 for SNAP, C6-1 (docs/reviews/coverage6-snap.md): each prorated member's share is left out of every prorated member's income and expenses, not only that member's own share. 273.11(c)(2)(ii) divides the income "evenly among the household members, including the ineligible members" and counts "All but the ineligible members' share"; (iii) does the same for the child support, shelter and dependent care expenses. Colorado's 4.411.1.B.2.b and c say "All but the disqualified member's share" for "the disqualified and/or sanctioned member(s)" and are read with the federal paragraph they carry out: with two prorated members, each one's income counts at (n - 2) / n. A member counted in full (snap_is_disqualified_member_counted_in_full, CO-2302) is not one of the k: 273.11(c)(1) counts that member's income in its entirety. Unknown when any member's prorated status is unknown. Read for the person whose income or expense is prorated, as their own household's figure.

Type rate, scope person-month, program SNAP.
Uses: `snap_household_members_other_than_ineligible_students`, `snap_is_ineligible_member_prorated`.

```
if (the number of persons in SNAP: household members other than ineligible students) is equal to 0
  then 0
otherwise ((the number of persons in SNAP: household members other than ineligible students) minus (the number of persons in all persons in SNAP: household members other than ineligible students such that that person's SNAP: is an ineligible member whose income is prorated)) divided by (the number of persons in SNAP: household members other than ineligible students)
```

### CO-7672 SNAP: persons living with the person in the month `@engine`

The persons of the case who live with this person in the month, for SNAP's household of the month (7 CFR 273.1(a), S1: a household is individuals who "live together"; 273.10(a)(1)(i), S5091: the application month is determined on "the household's circumstances for the entire month of application"; 10 CCR 2506-1 4.402.1.A, S4734: each issuance month on its own circumstances): in the determination month and after, the persons who live in this person's home on the determination date (lives_with, CO-1925); in a month before the determination month, those of them who already lived there in the month (neither of the two moved in after it, moved_into_home_date CO-7671), and a person joined to this person by a household edge (spouse or person held out as a spouse, parent, stepparent, child, stepchild, a person the two buy and prepare meals with, a child in this person's care or guardianship, or the caretaker or guardian) who lives elsewhere on the determination date but lived with this person on the month's first day. In any month, a person who lives elsewhere on the determination date and whose separation the case dates lives with this person in a month that began before the date the two ceased to live together. Two persons who have lived apart throughout the months evaluated (has_lived_apart_throughout_months_evaluated, CO-7860, true on either, or persons_lived_apart_from_throughout_months_evaluated, CO-7891, on either naming the other) live apart in every month.

Precision. Coverage pass 7 for SNAP, C7-1 (docs/reviews/coverage7-snap.md). The date the two ceased to live together is, for spouses or persons held out as spouses, ceased_living_with_spouse_date (CO-7352); for a parent, stepparent, child or stepchild, ceased_living_with_parent_or_child_date (CO-7506); for any other two persons, ceased_living_with_housemate_date (CO-7670); each stated on either of the two, and where one of them lives in a facility (residence_setting_type other than private_dwelling) and no date is stated, that one's institution_entry_date, as the SSI method reads the same dates (ma_ssi_lives_with_in_month, CO-7505). The day is OQ-1405's: a change that takes a person out counts only for a month on every day of which it holds, so the two live together in a month whose first day is before the date they ceased to (a husband who moved out on November 2 is a member of November); a change that brings a person in counts for the month if it holds on any day of it, so a person who moved in during a month lives in the home that month. The dates are required where read (decision 4): in a month before the determination month, two persons joined by a household edge who live apart on the determination date and state no separation date cannot be determined. In the determination month and after, the homes of the determination date are read, and a stated separation date dates a separation made during the determination month (OQ-1405's day); with none stated, the two live apart in the determination month, the determination month being read on the determination date as every status SNAP reads for it (OQ-1450). A person who moved in states moved_into_home_date; one who does not state it lived in the home before the first month evaluated (CO-7671's meaning). Persons of the case not joined by a household edge who live apart on the determination date are not asked for a date: SNAP's household is reached only along those edges (snap_household_members, CO-305). Death and institution status are read by CO-305 and snap_is_household_member (CO-304), not here. Coverage verification 7 (docs/reviews/verify-coverage7-fixes.md): V7-1, a pair who never lived together, or who parted before the first month evaluated, has no separation date to state; has_lived_apart_throughout_months_evaluated (CO-7860), true on either of the two, places them apart in a month before the determination month without a date (S1-M: a daughter's father who has never lived with her, October {p1, p3}, $217, was cannot determine). V7-5, one move of a stepparent is read from either date: for a stepparent and stepchild with no parent-or-child date stated, the date the stepparent ceased to live with his spouse (ceased_living_with_spouse_date, stated on the stepparent or on a spouse of the stepparent); for spouses with no spouse date stated, the parent-or-child date of the one who is a stepparent (S1-B: the husband's move stated only as his spouse date, October $280, was cannot determine). A stepparent who left the spouse's home left the spouse's children who lived there with it; a stepchild who lives elsewhere from the stepparent's spouse states the parent-or-child date. Close-out verification F3 (KL-SNAP-5, docs/reviews/known-limits.md; 2026-11-24): CO-7860 says the person lived apart from every person of the case in another home, so a pair who never lived together, one of whom lived in an evaluated month with someone else who has since moved, could not be placed (probe G4: October cannot determine where 273.10(a)(1)(i) gives $217). The pair is read from persons_lived_apart_from_throughout_months_evaluated (CO-7891) too: the other person named in this person's list, or this person named in the other's (the group of this person alone is written as the persons joined to this person by spouse, crossing no edge), places the two apart in every month without a date; a separation from anyone else is dated as before.

### CO-7892 SNAP: household members before an elderly and disabled separate household `@engine`

The persons who would make up this person's SNAP household in the month (snap_household_members, CO-305) if no member were granted separate household status as a person sixty or older unable to purchase and prepare meals because of a disability (7 CFR 273.1(b)(2), S1604; 10 CCR 2506-1 4.304.3.A, S1605): everyone reachable from this person by a chain of the edges CO-305 crosses (spouse, mandatory parent and child, mandatory caretaker and dependent, and a purchase-and-prepare edge not into or out of a roomer or live-in attendant), each pair living together in the month (snap_lives_with_in_month, CO-7672), less a person who is not a household member (an institution resident, a boarder, one receiving SNAP in another household), one who died before the month or one not yet born. A purchase-and-prepare edge is crossed whatever the separate household test gives. It contains every member of CO-305's household; a person outside it is in no SNAP household with this person in the month (7 CFR 273.1(a): one who lives elsewhere, or who lives in the home but buys and prepares food apart and is no mandatory member).

Precision. Close-out verification F2 (KL-SNAP-4, docs/reviews/known-limits.md; 2026-11-24). SNAP's counted receipts (snap_counted_recurring_receipts, CO-5011) take off the part of a payment intended for a beneficiary who is not a household member (10 CCR 2506-1 4.405.B, S3100) and so need the household's membership; CO-305 reads income through the elderly and disabled separate household test (snap_is_in_elderly_disabled_separate_household CO-2304, snap_meets_elderly_disabled_separate_household_election CO-419: the 165 percent test of the others' income, 7 CFR 273.1(b)(2), S20, which reads each other's snap_person_gross_income_before_sponsor_income, CO-3712, and so CO-5011), so CO-5011 cannot read CO-305 without a dependency cycle. This group is CO-305's derivation with the separate household test left out: everything else CO-305 reads (the homes of the month, the edges, the mandatory ages, institution, boarder, death and birth) reads no income. A person outside this group is outside CO-305's household whatever the test gives (CO-305 crosses only the edges this group crosses, and fewer), so CO-5011 takes the part off for that person with no cycle. A person inside it whom only a separate household would take out of CO-305's household (a dependent of sixty or older with a disability who buys and prepares with the household and asks to be a separate household) is not told apart here: the test reads the others' income, which is this payment's own question (OQ-1510). Registered as CO-305's sibling: a change to the edges or the membership tests of one is a change to the other.

Type group of persons, scope person-month, program SNAP.
Uses: `date_of_birth`, `date_of_death`, `relationships`, `snap_is_household_member`, `snap_is_roomer_or_live_in_attendant`, `snap_is_under_parental_control_of_household_member`, `snap_lives_with_in_month`, `snap_mandatory_child_age`, `snap_parental_control_age`.

### CO-087 Mother was enrolled in Medicaid at birth `@engine`

Whether the person's mother was eligible for and receiving Medical Assistance at the time of the person's birth (including through retroactive Medical Assistance covering the birth), the condition 10 CCR 2505-10 8.100.4.G.7 and 42 CFR 435.117(b)(1) make an "Eligible Needy Newborn", and on which the citizenship documentation exemption for a deemed newborn rests at any age.

Precision. Read from the birth mother's enrollment in the birth month (birth_mother_coverage_at_birth, CO-3322); the child need not live with the mother, per 8.100.4.G.7's third sentence, so no co-residence is read. Where the enrollment record does not show Medical Assistance in the birth month and the birth mother is a person of the case, her Pregnant Women coverage period as this case determines it (ma_is_in_pregnancy_coverage_period, CO-566) is read for the birth month, so a birth covered by the mother's retroactive coverage under the same application makes the child a needy newborn (8.100.4.G.7: 'This coverage also applies in instances where the mother received Medical Assistance to cover the child's birth through retroactive Medical Assistance').

### CO-1150 Medicaid: meets every requirement other than citizenship or immigration status `@engine`

Whether the person is a Colorado resident who meets the criteria of one of the categorical Medical Assistance programs apart from citizenship and immigration status - not excluded as a patient in an institution for mental diseases (§ 8.100.3.G.1.c), and a MAGI category (whose income test is part of the category), the SSI-related aged, blind or disabled income and resource standards, OAP SISC B (an aged, blind or disabled OAP recipient within the SSI resource standard, § 8.100.6.K.4), or institutional long-term care financial eligibility with the nursing facility level of care - the "otherwise meets the eligibility requirements" condition of 42 U.S.C. 1396b(v)(2)(B), 42 CFR 440.255(c)(2) and 10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.3.F.1.k.

Precision. The routes are the categorical programs this volume derives without reading citizenship: ma_magi_category (CO-551), the SSI-related financial tests (CO-603, CO-609, CO-610; ma_is_ssi_related_eligible itself reads citizenship and so cannot be used), OAP SISC B without its status term (OAP receipt, adult_financial_program_received, CO-2710, with CO-603 and CO-610; ma_oap_sisc_b_eligible, CO-1177, reads status), and the institutional long-term care tests (CO-640, CO-651). The non-MAGI routes require the person to be aged, blind or disabled, as §§ 8.100.3.F.1.b-d and f-g state, so a person who is not is settled without the long-term care facts. The Buy-In programs, HCBS waivers and PACE are not routes: their own items read status (CO-618, CO-620 through CO-1174; CO-653 and CO-654), and an HCBS or PACE applicant who fails status is emergency-eligible here only through the SSI-related or OAP route (OQ-200). 1396b(v)(2)(B) excludes the requirement of receiving SSI or a State supplementary payment, which the SSI-related route does not test.

### CO-1151 Medicaid: emergency Medicaid status `@engine`

The emergency Medicaid determination for the month. A Colorado resident who meets the citizenship and immigration status requirement (CO-509), or a child, pregnant or postpartum person who is fully covered under Cover All Coloradans in a category § 8.100.3.G.1.g.ix.1.a-b lists (CO-1175) or eligible for CHP+ under 10 CCR 2505-3 § 110.1.B.5.o, is not limited to emergency coverage (not_applicable_status_met). A resident who fails status but meets every other requirement of a categorical program is limited to emergency (and reproductive) services (10 CCR 2505-10 §§ 8.100.3.F.1.k, 8.100.3.G.1.g.ix.2; 42 U.S.C. 1396b(v); 42 CFR 435.406(b), 435.350, 440.255(c)); the coverage pays for this month's care when the person has an emergency medical condition (eligible_emergency_condition) and otherwise stands without a covered service (eligible_no_current_emergency). ineligible_residency and ineligible_other_requirements report the failing condition.

Precision. Residency first, then status, then the other requirements (ma_is_emergency_medicaid_only, CO-510, which reads ma_meets_requirements_other_than_status, CO-1150), then the month's emergency medical condition. Colorado's emergency eligibility does not wait for an emergency: the application is complete without a physician statement and an approved member is not asked to reapply for 12 months (§ 8.100.3.G.1.g.ix.2), so eligible_no_current_emergency is an eligible member with nothing to pay for this month, not a denial. Prenatal care and follow-up care are outside emergency-only coverage (§ 8.100.3.G.1.g.ix.2); a pregnant person regardless of status is instead covered through MAGI Pregnant or CHP+ prenatal under Cover All Coloradans (§ 8.100.3.G.1.g.ix.1; 10 CCR 2505-3 § 110.1.B.5.o), so reaches not_applicable_status_met here when either covers her. A lawfully present adult who is not pregnant (Temporary Protected Status, for example) no longer meets status (B-1), so is emergency-only when otherwise eligible; a child, pregnant or postpartum person meets status here only when covered in a listed category or by CHP+, so an undocumented postpartum adult whose only category is Adult is emergency-only (S-2); and long-term care now tests status (B-3), so an undocumented nursing facility resident is ineligible_status there and emergency-eligible here, not both eligible. The fetched 10 CCR 2505-3 states no separate unborn-child (from-conception) CHIP category. HCPF review note N-1: eligible_emergency_condition pays for the treatment of the emergency medical condition (42 U.S.C. 1396b(v)(2)-(3)), not for ongoing nursing facility care, which is not an emergency service.

Type one of, scope person-month, program Medicaid.
Uses: `chp_eligibility_status`, `has_emergency_medical_condition`, `ma_is_cover_all_coloradans_person_in_month`, `ma_is_covered_under_cover_all_coloradans`, `ma_is_emergency_medicaid_only`, `ma_meets_citizenship_requirement_in_month`, `ma_meets_residency_in_month`.

```
if it is not the case that Medicaid: meets the residency requirement in the month
  then ineligible_residency
else if any of the following is true:
    - Medicaid: meets the citizenship requirement in the month
    - Medicaid: is covered under Cover All Coloradans
    - all of the following are true:
      - Medicaid: in the Cover All Coloradans population in the month
      - CHP+: eligibility status is one of: eligible_child, eligible_prenatal
  then not_applicable_status_met
else if it is not the case that Medicaid: is emergency Medicaid only
  then ineligible_other_requirements
else if Has an emergency medical condition
  then eligible_emergency_condition
otherwise eligible_no_current_emergency
```

Whether the person is eligible for the Breast and Cervical Cancer Program (10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.715.2; 42 U.S.C. 1396a(a)(10)(A)(ii)(XVIII) and (aa)) - a woman under 65, screened by a Colorado Women's Cancer Control Initiative Qualified Entity and found In Need of Treatment, a Colorado resident, a citizen or qualifying non-citizen (or a person within the Cover All Coloradans exception), without creditable coverage, and not eligible under another Medicaid program - and, if not, the first failing condition.

Precision. Status reads ma_meets_status_for_cover_all_coloradans_categories (CO-1174): the citizen and qualified non-citizen categories § 8.715.2.C.3 names (ma_meets_citizenship_requirement, CO-509, which also covers § 8.100.3.G.1.g.v's Cuban/Haitian entrants and COFA migrants that C.3's '(ii)-(iv)' skips) and the exception C.3 cross-references as '8.100.3(G)(1)(g)(viii)', read as the Cover All Coloradans exception now numbered ix (OQ-202). Creditable coverage reads the BCCP-specific facts ma_bccp_has_creditable_coverage (CO-1191: C.R.S. 10-16-102(16) less § 8.715.3.B's exclusions, with § 8.715.3.D) and ma_bccp_creditable_coverage_exception_applies (CO-1192: § 8.715.3.C), in place of the CHP+ coverage fact (OQ-203). The one-year eligibility period and treatment-start timing of §§ 8.715.2.F and 8.715.5 are not modeled; the status is evaluated for the month. Time audit T-1 (2026-11-23): "has not yet attained the age of 65" reads ma_age_on_first_day_of_month (CO-4978): under 65 on some day of the month; that the whole month counts for this group is OQ-950's assumption; it read age (CO-300), the age on the determination date, in every month.

### CO-1154 Medicaid: family planning and reproductive health care status `@engine`

Which route, if any, gives the person family planning services this month. A person eligible for a Medicaid category that provides full coverage (ma_has_full_coverage_category, CO-1176) or for the Breast and Cervical Cancer Program (whose clients receive all State Plan benefits, § 8.715.7.A) gets family planning services as a Medicaid client (10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.730.2.A), as does a child under ma_magi_child_age_limit eligible for state medical assistance (C.R.S. 25.5-2-104(2)) - full_coverage. A resident who meets the citizenship and immigration status requirement, is not fully covered, and whose family planning household income is within 260% FPL (ma_family_planning_income_in_band, CO-1155, which follows the approved state plan's S59 and tests no floor; coverage review 3, C3-01) qualifies for Limited Family Planning Medical Assistance (§ 8.100.4.G.8) - limited_family_planning. A resident with reproductive capacity who would be eligible for Medical Assistance but for immigration status qualifies for the state-only reproductive health-care program (C.R.S. 25.5-2-103; § 8.100.3.G.1.g.ix.2's reproductive care regardless of status) - reproductive_health_care_program. A month the application being determined cannot cover (ma_month_is_before_coverage_period, CO-4101: before the month of birth, or before the month of application and outside a requested retroactive period, 10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.3.E.1-2) is ineligible_before_coverage_period (KL-MAGI-3). A month after the month of the person's death (date_of_death) is ineligible_deceased (coverage pass 7, C7-06).

Precision. MAGI close-out, KL-MAGI-3 (2026-11-24): a month the application cannot cover is ineligible_before_coverage_period, tested first, as ma_magi_eligibility_status (CO-554) and chp_eligibility_status (CO-707) test it. Limited Family Planning is a category of Medical Assistance for 'Applicants applying for Medical Assistance' (§ 8.100.4.G.8, S613), so its months are those of the application: 'An applicant for Medical Assistance shall be provided such assistance any time during the three months preceding the date of application' (§ 8.100.3.E.1, S1503), on a request made on the application or after it (§ 8.100.3.E.2, S2411). Full coverage is Medical Assistance under a category, bound by the same paragraphs; and the reproductive health-care program is for an individual who 'would be eligible to enroll in the medical assistance program' but for immigration status (C.R.S. 25.5-2-103(1)(b), S615), which no one is in a month the application cannot cover. The months are ma_month_is_before_coverage_period (CO-4101), the reading coverage pass 7 (C7-01) gave the MAGI and CHP+ outcomes: a month before the month of birth, or before the month of application and outside the requested retroactive window (before the widest window the application date allows; between the widest and the narrowest decided by the window's length, unknown where that is not known); with no application date stated, a month before the determination month cannot be determined. Before, such a month was answered by the person's category and income as if covered (CO-1130, DIED-RETRO: applied 2026-09-15 with a request, the window June to August 2026: May 2026 full_coverage; it is ineligible_before_coverage_period). Coverage pass 7, C7-06 (2026-11-24): a month after the month of the person's death is ineligible_deceased, tested after the months the application cannot cover. An application may be made for a person who has died (42 CFR 435.915(a)(2), S218: 'regardless of whether the individual is alive when application for Medicaid is made'; 42 U.S.C. 1396a(a)(34) as amended, S1706: 'application was made on the individual's behalf in the case of a deceased individual'), and it covers the months in which the person would have been eligible 'at the time he received the services' (S218); the month of death is such a month, since a person eligible at any time during a calendar month is eligible for the entire month (10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.4.G.1, S3351). No month after it is: the rule ends even the periods that continue regardless of other changes when 'The member is deceased' or the 'Child is deceased', effective in the earliest possible month (§ 8.100.4.G.6.a.i, S3755; § 8.100.3.Q.1.b.i, S1502; 10 CCR 2505-3 § 430.2.B.i, S1714), and no category covers a person after death. The death is read from date_of_death (CO-2868, 'Not stated for a living person'), through is_deceased (CO-2200) for the month before. Before, such a month was answered by the person's facts as if alive (DIED-RETRO: died 2026-08-20, application 2026-09-15 with a request, $1,000: September to December eligible). Order: residency; full coverage; for a person meeting status (CO-509), the income band (otherwise ineligible_income); for a person failing status, reproductive capacity and eligibility but for status (otherwise ineligible). Limited family planning is not among the categories Cover All Coloradans reaches (§ 8.100.3.G.1.g.ix.1.a-b) and § 8.100.4.G.8 requires 'immigration or citizenship status', so the status test is CO-509 alone and an undocumented pregnant woman who is not fully covered reaches the reproductive health-care program (OQ-214). 'Would be eligible to enroll in the medical assistance program... but is not eligible due solely to the individual's immigration status' (25.5-2-103(1)(b)) is read as meeting a categorical program other than status (ma_is_emergency_medicaid_only, CO-510) or the Limited Family Planning income band (OQ-205). A child under ma_magi_child_age_limit who fails status and meets either is eligible for state medical assistance (C.R.S. 25.5-2-104(2)), which includes all Medical Assistance benefits, and so is reported full_coverage, not the reproductive health-care program, which 25.5-2-103(1)(b) closes to a person eligible for state medical assistance; a child who has declined state medical assistance (ma_has_declined_state_medical_assistance, CO-2207; OQ-205, resolved) is not reported full_coverage, and reaches the reproductive health-care program when the child has reproductive capacity. Limited family planning is read by the letter of § 8.100.4.G.8 ('no age or gender restriction'), although § 8.730.1 defines family planning services as services to individuals of child-bearing age (OQ-215). Full coverage reads the shared union CO-1176, which adds the protected groups and OAP SISC B, and BCCP is added here. A child in a continuous eligibility period that began in Limited Family Planning (§ 8.100.3.Q.2.g) keeps limited_family_planning for the period whatever the month's income. No age or gender restriction, deliberately (OQ-215, resolved): § 8.100.4.G.8 says the limited family planning category "has no age or gender restriction" (S613), and the federal group it implements is defined by income and not being pregnant alone (42 U.S.C. 1396a(ii)(1), S2114). § 8.730.1's "individuals of child-bearing age" (S677) and § 8.730.2.A (S616) define family planning services, the benefit, as 42 U.S.C. 1396d(a)(4)(C) does (S2114); they do not narrow who is eligible for the category. So an 81-year-old man or a six-year-old in the income band is reported limited_family_planning: that is the rule's eligibility answer, not a bug; which family planning services such a person can use is a benefit question this volume does not model. The reproductive health-care program route reads has_reproductive_capacity because C.R.S. 25.5-2-103 conditions that program on it. Coverage review 2, N-02 sweep: the child arm reads ma_is_under_child_age_or_turns_nineteen_this_month (CO-564), the Cover All Coloradans age condition (§ 8.100.3.G.1.g.ix.1: 'whose 19th birthday occurred in the current month'). Coverage pass 5, C5-04 (2026-11-23): Limited Family Planning (§ 8.100.4.G.8) is Medical Assistance, so § 8.100.3.G.1.c (S659) conditions it as it does every category: a patient of 21 to 64 in an institution for mental diseases (ma_meets_imd_requirement false, CO-1179) who is not fully covered is ineligible_institution, not limited_family_planning; and since such a person would not be eligible for Medical Assistance whatever the status, the reproductive health-care program's "would be eligible ... but for immigration status" does not reach them. Tested after full coverage and the continuous eligibility row (a child under 21 is never excluded). OQ-1325 (the SUD demonstration) applies here too. Pattern sweep, MAGI (2026-11-24, PS-01, PS-02): status and the Cover All Coloradans population are read for the month evaluated (ma_meets_citizenship_requirement_in_month, CO-7551; ma_is_cover_all_coloradans_person_in_month, CO-7552; ma_meets_status_for_cover_all_coloradans_categories_in_month, CO-7553), not on the determination date: 8.100.4.G.1 (S3351), 8.100.3.E.1 (S217), 8 U.S.C. 1613(a) (S176), ix.1's 'current month' (S607).
