### CO-1156 Medicaid: Old Age Pension Health Care Program status `@engine`

Whether an Old Age Pension recipient gets medical care through the state-only Old Age Pension Health Care Program (SISC C). The program serves persons receiving OAP-A or OAP-B who do not qualify for Medicaid (10 CCR 2505-10 §§ 8.941.1, 8.941.1.A, 8.941.3; § 8.100.3.F.1.j; § 8.100.6.K.7) and who are not patients in an institution for tuberculosis or behavioral or mental health disorders (C.R.S. 25.5-2-101(2)). An OAP recipient who receives SSI or meets SSI eligibility criteria, even except for income, is Medicaid-eligible instead (SISC B, § 8.100.6.K.2-4).

Precision. OAP receipt reads the Adult Financial case record adult_financial_program_received (CO-2710) as oap (9 CCR 2503-5 now states a single OAP category; OAP-A/OAP-B survive only as the Medicaid labels of 8.100.6.K.1, OQ-111); AND-CS, AND-SO and AB recipients are not OAP recipients (§ 8.941.3.B). 'Meets SSI eligibility criteria except for the level of their income' (§ 8.100.6.K.4) is ma_oap_sisc_b_eligible (CO-1177): residency, Medicaid's citizenship and immigration requirement (CO-509), aged, blind or disabled (CO-603) and within the SSI resource standard (CO-610) - OAP itself has no five-year bar (9 CCR 2503-5 3.520.67.E, af_meets_citizenship_requirement_oap, CO-929), so a qualified non-citizen inside the bar can receive OAP but not SSI-related Medicaid, which is the population SISC C serves; full MAGI eligibility (CO-562) also counts as qualifying for Medicaid. OAP-C (court-committed) recipients are excluded by § 8.941.3.B; receipt of OAP-C is the oap_c option of the same record (receives_oap_c, CO-2208) and such a recipient who does not qualify for Medicaid is reported ineligible_oap_c (OQ-206, resolved). Eligibility is not retroactive (§ 8.941.1.E, 'shall begin on the date of application or date eligibility is established, whichever is later'): a month before the month of the application (ma_application_date) is ineligible_before_application, while a Medicaid-eligible recipient keeps medicaid_eligible there, since Medical Assistance has retroactive months; a month in which the person did not receive OAP is not_oap_recipient. § 8.100.6.K.7's OAP-A, OAP-B and OAP Refugee recipients who lost OAP to a cost of living adjustment other than OASDI remain in SISC C: ma_lost_oap_to_non_oasdi_cost_of_living_adjustment (CO-2209) brings them in as if they still received OAP (OQ-206, resolved); a current OAP Refugee recipient is an OAP recipient in adult_financial_program_received. The institutional exclusion reads ma_oap_is_patient_in_tb_or_mental_health_institution (CO-1748). "Do not qualify for Medicaid under Title XIX" (§ 8.941.1) and "do not otherwise qualify for the Colorado Medicaid Program" (§ 8.941.3.A) are read as ma_has_full_coverage_category (CO-1176), which adds the protected groups (Pickle, disabled widow(er)s, DAC), the Buy-In programs, long-term care and the needy-under-21 group to SSI-related, MAGI and SISC B eligibility (final verification pass 3, pattern sweep after F3-2: the item had named four categories). Coverage pass 6, non-MAGI F6-5 (docs/reviews/coverage6-medicaid-nonmagi.md): the SSI branch reads ma_receives_ssi_in_month (CO-7351), SSI from the month of the original SSI eligibility date (10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.6.C.1.a, C.7, S5030), so a retroactive month before an SSI award is judged by the SSI-related tests of that month; before, receives_ssi (the award as of the determination date) made every month an SSI month.

### CO-1159 Medicaid: is Pickle eligible `@engine`

Whether the person is eligible under the Pickle Amendment (10 CCR 2505-10 §§ 8.100.3.F.1.e, 8.100.6.D-E) - an aged, blind or disabled Colorado resident meeting status who lost SSI or OAP because of OASDI benefits, or who lost SSI, a State supplement or OAP for any reason after April 1977 while receiving it with OASDI (42 CFR 435.135(a)), whose countable income after the Pickle disregard is less than the current SSI or OAP standard and who meets the SSI resource standard.

Precision. 'Less than the current SSI or OAP standard' (§ 8.100.6.E.2) is read as less than either: the SSI federal benefit rate for the SSI household size, or, for a person of Old Age Pension age (af_is_oap_age, CO-940: 60 or older), the OAP grant standard (af_oap_grant_standard, CO-289) where it is higher - the OAP standard can only be met by a person who could receive OAP, which § 8.100.6.D.2.c's 'would be eligible for OAP and/or SSI' requires. Strictly less than. 'Meets all other eligibility criteria' is read as residency, status, aged/blind/disabled and the SSI resource standard. § 8.100.6.E.3's disregard of a parent's or spouse's OASDI cost of living increases is not applied (OQ-207). A child in a continuous eligibility period that began in Pickle (§ 8.100.3.Q.2.e) stays eligible for the period. Coverage pass 6, non-MAGI F6-6 (docs/reviews/coverage6-medicaid-nonmagi.md): where no income of an ineligible spouse is deemed (ma_ssi_ineligible_spouse_income_is_not_deemed, CO-7353; 20 CFR 416.1163(d)(1), S5031: 'we subtract only your own countable income from the Federal benefit rate for an individual'), the person's own Pickle income (ma_pickle_own_countable_income, CO-7356) is compared with the individual rate. Coverage pass 6, non-MAGI F6-8 (docs/reviews/coverage6-medicaid-nonmagi.md): the loss is a loss caused by OASDI (lost_ssi_or_oap_due_to_social_security_benefits, CO-1108; § 8.100.6.D.2, S623) or any loss of SSI, a State supplement or OAP after April 1977 while it was received with OASDI (lost_ssi_or_oap_received_with_social_security, CO-7358; 42 CFR 435.135(a)(2), S1233), and the disregard is measured from the OASDI of the last month of that concurrent receipt (social_security_income_when_ssi_or_oap_lost, CO-1109; 435.135(a)(3)). D.1 itself names no cause ("Medical Assistance must be provided to an individual if their countable income is below the current years SSI standard after a cost of living adjustment (COLA) disregard is applied to their OASDI"); D.2's list is narrower than the mandatory federal group, which a State plan must cover (statute_override). Before, a person who lost SSI when a pension began was never Pickle (PICKLE-PENSION, CO-910). Pattern sweep, non-MAGI Medicaid (docs/reviews/pattern-sweep-nonmagi.md, P1): aged, blind or disabled is read in the month with the disability onset gate (ma_is_aged_blind_or_disabled_in_month, CO-5201; 10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.5.C.4.b, S3623: disability approved, or 'a disability onset date determined on or prior to the date of a medical service'; § 8.100.3.E.1, S1503), as the SSI-related groups (CO-611) and OAP SISC B (CO-1177) already read it. Before, it read ma_is_aged_blind_or_disabled (CO-603), which has no onset gate, so a retroactive month before the onset of a disability was a disabled month.

### CO-1160 Medicaid: Disabled Adult Child countable income `@engine`

The person's SSI-related countable income with the current OASDI income disregarded, for the Disabled Adult Child test (10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.6.J.1.c.i, iii).

Precision. OQ-208 resolved: § 8.100.6.J.1.c disregards the current OASDI income and tests other countable income, so the OASDI comes off the unearned income first and the ssi_general_income_exclusion general exclusion (with any unused part carried to earned income, as in CO-605) applies to the income that remains. Duplicate-paths audit D-M2 (P1, fixed): the figure is the SSI-related countable income (CO-605, CO-606) with the person's current OASDI (ma_social_security_receipts) taken out of the unearned income the $20 applies to (ma_ssi_household_unearned_income_counted, CO-2281: the Ineligible Child Allocation taken from an ineligible spouse's unearned income, the one-third child support reduction, and the parental income deemed to a child), and the earned income after the allocation taken from the spouse's earnings (CO-2279; the couple's earned income, CO-6051). Before, this item copied the SSI formula without the Ineligible Child Allocation, the child support reduction or the deemed parental income: the household of D-M1 gave 1,607.50 against 1,359, and a child's ma_ssi_income_test_status (CO-5516) could read met_with_oasdi_disregarded where the deemed income makes the child's income too high. The earned arithmetic is CO-605's (registered siblings) Receipts harness after the generated households state earnings: the OASDI taken out is the OASDI the SSI method counts (ma_ssi_counted_social_security_receipts, CO-6250), net of a PASS set-aside (8.100.5.F.6.q), which the unearned income counted already leaves out; the gross benefit took the set-aside out twice, and as much of the other countable income with it. NM-KL-2 (2026-11-24; docs/reviews/known-limits.md): the disabled widow(er) group no longer reads this figure: 42 U.S.C. 1383c(d)(2) (S3416) takes out only the benefits under 42 U.S.C. 402, not a disability insurance benefit on the person's own record, so the group reads its own sibling copy (ma_disabled_widow_countable_income, CO-7941).

Whether the person is eligible as a disabled widow(er) (10 CCR 2505-10 §§ 8.100.3.F.1.e, 8.100.6.I) - a disabled widow or widower aged ma_disabled_widow_min_age through 64 who received SSI in the past and no longer receives SSI payments because of Social Security benefits, has no Medicare hospital insurance, and meets the other Medical Assistance requirements; the group ends when the person becomes eligible for Medicare Part A.

Precision. 'Meet all other Medical Assistance requirements' (§ 8.100.6.I.1.f) is read as residency, status, and the SSI-related income and resource criteria of § 8.100.5 that § 8.100.6.A.1 gives every ABD category, applied as 42 U.S.C. 1383c(d)(2) and 42 CFR 435.138(a) deem the group SSI recipients 'for so long as such person ... would be eligible for such supplemental security income benefits ... in the absence of' the widow(er)'s benefits: the SSI resource standard (ma_meets_ssi_resource_standard), and the SSI income test in the absence of the benefits 1383c(d)(1)(A) describes (ma_disabled_widow_meets_ssi_income_test, CO-7943: the SSI income test, CO-5516, met, or met by the countable income with the Social Security benefits under 42 U.S.C. 402 taken out, ma_disabled_widow_countable_income, CO-7941): income at a rate of not more than the SSI Federal Benefit Rate (42 U.S.C. 1382(a), S3950), the test 1383c(d) names. T-9 hand check A-4 (receipts migration phase 2): the item read "below" by analogy with the Disabled Adult Child group (OQ-209), the opposite of CO-609 for the same SSI test; both now read CO-5516. The Social Security disregarded is every benefit under 42 U.S.C. 402 (S5361): 1383c(d)(1)(A) names a benefit under 402(e) or (f) 'or under any other subsection of section 402' where the person is also eligible under (e) or (f); a disability insurance benefit on the person's own record is a benefit under 42 U.S.C. 423 (S5362) and stays counted, read from the benefit type each Social Security receipt states (CO-5000, title_ii_benefit_type; ma_disabled_widow_disregarded_social_security_receipts, CO-7940). NM-KL-2 (2026-11-24; coverage pass 7, non-MAGI F7-10): before, every Social Security benefit was disregarded, as the Disabled Adult Child test disregards 'the current OASDI income' (§ 8.100.6.J.1.c.i, S626), so a widow with her own disability benefit of 1,100 and a widow's benefit of 300 was eligible (countable 0) where the text gives 1,100 - 20 = 1,080 > 994 (WIDOW-OWN-DIB, stored household CO-1202). 'Have received SSI in the past' and 'no longer receive SSI payments because of Social Security payments' (§ 8.100.6.I.1.b, d) read lost_ssi_due_to_social_security_benefits (CO-1180), not the SSI-or-OAP fact. ### CO-1163 Medicaid: protected SSI-related group `@engine`

Which protected group keeps an aged, blind or disabled person on Medical Assistance after SSI or OAP cash ends: SSI recipients who remain eligible as SSI recipients without a payment, including section 1619(b) (10 CCR 2505-10 §§ 8.100.1, 8.100.6.C.8) - continued_ssi_status; Disabled Adult Children (§ 8.100.6.J) - disabled_adult_child; disabled widow(er)s aged 50 through 64 (§ 8.100.6.I) - disabled_widow; the Pickle Amendment group (§ 8.100.6.D-E) - pickle; or none.

Precision. A person who is not aged, blind or disabled (CO-603) is none without further facts. The groups are tested in the order listed and the first that applies is reported. Continued SSI status also requires residency and status, as the other groups do. The 1972-disregard, 1973 and 1983-actuarial-change groups (§§ 8.100.6.F-H) are closed historical cohorts and are not modeled (OQ-209). Disabled widow(er)s meet the SSI-related income and resource criteria without the widow(er)'s benefit (CO-1162, coverage review NM-9). The non-cooperation denial (ma_abd_denied_for_noncooperation, CO-4886) is tested after continued SSI status: a member who remains eligible as an SSI recipient without a payment, 1619(b) included, "shall receive Medical Assistance benefits" (§ 8.100.6.C.8) on the SSA's determination, as ma_ssi_related_category (CO-612) and ma_is_ssi_related_eligible (CO-611) exempt an SSI recipient from the denial (coverage pass 3 C3-9). Pattern sweep, non-MAGI Medicaid (docs/reviews/pattern-sweep-nonmagi.md, P1): aged, blind or disabled is read in the month with the disability onset gate (ma_is_aged_blind_or_disabled_in_month, CO-5201; 10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.5.C.4.b, S3623: disability approved, or 'a disability onset date determined on or prior to the date of a medical service'; § 8.100.3.E.1, S1503), as the SSI-related groups (CO-611) and OAP SISC B (CO-1177) already read it. Before, it read ma_is_aged_blind_or_disabled (CO-603), which has no onset gate, so a retroactive month before the onset of a disability was a disabled month. Pattern sweep, non-MAGI Medicaid (docs/reviews/pattern-sweep-nonmagi.md, P1): SSI status without payment (1619(b)) is read in the month (ma_retains_ssi_status_in_month, CO-7504: for a month before the determination month, not before the month of the SSI award's eligibility date). Before, the status of the determination date was read in every month.

Whether the person's age (and, for CES, marital status) fits the target group of the HCBS waiver the Case Management Agency designated (meets_hcbs_waiver_target_group, CO-821), per 10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.7101: Children's Extensive Support - unmarried and under ma_hcbs_ces_age_limit; Children's Habilitation Residential Program - under ma_hcbs_chrp_age_limit; Children with Complex Health Needs - under ma_hcbs_cwchn_age_limit; Brain Injury - ma_hcbs_bi_min_age or older; Community Mental Health Supports, Elderly, Blind and Disabled, Complementary and Integrative Health, Supported Living Services and Developmental Disabilities - ma_hcbs_adult_min_age or older. False when no waiver is designated.

Precision. EBD's age follows the subgroup the Case Management Agency finds (ma_hcbs_ebd_subgroup, CO-2264): aged, ma_aged_age or older; physically disabled or blind, ma_hcbs_adult_min_age or older (§ 8.7101.G.2.c.i bounds the subgroup at 64 but reclassifies a participant who reaches ma_aged_age as aged without a break, so no upper bound is applied); HIV/AIDS, ma_hcbs_adult_min_age or older. The diagnoses, settings and BI's injury-before-65 condition are ma_meets_hcbs_waiver_condition_criteria (CO-2270) and the level of care CO-1178 (OQ-210, resolved). Coverage pass 4, non-MAGI N4-9 (docs/operators.md, "Ages in a month"): the age is taken in the month evaluated, not on the determination date: an "under N" test on the first day of the month (ma_age_on_first_day_of_month, CO-4978), an "N or older" test on the last day (ma_age_on_last_day_of_month, CO-5402), and a test that excludes the person from what is favorable on the other day. Per month: its reader (ma_hcbs_waiver_eligible, CO-653) is per month. Pattern sweep, non-MAGI Medicaid (docs/reviews/pattern-sweep-nonmagi.md, P2, P3): whether the person is married is read from a spouse of the case or the marital status as stated, required where read (decision 4 of 2026-11-23); before, is_married (CO-930) read a person with neither stated as not married. Coverage pass 7, non-MAGI F7-4: a legally separated person (marital_status legally_separated, CO-844) is still married, so not 'unmarried' for Children's Extensive Support; before, a legal separation was stated as other and read as unmarried.

Type yes/no, scope person-month, program Medicaid.
Uses: `ma_age_on_first_day_of_month`, `ma_age_on_last_day_of_month`, `ma_aged_age`, `ma_hcbs_adult_min_age`, `ma_hcbs_bi_min_age`, `ma_hcbs_ces_age_limit`, `ma_hcbs_chrp_age_limit`, `ma_hcbs_cwchn_age_limit`, `ma_hcbs_ebd_subgroup`, `marital_status`, `meets_hcbs_waiver_target_group`, `relationships`.

### CO-1172 Medicaid: is exempt from the five-year rule `@engine`

Whether a qualified non-citizen is exempt from Medical Assistance's five-year rule under 10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.3.G.1.g.iv-v and viii: a refugee, asylee, Cuban or Haitian entrant or Compact of Free Association migrant (iv.9-10, v.1-2, "on any date"); an honorably discharged veteran or a person on active duty, or the spouse or dependent child of one (iv.2-3); a Lawful Permanent Resident who has worked federal_qualifying_quarters_threshold work quarters (iv.1), is a Hmong or Highland Lao veteran (iv.6), or is an Iraqi or Afghan special immigrant who arrived on or after December 26, 2007 and adjusted to LPR (iv.7-8); an American Indian born in Canada or a tribal member (iv.4); a victim of a severe form of trafficking (iv.11); or an Afghan humanitarian parolee through the later of March 31, 2023 and the end of parole (viii).

Precision. Coverage pass 7, C7-09 (2026-11-24): a lawful permanent resident's earlier status (status_before_lpr_adjustment, CO-2700) is required where this item reads it (decision 4 of 2026-11-23): not stated, whether the person adjusted from an exempt status cannot be determined, where before it was read as admitted directly and the person barred (CO-1063 without it: November eligible, read emptied to emergency_only). The 1613(b) adjusted classes are read here as stated, beside the shared is_exempt_from_five_year_bar (CO-1725), which reads an unstated earlier status as none for its cash readers. Refugees and asylees are exempt whether or not they have adjusted to LPR: § 8.100.3.G.1.g.iv opens with "Be a Legal Permanent Resident" but lists persons "granted asylum" and "refugee" (iv.9-10) and trafficking victims (iv.11), and 8 U.S.C. 1613(b)(1), which iv cites, exempts refugees and asylees as such; reading iv as excluding an unadjusted refugee would leave refugees and asylees under no adult category at all (OQ-213). The 40-quarters exemption is read for a Lawful Permanent Resident only, as iv states it; qualifying_quarters (CO-004) counts quarters credited from a parent's or spouse's work as 8 U.S.C. 1612(b)(2)(B), which iv.1 cites, allows. The veteran and active-duty exemption is read for any qualified non-citizen, as the item it replaces did. This item does not itself test that the person is a qualified non-citizen; ma_meets_citizenship_requirement (CO-509) reads it only for one. The 8 U.S.C. 1613(b) categories (refugee, asylee, Cuban or Haitian entrant, COFA migrant, veteran or active duty, and a refugee or asylee adjusted to LPR or an Amerasian immigrant) are read from the shared is_exempt_from_five_year_bar (CO-1725), so Medicaid and the cash programs cannot disagree on them; the categories of iv that 1613(b) does not list are read here from immigration_status and the history facts (CO-2700 to CO-2703). From October 1, 2026 an exemption admits a qualified non-citizen to full Medical Assistance only if the person is also in a 42 U.S.C. 1396b(v)(5)(B) status (ma_is_in_federal_payment_status_category, CO-2400): ma_meets_citizenship_requirement (CO-509) reads both. An exempt refugee or asylee who has not adjusted to lawful permanent residence is then no longer admitted as an adult (HCPF review B-1); this item still states the exemption, which keeps meaning for the five-year rule once the person adjusts. The Hmong veteran (iv.6) and special immigrant (iv.7-8) categories are read for a Lawful Permanent Resident, as iv.6 and iv.7-8 state; the American Indian born in Canada (iv.4) and the trafficking victim (iv.11) are read whatever the status, like the refugee and asylee (OQ-213). viii is read from parole_end_date (CO-2703) and ma_afghan_humanitarian_parolee_exemption_end_date (CO-2705); from October 1, 2026 an Afghan parolee who has not adjusted is outside 1396b(v)(5)(B), so the exemption no longer admits the person to full coverage (CO-509).

Type yes/no, scope person, program Medicaid.
Uses: `federal_qualifying_quarters_threshold`, `immigration_status`, `iraqi_afghan_special_immigrant_entry_start_date`, `is_american_indian_born_in_canada_or_tribal_member`, `is_exempt_from_five_year_bar`, `is_hmong_or_highland_lao_veteran`, `ma_afghan_humanitarian_parolee_exemption_end_date`, `parole_end_date`, `qualifying_quarters`, `status_before_lpr_adjustment`, `us_entry_date`.

```
any of the following is true:
  - Is exempt from the five-year bar (8 U.S.C. 1613(b))
  - Immigration status is equal to trafficking_victim
  - American Indian born in Canada or tribal member (non-citizen category), otherwise no
  - all of the following are true:
    - Immigration status is equal to lawful_permanent_resident
    - any of the following is true:
      - Qualifying quarters is at least Federal qualifying quarters threshold (40)
      - Hmong or Highland Lao veteran of the Vietnam conflict, otherwise no
      - all of the following are true:
        - Status before lawful permanent residence is equal to iraqi_afghan_special_immigrant
        - Date of entry into the United States is at least Iraqi and Afghan special immigrant arrival start date (2007-12-26)
      - Status before lawful permanent residence is one of: refugee, asylee, deportation_withheld, cuban_haitian_entrant, amerasian_immigrant
  - all of the following are true:
    - Immigration status is equal to afghan_humanitarian_parolee
    - any of the following is true:
      - the Determination Date is at most Medicaid: Afghan humanitarian parolee five-year exemption end date (2023-03-31)
      - the Determination Date is at most Parole end date
```

### CO-1173 Medicaid: is a Cover All Coloradans person `@engine`

Whether the person is in the population 10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.3.G.1.g.ix.1 (Cover All Coloradans) protects from exclusion on the basis of immigration status - under 19 or turning 19 this month, pregnant, or within 12 months of the beginning of the postpartum period. The rule's protection reaches the categories ix.1.a-b list (ma_meets_status_for_cover_all_coloradans_categories, CO-1174); for a child under 19 and a pregnant person, C.R.S. 25.5-2-104(2) and 25.5-5-201(6)(a) reach every category (ma_magi_is_fully_eligible, CO-562; ma_is_covered_under_cover_all_coloradans, CO-1175; OQ-214).

Precision. Medicaid status by month (2026-11-24, docs/reviews/medicaid-status-by-month.md, MS-3): the determination date's population, read by person-scope items only (ma_meets_status_for_cover_all_coloradans_categories CO-1174, the hospital presumptive category CO-2439); every month-scoped reader reads ma_is_cover_all_coloradans_person_in_month (CO-7552). The postpartum extension is read as 12 months after the month the person's most recent pregnancy ended (ma_postpartum_coverage_end_month, CO-560), through the last day of that month; a person with no known pregnancy_end_date is treated as not postpartum (known false), not unknown, so this term does not turn the item unknown for a person for whom postpartum status is simply inapplicable or not yet stated. The age term is ma_is_under_child_age_or_turns_nineteen_this_month (CO-564), since ix.1 states the same month-of-19th-birthday extension as § 8.100.4.G.2.a.

Type yes/no, scope person, program Medicaid.

```
any of the following is true:
  - Medicaid: under the child age limit, or turns 19 this month for the month containing the Determination Date
  - Is pregnant
  - all of the following are true:
    - it is not the case that Most recent pregnancy end date, as the case records it is unknown
    - the Determination Date is less than the first day of the month after Medicaid: postpartum coverage end month
```

### CO-1175 Medicaid: is covered under Cover All Coloradans `@engine`

Whether a person who does not meet the citizenship and immigration status requirement (ma_meets_citizenship_requirement, CO-509) is nevertheless fully covered this month through Cover All Coloradans (10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.3.G.1.g.ix.1): a child, pregnant or postpartum person (ma_is_cover_all_coloradans_person, CO-1173) who qualifies for a Medical Assistance category ix.1.a-b lists - the MAGI Children or Pregnant category (including a needy newborn), a Buy-In program, or an HCBS waiver.

Precision. The MAGI categories are read from ma_magi_category (CO-551), which does not read status; needy_newborn is counted with child, since a needy newborn is a child under 19 in the Children's group. Transitional Medical Assistance, the 4 Month Extended Medical Assistance and Psych <21 are not modeled in this volume. CHP+ is not a Medical Assistance category; ma_emergency_medicaid_status (CO-1151) reads CHP+ eligibility separately. OQ-214 sweep: a child under 19 or a pregnant person who meets every requirement of any categorical program other than status (ma_meets_requirements_other_than_status, CO-1150) is covered here too, by C.R.S. 25.5-2-104(2) (state medical assistance for a child, the same benefits) and 25.5-5-201(6)(a) (medical assistance for a pregnant non-citizen); a postpartum person who was not covered while pregnant still reaches only the ix.1.a-b list. A person covered here is not limited to emergency coverage (ma_is_emergency_medicaid_only, CO-510). Coverage pass 5 (2026-11-23, the class of C5-02 and C5-03): pregnancy is read for the month evaluated (ma_is_pregnant_in_month, CO-3601), not on the determination date (is_pregnant), so a retroactive month in which the person was pregnant is a pregnant month although the pregnancy has ended, and a month before a pregnancy began is not. Pattern sweep, MAGI (2026-11-24, PS-01, PS-02): status and the Cover All Coloradans population are read for the month evaluated (ma_meets_citizenship_requirement_in_month, CO-7551; ma_is_cover_all_coloradans_person_in_month, CO-7552; ma_meets_status_for_cover_all_coloradans_categories_in_month, CO-7553), not on the determination date: 8.100.4.G.1 (S3351), 8.100.3.E.1 (S217), 8 U.S.C. 1613(a) (S176), ix.1's 'current month' (S607).

Type yes/no, scope person-month, program Medicaid.
Uses: `ma_buy_in_category`, `ma_hcbs_waiver_eligible`, `ma_is_cover_all_coloradans_person_in_month`, `ma_is_pregnant_in_month`, `ma_is_under_child_age_or_turns_nineteen_this_month`, `ma_magi_category`, `ma_meets_citizenship_requirement_in_month`, `ma_meets_requirements_other_than_status`.

```
  - it is not the case that Medicaid: meets the citizenship requirement in the month
```

### CO-1177 Medicaid: is eligible as an OAP recipient meeting SSI criteria except income (SISC B) `@engine`

Whether the person is an Old Age Pension recipient who receives Medical Assistance under SISC B because the person also meets SSI eligibility criteria except for the level of income - 10 CCR 2505-10 §§ 8.100.6.K.2-4, 8.100.3.F.1.c-d and 8.100.3.M.2.b: receives OAP (adult_financial_program_received, CO-2710), a Colorado resident, meets Medicaid's citizenship and immigration status requirement, aged, blind or disabled, and within the SSI resource standard.

Precision. 'Meets SSI eligibility criteria except for the level of their income' is read as residency, status (CO-509), aged, blind or disabled in the month (CO-5201, which applies the disability onset of § 8.100.5.C.4.b) and the SSI resource standard (CO-610), and Medical Assistance not denied for non-cooperation (ma_abd_denied_for_noncooperation, CO-4886; § 8.100.5.E.6, § 8.100.7.V.2.c), since SISC B is a Medical Assistance category; the SSI income standard is not tested, so an OAP grant above the SSI federal benefit rate does not defeat it. § 8.100.3.M.2.b names only OAP "A" for code B while § 8.100.6.K.4 names OAP-A and OAP-B; the Adult Financial record carries a single OAP category, so both are read (OQ-206). OAP recipients who lost OAP to a non-OASDI cost of living adjustment (§ 8.100.6.K.7) are SISC C, not SISC B, so this item reads current OAP receipt only; ma_oap_health_care_status (CO-1156) brings them in through ma_lost_oap_to_non_oasdi_cost_of_living_adjustment (OQ-206, resolved). ### CO-1179 Medicaid: meets the institution for mental diseases requirement `@engine`

Whether the person meets the general Medical Assistance requirement of 10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.3.G.1.c: not a patient in an institution for tuberculosis or mental disease this month, unless under ma_imd_exclusion_min_age or ma_aged_age or older (the ages at which inpatient psychiatric treatment is a covered service).

Precision. The ages are tested first, so a person under ma_imd_exclusion_min_age or ma_aged_age or older meets the requirement without the institution fact. § 8.100.3.G.1.c conditions the under-21 and 65-or-older exception on the person 'receiving active treatment as an inpatient in a psychiatric facility eligible for Medical Assistance reimbursement'; is_patient_in_institution_for_mental_diseases (CO-1104) does not distinguish active treatment, so a patient of those ages is read as within the exception. The § 8.100.4.H extension for a patient who turns ma_imd_exclusion_min_age during inpatient psychiatric treatment is not modeled. Read by the MAGI full-coverage test (CO-562), the SSI-related test (CO-611), the emergency-only route (CO-1150) and, from coverage pass 7 (non-MAGI F7-5), the long-term care requirements (CO-3310), the Medicare Savings Programs (CO-617) and the Buy-Ins (CO-622). Coverage review 2, N-12: the ages are taken on the determination date, and this item is read by non-MAGI groups too (CO-611, CO-1150). A person who reaches 65 during the month is within the exception on the determination date. A MAGI person who turns 21 during the month and is a patient of an institution for mental diseases loses the exception from that date, though § 8.100.4.G.1's whole month would keep the month; the case is narrow (an inpatient under 21 is ordinarily within the § 8.100.4.H.1.a psychiatric group, CO-2419, which keeps the month). Time audit T-1 (2026-11-23): the exclusion's ages flip the day, since the person is excluded for the whole month only when both hold on every day of it: 21 or older on the first day (ma_age_on_first_day_of_month, CO-4978) and under 65 on the last day (ma_age_on_last_day_of_month, CO-5402); § 8.100.5.C.1 (S3900) read for an institutional resident, OQ-950; it read age (CO-300), the age on the determination date, in every month.

Uses: `is_patient_in_institution_for_mental_diseases`, `ma_age_on_first_day_of_month`, `ma_age_on_last_day_of_month`, `ma_aged_age`, `ma_imd_exclusion_min_age`.


### CO-1185 Medicaid: months over which lottery or gambling winnings are spread `@engine`

The number of months over which the lottery or gambling winnings the person received this month are divided equally and counted as MAGI income - 42 U.S.C. 1396a(e)(14)(K)(i) and 10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.4.C.1.b.xiv.1-3: one month (the month received) for winnings less than ma_lottery_winnings_spread_floor ($80,000); two months from it up to the next ma_lottery_winnings_spread_increment ($90,000); and one more month for each further whole ma_lottery_winnings_spread_increment, at most ma_lottery_winnings_spread_max_months. Read [at] the month of each receipt (CO-1187).

Precision. Computed as 2 plus the number of whole $10,000 increments in the amount above $80,000 (the floor written -ceil(-x)): under $80,000 one month; $80,000 to $89,999.99 two; $90,000 to $99,999.99 three; $100,000 to $109,999.99 four ("3 months plus 1 additional month for each increment of $10,000", (K)(i)(IV)); $1,260,000 or more 120. Colorado's "over $79,999 but less than $89,999" and "For every additional $10,000 over $89,999" (S669) agree with the federal bands at whole dollars; between them (for example $89,999.50, "over $89,999" in Colorado's words and under $90,000 in the statute's) the statute governs (statute_override). Time audit T-4: the rule had compared with $79,999 and counted each started $10,000 above it, which matched only at whole dollars, so $79,999.50 was spread over two months and $89,999.50 over three (CO-535). OQ-216.

Type whole number, scope person-month, program Medicaid.


### CO-1402 Medicaid: income is reasonably compatible `@engine`

Whether the attested household income is reasonably compatible with the electronic data source's, the applicable income standard being the highest MAGI standard the person could qualify under plus the ma_magi_income_disregard_pct disregard (the income up to which the category items grant eligibility, § 8.100.4.D.1): both at or below the applicable income standard; the attested figure above the standard, whatever the data figure (both above, § 8.100.4.C.2.a.iii; or the data figure below, which Colorado's verification plan takes as attested, the person ineligible, with no further information requested); or the attested figure at or below the standard and the data figure no more than ma_reasonable_compatibility_threshold_pct above the attested figure (C.2.a.ii). The same three arms are applied a second time at the limited Family Planning standard (ma_family_planning_income_upper_pct plus the disregard), on that category's own figures (the attested ma_family_planning_household_income_pct_fpl, CO-1153, and the data ma_electronic_data_source_family_planning_income_pct_fpl, CO-4977, both on the household counted with the applicant as two), and the income is compatible only when it is compatible at both.

Precision. Coverage review 3, C3-03: limited Family Planning's 260% is the applicable standard for an applicant over every full-coverage standard; compared at the full-coverage standard alone, every Family Planning attestation was above the standard and so compatible, and no income verification was asked whatever the data source reported. The Family Planning arms read the category's own attested figure (CO-1153, the budget-period income over the household counted with the applicant as two) and the data source on the same size (CO-4977), the figures the category item compares, as the full-coverage arms read CO-504 and CO-1344. Coverage review F-12 (OQ-302): Colorado's MAGI verification plan (D-317, S3364) says that when "an individual attests to income above the applicable standard and data source indicates income below the standard, the state will take the attestation and make the person ineligible ... Additional information will not be requested"; the item had treated that combination as not compatible, so CO-1403 asked for earned income documentation. The attested figure is then the one eligibility uses, and the person is ineligible on it. The plan's threshold (10%) predates the rule's 20% (ma_reasonable_compatibility_threshold_pct), which governs; neither says 20% of what (OQ-302). With both at or below the standard the any is true on its second term; with the attested figure at or below and the data above, only the threshold term can be true. Coverage review 2, N-04: the standard had been compared without the 5% disregard, so an attestation between the standard and the standard plus the disregard counted as above the standard (compatible) while the category items (CO-545 to CO-548) granted eligibility on it, and no verification was asked even with a data figure far above. C.2.a.iii's 'ineligible due to income' and the plan's 'make the person ineligible' are true on the attestation only above the standard after the disregard (§ 8.100.4.D.1.a: the disregard is the last step of each eligibility test), so that is the standard compared here.

### CO-1403 Medicaid: requires verification of earned income `@engine`

Whether the person must document earned income for Medical Assistance: wages that an electronic data source could not verify, or that are questionable; earnings the data reports when the attested and data figures are not reasonably compatible against the applicable standard (MAGI, or aged, blind and disabled), including for an adult who attested no earnings; and self-employment income only when the ledger is questionable; unless documentation is not reasonably available.

Precision. The MAGI data figure is household-level, so the not-reasonably-compatible arm asks each adult member and each member attesting earnings, not a child with none (OQ-302). Coverage review 2, N-04: compatibility is judged at each applicant's own standard (CO-1402), so the arm also asks the earners of a household in which any member requesting coverage has income that is not reasonably compatible at that member's standard; a parent whose own attestation is above her standard (and is taken as attested) still documents the earnings her child's eligibility rests on. Earned-income records, Medicaid and CHP+ track E1: the wages and the self-employment receipts are the earnings records (ma_employer_pay_for_verification, CO-5163; ma_self_employment_receipts_for_verification, CO-5164), replacing wages_gross and self_employment_gross_receipts. Pattern sweep, MAGI (2026-11-24, PS-06): whether a member whose income is not reasonably compatible requests coverage (ma_is_requesting_coverage) is read as stated, required where read (decision 4; was read as not requesting). Pattern sweep, MAGI (2026-11-24, PS-01): the adult's age (19 or older) is taken in the month evaluated, on its last day (ma_age_on_last_day_of_month, CO-5402; docs/operators.md, Ages in a month), not on the determination date (age, CO-300).

### CO-1404 Medicaid: requires verification of unearned income `@engine`

Whether the person's unearned income must be verified for Medical Assistance: for an aged, blind or disabled applicant whenever unearned income was received in the month or in the month before (§ 8.100.5.B.1.d), except that a Medicare Savings Program applicant's interest and dividends are taken on attestation (42 CFR 435.952(e)(1)(i)); for others, who may self-attest it, only when questionable; unless documentation is not reasonably available.

Precision. Heavier-definitions audit L-5 (audit fix round 4): "received in the month for which eligibility is being determined or during the previous month" is read as the month evaluated and the calendar month before it, so income that stopped last month is still verified. Audit H-14: for an MSP-only application (ma_application_is_msp_only) the aged, blind or disabled arm reads ma_has_unearned_income_other_than_interest_and_dividends (CO-5520), so interest and dividends alone require no verification; the resources half of 435.952(e) is ma_requires_verification_of_resources (CO-1405). Final verification pass 3, P2-2: an application for the Children with Disabilities Buy-In only (ma_application_is_children_buy_in_only, CO-4206) follows the MAGI verification requirements of § 8.100.4.B (§ 8.100.6.Q.3, S3000): unearned income is self-attested and verified only when questionable.

### CO-1405 Medicaid: requires verification of resources `@engine`

Whether the resources of an aged, blind or disabled applicant and of a spouse living with the applicant (ma_ssi_couple_members, CO-3626) must be verified for Medical Assistance: for full Medical Assistance, any resources of either available in the month, counted or excluded (MAGI categories have no resource test); for an applicant for a Medicare Savings Program only, the liquid resources (cash, accounts, stocks and bonds, and retirement accounts that can be withdrawn), or any resource whose attested value is questionable, since the attested value of non-liquid resources, burial funds and life insurance is accepted (42 CFR 435.952(e)(2)-(4)); unless documentation is not reasonably available.

Precision. Liquid and non-liquid follow 20 CFR 416.1201(b)-(c) (S2420): cash, financial institution accounts, stocks, bonds and mutual fund shares (liquid_resources_value) and retirement accounts that can be converted to cash within 20 days (retirement_accounts_value) are liquid; real property, vehicles and household goods are not. Life insurance, which 416.1201(b) lists as liquid, is taken on attestation under 435.952(e)(4)(i) (S2419), the State accepting the attested cash surrender value under (e)(4)(i)(A); burial funds under (e)(3). A non-liquid value is verified only when the attestation is questionable (435.952(e)(2)(ii), S2418; resources_attestation_is_questionable); verification after eligibility under (e)(2)(iii) is not modeled. The couple's resources are verified once, through the applicant's resources_are_verified, as the couple's resources are counted together (ma_ssi_countable_resources, CO-608). 435.952(e)(1) on interest and dividends is ma_requires_verification_of_unearned_income (CO-1404). Final verification pass 3, P2-2: an application for the Children with Disabilities Buy-In only (ma_application_is_children_buy_in_only, CO-4206) has no resource verification: the program counts no resources (§ 8.100.6.Q.1.c) and follows the MAGI verification requirements (Q.3, S3000). A disabled child whose application is not so limited is screened in the SSI-related categories too, which count resources, so the resources are verified as before. Resource records, Medicaid track H1 (docs/reviews/records-holdings-medicaid.md): the liquid resources of the Medicare Savings Program arm are ma_liquid_holdings_value_in_month (CO-5328): the person's cash, accounts, securities, retirement accounts and the money of any source still held, counted or not, in place of liquid_resources_value (CO-3390) and retirement_accounts_value (CO-3392).

```
  - it is not the case that Documentation not reasonably available
```

### CO-1413 Medicaid: reasonable opportunity period end date `@engine`

The last day of the person's reasonable opportunity period: ma_reasonable_opportunity_period_days days after the notice is considered received, which is five days after the notice date, or a later date to which the eligibility site extended the period for a good faith effort (10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.3.H.10.a; 42 CFR 435.956(b)(2)(ii)(B)).

Precision. The period runs from ma_reasonable_opportunity_notice_date (CO-1747), the notice that opens it, not the verification checklist date. An extension (ma_reasonable_opportunity_extended_end_date, CO-2221) replaces the end only when it is later (OQ-316).

Type calendar date, scope person, program Medicaid.
Uses: `ma_notice_receipt_days`, `ma_reasonable_opportunity_extended_end_date`, `ma_reasonable_opportunity_notice_date`, `ma_reasonable_opportunity_period_days`.

```
if Reasonable opportunity period extended end date is more than Medicaid reasonable opportunity period days (90) days after Medicaid notice receipt days (5) days after Medicaid: reasonable opportunity notice date, otherwise no
  then Reasonable opportunity period extended end date
otherwise Medicaid reasonable opportunity period days (90) days after Medicaid notice receipt days (5) days after Medicaid: reasonable opportunity notice date
```

### CO-1415 Medicaid: verification status `@engine`

Where this person's Medical Assistance verification stands: not applicable (coverage is not requested for the person); none required; complete; pending within the time allowed; past the time allowed with documentation other than status outstanding; only citizenship, identity or immigration status outstanding within the reasonable opportunity period (benefits are furnished meanwhile to an otherwise eligible person); or the reasonable opportunity period expired with status unverified.

Precision. past_due and reasonable_opportunity_expired state that the time allowed has run; the termination itself (within 30 days, with notice) is processing outside this item. An extension of the time to verify (§ 8.100.3.D.2) or of the reasonable opportunity period for a good faith effort (§ 8.100.3.H.10) moves the due date and the period's end (CO-1414, CO-1413; OQ-316, resolved for Medical Assistance). Medical Assistance's own request fact (ma_is_requesting_coverage) is read before the shared one (OQ-382). At a renewal the renewal form allows at least 30 days (435.916(a)(3)(i)(B)), the same period ma_verification_due_date uses.

Type one of, scope person-month, program Medicaid.
Uses: `ma_is_requesting_coverage`, `ma_pending_status_verification_count`, `ma_pending_verification_count`, `ma_reasonable_opportunity_period_end_date`, `ma_required_verification_count`, `ma_verification_due_date`.

```
if it is not the case that Medical Assistance is requested for the person
  then not_applicable
else if Medicaid: required verification count is equal to 0
  then not_required
else if Medicaid: pending verification count is equal to 0
  then complete
else if all of the following are true:
    - (Medicaid: pending verification count minus Medicaid: pending status verification count) is more than 0
    - the Determination Date is more than Medicaid: verification due date
  then past_due
else if all of the following are true:
    - Medicaid: pending status verification count is more than 0
    - the Determination Date is more than Medicaid: reasonable opportunity period end date
  then reasonable_opportunity_expired
else if (Medicaid: pending verification count minus Medicaid: pending status verification count) is more than 0
  then pending
otherwise pending_reasonable_opportunity
```

```json
["case",[["not","ma_is_requesting_coverage"],"not_applicable"],[["=","ma_required_verification_count",0],"not_required"],[["=","ma_pending_verification_count",0],"complete"],[["all",[">",["-","ma_pending_verification_count","ma_pending_status_verification_count"],0],[">",["det_date"],"ma_verification_due_date"]],"past_due"],[["all",[">","ma_pending_status_verification_count",0],[">",["det_date"],"ma_reasonable_opportunity_period_end_date"]],"reasonable_opportunity_expired"],[[">",["-","ma_pending_verification_count","ma_pending_status_verification_count"],0],"pending"],["else","pending_reasonable_opportunity"]]
```

### CO-1634 Medical Assistance: requires verification of a trust `@engine`

Whether trust documents must be submitted: for a long-term care applicant who (or whose spouse) holds an interest in a trust (ma_holds_trust_interest_in_month, CO-5329: a trust_interest holdings record), or has an income trust.

Precision. Coverage review NM-13: a person determined eligible under the Working Adults Buy-In owes no B.2.a documents (§ 8.100.7.B.2.c; ma_owes_long_term_care_asset_disclosure, CO-4631). Resource records, Medicaid track H1 (docs/reviews/records-holdings-medicaid.md): a trust interest is a trust_interest holdings record (CO-5300), in place of has_trust_interest (CO-1577); a person whose holdings are stated with no such record has none. has_income_trust (CO-823) stays a person fact (an income arrangement). Pattern sweep, non-MAGI Medicaid (docs/reviews/pattern-sweep-nonmagi.md, P2): the person's spouse is read from the person's relationships as stated, required where read (decision 4 of 2026-11-23): before, a person with no relationships stated was read as having no spouse, so a spouse's transfers, trust or annuity were not asked for.

```
  - any of the following is true:

    - there is a person in all persons in every person in the case such that this person is a spouse of that person such that
      that person's Medicaid: the person holds an interest in a trust in the month
    - Has income trust
```

### CO-1640 Medical Assistance: aged, blind and disabled income is reasonably compatible `@engine`

Whether an aged, blind or disabled applicant's attested monthly income is reasonably compatible with the electronic data source's figure, judged against the applicable income standard: both at or below it, both above it, or the attested figure at or below it and the data no more than ma_reasonable_compatibility_threshold_pct above the attested figure. For a long-term care applicant the figures are gross income and the standard is ma_special_income_group_pct of the SSI individual rate (the special income group); for any other aged, blind or disabled applicant they are SSI-related countable income (ma_ssi_countable_income, and ma_ssi_countable_income_reported_by_data_source for the data) and the standard is the SSI rate for the household size, the couple rate for a couple (ma_ssi_income_standard).

Precision. The long-term care comparison stays on gross income because the special income group tests gross income (§ 8.100.7.A.1). The countable comparison applies the same $20, $65 and one-half disregards to both figures and combines a spouse living with the person (OQ-374, resolved). The ma_reasonable_compatibility_threshold_pct threshold is applied to the attested figure, OQ-302's first half.

Type yes/no, scope person-month, program Medicaid.
Uses: `electronic_data_source_monthly_gross_income`, `ma_is_long_term_care_applicant`, `ma_reasonable_compatibility_threshold_pct`, `ma_special_income_group_pct`, `ma_ssi_countable_income`, `ma_ssi_countable_income_reported_by_data_source`, `ma_ssi_gross_earned_income`, `ma_ssi_gross_unearned_receipts`, `ma_ssi_income_standard`, `ssi_federal_benefit_rate_individual`.

```
if Medical Assistance: long-term care applicant
  then (any of the following is true:;   - all of the following are true:;     - (Medicaid SSI method: a person's gross earned income plus Medicaid SSI method: a person's gross unearned receipts) is at most (SSI federal benefit rate, individual (1029) times Special income group percentage of SSI benefit (3));     - Electronic data source monthly gross income is at most (SSI federal benefit rate, individual (1029) times Special income group percentage of SSI benefit (3));   - all of the following are true:;     - (Medicaid SSI method: a person's gross earned income plus Medicaid SSI method: a person's gross unearned receipts) is more than (SSI federal benefit rate, individual (1029) times Special income group percentage of SSI benefit (3));     - Electronic data source monthly gross income is more than (SSI federal benefit rate, individual (1029) times Special income group percentage of SSI benefit (3));   - all of the following are true:;     - (Medicaid SSI method: a person's gross earned income plus Medicaid SSI method: a person's gross unearned receipts) is at most (SSI federal benefit rate, individual (1029) times Special income group percentage of SSI benefit (3));     - Electronic data source monthly gross income is at most ((Medicaid SSI method: a person's gross earned income plus Medicaid SSI method: a person's gross unearned receipts) times (1 plus Medicaid reasonable compatibility threshold (0.2))))
otherwise (any of the following is true:;   - all of the following are true:;     - Medicaid: SSI-related countable income is at most Medicaid: SSI income standard for the person's household size;     - Medicaid: SSI-related countable income reported by electronic data is at most Medicaid: SSI income standard for the person's household size;   - all of the following are true:;     - Medicaid: SSI-related countable income is more than Medicaid: SSI income standard for the person's household size;     - Medicaid: SSI-related countable income reported by electronic data is more than Medicaid: SSI income standard for the person's household size;   - all of the following are true:;     - Medicaid: SSI-related countable income is at most Medicaid: SSI income standard for the person's household size;     - Medicaid: SSI-related countable income reported by electronic data is at most (Medicaid: SSI-related countable income times (1 plus Medicaid reasonable compatibility threshold (0.2))))
```

### CO-1703 Medicaid: self-employment business costs `@engine`

The person's cost of doing business for the month that 10 CCR 2505-10 8.100.3.K.9 allows (rent of business premises, wholesale cost of merchandise, utilities, taxes, labor, upkeep of necessary equipment): the operating costs; not depreciation, payments on the principal of loans for capital assets, or personal expenses.

Precision. Earned-income records, Medicaid and CHP+ track E1: the cost records of the month the SSI method's earnings counting table deducts (ma_ssi_earnings_treatment_table, CO-5107, row deducted: the operating costs, K.9.a), each at its amount; the cost kinds K.9.b disallows (depreciation, payments on the principal of loans for capital assets) are rows not_deducted, and the kinds no text on file names are rows for the owner's signature. Replaces self_employment_operating_costs (CO-3370); a cost not stated is not deducted, since only stated records are summed (the old reader's otherwise 0 is gone with the fact). Field-effect sweep (docs/reviews/field-sweep-snap-cash-nonmagi.md), FS-MA-2: a record stated as a stream (no month and no date) is received only in the months from the month its job or business began through the month it ended (job_start_date, job_end_date; each absent: before, or through, the months the case covers; CO-5100), since earned income "is countable as income in the month received" (10 CCR 2505-10 8.100.5.F.4, S3001) and wages are counted "when you receive them" (20 CFR 416.1111(a), S4940); a pay stated with its month or date is placed by it, a final pay after the job ended included. Before, a stream was counted in every month whatever its job's dates. The clause is Adult Financial's and Colorado Works' (af_earned_pay, CO-5130; cw_earned_pay, CO-5140).

Type money, scope person-month, program Medicaid.
Uses: `earnings`, `ma_ssi_earnings_treatment_table`.

```
the sum for each receipt in Earnings where
    all of the following are true:
      - that receipt is received in the month
      - any of the following is true:
        - it is not the case that that receipt's month is unknown
        - all of the following are true:
          - any of the following is true:
            - that receipt's job start date is unknown
            - the month containing that receipt's job start date is at most the month
          - any of the following is true:
            - that receipt's job end date is unknown
            - the month containing that receipt's job end date is at least the month
      - Medicaid SSI method: how each kind of earnings is treated (table), for that receipt's kind is equal to deducted
  of
    that receipt's amount
```

### CO-1715 Medicaid: Working Adults with Disabilities countable income `@engine`

The applicant's own countable income for the month for the Buy-In Program for Working Adults with Disabilities (10 CCR 2505-10 8.100.6.P.1.b, 'only the applicant's income will be considered'): earned income (gross wages and net earnings from self-employment) less the ssi_earned_income_exclusion earned income exclusion and any part of the ssi_general_income_exclusion general income exclusion unearned income did not use, and then one half, plus unearned income (the receipts the SSI method's counting table counts, ma_ssi_unearned_receipts, with in-kind support and maintenance and gambling winnings) less the ssi_general_income_exclusion general income exclusion.

Precision. The SSI-method disregards of 8.100.5.H.4 applied to the applicant alone, without a living-together spouse's income. The unused part of the ssi_general_income_exclusion general income exclusion is carried to earned income, as § 8.100.5.H (which P.1.b points to) and 20 CFR 416.1124(c)(12) direct and as ma_ssi_countable_earned_income (CO-605) does. Final verification pass 3, pattern sweep (income methods): lottery and gambling winnings in the month received count as unearned income (§ 8.100.5.F.5.i, S3001) unless the hardship exemption is granted (CO-2222), and in-kind support and maintenance is not counted for an unemancipated child of 16 to 20 (§ 8.100.5.H.1.b). Coverage review NM-7, NM-8: the unearned income the SSI method excludes (tax refunds, loans, educational and energy assistance, federally excluded payments, retroactive SSI and Title II lump sums, foster care payments and income set aside under a plan for self-support) is left out: the applicant's unearned income is ma_ssi_unearned_receipts (CO-5511), read through the SSI method's counting table (CO-5510), and the 20 CFR 416.1112(c) exclusions incorporated by § 8.100.5.H.4.e apply to the applicant's earnings: impairment-related work expenses (not blind) before the one half, blind work expenses (blind) and earned income set aside under an approved plan after it. A Buy-In applicant meets the disability criteria (ma_wawd_eligible, CO-618), so (c)(6)'s conditions are read from blindness and age: (c)(6) and (c)(8) apply "if you are disabled (but not blind) and under age 65" and "if you are blind and under age 65", and P.1.a sets no upper age for the Buy-In, so the exclusions stop at ma_aged_age, as in CO-4628 and CO-4629 (coverage pass 3 C3-7; the SSI-before-65 continuation is not stated). The earned income 20 CFR 416.1112(c)(2)-(3) and § 8.100.5.F.6.z exclude (ma_ssi_excluded_earned_income, CO-2471: student, infrequent, Census) comes off the applicant's earnings before the $65 (coverage pass 3 C3-6). Coverage pass 4, non-MAGI N4-9 (docs/operators.md, "Ages in a month"): the age is taken in the month evaluated, not on the determination date: an "under N" test on the first day of the month (ma_age_on_first_day_of_month, CO-4978), an "N or older" test on the last day (ma_age_on_last_day_of_month, CO-5402), and a test that excludes the person from what is favorable on the other day. Coverage pass 6, non-MAGI F6-10 (decision 4 of 2026-11-23: each supplied fact states once whether it is required or what its rule-given default is; readers do not invent defaults): the person's own blindness (is_blind) is read as stated, no longer as false when unstated (blind work expenses and the impairment-related work expenses turn on it, 20 CFR 416.1112(c)(6), (c)(8)). The lottery hardship exemption keeps the default its fact declares. Blindness is asked only where it decides an amount: impairment-related work expenses or blind work expenses stated above 0 (with none, there is nothing for 20 CFR 416.1112(c)(6) or (c)(8) to exclude). Precision. Relatives (B) are read from the case's relationship edges: parent, child, grandparent, grandchild, spouse, caretaker or dependent edges and siblings (persons sharing a parent). An adult family member who is listed in lives_with is read as primarily residing there. Precision. Subclause by subclause (OQ-413 part (1), resolved): (I)'s plans under titles I, X and XIV were repealed for the States from January 1, 1974 (Pub. L. 92-603 sec. 303, S2106), and title XVI cash for Colorado residents is the federal SSI program, read under (II); (III), (IV), (VI) and (VII) describe pregnant women and children under 19, who are deemed for the month already, under 19 by 435.553(a)(1) (the age arm of CO-1969, under 19 on the first day of the month) and pregnant or postpartum as specified excluded individuals by 435.553(a)(4) (CO-1965); (V), qualified family members, is empty: "No individual shall be a qualified family member for any period after September 30, 1998" (42 U.S.C. 1396d(m)(2), S2105). So the Pregnant and Children categories are not read here; they had been, and a Colorado category above the mandatory income level (195% for pregnant women, 142% for children) is not the mandatory group in any case. ### CO-1974 Medicaid community engagement status `@engine`

The community engagement result for the person at this determination under 42 CFR 435.550-435.559: not_assessed (no application, renewal or change-in-circumstances review at this determination, including an enrolled beneficiary before the first renewal on or after the implementation date, 435.559(c)); excluded (a specified excluded individual in the determination month, so not an applicable individual, 435.551, 435.554(b)); met (at application, every month of the look-back met; at renewal or a change-in-circumstances redetermination, at least ma_community_engagement_renewal_required_months months met); notice_required (the information does not show the requirement met and no notice of noncompliance has been sent, which must precede any denial or disenrollment, 435.558(a)(1)); notice_period (a notice has been sent and the 30 days to make a satisfactory showing have not ended on the determination date, 435.558(a)(2)); or not_met (the period has ended with no satisfactory showing).

Precision. The result is the same for every month of the determination; it is stated per month so the look-back can read each month assessed. Specified excluded status is tested in the determination month; in a look-back month it is a mandatory exception (435.553(a)(4)), so a person excluded in some look-back months and not now still meets those months. A satisfactory showing made during the notice period is new information in the facts the look-back reads, and the status is then met or excluded. OQ-413 part (4), resolved: the notice, the showing period and continued coverage of 435.558 are modeled (CO-3161 to CO-3165; ma_meets_adult_group_community_engagement_condition, CO-1975). The verification rules of 435.557 are not: notice_required is the result once the facts the case states do not show the requirement met. Part (3): the applicable individual of 435.551 is the Adults group of § 435.119 (branch (a)); branch (b), a section 1115 demonstration covering adults not otherwise eligible under the State plan, has no Colorado population (OQ-413).

Type one of, scope person-month, program Medicaid.
Uses: `ma_community_engagement_noncompliance_notice_date`, `ma_community_engagement_renewal_required_months`, `ma_community_engagement_response_period_end_date`, `ma_community_engagement_review_months`, `ma_community_engagement_review_type`, `ma_is_specified_excluded_individual`, `ma_meets_community_engagement_for_month`.

```
if Community engagement review type is equal to none
  then not_assessed
else if Medicaid community engagement: is a specified excluded individual for the month containing the Determination Date
  then excluded
else if if Community engagement review type is equal to application
    then (in each of Medicaid community engagement: months assessed:;   Medicaid community engagement: met for the month for the month)
  otherwise (the number of months in Medicaid community engagement: months assessed for which Medicaid community engagement: met for the month for the month) is at least Medicaid community engagement: months required at renewal (1)
  then met
else if Medicaid community engagement: date of the notice of noncompliance is unknown
  then notice_required
else if the Determination Date is at most Medicaid community engagement: last day to make a satisfactory showing
  then notice_period
otherwise not_met
```

### CO-1975 Medicaid: Adults group community engagement condition `@engine`

Whether the community engagement condition 42 CFR 435.119(d) attaches to the Adults group is satisfied for the month: the month is before ma_community_engagement_start_date, the requirement is not yet in force on the determination date (ma_community_engagement_requirement_in_force, CO-3035), the person's community engagement status (CO-1974) is not_assessed, excluded or met, or the person is an enrolled beneficiary (a renewal or a change-in-circumstances review) whose coverage continues: while a notice of noncompliance is due or its showing period runs (435.558(a)(3); 42 U.S.C. 1396a(xx)(6)(A)(ii)(II)), and after the period ends with no satisfactory showing, through the month after the month it ended, the latest month the State may disenroll (435.558(d)(2)(ii)).

Precision. Medical assistance furnished before the start date is not conditioned (435.559(a)), so a retroactive month before it passes even at a later determination; a determination made before the start date does not assess the requirement at all. Hard-coded numbers audit E-1: the second arm compared the determination date with the start date; it reads the versions of CO-3035 instead. ### CO-1976 Medicaid: claimed dependent has the non-filer household `@engine`

Whether a person who expects to be claimed as a tax dependent has the non-filer MAGI household instead of the claiming filer's under 42 CFR 435.603(f)(2)(i)-(iii) and 10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.4.E.1.c and E.5: (i) claimed by someone other than a spouse or parent (ma_is_dependent_claimed_by_non_parent); or, for a child under 19, (ii) claimed by one parent while living with both parents who do not expect to file jointly, (iii) claimed by a non-custodial parent, or (E.5) claimed by married parents filing jointly when one parent lives outside the household because of separation or pending divorce.

Precision. Living with both parents is two parents of the child in the child's lives_with (CO-1925); where lives_with is not stated, whether a parent lives with the child cannot be determined (C6-10 (2026-11-24): living together is read from lives_with (CO-1925) as stated, required where read (decision 4 of 2026-11-23): no text on file says the persons of one Single Streamlined Application live together unless it says otherwise (10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.4.E.1 asks for the relationship to the tax filer 'as declared on the Single Streamlined Application' and E.1.a.ii, E.1.b.ii-iv, E.1.d for living in the home; 42 CFR 435.907, D-196, says nothing of the home), so a case that states no dwelling_id cannot be determined where MAGI asks whether two persons live together; before, a stated relationship edge was read as living together (convention rule 17's fallback), which the other programs' readers still do). The claiming parent is the person the child has a tax_dependent edge to who is also the child's parent. Coverage pass 4, C4-08: per month, "a child under 19" read on the first day of the month evaluated (ma_age_on_first_day_of_month, CO-4978), as the household (CO-500) is. Coverage pass 4, C4-06 (2026-11-23): where the custodial parent (ma_custodial_parent, CO-1946) is not stated, it is read from the stated home, which is where the child spends most nights: a claiming parent the child lives with is custodial (also where no home is stated, the convention above); a claiming parent the child does not live with is non-custodial, so (iii) routes the child to the non-filer rules, whether or not another parent lives with the child (coverage pass 5, C5-11: 42 CFR 435.603(f)(2)(iii) reads the custodial parent from where the child lives, "the parent with whom the child spends most nights", and a parent the child does not live with is not that parent; before, a child living with neither parent, in a third home, was cannot determine, KIN-CLAIMED). Where no home is stated the volume's convention reads the claiming parent as living with the child, so no case is left undetermined by this reading. Before, an unstated custodial parent was read as the claiming parent, a default no rule gives, so a child living with her non-filer mother and claimed by her father in another home was placed in the father's household (H3). Pattern sweep, MAGI (2026-11-24, PS-04): the parents living with the child are those living in the home in the month (ma_lives_with_in_month, CO-7554): a parent who died before the month does not live with the child (E.1.c.ii, S169). Pattern sweep, MAGI (2026-11-24, PS-06): E.4's separation (ma_lives_apart_due_to_separation_or_pending_divorce) is read for a parent who does not live in the child's home in the month, required there (S170; was read as not separated); a parent in the home is not separated from it.

### CO-2205 Medicaid: a continuous eligibility exception applies `@engine`

Whether, this month, one of the exceptions of 10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.3.Q.1.b ends a child's continuous eligibility period other than the residency exception, which ma_child_is_in_continuous_eligibility_period (CO-561) tests itself: the child has died (i); is no longer part of the Medical Assistance required household (iii); is unable to be located (v); has requested withdrawal (vi); failed to provide documentation during a reasonable opportunity period (vii); or the eligibility was erroneously granted through agency error, fraud or perjury (viii).

Precision. The period ends 'effective the earliest possible month', so each month fact is read as true from the month of the event on. An inmate's coverage moves to the limited incarceration benefit and full coverage is reinstated for the rest of the period on release (Q.1.b.ii.1), so the inmate prong reads the month's own inmate status (is_inmate_of_public_institution, CO-1105) and the period resumes in a later month the child is not an inmate. Exception vii is read from the volume's reasonable opportunity items: a month after the month the reasonable opportunity period ended (ma_reasonable_opportunity_period_end_date) with citizenship, identity or immigration status still pending (ma_pending_status_verification_count). A person to whom no reasonable opportunity notice was sent (ma_reasonable_opportunity_notice_date not stated) had no reasonable opportunity period and cannot fail to provide documentation during one, so the prong is false for that person. An inmate of a public institution (ii) no longer ends the period here: § 8.100.3.Q.1.b.ii.1 moves the child to a limited Incarceration benefit and reinstates full coverage on release within the period, which ma_magi_eligibility_status (CO-554) reports as incarceration_limited.

Uses: `is_deceased`, `ma_eligibility_was_erroneously_granted`, `ma_has_left_required_household`, `ma_has_requested_withdrawal_from_continuous_eligibility`, `ma_is_unable_to_be_located`, `ma_pending_status_verification_count`, `ma_reasonable_opportunity_period_end_date`.

```
  - all of the following are true:

    - Medicaid: pending status verification count is more than 0
```

Whether the period of ineligibility from a transfer of assets is apportioned equally between this person and the person's spouse because the spouse became institutionalized and is otherwise eligible for Medical Assistance (10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.7.F.8.a): a spouse of the case who, in the determination month, is institutionalized, meets every Long-Term Care requirement apart from the transfer penalty (ma_ltc_unmet_requirement none) and the institutional setting's level of care and status; a spouse outside the case so found; or an apportionment whose spouse's remaining months have since been assigned to this person (F.8.b).

Federal residency for a person receiving a State supplementary payment (the paying State, 435.403(f)) and for a title IV-E child (the State where the child lives, 435.403(g)) is not restated by Colorado and not modeled. Coverage pass 6, C6-05(a) (2026-11-24): where neither state_of_residence nor county_of_residence is stated, residence cannot be determined (decision 4 of 2026-11-23: no rule makes an unstated residence a non-resident); before, is_colorado_resident (CO-505) read it as not a resident, so the MAGI outcomes and family planning reported ineligible_residency (CO-226 without state_of_residence). is_colorado_resident itself, shared with other programs, is unchanged; every Medicaid category reads residency through this item, so the non-MAGI categories that read it get the same answer (8.100.3.B governs them all).

### CO-2271 Is applying for or eligible for SSI `@engine`

Whether the person is applying for or eligible for Supplemental Security Income. 10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.5.H.2.b-c defines an ineligible child, parent or spouse as one 'who is not applying or eligible for SSI', and the income allocations of § 8.100.5.H.3 are made for those persons.

Precision. Eligible for SSI is read as SSA's award (receives_ssi) or continued SSI status without payment (1619(b)); the volume does not determine SSI. If no application is stated, Medicaid reads the person as not applying. Coverage pass 4, non-MAGI N4-13 (decision 4 of 2026-11-23: missing information is cannot determine unless the rule says otherwise; readers do not invent defaults): whether the person has applied for SSI and whether the person keeps SSI status without payment are read as stated; neither was read as no when unstated any more, since who is an ineligible parent, spouse or child (10 CCR 2505-10 8.100.5.H.2.b) turns on them and no rule gives a default. Pattern sweep, non-MAGI Medicaid (docs/reviews/pattern-sweep-nonmagi.md, P1): per month. Eligible for SSI is read in the month: SSA's award (ma_receives_ssi_in_month, CO-7351) or SSI status without payment (ma_retains_ssi_status_in_month, CO-7504), each from the month of the award's eligibility date in a month before the determination month (8.100.6.C.7, S5030), so a parent or spouse awarded SSI from October is an ineligible parent or spouse in a retroactive August. Applying is the application as stated on the determination date (H.2.b-c, 'who is not applying'); no fact dates an application.

Type yes/no, scope person-month, program Medicaid.
Uses: `has_applied_for_ssi`, `ma_receives_ssi_in_month`, `ma_retains_ssi_status_in_month`.

```
any of the following is true:
  - Has applied for Supplemental Security Income benefits
  - Medicaid: receives SSI in the month
  - Medicaid: retains SSI status in the month
```

```json
["any","has_applied_for_ssi","ma_receives_ssi_in_month","ma_retains_ssi_status_in_month"]
```

### CO-2277 Medicaid: ineligible child allocation `@engine`

The total Ineligible Child Allocation for the person's SSI-related household (the person and a spouse living with the person): for each child of either who is an unemancipated child in the home and is not applying for or eligible for SSI, one half of the SSI individual Federal Benefit Rate, reduced by the child's own gross income (10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.5.H.3.a.i, H.2.a-b).

Precision. Duplicate-paths audit D-M4 (P1, fixed): the child must be in the home (H.3.a.i: 'available for each ineligible child in the home'): one of the persons who live with the person (lives_with, the same home, a temporary absence notwithstanding; 20 CFR 416.1167(a)), or, where the household states no homes, a child the parent edge joins who does not reside in a medical institution (the volume's convention for living together); the amount is the one per-child statement ma_ssi_ineligible_child_allocation_generated (CO-6050), which the parental deeming allocation (CO-4633) reads too, with the same test of the home. Before, this item tested no home, so an applicant's child living away in a medical institution generated a $497 allocation that CO-4633 did not give. The child's own income is its earned income and the unearned income the SSI method counts, child support included in full, since the one-third reduction of § 8.100.5.H.4.c 'does not apply to ineligible children when calculating the ineligible child allocation disregard'. A child is in the home through the parent edge, the volume's convention for living together. Pattern sweep, non-MAGI Medicaid (docs/reviews/pattern-sweep-nonmagi.md, P1, P2, P3): the household of the month is ma_ssi_lives_with_in_month (CO-7505): those living in the person's home, and a spouse, parent or child who lives elsewhere through the month the two ceased to live together (20 CFR 416.1165(g)(4), S5122; 416.1167(a)(1), S5120; § 8.100.7.C.2.b, S1759), a person who died through the month of death ((g)(3), S5122; 416.1163(f)(4), S5121); a person who lives in a facility (its dwelling_id the facility's) is a member through the month of entry (institution_entry_date) and not from the month after (§ 8.100.7.A.1, S3406: from 'the first day of the month following the month during which a child under the age of 18 ceases to live with his or her parent(s)'; 416.1167(a)(1)), while a person away for a stay the person returns from keeps the home's dwelling_id and stays a member (a temporary absence, 416.1167(a); duplicate-paths D-M4). Living together is read as stated, required where read (decision 4 of 2026-11-23; convention rule 17): no text on file says the persons of one application live together unless it says otherwise. A child not yet born in the month is not a child in the home (ma_is_ssi_unemancipated_child, CO-2275). Before, a child whose home was not stated was read as in the home unless the child lived in a medical institution, in every month.
