### CO-2419 Medicaid: needy persons under 21 category `@engine`

The needy-persons-under-21 group of 10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.4.H.1 the person is covered under this month, or none: Psych <21 (a: in a long-term care institution or a psychiatric facility, household income below the MAGI needs standard, under ma_needy_person_age_limit, or under ma_psych_inpatient_extended_age_limit if still inpatient at the first); Alternatives to Foster Care (d: income below the same standard); or foster care and adoption (b, c, e, f, g: no income test in the text; under ma_needy_person_age_limit, and for g not receiving subsidized adoption payments from ma_foster_care_age_at_responsibility, CO-3028). The person must be a Colorado resident and meet the citizenship and immigration status requirement - for Psych <21, the requirement of a Cover All Coloradans category (§ 8.100.3.G.1.g.ix.1.a lists Psych <21).

Precision. "The MAGI needs standard for his/her family size" (a, d) is not defined in § 8.100; it is read as the highest MAGI income standard among the groups whose demographic criteria the person meets (ma_magi_highest_income_standard_pct, CO-539), compared with the MAGI household income, strictly below as the text says "less than" (OQ-512). The Department of Human Services' assumption of responsibility, and for g the foster care maintenance or subsidized adoption payments before 18, are part of the supplied basis. Coverage review 2, N-02 sweep: the under-21 and under-22 limits read ma_age_before_month (CO-4790), so a person in the month of the 21st (or, in inpatient treatment, the 22nd) birthday stays in the group for that month (§ 8.100.4.G.1); the test of 18 at the time of responsibility is a lower limit and reads age on the determination date. Coverage pass 4, C4-05: the month's figure (ma_magi_monthly_household_income_pct_fpl, CO-6452) is tested first, and the budget figure of C.4.a and C.5 only where it fails, so an applicant eligible on the month is determined where the annualized figure cannot be. Coverage pass 6, C6-05(b) (2026-11-24): the basis (ma_needy_young_person_basis, CO-2414) is required where read, for a person under the psychiatric extended age (22) through the month before: no rule makes an unstated situation none (decision 4 of 2026-11-23), and a person in one of the H.1 situations is covered whatever her income for b, c, e, f and g; before, it was read as none, so CO-226 as a 20-year-old with the basis unstated was none, and with independent_living_after_foster_care foster_care_or_adoption. A person at or over that age in the month is none without it. Pattern sweep, MAGI (2026-11-24, PS-01, PS-02): status and the Cover All Coloradans population are read for the month evaluated (ma_meets_citizenship_requirement_in_month, CO-7551; ma_is_cover_all_coloradans_person_in_month, CO-7552; ma_meets_status_for_cover_all_coloradans_categories_in_month, CO-7553), not on the determination date: 8.100.4.G.1 (S3351), 8.100.3.E.1 (S217), 8 U.S.C. 1613(a) (S176), ix.1's 'current month' (S607). Pattern sweep, MAGI (2026-11-24, PS-06): the extension to 22 reads ma_is_in_inpatient_treatment_at_twenty_one as stated, required where read (a Psych <21 client of 21; H.1.a, S1717, gives no reading for an unstated one); the subsidized adoption exclusion of a youth in the State's responsibility at 18 keeps the rule's 'not receiving' reading. Pattern sweep, MAGI (2026-11-24, PS-01): the age at which the subsidized adoption exclusion of the State-responsibility-at-18 basis applies is taken in the month evaluated (its last day, ma_age_on_last_day_of_month, CO-5402), not on the determination date.

### CO-2430 Medicaid: is eligible for Transitional Medical Assistance `@engine`

Whether the person is eligible for Transitional Medical Assistance this month under 10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.4.I.1-3: either the person is a parent or caretaker relative who lost the Parent/Caretaker Relative category to earnings and is in the twelve months (ma_tma_parent_caretaker_is_in_transitional_period, CO-4205: three of the six months before, still an employed parent or caretaker in the household, the household still includes a dependent child), or the person is a dependent child or a Parent/Caretaker Relative of a dependent child, or received Medical Assistance in the month before the determination month, and is in the household of such a parent or caretaker (I.2, I.2.a-b: "the family's remaining months"); and the person is a Colorado resident meeting the status requirement of a Cover All Coloradans category (§ 8.100.3.G.1.g.ix.1.a lists Transitional Medical Assistance).

Precision. The family's remaining months are the months in which a member of the person's TMA household (ma_tma_household_members, CO-4204) is in the transitional period this month, read from that member's own record of the first month of ineligibility and enrollment history; nothing is restated on the child or the joining member. I.2 names "any dependent child or Parent/Caretaker Relative who was or becomes part of the Medical Assistance household"; I.2.b adds "an individual in the household who received Medical Assistance, but is no longer eligible ... based on a redetermination", read as enrolled in any Medical Assistance (ma_prior_enrollment_category other than none) in the month before the determination month. ma_magi_category (CO-551) tests TMA after the other groups, so a member who still qualifies in the Children's or another group is reported there. The dependent child is ma_is_dependent_child (CO-544); "parent or caretaker relative" is ma_caretaker_relative_of (CO-2606). Final verification pass 3, F3-4: the item had required the person to be the parent or caretaker of a dependent child, so a dependent child of the family could never be eligible, and its precision had a joining member restate the parent's month of ineligibility and history. Pattern sweep, MAGI (2026-11-24, PS-01, PS-02): status and the Cover All Coloradans population are read for the month evaluated (ma_meets_citizenship_requirement_in_month, CO-7551; ma_is_cover_all_coloradans_person_in_month, CO-7552; ma_meets_status_for_cover_all_coloradans_categories_in_month, CO-7553), not on the determination date: 8.100.4.G.1 (S3351), 8.100.3.E.1 (S217), 8 U.S.C. 1613(a) (S176), ix.1's 'current month' (S607).

### CO-2439 Medicaid: hospital presumptive eligibility category `@engine`

The group under which a qualified hospital site may find the applicant presumptively eligible under 10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.3.R, from the applicant's declarations, or none: a pregnant woman at or below ma_income_limit_pregnant_pct of the poverty level (R.2.a, once per pregnancy); a child under ma_magi_child_age_limit at or below ma_income_limit_child_pct (R.2.b); a parent or caretaker relative of a dependent child at or below ma_income_limit_parent_caretaker_pct (R.2.e); an adult ma_magi_child_age_limit to ma_adult_upper_age_limit at or below ma_income_limit_adult_pct (R.2.d); an employed applicant ma_hospital_pe_employed_disabled_min_age or older declaring a disability, own income at or below ma_wawd_income_limit_pct (R.2.f); or limited family planning, above ma_family_planning_income_lower_pct and at or below ma_family_planning_income_upper_pct (R.2.c). Outside the pregnant and child groups the applicant declares citizenship or a lawful status; is not already receiving Medical Assistance (R.8) and, except during a new pregnancy, has not had presumptive eligibility in the last 12 months (R.9). From October 1, 2026 only a citizen, national, lawful permanent resident, Cuban or Haitian entrant or COFA migrant qualifies outside the pregnant and child groups (42 U.S.C. 1396b(v)(5)). A pregnant woman and a child need not declare a status (R.2.a-b, 'unless they meet the exceptions'), and a person under 19, pregnant or postpartum (§ 8.100.3.G.1.g.ix.1) qualifies for the employed-disabled group without one (R.2.f; ix.1.b names the Buy-In for working adults with disabilities).

Precision. Groups are tested in the order listed, so a parent at or below ma_income_limit_parent_caretaker_pct is reported parent_caretaker rather than adult. "Aged 19-65" (R.1.c, R.2.d) is read as the Adults group's own range, ma_magi_child_age_limit through the end of the month the person turns 65 (ma_is_under_adult_upper_age_through_birthday_month, CO-4550; § 8.100.1, S3350): Colorado's hospital presumptive eligibility state plan page (CO-13-051-MM, S21, S3363) opens it to the "Adult Group, if covered by the state" and selects none of the "Eligibility groups for individuals age 65 and over" (OQ-513, resolved by the coverage round). R.2.c's "cannot be eligible for a Medicaid eligibility category that provides full coverage" is read through R.8 (not already receiving Medical Assistance), since a presumptive determination is made from declarations before any full determination. Every group is decided on the applicant's declarations (heavier-definitions audit H-9, H-10): household income through declared_household_income_pct_fpl (CO-3151, the declared amount and size, CO-092 and CO-3150); the limited family planning group's "counted individually as a household member of two" through CO-3152, the declared size counting the applicant as two (OQ-590); the employed-disabled group's own income through ma_declared_own_income_pct_fpl (CO-3153); and the parent or caretaker relative, guardian or conservator of a dependent child through the declaration ma_declares_parent_or_caretaker_of_dependent_child (CO-3154), not relationship edges. R.2.a, R.2.b and R.2.f except from the status declaration persons who 'meet the exceptions outlined under 8.100.3.G.1.g.viii'; the paragraph that names these categories is ix (ix.1.a: MAGI Pregnant, MAGI Children and the MAGI presumptive categories; ix.1.b: the Buy-In for Working Adults with Disabilities), so the cross-reference is read as ix, as for § 8.100.4.F.2.a-b (CO-558, CO-559; OQ-56, resolved). Every pregnant woman and every child under 19 meets ix.1; an employed applicant with a disability meets it when under 19, pregnant or within 12 months postpartum (ma_is_cover_all_coloradans_person, CO-1173). R.2.c-e (limited family planning, adults, parents and caretakers) have no exception. Coverage review 2, N-02 sweep: the child group reads ma_is_under_child_age_or_turns_nineteen_this_month (CO-564), as the adult group's upper age reads CO-4550 (F-06), so a child in the month of the 19th birthday is in the child group for that month. MAGI close-out, MAGI-SW-1 (2026-11-24): the declared household income percentage and the Children and Pregnant Women standards are per month (CO-540, CO-543, CO-3151), so this rule, a determination made on one day from the declarations, reads them in the determination month (at the determination month), whose figures are those in force on the determination date, as before.

### CO-2442 Medicaid: Express Lane status `@engine`

The Express Lane outcome for a child under 10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.4.J: not applicable (no forwarded referral, or the family did not opt in); enrolled (the child meets every eligibility requirement, judged on the income declared on the source application, ma_express_lane_child_meets_requirements, CO-3156); enrolled pending citizenship or identity verification (the same, except that verification of U.S. citizenship or identity is outstanding, giving 90 days of eligibility); the 90 days of eligibility ended with citizenship or identity still unverified (verification_period_expired, after ma_express_lane_verification_period_end_date, CO-2445); or referred to the Single Streamlined Application (the child does not satisfy a requirement, J.1.a.vi, J.2.a.vi).

Precision. J.1.a.v and J.2.a.v ("Eligibility is based on income declared on the [source] application as well as eligibility requirements outlined in this volume", S1723, the complete § 8.100.4.J since heavier-definitions audit H-8) are read through CO-3156, which compares the source application's declared household income with the children's standard instead of building the MAGI household (audit H-7); 42 U.S.C. 1396a(e)(13)(A)(i)(I) (S2102) has a child whom the finding would make ineligible determined by regular procedures, which is the referral. Additional verification requested before automatic enrollment (J.1.a.iv, J.2.a.iv) is reported by ma_verification_status. Coverage review 2, N-05: a child who fails the Medicaid requirements but meets CHP+'s on the declared income is enrolled in CHP+ under 10 CCR 2505-3 § 180 (chp_express_lane_status, CO-4793); this item still reports the Medicaid referral (J.1.a.vi, J.2.a.vi).

### CO-2445 Medicaid: end of the Express Lane verification period `@engine`

The last day of the ma_express_lane_verification_days days of eligibility an Express Lane child receives while U.S. citizenship and identity verification is awaited (10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.4.J.1.a.iii, J.2.a.iii: "shall receive 90 days of eligibility while awaiting this verification"), the enrollment date being the first of them: the enrollment date plus 89 days.

Precision. T-9 hand check A-6, A-7 (fixed, 2026-11-23): the item was the enrollment date plus 90 days, the 91st day of eligibility when the enrollment day is the first. ### CO-2448 Medicaid: child is in a non-MAGI continuous eligibility period `@engine`

Whether this month falls inside a child's 12-month continuous eligibility period that began in the Children with Disabilities Buy-In, Pickle, Disabled Adult Child or Limited Family Planning program (10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.3.Q.2.d-g): the child is under 19 (or turns 19 this month), a Colorado resident, the month is within 11 months after the period's first month, no exception of § 8.100.3.Q.1.b ends it, and, for the Buy-In, enrollment was not discontinued for unpaid premiums (Q.2.d.i). A period that began in SSI Mandatory or long-term care continues in the MAGI Children's category (Q.2.b.i, c.i) through ma_child_is_in_continuous_eligibility_period (CO-561).

Pattern sweep, non-MAGI Medicaid (docs/reviews/pattern-sweep-nonmagi.md, P2): where a recorded period's start month is stated, the program it began in is required (ma_continuous_eligibility_program, CO-2446; § 8.100.3.Q.2-3, S1724, run the period by its program; the MAGI sweep's PS-06 for the MAGI readers); with no period recorded, an unstated program is no non-MAGI period (a period this determination would open is not one of Q.2.d-g's). Before, an unstated program was read as magi in every case, so a recorded Pickle or Buy-In period whose program was not stated was lost.

### CO-2467 Medicaid: community spouse's income `@engine`

The community spouse's own gross monthly income from sources other than the institutionalized spouse, less mandatory FICA and Medicare taxes (10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.7.R.2), read from the income of the person's spouse who does not reside in a medical institution: wages, net self-employment earnings, the unearned receipts the spousal impoverishment rules count (ma_spousal_unearned_receipts) and gambling winnings.

Precision. The institutionalized spouse's own income is left out because the group keeps only spouses not residing in a medical institution; the person evaluated is the institutionalized spouse. Income from the institutionalized spouse (the community spouse income allowance) is not among the receipts summed. Child support the community spouse receives (support for a child, the child's income) and Colorado Works or Adult Financial cash are left out as before receipt records (OQ-974); a loan, an income tax refund and VA Aid and Attendance are not income. Field-effect sweep (docs/reviews/field-sweep-snap-cash-nonmagi.md), CO-2467: the community spouse's receipts are read at their gross amount, an award's claim expenses (claim_expense) and a retroactive payment's legal fees included, since 8.100.7.R.2 (S1756) takes "the gross income less mandatory deduct ions for FICA and Medicare tax" and names no other deduction; the SSI method's 20 CFR 416.1123(b)(3), which subtracts them (ma_ssi_unearned_receipts, CO-5511), is the eligibility rule for the person's own income, not R.2's. Recorded as a state policy choice, OQ-1345. Streams are placed by their dates (FS-MA-1, through ma_spousal_unearned_receipts, CO-5531). Coverage pass 6, non-MAGI F6-10 (decision 4 of 2026-11-23: each supplied fact states once whether it is required or what its rule-given default is; readers do not invent defaults): the community spouse's withheld FICA and Medicare taxes (§ 8.100.7.R.2) are read as stated, no longer as 0 when unstated. A community spouse with no earned income in the month has no FICA or Medicare tax withheld (the taxes R.2 names are levied on earnings), so the withheld amount is asked only of a spouse with earnings. Coverage pass 7, non-MAGI F7-3 (docs/reviews/coverage7-medicaid-nonmagi.md): the community spouse is the person's spouse (a spouse edge to the person evaluated) who is not in a medical institution in the month (ma_resides_in_medical_institution_in_month, CO-7500), as ma_ltc_couple (CO-643) reads her; § 8.100.7.K.1 (S1754): "A community spouse is defined as the spouse of an institutionalized spouse". Before, the group was every person reachable over the spouse edge, the person evaluated included, not in a medical institution on the determination date, so an HCBS or PACE spouse living at home (K.2.b-c) was counted as part of the community spouse (her income, shelter and medical needs), which raised the MMMNA and the community spouse's income together and removed the increased CSRA of § 8.100.7.S (HCBS-CSRA, stored household CO-1102); and a spouse who entered a facility after a retroactive month was not the community spouse of that month although CO-643 read her as one.

### CO-2469 Medicaid: family members for the family allowance `@engine`

The family members for whom an institutionalized spouse's income provides a family allowance (10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.7.T.1.c.ii): persons who are a child or parent of either spouse, reside with the community spouse, and are claimed as a tax dependent by either spouse.

Precision. Living with the community spouse is read from the family member's lives_with (CO-1925): the group must contain a spouse of the person who does not reside in a medical institution (dual-entry audit 1.4; ma_resides_with_community_spouse, CO-2468, retired). (Until the pattern sweep: if lives_with was not stated, Medicaid read the family member as not living with the community spouse.) A sibling of either spouse, whom T.1.c.ii also names, is a child of a parent of either spouse who is not a spouse: siblings are derived from shared parents (same-word audit SW-2), so the case states the spouse's parent and the sibling's parent edge, not a sibling edge (OQ-95 resolved). A half sibling (one shared parent) is a sibling; a step-sibling is not. The spouses themselves are not children or parents of either spouse, so they are never in the group. Pattern sweep, non-MAGI Medicaid (docs/reviews/pattern-sweep-nonmagi.md, P2): living with the community spouse is read as stated, required where read (decision 4 of 2026-11-23; convention rule 17): no rule on file gives a family member whose home is not stated a home apart from the community spouse, and T.1.c.ii (S1736) allows the family allowance for family members who 'reside with the community spouse'.

Type group of persons, scope person, program Medicaid.
Uses: `lives_with`, `relationships`, `resides_in_medical_institution`.

```
all persons in every person in the case such that
  all of the following are true:
    - any of the following is true:
      - that person is a child or parent of a person in the persons joined to this person by spouse
      - all of the following are true:
        - that person is a child of a person in all persons in every person in the case such that that person is a parent of a person in the persons joined to this person by spouse
        - it is not the case that that person is in the persons joined to this person by spouse
    - that person is a tax_dependent of a person in the persons joined to this person by spouse
    - there is a person in that person's Lives with such that
      all of the following are true:
        - that person is in the persons joined to this person by spouse
        - it is not the case that that person's Resides in a medical institution
```

The part of the person's gross earned income for the month that the SSI method does not count for the SSI-related Medical Assistance groups: the student earned income exclusion of 20 CFR 416.1112(c)(3) - for a student under 22 regularly attending school, the earned income of the month up to the monthly maximum, and no more than what remains of the yearly maximum after the months of the calendar year before; the first $30 of infrequent or irregular earned income in a calendar quarter (416.1112(c)(2), ma_ssi_excluded_infrequent_earned_income, CO-4883); and wages the Census Bureau pays for temporary decennial Census work, which 10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.5.F.6.z exempts (the earnings the SSI method's earnings counting table holds exempt, ma_ssi_exempt_earned_receipts, CO-5172).

Precision. The month's exclusion is the yearly running total of each month's basis (ma_ssi_student_earned_income_exclusion_basis, CO-5174: the month's earned income, ma_ssi_gross_earned_income, up to the monthly maximum, for a student under 22) capped at the yearly maximum, less the same total through the month before (P54), so no item reads itself. The maxima are the SSA's figures for the year (CO-3379, CO-3380, D-206). § 8.100.5.H.4.d states $400 a month and $1,620 a year, the figures of 20 CFR 416.1112(c)(3) before 2002; the edition H.4.e incorporates (2012) indexes them yearly from 2002 ((c)(3)(ii)), so SSA's figures for the year govern (coverage review NM-31). Coverage pass 3 C3-11, fixed in earned-income records E1: 20 CFR 416.1112(a) (S3412) excludes first the income other Federal laws exclude and then applies the exclusions "in the order listed in paragraph (c) ... to the rest of your income". The parts are disjoint records: the exempt pay (Census wages, F.6.z; a dependent child's WIOA wages, 8.100.3.K.8.c, ma_ssi_excluded_wioa_wages, CO-5179) and then the infrequent pay ((c)(2)) are taken before the student exclusion ((c)(3)), whose basis is the earned income left after them (CO-5174), so pay already excluded no longer uses up the student exclusion's yearly maximum.

### CO-2606 Medicaid: persons of whom this person is a parent or caretaker relative `@engine`

The persons of whom this person is a parent (natural, adoptive or step, as the MAGI rules read parent, S169) or a caretaker relative: under § 8.100.1 (S1500) "a person who is related to the dependent child or any adult with whom the dependent child is living and who assumes responsibility for the dependent child's care". Read from the neutral roles parent, stepparent and has_primary_responsibility_for.

Precision. Same-word audit SW-1/SW-3 (OQ-396 resolved): the caretaker role is retired; a relative or other adult who has assumed responsibility for the child's care is stated with has_primary_responsibility_for, whether or not related, since Colorado's definition takes 42 CFR 435.4's option for any adult the child lives with (S1500, S205). A grandparent or other relative who lives with the child but has not assumed responsibility is not a caretaker relative. Whether S1500's "assumes responsibility" is met by care shared with a parent in the home, which has_primary_responsibility_for may not state, is OQ-540. Whether the person is a dependent child is tested by the reader. Same-word audit SW-7 (convention rule 17): an edge joins persons who live together (lives_with, CO-1925, from dwelling_id); where a case states no dwelling_id, whether they live together cannot be determined (C6-10 (2026-11-24): living together is read from lives_with (CO-1925) as stated, required where read (decision 4 of 2026-11-23): no text on file says the persons of one Single Streamlined Application live together unless it says otherwise (10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.4.E.1 asks for the relationship to the tax filer 'as declared on the Single Streamlined Application' and E.1.a.ii, E.1.b.ii-iv, E.1.d for living in the home; 42 CFR 435.907, D-196, says nothing of the home), so a case that states no dwelling_id cannot be determined where MAGI asks whether two persons live together; before, a stated relationship edge was read as living together (convention rule 17's fallback), which the other programs' readers still do). The parent or caretaker relative lives with the child (§ 8.100.1, S1500; 42 CFR 435.4). Coverage round (OQ-540, Medicaid half resolved): Colorado's state plan page S25 (CO-13-0045-MM1, S3362) defines the caretaker relative as "any adult with whom the child is living and who assumes primary responsibility for the dependent child's care", so the role is read as primary responsibility, as 42 CFR 435.4 says; a relative who only shares the care with a parent at home is not a caretaker relative. Pattern sweep, MAGI (2026-11-24, PS-04): per month since the sweep, reading the persons living in the home in the month (ma_lives_with_in_month, CO-7554), so a child who died before a month is not a child the person lives with in it (8.100.4.G.3, S3351); its readers are month-scoped, and ma_is_parent_or_caretaker_relative_of_dependent_child (CO-2869) reads it for the determination month.

Type group of persons, scope person-month, program Medicaid.
Uses: `ma_lives_with_in_month`, `relationships`.

```
all persons in every person in the case such that
  all of the following are true:
    - this person is a parent or stepparent or has_primary_responsibility_for of that person
    - that person is in Medicaid: the persons living with the person in the month
```

### CO-2802 Medicaid: community spouse's shelter costs `@engine`

The community spouse's monthly shelter expenses for the excess shelter allowance of 10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.7.Q.1.b: the community spouse's own rent or mortgage (principal and interest), taxes and insurance, plus a condominium or cooperative's required maintenance fee, plus the larger of the standard utility allowance Colorado uses under 7 U.S.C. 2014(e) and the community spouse's actual verified utility expenses. ### CO-3156 Medicaid: Express Lane child meets the eligibility requirements `@engine`

Whether a child referred through Express Lane meets the eligibility requirements of 10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.4.J, judged on the income declared on the source application (J.1.a.v, J.2.a.v: "Eligibility is based on income declared on the [Free/Reduced Lunch, or Food Assistance or Colorado Works] application as well as eligibility requirements outlined in this volume"): under ma_magi_child_age_limit or turning 19 this month, a Colorado resident, and declared household income within the children's standard, with the 5% disregard where the children's standard is the child's highest (§ 8.100.4.D.1.a, as the Children category applies it).

Precision. The income is the source application's declared household income and size (declared_household_income_pct_fpl, CO-3151), not the MAGI household and income the full determination builds: the source application collects no tax-filing or dependency facts, and J.1.a.v and J.2.a.v make the declared income the basis. Citizenship and immigration status are not a condition here: every child under 19 is in the Cover All Coloradans population (§ 8.100.3.G.1.g.ix.1, S607; ma_magi_is_fully_eligible, CO-562, reads the same), and J.1.a.iii and J.2.a.iii's citizenship and identity verification is reported by ma_express_lane_status (CO-2442). The institution for mental diseases exclusion (§ 8.100.3.G.1.c) reaches no one under its minimum age (ma_imd_exclusion_min_age, 21). Coverage pass 5, C5-16 (2026-11-23): the general requirements of § 8.100.3.G.1.b-c are not tested here, by their own terms: the institution for mental diseases exclusion (G.1.c) reaches no one under 21, and an inmate of a public institution "may be enrolled, if eligible, with benefits limited to" an inpatient stay and reentry services (G.1.b.ii, S3361): incarceration limits the benefits, not the enrollment J.1.a.ii and J.2.a.ii provide, so an inmate child referred through Express Lane is enrolled, and the limit is reported where every child's is, by ma_magi_eligibility_status (CO-554, incarceration_limited), from the child's regular determination.

### CO-3157 Medicaid and CHP+: verification applies to the person `@engine`

Whether coverage is requested for the person, so that verification of the person's own eligibility elements (citizenship and identity, immigration status, residency, age) applies: Medical Assistance is requested (ma_is_requesting_coverage) or CHP+ is (chp_is_requesting_coverage), since CHP+ reads the same per-element items. A person who only appears on the application owes none of those documents (10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.3.H.1 and G.2, a person who declares citizenship or a status; § 8.100.3.I.1, "does not apply to those individuals who are not requesting Medical Assistance yet appear on the application"; 42 CFR 435.907(e)(1), only the information necessary to make an eligibility determination).

Precision. Not a gate on the elements that enter another person's determination: earned and unearned income (the member's income counts in an applicant's MAGI household), resources and real property (a spouse's resources count for an aged, blind or disabled applicant), pregnancy (a pregnant member enlarges every household member's MAGI household, § 8.100.4.E.2) and household composition stay owed for a non-requesting member. The long-term care elements already read ma_is_long_term_care_applicant. Unlike ma_verification_status (CO-1415), which reports not_applicable from the Medical Assistance request alone, this counts a CHP+-only request, because CHP+'s verification status reads these elements.

### CO-3601 Medicaid: is pregnant in the month `@engine`

Whether the person was pregnant at some time in the month, the condition of the Pregnant Women MAGI category (10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.4.G.5) for that month. Never a month before the month the pregnancy began, where pregnancy_start_date is stated. Otherwise: for the determination month and later months, and the months from the application month on, the person's current pregnancy (is_pregnant), never in or before the month a recorded earlier pregnancy ended (most_recent_pregnancy_end_date, CO-7400: the current pregnancy began after it), and for a month before the determination month that is after such an end only where the end is before the application month or the pregnancy's start is stated; for an earlier month, a retroactive month under § 8.100.3.E, a month from the month the pregnancy began; for a pregnancy that has ended (most_recent_pregnancy_end_date, CO-7400: the stated end, or the date of birth of the child of the case she gave birth to), the month it ended and the months from the month it began through it; and, for a person not pregnant now who states the start of a pregnancy but no end, the months from its start cannot be determined. A month in which a recorded pregnancy ended (pregnancy_ended_in_month, CO-7841) is a pregnant month. A month on or before a recorded end (pregnancy_ended_on_or_after_month, CO-7773) is read from the ended pregnancy, not from the current one: a month after every recorded end before the most recent end's month is of the pregnancy that ended most recently, pregnant from the month it began (pregnancy_start_date where stated on or before that end, else, for a person pregnant now, previous_pregnancy_start_date, CO-7840); a month on or before an earlier end, other than the month of an end, cannot be determined (no fact states an earlier pregnancy's start).

Precision. MAGI close-out, KL-MAGI-2 (2026-11-24; docs/reviews/known-limits.md): a stated pregnancy_start_date governs only the months after the last recorded end before it. Pregnancies do not overlap, so a month on or before a recorded end (CO-7773) belongs to an ended pregnancy, never to the current one: the month of a recorded end is a pregnant month (CO-7841; its last day is in it); a month after the month of every recorded end before the most recent end's month (latest_pregnancy_end_date_before_month, CO-7772, at that month) is of the pregnancy that ended most recently, pregnant from the month it began: its start is pregnancy_start_date where that is on or before the end (CO-3600: for a pregnancy that has ended, the date it began), otherwise, for a person pregnant now, whose pregnancy_start_date is the current pregnancy's, previous_pregnancy_start_date (CO-7840), required where read (decision 4 of 2026-11-23); a month on or before an earlier end that is not itself the month of an end cannot be determined. The months after every recorded end are read as before. Before, a stated start of the current pregnancy made every month before it not pregnant, the months of an earlier pregnancy and its birth month included (CO-1123 with March to August 2025 recorded as other Medical Assistance and the current start 2026-10-05 stated: March to September 2025 not pregnant, so no period opened from them, though she gave birth on 2025-09-10). Ends in the same month are one end for the span: twins born on two days are one pregnancy. Coverage pass 7, C7-02 (2026-11-24): the current pregnancy (is_pregnant) began after the last recorded end of an earlier pregnancy, so it is not read in or before that end's month; and where an earlier pregnancy ended after the application month (a renewal, whose application date is the original application's, CO-088), the months between that end and the determination month are of the current pregnancy only from its stated start: with no start stated they cannot be determined (decision 4 of 2026-11-23). Before, every month from the application month on was a month of the current pregnancy, so a postpartum month of the first pregnancy the history records as Pregnant Women opened a coverage period for the second (PG-SECOND without pregnancy_start_date). A month counts if the person was pregnant on any day of it, so the month of a birth is a pregnant month, as coverage under § 8.100.4.G.1 is for whole months; the month a pregnancy ended is a pregnant month whether or not its start is stated (the end date is the last day of the pregnancy). A current pregnancy is not dated for the determination month and later months, nor for the months from the application month on: is_pregnant answers for them where no start date is stated. For a retroactive month the dates decide; the start date is read only when the month is not settled otherwise, and an unstated start date leaves such a month unknown, not silently pregnant or not. § 8.100.3.E.2 (S2411): 'An applicant does not have to be eligible in the month of application to be eligible for retroactive Medical Assistance'. Coverage pass 6 (2026-11-24): C6-06, a stated pregnancy_start_date governs the months before it whatever is_pregnant says (§ 8.100.4.G.1: eligibility in a month is judged on that month's facts; before, a pregnancy that began after the application month was read as a pregnancy in the application month, PG-STARTS-LATER: applied 2026-09-20, pregnant from 2026-10-12, $2,200; September was read as size 2, 2,200 / 1,803.33 = 122.0%, eligible, and is size 1, 2,200 / 1,330 = 165.4%, less 5 = 160.4% > 133%, ineligible_income). C6-03, an ended pregnancy is read from most_recent_pregnancy_end_date (CO-7400), so a birth recorded by the child's date of birth and the gave_birth_to relationship ends the pregnancy without a separate pregnancy_end_date; a person not pregnant now (is_pregnant false) who states a pregnancy_start_date and no end, with no birth recorded, cannot be determined for the months from its start (the end is the missing fact); with neither a start nor an end stated nor a birth recorded she is read as having no ended pregnancy, the reading pregnancy_end_date (CO-089) states.

Type yes/no, scope person-month, program Medicaid.
Uses: `is_pregnant`, `latest_pregnancy_end_date_before_month`, `ma_application_date`, `most_recent_pregnancy_end_date`, `pregnancy_end_date`, `pregnancy_ended_before_month`, `pregnancy_ended_in_month`, `pregnancy_ended_on_or_after_month`, `pregnancy_start_date`, `previous_pregnancy_start_date`.

### CO-3616 Medicaid: income available for the patient payment after the personal needs allowance `@engine`

A Long-Term Care institution resident's income left for the patient payment after the personal needs allowance (ma_personal_needs_allowance, CO-1987) and the earned income reserve, before the other deductions (10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.7.T.1.a, V.3.b.ii.1, V.3.d.iii, V.3.f): the unearned income less the allowance, plus the countable earned income - the earned income less any part of the allowance the unearned income could not meet, less ma_ltc_earned_income_reserve_base, times ma_ltc_earned_income_reserve_rate. For a person with an income trust, the trust's monthly distribution (ma_income_trust_distribution, CO-2238) less the allowance.

Precision. Earned income is the resident's gross earned income as the SSI method counts it (ma_ssi_gross_earned_income, CO-5171): every earned income of a Long-Term Care institution resident is read as coming from an income-producing activity of § 8.100.7.V.3.e (sheltered work, protected employment, vocational rehabilitation, employment training, work within the facility), since a resident's earnings come from such an activity in practice and no fact separates them (earned-income records, step E1: ma_ltc_earned_income, CO-3615, which held that reading and had become the same figure, is removed). V.3.f.i reserves the personal needs allowance from earned income only when unearned income cannot meet it, and V.3.f.iii computes the additional reserve on the total gross earned income when the allowance comes from unearned income; so the part of the allowance unearned income leaves unmet is taken from earned income first, and the $65 and one-half are then applied to the rest. SSI paid to an institutionalized person is not in ma_ltc_gross_income (CO-641), which § 8.100.7.V.3.i.ii requires. For a trust user the distribution is the income the rule names (OQ-96), and no earned income reserve is applied to it. Each part is floored at zero. Blocked (OQ-1060): the personal needs allowance it deducts (CO-1987, CO-887) rests on S1228, which is not a quotation. HCPF Operational Memo OM 25-073 (D-125), the only document that states them, could not be fetched on 2026-11-23 (hcpf.colorado.gov refused, HTTP 403; medicaid.gov, sos.state.co.us, ecfr.gov, law.cornell.edu, govinfo.gov and federalregister.gov answered but state no Colorado figure), so the item stays Draft until the memo is stored and the excerpt replaced by its quotation.

```
otherwise (the greater of 0 and ((the greater of 0 and (Medicaid: LTC gross income minus Medicaid SSI method: a person's gross earned income)) minus Medicaid: personal needs allowance)) plus (the greater of 0 and (((Medicaid SSI method: a person's gross earned income minus (the greater of 0 and (Medicaid: personal needs allowance minus (the greater of 0 and (Medicaid: LTC gross income minus Medicaid SSI method: a person's gross earned income))))) minus Patient payment: earned income reserve base (65)) times Patient payment: earned income reserve rate (0.5)))
```

### CO-3618 Medicaid: Home Maintenance Allowance `@engine`

The amount reserved from a Long-Term Care institution resident's income for the upkeep of the resident's home (10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.7.V.3.g.ii): for a resident with no family at home whom a physician has certified as likely to return home (ma_physician_certified_return_home), in the month of entry (institution_entry_date) and the following months up to ma_home_maintenance_allowance_max_months in all, the home's actual verified shelter expenses (verified: shelter_costs_verification_document_received) - the rent or mortgage, taxes and insurance the resident pays (shelter_cost_monthly), a condominium or cooperative fee (housing_maintenance_fee), and utilities at the lesser of the standard utility allowance and the actual verified utility expenses - up to ma_home_maintenance_allowance_max; otherwise 0.

Precision. V.3.g.ii: the deduction 'must be based on actual and verified shelter expenses', and utilities are 'actual, verified': until the shelter and utility costs are verified (shelter_costs_verification_document_received, CO-1324) no allowance is reserved; the verification is read only for a resident who otherwise qualifies. 'No family at home' is read as no spouse in the community (ma_ltc_couple false; a community spouse is provided for by the spousal rules of V.3.g.i) and no relative of the resident living in the home the resident usually lives in (lives_with, is_related_to). The six months are counted from the month the resident entered the institution. The standard utility allowance is the SNAP allowance the resident's home reaches (snap_utility_allowance_amount, CO-1500), as the community spouse's excess shelter allowance reads it (CO-2802); it is read only when the resident has actual utility expenses, since the lesser of the two is then never more than those expenses. Final verification pass 3, P3-4: "no family at home" (V.3.g.ii) is read from lives_with, the persons who share the resident's dwelling_id, so the case states the resident's dwelling_id as the home the allowance keeps up, not the facility (a facility dwelling would read no family at home whatever the family's situation); the six months are counted from institution_entry_date, the month of admission, which the text does not fix: counted from Long-Term Care eligibility they would end later for a resident admitted before becoming eligible, the same choice OQ-721 records for the Part B premium months, and the volume takes the admission reading for both. Coverage pass 6, non-MAGI F6-10 (decision 4 of 2026-11-23: each supplied fact states once whether it is required or what its rule-given default is; readers do not invent defaults): the maintenance fee is read as stated, no longer as 0 when unstated; the physician's certification and the actual utility expenses keep the defaults their facts declare (V.3.g.ii; Q.1.b.ii).

### CO-3619 Medicaid: community spouse's approved medical expenses and premiums `@engine`

The additional amount 10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.7.Q.2 adds to the community spouse's minimum monthly needs: the documented medical and remedial care expenses not paid by a third party (medical_expenses_out_of_pocket, counted once that person's medical expenses are documented: medical_expenses_verification_document_received) and the Medicare, Long-Term Care insurance and health insurance premiums (health_insurance_premiums_paid) of the community spouse and of each dependent family member living with the community spouse (ma_family_allowance_members, CO-2469), read from those persons' facts.

Precision. The person evaluated is the institutionalized spouse; the community spouse is the spouse who does not reside in a medical institution, as in ma_community_spouse_income (CO-2467). medical_expenses_out_of_pocket already excludes expenses reimbursed by insurance or another third party (Q.2.a.ii); Q.2.a: 'Each medical or remedial care expense claimed for deduction must be documented'; a person's expenses count only once the agency has received the documents (medical_expenses_verification_document_received, CO-1326), and the documentation's content (service, date, amount, provider) and Q.2.a.i's licensed practitioner are the eligibility site's check of the documents. Q.2.b's premiums carry no documentation sentence and are read as stated. Q.4's cap applies to the MMMNA and the excess shelter allowance only, so this amount is added after the cap (ma_mmmna, CO-655). Coverage pass 7, non-MAGI F7-3 (docs/reviews/coverage7-medicaid-nonmagi.md): the community spouse is the person's spouse (a spouse edge to the person evaluated) who is not in a medical institution in the month (ma_resides_in_medical_institution_in_month, CO-7500), as ma_ltc_couple (CO-643) reads her; § 8.100.7.K.1 (S1754): "A community spouse is defined as the spouse of an institutionalized spouse". ### CO-3626 Medicaid: SSI-method couple `@engine`

The person and, where the person lives with a spouse (or a person held out as a spouse) and neither is excluded from the other's SSI household, that spouse: the persons whose income and resources an SSI-related, Old Age Pension or Medicare Savings Program determination counts together (10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.5.H.1.a, 8.100.6.L.3). An institutionalized spouse in the institution is counted alone from the month of admission, because no income of the community spouse is deemed to that spouse (42 U.S.C. 1396r-5(b)(1); § 8.100.7.C.1, C.2.c); the community spouse keeps the couple until the month after admission (§ 8.100.7.C.2.b). Spouses who live apart for any other reason are counted together through the month they ceased to live together and each alone from the month after (§ 8.100.7.C.2.b; § 8.100.5.H.1.a: "Income of spouses living together is considered mutually available").

Precision. The same group ma_ssi_household_size (CO-604) counts and the SSI countable income items sum over. The walk is directional (docs/operators.md, reachable): the edge from an institutionalized spouse in the institution (ma_is_institutionalized_spouse_in_institution, CO-5200) to the community spouse is not crossed, while the edge from the community spouse to the newly admitted spouse is crossed through the admission month. So in the admission month the community spouse's couple is both spouses and the institutionalized spouse's is the person alone; from the month after, each is alone (ma_excluded_from_ssi_household, CO-661). Coverage pass 4, non-MAGI N4-7: per month: who is excluded from the other's household and who is an institutionalized spouse in the institution are taken for the month evaluated (ma_excluded_from_ssi_household, CO-661; ma_is_institutionalized_spouse_in_institution, CO-5200), so a retroactive month before an admission keeps the couple together and the admission month and after split it as 8.100.7.C.2.b and 42 U.S.C. 1396r-5(b)(1) say; before, every month read the couple as it stood on the determination date. Coverage pass 6, non-MAGI F6-1 (docs/reviews/coverage6-medicaid-nonmagi.md): an edge is crossed only while the two live together (lives_with, CO-1925: the same dwelling_id) or in a month not after the month they ceased to (§ 8.100.7.C.2.b, S1759). The date is ceased_living_with_spouse_date (CO-7352), stated on either spouse, or, where one of them lives in a facility (residence_setting_type other than private_dwelling: a nursing facility, an assisted living residence), that one's institution_entry_date; with the two in different homes and no date it cannot be determined (decision 4). (Until the pattern sweep, a case that stated no dwelling_id for them read the edge as living together.) Before, the spouse edge was crossed whatever the spouses' homes, so a separated couple, or a spouse in an assisted living residence on a waiver, stayed one SSI household (SEPARATED, CO-903; SEPARATED-QMB, CO-904; ACF-SPOUSE, CO-905). An institutionalized spouse in the institution keeps the directional rule above (42 U.S.C. 1396r-5(b)(1)), which takes effect from the admission month. Pattern sweep, non-MAGI Medicaid (docs/reviews/pattern-sweep-nonmagi.md, P2, P3): whether the spouse lives with the person in the month is ma_ssi_lives_with_in_month (CO-7505), which keeps F6-1's dates and adds the spouse's death: a spouse who died is in the couple through the month of death and not after (20 CFR 416.1163(f)(4), S5121; § 8.100.7.C.2.b). Living together is read as stated, required where read (decision 4 of 2026-11-23; convention rule 17): no text on file says the persons of one application live together unless it says otherwise (§ 8.100.5.H.1.a, S1746, counts only 'spouses living together').

Type group of persons, scope person-month, program Medicaid.
Uses: `ma_excluded_from_ssi_household`, `ma_is_institutionalized_spouse_in_institution`, `ma_ssi_lives_with_in_month`, `relationships`.

```
the persons joined to this person by spouse or holds_out_as_spouse_with, crossing an edge only where
  all of the following are true:

    - it is not the case that that person's Medicaid: excluded from SSI-related household by institutionalization
```

The income a Medicare Savings Program member keeps disregarded after the annual Social Security cost-of-living adjustment (ma_title_ii_cola_increase): for a QMB or QI-1 member, from January until the year's federal poverty guidelines are published (10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.6.L.12, N.6), and for an SLMB member through the month following the month in which they are published (M.7); otherwise 0. The member is the person enrolled in the program in the December before the month (ma_msp_december_category).

Precision. The disregard is subtracted from countable income only in the test of the program the person was a member of (CO-613, CO-614, CO-615), so it keeps the member in that program and moves no one into another. The months run from January of the month's year: the publication date read is the version in force on January 1 of that year. OQ-515 dates the guidelines themselves from January 1, so in the volume the new limits apply from January; the disregard then matters only where the adjustment still raises income over the new limit.

Type money, scope person-month, program Medicaid.
Uses: `federal_poverty_guideline_publication_date`, `ma_msp_december_category`, `ma_title_ii_cola_increase`.

```
if it is not the case that Medicaid: Medicare Savings Program category in the December before the month is one of: qmb, slmb, qi
  then 0
else if any of the following is true:
    - the calendar year of Federal poverty guidelines: publication date (2026-01-15) as of the first day of the most recent month number 1 on or before the month is less than the calendar year of the month
    - the month is at most (if Medicaid: Medicare Savings Program category in the December before the month is equal to slmb;   then the month after the month containing Federal poverty guidelines: publication date (2026-01-15) as of the first day of the most recent month number 1 on or before the month; otherwise the month containing Federal poverty guidelines: publication date (2026-01-15) as of the first day of the most recent month number 1 on or before the month)
  then Medicaid: Title II cost-of-living increase
otherwise 0
```

### CO-3633 Medicaid: persons whose income the determination verifies `@engine`

The persons whose earned and unearned income enters this person's Medical Assistance determination, so that its verification is owed for this person: for an aged, blind or disabled person, the SSI-method couple (ma_ssi_couple_members, CO-3626: the person and a spouse living with the person); for anyone else, the person's MAGI household (ma_magi_household_members). The person is always one of them.

Precision. An aged, blind or disabled person under 65 may also be tested under a MAGI group whose household holds members other than a spouse; their income enters only that test and is verified for them as members of their own households. Whether each member's income needs documents is that member's own element (ma_requires_verification_of_earned_income, ma_requires_verification_of_unearned_income), which is not gated on the member's request (ma_verification_is_applicable, CO-3157).

Type group of persons, scope person-month, program Medicaid.
Uses: `ma_is_aged_blind_or_disabled`, `ma_magi_household_members`, `ma_ssi_couple_members`.

```
if Medicaid: is aged, blind, or disabled
  then Medicaid: SSI-method couple
otherwise Medicaid: MAGI household members
```

### CO-4101 Medicaid: month is before any MAGI coverage can begin `@engine`

Whether the month is one in which the person cannot have MAGI Medical Assistance coverage from the application being determined: a month before the month of the person's birth, or a month before the month of application (ma_application_date) that is not a retroactive coverage month - no retroactive coverage was requested (ma_retroactive_coverage_requested, CO-4100), or the month is before the first month of the retroactive period (ma_retroactive_coverage_start_month, CO-557) (10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.3.E.1-2; 42 CFR 435.915(a); 42 U.S.C. 1396a(a)(34) as Pub. L. 119-21 sec. 71112 amended it). A month before the widest window the application date allows (three months before an application made before ma_retroactive_coverage_change_date, then the longer of the expansion adult's and everyone else's window) is before coverage whatever the window's length; a month inside every window the date allows is not; a month between the two is decided by the window's length, unknown where that is not known. A month inside the window is a retroactive month, and whether the person is covered in it is decided by that month's own facts.

Precision. Coverage pass 7, C7-01 and C7-08 (2026-11-24): the window's first month (CO-557) no longer reads a supplied date the person became eligible (ma_eligibility_start_date, retired): 42 CFR 435.915(a)(2) (S218) covers a retroactive month in which the person 'Would have been eligible for Medicaid at the time he received the services', and 42 U.S.C. 1396a(a)(34) as amended (S1706) one in which the person 'was (or upon application would have been) eligible for such assistance at the time such care and services were furnished', so E.1's 'as of the date the person became eligible ... whichever is later' is the first month whose own facts make the person eligible, which ma_magi_eligibility_status (CO-554) decides month by month. And an unknown window length no longer reads as covered: before, with the start date not stated (CO-557 unknown) every requested month was read as covered (RETRO-NOSTART: application 2026-11-02, April to July eligible; by hand before the August to October window), and from 2027 a month the shortened window excludes was covered where the category of the application month, and so the window's length (CO-2472), was not known (RETRO-2027-UNKNOWN: application 2027-01-15, September and October 2026 eligible; by hand before any window, November unknown). Coverage pass 7, C7-10: a date of birth not stated leaves the month unknown (was: not before birth; decision 4 of 2026-11-23). Coverage pass 6, C6-05(c) (2026-11-24): with no application date stated, a month before the determination month cannot be determined (whether the application reaches it is not known; decision 4 of 2026-11-23), and the determination month and later months are not before coverage; before, every past month was read as covered, as a screening does, so CO-226 at $1,000 without an application date was eligible in March 2026 (75.2%). A month a continuous eligibility or pregnancy coverage period covers is never before the application without being a requested retroactive month, so the order in ma_magi_eligibility_status (CO-554), which tests this first, takes nothing from those periods. The retroactive period's length is the one CO-557 states (three months for an application before 2027; then one for an expansion adult and two for anyone else).

Type yes/no, scope person-month, program Medicaid.
Uses: `date_of_birth`, `ma_application_date`, `ma_retroactive_coverage_change_date`, `ma_retroactive_coverage_months`, `ma_retroactive_coverage_months_expansion_adult`, `ma_retroactive_coverage_months_other_after_change`, `ma_retroactive_coverage_requested`, `ma_retroactive_coverage_start_month`.

```
any of the following is true:
  - the month is less than the month containing Date of birth
  - if Medicaid: application date is unknown
    then (if the month is at least the month containing the Determination Date;   then no; otherwise the month is less than the month containing Medicaid: application date)
  otherwise (all of the following are true:;   - the month is less than the month containing Medicaid: application date;   - any of the following is true:;     - it is not the case that Retroactive Medical Assistance coverage requested, otherwise no;     - the month is less than (if Medicaid: application date is less than Medicaid: first application date under the shorter retroactive periods (2027-01-01);   then Retroactive Medical Assistance coverage period, months (3); otherwise the greater of Medicaid: retroactive months for an expansion adult from 2027 (1) and Medicaid: retroactive months for other applicants from 2027 (2)) months before the month containing Medicaid: application date;     - all of the following are true:;       - the month is less than (if Medicaid: application date is less than Medicaid: first application date under the shorter retroactive periods (2027-01-01);   then Retroactive Medical Assistance coverage period, months (3); otherwise the lesser of Medicaid: retroactive months for an expansion adult from 2027 (1) and Medicaid: retroactive months for other applicants from 2027 (2)) months before the month containing Medicaid: application date;       - the month is less than Medicaid: retroactive coverage start month)
```

### CO-4103 Medicaid: VA Aid and Attendance is used as patient payment `@engine`

Whether the portion of the person's VA pension for Aid and Attendance and Unusual Medical Expenses (ma_va_aid_and_attendance_receipts) is used as patient payment to the medical facility, under 10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.5.K.2: the person receives that portion (a receipt of kind va_aid_and_attendance in the month), lives in a State Veterans Home (resides_in_state_veterans_home) and has no dependents - is not married and has no child who is a dependent child under the Medical Assistance rules (ma_is_dependent_child). Otherwise (K.1.a-b) the portion is not used as patient payment.

Precision. K speaks only of 'a veteran or surviving spouse of a veteran': K.1.a, K.1.b and K.2 together cover every such person in a medical facility, so the rule treats a recipient of the pension's A&A or UME portion as one, and the volume reads no separate veteran or surviving-spouse fact. Eligibility is unchanged: K's lead-in excludes the portion from income 'when determining eligibility', which ma_ltc_gross_income (CO-641) does in every case; this item only decides whether ma_patient_payment (CO-658) adds the portion back. Pattern sweep, non-MAGI Medicaid (docs/reviews/pattern-sweep-nonmagi.md, P2, P3): whether the person is married is read from a spouse of the case or the marital status as stated, required where read (decision 4 of 2026-11-23); before, is_married (CO-930) read a person with neither stated as not married.

Type yes/no, scope person-month, program Medicaid.
Uses: `ma_is_dependent_child`, `ma_va_aid_and_attendance_receipts`, `marital_status`, `relationships`, `resides_in_state_veterans_home`.

```
all of the following are true:
  - Medicaid: VA Aid and Attendance received in the month is more than 0
  - Resides in a State Veterans Home
  - it is not the case that (any of the following is true:;   - (there is a person of whom this person is a spouse such that;   yes), otherwise no;   - Marital status is equal to married)
  - it is not the case that (there is a person in all persons in every person in the case such that this person is a parent of that person such that;   that person's Medicaid: is a dependent child)
```

### CO-4200 Medicaid: Children with Disabilities Buy-In household earned income `@engine`

The gross earned income for the month of the child's Children with Disabilities Buy-In household - the MAGI household of 10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.4.E (ma_magi_household_members, § 8.100.6.Q.1.b.i) - counted under § 8.100.5.F (Q.1.b.ii): each member's wages and net earnings from self-employment (§ 8.100.5.F.4.a-b), less, for a blind or disabled child of the Buy-In's age who is a student regularly attending school, the student earned income exemption (§ 8.100.5.H.4.d, ma_ssi_excluded_earned_income).

Precision. Every member of the MAGI household counts, not only the members whose income MAGI's tax-dependent rule (§ 8.100.4.C.1.f; 42 CFR 435.603(d)(2)) would count: Q.1.b takes from § 8.100.4 only the household (E), and the income rules from § 8.100.5.F (OQ-740). Net earnings from self-employment are the non-MAGI figure (ma_self_employment_net_earnings, CO-1704). The student exemption is the one the SSI-related groups apply (ma_ssi_excluded_earned_income, CO-2471, with SSA's figures for the year), read for a member who is ma_cbwd_max_age or younger and meets the SSA disability criteria or is blind. An unstated exemption is 0. Coverage pass 3 C3-8: the infrequent or irregular earned income exclusion (ma_ssi_excluded_infrequent_earned_income, CO-4883; 20 CFR 416.1112(c)(2)) and decennial Census wages (§ 8.100.5.F.6.z) apply to any earner, so they come off every member's earnings; a blind or disabled child of the Buy-In's age takes the whole of CO-2471, which holds both and the student exclusion. Coverage pass 4, non-MAGI N4-9 (docs/operators.md, "Ages in a month"): the age is taken in the month evaluated, not on the determination date: an "under N" test on the first day of the month (ma_age_on_first_day_of_month, CO-4978), an "N or older" test on the last day (ma_age_on_last_day_of_month, CO-5402), and a test that excludes the person from what is favorable on the other day. Coverage pass 4, non-MAGI N4-13 (decision 4 of 2026-11-23: missing information is cannot determine unless the rule says otherwise; readers do not invent defaults): a member's blindness and disability (the SSA's or the Department's finding, 8.100.6.B) are read as stated for every member, no longer as no for a member whose finding is unstated. Pattern sweep, non-MAGI Medicaid (docs/reviews/pattern-sweep-nonmagi.md, P2): the SSI method's excluded earned income (ma_ssi_excluded_earned_income, CO-2471; the infrequent part, CO-4883) and in-kind support and maintenance (ssi_in_kind_support_and_maintenance, CO-802) are read as computed, required where read (decision 4 of 2026-11-23): they are unknown only where a fact they rest on is not stated (a student's school attendance, the shelter costs others pay), and no rule reads that as none; before, an unknown figure was read as 0.

Type money, scope person-month, program Medicaid.

### CO-4201 Medicaid: Children with Disabilities Buy-In household unearned income `@engine`

The gross unearned income for the month of the child's Children with Disabilities Buy-In household (the MAGI household, ma_magi_household_members, 10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.6.Q.1.b.i) counted under § 8.100.5.F (Q.1.b.ii-iii): each member's unearned receipts the SSI method counts (ma_ssi_unearned_receipts: Social Security, pensions, unemployment and the other kinds the SSI method's counting table counts, less what it exempts), lottery and gambling winnings in the month received, child support received (ma_ssi_child_support_receipts), and, for a member who is not an unemancipated child, in-kind support and maintenance (§ 8.100.5.F.5, H.1.b); child support received by a blind or disabled child of the Buy-In's age is reduced by one third (§ 8.100.5.H.4.c).

Precision. SSI, OAP, General Assistance and TANF cash are exempt (§ 8.100.5.F.6.y) and are not read. Child support is stated on the child for whom it is paid (child_support_received). The one-third reduction is read for every member who could be an applicant or recipient child (ma_cbwd_max_age or younger, meeting the SSA disability criteria or blind), so two disabled siblings have the same household figure. Lottery and gambling winnings count in the month received (§ 8.100.5.F.4-5, F.5.i); the hardship exemption of F.5.i.1, once granted to the child (ma_lottery_winnings_hardship_exemption_granted), removes them. Unstated in-kind support is 0; the receipts state each member's money once (unstated receipts cannot determine). Every member of the MAGI household counts (OQ-740). Subsidized adoption funds (a receipt of kind adoption_subsidy, received by the adoptive parent, which the SSI method's counting table exempts, so ma_ssi_unearned_receipts does not hold it; before receipt records migration phase 3, adoption_subsidy_received was subtracted here) are exempt: § 8.100.5.F.6.t excludes the child receiving them from the budget unit and exempts "his income", and Q.1.b.iii applies F.6 to the Buy-In household. F.6.t's "unless such exclusion results in ineligibility for the other members of the household" concerns the budget unit of a household whose other members apply; the Buy-In household's income is figured for the disabled child alone, so it is not read. Coverage pass 4, non-MAGI N4-9 (docs/operators.md, "Ages in a month"): the age is taken in the month evaluated, not on the determination date: an "under N" test on the first day of the month (ma_age_on_first_day_of_month, CO-4978), an "N or older" test on the last day (ma_age_on_last_day_of_month, CO-5402), and a test that excludes the person from what is favorable on the other day. Coverage pass 4, non-MAGI N4-13 (decision 4 of 2026-11-23: missing information is cannot determine unless the rule says otherwise; readers do not invent defaults): a member's blindness and disability (the SSA's or the Department's finding, 8.100.6.B) are read as stated for every member, no longer as no for a member whose finding is unstated. Pattern sweep, non-MAGI Medicaid (docs/reviews/pattern-sweep-nonmagi.md, P2): the SSI method's excluded earned income (ma_ssi_excluded_earned_income, CO-2471; the infrequent part, CO-4883) and in-kind support and maintenance (ssi_in_kind_support_and_maintenance, CO-802) are read as computed, required where read (decision 4 of 2026-11-23): they are unknown only where a fact they rest on is not stated (a student's school attendance, the shelter costs others pay), and no rule reads that as none; before, an unknown figure was read as 0.

Type money, scope person-month, program Medicaid.
Uses: `is_blind`, `ma_age_on_first_day_of_month`, `ma_cbwd_max_age`, `ma_is_ssi_unemancipated_child`, `ma_lottery_winnings_hardship_exemption_granted`, `ma_magi_household_members`, `ma_ssi_child_support_receipts`, `ma_ssi_child_support_reduction_divisor`, `ma_ssi_gambling_receipts`, `ma_ssi_unearned_receipts`, `meets_ssa_disability_criteria`, `ssi_in_kind_support_and_maintenance`.

### CO-4202 Medicaid: Children with Disabilities Buy-In countable household income `@engine`

The child's Children with Disabilities Buy-In household income for the month after the income disregards of 10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.5.H.4 (§ 8.100.6.Q.1.b.iv): the household's unearned income (ma_cbwd_household_unearned_income) less the ssi_general_income_exclusion general income disregard, plus the household's earned income (ma_cbwd_household_earned_income) less any part of that disregard unearned income did not use and the ssi_earned_income_exclusion earned income disregard, then one half.

Precision. One general and one earned income disregard are applied to the household's pooled income, as § 8.100.5.H.4.a.iii allows one $20 disregard per couple and H.4.b deducts "the first $65 of all earned income"; no Ineligible Child or Ineligible Parent allocation (H.3) is taken, since the household's size already enters the poverty-level comparison (OQ-740). The unused part of the general disregard is carried to earned income (H.4.a.ii), as ma_ssi_countable_earned_income (CO-605) and ma_wawd_countable_income (CO-1715) do.

Type money, scope person-month, program Medicaid.
Uses: `ma_cbwd_household_earned_income`, `ma_cbwd_household_unearned_income`, `ssi_earned_income_disregard_rate`, `ssi_earned_income_exclusion`, `ssi_general_income_exclusion`.

```
(the greater of 0 and (Medicaid: Children with Disabilities Buy-In household unearned income minus SSI-related general income exclusion (20))) plus ((the greater of 0 and (Medicaid: Children with Disabilities Buy-In household earned income minus (SSI-related earned income exclusion (65) plus (the greater of 0 and (SSI-related general income exclusion (20) minus Medicaid: Children with Disabilities Buy-In household unearned income))))) times SSI-related earned income disregard rate (0.5))
```

### CO-4204 Medicaid: Transitional Medical Assistance household `@engine`

The persons who share this person's Medical Assistance household for Transitional Medical Assistance (10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.4.I.2-3: "part of the Medical Assistance household", "the household must include a dependent child"): the members of the person's MAGI household (ma_magi_household_members), the persons of whom the person is a parent or caretaker relative (ma_caretaker_relative_of), and the persons who are the person's parent, stepparent or caretaker relative and live with the person.

Precision. The MAGI household alone would leave out a caretaker relative's dependent child (a grandchild the grandparent does not claim has a non-filer household of its own) and, from the child's side, that caretaker; the parent and caretaker edges are read both ways so the family the Parent/Caretaker Relative category was granted on is one household. Living together is read from lives_with (CO-1925); where a case states no dwelling_id, whether they live together cannot be determined, as ma_caretaker_relative_of (CO-2606) reads it (C6-10). Pattern sweep, MAGI (2026-11-24, PS-04): the parents living with the child are those living in the home in the month (ma_lives_with_in_month, CO-7554): a parent who died before the month does not live with the child (E.1.c.ii, S169).

Type group of persons, scope person-month, program Medicaid.
Uses: `ma_caretaker_relative_of`, `ma_lives_with_in_month`, `ma_magi_household_members`, `relationships`.

```
all persons in every person in the case such that
  any of the following is true:
    - that person is in Medicaid: MAGI household members
    - that person is in Medicaid: persons of whom this person is a parent or caretaker relative
    - all of the following are true:
      - this person is a child or stepchild or in_primary_care_of of that person
      - that person is in Medicaid: the persons living with the person in the month
```

```json
["filter",["persons"],["any",["in_group",["P"],"ma_magi_household_members"],["in_group",["P"],"ma_caretaker_relative_of"],["all",["rel",["child","stepchild","in_primary_care_of"],["P"]],["in_group",["P"],"ma_lives_with_in_month"]]]]
```

### CO-4205 Medicaid: lost the Parent/Caretaker Relative category to earnings and is in the twelve Transitional Medical Assistance months `@engine`

Whether the person is one of the individuals 10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.4.I.1 grants Transitional Medical Assistance to, this month: the person lost the Parent/Caretaker Relative category because of new or increased earnings, was in that category in at least ma_extension_prior_months_required of the ma_extension_lookback_months months before the first month of ineligibility (I.1.a), this month is one of the ma_transitional_medical_assistance_months months beginning with that month, a parent or caretaker relative in the household is still employed (I.1.b.i), and the household still includes a dependent child (I.3).

Precision. I.3's "the household must include a dependent child" is tested over the TMA household (ma_tma_household_members, CO-4204), not over the person's own caretaker relationships. The dependent child is the 42 CFR 435.4 dependent child ma_is_dependent_child (CO-544) states. The family's other members reach the remaining months through ma_is_eligible_for_transitional_medical_assistance (CO-2430, I.2), which reads this item for a member of their household; residency and status are tested there. Coverage review 2, N-07: I.3 ends Transitional Medical Assistance 'at the end of the month in which the household does not include a dependent child'. The dependent child is ma_is_dependent_child_in_month (CO-4791), so a child who turns 18 (or 19, as a student) during the month keeps the household within I.3 through the end of that month. Household membership is not dated within a month: for the month in which the last dependent child moves out, the household is stated as it stood during that month (the child still in it), and from the next month without the child, so the period ends at the end of the month the child left. Coverage pass 5, C5-17 (2026-11-23): a case that states why the person stopped being eligible (ma_ineligibility_reason) but not the first month of ineligibility cannot be determined (decision 4): the loss is recorded and its month decides the period. Where neither is stated, no loss of eligibility is recorded (ma_first_month_of_ineligibility, CO-2422, says so) and the person is not in a transitional period. Before, an unstated first month was read as no period even where the reason was stated.

### CO-4550 Medicaid: under the Adults group's upper age, through the month of that birthday `@engine`

Whether the person's 65th birthday (ma_adult_upper_age_limit) falls in the month evaluated or later - the person was under ma_adult_upper_age_limit on the last day of the month before (ma_age_before_month, CO-4790) - the upper age of the Adult MAGI Medical Assistance Group, which 10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.1 states as "from the age of 19 through the end of the month that the individual turns 65" (with § 8.100.4.G.1's whole-month rule).

Precision. Age is taken on the day before the first day of the month evaluated, the idiom of ma_is_under_child_age_or_turns_nineteen_this_month (CO-564) for the 19th birthday. A person under 65 on that day is either still under 65 on the determination date or turned 65 during the determination month; both are inside "the month that the individual turns 65". 42 CFR 435.119(b)(1) says "under age 65"; Colorado's definition and G.1 keep the person for the rest of the birthday month, and only a person who is not entitled to or enrolled in Medicare that month is affected (the Adults group excludes Medicare in both texts). Time audit T-1 (2026-11-23): measured in the month evaluated, not the determination month, so a retroactive month (42 CFR 435.915(a)(2), S218: "would have been eligible ... at the time") and an application month before the determination month read the person's age in that month; a rule about the determination itself reads it [at] the determination month.

### CO-4551 Medicaid: sponsor income deemed to a sponsored non-citizen `@engine`

The income of this sponsored non-citizen's sponsors and of the sponsors' spouses that counts to the person for the month under 10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.3.K.1 and 8 U.S.C. 1631(a)-(b): each such person's own MAGI-based income (ma_person_magi_income), for a person who is not a citizen or national, whose sponsor executed an affidavit of support (is_sponsored_non_citizen), who has fewer than federal_qualifying_quarters_threshold qualifying quarters, and who is not a pregnant woman or a child (K.1.a); none when 8 U.S.C. 1631(f)'s battered spouse and child rule applies (ma_sponsor_deeming_battery_exception_applies); and, for the federal_sponsor_deeming_exception_months after an indigence determination (8 U.S.C. 1631(e)), no more than the support the sponsors actually provide.

Precision. K.1 counts the income "to the sponsored alien": it is added to this person's own MAGI household income (ma_magi_household_income, CO-503) for this person's own determination, not to the other members' households. A sponsor or sponsor's spouse who is already a member of this person's MAGI household (a sponsoring spouse living in the home) is left out, since that income already counts. The income counted is each one's MAGI-based income for the month, the measure § 8.100.4.C applies to the household; K.1 states no allowance or deduction for the sponsor. "A child" (K.1.a) is read as the Children's group's age, under 19 through the birthday month (ma_is_under_child_age_or_turns_nineteen_this_month, CO-564), and "a pregnant woman" as a woman pregnant in the month (ma_is_pregnant_in_month, CO-3601). qualifying_quarters (CO-004) is SSA's credited total, including a spouse's or parent's quarters; quarters in which the person received a federal means-tested benefit after 1996 are the supplier's to leave out (1631(b)(2)(B)). Coverage pass 4, C4-10 (2026-11-23): a person is sponsored where the case declares a sponsor (the sponsor edge, sponsors, CO-2713) or states is_sponsored_non_citizen (CO-1573); for a non-citizen who is not exempt (fewer than the qualifying quarters, not pregnant, not a child, no battery exception), a sponsorship neither declared nor stated is unknown (decision 4); before, it was read as not sponsored, a default no rule gives, and a sponsor declared in the case with the fact unstated deemed nothing. The sponsors are persons of the case (sponsors, CO-2713; sponsor_spouses_not_cosigning, CO-2714); a sponsor who is not declared contributes nothing. Coverage pass 5, C5-06 (2026-11-23): the sponsor's income is read from the sponsor as a person of the case (sponsors, CO-2713: the sponsored_by relationship), the one place the case states it. A person who is sponsored (is_sponsored_non_citizen) and reached by the deeming, whose sponsor is not declared as a person of the case (the usual case: the sponsor lives elsewhere), has a sponsor whose income counts (K.1) and is not stated, so the deemed income is unknown (cannot determine; decision 4): the case is asked to declare the sponsor, with the sponsor's income. Before, the sum over the sponsors of the case was 0, and a sponsored lawful permanent resident with no sponsor in the case was tested on her own income alone (SPONSOR-OUT: 90.2%, adult, eligible; the affidavit of support requires the sponsor's income to be at least 125% of the guideline for the sponsor's household, so the answer is almost always ineligible). The trace names no missing fact here (no supplied fact is unstated; the sponsor is missing from the case), as for a child living with neither parent (CO-1976). Coverage pass 6, C6-05(d) (2026-11-24): during the indigence period the sponsors' support actually provided (support_received_from_sponsor, CO-4555) is required: unstated, the deemed income cannot be determined (8 U.S.C. 1631(e)(1), 'the amount actually provided'; decision 4); before, it was read as 0, so CO-817 with its sponsor in the case (wages $6,000) and an indigence determination of 2026-10-05 was 1,200 / 1,330 = 90.2%, eligible, where $800 of support makes it 2,000 / 1,330 = 150.4%, ineligible_income.

Type money, scope person-month, program Medicaid.
Uses: `federal_qualifying_quarters_threshold`, `federal_sponsor_deeming_exception_months`, `is_sponsored_non_citizen`, `is_us_citizen_or_national`, `ma_is_pregnant_in_month`, `ma_is_under_child_age_or_turns_nineteen_this_month`, `ma_magi_household_members`, `ma_person_magi_income`, `ma_sponsor_deeming_battery_exception_applies`, `ma_sponsor_indigence_determination_date`, `qualifying_quarters`, `sponsor_spouses_not_cosigning`, `sponsors`, `support_received_from_sponsor`.
