### CO-4559 Medicaid: annualized MAGI household income `@engine`

This person's MAGI household income for the month with the self-employment, seasonal and commission income of each counted member who has such earnings (ma_has_annualizable_earnings, CO-6451) annualized: that member's month income from such work (ma_annualizable_earnings_in_month, CO-7404) replaced by one twelfth of the member's expected income for the year from it (expected_annual_self_employment_seasonal_commission_income, CO-7403), the member's other income kept as the month's; the annualized figure 10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.4.C.4.a applies to an applicant found ineligible on monthly income whose household has such earnings.

Precision. C.4.a annualizes "self-employment, seasonal employment, and commission-based employment income" (S3356): coverage pass 6, C6-07 (2026-11-24), only that income is annualized; the member's other income, a lump sum among it (C.1.d.i: "counted as income only in the month received"), stays the month's. Before, the member's whole income was replaced by a twelfth of the year's expected income (expected_annual_income), which spread a lump sum over the year (SE-LUMP: a business netting $1,000 a month, a taxable lump sum of $6,000 in November, $18,000 expected for 2026: 18,000 / 12 = 1,500, 112.8%, eligible; now 7,000 - 1,000 + 12,000 / 12 = 7,000, 526.3%). Coverage pass 4, C4-05 (2026-11-23): a member with such earnings whose expected year from them is not stated, or a member whose earnings are not stated, makes the figure unknown (decision 4); every other member keeps the month's income, so the figure equals ma_magi_household_income (CO-503) when nothing is annualized; it includes the lottery spread and sponsor income CO-503 adds for this person. The year is the calendar year of the determination (OQ-810, now only the period). Not rounded (coverage pass 4, C4-13). ma_magi_household_income_pct_fpl (CO-504, through CO-4567) takes the lower of the monthly and annualized figures, which is C.4.a's order: the annualized figure is reached only when the monthly one is ineligible.

The family whose income the premium tax credit methodology counts for this person (26 CFR 1.36B-1(d)): for a tax filer, the filer, a spouse filing jointly, and the persons either claims as a tax dependent; for a claimed tax dependent, the family of the filer claiming the person. ### CO-4561 Medicaid: household income under the premium tax credit methodology, as a share of the poverty line `@engine`

This person's household income for the calendar year of the determination as the premium tax credit methodology computes it (26 CFR 1.36B-1(e)): the expected annual income (expected_annual_income) of each taxpayer in the person's premium tax credit family (ma_premium_tax_credit_family) and of each other member of the family who is required to file a return, as a fraction of the annual federal poverty guideline for the family's size in effect on the first day of the open enrollment period before that year (1.36B-1(h)).

Precision. A taxpayer is a member not claimed as another's dependent (the filer and a spouse filing jointly); a claimed member counts only where required to file (is_required_to_file_tax_return, CO-078). The guideline is the one in force on the first day of the federal_exchange_open_enrollment_start_month before the determination's calendar year (45 CFR 155.410(e): November 1 of the preceding year), so a 2026 determination reads the 2025 guidelines, unlike the MAGI ratio, which reads the guideline in force on the determination date (ma_magi_household_income_pct_fpl, CO-504; OQ-515). Unknown where a counted member's expected annual income is not stated; the C.5 test then does not apply (CO-4564). Coverage pass 5 (2026-11-23, with C5-07): for a sponsored non-citizen the deeming of 8 U.S.C. 1631(a) (S2970: "Notwithstanding any other provision of law, in determining the eligibility ... of an alien for any Federal means-tested public benefits program ..., the income and resources of the alien shall be deemed to include" the sponsor's and the sponsor's spouse's) and § 8.100.3.K.1 (S3352) apply to this figure too, since § 8.100.4.C.5 and 42 CFR 435.603(i) determine Medicaid financial eligibility on it: the year's deemed income is twelve times the determination month's (ma_sponsor_deemed_income, CO-4551, which applies K.1.a's exemptions, 1631(e) and 1631(f)), 0 for a person who is not sponsored or is exempt. Before, a sponsored person whose own year's income was below 100% was eligible under C.5 though the deeming put her over every standard (CO-183, once its year's income was stated).

Type rate, scope person, program Medicaid.
Uses: `expected_annual_income`, `expects_to_be_claimed_as_dependent`, `federal_exchange_open_enrollment_start_month`, `federal_poverty_guideline_annual_each_additional`, `federal_poverty_guideline_annual_table`, `is_required_to_file_tax_return`, `ma_premium_tax_credit_family`, `ma_sponsor_deemed_income`.

(table) as of the first day of the most recent month number Exchange annual open enrollment start month (11) on or before the calendar month number of the month containing the Determination Date months before the month containing the Determination Date), for (the number of persons in Medicaid: premium tax credit family), adding (HHS federal poverty guideline, each additional household member, annual (48 states and D.C.) (5680) as of the first day of the most recent month number Exchange annual open enrollment start month (11) on or before the calendar month number of the month containing the Determination Date months before the month containing the Determination Date) for each beyond its last row)

### CO-4564 Medicaid: income below the limit under the premium tax credit methodology `@engine`

Whether this person, a tax filer or a claimed tax dependent, has household income under the premium tax credit methodology (ma_premium_tax_credit_household_income_pct_fpl) below ma_premium_tax_credit_methodology_income_limit_pct of the poverty level, so that § 8.100.4.C.5 and 42 CFR 435.603(i) determine the person's Medicaid financial eligibility on that income.

Precision. False for a person who neither files nor is claimed (an empty premium tax credit family, CO-4560). Where a counted family member's expected annual income is not stated the figure is unknown, and so is this test; ma_magi_household_income_pct_fpl (CO-504) is then unknown (coverage pass 5, C5-07: before, it read the test as not met, a default no rule gives). The rate is compared, not rounded.

Type yes/no, scope person, program Medicaid.
Uses: `ma_premium_tax_credit_family`, `ma_premium_tax_credit_household_income_pct_fpl`, `ma_premium_tax_credit_methodology_income_limit_pct`.

```
all of the following are true:
  - (the number of persons in Medicaid: premium tax credit family) is more than 0
  - Medicaid: household income under the premium tax credit methodology, as a share of the poverty line is less than Medicaid: premium tax credit methodology income limit (1)
```

### CO-4567 Medicaid: MAGI household income for the budget period, as a share of the poverty guideline `@engine`

This person's MAGI household income under the budget period rules of 10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.4.C.4 - the month's income (ma_magi_household_income), or, where it is lower, the annualized income of a household with self-employment, seasonal or commission earnings (ma_annualized_household_income, C.4.a) - as a fraction of the monthly federal poverty guideline for ma_magi_household_size.

Precision. C.4.a applies the annualized figure to "Applicants who are found financially ineligible based on current or previous monthly household income": an applicant eligible on the month's income keeps it, and one ineligible on it is tested on the annualized income, which the lower of the two gives for every income standard, since each MAGI standard is a ceiling. Where nothing is annualized the two are the same. The guideline is read as ma_magi_household_income_pct_fpl read it before the coverage round (lookup_extended beyond the table's last row, divided by 12, no rounding of the ratio).

Type rate, scope person-month, program Medicaid.
Uses: `federal_poverty_guideline_annual_each_additional`, `federal_poverty_guideline_annual_table`, `ma_budget_period_household_income`, `ma_magi_household_size`.

```
Medicaid: MAGI household income for the budget period divided by ((HHS federal poverty guideline by household size, annual (48 states and D.C.) (table), for Medicaid: MAGI family size, adding HHS federal poverty guideline, each additional household member, annual (48 states and D.C.) (5680) for each beyond its last row) divided by 12)
```

### CO-4620 Medicaid: excess real property left out while for sale or co-owned `@engine`

The part of the person's real property other than the home that the aged, blind and disabled resource test leaves out in the month: property the person is making reasonable but unsuccessful efforts to sell (10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.5.M.2.b), and the person's share of property whose sale would cause the co-owner who lives in it undue hardship through loss of housing (§ 8.100.5.M.3.h): the equity, at the person's share, of each real property holdings record (CO-5300) valued in the month that the eligibility site has found so (the record's ma_sale_efforts_unsuccessful or co_owner_would_lose_housing, decision D9).

Precision. Resource records, Medicaid track H1 (docs/reviews/records-holdings-medicaid.md): read in the month in context (ma_ssi_countable_resources_individual, CO-4623, reads it at the determination month, as the scalar findings were read; ma_ssi_countable_resources_in_month, CO-5322, in any month). The findings are fields of the property's record, so a person with a lot for sale and another lot not for sale states two records, and the finding names the one it is about. A record that does not state a finding is read as not found (the exclusion is the person's to show: resources are available unless shown otherwise, 8.100.5.E.3, S4670), the reading the scalar facts' reader gave. Income-producing property is not real property this item reads (CO-4621 counts it above its exclusion). The documents the two findings need are verification items (CO-2246 to CO-2249), which keep the case pending until they arrive. Once the property sells, the proceeds are a bank account or cash (M.2.b.vii, § 8.100.5.P). Never more than the real property the SSI method counted, since it is a part of the same records. Coverage pass 4, non-MAGI N4-8 (20 CFR 416.1207(a), S4501: "Resources determinations are made as of the first moment of the month"): a holding the person disposed of is still held at the first moment of the month of its disposed_date and of every month before it, so it is read in those months and left out from the month after (it is then a transfer, ma_uncompensated_transfers_in_lookback, CO-5325); it was left out of every month, the month of disposal included. Coverage pass 4, non-MAGI N4-13 and OQ-1243 (decision 4 of 2026-11-23): the record fields an exclusion rests on (income_producing, produces_for_household_use, ma_sale_efforts_unsuccessful, co_owner_would_lose_housing) take the default the holdings schema now declares from 8.100.5.E.3 (not so unless shown), not a default of this reader. Field-effect sweep (docs/reviews/field-sweep-snap-cash-nonmagi.md), FS-MA-4: a holding the person cannot get at (accessible false) because it is in probate, frozen by a creditor's lien or levy or a court order, or held under a trust's terms the person can neither revoke nor direct (inaccessible_reason) is not read: Medical Assistance deems available a resource the person "is not legally restricted from using" (10 CCR 2505-10 8.100.5.E.3.c, S4670), and "If a property right cannot be liquidated, the property will not be considered a resource" (20 CFR 416.1201(a)(1), S4500). One a co-owner refuses to release is still read, since a resource is not "unavailable merely because the individual ... may need to initiate legal proceedings to access" it (E.4, S4670). accessible defaults to true (CO-5300); the reason is required where it is false (decision 4). Before, accessible was not read.

Type money, scope person-month, program Medicaid.
Uses: `holdings`, `ma_ssi_holding_treatment_table`.

```
the sum for each holding in Holdings where
    all of the following are true:
      - Medicaid, SSI method: how each kind of holding is treated (table), for that holding's kind is equal to counted_less_real_property_exclusions
      - that holding is valued in the month
      - any of the following is true:
        - that holding's accessible
        - it is not the case that that holding's inaccessible reason is one of: probate, lien_or_court_order, trust_terms
      - any of the following is true:
        - that holding's disposed date is unknown
        - the month containing that holding's disposed date is at least the month
      - it is not the case that that holding's income producing
      - it is not the case that that holding's produces for household use
      - any of the following is true:
        - that holding's ma sale efforts unsuccessful
        - that holding's co owner would lose housing
  of
    (that holding's share, otherwise 1) times (that holding's value minus that holding's amount owed)
```

```json
["sum_receipts","holdings",["all",["=",["lookup","ma_ssi_holding_treatment_table",["receipt","kind"]],"counted_less_real_property_exclusions"],["received_in",["month"]],["any",["receipt","accessible"],["not",["in",["receipt","inaccessible_reason"],["probate","lien_or_court_order","trust_terms"]]]],["any",["unknown",["receipt","disposed_date"]],[">=",["month_of",["receipt","disposed_date"]],["month"]]],["not",["receipt","income_producing"]],["not",["receipt","produces_for_household_use"]],["any",["receipt","ma_sale_efforts_unsuccessful"],["receipt","co_owner_would_lose_housing"]]],["*",["otherwise",["receipt","share"],1],["-",["receipt","value"],["receipt","amount_owed"]]]]
```

### CO-4621 Medicaid: countable income-producing property `@engine`

The part of the person's income-producing and self-support property that counts as a resource in the month for the aged, blind and disabled groups: the equity, at the person's share, of the real property holdings records, and the personal property records other than household goods and personal effects (CO-5300) stated as producing income (income_producing) or goods for the household's own use (produces_for_household_use), less ma_income_producing_property_exclusion, which is excluded for non-business property essential to self-support (10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.5.J.2) and for property used in a trade or business only if its yearly net return is at least ma_income_producing_property_min_return_rate of the excluded value (J.3); above the exclusion the property counts (M.3.g).

Precision. Resource records, Medicaid track H1 (docs/reviews/records-holdings-medicaid.md): the non-business property and the trade or business property are each excluded up to the $6,000 their paragraph names (J.2, J.3), the return of the business records against 6% of the business property's excluded value. Property the person uses to produce income or goods or services for the person's own support is read as essential to self-support, so property producing goods for the household's own use (stated for Adult Financial before the records, home_use_production_property_equity_value, CO-4425) is J.2 property too, and non-business income-producing property stated for Adult Financial (CO-4423) is the same property Medicaid reads (one statement, one record). A record that does not state used_in_trade_or_business is read as not a trade or business, the reading the scalar facts' reader gave (J.2 is the general exclusion); a business record with no net return stated cannot be tested against J.3 and is unknown. Coverage pass 4, non-MAGI N4-8 (20 CFR 416.1207(a), S4501: "Resources determinations are made as of the first moment of the month"): a holding the person disposed of is still held at the first moment of the month of its disposed_date and of every month before it, so it is read in those months and left out from the month after (it is then a transfer, ma_uncompensated_transfers_in_lookback, CO-5325); it was left out of every month, the month of disposal included. Coverage pass 4, non-MAGI N4-13 and OQ-1243 (decision 4 of 2026-11-23): the record fields an exclusion rests on (income_producing, produces_for_household_use, used_in_trade_or_business) take the default the holdings schema now declares from 8.100.5.E.3 (not so unless shown), not a default of this reader. Field-effect sweep (docs/reviews/field-sweep-snap-cash-nonmagi.md), FS-MA-4: a holding the person cannot get at (accessible false) because it is in probate, frozen by a creditor's lien or levy or a court order, or held under a trust's terms the person can neither revoke nor direct (inaccessible_reason) is not read: Medical Assistance deems available a resource the person "is not legally restricted from using" (10 CCR 2505-10 8.100.5.E.3.c, S4670), and "If a property right cannot be liquidated, the property will not be considered a resource" (20 CFR 416.1201(a)(1), S4500). One a co-owner refuses to release is still read, since a resource is not "unavailable merely because the individual ... may need to initiate legal proceedings to access" it (E.4, S4670). accessible defaults to true (CO-5300); the reason is required where it is false (decision 4). Before, accessible was not read. Field-effect sweep (docs/reviews/field-sweep-snap-cash-nonmagi.md), FS-MA-6: 8.100.5.J.2-3 (S3402) speak of "Non-business property" and "Property used in a trade or business", not real property alone, and M.3.i (S4505) counts personal property "that is not income producing": personal property that produces income or goods for the person's support is read here with real property, under the one $6,000 exclusion; household goods and personal effects are excluded whole (M.2.d-e, S4504).

### CO-4622 Medicaid: the home is a countable resource `@engine`

Whether the person's home (a holdings record of kind home, holdings, CO-5300) is a countable resource for the aged, blind and disabled groups (10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.5.M.2.a, M.3.e): when a beneficiary deed on it has been executed and recorded (xiv); for a person in a long-term care institution, receiving HCBS or enrolled in PACE, when it has been transferred to a trust or other entity (xiii); or when the person no longer lives in it and neither a spouse nor a dependent relative lives there (ix), unless the person intends to return and, for a person living in an institution or facility, the intent is documented in writing (iv, v, vii, viii, xii). A home outside Colorado that the person intends to return to is not counted here: the person fails residency instead (iii).

Precision. Whether the person lives in the home is lives_in_owned_home (CO-4610), read from residence_setting_type when not stated; an institution, assisted living residence or other facility is read as living away (v, xii). A spouse or dependent relative in the home is ma_spouse_or_dependent_relative_lives_in_home (CO-4880): a person the person or the spouse claims as a tax dependent (§ 8.100.1's definition, S3616), or a spouse or a child under 21 or blind or disabled (CO-889, the 42 U.S.C. 1396p(f)(2) relatives, which alone govern the equity-limit exception of CO-650). A home the person has left for a private dwelling elsewhere, with intent to return, stays exempt without a written statement: § 8.100.5.M.2.a.v asks for the writing only of an institutionalized person, and the SSI rule (20 CFR 416.1212(c)), which 42 CFR 435.601(b) does not let the state make stricter, asks none (coverage pass 2, N2-6). The equity limit of M.2.a.ii and vi is ma_home_equity_disqualifies (CO-650), read for long-term care only (OQ-820); this item does not test it. Long-term care for xiii is a medical institution, an HCBS waiver designation or PACE enrollment. The month after the home stops being the principal residence (x) is not separated: the determination date's facts decide. The arms other than the beneficiary deed are ma_home_is_countable_resource_without_beneficiary_deed (CO-5204). A beneficiary deed (xiv) counts the home only when it "is subject to estate recovery" (ma_home_is_subject_to_estate_recovery, CO-5203: 55 or older, or in a medical institution, 42 U.S.C. 1396p(b)(1)); the Medicare Savings Program tests leave such a home out (ma_msp_countable_resources, CO-5206; OQ-900). Resource records, Medicaid track H1 (docs/reviews/records-holdings-medicaid.md): the home is the home holdings record (CO-5300) at the determination month; a recorded beneficiary deed is its beneficiary_deed (read as none when not stated, as the scalar fact was), its equity the person's share of the record's equity (ma_home_equity_interest_in_month, CO-5327). A person who states no holdings has a home whose countability cannot be determined (decision 4); a stated list with no home record has none. Coverage pass 4, non-MAGI N4-8 (20 CFR 416.1207(a), S4501: "Resources determinations are made as of the first moment of the month"): a holding the person disposed of is still held at the first moment of the month of its disposed_date and of every month before it, so it is read in those months and left out from the month after (it is then a transfer, ma_uncompensated_transfers_in_lookback, CO-5325); it was left out of every month, the month of disposal included. Coverage pass 4, non-MAGI N4-7 and N4-9: per month, the home record as of the month's first moment (20 CFR 416.1207(a)) and the person's age in the month, since every reader is per month (the person's resources in the month, ma_ssi_countable_resources_in_month, CO-5322; the Medicare Savings Program and parental resource figures); before, every month read the determination month. Coverage pass 4, non-MAGI N4-13 and OQ-1243 (decision 4 of 2026-11-23): the record fields an exclusion rests on () take the default the holdings schema now declares from 8.100.5.E.3 (not so unless shown), not a default of this reader. The fields that would take an exemption away (beneficiary_deed) are read as the record states them: a record that does not state them cannot be determined, no longer read as not so.

Type yes/no, scope person-month, program Medicaid.
Uses: `holdings`, `ma_home_is_countable_resource_without_beneficiary_deed`, `ma_home_is_subject_to_estate_recovery`, `ma_ssi_holding_treatment_table`.

### CO-4623 Medicaid: SSI-related countable resources of the individual `@engine`

This person's own countable resources for the aged, blind and disabled groups and long-term care (10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.5.J, M) on the determination date: ma_ssi_countable_resources_in_month (CO-5322) at the determination month: the SSI method's holdings counted (ma_ssi_holdings_countable_in_month, CO-5320, by the holdings counting table CO-5303), less the real property left out while for sale or co-owned with a resident (ma_excluded_real_property_value), plus income-producing property above its exclusion (ma_countable_income_producing_property_value), the home when § 8.100.5.M.2.a makes it countable (ma_home_is_countable_resource), and the value the Department finds available from a trust, an annuity or a life estate (§ 8.100.7.E, H, I). An ABLE account is left out (M.2.k) and personal property held as an investment (M.3.j) counted, by their rows.

Precision. The person's own holdings, not combined with a spouse's; ma_ssi_countable_resources (CO-608) and ma_institutionalized_spouse_countable_resources (CO-647) combine the spouses' figures, with the couple's one automobile. Resource records, Medicaid track H1 (docs/reviews/records-holdings-medicaid.md): read from the holdings records (CO-5300) through CO-5322, which states the figure for any month; this item is its determination-month value, which every person-scope reader reads.

### CO-4624 Medicaid: parents whose income and resources are deemed to the child `@engine`

For a child under ma_ssi_unemancipated_child_age_limit who is not emancipated and does not reside in a medical institution, the child's parents and stepparents who live with the child, do not reside in a medical institution, and are not applying for or eligible for SSI (ineligible parents, 10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.5.H.2.c): the persons whose income and resources are deemed to the child (42 U.S.C. 1382c(f)(2)(A), 20 CFR 416.1165, 416.1202(b)); empty for anyone else.

Precision. Deeming stops once the child is institutionalized (§ 8.100.7.A.1). Coverage pass 2, N2-7: A.1 provides Medical Assistance "beginning the first day of the month following the month during which a child under the age of 18 ceases to live with his or her parent(s)", which leaves the month of admission deemed; this item is read once for the case (person scope, as the deemed resources, CO-4627, are), so it cannot keep deeming for the admission month alone without keeping it for the months after. It stops deeming from the month of admission: the only answer that differs is the SSI-related category for that one month, and in the child's favour. Living together is lives_with (read as together when not stated). A parent or stepparent who is applying for or eligible for SSI (ma_is_applying_for_or_eligible_for_ssi, CO-2271) is not an ineligible parent. The exception of 20 CFR 416.1165(i) and 416.1202(b)(2) for a child previously paid the reduced SSI benefit of a medical facility is not modeled: a disabled child served by an HCBS waiver reaches Medicaid through the 300% special income group, which counts only the child's own income. Coverage pass 4, non-MAGI N4-9 (docs/operators.md, "Ages in a month"): the age is taken in the month evaluated, not on the determination date: an "under N" test on the first day of the month (ma_age_on_first_day_of_month, CO-4978), an "N or older" test on the last day (ma_age_on_last_day_of_month, CO-5402), and a test that excludes the person from what is favorable on the other day. Per month: the deeming of 20 CFR 416.1165 stops with the month the child is no longer under 18, so a retroactive month before the birthday is deemed and a month after it is not; every reader is per month (ma_ssi_parental_resources_deemed, CO-4627, is per month too). Pattern sweep, non-MAGI Medicaid (docs/reviews/pattern-sweep-nonmagi.md, P1, P2, P3): the household of the month is ma_ssi_lives_with_in_month (CO-7505): those living in the person's home, and a spouse, parent or child who lives elsewhere through the month the two ceased to live together (20 CFR 416.1165(g)(4), S5122; 416.1167(a)(1), S5120; § 8.100.7.C.2.b, S1759), a person who died through the month of death ((g)(3), S5122; 416.1163(f)(4), S5121); a person who lives in a facility (its dwelling_id the facility's) is a member through the month of entry (institution_entry_date) and not from the month after (§ 8.100.7.A.1, S3406: from 'the first day of the month following the month during which a child under the age of 18 ceases to live with his or her parent(s)'; 416.1167(a)(1)), while a person away for a stay the person returns from keeps the home's dwelling_id and stays a member (a temporary absence, 416.1167(a); duplicate-paths D-M4). Living together is read as stated, required where read (decision 4 of 2026-11-23; convention rule 17): no text on file says the persons of one application live together unless it says otherwise. A stepparent is deemed only in a month the child's own parent who is the stepparent's spouse lives in the child's household (416.1165(g)(3), S5122: 'If you live with a stepparent following the death of your natural or adoptive parent, we do not deem income from the stepparent'; (g)(4): no deeming from the stepparent 'if your natural or adoptive parent has permanently left the household'). The child's relationships are read as stated, required where read. Before, every month read the institution (any stay in a medical institution, even one the child returns from) and the homes of the determination date, a case with no homes stated was read as one home, a child with no relationships stated had no parent, and a stepparent was deemed whatever the parent's presence.

### CO-4625 Medicaid: blind or disabled children sharing the deemed parental income `@engine`

The blind or disabled children under ma_ssi_unemancipated_child_age_limit, not emancipated and not in a medical institution, who are children or stepchildren of a parent in this person's ma_ssi_deeming_parents (this person among them when blind or disabled): the eligible children among whom the parents' deemed income is divided equally (20 CFR 416.1165(e)(2)).

Precision. Blind is is_blind and disabled is meets_ssa_disability_criteria. A child whose own income already makes the child ineligible stays in the group: 416.1165(e)(3) does not take it out of the division but limits what it is deemed and passes the rest to the others, which ma_ssi_parental_income_deemed (CO-4626) does through ma_ssi_deeming_share_zeroes_benefit (CO-5904); the division is equal only among the children whose limit is not reached. Coverage pass 4, non-MAGI N4-9 (docs/operators.md, "Ages in a month"): the age is taken in the month evaluated, not on the determination date: an "under N" test on the first day of the month (ma_age_on_first_day_of_month, CO-4978), an "N or older" test on the last day (ma_age_on_last_day_of_month, CO-5402), and a test that excludes the person from what is favorable on the other day. Per month, as the deeming parents it reads (CO-4624). Coverage pass 4, non-MAGI N4-13 (decision 4 of 2026-11-23: missing information is cannot determine unless the rule says otherwise; readers do not invent defaults): a member's blindness and disability (the SSA's or the Department's finding, 8.100.6.B) are read as stated for every member, no longer as no for a member whose finding is unstated. Pattern sweep, non-MAGI Medicaid (docs/reviews/pattern-sweep-nonmagi.md, P1, P3): the blind or disabled children who share the deemed income are those in the child's household in the month (ma_ssi_lives_with_in_month, CO-7505; 20 CFR 416.1165, S3413: the deeming rules apply to 'a child living with your parents'); a child who lives in a facility is in it through the month of entry and not after (§ 8.100.7.A.1, S3406), and a child away for a stay the child returns from stays a member (416.1167(a)). Living together is read as stated, required where read (decision 4; convention rule 17). Before, a sibling living in another home shared the deemed income, and a sibling in a hospital was left out of every month. Pattern sweep, non-MAGI Medicaid (docs/reviews/pattern-sweep-nonmagi.md, P1): disability is read in the month: not in a month before the disability onset (ma_month_is_before_disability_onset, CO-4888; the onset is 'the date on which the person's disability began', CO-4887; 10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.5.C.4.b, S3623; § 8.100.3.E.1, S1503). Before, the undated finding was read in every month.

### CO-4626 Medicaid: parental income deemed to the child `@engine`

The income of this child's ineligible parents deemed to the child as unearned income for the month (10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.5.H.3.a, H.3.b.iii; 42 U.S.C. 1382c(f)(2)(A); 20 CFR 416.1165(d)-(e)): the parents' income that remains to be deemed after the allocations and disregards and the Ineligible Parent(s) Allocation (ma_ssi_parental_income_to_be_deemed), divided among the blind or disabled children sharing it (ma_ssi_deeming_children) so that no child is deemed more than reduces its SSI benefit to zero (416.1165(e)(2)-(3)): a child whose share would reduce its benefit to zero (ma_ssi_deeming_share_zeroes_benefit) is deemed that limit (ma_ssi_deeming_benefit_zero_amount), and the rest is divided equally among the children whose limit is not reached; zero when no parent's income is deemed.

Precision. The child's own $20 general income exclusion then applies to the child's unearned income with the deemed income in it (416.1165(e)(1)): ma_ssi_household_unearned_income_counted (CO-2281) adds this amount. With no child's limit reached this is the equal division of (e)(2). A child whose limit is reached is deemed exactly its limit, so its countable income is the Federal Benefit Rate, and it is ineligible by (e)(3) ('makes that child ineligible (reduces the amount to zero)'): ma_ssi_income_test_status (CO-5516) reads CO-5904 for that. When every child's limit is reached, each is deemed its limit and what is left is deemed to no one ('We do not deem more income to an eligible child than ...'). The only eligible child is deemed all of it ((e)(1); see CO-5904). The division is figured from this child's parents' income and this child's group, each other child's limit and test read for that child, as the equal division was. A child of the parents who is not in the group (not blind or disabled) is given an equal part of what the children whose limit is reached leave, as it was given an equal part before; it is not an eligible child, and no SSI-related category reads its deemed income.

Type money, scope person-month, program Medicaid.
Uses: `ma_ssi_deeming_benefit_zero_amount`, `ma_ssi_deeming_children`, `ma_ssi_deeming_parents`, `ma_ssi_deeming_share_zeroes_benefit`, `ma_ssi_parental_income_to_be_deemed`.

```
if (the number of persons in Medicaid: parents whose income and resources are deemed to the child) is equal to 0
  then 0
else if Medicaid: the parental income shared with other eligible children zeroes this child's SSI benefit
  then Medicaid: most parental income that can be deemed to the child
otherwise (Medicaid: parental income to be deemed to the eligible children minus (the sum of that person's Medicaid: most parental income that can be deemed to the child for each person in all persons in Medicaid: blind or disabled children sharing the deemed parental income such that that person's Medicaid: the parental income shared with other eligible children zeroes this child's SSI benefit)) divided by (the greater of 1 and (the number of persons in all persons in Medicaid: blind or disabled children sharing the deemed parental income such that it is not the case that that person's Medicaid: the parental income shared with other eligible children zeroes this child's SSI benefit))
```

### CO-4627 Medicaid: parental resources deemed to the child `@engine`

The resources of this child's ineligible parents deemed to the child (42 U.S.C. 1382c(f)(2)(A); 20 CFR 416.1202(b)): the parents' own countable resources (ma_ssi_countable_resources_individual) less their self-funded retirement accounts, above the resource limit for a couple when two deemed parents live with the child or for an individual when one does; zero when no parent's resources are deemed.

Precision. Pension funds of a parent or stepparent are excluded (416.1202(b)(1)(i)); the parent's retirement accounts are read as them. The excess is deemed to each eligible child in full: 416.1202(b) divides nothing. A parent's home that counts only because of a recorded beneficiary deed (ma_home_equity_counted_only_by_beneficiary_deed, CO-5205) is left out: § 8.100.5.M.2.a.xiv counts a home "which is subject to estate recovery", and nothing paid for the child is recovered from the parent's estate (42 U.S.C. 1396p(b)(1)). Resource records, Medicaid track H1 (docs/reviews/records-holdings-medicaid.md): the parent's pension funds left out are what the parent's own figure counted for the parent's retirement accounts (ma_ssi_retirement_accounts_counted_in_month, CO-5326, at the determination month). Each parent's own figure excludes that parent's one automobile; whether two deeming parents exclude one automobile between them, as a couple does (416.1218(b)), is OQ-1241. Coverage pass 4, non-MAGI N4-7 and N4-9: per month, the deeming parents of the month (ma_ssi_deeming_parents, CO-4624) and their resources at the month's first moment (ma_ssi_countable_resources_in_month, CO-5322; 20 CFR 416.1207(a)), as the child's own resources are read (ma_ssi_countable_resources, CO-608).

The combined income of this child's ma_ssi_deeming_parents for the month after the Ineligible Child Allocation (ma_ssi_deeming_ineligible_child_allocation, taken from unearned income first) and the standard disregards: the ssi_general_income_exclusion from unearned income, any unused part of it and the ssi_earned_income_exclusion from earned income, and one half of the earned remainder (10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.5.H.3.b.i-ii, H.4.a-b; 20 CFR 416.1165(a)-(b), (d)(1)-(2)).

Subsidized adoption funds are not deemed: § 8.100.5.F.6.t (S4041) exempts the income of the child receiving them, and the subsidy is paid for the child although received by the adoptive parent. Receipt records, migration phase 3: the subsidy is a receipt kind of its own (adoption_subsidy), which the SSI method's counting table exempts, so ma_ssi_unearned_receipts no longer holds it and it is no longer subtracted here (it was adoption_subsidy_received, CO-4451, stated inside the other non-taxable receipts). ### CO-4880 Medicaid: spouse or dependent relative lives in the home `@engine`

Whether this person's spouse or a dependent relative lives in this person's home, the condition that keeps a home the person has left exempt under 10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.5.M.2.a.iv, vi, vii, ix and xi. A dependent relative is "one who is claimed as a dependent by an applicant for federal income tax purposes" (§ 8.100.1); a spouse, or a child under 21 or blind or disabled (ma_spouse_or_qualifying_child_lives_in_home, CO-889), counts as well.

Precision. A dependent relative is a person whom this person, or this person's spouse, claims as a tax dependent (the tax_filer / tax_dependent edge; a joint return's claim reaches both spouses), whatever the family tie. Living in the home is read as in CO-889: the relative does not reside in a medical institution and, where this person's lives_with is stated, is in it; for a person in a facility, a relative who lives in a private dwelling is read as living in the person's home. The relatives of CO-889 are kept beside the tax dependents: they are the 42 U.S.C. 1396p(f)(2) relatives and a minor or disabled child at home is a dependent relative under the SSI rule (20 CFR 416.1212(c)) that 42 CFR 435.601(b) does not let the state narrow. (Until the pattern sweep: if the person had no stated relationships, Medicaid read no such relative.) Coverage pass 3 C3-12 (P3, noted): for a person in a facility, a dependent relative is read as living in the home when the relative's dwelling_id is a private dwelling; a case whose relative lives elsewhere (an adult child in her own apartment) should state the relative's dwelling_id as that apartment, not as the person's home, or the home stays exempt under ix. Pattern sweep, non-MAGI Medicaid (docs/reviews/pattern-sweep-nonmagi.md, P1, P2): per month, as CO-889: a dependent relative is in the home in the month when not in a medical institution in the month (CO-7500). The homes (lives_with) and settings are read as stated, required where read (decision 4 of 2026-11-23; convention rule 17). The remaining read of another person's tax-dependent edge as none when that person states no relationships follows docs/operators.md (Relationships: another person's unstated relationships are read as none); the person's own relationships are required through CO-889. Living in the home in the month is read from ma_ssi_lives_with_in_month (CO-7505): a spouse, parent or child who lives elsewhere on the determination date is in the home through the month the two ceased to live together (for one who entered a facility, the month of entry).

### CO-4888 Medicaid: month is before the disability onset `@engine`

Whether the month ends before the person's disability onset date (disability_onset_date), so that no medical service in it was on or after the onset and the person does not meet the SSA definition of disability for that month (10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.5.C.4.b.ii).

Precision. A month is before the onset when it is earlier than the month containing the onset date; the onset month itself is not, because a service on or after the onset day in it qualifies (C.4.b reads the date of the medical service, and the volume determines whole months). (Until the pattern sweep an unstated onset date was read as no such month.) C.4.b.i (SSI or SSDI approved on or before the service) is not separated: an approval follows the onset. Pattern sweep, non-MAGI Medicaid (docs/reviews/pattern-sweep-nonmagi.md, P1, P2): the determination month and the months after are not before the onset (the SSA finding stated on the determination date is of a disability that has begun); for a month before the determination month the onset date is required where read (decision 4 of 2026-11-23): no rule on file reads an undated disability as begun before every retroactive month, and C.4.b (S3623) asks for the onset or the approval 'on or prior to the date of a medical service'. The long-term care, HCBS, PACE and protected groups read the gate too (through CO-5201): a person is disabled only from the onset of the disability (disability_onset_date, CO-4887, 'the date on which the person's disability began'; § 8.100.7.A.2.b, S1753, 'Have met the requirements according to the definition of disability'; A.2.c.iii, benefits start 'if all other eligibility requirements were met as of that date').

### CO-4978 Medicaid: age on the first day of the month `@engine`

The person's whole number of completed years of age on the first day of the month evaluated: the age an "under N" limit reads where any day of the month counts (10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.4.G.1 for MAGI, S3351; § 8.100.5.C.1 and C.3 for the Aged, Blind and Disabled groups and the Children's Buy-In, S3900), so that a person who is under the limit on any day of the month is within it for the whole month, and a person who reaches the limit on the first day is not.

Precision. A person under N on the first day of the month is under N on at least that day; a person who is N or older on the first day is N or older on every day of the month. So the test is exact for an "under N" limit: the Eligible Needy Newborn's one year (§ 8.100.4.G.7, ma_is_needy_newborn, CO-550) and the dependent child's "under the age of 18" (§ 8.100.1, ma_is_dependent_child_in_month, CO-4791). Limits worded "through the end of the month" of a birthday (the Children's 19 and the Adults' 65, § 8.100.1) read ma_age_before_month (CO-4790), the age on the last day of the month before, which is exact for them; an "N or older" limit reads ma_age_on_last_day_of_month (CO-5402). A birthday is reached at the start of the day (years_between). Time audit T-1 (2026-11-23): measured in the month evaluated, not the determination month, so a retroactive month (42 CFR 435.915(a)(2), S218: "would have been eligible ... at the time") and an application month before the determination month read the person's age in that month; a rule about the determination itself reads it [at] the determination month.

Type whole number, scope person-month, program Medicaid.

```
the number of whole years between Date of birth and the first day of the month
```

### CO-500 Medicaid: MAGI household members `@engine`

This person's MAGI household under 42 CFR 435.603(f) and 10 CCR 2505-10 8.100.4.E.1 - a tax filer not claimed as a dependent's household is the filer, the filer's spouse if living in the home, and everyone the filer claims as a tax dependent; a claimed tax dependent's household is the claiming filer's household (the filer, the filer's spouse living in the home, the filer's other dependents, and the dependent's own spouse living with the dependent), unless the filer claiming them is someone other than their spouse or parent, in which case (and for a true non-filer) the household is the non-filer household of that person, their spouse, their own children and stepchildren under ma_magi_child_age_limit (not a child's child or a child's spouse), and, if this person is themselves under that age, their own parents and siblings under that age living with them.

Precision. Household membership is symmetric within the case model but each person's own value of this item is their own household, per 8.100.4.E's per-applicant test. A claimed dependent who meets any exception of 435.603(f)(2)(i)-(iii) or § 8.100.4.E.5 (ma_dependent_is_routed_to_non_filer_rules, CO-1976, OQ-42 resolved) has the non-filer household. In the non-filer household only persons in this person's lives_with (CO-1925) are counted, so a parent outside the home (a non-custodial parent, or the parent living apart under E.5) is not; where lives_with is not stated, whether two persons live together cannot be determined (C6-10 (2026-11-24): living together is read from lives_with (CO-1925) as stated, required where read (decision 4 of 2026-11-23): no text on file says the persons of one Single Streamlined Application live together unless it says otherwise (10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.4.E.1 asks for the relationship to the tax filer 'as declared on the Single Streamlined Application' and E.1.a.ii, E.1.b.ii-iv, E.1.d for living in the home; 42 CFR 435.907, D-196, says nothing of the home), so a case that states no dwelling_id cannot be determined where MAGI asks whether two persons live together; before, a stated relationship edge was read as living together (convention rule 17's fallback), which the other programs' readers still do). 'Siblings' is read through the engine's shared_relative pattern (P43, docs/conventions.md), which finds the persons who share a parent edge with this person directly - not by re-walking the parent-then-child chain that over-included an unrelated person in this item's earlier draft (see the batch-6 report). Same-word audit SW-1/SW-2: parents and children are natural, adopted and step (the parent and stepparent roles), and siblings are siblings (CO-2609) and step_siblings (CO-2610), as 42 CFR 435.603(f)(3) and § 8.100.4.E read them (S169). Coverage review F-01: the non-filer household takes single steps from this person (this person, read as the walk over spouse edges that crosses none; a child or stepchild under the age limit, including a child of this person's spouse; and for a person under the limit, parents and siblings), so a grandchild or a child's spouse is not reached through a child, as E.1.d.iii lists only the applicant's own children. Coverage review F-02: in the filer and claimed-dependent households a spouse edge is crossed only where the spouse is in the lives_with of the person the chain has reached (E.1.a.ii 'if living in the home', E.1.b.ii and b.iv, E.4 'Married couples living together'); where no dwelling_id is stated whether the spouse lives in the home cannot be determined, as the non-filer arm reads it (C6-10). A spouse living elsewhere is in neither person's household, whether or not they file jointly. Coverage review 2, N-03: the filer and claimed-dependent households also take single steps, as F-01 made the non-filer household do; the closure over spouse, tax_filer and tax_dependent edges had reached a claimed dependent's own spouse, and anyone that spouse claims, from the filer, which E.1.a does not list. The filer's household (E.1.a.i-iii) is the filer, the filer's spouse living in the home, and the persons the filer claims or a spouse living in the home claims on a joint return (a spouse is read as filing jointly unless files_jointly_with_spouse is stated false). A claimed dependent's household (E.1.b.i-iv) is the dependent; the claiming filer; the filer's spouse living with the filer; the filer's other dependents, including those a joint-filing spouse claims; and the dependent's own spouse living with the dependent. Coverage pass 4, C4-08 (2026-11-23; time contract month-v1): the household is built for each month, and the ages in the non-filer household (E.1.d, "children under the age of 19") are taken in the month evaluated: a person under 19 on the first day of the month (ma_age_on_first_day_of_month, CO-4978) is under 19 on that day, and G.1 makes a person eligible for the whole month on any day of it, so a retroactive month reads the household as it was then (42 CFR 435.915(a)(2), S218: "would have been eligible ... at the time"). A child who turns 19 during a month is in a parent's non-filer household for that month and out of it from the next. Before, the household was built once on the determination date's ages and every month read it, so a son who turned 19 in October was out of his mother's household in a retroactive September (RETRO19, stored household CO-722). Coverage pass 5, C5-05 (2026-11-23): the claimed-dependent household (E.1.b) is the claiming filer's household; where the claimer is not a person of the case (is_claimed_by_filer_outside_case, CO-2716, with no tax_dependent edge in the case) and the person is not routed to the non-filer rules (a claimer who is a parent, outside_claimer_is_parent, CO-7052, and none of E.1.c.ii-iii or E.5), the filer, the filer's spouse and other dependents are not stated, so the household is unknown (cannot determine; decision 4) unless the claimer is declared as a person of the case with the tax_filer edge. Before, it was the person alone (and the spouse), as if the claimer had no household. Pattern sweep, MAGI (2026-11-24, PS-03, PS-04): living in the home is read for the month (ma_lives_with_in_month, CO-7554), so a spouse, parent or other member who died before the month no longer lives in the home (E.1.a.ii, E.1.b.ii and iv, E.1.d, E.3; 8.100.4.G.1, S3351); a person the filer expects to claim (E.1.a.iii) stays a member by the claim. The two readings that took a claimer's spouse as living in the claimer's home when the spouse's home was not stated (an 'otherwise' to every person of the case) and a spouse as filing jointly when that was not stated are removed: decision 4, as C6-10 decided for the rest of this item; an unstated relationship of another person is still read as none (docs/operators.md, Relationships).

Type group of persons, scope person-month, program Medicaid.
Uses: `expects_to_be_claimed_as_dependent`, `files_jointly_with_spouse`, `is_tax_filer`, `ma_age_on_first_day_of_month`, `ma_dependent_is_routed_to_non_filer_rules`, `ma_lives_with_in_month`, `ma_magi_child_age_limit`, `relationships`, `siblings`, `step_siblings`.

```
if all of the following are true:
    - any of the following is true:
      - Is tax filer
      - there is a person of whom this person is a tax_filer such that
```

### CO-501 Medicaid: MAGI family size `@engine`

This person's MAGI family size under 42 CFR 435.603(b) and 10 CCR 2505-10 8.100.4.E.2 - the count of this person's ma_magi_household_members, except that any pregnant member of the household counts as herself plus the number of children she is expected to deliver. It is the MAGI family size: it counts an expected child of a pregnant member (vocabulary fix round C-3).

Precision. Applies the pregnant-member addition to every pregnant member of the household, not only to the person the size is computed for, per 8.100.4.E.2 ("regardless of the Medical Assistance category" and without limiting it to the pregnant woman's own family size). Coverage pass 5, C5-02 (2026-11-23): the size is the month's, so the addition is the month's pregnancy: a member pregnant at some time in the month (ma_is_pregnant_in_month, CO-3601) counts as herself plus the children she is expected to deliver less any born to her that month who are persons of the case (ma_expected_children_in_month, CO-7050), and a member not yet born in the month (a newborn of the case, in a retroactive month before the birth) is not counted, since the expected child stands for the child until it is born. Before, the addition read is_pregnant, the pregnancy on the determination date, in every month: a pregnancy that ended before the application was not counted in the retroactive months it covered, and one that began after them was.

Type whole number, scope person-month, program Medicaid.
Uses: `date_of_birth`, `ma_expected_children_in_month`, `ma_is_pregnant_in_month`, `ma_magi_household_members`.

```
the sum for each person in Medicaid: MAGI household members of
  if the month containing that person's Date of birth is more than the month
    then 0
  else if that person's Medicaid: is pregnant in the month
    then 1 plus that person's Medicaid: children a pregnant member is expected to deliver, counted in the month
  otherwise 1
```

### CO-502 Medicaid: person's MAGI-based income `@engine`

This person's own MAGI-based income for the month under 42 CFR 435.603(e) and 10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.4.C - taxable earned and unearned income (including Social Security benefits, whether or not taxable, capital gains, lottery and gambling winnings in the month received, and countable discharged student loan debt), plus tax-exempt interest and excluded foreign earned income added back in, minus above-the-line pretax deductions (including pre-tax 401(k)/403(b) contributions, net operating losses and capital losses).

Precision. Monthly amount for the month in context. Child support received, Supplemental Security Income, and TANF cash assistance are excluded per § 8.100.4.C.1.d; a lump sum is counted only in the month received (§ 8.100.4.C.1.d.i and 435.603(e)(1)), which the receipts state by their month or date - except lottery and gambling winnings over $79,999, which § 8.100.4.C.1.b.xiv spreads over two or more months for the winner: this item counts winnings in the month received (ma_magi_gambling_receipts, CO-5502), which is how they count for the other members of the winner's household (xiv.4), and ma_magi_household_income (CO-503) substitutes the spread amount when the household is the winner's own. Capital gains (xiii) are in magi_other_taxable_income (CO-079); discharged student loan debt (xv) is ma_countable_discharged_student_loan_income (CO-1190), not magi_other_taxable_income or other_unearned_income_nontaxable; pre-tax 401(k) or 403(b) contributions, net operating losses and capital losses (§ 8.100.4.C.1.e.viii, xiii-xv) are in pretax_deductions (CO-080), since the earnings records state gross pay. Not rounded: 10 CCR 2505-10 8.100.4.C and D and 42 CFR 435.603(e) state no rounding, and a money value no rule rounds is not rounded (docs/conventions.md, P41). Coverage pass 4, C4-13 (2026-11-23): before, the figure was rounded to the nearest dollar following SNAP's convention, which no MAGI text supports; at a limit it decided the answer (a single adult with 1,835.45, 138.004% of the guideline, was read as 1,835, 137.97%, eligible). Phase 7 fix round (S-9) added the winnings and student loan terms. Unearned income is the receipts the MAGI counting table counts (ma_magi_unearned_receipts, CO-5501; ma_magi_receipt_treatment_table, CO-5500), each kind with its paragraph of 8.100.4.C.1; non-taxable money (gifts, veterans' benefits, workers' compensation) is not MAGI income (8.100.4.C.1.d). Earned income is the earnings records the MAGI earnings counting table counts (ma_magi_earnings_treatment_table, CO-5106): pay from employment at its gross amount (ma_magi_wage_earnings, CO-5160) and each business's net earnings for tax (ma_magi_self_employment_earnings, CO-5161). Coverage review F-18 (fix round 2026-11-23): Difficulty of Care payments are counted in the pay (CO-5160) and subtracted when § 8.100.3.K.7 excludes them (ma_excluded_difficulty_of_care_payments, CO-5214). Coverage pass 4, C4-03: boarders' payments are counted net of the costs of providing the room or meals (ma_magi_boarder_earnings, CO-6450; 8.100.3.K.10.c-e, 26 U.S.C. 62(a)(4)), no longer at their gross amount in the pay.

### CO-503 Medicaid: MAGI household income `@engine`

This person's MAGI household's total countable income for the month under 42 CFR 435.603(d) and 10 CCR 2505-10 8.100.4.C.1.f - the sum of each household member's own ma_person_magi_income, except that a member's income is left out when the member is expected to be claimed as a tax dependent and is not required to file a tax return (the members counted are ma_magi_household_income_members, CO-4558) - plus, for a sponsored non-citizen, the sponsor income § 8.100.3.K.1 counts to this person (ma_sponsor_deemed_income, CO-4551).

Precision. Not rounded (coverage pass 4, C4-13: 8.100.4.C and D state no rounding; before, the sum was rounded to the nearest dollar, as each member's figure was). Coverage review 3, C3-04: the parent of clause (a) below is a natural, adopted or step parent, as C.1.f.i says (ma_magi_household_income_members, CO-4558, reads the child and stepchild roles). Coverage review F-03: the sponsor income deemed to this person (CO-4551) is added for this person's own household figure only, since § 8.100.3.K.1 counts it "to the sponsored alien"; the other members' households do not include it. Coverage review F-04: the members whose income counts are the group ma_magi_household_income_members (CO-4558), factored out unchanged so the annualized figure (CO-4559) counts the same members. Sums over ma_magi_household_members. A member's income is excluded only when the member is not required to file a tax return AND either (a) 435.603(d)(2)(i): someone in THIS household (the group being summed, read as a bare `ma_magi_household_members`, not the member's own independently-computed household) is that member's parent, or (b) 435.603(d)(2)(ii): the member is a dependent claimed by someone other than a spouse or parent (ma_is_dependent_claimed_by_non_parent, CO-563). Clause (a) is deliberately evaluated against the SUMMING household, not the member's own ma_magi_household_members value: 8.100.4.C.1.f.iii states 'the income of a child or tax dependent who does not live with their natural, adopted, or step parent will always count towards the determination of their own eligibility' - and 'their own eligibility' is decided per household, so a dependent whose parent is not a member of THIS particular household (for example a grandchild's non-filer household that excludes the claiming grandparent's own household) counts fully here even though the same dependent's income is excluded when the parent IS a co-member of a different household being summed. Replaced the prior expects_to_be_claimed_as_dependent proxy, which both over- and under-counted relative to this test. A member's income is excluded only when the member is not required to file and either a parent of the member, or the non-parent who claims the member, is in the household being summed (P45); so a child with no parent in her own household counts her own income, as 8.100.4.C.1.f.iii requires. Each member's income counts lottery or gambling winnings only in the month received (CO-502, § 8.100.4.C.1.b.xiv.4); for this person's own winnings the household total then swaps that for the amount spread over months (ma_lottery_winnings_countable_for_recipient, CO-1187, xiv.1-3). The swap assumes this person's own income is counted in the household, which holds for anyone with winnings large enough to spread (they must file a return); it is not made conditional on the exclusion clauses above.

Type money, scope person-month, program Medicaid.
Uses: `ma_lottery_winnings_countable_for_recipient`, `ma_lottery_winnings_hardship_exemption_granted`, `ma_magi_gambling_receipts`, `ma_magi_household_income_members`, `ma_person_magi_income`, `ma_sponsor_deemed_income`.

```
(if Lottery winnings hardship exemption granted, otherwise no;   then the sum of that person's Medicaid: person's MAGI-based income minus that person's Medicaid MAGI: a person's gambling winnings received in the month for each person in Medicaid: MAGI household members whose income counts; otherwise (the sum of that person's Medicaid: person's MAGI-based income for each person in Medicaid: MAGI household members whose income counts) plus (Medicaid: lottery or gambling winnings counted for the winner this month minus Medicaid MAGI: a person's gambling winnings received in the month)) plus Medicaid: sponsor income deemed to a sponsored non-citizen
```

### CO-504 Medicaid: MAGI household income as a percentage of the poverty guideline `@engine`

This person's MAGI household income for the month, expressed as a decimal fraction of the monthly federal poverty guideline for ma_magi_household_size (1.00 = 100% of the guideline) - the figure 10 CCR 2505-10 8.100.4.G's covered-group income limits and the 8.100.4.D 5% disregard are stated against: the budget period figure of § 8.100.4.C.4 (ma_budget_period_household_income_pct_fpl, CO-4567: the month's income, or the annualized income of C.4.a where lower), or, where the person's household income under the premium tax credit methodology is below 100% of the poverty level and lower still, that figure (§ 8.100.4.C.5; 42 CFR 435.603(i)).

Precision. The monthly poverty guideline is the annual federal_poverty_guideline_annual_table figure (plus federal_poverty_guideline_annual_each_additional for a household size above 8) divided by 12 (CO-4567); no rounding is applied to the ratio itself. Coverage review F-04 and F-05: C.4.a's annualized figure (CO-4559) and C.5's premium tax credit figure (CO-4561, CO-4564) are reached only where the figure before each is higher, which is their order in the rule (each applies to an applicant "found financially ineligible", or who "does not meet the financial eligibility requirements", on the figure before it), since each MAGI standard is a ceiling. 42 CFR 435.603(i) determines financial eligibility "in accordance with 26 CFR 1.36B-1(e)": the C.5 figure replaces the MAGI one in every category's test, so a person below 100% meets every standard but the Parents and Caretaker Relatives 68%, and C.5's "shall be found eligible" is read through the Adults, Children's and Pregnant Women standards such a person meets. CHP+ reads this ratio too (10 CCR 2505-3 § 150.1 adopts § 8.100.4.C): a child the C.5 figure brings under the Children's standard is Medicaid eligible, not CHP+. Reasonable compatibility (ma_income_is_reasonably_compatible, CO-1402) compares the data source with this figure. Coverage pass 5, C5-07 (2026-11-23): the C.5 test is read as it is: where it cannot be determined (the expected annual income of a counted member of the premium tax credit family not stated, CO-4556; or that family not known, CO-4560), this figure is unknown, so a person over every standard on the month's figure cannot be determined, since C.5 may make the person eligible; before, an unknown test was read as not met, a default no rule gives. A person eligible on the month's figure is determined without it, since every MAGI and CHP+ income test reads the month's figure first (ma_magi_monthly_household_income_pct_fpl, CO-6452). A person with no premium tax credit family (a non-filer who is not claimed) has the test false (CO-4564). Coverage pass 6, C6-09 (2026-11-24): for a month of a calendar year before the determination's (a retroactive month of an application made in January to March), C.5 is tested on that year's income under the methodology (ma_premium_tax_credit_previous_year_income_pct_fpl, CO-7408), not the determination year's, which is an annual, taxable-year figure (26 CFR 1.36B-1(e)); a person with no premium tax credit family has none in either year.

Type rate, scope person-month, program Medicaid.
Uses: `ma_budget_period_household_income_pct_fpl`, `ma_meets_premium_tax_credit_income_test`, `ma_premium_tax_credit_family`, `ma_premium_tax_credit_household_income_pct_fpl`, `ma_premium_tax_credit_methodology_income_limit_pct`, `ma_premium_tax_credit_previous_year_income_pct_fpl`.

```
if all of the following are true:
    - the calendar year of the month is less than the calendar year of the month containing the Determination Date
    - (the number of persons in Medicaid: premium tax credit family) is more than 0
  then (if Medicaid: household income under the premium tax credit methodology for the previous calendar year, as a share of the poverty level is less than Medicaid: premium tax credit methodology income limit (1);   then the lesser of Medicaid: household income under the premium tax credit methodology for the previous calendar year, as a share of the poverty level and Medicaid: MAGI household income for the budget period, as a share of the poverty guideline; otherwise Medicaid: MAGI household income for the budget period, as a share of the poverty guideline)
else if Medicaid: income below the limit under the premium tax credit methodology

otherwise Medicaid: MAGI household income for the budget period, as a share of the poverty guideline
```

### CO-509 Medicaid: meets the citizenship requirement `@engine`

Whether the person falls into one of the citizenship and immigration status categories of 10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.3.G.1.g (and 42 CFR 435.406(a)) that admit a person to full Medical Assistance: a citizen or national (i); a lawfully residing non-citizen who entered the United States before August 22, 1996 (ii); a qualified non-citizen who has held the status for five years (iii) or is exempt from the five-year rule (iv-v, ma_is_five_year_bar_exempt, CO-1172), and, from October 1, 2026, is also a lawful permanent resident, a Cuban or Haitian entrant or a Compact of Free Association migrant (42 U.S.C. 1396b(v)(5), ma_is_in_federal_payment_status_category, CO-2400); or a lawfully residing non-citizen who is a pregnant woman or a child under ma_magi_child_age_limit (vii, the CHIPRA 214 option, which 1396b(v)(5) keeps through its paragraph (4)). The Cover All Coloradans exception (ix.1) is not part of this test: it reaches only the categories ix.1.a-b list, which read ma_meets_status_for_cover_all_coloradans_categories (CO-1174) instead.

Precision. Medicaid status by month (2026-11-24, docs/reviews/medicaid-status-by-month.md, MS-2): the status of the determination date, read only by person-scope items (ma_meets_status_for_cover_all_coloradans_categories CO-1174; the spouse's status in ma_transfer_penalty_is_apportioned_with_spouse CO-2232). Every month-scoped Medicaid item, MAGI and non-MAGI, reads ma_meets_citizenship_requirement_in_month (CO-7551), which reads the five years, the pregnancy, the child's age and the qualified status for the month. The five-year rule is Medicaid's month reading for the determination month (ma_has_held_qualified_status_five_years_in_month, CO-7550, read at the determination month), counted from the first qualified status (first_qualified_status_date, CO-7770; coverage pass 7, C7-04: 8 U.S.C. 1613(a) runs it from entry with a qualified status, and the shared has_held_qualified_status_five_years, CO-508, which counted it from the status held now on the determination date, is no longer read by Medicaid); § 8.100.3.G.1.g.iii counts it from the date of entry, which for a person admitted directly as a Lawful Permanent Resident is the same date. The lawfully residing arm (vii) reads ma_is_lawfully_present (CO-507), which includes every qualified non-citizen, so a Lawful Permanent Resident inside the five-year rule who is pregnant or under ma_magi_child_age_limit meets status through vii ("falls into one of the categories listed in Section 8.100.3.G.1.g.iii... not subject to the five-year rule"), as the text states; the age is read strictly as "under the age of 19 years". ii (a lawfully residing non-citizen who entered before August 22, 1996) reads ma_is_lawfully_present (CO-507) and us_entry_date (CO-1726) against qualified_non_citizen_entry_cutoff_date (CO-279), and from October 1, 2026 is subject to the same 1396b(v)(5)(B) limit as the qualified arm. viii (Afghan humanitarian parolees) is an exemption from the five-year rule and is read in ma_is_five_year_bar_exempt (CO-1172). B-1 limited the lawfully present arm to pregnant women and children, as vii states; B-2 replaced the veteran-only exemption with CO-1172; S-2 moved the Cover All Coloradans disjuncts to ma_is_cover_all_coloradans_person (CO-1173). See OQ-213 and OQ-214. The citizen-or-national arm reads is_us_citizen_or_national (CO-1358). From October 1, 2026 (ma_alien_payment_restriction_applies, CO-3034) the qualified non-citizen arm also requires a 1396b(v)(5)(B) status (CO-2400): a refugee, asylee, parolee, trafficking victim or other qualified non-citizen adult who is not a lawful permanent resident fails status and is reported emergency-only (CO-510), as CMS SHO #26-001 directs; a refugee or asylee child under ma_magi_child_age_limit or pregnant woman keeps full coverage through vii, since qualified non-citizens are lawfully residing for the CHIPRA 214 option (S1705). The determination date decides which rule applies, so a retroactive month before October 2026 on a later application is judged by the October 2026 rule (OQ-510). Colorado's § 8.100.3.G.1.g (version effective 11/14/2026) has not been amended; the federal limit is applied regardless (HCPF review B-1).

Type yes/no, scope person, program Medicaid.
Uses: `age`, `immigration_status`, `is_pregnant`, `is_qualified_non_citizen`, `is_us_citizen_or_national`, `ma_alien_payment_restriction_applies`, `ma_has_held_qualified_status_five_years_in_month`, `ma_is_five_year_bar_exempt`, `ma_is_in_federal_payment_status_category`, `ma_is_lawfully_present`, `ma_magi_child_age_limit`, `qualified_non_citizen_entry_cutoff_date`, `us_entry_date`.

```
any of the following is true:
  - Is a U.S. citizen or national
  - all of the following are true:
    - any of the following is true:
      - all of the following are true:
        - Is a qualified non-citizen
        - any of the following is true:
          - Medicaid: has held qualified non-citizen status for five years by the end of the month for the month containing the Determination Date
          - Medicaid: is exempt from the five-year rule
      - Immigration status is equal to iraqi_afghan_special_immigrant
      - all of the following are true:
        - Medicaid: is lawfully present
        - Date of entry into the United States is less than PRWORA qualified-alien entry date cutoff (1996-08-22)
    - any of the following is true:
      - it is not the case that Medicaid: the federal payment limit for non-citizens applies (yes)
      - Medicaid: is in a status category for which federal payment is available from October 2026
  - all of the following are true:
    - Medicaid: is lawfully present
    - any of the following is true:
      - Is pregnant
      - Age is less than MAGI household child age limit (19)
```

### CO-510 Medicaid: is emergency Medicaid only `@engine`

Whether the person fails citizenship and immigration requirements but meets every other requirement of a categorical Medical Assistance program (ma_meets_requirements_other_than_status, CO-1150), and so is limited to emergency medical services (and reproductive health care) under 42 CFR 435.406(b), 42 U.S.C. 1396b(v) and 10 CCR 2505-10 §§ 8.100.3.F.1.k and 8.100.3.G.1.g.ix.2 (numbered viii.2 in the Cornell copy, D-39), rather than full Medical Assistance benefits.

Precision. A person who fails the status test (CO-509) is emergency-only when every other requirement of a categorical program is met (ma_meets_requirements_other_than_status, CO-1150: residency, the institution for mental diseases requirement, and a MAGI category, the SSI-related standards, OAP SISC B, or institutional long-term care) and the person is not fully covered through Cover All Coloradans in a category § 8.100.3.G.1.g.ix.1.a-b lists (ma_is_covered_under_cover_all_coloradans, CO-1175). So an undocumented child in the Children's category is fully covered, not emergency-only, while an undocumented postpartum adult whose only category is Adult is emergency-only. A person who meets no category, or is over every income standard, is not emergency-only; ma_magi_eligibility_status (CO-554) reports ineligible_income for that person. The emergency-only benefit is itself limited to a true emergency medical condition (including labor and delivery); this item states eligibility for the coverage category, and ma_emergency_medicaid_status (CO-1151) reads the month's emergency medical condition. Pattern sweep, MAGI (2026-11-24, PS-01, PS-02): status and the Cover All Coloradans population are read for the month evaluated (ma_meets_citizenship_requirement_in_month, CO-7551; ma_is_cover_all_coloradans_person_in_month, CO-7552; ma_meets_status_for_cover_all_coloradans_categories_in_month, CO-7553), not on the determination date: 8.100.4.G.1 (S3351), 8.100.3.E.1 (S217), 8 U.S.C. 1613(a) (S176), ix.1's 'current month' (S607).

Type yes/no, scope person-month, program Medicaid.
Uses: `ma_is_covered_under_cover_all_coloradans`, `ma_meets_citizenship_requirement_in_month`, `ma_meets_requirements_other_than_status`.

```
all of the following are true:
  - it is not the case that Medicaid: meets the citizenship requirement in the month
  - it is not the case that Medicaid: is covered under Cover All Coloradans
  - Medicaid: meets every requirement other than citizenship or immigration status
```

```json
["all",["not","ma_meets_citizenship_requirement_in_month"],["not","ma_is_covered_under_cover_all_coloradans"],"ma_meets_requirements_other_than_status"]
```

### CO-5160 Medicaid MAGI: a person's counted pay from employment `@engine`

The person's earnings of the month, other than a business's (ma_magi_self_employment_earnings, CO-5161), that Medicaid's MAGI counting table counts (ma_magi_earnings_treatment_table, CO-5106), each at its gross amount: the rows counted (wages, salaries, tips, compensation for services, 10 CCR 2505-10 8.100.4.C.1.a.i, a.v), counted because no rule excludes them, and Difficulty of Care payments (counted here; ma_excluded_difficulty_of_care_payments, CO-5214, subtracts them where 8.100.3.K.7 excludes them); uniformed services special pay unless it is paid for service in a combat zone (combat_zone), which 26 U.S.C. 112 leaves out of gross income; and pay in kind (8.100.3.K.3-4; C.1.a.v) unless it is meals or lodging furnished for the employer's convenience (employer_convenience_meals_or_lodging, 26 U.S.C. 119(a)). A pay the record states as combat zone compensation (combat_zone_compensation: for a month during any part of which a member of the Armed Forces served in a combat zone, all of an enlisted member's pay, or the part of an officer's up to the maximum enlisted amount stated as its own record, 26 U.S.C. 112(a)-(b)) is left out. Boarders' payments are counted net of their costs apart (ma_magi_boarder_earnings, CO-6450). A pay received once counts in the month received (42 CFR 435.603(e)(1); 8.100.4.C.1.d.i).

Precision. Earned-income records, Medicaid and CHP+ track E1 (docs/reviews/records-earnings-medicaid.md): replaces wages_gross in ma_person_magi_income (CO-502). The rows are the table's; this item reads no kind by name. Pretax deductions stay the tax-return fact pretax_deductions (CO-080), which CO-502 subtracts. Coverage pass 4 (2026-11-23): pay in kind and an employer's vendor payment are counted (C4-04; before, the table did not count them); basic pay for a combat-zone month is left out as the record states it (C4-02, OQ-1123 settled; before, counted); boarders' payments moved to CO-6450, net of their costs (C4-03, OQ-1121 settled; before, counted here at their gross amount). Field sweep (coverage pass 5, docs/reviews/field-sweep-magi.md): a stream of pay (a record with no month and no date) is the pay of the months its job ran, from the month of its job_start_date through the month of its job_end_date (CO-5100), and MAGI counts the month's income (10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.4.C.4: "current or previous monthly household income"; § 8.100.4.G.1, the month evaluated), so a stream is counted only in those months. Before, a stream was counted in every month, a job that ended in September included in a retroactive or later month.

Type money, scope person-month, program Medicaid.
Uses: `earnings`, `ma_magi_earnings_treatment_table`.

```
the sum for each receipt in Earnings where
    all of the following are true:
      - that receipt is received in the month
      - any of the following is true:
        - it is not the case that that receipt's month is unknown
        - all of the following are true:
          - any of the following is true:
            - that receipt's job start date is unknown
            - the month containing that receipt's job start date is at most the month
          - any of the following is true:
            - that receipt's job end date is unknown
            - the month containing that receipt's job end date is at least the month
      - it is not the case that that receipt's combat zone compensation
      - any of the following is true:
        - Medicaid MAGI: how each kind of earnings is treated (table), for that receipt's kind is one of: counted, counted_no_rule_excludes, excluded_live_in_provider
        - all of the following are true:
          - Medicaid MAGI: how each kind of earnings is treated (table), for that receipt's kind is equal to counted_unless_employer_convenience
          - it is not the case that that receipt's employer convenience meals or lodging
        - all of the following are true:
          - Medicaid MAGI: how each kind of earnings is treated (table), for that receipt's kind is equal to excluded_in_combat_zone
          - it is not the case that that receipt's combat zone
  of
    that receipt's amount
```

### CO-5170 Medicaid SSI method: a person's gross pay from employment `@engine`

The person's earned income of the month other than from self-employment and boarders, before any exclusion, as the SSI method's earnings counting table reads it (ma_ssi_earnings_treatment_table, CO-5107): each earnings record the table counts (wages, salaries, commissions, bonuses and other special payments received because of employment, 10 CCR 2505-10 8.100.5.F.4.a; the kinds counted because no rule excludes them), and each it holds exempt (8.100.5.F.6), or exempt for a dependent child (8.100.3.K.8.c): earned income in gross income, which ma_ssi_excluded_earned_income (CO-2471) then leaves out, at its gross amount, a pay received once in the month received (8.100.5.F.4: 'countable as income in the month received').

Precision. Earned-income records, Medicaid and CHP+ track E1 (docs/reviews/records-earnings-medicaid.md): replaces wages_gross in every SSI-method, long-term care, spousal and buy-in item, through ma_ssi_gross_earned_income (CO-5171). The rows are the table's; this item reads no kind by name. The part set aside under a plan for self-support stays in the pay: it is excluded after the one half (ma_ssi_pass_set_aside_earned_income, CO-5176; 20 CFR 416.1112(c)(9)).
