### CO-5174 Medicaid SSI method: student earned income exclusion basis for the month `@engine`

For a student under 22 regularly attending school, the month's earned income as the SSI method counts it (ma_ssi_gross_earned_income, CO-5171), less the earned income excluded before the student exclusion (the exempt pay, ma_ssi_exempt_earned_receipts, CO-5172, and ma_ssi_excluded_wioa_wages, CO-5179; the infrequent or irregular pay excluded under 416.1112(c)(2), ma_ssi_excluded_infrequent_earned_income, CO-4883), up to the monthly maximum of the student earned income exclusion (20 CFR 416.1112(c)(3), incorporated by 10 CCR 2505-10 8.100.5.H.4.e; H.4.d); 0 for anyone else. ma_ssi_excluded_earned_income (CO-2471) applies the yearly maximum to the running total of it.

Precision. Earned-income records, Medicaid and CHP+ track E1: Medicaid's own statement of the basis, which the shared ssi_student_earned_income_exclusion_basis (CO-3387) said it was to become (its link_basis); CO-2471 reads this item, and CO-3387, which then had no reader, is removed (the split the cross-program allowlist held it for). Coverage pass 3 C3-11, fixed: the exclusions apply in order to the rest of the income (20 CFR 416.1112(a), S3412), so the basis is what the earlier exclusions leave. Coverage pass 4, non-MAGI N4-9 (docs/operators.md, "Ages in a month"): the age is taken in the month evaluated, not on the determination date: an "under N" test on the first day of the month (ma_age_on_first_day_of_month, CO-4978), an "N or older" test on the last day (ma_age_on_last_day_of_month, CO-5402), and a test that excludes the person from what is favorable on the other day.

### CO-5177 Medicaid SSI method: a person's earned income from boarders `@engine`

The part of the person's payments of the month from persons who board or lodge in the person's home that is earned income (10 CCR 2505-10 8.100.3.K.10.c-e, the general income rules the SSI method applies, 8.100.5.F.1): for regular meals only, what the payments exceed the maximum food stamp allotment for a one-person household per boarder and the documentable costs of providing the meals (K.10.c); for lodging only, what they exceed the documentable costs of providing the room (K.10.d); for room and board, what they exceed the one-person allotment per room and boarder and the documentable costs of providing them (K.10.e); each not below zero. Payments for providing foster care are exempt (8.100.5.F.6.l) and are not read.

Precision. Earned-income records, Medicaid and CHP+ track E1 (OQ-1023, settled): the boarder payments are the earnings records the SSI method's counting table counts above the boarder allowance (ma_ssi_earnings_treatment_table, CO-5107, row counted_above_boarder_allowance), each record's boarders and provides read; the costs are the business_cost_boarder_provision records the table deducts from boarder payments (row deducted_from_boarder_payments), each by what it provides. The allotment is the SNAP maximum allotment for a household of one in force in the month (snap_maximum_allotment_table, CO-130), which K.10.c and e name ('the maximum food stamp allotment for one-person household'), read by its adopted-method link. A boarder record that does not state how many boarders it is for, or what they receive, cannot be counted (both required where read, decision 4). Before E1 the SSI method counted payments for a room only or meals only in full as unearned income and room and board payments not at all. Field-effect sweep (docs/reviews/field-sweep-snap-cash-nonmagi.md), FS-MA-2: a record stated as a stream (no month and no date) is received only in the months from the month its job or business began through the month it ended (job_start_date, job_end_date; each absent: before, or through, the months the case covers; CO-5100), since earned income "is countable as income in the month received" (10 CCR 2505-10 8.100.5.F.4, S3001) and wages are counted "when you receive them" (20 CFR 416.1111(a), S4940); a pay stated with its month or date is placed by it, a final pay after the job ended included. Before, a stream was counted in every month whatever its job's dates. The clause is Adult Financial's and Colorado Works' (af_earned_pay, CO-5130; cw_earned_pay, CO-5140).

### CO-5178 Medicaid SSI method: a person's WIOA program wages `@engine`

The person's wages of the month from participation in a program under the Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act (the successor of the Workforce Investment Act that 10 CCR 2505-10 8.100.3.K.8 names): the earnings records the SSI method's earnings counting table counts except for a dependent child applying for or receiving Medical Assistance (ma_ssi_earnings_treatment_table, CO-5107, row exempt_dependent_child_six_months; K.8.a, K.8.c).

Precision. Earned-income records, Medicaid and CHP+ track E1 (OQ-1023): read by ma_ssi_excluded_wioa_wages (CO-5179), which counts the months of the calendar year the wages are exempted in. Field-effect sweep (docs/reviews/field-sweep-snap-cash-nonmagi.md), FS-MA-2: a record stated as a stream (no month and no date) is received only in the months from the month its job or business began through the month it ended (job_start_date, job_end_date; each absent: before, or through, the months the case covers; CO-5100), since earned income "is countable as income in the month received" (10 CCR 2505-10 8.100.5.F.4, S3001) and wages are counted "when you receive them" (20 CFR 416.1111(a), S4940); a pay stated with its month or date is placed by it, a final pay after the job ended included. Before, a stream was counted in every month whatever its job's dates. The clause is Adult Financial's and Colorado Works' (af_earned_pay, CO-5130; cw_earned_pay, CO-5140).

Type money, scope person-month, program Medicaid.
Uses: `earnings`, `ma_ssi_earnings_treatment_table`.

```
the sum for each receipt in Earnings where
    all of the following are true:
      - that receipt is received in the month
      - any of the following is true:
        - it is not the case that that receipt's month is unknown
        - all of the following are true:
          - any of the following is true:
            - that receipt's job start date is unknown
            - the month containing that receipt's job start date is at most the month
          - any of the following is true:
            - that receipt's job end date is unknown
            - the month containing that receipt's job end date is at least the month
      - Medicaid SSI method: how each kind of earnings is treated (table), for that receipt's kind is equal to exempt_dependent_child_six_months
  of
    that receipt's amount
```

### CO-5179 Medicaid SSI method: WIOA wages of a dependent child exempt for the month `@engine`

The person's wages of the month from a Workforce Innovation and Opportunity Act program (ma_ssi_wioa_earned_receipts, CO-5178) that 10 CCR 2505-10 8.100.3.K.8.c exempts: wages 'paid to any dependent child who is applying for or receiving Medical Assistance are exempt in determining eligibility for a period not to exceed six months in each calendar year'. The person is a dependent child as 8.100.1 defines it: under 18, or 18 and a full-time student expected to graduate by 19 (ma_is_dependent_child, CO-544), who lives with a parent, legal guardian, caretaker relative or foster parent (a person of the home, lives_with, toward whom the person is a child, stepchild, ward, foster child or in that person's primary care). The six months are the first six months of the calendar year, through the month, in which the person had such wages; in a seventh or later month the wages are counted (K.8.a counts a caretaker relative's). Otherwise 0.

Precision. Earned-income records, Medicaid and CHP+ track E1 (OQ-1023, settled by K.8.c as written): before E1 every WIOA on-the-job training wage was counted as part of wages_gross. 'Applying for or receiving Medical Assistance' is read as the person whose eligibility the SSI-related figure is for: the exemption is read through ma_ssi_excluded_earned_income (CO-2471), which the applicant's and the couple's countable income read; the ineligible child allocation reads the child's gross income, as before. A month with no WIOA wages uses none of the six.

Type money, scope person-month, program Medicaid.
Uses: `lives_with`, `ma_is_dependent_child`, `ma_ssi_wioa_dependent_child_exempt_months`, `ma_ssi_wioa_earned_receipts`, `relationships`.

```
if Medicaid SSI method: a person's WIOA program wages is at most 0
  then 0
else if it is not the case that (all of the following are true:;   - Medicaid: is a dependent child;   - there is a person in Lives with such that;     this person is a child or stepchild or ward or foster_child or in_primary_care_of of that person)
  then 0
else if (the number of months in the months from the most recent month number 1 on or before the month through the month for which Medicaid SSI method: a person's WIOA program wages is more than 0) is more than Medicaid: months a year a dependent child's WIOA wages are exempt (6)
  then 0
otherwise Medicaid SSI method: a person's WIOA program wages
```

### CO-5200 Medicaid: institutionalized spouse in the institution `@engine`

Whether the person is an institutionalized spouse who is in the institution: in a medical institution or nursing facility, expected to stay at least 30 consecutive days, and married to a spouse who is not (ma_ltc_couple, CO-643). From the month of admission no income of the community spouse is deemed available to this person (42 U.S.C. 1396r-5(b)(1); 10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.7.C.1, C.2.c).

Precision. Only the medical-institution arm of 1396r-5(h)(1)(A): (b)(1) applies "During any month in which an institutionalized spouse is in the institution", so an HCBS or PACE participant living at home with the spouse (an institutionalized spouse for the CSRA and the income allowances under § 8.100.7.K.2.b-c) keeps the couple's mutual availability (§ 8.100.5.H.1.a). The community spouse is not affected: the couple's incomes stay mutually available to that spouse until the month after admission (§ 8.100.7.C.2.b; ma_excluded_from_ssi_household, CO-661). Coverage pass 4, non-MAGI N4-7: per month. 42 U.S.C. 1396r-5(b)(1) speaks of "any month in which an institutionalized spouse is in the institution": for a month before the determination month the person is in the institution from the month of institution_entry_date on (a retroactive month before the admission is not one; the entry date is needed for such a month, decision 4); the determination month and the months after read the setting on the determination date.

Type yes/no, scope person-month, program Medicaid.
Uses: `institution_entry_date`, `ma_ltc_couple`, `resides_in_medical_institution`.

```
all of the following are true:
  - Resides in a medical institution
  - Medicaid: LTC couple with a community spouse
  - if the month is at least the month containing the Determination Date
    then yes
  otherwise the month containing Institution entry date is at most the month
```

### CO-5203 Medicaid: home is subject to estate recovery `@engine`

Whether the person's home is subject to estate recovery for the medical assistance the person would receive under a full-coverage aged, blind or disabled group, so that a recorded beneficiary deed makes it countable (10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.5.M.2.a.xiv, M.3.e): the person is ma_estate_recovery_min_age or older, or lives in a medical institution (42 U.S.C. 1396p(b)(1)(A)-(B)).

Precision. 1396p(b)(1) allows no recovery from anyone else. Its (A) is an inpatient of a nursing facility or other medical institution whom the State finds cannot reasonably be expected to be discharged and return home (1396p(a)(1)(B)); resides_in_medical_institution stands for it, since the volume states no such finding (if not stated, read as not in an institution, as ma_home_is_countable_resource reads it). Medicare cost-sharing and the Medicare Savings Program benefits are never recovered (1396p(b)(1)(B)(ii)); the Medicare Savings Program tests read ma_msp_countable_resources (CO-5206), which leaves the beneficiary-deed home out (OQ-900). Coverage pass 4, non-MAGI N4-9: per month. 42 U.S.C. 1396p(b)(1)(B) reaches assistance an individual received at 55 or older, so the age is taken in the month evaluated; a condition that makes the home countable is met for the month only if it holds on every day of it, so the age is the one on the first day (docs/operators.md, "Ages in a month": a disqualifying condition takes the other day). Before, the determination date's age was read in every month. Pattern sweep, non-MAGI Medicaid (docs/reviews/pattern-sweep-nonmagi.md, P1): whether the person is in a medical institution is read in the month (ma_resides_in_medical_institution_in_month, CO-7500: for a month before the determination month, from the month of institution_entry_date; § 8.100.7.A.2.c.iii, S1753; § 8.100.3.E.1, S1503). Before, the setting of the determination date was read in every month, so a retroactive month before the admission was a month in the institution.

Type yes/no, scope person-month, program Medicaid.
Uses: `ma_age_on_first_day_of_month`, `ma_estate_recovery_min_age`, `ma_resides_in_medical_institution_in_month`.

```
any of the following is true:
  - Medicaid: age on the first day of the month is at least Medicaid: estate recovery age (55)
  - Medicaid: resides in a medical institution in the month, otherwise no
```

### CO-5204 Medicaid: home is a countable resource other than by a beneficiary deed `@engine`

Whether the person's home (a holdings record of kind home, holdings, CO-5300) is a countable resource for the aged, blind and disabled groups for a reason other than a beneficiary deed (10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.5.M.2.a): for a person in a long-term care institution, receiving HCBS or enrolled in PACE, when it has been transferred to a trust or other entity (xiii); or when the person no longer lives in it and neither a spouse nor a dependent relative lives there (ix), unless the person intends to return and, for a person living in an institution or facility, the intent is documented in writing (iv, v, vii, viii, xii).

Precision. The arms of ma_home_is_countable_resource (CO-4622) other than xiv, as that item states them; read alone by ma_home_equity_counted_only_by_beneficiary_deed (CO-5205), which the Medicare Savings Program resources and parental deeming subtract. Resource records, Medicaid track H1 (docs/reviews/records-holdings-medicaid.md): read from the home holdings record (CO-5300) at the determination month: lives_in, intends_to_return, intent_in_writing, outside_colorado and held_in_trust_or_entity are its fields (each read as not so when the record does not state it, as the scalar facts were, except lives_in, which is read from residence_setting_type when not stated, as before; owns_and_lives_in_home, CO-3401, and lives_in_owned_home, CO-4610, the same fact stated twice, are its one field lives_in). A home whose equity the record does not state is read as no home here, as home_equity not stated was (only its countability turns on it; CO-650 reads the equity itself). Coverage pass 4, non-MAGI N4-8 (20 CFR 416.1207(a), S4501: "Resources determinations are made as of the first moment of the month"): a holding the person disposed of is still held at the first moment of the month of its disposed_date and of every month before it, so it is read in those months and left out from the month after (it is then a transfer, ma_uncompensated_transfers_in_lookback, CO-5325); it was left out of every month, the month of disposal included. Coverage pass 4, non-MAGI N4-7 and N4-9: per month, the home record as of the month's first moment (20 CFR 416.1207(a)) and the person's age in the month, since every reader is per month (the person's resources in the month, ma_ssi_countable_resources_in_month, CO-5322; the Medicare Savings Program and parental resource figures); before, every month read the determination month. Coverage pass 4, non-MAGI N4-13 and OQ-1243 (decision 4 of 2026-11-23): the record fields an exclusion rests on (intends_to_return, intent_in_writing) take the default the holdings schema now declares from 8.100.5.E.3 (not so unless shown), not a default of this reader. The fields that would take an exemption away (outside_colorado, held_in_trust_or_entity) are read as the record states them: a record that does not state them cannot be determined, no longer read as not so. Pattern sweep, non-MAGI Medicaid (docs/reviews/pattern-sweep-nonmagi.md, P1): whether the person is in a medical institution is read in the month (ma_resides_in_medical_institution_in_month, CO-7500: for a month before the determination month, from the month of institution_entry_date; § 8.100.7.A.2.c.iii, S1753; § 8.100.3.E.1, S1503). Before, the setting of the determination date was read in every month, so a retroactive month before the admission was a month in the institution.

### CO-5205 Medicaid: home equity counted only because of a beneficiary deed `@engine`

The person's home equity when the home is a countable resource only because a beneficiary deed on it has been executed and recorded (10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.5.M.2.a.xiv, M.3.e): the equity of the person's interest in the home in the month (ma_home_equity_interest_in_month) when ma_home_is_countable_resource holds and ma_home_is_countable_resource_without_beneficiary_deed does not; otherwise 0.

### CO-5222 Medicaid: parental income deemed to a Pickle child `@engine`

The income of this child's ineligible parents deemed to the child for the Pickle test (10 CCR 2505-10 §§ 8.100.6.D-E; 20 CFR 416.1165(d)-(e)), as ma_ssi_parental_income_deemed (CO-4626) deems it but from the Pickle parental income to be deemed (ma_pickle_parental_income_to_be_deemed: the parents' countable income with their OASDI cost-of-living increases since the child lost SSI disregarded, § 8.100.6.E.3, less the Ineligible Parent(s) Allocation), divided among the blind or disabled children sharing it so that no child is deemed more than reduces its SSI benefit to zero (416.1165(e)(2)-(3)): this child, if its share would reduce its benefit to zero (ma_pickle_deeming_share_zeroes_benefit), is deemed its Pickle limit (ma_pickle_deeming_benefit_zero_amount); otherwise what is left after each other child whose limit binds is given its limit is divided equally among this child and the other children whose limit does not bind. Zero when no parent's income is deemed.

Precision. Duplicate-paths audit D-M3 (P1, fixed): before, this item kept the equal division CO-4626 made before the 416.1165(e)(3) fill-up of 2026-11-23, so a Pickle child sharing deemed income with another disabled child was deemed its equal share even where the other child's share reduced that child's benefit to zero and passed the rest on. Each other child's limit is its SSI-related one (CO-5902); this child's is its Pickle limit, figured from its own Pickle income (CO-6056, CO-6057), so only this child's income is read with the Pickle disregard. Whether another child's limit binds is read from that child's own sum at its limit (ma_ssi_deeming_limit_sum, CO-6059) with this child's term changed from its SSI-related limit to its Pickle limit. This child is told from the other children as the one member of its own SSI household (ma_ssi_couple_members: a child to whom parental income is deemed is unmarried, 20 CFR 416.1856), as CO-4626 reads this child among the children.

Type money, scope person-month, program Medicaid.
Uses: `ma_pickle_deeming_benefit_zero_amount`, `ma_pickle_deeming_share_zeroes_benefit`, `ma_pickle_parental_income_to_be_deemed`, `ma_ssi_couple_members`, `ma_ssi_deeming_benefit_zero_amount`, `ma_ssi_deeming_children`, `ma_ssi_deeming_limit_sum`, `ma_ssi_deeming_parents`.

```
else if Medicaid Pickle: the child's share of the deemed income would reduce its benefit to zero
  then Medicaid Pickle: the parental income that reduces a Pickle child's benefit to zero
otherwise (Medicaid Pickle: the parents' income to be deemed to the children minus (the sum of that person's Medicaid: most parental income that can be deemed to the child for each person in all persons in Medicaid: blind or disabled children sharing the deemed parental income such that (all of the following are true:;   - it is not the case that that person is in Medicaid: SSI-method couple;   - ((that person's Medicaid SSI method: deemed income the children can take at this child's limit minus (the lesser of Medicaid: most parental income that can be deemed to the child and that person's Medicaid: most parental income that can be deemed to the child)) plus (the lesser of Medicaid Pickle: the parental income that reduces a Pickle child's benefit to zero and that person's Medicaid: most parental income that can be deemed to the child)) is less than Medicaid Pickle: the parents' income to be deemed to the children))) divided by (the greater of 1 and (the number of persons in all persons in Medicaid: blind or disabled children sharing the deemed parental income such that (any of the following is true:;   - that person is in Medicaid: SSI-method couple;   - it is not the case that ((that person's Medicaid SSI method: deemed income the children can take at this child's limit minus (the lesser of Medicaid: most parental income that can be deemed to the child and that person's Medicaid: most parental income that can be deemed to the child)) plus (the lesser of Medicaid Pickle: the parental income that reduces a Pickle child's benefit to zero and that person's Medicaid: most parental income that can be deemed to the child)) is less than Medicaid Pickle: the parents' income to be deemed to the children)))
```

### CO-5320 Medicaid SSI method: the person's holdings counted in the month `@engine`

The person's own countable resources in the month by the SSI method's holdings counting table (ma_ssi_holding_treatment_table, CO-5303), before the rules that turn on Medicaid's own findings and on the home: each holding the person holds in the month (holdings, CO-5300; not transferred) and is not legally restricted from using (8.100.5.E.3.c, E.4; 20 CFR 416.1201(a)(1): accessible, inaccessible_reason), at the person's share, as its row says. Rows counted: cash, accounts, securities and the rows counted because no rule excludes them (business cash, prorated income held) at the value (10 CCR 2505-10 8.100.5.M.3.a-d; 20 CFR 416.1201(a)-(b)), and an account held jointly with someone other than the spouse at its whole value, "All funds in a joint account are presumed to be a resource of the applicant", unless Medicaid finds the presumption rebutted, then at the person's share (M.3.d; 416.1208(c): ma_joint_account_presumption_rebutted); investment personal property, installment contracts and notes, and other property at their equity, the value less what is owed (M.3.j; 416.1201(c)(1): "Nonliquid resources are evaluated according to their equity value", S2420). The unspent part of a retroactive SSI or Social Security payment: counted from the tenth month after the month of receipt (8.100.5.F.6.c). A federal income tax refund held: counted from the thirteenth month after the month of receipt (26 U.S.C. 6409; ma_federal_tax_refund_resource_exclusion_months, CO-6500); a State or local refund: counted. A State or local earned income tax credit held: counted from the second month after the month of receipt (8.100.5.F.6.u). Proceeds held for replacement, by their source (proceeds_source): from the sale of the home, counted from the fourth month after the month of receipt (8.100.5.P.4; ma_replacement_proceeds_exclusion_months, CO-6501); a relocation payment toward a replacement dwelling, from the seventh (F.6.f; ma_relocation_payment_exclusion_months, CO-7150); cash from insurance or any other source to repair or replace a lost, damaged or stolen excluded resource, from the tenth (20 CFR 416.1232(a); ssi_replacement_cash_exclusion_months, CO-7151; ma_replaces_lost_excluded_resource), and other such cash counted; a condemnation award toward real property from the fourth, toward personal property counted (OQ-1240). Loan proceeds and the payments 8.100.5.F.6 exempts (relocation, disaster and emergency assistance, Civil Liberties Act, Agent Orange, Radiation Exposure and Nazi persecution payments) held: not counted (F.6.a, f, k, r, s, v, x). Retirement accounts: ma_ssi_retirement_accounts_counted_in_month (CO-5326; 8.100.5.N.2). Real property other than the home and other than property producing income or goods for the person's support: its equity (M.3.g; 416.1201(c)(2)). Vehicles: their equity, each floored at 0, less the one automobile used for transportation (ma_ssi_excluded_automobile_equity_in_month, CO-5321; M.2.c, M.3.k; 416.1218(b)). Life insurance: the cash surrender value when the face value of the person's policies is over ssi_life_insurance_face_value_exclusion_limit (M.2.f; 416.1230(a)). Revocable burial funds and contracts, less the interest left in them, over ssi_burial_funds_exclusion reduced by the irrevocable burial funds and by the face value of life insurance whose cash surrender value is excluded (M.2.i-j). Burial spaces not for the person, the spouse or the immediate family, at their equity (8.100.5.M.2.h: for_immediate_family); personal property other than household goods and personal effects, not producing income or goods for the person's support (those are counted above their exclusion by ma_countable_income_producing_property_value, CO-4621), at its equity (M.3.i, M.2.d-e: household_goods_or_personal_effects). ABLE accounts, burial spaces for the immediate family, and household goods and personal effects are not counted.

Precision. Resource records, Medicaid track H1 (docs/reviews/records-holdings-medicaid.md): the figure ssi_countable_resources_individual (CO-800) states for the determination month, read in any month, so the spousal assessment at the application month (ma_spousal_resources_at_snapshot, CO-888) reads the holdings valued in that month. A holding is read in the month it is valued in (P57: its month; one with no month has the same value in every month the case covers; the first moment of the month, 20 CFR 416.1207(a), S4501), and a holding with a disposed_date is a transfer, read by ma_uncompensated_transfers_in_lookback (CO-5325), not held. The person's share is the record's share (absent: the whole holding, CO-5300's declaration); an account is read at its value (liquid, 416.1201(b)), property at its equity, value less what is owed (416.1201(c)(2), S4500). Personal property held as an investment is read at its equity since the holdings H1 integration (docs/reviews/records-holdings-h1-integration.md, I-1): the Medicaid track read it at its value, so an encumbrance stated on it (household CO-740, the Adult Financial track's) was counted, and what is owed on it is required where read, as Adult Financial reads it (af_countable_personal_property, CO-5345). Real property stated income-producing or producing goods for the household's use is counted above its exclusion by ma_countable_income_producing_property_value (CO-4621), not here; a real property record that does not state either is read as neither, and a revocable burial record that does not state accrued interest as having none (each the reading the scalar facts' readers gave, kept for the decision-4 round: docs/reviews/records-holdings-medicaid.md, requests). The face value test and the burial fund exclusion are the person's own (M.2.f, M.2.j: a separate $1,500 for each spouse). Medicaid's findings on real property (CO-4620), the income-producing excess (CO-4621), the home (CO-4622) and the value found available from a trust, an annuity or a life estate are added by ma_ssi_countable_resources_in_month (CO-5322). A couple excludes one automobile: the couple's figures add back the smaller spouse's (CO-608, CO-647, CO-801, CO-888). Coverage pass 4, non-MAGI N4-8 (20 CFR 416.1207(a), S4501: "Resources determinations are made as of the first moment of the month"): a holding the person disposed of is still held at the first moment of the month of its disposed_date and of every month before it, so it is read in those months and left out from the month after (it is then a transfer, ma_uncompensated_transfers_in_lookback, CO-5325); it was left out of every month, the month of disposal included. Coverage pass 4, non-MAGI N4-13 and OQ-1243 (decision 4 of 2026-11-23): the record fields an exclusion rests on (income_producing, produces_for_household_use) take the default the holdings schema now declares from 8.100.5.E.3 (not so unless shown), not a default of this reader. The fields that would take an exemption away (accrued_interest) are read as the record states them: a record that does not state them cannot be determined, no longer read as not so. Field-effect sweep (docs/reviews/field-sweep-snap-cash-nonmagi.md), FS-MA-4: a holding the person cannot get at (accessible false) because it is in probate, frozen by a creditor's lien or levy or a court order, or held under a trust's terms the person can neither revoke nor direct (inaccessible_reason) is not read: Medical Assistance deems available a resource the person "is not legally restricted from using" (10 CCR 2505-10 8.100.5.E.3.c, S4670), and "If a property right cannot be liquidated, the property will not be considered a resource" (20 CFR 416.1201(a)(1), S4500). One a co-owner refuses to release is still read, since a resource is not "unavailable merely because the individual ... may need to initiate legal proceedings to access" it (E.4, S4670). accessible defaults to true (CO-5300); the reason is required where it is false (decision 4). Before, accessible was not read. Field-effect sweep (docs/reviews/field-sweep-snap-cash-nonmagi.md), FS-MA-5: a burial space is excluded only when it is for the person, the spouse or another member of the immediate family (8.100.5.M.2.h, S4504; 20 CFR 416.1231(a)(1), (a)(4), S4943), the record's for_immediate_family; any other is counted at its equity (416.1201(c), S2420). The field's class (CO-5300: the immediate family, "or a brother or sister of one of them, or that person's spouse", Adult Financial's 3.520.77.I) is read as 416.1231(a)(4)'s (children, brothers, sisters, parents and their spouses); where they differ is OQ-1346. FS-MA-6: personal property other than household goods and personal effects (a mobile home or trailer not lived in, equipment, tools) is counted at its equity (M.3.i, S4505), unless it produces income or goods for the person's support, which 8.100.5.J (S3402) excludes up to its limits (CO-4621); before, the row excluded the whole kind. FS-MA-7: a financial institution account (bank_account) held jointly with someone outside the case or another person of the case is counted whole, since M.3.d (S4941) and 20 CFR 416.1208(c)(1) (S4502) presume all the funds the applicant's until the evidence of M.3.d and 416.1208(c)(4) (S4942) rebuts it (ma_joint_account_presumption_rebutted, default false, the rule's); rebutted, at the share the record states. An account held with the spouse is read at its share: the spouse's list states the rest, so a couple counts it once, and a deemed spouse's resources are counted with the person's (416.1202(a)). A person of the case who is also a claimant on the account (416.1208(c)(1), equal shares between claimants) is OQ-1347. FS-MA-9 (OQ-1240 narrowed): held replacement proceeds are read by their source; the good-cause and disaster extensions of 416.1232(b)-(c) (S4944) are a finding no field states (OQ-1240).

### CO-5321 Medicaid SSI method: the equity of the person's one automobile excluded `@engine`

The equity of the one automobile the SSI method excludes for the person in the month: the largest equity (value less what is owed, at the person's share, floored at 0) of the vehicles the person holds that are used for transportation for the person or a member of the household (10 CCR 2505-10 8.100.5.M.2.c, S4504: "One automobile is totally excluded regardless of its value if it is used for transportation"; 20 CFR 416.1218(b)(1), S4660); 0 when none is.

Precision. Resource records, Medicaid track H1: P58 largest (docs/operators.md), over the vehicle records (the holdings table's row counted_less_one_transportation_vehicle) valued in the month and not transferred, whose used_for_transportation is true; a vehicle record that does not state whether it is used for transportation makes the figure unknown (the exclusion turns on it). The equity is floored at 0 record by record, as P58 returns the true largest (a car owing more than it is worth has equity 0, not a negative figure). Excluding the vehicle with the largest equity is the reading most advantageous to the person, the one P58 returns (the market-value reading is OQ-1205's question for Adult Financial; 416.1218(b)(1) and M.2.c exclude one automobile "regardless of value"). 416.1218(b) excludes one automobile "In determining the resources of an individual (and spouse, if any)": the person's own figure (ma_ssi_holdings_countable_in_month, CO-5320) subtracts this, and each figure that adds a couple's resources (ma_ssi_countable_resources, CO-608; ma_institutionalized_spouse_countable_resources, CO-647; ssi_countable_resources_couple, CO-801; ma_spousal_resources_at_snapshot, CO-888) adds back the smaller of the two spouses' figures, so the couple excludes one automobile, the larger. Coverage pass 4, non-MAGI N4-8 (20 CFR 416.1207(a), S4501: "Resources determinations are made as of the first moment of the month"): a holding the person disposed of is still held at the first moment of the month of its disposed_date and of every month before it, so it is read in those months and left out from the month after (it is then a transfer, ma_uncompensated_transfers_in_lookback, CO-5325); it was left out of every month, the month of disposal included. Field-effect sweep (docs/reviews/field-sweep-snap-cash-nonmagi.md), FS-MA-4: a holding the person cannot get at (accessible false) because it is in probate, frozen by a creditor's lien or levy or a court order, or held under a trust's terms the person can neither revoke nor direct (inaccessible_reason) is not read: Medical Assistance deems available a resource the person "is not legally restricted from using" (10 CCR 2505-10 8.100.5.E.3.c, S4670), and "If a property right cannot be liquidated, the property will not be considered a resource" (20 CFR 416.1201(a)(1), S4500). One a co-owner refuses to release is still read, since a resource is not "unavailable merely because the individual ... may need to initiate legal proceedings to access" it (E.4, S4670). accessible defaults to true (CO-5300); the reason is required where it is false (decision 4). Before, accessible was not read.

Type money, scope person-month, program Medicaid.
Uses: `holdings`, `ma_ssi_holding_treatment_table`.

```
the largest for each holding in Holdings where
    all of the following are true:
      - Medicaid, SSI method: how each kind of holding is treated (table), for that holding's kind is equal to counted_less_one_transportation_vehicle
      - that holding is valued in the month
      - any of the following is true:
        - that holding's accessible
        - it is not the case that that holding's inaccessible reason is one of: probate, lien_or_court_order, trust_terms
      - any of the following is true:
        - that holding's disposed date is unknown
        - the month containing that holding's disposed date is at least the month
      - that holding's used for transportation
  of
    the greater of 0 and ((that holding's share, otherwise 1) times (that holding's value minus that holding's amount owed))
```

```json
["largest","holdings",["all",["=",["lookup","ma_ssi_holding_treatment_table",["receipt","kind"]],"counted_less_one_transportation_vehicle"],["received_in",["month"]],["any",["receipt","accessible"],["not",["in",["receipt","inaccessible_reason"],["probate","lien_or_court_order","trust_terms"]]]],["any",["unknown",["receipt","disposed_date"]],[">=",["month_of",["receipt","disposed_date"]],["month"]]],["receipt","used_for_transportation"]],["max",0,["*",["otherwise",["receipt","share"],1],["-",["receipt","value"],["receipt","amount_owed"]]]]]
```

### CO-5322 Medicaid: SSI-related countable resources of the individual in the month `@engine`

This person's own countable resources in the month for the aged, blind and disabled groups and long-term care (10 CCR 2505-10 8.100.5.J, M; 8.100.7.E, H, I): the SSI method's holdings counted in the month (ma_ssi_holdings_countable_in_month, CO-5320), less the real property left out while efforts to sell it are unsuccessful or because its sale would cost a co-owner the co-owner's home (ma_excluded_real_property_value, CO-4620), plus income-producing and self-support property above its exclusion (ma_countable_income_producing_property_value, CO-4621), the person's equity interest in the home when 8.100.5.M.2.a makes it countable (ma_home_is_countable_resource, CO-4622; ma_home_equity_interest_in_month, CO-5327), and the value the Department finds available from a trust, an annuity or a life estate the person holds (each record's ma_found_available_value).

Precision. Resource records, Medicaid track H1: ma_ssi_countable_resources_individual (CO-4623) is this figure at the determination month; ma_spousal_resources_at_snapshot (CO-888) reads it at the application month. Whether the home is countable is judged on the determination date's facts (CO-4622 reads the home's record at the determination month and the person's residence), and its equity in the month in context. A trust, annuity or life estate record whose ma_found_available_value is not stated adds nothing: the Department's determination (8.100.7.E.7.c) is what makes a value available, the reading the scalar fact's reader gave (kept for the decision-4 round). The person's own holdings, not combined with a spouse's. Coverage pass 4, non-MAGI N4-8 (20 CFR 416.1207(a), S4501: "Resources determinations are made as of the first moment of the month"): a holding the person disposed of is still held at the first moment of the month of its disposed_date and of every month before it, so it is read in those months and left out from the month after (it is then a transfer, ma_uncompensated_transfers_in_lookback, CO-5325); it was left out of every month, the month of disposal included. Coverage pass 4, non-MAGI N4-13 (decision 4 of 2026-11-23: missing information is cannot determine unless the rule says otherwise; readers do not invent defaults): the value the Department or the eligibility site found available from a trust, an annuity or a life estate (ma_found_available_value; 8.100.7.E, H.2, I) is read as the record states it; a record of such a holding that states no finding cannot be determined (OQ-1243, resolved for this field), no longer counted as nothing found.

Type money, scope person-month, program Medicaid.

```
(the greater of 0 and (Medicaid SSI method: the person's holdings counted in the month minus Medicaid: excess real property left out while for sale or co-owned)) plus Medicaid: countable income-producing property plus (if Medicaid: the home is a countable resource;   then Medicaid: the person's equity interest in the home in the month; otherwise 0) plus (the sum of that holding's ma found available value for each holding in Holdings where ((all of the following are true:;   - Medicaid, SSI method: how each kind of holding is treated (table), for that holding's kind is equal to counted_value_found_available;   - that holding is valued in the month;   - any of the following is true:;     - that holding's disposed date is unknown;     - the month containing that holding's disposed date is at least the month)))
```

### CO-5325 Medicaid: the person's uncompensated transfers on or after the look-back date `@engine`

The uncompensated value of the holdings the person gave away, sold or otherwise transferred on or after the look-back date (10 CCR 2505-10 8.100.7.F.1.d, F.2.a: the months "prior to the month of application for long-term care services", 60 months for a transfer on or after February 8, 2006, S365, S4671): for each holdings record (CO-5300) with a disposed_date in or after the month ma_transfer_lookback_months before the month of the person's Medical Assistance application (ma_application_date), its fair market value at the transfer, at the person's share and less what was owed against it, less the compensation received (F.1.b, F.1.f, F.2.c.i), never below 0; a transfer the eligibility site finds exempt (the record's ma_transfer_exempt, decision D9; 8.100.7.G.12.a-b, S4672) or that has been returned in whole (G.12.c) is left out.

Precision. Resource records, Medicaid track H1: one transfer, one record, read by every program's look-back (design 3.1); replaces uncompensated_transfer_value_in_lookback (CO-824) and transfer_was_exempt (CO-825), a total with no date and one finding for all of a person's transfers. The look-back is counted in months, as F.1.d defines the period ("the number of months prior to the month of application"): a transfer in the first month of the period is in it whatever its day. The application is the person's (ma_application_date); unknown when it is not stated, as the look-back date then is (decision 4). A transfer after the application is in the period too (F.2: "on or after the look-back period"; F.2.i). A transfer whose holding has been returned in whole (the record's returned_date) is left out: "No period of ineligibility shall be assessed" when "All of the resources transferred without fair consideration have been returned to the individual" (8.100.7.G.12.c, S4672); the scalar total could not say so. Counting the look-back in months rather than from the day 60 months before the application (F.2.a) is OQ-1244. The spouse's transfers are the spouse's records, added by ma_transfer_penalty_months (CO-649). Coverage pass 4, non-MAGI N4-10: the look-back runs from the month of the long-term care application or request (ma_ltc_request_date, CO-6734; § 8.100.7.F.1.d, "the month of application for long-term care services"; 42 U.S.C. 1396p(c)(1)(B)(ii)(I)), read as the Medical Assistance application where the case states no separate request, as that fact's meaning says; it had been counted from the Medical Assistance application date in every case.

Type money, scope person, program Medicaid.
Uses: `holdings`, `ma_application_date`, `ma_ltc_request_date`, `ma_transfer_lookback_months`.

```
the sum of (the greater of 0 and (((that holding's share, otherwise 1) times (that holding's value minus that holding's amount owed)) minus that holding's compensation received)) for each holding in Holdings where ((all of the following are true:;   - it is not the case that that holding's disposed date is unknown;   - the month containing that holding's disposed date is at least Transfer look-back period, months (60) months before the month;   - that holding's returned date is unknown;   - it is not the case that that holding's ma transfer exempt)) for the month containing Medicaid: long-term care application or request date, otherwise Medicaid: application date
```

### CO-5326 Medicaid SSI method: the person's retirement accounts counted in the month `@engine`

The value at which the person's retirement accounts held in the month count as the person's resource (10 CCR 2505-10 8.100.5.N.2, S3401: "Self-funded retirement accounts in the name of the applicant are countable as a resource to the applicant"), at "The gross value of the account, less any taxes due" (N.5.a, S4667: the record's value less its taxes_on_withdrawal), or, when the applicant is not able to provide the taxes due, less ma_retirement_account_default_tax_rate of the gross value (N.5.b: "deducting 20% from the gross value of the account"), at the person's share: each retirement_account holdings record (CO-5300) valued in the month and not transferred.

Precision. Resource records, Medicaid track H1: read by ma_ssi_holdings_countable_in_month (CO-5320) for the person's own figure, and subtracted for a spouse living with the applicant (8.100.5.N.3, by ma_ssi_countable_resources, CO-608) and for a deeming parent (20 CFR 416.1202(b)(1)(i), S3414: pension funds, by ma_ssi_parental_resources_deemed, CO-4627), so the amount subtracted is the amount the spouse's or the parent's own figure counted. N.5 is read for every retirement account record, and the record's self_funded field is not read: retirement_accounts_value (CO-3392), which the records restate, did not tell self-funded accounts from pensions, and N.3 and 416.1202(b)(1)(i) leave both out for the spouse and the parent. Coverage pass 4, non-MAGI N4-8 (20 CFR 416.1207(a), S4501: "Resources determinations are made as of the first moment of the month"): a holding the person disposed of is still held at the first moment of the month of its disposed_date and of every month before it, so it is read in those months and left out from the month after (it is then a transfer, ma_uncompensated_transfers_in_lookback, CO-5325); it was left out of every month, the month of disposal included. Field-effect sweep (docs/reviews/field-sweep-snap-cash-nonmagi.md), FS-MA-4: a holding the person cannot get at (accessible false) because it is in probate, frozen by a creditor's lien or levy or a court order, or held under a trust's terms the person can neither revoke nor direct (inaccessible_reason) is not read: Medical Assistance deems available a resource the person "is not legally restricted from using" (10 CCR 2505-10 8.100.5.E.3.c, S4670), and "If a property right cannot be liquidated, the property will not be considered a resource" (20 CFR 416.1201(a)(1), S4500). One a co-owner refuses to release is still read, since a resource is not "unavailable merely because the individual ... may need to initiate legal proceedings to access" it (E.4, S4670). accessible defaults to true (CO-5300); the reason is required where it is false (decision 4). Before, accessible was not read. Field-effect sweep (docs/reviews/field-sweep-snap-cash-nonmagi.md), defaults list: taxes_on_withdrawal is no longer a required field read with a reader's default; the holdings schema (CO-5300) declares what its absence means, 20% of the value (8.100.5.N.5.b, S4667), so a record that leaves it out is not reported as missing a fact.

### CO-539 Medicaid: highest MAGI income standard the person could qualify under `@engine`

The greatest MAGI income standard, as a decimal fraction of FPL, among the covered groups whose non-income (demographic) criteria this person meets this month - the standard 42 CFR 435.603(d)(4) means by "the eligibility group with the highest income standard" for the 5% disregard.

Precision. Tests each of the four income-tested groups' own non-income criteria directly (not their full category rules, which already fold in the income test the disregard would otherwise be deciding), and takes the greatest of the standards for the groups the person could qualify under, 0 for the rest, via P40 (the greater of two numbers, nested). The Former Foster Care and Needy Newborn groups take no income test at all (8.100.4.H.2.b, 8.100.4.G.7) and so never bound the disregard; they are not inputs to this item. Same-word audit SW-1/SW-3 (engineering follow-up pass, OQ-396): "parent or caretaker relative" is ma_caretaker_relative_of (CO-2606), Medicaid's own reading of the neutral parent, stepparent and has_primary_responsibility_for roles. The children's arm reads ma_is_under_child_age_or_turns_nineteen_this_month (CO-564), the Children's group's own age condition (through the end of the month of the 19th birthday, § 8.100.4.G.2.a), so a person in the month of the 19th birthday has the children's standard for the disregard (final verification pass 3, F3-3). Coverage review F-06: the adult arm's upper age reads CO-4550 (through the end of the 65th-birthday month), as CO-548 does. Coverage review 2, N-01: the adult arm also tests § 8.100.4.G.4.a's condition that every child under ma_magi_child_age_limit of whom the person is a parent or caretaker relative has minimum essential coverage, as CO-548 and CO-552 do. Without it a parent whose child lacks coverage had the Adults group's 133% as her highest standard though the group is closed to her, and so had the disregard in neither group. The parent and caretaker arm reads the dependent child through ma_is_dependent_child_in_month (CO-4791), the child's 18th-birthday month included (§ 8.100.4.G.1). Time audit T-1 (2026-11-23): the Adults group's lower limit (19) reads ma_age_on_last_day_of_month (CO-5402) and the bar for a parent of a child under 19 without coverage reads the child's age on the last day of the month, so each is met if it is met on any day of the month (§ 8.100.4.G.1); it read age (CO-300), the age on the determination date, in every month.

### CO-540 Medicaid: MAGI Children category income standard `@engine`

The income standard in force in the month, as a decimal fraction of the federal poverty level (MAGI-equivalent), that governs the Children's MAGI Medical Assistance category - the greater of the federal minimum floor 42 CFR 435.118(c)(1)(i) sets and Colorado's own percentage stated at 10 CCR 2505-10 8.100.4.G.2.

Precision. Colorado's percentage (ma_income_limit_child_pct, current § 8.100.4.G.2) is above the federal ma_federal_magi_floor_pct floor, so the floor does not bind; it is modeled as a comparison (not a restatement) so a future federal floor increase above Colorado's own percentage would be caught. MAGI close-out, MAGI-SW-1 (2026-11-24; docs/reviews/known-limits.md): per month. A global item is one value per case, so the parameter was read on the determination date in every month that read it (docs/operators.md, Resolution step 2), and a retroactive or application month in another version period of ma_income_limit_child_pct (CO-191: 133% from 2022-04-14, 142% from 2022-06-30) took the determination date's figure. Eligibility in a month is judged on that month (10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.4.G.1, S3351: 'any person who is determined to be eligible for Medical Assistance based on MAGI at any time during a calendar month shall be eligible for benefits during the entire month'), and a retroactive month is one in which the person 'met all applicable eligibility requirements' (§ 8.100.3.E.1, S1503), so the figure of a month is the one in force in it: the version in force on the month's first day, or on the determination date in the determination month, as non-MAGI F7-2 made the personal needs allowance (CO-1987). Rules about the determination itself (presumptive eligibility, CO-2439, CO-3155, CO-708) read it in the determination month.

Type rate, scope person-month, program Medicaid.
Uses: `ma_federal_magi_floor_pct`, `ma_income_limit_child_pct`.

```
the greater of Federal MAGI income floor, percent of FPL (Children, Adults, and Pregnant Women groups) (1.33) and MAGI income limit, Children category, percent of FPL (1.42)
```

### CO-5402 Medicaid: age on the last day of the month `@engine`

The person's whole number of completed years of age on the last day of the month evaluated: the age an "N or older" limit reads where any day of the month counts (10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.4.G.1 for MAGI, S3351; § 8.100.5.C.1, "the first day of the month the person becomes eligible", for the Aged, Blind and Disabled groups, S3900), so that a person who reaches the limit on any day of the month is within it for the whole month.

Precision. A person who is N or older on the last day of the month is N or older on at least that day; one who is under N on the last day is under N on every day of it. So the test is exact for a lower limit (aged 65, the Adults group's 19, the Disabled Adult Child's 18, the Working Adults Buy-In's 16, PACE's 55). A disqualifying age condition flips the day: a person is outside a group for the whole month only when the condition holds on every day, so a disqualifying "N or older" reads the first day (ma_age_on_first_day_of_month, CO-4978) and a disqualifying "under N" this item (the IMD exclusion, CO-1179; the Adults group's bar for a parent of a child under 19 without coverage, CO-548). Time audit T-1 (2026-11-23): the month-scoped age conditions of the Medicaid groups read the age in the month they evaluate, not on the determination date (42 CFR 435.915(a)(2), S218).

Type whole number, scope person-month, program Medicaid.
Uses: `date_of_birth`.

```
the number of whole years between Date of birth and -1 days after the first day of the month after the month
```

### CO-547 Medicaid: meets the Parents and Caretaker Relatives MAGI category `@engine`

Whether the person meets the Parents and Caretaker Relatives MAGI Medical Assistance category under 10 CCR 2505-10 8.100.4.G.3 - a parent or caretaker relative of a dependent child living with them, with household income at or below ma_income_limit_parent_caretaker_pct, applying the ma_magi_income_disregard_pct income disregard of 42 CFR 435.603(d)(4) and 8.100.4.D as the last step only if income above the plain standard would otherwise make the person ineligible.

Precision. 'Living with them' is read from lives_with (CO-1925, from dwelling_id) through ma_caretaker_relative_of (CO-2606); where a case states no dwelling_id, a stated parent or caretaker edge is read as living together (same-word SW-7, convention rule 17). 'Parent or caretaker relative' reads the case's parent and caretaker relationship roles; no degree of relation is tested because Colorado's definition takes 42 CFR 435.4's State option (3): a Caretaker Relative is 'a person who is related to the dependent child or any adult with whom the dependent child is living and who assumes responsibility for the dependent child's care' (§ 8.100.1, S1500), so any relative, and any adult living with the child who assumes responsibility for the child's care, qualifies; a caretaker edge states exactly that (OQ-51, resolved). Per 42 CFR 435.603(d)(4), the disregard disjunct is gated on ma_income_limit_parent_caretaker_pct being this person's highest standard (ma_magi_highest_income_standard_pct, CO-539): it is available here only for a person the Adults group is closed to (65+, Medicare-entitled), not for every parent/caretaker between the parent and caretaker relative limit (ma_income_limit_parent_caretaker_pct, CO-192) and that limit plus the ma_magi_income_disregard_pct disregard, who is placed in the Adults group instead (hard-coded numbers audit R-1: the precision stated 60% and 65%, which the limit has not been since 2022). Dropped the minimum-essential-coverage condition on the dependent child: 8.100.4.G.3 states only the dependent-child relationship, with no MEC condition; the MEC condition belongs to the Adults category (8.100.4.G.4.a, 42 CFR 435.119(c)(1)). Same-word audit SW-1/SW-3 (engineering follow-up pass, OQ-396): "parent or caretaker relative" is ma_caretaker_relative_of (CO-2606), Medicaid's own reading of the neutral parent, stepparent and has_primary_responsibility_for roles. Coverage pass 4, C4-05: the month's figure (ma_magi_monthly_household_income_pct_fpl, CO-6452) is tested first, and the budget figure of C.4.a and C.5 only where it fails, so an applicant eligible on the month is determined where the annualized figure cannot be.

### CO-549 Medicaid: meets the Former Foster Care Children category `@engine`

Whether the person meets the Former Foster Care Children Medical Assistance category under 42 CFR 435.150(b) and 10 CCR 2505-10 8.100.4.H.2.a - under ma_former_foster_care_age_limit or in the month of that birthday (H.2, "until the end of the month of the individual's 26th birthday"), exited foster care at an age from ma_former_foster_care_exit_min_age (CO-3025) through ma_former_foster_care_exit_age_max, and was enrolled in Medicaid at the point their foster care assistance ended. It does not apply to a youth receiving subsidized adoption payments (8.100.4.H.2.a.i); a youth who was in another state's foster care at 18 and enrolled in that state's Medicaid qualifies if the birthday at that minimum age fell on or after ma_former_foster_care_out_of_state_start_date (H.2.a.iii).

Precision. Coverage runs "until the end of the month of the individual's 26th birthday" (H.2): the age is taken on the last day of the month before the month evaluated (ma_age_before_month, CO-4790), so a youth whose 26th birthday falls in the month is in the category for all of it, and one whose birthday fell in an earlier month is not (final verification pass 3, F3-3; the same idiom as ma_is_under_child_age_or_turns_nineteen_this_month, CO-564). Not subject to an income or resource test, per 8.100.4.H.2.b - this item's own test does not read income at all, and no income test is added downstream for a person in this category. The exit-age test now reads ma_age_at_foster_care_exit (CO-095) against the range [18, ma_former_foster_care_exit_age_max], replacing was_foster_youth_at_eighteen's single age-18 test, per 8.100.4.H.2.a's own text ('on their 18th, 19th, 20th or up to their 21st birthday'), which Colorado's extended foster care program makes a real population, not an edge case. H.2.a.ii's exclusion of youth "enrolled in mandatory Medical Assistance" is carried by ma_magi_category's order (CO-551), which tests the Children's, Pregnant and Parent/Caretaker groups before former foster care. H.2.c (the youth's newborn is a needy newborn) needs no rule here: the mother is enrolled in Medical Assistance at the birth, so ma_is_needy_newborn (CO-550) already applies. Pattern sweep, MAGI (2026-11-24, PS-06): whether the foster care at 18 was another state's (ma_foster_care_was_in_another_state) is read as stated, required where read (decision 4: no text presumes Colorado's); H.2.a.i's subsidized adoption exclusion keeps its reading 'not receiving' where the payment type is not stated, the rule's own form ('This extension does not apply to youth that are receiving subsidized adoption payments', S1718).

### CO-5501 Medicaid MAGI: a person's counted unearned receipts `@engine`

The person's receipts of the month that Medicaid's MAGI counting table counts (ma_magi_receipt_treatment_table, CO-5500: counted, or counted because no rule excludes it), each at its gross amount, except a kind the table counts at its taxable amount (counted_taxable_amount: a savings account distribution, cash value taken from an insurance policy), which counts the part in federal gross income the record states (taxable_amount; 26 U.S.C. 61(a), 223(f)(1), 408A(d)(1), 529(c)(3)(B)), a receipt paid once in the month received (42 CFR 435.603(e)(1); 10 CCR 2505-10 8.100.4.C.1.d.i). Gambling winnings are counted apart (ma_magi_gambling_receipts, CO-5502), since b.xiv spreads them for the winner. A pension or annuity counts the taxable part the record states, else its whole amount (counted_taxable_amount_where_stated; 26 U.S.C. 61(a)(8), (10), 72(b)(1), 104(a)(4)), and an income tax refund the taxable part the record states, else nothing (counted_stated_taxable_amount_only; 111(a)) (coverage pass 5, C5-09). Educational assistance counts the part used for living expenses that is in federal gross income, the smaller of for_living_expenses and taxable_amount (counted_taxable_living_expense_part; 10 CCR 2505-10 8.100.4.C.1.d.ii excludes only what is "used for educational purposes and not for living expenses"; coverage pass 7, C7-03). A social security benefit counts its amount less the part recouped for an earlier overpayment and the part received for a person living elsewhere (26 U.S.C. 86(d)(1), (2)(A); field sweep, coverage pass 5).

Precision. Field sweep (coverage pass 5, docs/reviews/field-sweep-magi.md): a stream of receipts (a record with no month and no date) is the payment of the months its source ran, from the month of its start_date through the month of its end_date (CO-5000), and MAGI counts the month's income (10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.4.C.4: "current or previous monthly household income"), so a stream is counted only in those months. Before, a stream was counted in every month. Coverage verification 7, V7-3 (docs/reviews/verify-coverage7-fixes.md): educational assistance tests the taxable amount first: a record whose taxable_amount is 0 (an educational loan, a grant used only for tuition and fees) counts 0 whatever part is for living expenses, the smaller of the two being 0, so for_living_expenses is read only where the taxable amount is more than 0 (M3-C: a tuition-only grant with the living-expense part not stated, wages 1,200 / 1,330 = 90.2%, eligible, was cannot determine).

### CO-551 Medicaid: MAGI covered group `@engine`

Which MAGI Medical Assistance covered group, if any, the person qualifies under this month, evaluated under 10 CCR 2505-10 8.100.4.G's mandatory groups - needy newborn, children, pregnant women, parents and caretaker relatives, former foster care children, and adults - or "none" if the person qualifies under none of them. Transitional Medical Assistance and the four-month extension (§ 8.100.4.I) are reported after the other groups, since they continue coverage for a person who no longer fits one.

Precision. A month before the month of the person's birth is none: no group covers a person not yet born (final verification pass 2, P3-3; ma_magi_eligibility_status, CO-554, reports such a month, and a month before the application outside a requested retroactive period, as ineligible_before_coverage_period). The Pregnant Women group is one test: the person meets the category this month (ma_is_pregnant_category, CO-546) or is in a locked-in pregnancy coverage period (ma_is_in_pregnancy_coverage_period, CO-566); either is enough, so a pregnant woman who meets the category this month is reported pregnant even when the start of her coverage period is not known (an unstated pregnancy_start_date with a retroactive request, F2-1). Evaluated in the order 8.100.4.G lists the mandatory groups, with needy newborn checked first because 8.100.4.G.7 grants it without an income test and it can otherwise overlap with the Children's category for an infant under 1; each subsequent category's own test already excludes anyone who qualified under an earlier-listed category (see ma_is_adult_category, CO-548, and ma_is_former_foster_care_category's federal basis, 435.150(b)(2)), so a person who could qualify under more than one category is placed in the first (highest-priority) one this case expression checks, not necessarily the one with the highest income standard. A child in an open continuous eligibility period (ma_child_is_in_continuous_eligibility_period, CO-561) is reported 'child' ahead of the ordinary category tests, per 42 CFR 435.926(d)/10 CCR 2505-10 8.100.3.Q.1.a's 'without regard to changes in income' rule (the phase-3 review's C-4(a) finding) - but only when the person is not a needy newborn, so a newborn who is also in a CE period (opened by an older sibling's application, for example) still reports needy_newborn, the stronger unconditional entitlement. From January 1, 2027 the Adults group also requires the community engagement condition of 42 CFR 435.119(d) (ma_meets_adult_group_community_engagement_condition, CO-1975, OQ-65): a person who meets the Adults criteria (CO-548) but not the condition is reported none, and ma_magi_eligibility_status (CO-554) gives the reason.

Type one of, scope person-month, program Medicaid.
Uses: `date_of_birth`, `ma_child_is_in_continuous_eligibility_period`, `ma_is_adult_category`, `ma_is_child_category`, `ma_is_eligible_for_four_month_extension`, `ma_is_eligible_for_transitional_medical_assistance`, `ma_is_former_foster_care_category`, `ma_is_in_pregnancy_coverage_period`, `ma_is_needy_newborn`, `ma_is_parent_caretaker_category`, `ma_is_pregnant_category`, `ma_meets_adult_group_community_engagement_condition`.

```
if the month is less than the month containing Date of birth, otherwise no
  then none
else if Medicaid: is an Eligible Needy Newborn
  then needy_newborn
else if Medicaid: child is in a continuous eligibility period
  then child
else if Medicaid: meets the Children MAGI category
  then child
else if any of the following is true:
    - Medicaid: meets the Pregnant Women MAGI category
    - Medicaid: is in the pregnancy coverage period
  then pregnant
else if Medicaid: meets the Parents and Caretaker Relatives MAGI category
  then parent_caretaker
else if Medicaid: meets the Former Foster Care Children category
  then former_foster_care
else if all of the following are true:
    - Medicaid: meets the Adults MAGI category
    - Medicaid: Adults group community engagement condition
  then adult
else if Medicaid: is eligible for Transitional Medical Assistance
  then transitional_medical_assistance
else if Medicaid: is eligible for the four-month extension
  then four_month_extended
otherwise none
```

Field-effect sweep (docs/reviews/field-sweep-snap-cash-nonmagi.md), FS-MA-1: a receipt stated as a stream (no month and no date) is received only in the months from the month of its start_date through the month of its end_date (each absent: before, or through, the months the case covers; CO-5000), since unearned income "is countable as income in the month received" (10 CCR 2505-10 8.100.5.F.5, S3001) and is counted "when you receive it" (20 CFR 416.1123(a), S4940); in its first and last months it is read at its amount, and a payment stated with its month or date is placed by it, a final payment after the stream ended included. ### CO-5512 Medicaid SSI method: a person's gambling winnings received in the month `@engine`

The person's lottery and gambling winnings received in the month (receipts the SSI method's counting table, CO-5510, gives counted_winnings), unearned income in the month received (10 CCR 2505-10 8.100.5.F.4-5, F.5.i). The rules that read it leave it out for a person granted the hardship exemption of F.5.i.1.

Precision. Field-effect sweep (docs/reviews/field-sweep-snap-cash-nonmagi.md), FS-MA-1: a receipt stated as a stream (no month and no date) is received only in the months from the month of its start_date through the month of its end_date (each absent: before, or through, the months the case covers; CO-5000), since unearned income "is countable as income in the month received" (10 CCR 2505-10 8.100.5.F.5, S3001) and is counted "when you receive it" (20 CFR 416.1123(a), S4940); in its first and last months it is read at its amount, and a payment stated with its month or date is placed by it, a final payment after the stream ended included. Before, a stream was counted in every month whatever its dates. The clause is SNAP's (snap_counted_recurring_receipts, CO-5011).

```
    that receipt's amount
```

### CO-5514 Medicaid SSI method: a person's gross unearned receipts `@engine`

The person's unearned income received in the month before any exemption, deduction or disregard: every receipt the SSI method's counting table (CO-5510) treats as income (counted, counted because no rule excludes it, rents, child support, exempt) and a retroactive SSI payment, at its gross amount less the parts that are not the person's income at all (what a death benefit, an inheritance or a settlement paid toward the deceased's last illness and burial or the costs it covers, 10 CCR 2505-10 8.100.5.F.5.a and 20 CFR 416.1121(e), (g); what an award includes for the claim's expenses, 416.1123(b)(3); a veterans benefit's amount for a dependent, 416.1123(e)(1)), plus the amount of a veterans benefit attributable to the person as a dependent, from the stated receipts of any person of the case who receives it and with whom the person resides (the record's for_dependent, on a record whose for_person names this person; 20 CFR 416.1123(e)(2)(i): "we count the amount attributable to you as your unearned cash income if ... You reside with the individual who receives the veterans benefit"); not a loan, an income tax refund, VA Aid and Attendance, a reverse mortgage payment, a reimbursement, the proceeds of converting a resource or a government program's social services or vocational rehabilitation assistance, which are not income (20 CFR 416.1103; 8.100.5.K, L.1, P.1, F.6.w), not current SSI, not money from a sponsor (OQ-972), and not gambling winnings, which the readers add with the hardship exemption (ma_ssi_gambling_receipts). The gross income of long-term care (8.100.7.A.1, ma_ltc_gross_income) and the unearned income to verify for an aged, blind or disabled applicant (8.100.5.B.1.d).

Precision. Coverage pass 4, non-MAGI N4-1, N4-2 and N4-4: the rows the counting table now reads as not income (reverse_mortgage, reimbursement, resource_liquidation, savings_account_distribution, insurance_cash_value, in_home_care_allowance, vocational_training_allowance) are out of the gross income, as loans and tax refunds were (coverage pass 3 C3-10); the 416.1121(e) and 416.1123(b)(3) parts are not income received, so they are out too. The $60 a quarter of 416.1124(c)(6) and the PASS set-aside are exclusions, not "not income", so they stay in (8.100.7.A.1: "before application of deductions, exemptions or disregards"). Field-effect sweep (docs/reviews/field-sweep-snap-cash-nonmagi.md), FS-MA-1: a receipt stated as a stream (no month and no date) is received only in the months from the month of its start_date through the month of its end_date (each absent: before, or through, the months the case covers; CO-5000), since unearned income "is countable as income in the month received" (10 CCR 2505-10 8.100.5.F.5, S3001) and is counted "when you receive it" (20 CFR 416.1123(a), S4940); in its first and last months it is read at its amount, and a payment stated with its month or date is placed by it, a final payment after the stream ended included. Before, a stream was counted in every month whatever its dates. The clause is SNAP's (snap_counted_recurring_receipts, CO-5011). Field-effect sweep (docs/reviews/field-sweep-snap-cash-nonmagi.md), FS-MA-8: of a retroactive payment from a benefit program other than SSI, the legal fees connected with the claim (designated_for_legal_fees, the part of designated_for_lump_sum_costs that is legal fees) are subtracted, and the payment's other designated costs are not: 20 CFR 416.1123(b)(3) (S4756), "If you receive a retroactive check from a benefit program other than SSI, legal fees connected with the claim are subtracted. We do not subtract from any taxable unearned income the part you have to use to pay personal income taxes"; the legal fees are required where read (decision 4 of 2026-11-23): a retroactive payment that does not state them cannot be determined. Before, nothing of designated_for_lump_sum_costs was read. Cross-list records round (docs/reviews/cross-list-records.md), OQ-1348 resolved: the amount of a veterans benefit attributable to the person as a dependent of a person of the case she lives with is her gross unearned income (416.1123(e)(2)(i), S4756), read from that person's receipts as ma_ssi_unearned_receipts (CO-5511) reads it, on the receipts this item reads; so the long-term care gross income and the verification of a dependent living with a veteran include it. Before, the part was taken from the veteran's gross income and added to no one's.

The benefit the Pickle, Disabled Adult Child and disabled widow(er) groups disregard in whole or in part (10 CCR 2505-10 8.100.6.D-E, J; 42 U.S.C. 1383c(d)) and whose January cost-of-living increase the Medicare Savings Programs disregard (8.100.6.L.12, M.7, N.6).

Field-effect sweep (docs/reviews/field-sweep-snap-cash-nonmagi.md), FS-MA-1: a receipt stated as a stream (no month and no date) is received only in the months from the month of its start_date through the month of its end_date (each absent: before, or through, the months the case covers; CO-5000), since unearned income "is countable as income in the month received" (10 CCR 2505-10 8.100.5.F.5, S3001) and is counted "when you receive it" (20 CFR 416.1123(a), S4940); in its first and last months it is read at its amount, and a payment stated with its month or date is placed by it, a final payment after the stream ended included. ### CO-5516 Medicaid: SSI income test `@engine`

The SSI income test as the SSI-related groups apply it (10 CCR 2505-10 8.100.6.C.1, 8.100.6.K.3-4) and as the disabled widow(er) group starts from it: met when the person's SSI-related countable income (ma_ssi_countable_income) is at a rate of not more than the SSI Federal Benefit Rate for the SSI household size (ma_ssi_income_standard), the income test of 42 U.S.C. 1382(a)(1)(A) and (2)(A); otherwise not met. The disabled widow(er) group's test in the absence of the widow(er)'s benefits (42 U.S.C. 1383c(d)(2)) is ma_disabled_widow_meets_ssi_income_test (CO-7943), which reads this one first. Not met, first, for a child whose share of the parental income deemed to several eligible children reduces its SSI benefit to zero (ma_ssi_deeming_share_zeroes_benefit): 20 CFR 416.1165(e)(3) deems no more to such a child than brings its countable income to the Federal Benefit Rate, and says the share 'makes that child ineligible (reduces the amount to zero)'. The one statement of the test both ma_meets_ssi_income_standard (CO-609) and the disabled widow(er) group (CO-1162, through CO-7943) read, so the two cannot read the boundary two ways (T-9 hand check A-3, A-4).

Precision. "At a rate of not more than" (S3950): income equal to the Federal Benefit Rate meets the test. Colorado's texts on file give the SSI-related groups and the disabled widow(er) group no comparison word of their own (S303, S319, S625), so the statute's governs both. The Disabled Adult Child and Pickle groups keep their own Colorado wording ("below", S626; "less than", S624) and do not read this item. The 416.1165(e)(3) arm is read first because the limit is the amount that brings the child's countable income to the rate itself, where "not more than" would otherwise meet the test; (e)(3) settles that child's case in its own words. It is false for everyone but a blind or disabled child sharing deemed parental income with another eligible child (CO-5904). Coverage pass 6, non-MAGI F6-6 (docs/reviews/coverage6-medicaid-nonmagi.md): where no income of an ineligible spouse is deemed (ma_ssi_ineligible_spouse_income_is_not_deemed, CO-7353; 20 CFR 416.1163(d)(1), S5031: 'we subtract only your own countable income from the Federal benefit rate for an individual'), the person's own countable income (ma_ssi_own_countable_income, CO-7354) is compared with the individual rate (ma_ssi_income_standard, CO-2240, then the individual rate). Before, the couple's combined income was compared with the couple rate whatever the spouse's income (INELIG-SPOUSE, CO-906). NM-KL-2 (2026-11-24; docs/reviews/known-limits.md; coverage pass 7, non-MAGI F7-10): the value met_with_oasdi_disregarded, which only the disabled widow(er) group read, compared the Disabled Adult Child figures (CO-1160, CO-7355), every current Social Security benefit taken out; 1383c(d)(2) takes out only the benefits under 42 U.S.C. 402, so the group's own test (CO-7943) reads its own figures (CO-7941, CO-7942), and this item no longer computes a figure that needs the benefit type of each Social Security receipt (CO-5000), so CO-609 never waits on it.

Type one of, scope person-month, program Medicaid.
Uses: `ma_ssi_countable_income`, `ma_ssi_deeming_share_zeroes_benefit`, `ma_ssi_income_standard`, `ma_ssi_ineligible_spouse_income_is_not_deemed`, `ma_ssi_own_countable_income`.

```
if Medicaid: the parental income shared with other eligible children zeroes this child's SSI benefit
  then not_met
else if Medicaid SSI method: an ineligible spouse's income is not deemed
  then (if Medicaid SSI method: the person's own countable income is at most Medicaid: SSI income standard for the person's household size;   then met; otherwise not_met)
else if Medicaid: SSI-related countable income is at most Medicaid: SSI income standard for the person's household size
  then met
otherwise not_met
```

### CO-552 Medicaid: meets a MAGI category's non-income requirements `@engine`

Whether the person meets at least one MAGI covered group's non-income requirements (age, pregnancy, dependent-child relationship, or former-foster-care history) regardless of whether their household income is within that group's standard - used to distinguish a person who has no income-eligible category from a person who has no category at all, whatever their income.

Precision. The former foster care term reads ma_is_former_foster_care_category (CO-549) itself, which has no income half (vocabulary review D-4: it had read the retired was_foster_youth_at_eighteen, CO-054, while the category rule read ma_age_at_foster_care_exit, so the two could disagree). Otherwise restates each category rule's own non-income conditions rather than reading the category rules themselves, because ma_is_child_category and its siblings already combine the demographic test with the income test and cannot be asked for only one half. The Parents/Caretaker demographic term no longer tests minimum essential coverage, mirroring CO-547's fix-round edit (C-3): the MEC condition belongs to the Adults category's own demographic term instead. Same-word audit SW-1/SW-3 (engineering follow-up pass, OQ-396): "parent or caretaker relative" is ma_caretaker_relative_of (CO-2606), Medicaid's own reading of the neutral parent, stepparent and has_primary_responsibility_for roles. The children's age arm reads ma_is_under_child_age_or_turns_nineteen_this_month (CO-564), the Children's group's own age condition (final verification pass 3, F3-3). Coverage review F-06: the adult arm's upper age reads CO-4550 (through the end of the 65th-birthday month), as CO-548 does. Coverage review 2, N-02: the needy newborn arm reads ma_is_needy_newborn (CO-550) itself, which takes the age on the last day of the month before the determination month; the dependent child is ma_is_dependent_child_in_month (CO-4791). Time audit T-1 (2026-11-23): the Adults group's lower limit (19) and the bar for a parent of a child under 19 without coverage read the age on the last day of the month (ma_age_on_last_day_of_month, CO-5402), as CO-548 does; it read age (CO-300), the age on the determination date, in every month.
