### CO-5531 Medicaid: a community spouse's or family member's unearned receipts `@engine`

The unearned income of a community spouse or a dependent family member received in the month, as the spousal impoverishment rules count the person's own income (10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.7.R.2, T.1.c; 42 U.S.C. 1396r-5(d)): every receipt the SSI method's counting table (CO-5510) treats as income other than child support and the cash assistance of Colorado Works and Adult Financial (counted, counted because no rule excludes it, rents, exempt), and a retroactive SSI payment, at its gross amount; not a loan, an income tax refund or VA Aid and Attendance, which are not income, and not the monthly income allowance the institutionalized spouse makes available (allowance_from_institutionalized_spouse), which R.2 leaves out of the community spouse's income 'from sources other than the institutionalized spouse'. Gambling winnings are added by the readers (ma_ssi_gambling_receipts).

Precision. Child support and Colorado Works or Adult Financial cash are left out, as the ledger read the community spouse's and the family members' income before receipt records (child_support_received, tanf_cash_income and adult_financial_cash_income were not among the facts summed); OQ-974 asks whether they belong. VA Aid and Attendance (the receipts of kind va_aid_and_attendance) is left out, an assumption pending OQ-1050: 8.100.5.K (S2900) says the portion "shall not be considered as income when determining eligibility", and this figure is post-eligibility (the community spouse monthly income allowance and the family allowance are deducted after the institutionalized spouse is determined eligible, 42 U.S.C. 1396r-5(d)(1)-(2), S4201; 8.100.7.T.1, S1736), where 8.100.7.R.2 (S1756) measures "gross income" and K.1-2 speak only of the institutionalized veteran's patient payment. The text does not settle it the other way either: 8.100.5.F.5.j.vi (S3001), the income section for the long-term care programs, lists "Veterans benefits other than Aid and Attendance (A&A) and Unusual Medical Expenses (UME)" as unearned income, and 20 CFR 416.1103(b)(1) (S4200) gives "Cash given you by the Department of Veterans Affairs to purchase aid and attendance" as not income at all; neither is tied to eligibility. Counting it would lower the allowance by the amount of the portion (OQ-1050 gives a worked example). Field-effect sweep (docs/reviews/field-sweep-snap-cash-nonmagi.md), FS-MA-1: a receipt stated as a stream (no month and no date) is received only in the months from the month of its start_date through the month of its end_date (each absent: before, or through, the months the case covers; CO-5000), since unearned income "is countable as income in the month received" (10 CCR 2505-10 8.100.5.F.5, S3001) and is counted "when you receive it" (20 CFR 416.1123(a), S4940); in its first and last months it is read at its amount, and a payment stated with its month or date is placed by it, a final payment after the stream ended included. Before, a stream was counted in every month whatever its dates. The clause is SNAP's (snap_counted_recurring_receipts, CO-5011). NM-KL-1 (2026-11-24; docs/reviews/known-limits.md): the allowance the institutionalized spouse makes available to the community spouse is income to her (8.100.5.I.4, S5360), so the SSI method's table counts it (CO-5510), and her own eligibility reads it; this figure leaves it out, since the allowance is figured from her income 'from sources other than the institutionalized spouse' (8.100.7.R.2, S1756) and counting it here would lower the allowance by itself.

### CO-554 Medicaid: MAGI eligibility status `@engine`

The reason code for the person's MAGI Medical Assistance eligibility this month - full eligibility, emergency-Medicaid-only, pending because an applicant who meets the Adults group criteria has not shown that the community engagement requirement is met and the notice of noncompliance is due or its 30-day showing period is running (42 CFR 435.558(a)), ineligible because the person meets the Adults group criteria but not the community engagement requirement that conditions that group from January 1, 2027 (42 CFR 435.119(d)) and the showing period has ended, ineligible because household income exceeds every category the person could otherwise fit, ineligible because the person is not a Colorado resident, or ineligible because the person fits no MAGI category's demographic requirements at all; or, for a month the application cannot cover - before the person's birth, or before the month of application and outside a requested retroactive period (ma_month_is_before_coverage_period, CO-4101) - ineligible_before_coverage_period; or, for a month after the month of the person's death (date_of_death), ineligible_deceased. An inmate of a public institution who meets a MAGI category, is in a pregnancy coverage period, or is a child in a continuous eligibility period is enrolled with benefits limited to an inpatient stay of 24 hours or longer in a medical institution and, in the 90 days before release, Reentry Demonstration Initiative services (incarceration_limited; 10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.3.G.1.b.ii, S3361; for a continuous eligibility child, § 8.100.3.Q.1.b.ii.1).

Precision. Coverage pass 7, C7-06 (2026-11-24): a month after the month of the person's death is ineligible_deceased, tested after the months the application cannot cover and before every other row. An application may be made for a person who has died (42 CFR 435.915(a)(2), S218: 'regardless of whether the individual is alive when application for Medicaid is made'; 42 U.S.C. 1396a(a)(34) as amended, S1706: 'application was made on the individual's behalf in the case of a deceased individual'), and it covers the months in which the person would have been eligible 'at the time he received the services' (S218); the month of death is such a month, since a person eligible at any time during a calendar month is eligible for the entire month (10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.4.G.1, S3351). No month after it is: the rule ends even the periods that continue regardless of other changes when 'The member is deceased' or the 'Child is deceased', effective in the earliest possible month (§ 8.100.4.G.6.a.i, S3755; § 8.100.3.Q.1.b.i, S1502; 10 CCR 2505-3 § 430.2.B.i, S1714), and no category covers a person after death. The death is read from date_of_death (CO-2868, 'Not stated for a living person'), through is_deceased (CO-2200) for the month before. Before, such a month was answered by the person's facts as if alive (DIED-RETRO: died 2026-08-20, application 2026-09-15 with a request, $1,000: September to December eligible). A month the application cannot cover (CO-4101) is checked first: whether the person would have met a category then does not make the month eligible (10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.3.E.1-2). Where whether the person is in a locked-in pregnancy coverage period is unknown (a retroactive request with no pregnancy_start_date, F2-1), a person who meets the Pregnant Women category this month and is not limited to emergency Medicaid is eligible without it. Residency is checked next because it is a threshold requirement of every category; a child in an open continuous eligibility period (ma_child_is_in_continuous_eligibility_period, CO-561) is reported eligible next, per 42 CFR 435.926(d)/10 CCR 2505-10 8.100.3.Q.1.a's 'without regard to changes in income' rule (the phase-3 review's C-4(a) finding) - checked ahead of emergency-only and the income/no-category branches so a CE period is not defeated by a later citizenship or income change; emergency-only is checked next because 8.100.3.G.1.g.viii.2 (S175) grants it to a resident who fails citizenship but otherwise meets the plan's requirements, matching ma_is_emergency_medicaid_only's own scope (CO-510); The emergency-only branch also requires a MAGI category, because ma_is_emergency_medicaid_only (CO-510) now covers the SSI-related and long-term care routes too, and this is the MAGI status (the cross-chapter emergency determination is ma_emergency_medicaid_status, CO-1151); the income/no-category distinction (ma_meets_some_category_demographics, CO-552) is checked last, only once residency, continuous eligibility, and citizenship are settled. Coverage review F-07: § 8.100.3.G.1.b.ii (S3361) limits every eligible inmate's benefits, not only a continuous eligibility child's, so an inmate of a public institution (CO-1105) who meets a MAGI category, or is in a pregnancy coverage period, is incarceration_limited; the row follows the continuous eligibility rows (an inmate child in a period is already incarceration_limited) and precedes the full-benefit rows. An inmate limited to emergency Medicaid by status stays emergency_only. G.1.b.ii says 'incarcerated in a correctional institution'; the row reads 435.1010's inmate of a public institution, as the continuous eligibility row and CHP+ (§ 120.1.C, 430.2.B) do. Whether the person is an inmate is read for the month (ma_is_inmate_in_month, CO-7555: in the institution on every day of the month, from institution_entry_date) and is required where read: where the setting facts are not stated the status cannot be determined (pattern sweep, MAGI, PS-05, 2026-11-24: the reading "not an inmate" had no rule; decision 4). Coverage pass 5, C5-04 (2026-11-23): § 8.100.3.G.1.c (S659), "To be eligible to receive Medical Assistance, an eligible person shall: ... Not be a patient in an institution for tuberculosis or mental disease, unless the person is under 21 years of age or has attained 65 years of age", is a condition of every category, and no row read it: a patient of 21 to 64 in an institution for mental diseases (ma_meets_imd_requirement false, CO-1179) was reported eligible although ma_magi_is_fully_eligible (CO-562) was false. Such a month is ineligible_institution, tested after the continuous eligibility rows (a child in a period is under 21, so the exclusion never reaches one) and before the inmate, pregnancy-period and category rows: the pregnancy coverage period continues coverage "regardless of changes in the woman's financial circumstances" (G.5), and G.1.c is not a financial circumstance, so the period does not lift it. Whether the CMS-approved 1115 demonstration Colorado Expanding the Substance Use Disorder Continuum of Care, which § 8.100.3.G.1.b.ii incorporates for reentry services, lifts the exclusion for a stay in an institution for mental diseases for substance use treatment is OQ-1325: G.1.c names no exception for it. Pattern sweep, MAGI (2026-11-24, PS-06): where whether she is in a pregnancy coverage period is not known, a month in which she meets the Pregnant Women category is eligible (F2-1) and any other month cannot be determined (it was read as not in the period, and the inmate row read an unknown period as none).

### CO-555 Medicaid: continuous eligibility applies `@engine`

Whether continuous eligibility under 10 CCR 2505-10 8.100.3.Q and 42 CFR 435.926 applies to the person this month - under 19, currently eligible for the Children's MAGI category on the plain category test (ma_is_child_category), and a Colorado resident. HCPF fix round (C-7): a period that began in SSI Mandatory or long-term care services, or when the child left Foster Care Medicaid to live with relatives, reunite with parents or under guardianship, also opens one, and the child is categorized in the MAGI Children's category for the rest of it (§ 8.100.3.Q.2.b.i, c.i, Q.3; ma_continuous_eligibility_program, CO-2446). Periods that began in the Children with Disabilities Buy-In, Pickle, Disabled Adult Child or Limited Family Planning stay in those programs (ma_child_is_in_non_magi_continuous_eligibility_period, CO-2448).

Precision. This item states the age, category and residency conditions of 8.100.3.Q.1 and 435.926(b) and the residency exception of 8.100.3.Q.1.b.iv; the other exceptions end a period already open, so ma_child_is_in_continuous_eligibility_period (CO-561) tests them month by month through ma_continuous_eligibility_exception_applies (CO-2205; OQ-53, resolved). This item is a per-month test (whether CE would open or continue to apply in the month it is asked about); ma_child_is_in_continuous_eligibility_period (CO-561) reads it [at] the period's start month specifically - not the current month - so that the category test that opens the period is not re-run, and defeated, by the very income change 435.926(d)/8.100.3.Q.1.a says the period protects against. The age condition reads ma_is_under_child_age_or_turns_nineteen_this_month (CO-564), the test the Children category itself uses, so the category and continuous eligibility agree in the month the child turns 19. Colorado's section 1115 authority for longer continuous eligibility (children up to age three, people leaving incarceration) was never implemented and expired June 30, 2026 (CMS letter of June 30, 2026, S1713), so § 8.100.3.Q's 12-month period is the whole rule (HCPF review C-10).

The first month of the retroactive Medical Assistance coverage period under 10 CCR 2505-10 8.100.3.E.1 and 42 CFR 435.915(a): ma_retroactive_coverage_months_for_application (CO-2472) months before the month of application - three for an application made before January 1, 2027, then one for an expansion adult and two for anyone else (42 U.S.C. 1396a(a)(34) as Pub. L. 119-21 sec. 71112 amended it). Whether the person is covered in a month of the period is decided by that month's own facts (ma_magi_eligibility_status, CO-554): a month before the person became eligible is a month whose facts do not make the person eligible. That date is an outcome of the months' own facts (the first month in which the person met every requirement), stated a second time, and a stated date later than the facts show closed retroactive months the facts make eligible (CO-137: May 2026 ineligible_before_coverage_period with the date 2026-06-01 stated, eligible on its own facts), while an unstated date left the whole window unknown (C7-01). 42 CFR 435.915(a)(2) (S218) covers a retroactive month in which the person 'Would have been eligible for Medicaid at the time he received the services', and 42 U.S.C. 1396a(a)(34) as amended (S1706) one in which the person 'was (or upon application would have been) eligible for such assistance at the time such care and services were furnished': eligibility is a fact of each month, which CO-554 decides month by month, so the later of the two dates is the first month the facts make the person eligible, and no date is stated twice (product-owner rule, 2026-11-21: facts another record can supply are read from it, not entered twice). Coverage is stated by month. Reads ma_retroactive_coverage_months_for_application (CO-2472), whose figures are parameters (ma_retroactive_coverage_months, CO-197, and the 2027 figures).

### CO-561 Medicaid: child is in a continuous eligibility period `@engine`

Whether this month falls inside a child's 12-month continuous eligibility period under 42 CFR 435.926(d) and 10 CCR 2505-10 8.100.3.Q.1.a - continuous eligibility applied at the period's start month, the person is still under ma_magi_child_age_limit, still meets residency, and this month is on or before ma_child_continuous_eligibility_end_month.

Precision. 435.926(d) is the operative sentence: 'A child's eligibility may not be terminated during a continuous eligibility period, regardless of any changes in circumstances,' subject to the listed exceptions: age 19 and residency are tested here, and the other exceptions of § 8.100.3.Q.1.b (death, inmate status, leaving the required household, being unable to be located, a withdrawal request, an expired reasonable opportunity period, an erroneous grant) through ma_continuous_eligibility_exception_applies (CO-2205), read in this month (OQ-53, resolved). A period CBMS has recorded (continuous_eligibility_period_start_month stated, CO-094) stands as recorded: the determination that opened it found the child eligible (§ 8.100.3.Q.1, "who through an eligibility determination, reassessment or redetermination, are found eligible"; 435.926(b)(2), "Eligible and enrolled"), so the past month's category test is not re-run from income facts that may not be stated for that month (heavier-definitions audit H-5). The recorded period counts here when it began in MAGI Medical Assistance, SSI Mandatory, long-term care or at a foster care exit (ma_continuous_eligibility_program, CO-2446; § 8.100.3.Q.2.b.i, c.i, Q.3); a period that began in the Buy-In, Pickle, DAC or Limited Family Planning is CO-2448's. Only a period the application being determined would open is computed: ma_continuous_eligibility_applies [at] the application month (not this month), per the note on CO-555, so a later month's income rise cannot retroactively make the period never have applied. The months run from the recorded start month, or the application month when none is recorded, through ma_child_continuous_eligibility_end_month (CO-556). The age condition reads ma_is_under_child_age_or_turns_nineteen_this_month (CO-564), the test the Children category itself uses, so the category and continuous eligibility agree in the month the child turns 19. Coverage pass 6, C6-08 (2026-11-24): with no recorded period, the period opens in the first month of the application, through the determination month, in which continuous eligibility applies (ma_child_continuous_eligibility_start_month, CO-7405; § 8.100.3.Q.2: the month all criteria are met, or the month of a transition from CHP+), not only in the application month. Pattern sweep, MAGI (2026-11-24, PS-06): a recorded period's program (ma_continuous_eligibility_program) is read as stated, required where the recorded start is (decision 4; was read as magi).

### CO-562 Medicaid: is fully eligible for MAGI Medical Assistance (not emergency-only) `@engine`

Whether the person is eligible for full-scope MAGI Medical Assistance benefits, as distinct from the emergency-only benefit 42 CFR 435.406(b) and 10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.3.G.1.g.ix.2 grant to a person who otherwise qualifies but fails citizenship - a Colorado resident, not excluded as a patient in an institution for mental diseases (§ 8.100.3.G.1.c), who qualifies under at least one MAGI covered group and either meets the citizenship and immigration status requirement (CO-509) or, in the Children's or Pregnant category (including a needy newborn), is a Cover All Coloradans person (§ 8.100.3.G.1.g.ix.1.a, CO-1173).

Precision. Distinct from ma_magi_is_eligible (CO-553), which is true for both full and emergency-only coverage. It is the MAGI part of what 10 CCR 2505-3-120.1.B's "eligible to receive assistance under Title XIX" exclusion and 42 CFR 457.310(b)(2)(i)'s "found eligible or potentially eligible for Medicaid" mean for CHP+: the whole test is ma_has_full_coverage_category (CO-1176), which adds the SSI-related, OAP SISC B, protected-group, Buy-In, long-term care and needy-under-21 categories (final verification pass 3, F3-2; this precision had called this item the whole test). A person whose only Title XIX entitlement is emergency services has nothing CHP+ needs to defer to. Cover All Coloradans reaches only the MAGI Children and Pregnant categories (ix.1.a; S-2, OQ-214), so an undocumented postpartum or 19-year-old person in the Adult or Parent and Caretaker Relative category is not fully eligible; and § 8.100.3.G.1.c's IMD exclusion is applied (S-5, CO-1179). OQ-214 sweep: C.R.S. 25.5-2-104(2) makes a child under 19 who would be eligible for medical assistance but for immigration status eligible for state medical assistance with the same benefits, and C.R.S. 25.5-5-201(6)(a) makes a pregnant non-citizen who meets every other requirement eligible for medical assistance; neither is limited to the categories § 8.100.3.G.1.g.ix.1.a-b lists, so a child or pregnant person in any MAGI category is fully eligible whatever their status. A postpartum person who was not covered while pregnant is reached only by the rule's ix.1 list (still OQ-214). Coverage pass 5 (2026-11-23, the class of C5-02 and C5-03): pregnancy is read for the month evaluated (ma_is_pregnant_in_month, CO-3601), not on the determination date (is_pregnant), so a retroactive month in which the person was pregnant is a pregnant month although the pregnancy has ended, and a month before a pregnancy began is not. Pattern sweep, MAGI (2026-11-24, PS-01, PS-02): status and the Cover All Coloradans population are read for the month evaluated (ma_meets_citizenship_requirement_in_month, CO-7551; ma_is_cover_all_coloradans_person_in_month, CO-7552; ma_meets_status_for_cover_all_coloradans_categories_in_month, CO-7553), not on the determination date: 8.100.4.G.1 (S3351), 8.100.3.E.1 (S217), 8 U.S.C. 1613(a) (S176), ix.1's 'current month' (S607).

### CO-564 Medicaid: under the child age limit, or turns 19 this month `@engine`

Whether the person's 19th birthday (ma_magi_child_age_limit) falls in the month evaluated or later - the person was under ma_magi_child_age_limit on the last day of the month before (ma_age_before_month, CO-4790) - the age condition 8.100.4.G.2.a states as "eligible ... through the end of the month in which they turn 19 years old," which 8.100.3.G.1.g.ix.1's Cover All Coloradans exception and 10 CCR 2505-3-110.1.B.5.o (CHP+) state as "under the age of 19, whose 19th birthday occurred in the current month".

Precision. Age is taken on the day before the first day of the month evaluated (the last day of the month before, ma_age_before_month, CO-4790), with the same day-before idiom snap_abawd_countable_month (CO-416) and af_is_oap_age (CO-940) use for a birthday month. A person who is under 19 on that day either is still under 19 on the determination date or turned 19 during the determination month, on or before the determination date; both are inside "the month in which they turn 19". A person who turned 19 in an earlier month is not. Final verification pass 3, F3-3: the test had been "age 19 and the birth month equals the determination month" with the birth month taken as a year-month (for example 2007-11 against 2026-11), which is never equal, so a person whose 19th birthday fell earlier in the determination month was outside the Children's group, Cover All Coloradans and CHP+. Time audit T-1 (2026-11-23): measured in the month evaluated, not the determination month, so a retroactive month (42 CFR 435.915(a)(2), S218: "would have been eligible ... at the time") and an application month before the determination month read the person's age in that month; a rule about the determination itself reads it [at] the determination month.

Type yes/no, scope person-month, program Medicaid.
Uses: `ma_age_before_month`, `ma_magi_child_age_limit`.

```
Medicaid: age on the last day of the month before the month is less than MAGI household child age limit (19)
```

### CO-565 Medicaid: pregnancy coverage period start month `@engine`

The first month of the pregnancy coverage period the month evaluated falls in, under 10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.4.G.5 and 42 U.S.C. 1396a(e)(5) and (e)(16): the first month, from ma_pregnancy_coverage_period_search_start_month (CO-7774: the application's first month - the first month of the requested retroactive period (ma_retroactive_coverage_requested, CO-4100; § 8.100.3.E.1-2), or else the month containing ma_application_date - or, where later, the month after the last pregnancy whose postpartum year ended before the month evaluated) through the determination month, in which a period begins (ma_pregnancy_coverage_period_begins_in_month, CO-7775: it opens in the month, ma_pregnancy_coverage_period_opens_in_month CO-7401, for a pregnancy with a recorded end on or after it or that continues); where no such month begins one, the month containing ma_application_date. Informational: ma_is_in_pregnancy_coverage_period (CO-566) reads the same months, not this item.

Precision. Coverage pass 7, C7-02 (2026-11-24): the months searched start after the last pregnancy whose postpartum year ended before the month evaluated (CO-7774), and a month begins a period only for a pregnancy that has a recorded end on or after it or continues (CO-7775), so a later pregnancy has its own start month (PG-SECOND: member since 2025-03, birth 2025-09-10, pregnant again from 2026-10-05; for November 2026 the search runs from 2025-10, the month after the 2025-09 birth, whose year ended with 2026-09, and finds nothing at $5,500; before, March 2025). The first month is counted with sum_months (P54) over the months searched, so the search start of the month evaluated is read for each candidate. Without a request for retroactive coverage (ma_retroactive_coverage_requested false or not stated) no retroactive month is read: § 8.100.3.E.1 provides retroactive assistance only to a person who 'shall have received medical services at any time during that period', and E.2 makes it a request on the application or a later verbal request. Month-level, matching this volume's month-keyed person-month outcomes; a coverage period that begins mid-month is treated as beginning with that whole month, consistent with 8.100.4.G.1's whole-month-eligibility rule. The retroactive window is the three months before the application month for an application made before ma_retroactive_coverage_change_date, and ma_retroactive_coverage_months_other_after_change (two) for a later one: a person whose period opens in a retroactive month is in the Pregnant Women category in the application month, never in the Adults group, so the one-month figure for expansion adults (CO-2472) never applies to her; reading CO-2472 here would make the rule circular (CO-2472 reads the application month's category, which reads this item). The months are tested in order and the first that opens the period is the start; a month whose opening is unknown before any month opens it leaves the start unknown. Coverage pass 6 (2026-11-24): C6-01, the months searched run from the application month (or the first requested retroactive month) through the determination month, not the application month alone, so a member enrolled before her pregnancy (her application month long before it) opens the period in the first month she received Medical Assistance while pregnant (42 U.S.C. 1396a(e)(5), S5060); C6-02, an applicant ineligible in the application month and eligible as a pregnant woman in a later month of the same application opens it in that month (G.5; 8.100.3.E.2, 'An applicant does not have to be eligible in the month of application'). Stated per person per month because the rule reads the months' facts; the value is the same in every month evaluated.

Type month, scope person-month, program Medicaid.

### CO-566 Medicaid: is in the pregnancy coverage period `@engine`

Whether the month falls within a pregnant or recently-pregnant person's locked-in Medical Assistance coverage period under 10 CCR 2505-10 8.100.4.G.5 and 42 U.S.C. 1396a(e)(5) and (e)(16), during which "coverage will be provided regardless of changes in the woman's financial circumstances": a period begins in a month of the application, through the determination month and no later than the month evaluated, in which it opens for a pregnancy (ma_pregnancy_coverage_period_begins_in_month, CO-7775; the opening test is ma_pregnancy_coverage_period_opens_in_month, CO-7401), and runs through the 12th month after the end of that pregnancy (ma_postpartum_coverage_months), or while it continues; the months searched for the month evaluated start at ma_pregnancy_coverage_period_search_start_month (CO-7774), after the last pregnancy whose postpartum year ended before it, so each pregnancy has its own period. With no application date stated: false for a person the case records as never pregnant or whose last pregnancy's postpartum year ended before the month (not pregnant now), otherwise unknown.

Precision. Coverage pass 7 (2026-11-24): C7-02, a period ended only when the person was no longer pregnant on the determination date, so a member whose first pregnancy's postpartum year had ended and who was pregnant again was read as still in the first period (PG-SECOND: member since 2025-03, birth 2025-09-10, pregnant again from 2026-10-05, $5,500; October and November 2026 were eligible as pregnant; by hand, size 3, 5,500 / 2,276.67 = 241.6%, less 5 = 236.6% > 195%: ineligible_income). Each period now ends with the postpartum year of the pregnancy current in its first month, and a later pregnancy opens its own period only in a month of that pregnancy (CO-7774, CO-7775; the history arm of CO-7401). C7-05: with no application date stated the period was read as closed (false), so a member in her postpartum year whose original application date was left out (a renewal, CO-088) was ineligible_income; now it cannot be determined, unless the case records no pregnancy at all or her last pregnancy's postpartum year ended before the month and she is not pregnant now (decision 4 of 2026-11-23). ma_pregnancy_coverage_period_start_month (CO-565) is informational. Recorded approval first, computed approval second, as continuous eligibility reads its period (CO-561). The computed arm reads ma_is_pregnant_category (CO-546) [at] the start month, not this month: without it every pregnant applicant was locked into Medicaid whatever her income, so CHP+ prenatal (10 CCR 2505-3 § 110.1.F) was unreachable. It reads the two income verification pending flags (CO-1624, CO-1625) [at] the start month after the category, so an applicant over the standard is decided without them; an applicant within the standard whose verification state is not stated is unknown, not locked in. A history not stated, none, or another category for the start month: the category is computed (C5-01). True for every month from ma_pregnancy_coverage_period_start_month (inclusive) through ma_postpartum_coverage_end_month (inclusive) for a currently pregnant person, or a person whose pregnancy has ended within that window; false once the postpartum coverage of each pregnancy whose period began in the months searched has run out; with no ma_application_date, as the meaning states (C7-05). Coverage review F-16 (fix round 2026-11-23): for the Legal Immigrant Prenatal population (ma_is_legal_immigrant_prenatal_population, CO-5219) the period ends on the events of § 8.100.4.G.6.a: death (i), leaving the required household (iii), unable to be located (v), a withdrawal request (vi) and an erroneous grant (viii), read from the same facts as the continuous-eligibility exceptions of § 8.100.3.Q.1.b (ma_continuous_eligibility_exception_applies, CO-2205). Residency (iv) and becoming an inmate (ii) are carried by ma_magi_eligibility_status (CO-554: ineligible_residency, incarceration_limited). A reasonable opportunity period that ends with documents pending (vii) is carried by the verification outcome, not here: the pending status verification count reads this period, so reading it back would be circular. Coverage pass 6, C6-03 (2026-11-24): the end of the pregnancy is read from most_recent_pregnancy_end_date (CO-7400), so a birth recorded by the child's date of birth and the gave_birth_to relationship ends it; a person not pregnant now who states a pregnancy_start_date with no end and no birth recorded cannot be determined after the start month (the end month is unknown), not read as never pregnant.

### CO-5900 Medicaid: SSI-related unearned income after allocations, before parental deeming `@engine`

The SSI-related household's own unearned income before the $20 general disregard and before any parental income is deemed (10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.5.H.3-4): the combined gross unearned income of the person and a spouse living with the person (ma_ssi_household_unearned_income_sum), less the Ineligible Child Allocation taken from an ineligible spouse's unearned income, plus, for an unemancipated child, the child support the child receives reduced by one third (H.4.c). For a child this is the child's own unearned income that 20 CFR 416.1165(e)(1) combines with the deemed parental income, and that 416.1165(e)(3) calls the child's own income.

### CO-5902 Medicaid: most parental income that can be deemed to the child `@engine`

The amount of parental income which, deemed to this child as unearned income and combined with the child's own income, reduces the child's SSI benefit to zero: the least deemed amount at which the child's countable income, figured as 20 CFR 416.1165(e)(1) figures it (the deemed income added to the child's own unearned income, ma_ssi_household_unearned_income_before_deeming, the $20 general exclusion applied to the sum, and the countable earned income added), reaches the SSI Federal Benefit Rate for an individual; zero when the child's own income already reaches it. No more than this is deemed to a child who shares the parents' income with other eligible children (416.1165(e)(3)).

Precision. Worked back from the countable income, not searched for. With E the child's countable earned income once the whole $20 is used against unearned income (ma_ssi_countable_earned_income_with_general_exclusion_used, CO-5901), U the child's own unearned income and F the Federal Benefit Rate: the deemed income first takes back the part of the $20 the child's own unearned income left for earned income (each dollar of it adding at most one half of a dollar, ssi_earned_income_disregard_rate, of countable earned income, and nothing while the earnings are within the exclusions), and each dollar beyond that adds a dollar of countable unearned income. When E is at most F, countable income first reaches F after the whole $20 is used, so the amount is F - E + 20 - U, and not below zero. When E is more than F, the child reaches F while the deemed income is still taking the $20 back from earned income, each dollar adding one half of a dollar: the amount is the unused part of the $20, max(0, 20 - U), less (E - F) divided by one half, and not below zero. The benefit is the Federal Benefit Rate for an individual less countable income ((e)(1)). (e)(3)'s SSI benefit includes a federally administered State supplement; Colorado's supplement for a blind or disabled child under 60, AND-CS (9 CCR 2503-5 3.546, S706), is paid to a client 'receiving SSI' who is not receiving the full SSI benefit standard, up to a grant standard equal to the Federal Benefit Rate ($994 in 2026), so it is nothing once the SSI benefit is nothing and adds nothing to this amount.

Type money, scope person-month, program Medicaid.
Uses: `ma_ssi_countable_earned_income_with_general_exclusion_used`, `ma_ssi_household_unearned_income_before_deeming`, `ssi_earned_income_disregard_rate`, `ssi_federal_benefit_rate_individual`, `ssi_general_income_exclusion`.

```
if SSI federal benefit rate, individual (1029) is at least Medicaid: SSI-related countable earned income with the whole $20 taken from unearned income
  then the greater of 0 and (((SSI federal benefit rate, individual (1029) minus Medicaid: SSI-related countable earned income with the whole $20 taken from unearned income) plus SSI-related general income exclusion (20)) minus Medicaid: SSI-related unearned income after allocations, before parental deeming)
otherwise the greater of 0 and ((the greater of 0 and (SSI-related general income exclusion (20) minus Medicaid: SSI-related unearned income after allocations, before parental deeming)) plus ((SSI federal benefit rate, individual (1029) minus Medicaid: SSI-related countable earned income with the whole $20 taken from unearned income) divided by SSI-related earned income disregard rate (0.5)))
```

### CO-5904 Medicaid: the parental income shared with other eligible children zeroes this child's SSI benefit `@engine`

Whether this child is a blind or disabled child who shares the deemed income of ineligible parents with at least one other eligible child (ma_ssi_deeming_children) and whose share of it, once each child sharing it has been given no more than reduces its SSI benefit to zero and the rest has gone to the others (20 CFR 416.1165(e)(2)-(3)), would reduce this child's benefit to zero: the parental income to be deemed (ma_ssi_parental_income_to_be_deemed) is more than the sum, over the children sharing it, of the lesser of each child's ma_ssi_deeming_benefit_zero_amount and this child's. Such a child is deemed no more than its own ma_ssi_deeming_benefit_zero_amount, and is ineligible: (e)(3) says the share 'makes that child ineligible (reduces the amount to zero)'.

Precision. The fill-up of (e)(3) as one test per child. Dividing equally, giving a child whose share exceeds its limit only its limit and dividing the rest equally among the others ((e)(2), 'in the manner described'), and repeating while any child's new share exceeds its limit, ends with every child given the lesser of its limit and one common level, the level at which the amounts given add up to the income to be deemed. A child's limit is below that level exactly when giving every child the lesser of its own limit and this child's limit leaves income over, which is what this item compares, with no ordering of the children and no loop. A child whose limit equals the level is given its limit, as the children above it are, and is not counted here. Each child's test reads its own parents' income and its own group of children sharing it, as ma_ssi_parental_income_deemed (CO-4626) did. An only eligible child is never counted: (e)(1) deems to the only eligible child 'any of your parents' current monthly income that remains', and (e)(3) passes the rest 'to other eligible children', of whom there are none; the child's eligibility is the same either way. Membership of this child in the group is read as being blind (is_blind) or disabled (meets_ssa_disability_criteria) with parents whose income is deemed, which is the group's test for this child. Coverage pass 4, non-MAGI N4-13 (decision 4 of 2026-11-23: missing information is cannot determine unless the rule says otherwise; readers do not invent defaults): the child's blindness and disability are read as stated, no longer as no when unstated. Pattern sweep, non-MAGI Medicaid (docs/reviews/pattern-sweep-nonmagi.md, P1): disability is read in the month: not in a month before the disability onset (ma_month_is_before_disability_onset, CO-4888; the onset is 'the date on which the person's disability began', CO-4887; 10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.5.C.4.b, S3623; § 8.100.3.E.1, S1503). Before, the undated finding was read in every month.

Type yes/no, scope person-month, program Medicaid.
Uses: `is_blind`, `ma_month_is_before_disability_onset`, `ma_ssi_deeming_children`, `ma_ssi_deeming_limit_sum`, `ma_ssi_deeming_parents`, `ma_ssi_parental_income_to_be_deemed`, `meets_ssa_disability_criteria`.

```
all of the following are true:
  - (the number of persons in Medicaid: parents whose income and resources are deemed to the child) is more than 0
  - (the number of persons in Medicaid: blind or disabled children sharing the deemed parental income) is at least 2
  - any of the following is true:
    - Is blind
    - all of the following are true:
      - Meets SSA disability criteria
      - it is not the case that Medicaid: month is before the disability onset
  - Medicaid SSI method: deemed income the children can take at this child's limit is less than Medicaid: parental income to be deemed to the eligible children
```

### CO-605 Medicaid: SSI-related countable earned income `@engine`

This person's (and, if living together, their spouse's) combined gross earned income for the month, after the ssi_earned_income_exclusion earned income exclusion, the unused portion of the ssi_general_income_exclusion general income exclusion carried over from unearned income, and the one-half remainder disregard of 20 CFR 416.1112(c), 416.1124(c)(12) and 10 CCR 2505-10 8.100.5.H.4.b.

Precision. Combines wages_gross across ma_ssi_household_size's spouse-living-together group (8.100.5.H.1.a's "mutually available" rule) before applying one ssi_earned_income_exclusion exclusion, plus any part of the combined group's ssi_general_income_exclusion general exclusion not already used against unearned income (20 CFR 416.1124(c)(12), "If you have less than $20 of unearned income in a month and you have earned income in that month, we will use the rest of the $20 exclusion to reduce the amount of your countable earned income"), and one one-half disregard, to the combined total. The unearned-income sum recomputed here to find the unused ssi_general_income_exclusion is the same group sum ma_ssi_countable_unearned_income (CO-606) uses. The Ineligible Child Allocation is deducted first, from an ineligible spouse's unearned income and then from that spouse's earned income (ma_ssi_child_allocation_from_spouse_earned, CO-2279), and the unused ssi_general_income_exclusion is measured on the unearned income after that allocation (ma_ssi_household_unearned_income_counted, CO-2281). Earned income includes net earnings from self-employment (ma_self_employment_net_earnings, CO-1704), which 8.100.5's earned income list names; it had read wages only. The couple is ma_ssi_couple_members (CO-3626), which reads resides_in_medical_institution (CO-1742) through ma_excluded_from_ssi_household and ma_is_institutionalized_spouse_in_institution, not SNAP's majority-of-meals institution fact. Earned income 20 CFR 416.1112 excludes is subtracted for each member before the exclusions (ma_ssi_excluded_earned_income, CO-2471, read as 0 when not stated). Coverage review NM-7, NM-8: the 20 CFR 416.1112(c) exclusions § 8.100.5.H.4.e incorporates are taken in their order: impairment-related work expenses of a disabled member who is not blind after the $65 and before the one half ((c)(6), ma_ssi_impairment_related_work_expenses, CO-4628), and blind work expenses and earned income set aside under an approved plan to achieve self-support after it ((c)(8)-(9), ma_ssi_earned_income_excluded_after_half, CO-4629). Deeming of a parent's income to an applicant child is ma_ssi_parental_income_deemed (CO-4626), added to unearned income in CO-2281 (OQ-83, resolved).

### CO-608 Medicaid: SSI-related countable resources `@engine`

This person's countable resources for SSI-related, OAP and Medicare Savings Program purposes, compared against the resource standards of 10 CCR 2505-10 8.100.5.M.1: the Medicaid countable resources (ma_ssi_countable_resources_individual) of the person and of a spouse living with the person (ma_ssi_couple_members, the group of ma_ssi_household_size), less the self-funded retirement accounts in the name of that spouse, which are exempt in determining the person's eligibility (§ 8.100.5.N.3); plus, for a child, the resources of ineligible parents deemed to the child (ma_ssi_parental_resources_deemed). For an institutionalized spouse in the institution, the resources 42 U.S.C. 1396r-5(c)(2) attributes to that spouse: both spouses' resources less the community spouse resource allowance (ma_institutionalized_spouse_countable_resources, CO-647).

Precision. A spouse admitted to a medical institution leaves the community spouse's couple from the month after admission (ma_excluded_from_ssi_household, CO-661), so the community spouse's own figure is compared with the individual limit. An institutionalized spouse in the institution (ma_is_institutionalized_spouse_in_institution, CO-5200) is tested on CO-647 against the individual limit, from the admission month: 1396r-5(c)(2) makes all the resources held by either spouse available to the institutionalized spouse to the extent they exceed the allowance, and 1396r-5(a)(1) makes the section supersede the SSI couple rule for that spouse's eligibility under every group, not only long-term care. The community spouse's retirement accounts count there (§ 8.100.5.N.4); for everyone else this item serves the SSI-related, OAP and MSP tests with § 8.100.5.N.3's exemption. Resource records, Medicaid track H1 (docs/reviews/records-holdings-medicaid.md): the spouse's self-funded retirement accounts left out (N.3) are what the spouse's own figure counted for them (ma_ssi_retirement_accounts_counted_in_month, CO-5326, at the determination month). The couple excludes one automobile (20 CFR 416.1218(b): "In determining the resources of an individual (and spouse, if any)", S4660; 8.100.5.M.2.c): each spouse's own figure excludes that spouse's automobile, so the smaller of the two (ma_ssi_excluded_automobile_equity_in_month, CO-5321) is added back. A joint holding of the spouses is stated on each spouse's list with each one's share, so the couple's figure counts it once (8.100.5.M.3.d). Coverage pass 4, non-MAGI N4-7 (docs/reviews/coverage4-medicaid-nonmagi.md): per month. Each month the determination evaluates (a retroactive month, the application month, the determination month and after) is judged on the holdings at that month's first moment (ma_ssi_countable_resources_in_month, CO-5322; 20 CFR 416.1207(a), S4501, the holdings record's own definition of its month) and on the couple as it stands in that month (ma_ssi_couple_members, CO-3626, now per month), as 10 CCR 2505-10 8.100.3.E.1 requires a retroactive month in which the person "met all applicable eligibility requirements" (OQ-952, resolved). Before, every month read the determination month's holdings. The figures read for a long-term care spouse in the institution (ma_institutionalized_spouse_countable_resources, CO-647) and for deeming parents (ma_ssi_parental_resources_deemed, CO-4627) are still taken at the determination month (the spousal snapshot and attribution of 8.100.7.L-O are made at the application and the determination). Coverage pass 4, non-MAGI N4-6: the couple excludes one automobile, a car the two own together counted once at its whole equity: the two spouses' own excluded automobiles (ma_ssi_excluded_automobile_equity_in_month, CO-5321) are added back less the couple's one, the larger of the two spouses' ma_ssi_couple_automobile_equity_in_month (CO-6733, a joint car at its whole equity), at least 0. For two different cars this is the smaller car, as before; for one joint car, nothing (it had added back the other spouse's half of the same car).

Type money, scope person-month, program Medicaid.
Uses: `ma_institutionalized_spouse_countable_resources`, `ma_is_institutionalized_spouse_in_institution`, `ma_ssi_countable_resources_in_month`, `ma_ssi_couple_automobile_equity_in_month`, `ma_ssi_couple_members`, `ma_ssi_excluded_automobile_equity_in_month`, `ma_ssi_parental_resources_deemed`, `ma_ssi_retirement_accounts_counted_in_month`, `relationships`.

```
if Medicaid: institutionalized spouse in the institution
  then Medicaid: institutionalized spouse's countable resources
otherwise ((the sum of that person's Medicaid: SSI-related countable resources of the individual in the month for each person in Medicaid: SSI-method couple) minus (the sum of that person's Medicaid SSI method: the person's retirement accounts counted in the month for each person in all persons in Medicaid: SSI-method couple such that this person is a spouse or holds_out_as_spouse_with of that person, otherwise no)) plus (the greater of 0 and ((Medicaid SSI method: the equity of the person's one automobile excluded plus (the sum of that person's Medicaid SSI method: the equity of the person's one automobile excluded for each person in all persons in Medicaid: SSI-method couple such that this person is a spouse or holds_out_as_spouse_with of that person, otherwise no)) minus (the greater of Medicaid SSI method: the couple's largest automobile equity on a spouse's list and (the sum of that person's Medicaid SSI method: the couple's largest automobile equity on a spouse's list for each person in all persons in Medicaid: SSI-method couple such that this person is a spouse or holds_out_as_spouse_with of that person, otherwise no)))) plus Medicaid: parental resources deemed to the child
```

### CO-611 Medicaid: is SSI-related eligible `@engine`

Whether the person is eligible for Medical Assistance under the SSI-related Aged, Blind and Disabled category - an SSI recipient, or aged/blind/disabled and meeting both the SSI income and resource standards, plus residency and citizenship - per 10 CCR 2505-10 8.100.6.C and 8.100.5.

Precision. A person receiving SSI is categorically eligible under 8.100.6.C.1.a-b without a separate income/resource test this item performs (SSA has already determined it); a person not receiving SSI must independently meet ma_is_aged_blind_or_disabled_in_month (CO-5201: a disabled person not in a month before the disability onset, § 8.100.5.C.4.b) and both standards, and is not eligible when Medical Assistance is denied for failing to pursue potential resources or income or refusing to release the patient payment (ma_abd_denied_for_noncooperation, CO-4886; § 8.100.5.E.6, § 8.100.7.V.2.c). The SSA's determination governs an SSI recipient's Medicaid, so neither gate reaches the receives_ssi arm, as in ma_ssi_related_category (CO-612). § 8.100.3.G.1.c's general requirement not to be a patient in an institution for mental diseases between 21 and 64 is applied (ma_meets_imd_requirement, CO-1179). Coverage pass 6, non-MAGI F6-5 (docs/reviews/coverage6-medicaid-nonmagi.md): the SSI branch reads ma_receives_ssi_in_month (CO-7351), SSI from the month of the original SSI eligibility date (10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.6.C.1.a, C.7, S5030), so a retroactive month before an SSI award is judged by the SSI-related tests of that month; before, receives_ssi (the award as of the determination date) made every month an SSI month.

Type yes/no, scope person-month, program Medicaid.
Uses: `ma_abd_denied_for_noncooperation`, `ma_is_aged_blind_or_disabled_in_month`, `ma_meets_citizenship_requirement_in_month`, `ma_meets_imd_requirement`, `ma_meets_residency_in_month`, `ma_meets_ssi_income_standard`, `ma_meets_ssi_resource_standard`, `ma_receives_ssi_in_month`.

```
all of the following are true:
  - Medicaid: meets the residency requirement in the month
  - Medicaid: meets the citizenship requirement in the month
  - any of the following is true:
    - Medicaid: receives SSI in the month
    - all of the following are true:
      - it is not the case that Medicaid: aged, blind and disabled groups denied for non-cooperation
      - Medicaid: aged, blind or disabled in the month
      - Medicaid: meets the SSI income standard
      - Medicaid: meets the SSI resource standard
  - Medicaid: meets the institution for mental diseases requirement
```

### CO-612 Medicaid: SSI-related category `@engine`

The single SSI-related Aged, Blind and Disabled category this person qualifies under for the month, tested in the order 10 CCR 2505-10 8.100.6.C-8.100.6.A lists them - an SSI recipient first, then aged, blind, or disabled (in that order, for a person who independently meets both SSI standards), or none. It answers whether the criteria are met for the month; whether the month falls inside the coverage period (not before the retroactive months of § 8.100.3.E.1, and for QMB not before the effective month) is not tested here, as ma_month_is_before_coverage_period (CO-4101) tests it for the MAGI and OAP outcomes (final verification pass 3, P3-1).

Precision. A person can meet more than one of aged/blind/disabled at once (for example, an aged blind person); this item reports the first the case order lists, matching the "otherwise" ordering pattern (P33) other category outcomes in this volume use (see snap_eligibility_status, CO-387). Tests [not, ma_is_ssi_related_eligible] before the receives_ssi branch - an SSI recipient who fails residency, citizenship, or (mechanically, though not for an actual SSI recipient) the income/resource standards is not SSI-related eligible, and this item's own meaning promises "the... category this person qualifies under", which must not name one when ma_is_ssi_related_eligible is false. An Old Age Pension recipient who meets SSI criteria except the level of income (§ 8.100.6.K.4, SISC B; ma_oap_sisc_b_eligible, CO-1177) is reported oap_sisc_b when not otherwise SSI-related eligible. Coverage pass 6, non-MAGI F6-5 (docs/reviews/coverage6-medicaid-nonmagi.md): the SSI branch reads ma_receives_ssi_in_month (CO-7351), SSI from the month of the original SSI eligibility date (10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.6.C.1.a, C.7, S5030), so a retroactive month before an SSI award is judged by the SSI-related tests of that month; before, receives_ssi (the award as of the determination date) made every month an SSI month.

Type one of, scope person-month, program Medicaid.
Uses: `is_blind`, `ma_abd_denied_for_noncooperation`, `ma_is_aged`, `ma_is_ssi_related_eligible`, `ma_month_is_before_disability_onset`, `ma_oap_sisc_b_eligible`, `ma_receives_ssi_in_month`, `meets_ssa_disability_criteria`.

```
if Medicaid: is SSI-related eligible
  then (if Medicaid: receives SSI in the month;   then ssi_recipient; else if Medicaid: aged, blind and disabled groups denied for non-cooperation;   then none; else if Medicaid: is aged;   then aged; else if Is blind;   then blind; else if all of the following are true:;     - Meets SSA disability criteria;     - it is not the case that Medicaid: month is before the disability onset;   then disabled; otherwise none)
else if all of the following are true:
    - Medicaid: is eligible as an OAP recipient meeting SSI criteria except income (SISC B)
    - it is not the case that Medicaid: aged, blind and disabled groups denied for non-cooperation
  then oap_sisc_b
otherwise none
```

### CO-613 Medicaid: is Qualified Medicare Beneficiary (QMB) eligible `@engine`

Whether the person is eligible as a Qualified Medicare Beneficiary - entitled to Medicare Part A, countable income (self, plus spouse if living together) at or below ma_qmb_income_limit_pct of the federal poverty level for their household size, and countable resources at or below the MSP resource limit - per 42 U.S.C. 1396d(p) and 10 CCR 2505-10 8.100.6.L.

Precision. The income limit is expressed as monthly (annual federal_poverty_guideline_annual_table figure divided by 12) times ma_qmb_income_limit_pct, matching how ma_magi_household_income_pct_fpl (CO-504) treats the same table for the MAGI chapter. Couples compare against the couple's guideline (ma_ssi_household_size 2) per 8.100.6.L.3, whether one or both spouses apply. Reads ma_ssi_poverty_guideline_monthly (CO-1750) instead of restating the lookup. For a QMB member in the December before the month, the annual Social Security cost-of-living increase is subtracted from countable income until the year's poverty guidelines are published (§ 8.100.6.L.12; ma_msp_cola_disregard, CO-3629; OQ-622). When the coverage takes effect is ma_qmb_is_in_effect (CO-3623), read by ma_msp_category (CO-617). L.2.d ('is enrolled in the mandatory SSI program with premium-free Medicare Part A') is not read as limiting QMB to SSI recipients (OQ-624). Pattern sweep, non-MAGI Medicaid (docs/reviews/pattern-sweep-nonmagi.md, P1): Part A entitlement is read in the month (ma_is_entitled_to_medicare_part_a_in_month, CO-7503; § 8.100.6.M.2.a, M.5, N.3-4, S2407, S1749; § 8.100.3.E.1, S1503). Before, the entitlement of the determination date was read in every month, so a retroactive month before Part A began was an MSP month.

Type yes/no, scope person-month, program Medicaid.
Uses: `ma_is_entitled_to_medicare_part_a_in_month`, `ma_msp_cola_disregard`, `ma_msp_countable_resources`, `ma_msp_december_category`, `ma_msp_resource_limit_couple`, `ma_msp_resource_limit_individual`, `ma_qmb_income_limit_pct`, `ma_ssi_countable_income`, `ma_ssi_household_size`, `ma_ssi_poverty_guideline_monthly`.

```
all of the following are true:
  - Medicaid: entitled to Medicare Part A in the month
  - (Medicaid: SSI-related countable income minus (if Medicaid: Medicare Savings Program category in the December before the month is equal to qmb;   then Medicaid: Medicare Savings Program COLA disregard; otherwise 0)) is at most (Medicaid: monthly poverty guideline for the SSI-method household times QMB income limit, percentage of FPL (1))
  - Medicaid: Medicare Savings Program countable resources is at most (if Medicaid: SSI-related household size (self and a spouse living together) is equal to 2;   then Medicare Savings Program resource limit (couple) (14910); otherwise Medicare Savings Program resource limit (individual) (9950))
```

### CO-617 Medicaid: Medicare Savings Program category `@engine`

The single Medicare Savings Program category this person qualifies under for the month, tested in the order Colorado's tiers of Medicare cost-sharing assistance run (10 CCR 2505-10 8.100.6.L-8.100.6.O) - QMB first (the most generous), then SLMB, then QI-1, then QDWI, or none. QMB is reported only for a month in which its coverage can be in effect (ma_qmb_is_in_effect, CO-3623: from the month after the month of determination, never retroactively, § 8.100.6.L.10-11), and QDWI from the month of determination (ma_qdwi_is_in_effect, CO-3624, § 8.100.6.O.5); a person who meets the QMB test in the determination month or a retroactive month is reported none for it, since SLMB and QI-1 cover only income above the QMB limit. It answers whether the criteria are met for the month; whether the month falls inside the coverage period (not before the retroactive months of § 8.100.3.E.1, and for QMB not before the effective month) is not tested here, as ma_month_is_before_coverage_period (CO-4101) tests it for the MAGI and OAP outcomes (final verification pass 3, P3-1).

Precision. QMB and SLMB/QI-1 are structured as increasing income bands that cannot overlap by construction (ma_slmb_eligible and ma_qi_eligible each exclude the tier below); QDWI is a separate track (Part A entitlement on a disability basis that has been or is being lost) that can coincide with none of the others, so testing it last is a matter of the category list's order, not exclusivity. The Medicare Savings Programs are Medical Assistance categories, so § 8.100.3.G.1.g's citizenship and immigration status requirement (ma_meets_citizenship_requirement, CO-509) applies to them, and from October 1, 2026 42 U.S.C. 1396b(v)(5) limits them like any partial benefit (CMS SHO #26-001, note 14, S1703). Coverage pass 7, non-MAGI F7-5 (docs/reviews/coverage7-medicaid-nonmagi.md): reads the general requirement of 10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.3.G.1.c (S659) through ma_meets_imd_requirement (CO-1179), as the SSI-related groups (CO-611) and the MAGI groups (CO-562) do: G.1 states what a person "shall" meet "To be eligible to receive Medical Assistance", and names no category it leaves out. Before, a patient aged 21 to 64 of an institution for mental diseases could be found eligible here although no other Medical Assistance category admitted him (IMD-LTC, stored household CO-1104). Coverage pass 7 (found while fixing F7-5, docs/reviews/coverage7-medicaid-nonmagi.md, F7-5a): residency, § 8.100.3.G.1.a (S661), read in the month (ma_meets_residency_in_month, CO-7650; S1518, S1503), as every other aged, blind and disabled category reads it since the Medicaid status by month round (MS-1); the Medicare Savings Programs read no residency at all before, so a month before a move to Colorado could be an MSP month (CO-617-T93). The residency and IMD requirements are read inside each category's arm, after the category's own test, so a person who meets no category is none whatever those facts say (a household that does not state its residence setting is not made cannot determine for a category it does not reach).

Type one of, scope person-month, program Medicaid.
Uses: `ma_abd_denied_for_noncooperation`, `ma_meets_citizenship_requirement_in_month`, `ma_meets_imd_requirement`, `ma_meets_residency_in_month`, `ma_qdwi_eligible`, `ma_qdwi_is_in_effect`, `ma_qi_eligible`, `ma_qmb_eligible`, `ma_qmb_is_in_effect`, `ma_slmb_eligible`.

Whether the child is eligible for the Medicaid Buy-In Program for Children with Disabilities - at most ma_cbwd_max_age (CO-3026), disabled, with household income after the 8.100.5.H disregards (ma_cbwd_countable_household_income_pct_fpl, CO-4203) at or below ma_cbwd_income_limit_pct (CO-243) of the federal poverty level, not a child of ma_wawd_min_age or older who is employed (such a child is determined for the Buy-In for Working Adults with Disabilities instead), and, where the family can enroll in employer-based family coverage toward which the employer pays at least ma_cbwd_employer_contribution_min_pct of the premium, enrolled in it - per 10 CCR 2505-10 8.100.6.Q.1.

Precision. 8.100.6.Q.1.b takes the household from the MAGI household rules of 8.100.4.E (unlike WAwD's applicant-only rule) and the income from 8.100.5.F, F.6 and H: the income tested is ma_cbwd_countable_household_income_pct_fpl (CO-4203), the MAGI household's 8.100.5.F income after the 8.100.5.H disregards against the poverty level for the MAGI household's size (final verification pass 3, F3-1; OQ-740 for how the disregards apply to a family). Resources are not counted (8.100.6.Q.1.c). Q.1.e: a child of ma_wawd_min_age (16) through ma_cbwd_max_age (18) with earned income in the month (ma_has_earned_income, CO-6200) is employed and is excluded here, so ma_buy_in_category (CO-622) reports the Working Adults program or none; the WAwD minimum age is read because Q.1.e's age 16 is the age from which that program takes the child. Q.1.f is read as a condition of eligibility: where employer family coverage with at least the minimum employer share is available (employer_family_coverage_employer_premium_share), the child must be enrolled in it (is_enrolled_in_employer_family_coverage; OQ-623). Status reads ma_meets_status_for_cover_all_coloradans_categories (CO-1174), since § 8.100.3.G.1.g.ix.1.b lists both Buy-In programs among the categories Cover All Coloradans reaches. A child in a continuous eligibility period that began in the Children with Disabilities Buy-In (§ 8.100.3.Q.2.d) stays eligible for the period unless enrollment is discontinued for unpaid premiums (Q.2.d.i). Coverage review 2 (non-MAGI N2-3, fixed in the MAGI round): the upper age reads ma_age_before_month (CO-4790), the age on the last day of the month before the determination month, so a child whose 19th birthday falls earlier in the determination month stays eligible for that month: § 8.100.6.Q.1.a and § 8.100.5.C.3 grant the whole month. The Q.1.e test of 16 (a lower limit) reads age on the determination date. Time audit T-1 (2026-11-23): the bar on a working child of ma_wawd_min_age or older reads ma_age_on_first_day_of_month (CO-4978): the child is barred for the whole month only when that old on every day of it (§ 8.100.5.C.3, S3900); it read age (CO-300), the age on the determination date, in every month. Before, the undated finding was read in every month.

### CO-6200 Medicaid: the person has pay for work or business receipts in the month `@engine`

The test of employment of the Working Adults Buy-In (8.100.6.P.1.e, 'Individuals must be employed'), of an employed child of 16 to 18 in the Children's Buy-In (8.100.6.Q.1.e) and of an employed parent or caretaker relative in Transitional Medical Assistance (8.100.4.I.1.b.i).

Pay in kind counts (K.3-4); CO-1356 did not read in_kind_compensation_value. ### CO-621 Medicaid: Children with Disabilities Buy-In monthly premium `@engine`

The monthly premium a Children with Disabilities Buy-In household owes, on the sliding scale by household income-as-a-percentage-of-FPL band 10 CCR 2505-10 8.100.6.Q.1.g.iv states. Informational: no rule reads it and it is not a declared outcome; it reports the premium beside ma_buy_in_category.

Precision. Reads the household band amount from ma_cbwd_premium_table (CO-2458, P48) on ma_cbwd_countable_household_income_pct_fpl (CO-4203), the figure ma_cbwd_eligible (CO-620) tests (final verification pass 3, F3-1: it had read the MAGI percentage), capped at ma_cbwd_premium_cap_pct_lower of the household's monthly MAGI income, read as the "family's adjusted gross income" of Q.1.g.i, at or below ma_cbwd_premium_cap_threshold_pct of FPL and ma_cbwd_premium_cap_pct_upper above (Q.1.g.i, which caps premiums and cost sharing together; cost sharing is not modeled, so the cap is applied to the premium). The household owes one premium however many children are eligible (Q.1.g.iii): it is reported on the oldest child in the MAGI household whose own premium is due in the month (ma_cbwd_premium_is_due_in_month, CO-7861: eligible, past its determination month, not postpartum), shared equally among such children born that same day, and is 0 for the others. No premium for the month of the determination or earlier (Q.1.g.ii; ma_buy_in_determination_month, CO-2462) or for a member within 12 months postpartum (Q.1.g.vi). § 8.100.6.Q.1.g's third and fourth bands say "individuals" where the first two say "households" (OQ-144); the volume reads every band as the household's. The public health emergency waiver (Q.1.g.vii) is read as ended (OQ-511). Dated parameter in place of literal bands. Coverage pass 7, non-MAGI F7-8 (docs/reviews/coverage7-medicaid-nonmagi.md): eligible children born on the same day as the oldest eligible child (twins, triplets) share the one premium equally, each reporting the household's amount divided by their number, so the amounts reported on the household's children add up to the one premium Q.1.g.iii charges; the rule names no order among children born the same day, and the dates of birth are the only order the case states. Before, each twin reported the whole premium (CBWD-TWINS, stored household CO-1108: 70 each, 140 in all, for a household that owes 70). The divisor counts the household members born that day who are eligible, this child included (never less than 1). Coverage verification 7, V7-4 (docs/reviews/verify-coverage7-fixes.md): the older-child arm and the divisor count only the children whose own premium is due in the month (CO-7861), so a child whose premium is waived in the month (its determination month, Q.1.g.ii) neither takes the premium from an older or same-day child nor shares it: twins determined in June and October owe 70 in October on the twin determined in June (was 35 + 0), and a younger child enrolled since June bears the 70 in the October an older child is determined (was 0 + 0). The order among children (the oldest bears it; same-day children share it equally) is the volume's presentation, which Q.1.g.iii does not settle (it fixes only the household's total): OQ-1495 records it for the Medicaid owner. The shares of three or more same-day children are not rounded to cents (70 / 3 = 23.33...): no operator orders persons who share a date of birth, so one child cannot be chosen to bear the remaining cent (known limit NM-KL-5, V7-9).

Type money, scope person-month, program Medicaid.
Uses: `date_of_birth`, `ma_buy_in_determination_month`, `ma_cbwd_countable_household_income_pct_fpl`, `ma_cbwd_premium_cap_pct_lower`, `ma_cbwd_premium_cap_pct_upper`, `ma_cbwd_premium_cap_threshold_pct`, `ma_cbwd_premium_is_due_in_month`, `ma_cbwd_premium_table`, `ma_magi_household_income`, `ma_magi_household_members`, `ma_postpartum_coverage_end_month`, `pregnancy_end_date`.

### CO-622 Medicaid: Buy-In category `@engine`

The single Medicaid Buy-In Program this person qualifies under for the month - Working Adults with Disabilities, Children with Disabilities, or none - per 10 CCR 2505-10 8.100.6.P and 8.100.6.Q. It answers whether the criteria are met for the month; whether the month falls inside the coverage period (not before the retroactive months of § 8.100.3.E.1, and for QMB not before the effective month) is not tested here, as ma_month_is_before_coverage_period (CO-4101) tests it for the MAGI and OAP outcomes (final verification pass 3, P3-1).

Precision. The two programs' age ranges (16+ for WAwD, 18 or younger for CBwD) overlap at 16-18, where 8.100.6.Q.1.e routes an employed 16-18-year-old to WAwD instead. ma_cbwd_eligible (CO-620) enforces Q.1.e itself: a child of 16 to 18 with earned income in the month is not CBwD-eligible. This item also tests WAwD first (ma_wawd_eligible requires is_employed), so a person who meets both tests is reported in WAwD, as Q.1.e directs for an employed child. Final verification pass 2, P3-1: the precision said Q.1.e was not enforced, which F-7 had changed. Coverage pass 7, non-MAGI F7-5 (docs/reviews/coverage7-medicaid-nonmagi.md): reads the general requirement of 10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.3.G.1.c (S659) through ma_meets_imd_requirement (CO-1179), as the SSI-related groups (CO-611) and the MAGI groups (CO-562) do: G.1 states what a person "shall" meet "To be eligible to receive Medical Assistance", and names no category it leaves out. Before, a patient aged 21 to 64 of an institution for mental diseases could be found eligible here although no other Medical Assistance category admitted him (IMD-LTC, stored household CO-1104). The IMD requirement is read inside each category's arm, after the category's own test, so a person who meets no category is none whatever its facts say (a household that does not state its residence setting is not made cannot determine for a category it does not reach).

Type one of, scope person-month, program Medicaid.
Uses: `ma_abd_denied_for_noncooperation`, `ma_cbwd_eligible`, `ma_meets_imd_requirement`, `ma_wawd_eligible`.

```
if Medicaid: aged, blind and disabled groups denied for non-cooperation
  then none
else if all of the following are true:
    - Medicaid: is Working Adults with Disabilities Buy-In eligible
    - Medicaid: meets the institution for mental diseases requirement
  then working_adults_with_disabilities
else if all of the following are true:
    - Medicaid: is Children with Disabilities Buy-In eligible
    - Medicaid: meets the institution for mental diseases requirement
  then children_with_disabilities
otherwise none
```

### CO-6250 Medicaid: the current OASDI the SSI method counts `@engine`

The person's current Social Security (Title II, OASDI) benefits of the month as the SSI method counts them: each receipt of kind social_security other than a retroactive payment (ma_social_security_receipts, CO-5515), less the part set aside under a plan for self-support, which 10 CCR 2505-10 8.100.5.F.6.q exempts (S3404) and ma_ssi_unearned_receipts (CO-5511) already leaves out. What the Disabled Adult Child test takes out of the SSI-related unearned income when it disregards the current OASDI income (8.100.6.J.1.c.i, S626).

Precision. Receipts harness after the generated households state earnings (docs/reviews/records-earnings-e1-integration.md): ma_dac_countable_income (CO-1160) took the gross OASDI (CO-5515) out of the unearned income counted, ma_ssi_household_unearned_income_counted (CO-2281), from which the PASS set-aside of that OASDI had already been left out (CO-5511), so the set-aside came off twice and other countable income was disregarded with it: the CBWD child of 10 with $1,763.50 of deemed parental income and $300 of OASDI, $100 of it set aside under a PASS, had 1,643.50 where the income other than the OASDI is 1,763.50 - 20 = 1,743.50. The gross figure stays for the Pickle and Medicare Savings Program cost-of-living disregards (CO-6052, CO-6053, CO-3627, CO-5221), which compare benefit amounts. Field-effect sweep (docs/reviews/field-sweep-snap-cash-nonmagi.md), FS-MA-1: a receipt stated as a stream (no month and no date) is received only in the months from the month of its start_date through the month of its end_date (each absent: before, or through, the months the case covers; CO-5000), since unearned income "is countable as income in the month received" (10 CCR 2505-10 8.100.5.F.5, S3001) and is counted "when you receive it" (20 CFR 416.1123(a), S4940); in its first and last months it is read at its amount, and a payment stated with its month or date is placed by it, a final payment after the stream ended included. Before, a stream was counted in every month whatever its dates. The clause is SNAP's (snap_counted_recurring_receipts, CO-5011).

### CO-640 Medicaid: is institutionalized `@engine`

Whether this person is institutionalized for Long-Term Care purposes in the month - in a medical institution or Long-Term Care institution in the month and expected to remain, or to receive HCBS/PACE, for at least 30 consecutive full days - per 42 CFR 435.1005/435.1009 and 10 CCR 2505-10 §§ 8.100.7.A.2.c and 8.100.7.K.2. A month before the month the person entered the institution is not one (§ 8.100.7.A.2.c.iii: benefits "start as of the first day when institutionalization began").

Precision. A person who dies before the 30th day (8.100.7.A.2.c.i-iii) meets the requirement on a physician's or case manager's statement that the stay would have lasted 30 days: expects_institutional_stay_of_thirty_days is read as that statement, and its documentation is ma_requires_verification_of_institutional_stay (CO-1632) (coverage review NM-34). A hospital or Long-Term Care institution is read as eligible for Medical Assistance reimbursement (A.2.d); a facility that is not is outside this item (NM-35). Reads resides_in_medical_institution (CO-1742), not SNAP's majority-of-meals institution fact. Coverage pass 6, non-MAGI F6-3 (docs/reviews/coverage6-medicaid-nonmagi.md): per month, as ma_is_institutionalized_spouse_in_institution (CO-5200) is. For a month before the determination month the person is institutionalized from the month of institution_entry_date (A.2.c.iii, S1753; 8.100.3.E.1, S1503: a retroactive month needs "all applicable eligibility requirements" met in it), so a retroactive month before the admission is not one; the entry date is needed for such a month (decision 4 of 2026-11-23). The determination month and the months after read the setting on the determination date. Before, every month read the determination date's setting, so a retroactive month before the admission was long-term care eligible with a patient payment.

### CO-641 Medicaid: LTC gross income `@engine`

This person's gross monthly income for Long-Term Care eligibility and patient payment purposes - all earned and unearned income, including in-kind support and maintenance and child support received, before any SSI-program deductions, exemptions or disregards (the gross unearned receipts of the SSI method, ma_ssi_gross_unearned_receipts, with gambling winnings) - not counting what is not income: a loan, an income tax refund, and the VA Aid and Attendance/Unusual Medical Expenses pension portion, per 10 CCR 2505-10 §§ 8.100.7.A.1 and 8.100.5.K.

Precision. Sums the gross earned income as the SSI method counts it from the earnings records (ma_ssi_gross_earned_income, CO-5171: wages and net earnings from self-employment), the gross unearned receipts (ma_ssi_gross_unearned_receipts, CO-5514: every receipt the SSI method's counting table treats as income, exempt receipts and child support included, and a retroactive SSI payment), ssi_in_kind_support_and_maintenance and the month's gambling winnings (ma_ssi_gambling_receipts, CO-5512) unless the hardship exemption is granted. § 8.100.7.A.1 (S351) defines gross income as "income before application of deductions, exemptions or disregards," and ISM is income under 42 U.S.C. 1382a(a)(2)(A) and § 8.100.5.F.5.k (S306, S311). The A&A/UME portion (a receipt of kind va_aid_and_attendance) is left out for every person, as § 8.100.5.K's lead-in (S2900) excludes it 'when determining eligibility'; for a veteran or surviving spouse with no dependents in a State Veterans Home, ma_patient_payment (CO-658) adds it back under K.2 (ma_va_aid_and_attendance_is_patient_payment, CO-4103). A loan and an income tax refund are not income (20 CFR 416.1103(d), (f); coverage C3-10). Coverage pass 6, non-MAGI F6-13: the precision named wages_gross and ma_self_employment_net_earnings, which the derivation has not read since the earned-income records (step E1); it now names the figure it reads. The lottery hardship exemption keeps the default its fact declares (F6-10). Coverage pass 7, non-MAGI F7-6 (docs/reviews/coverage7-medicaid-nonmagi.md): less the receipts a federal statute bars from being counted as income in any federally assisted program (ma_ltc_federally_excluded_unearned_receipts, CO-7720: LEAP under 42 U.S.C. 8624(f)(1), S5241; a Domestic Volunteer Service Act payment below the minimum wage under 42 U.S.C. 5044(f)(1), S5242; the federally excluded payments of § 8.100.5.F.6.h, i, r, s, v and x, S5246), which § 8.100.7.A.1's 'income' cannot include whatever OQ-822 decides; OQ-822 is narrowed to Colorado's own exemptions. Before, they were counted in the 300% test and the patient payment (FEDEXCL-LTC, LIHEAP-LTC: stored households CO-1105, CO-1106). NM-KL-3 (2026-11-24, docs/reviews/known-limits.md): CO-7720 also takes out student financial assistance under Title IV of the Higher Education Act or a Bureau of Indian Education program and the payments of the 29 U.S.C. 3174 programs for adults and dislocated workers (20 U.S.C. 1087uu, S5243, S5364), each stated as its own receipt kind (title_iv_or_bie_student_aid, wioa_adult_or_dislocated_worker_payment); before, a Pell grant stated as educational assistance was counted (STUDENTAID-LTC, stored household CO-1200: 3,100 > 2,982, ineligible_income, where the text gives 2,900). Other grants and scholarships (educational_assistance) and other workforce payments (workforce_program_payment) stay counted: Colorado's F.6 exemptions of them are OQ-822's.

Whether this person's gross income meets the ma_special_income_group_pct Institutionalized Special Income standard - gross income at or below ma_special_income_group_pct of the individual SSI federal benefit rate, or, for a person in a Long-Term Care institution (excluding a hospital) whose income exceeds that level, has established a qualifying income trust - per 10 CCR 2505-10 §§ 8.100.6.K.5 and 8.100.7.A.2.e.

OQ-99 resolved pending verification: with an income trust, gross income must also be below the average private-pay rate of the region in which the person resides and intends to remain (§ 8.100.7.G.6.a.i.a), ma_income_trust_gross_income_limit, CO-1985). The regional rates are unverified figures supplied by the product owner from HCPF OM 25-073 (S1230). The income trust route excludes a hospital patient (§ 8.100.7.A.2.e, 'in a Long-Term Care institution (excluding hospital)'); it is open in HCBS under § 8.100.7.E.6.a.i (coverage review NM-32). T-9 hand check A-2 (receipts migration phase 2), settled by the governing text: the eligibility rule says "gross income that does not exceed 300% of the current individual SSI benefit level" (§ 8.100.7.A.2.e, S351, S3422), as does the federal limit, "does not exceed 300 percent of the SSI benefit amount" (42 CFR 435.1005, S378); § 8.100.6.K.5's "whose income is under 300% of the SSI benefit level" (S352) introduces the group and is read as the same standard.
