### CO-643 Medicaid: LTC couple with a community spouse `@engine`

Whether this institutionalized person has a community spouse - a spouse who is not in a medical institution or nursing facility - triggering the spousal impoverishment rules of 42 U.S.C. 1396r-5 and 10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.7.K, unless the person is in a Medicaid Buy-In program, to whom those rules do not apply (§ 8.7100.C.3; ma_is_in_buy_in_program, CO-2210; OQ-127, resolved).

Precision. Does not create a separate ma_community_spouse item naming the spouse as a value (see OQ-97); downstream items read the community spouse's income and shelter facts as supplied facts stated for the institutionalized spouse instead. Reads resides_in_medical_institution (CO-1742), not SNAP's majority-of-meals institution fact. Coverage pass 6, non-MAGI F6-7 (docs/reviews/coverage6-medicaid-nonmagi.md): a person who is married (is_married, CO-930) with no spouse who is a person of the case (marital_status married, CO-844) has a spouse the rules of § 8.100.7.K-T reach (K.2.d: the institutionalized spouse 'Is married to a spouse who is not in a medical institution or nursing facility'; L: 'All non-exempt resources owned by a married couple are counted, whether owned jointly or individually'), and without the spouse's facts (where the spouse lives, the spouse's resources and income) whether there is a community spouse cannot be determined (decision 4 of 2026-11-23: missing information is cannot determine unless the rule says otherwise). Before, only the spouse edge was read, so such a person was read as having no community spouse: no CSRA, no attribution of the couple's resources and no income allowance (MARRIED-SPOUSE-NOT-IN-CASE, CO-909). A case states the spouse as a person of the case to determine these rules. The SSI method is not changed: a spouse who is not a person of the case is not on the household roster (dwelling_id, CO-3350), so does not live with the person, and the person's own income and resources are tested alone, as § 8.100.5.H.1.a and § 8.100.7.C.2.b count only spouses living together. Pattern sweep, non-MAGI Medicaid (docs/reviews/pattern-sweep-nonmagi.md, P1, P2, P3): per month. The community spouse is a spouse of the case who, in the month, is not in a medical institution (ma_resides_in_medical_institution_in_month, CO-7500) and is alive: a spouse who died is the community spouse through the month of death and not after (§ 8.100.7.C.2.b, S1759: from 'the first month following the month the couple ceases to live together'; 20 CFR 416.1163(f)(4), S5121). With no spouse in the case, the marital status is read as stated, required where read (decision 4 of 2026-11-23): before, an unstated marital status (or unstated relationships) was read as not married (is_married's default, CO-930), so the spousal rules were skipped; single, widowed or other stated is still no community spouse. Coverage pass 7, non-MAGI F7-4 (docs/reviews/coverage7-medicaid-nonmagi.md): a legally separated person (marital_status legally_separated, CO-844) is married for these rules: § 8.100.7.L (S3419) counts "All non-exempt resources owned by a married couple" and "There are no exceptions for legal separation, pre-nuptial, or post-nuptial agreements", and K.2.d (S1754) turns on being "married to a spouse who is not in a medical institution". With the spouse not a person of the case, whether there is a community spouse cannot be determined, as for married (F6-7). Before, a legal separation was stated as other and read as no community spouse: the person was determined on his own resources and income (SEPARATED-NF, stored household CO-1103).

### CO-6450 Medicaid MAGI: a person's boarder earnings, net of the costs of providing the room or meals `@engine`

The person's payments from boarders received in the month (earnings records the MAGI counting table counts net of provision costs: boarder_payments), less the documentable costs of providing the room or meals paid in the month (the records it deducts from them: business_cost_boarder_provision), and never less than zero: 10 CCR 2505-10 8.100.3.K.10.c-e count board, room, and room and board payments as earned income "to the extent that the payment ... exceeds ... documentable expenses directly related to the provision" of them, and 26 U.S.C. 62(a)(4), which 8.100.4.C.1 incorporates, takes the deductions attributable to property held for the production of rents out of adjusted gross income. The food stamp allotment per boarder of K.10.c and e is not subtracted: it is an income disregard, which 42 U.S.C. 1396a(e)(14)(B) bars for MAGI.

Precision. Coverage pass 4, C4-03 (2026-11-23; OQ-1121 settled): before, ma_magi_wage_earnings (CO-5160) counted the payments at their gross amount. The costs of the month are taken from the payments of the month, all boarders together, as K.10 states them per payment and the tax return reports rents net of their expenses; a month whose costs exceed the payments gives 0, not a loss set against other income (K.10's "to the extent that"). A cost record not stated is no cost: the earnings list is the whole statement of the person's pay and costs (decision 4 reads an unstated list as unknown, a stated one as complete). The SSI method's own figure, with the allotment, is ma_ssi_boarder_earned_income (CO-5177). Field sweep (coverage pass 5, docs/reviews/field-sweep-magi.md): a stream of pay (a record with no month and no date) is the pay of the months its job ran, from the month of its job_start_date through the month of its job_end_date (CO-5100), and MAGI counts the month's income (10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.4.C.4: "current or previous monthly household income"; § 8.100.4.G.1, the month evaluated), so a stream is counted only in those months. Before, a stream was counted in every month, a job that ended in September included in a retroactive or later month.

### CO-6451 Medicaid: has self-employment, seasonal or commission earnings, for annualized income `@engine`

Whether the person has earned income from self-employment, seasonal employment or commission-based employment, the earnings 10 CCR 2505-10 8.100.4.C.4.a annualizes, as the person's earnings records state it: a business or a farm (a record the MAGI earnings table counts net for tax: self_employment_receipts, farm_self_employment_receipts), or pay stated as seasonal or commission-based (the record's seasonal_or_commission, CO-5100).

Precision. Coverage pass 4, C4-05 (2026-11-23): before, a supplied fact (has_self_employment_seasonal_or_commission_earnings, CO-4557) said it, read as false where not stated, a default no rule gave, so a person whose own records stated a business was not annualized unless the fact was also stated, and the two statements could disagree. The records are now the one statement: a business record is self-employment, and seasonal or commission pay is a property of the pay (seasonal_or_commission; a person with a steady job and a seasonal one states the seasonal pay as its own record). A record of any month counts: C.4.a turns on the household having such income, which annualizing the year presumes. Earnings not stated: unknown (decision 4). Annualizing still needs the member's expected income for the year from such work, which has no default (expected_annual_self_employment_seasonal_commission_income, CO-7403, read by ma_annualized_household_income, CO-4559; coverage pass 6, C6-07). Coverage pass 5, C5-08 (2026-11-23): seasonal_or_commission is required where read (it had default false, which withheld C.4.a from seasonal and commission pay that was not marked, a default no rule gives; design decision D3 gives a field a default only where the rule does). It is read on the records MAGI counts as pay (the earnings table's counted, counted_no_rule_excludes and counted_unless_employer_convenience rows), not on a business's receipts (self-employment already), its costs, boarder payments or excluded pay; and only where the annualized figure is read, which is where the month's figure fails a standard (CO-4975, CO-6452), so a household eligible on the month is determined without it. A pay record that does not state it there cannot be determined (SEASONAL-UNSTATED: wages 3,000, 225.6% on the month; with the flag stated true and an expected year of 16,000, 16,000 / 12 / 1,330 = 100.3%, eligible). A business record decides the answer by itself (the first test), so a person with a business is annualized whether or not a pay record states the field.

Type yes/no, scope person, program Medicaid.
Uses: `earnings`, `ma_magi_earnings_treatment_table`.

```
any of the following is true:
  - (the sum of 1 for each receipt in Earnings where (Medicaid MAGI: how each kind of earnings is treated (table), for that receipt's kind is equal to counted_net_for_tax)) is more than 0
  - (the sum of 1 for each receipt in Earnings where ((all of the following are true:;   - Medicaid MAGI: how each kind of earnings is treated (table), for that receipt's kind is one of: counted, counted_no_rule_excludes, counted_unless_employer_convenience;   - that receipt's seasonal or commission))) is more than 0
```

### CO-6452 Medicaid: the month's MAGI household income, as a share of the poverty guideline `@engine`

This person's MAGI household income for the month (ma_magi_household_income, CO-503), before any annualized income (C.4.a) or premium tax credit income (C.5) is considered, as a fraction of the monthly federal poverty guideline for ma_magi_household_size: the "current ... monthly household income" on which 10 CCR 2505-10 8.100.4.C.4.a first tests an applicant.

Precision. Coverage pass 7, C7-07 (2026-11-24): the month evaluated is the current month of 8.100.4.C.4 (S3356, 'current or previous monthly household income'): the previous month's income is read as evidence of the current month's where the current month's is not yet verified (8.100.4.B.1.c, S5270), not as a second figure, and 42 CFR 435.603(h)(1) (S5271) bases an applicant's eligibility on current monthly income; the reading is OQ-1475, a state policy choice. Coverage pass 4, C4-05 (2026-11-23): each MAGI and CHP+ income test reads this figure first and the budget figure (ma_magi_household_income_pct_fpl, CO-504) only where this one fails, which is C.4.a's order ("Applicants who are found financially ineligible based on current or previous monthly household income") and C.5's: a ceiling is met if either figure meets it, and the CHP+ floor (over the Medicaid standard) only if both are over it. So an applicant who meets a standard on the month's income is determined although the annualized figure cannot be (an expected annual income not stated). The guideline is read as CO-4567 reads it.

### CO-646 Medicaid: Community Spouse Resource Allowance (CSRA) `@engine`

The amount of the couple's resources protected for the community spouse - the largest of (a) the couple's total resources at the § 8.100.7.L snapshot, but no more than the current CSRA maximum standard, (b) the increased CSRA of § 8.100.7.S (ma_csra_increased), and (c) an amount a court has ordered the institutionalized spouse to transfer to the community spouse - per 10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.7.M.1.

Precision. OQ-126 resolved: § 8.100.7.M.1 takes the largest of three amounts; (b) and (c) were added in the open-question sweep. Branch (a) gives the community spouse the couple's total resources up to the maximum, which 42 U.S.C. 1396r-5(f)(2)(A)(i) permits as a State plan standard set at the maximum (S1222): the spousal-share and minimum-standard terms never bind for such a State. § 8.100.7.M.1.a has no spousal-share (half-of-total) term and no minimum-standard floor; that shape belongs to 42 U.S.C. 1396r-5(f)(2)(A) (S371), which Colorado's fetched text does not adopt - see OQ-126. ma_csra_minimum (CO-827) is accordingly not read here. Reads ma_spousal_resources_at_snapshot (CO-888), not ssi_countable_resources_couple (CO-801): § 8.100.7.L's resource assessment is taken "at the time of initial Medical Assistance application" and § 8.100.7.M.1 says the CSRA is "established at intake only," while CO-801 is the current-month figure § 8.100.7.O.1 tests against the CSRA each month (CO-647) - the two must be able to differ once the couple spends down. Coverage pass 4, non-MAGI N4-13 (decision 4 of 2026-11-23: missing information is cannot determine unless the rule says otherwise; readers do not invent defaults): a court-ordered transfer to the community spouse (1396r-5(f)(3)) is read as stated, no longer as none when unstated.

Type money, scope person, program Medicaid.
Uses: `ma_court_ordered_transfer_to_community_spouse`, `ma_csra_increased`, `ma_csra_maximum`, `ma_spousal_resources_at_snapshot`.

```
the greater of (the greater of (the lesser of CSRA maximum standard (162660) and Medicaid: spouses' countable resources at the spousal impoverishment snapshot) and Medicaid: increased CSRA) and Court-ordered transfer to the community spouse
```

### CO-647 Medicaid: institutionalized spouse's countable resources `@engine`

The countable resources attributed to the institutionalized spouse for their own eligibility - the Medicaid countable resources (ma_ssi_countable_resources_individual) of the person and the spouse together minus the CSRA, for a person with a community spouse, or the person's own figure for the month otherwise (ma_ssi_countable_resources_in_month, CO-5322) - per 42 U.S.C. 1396r-5(c)(2) and 10 CCR 2505-10 §§ 8.100.7.O.1 and 8.100.5.N.4 (a community spouse's retirement accounts count).

Precision. The spouse is the legal spouse wherever each lives, as in ssi_countable_resources_couple (CO-801). When the CSRA has not been transferred to the community spouse by the deadline of § 8.100.7.M.3 (ma_csra_transfer_is_overdue, CO-4636), the couple's resources are attributed to the institutionalized spouse without the allowance (coverage review NM-19). Resource records, Medicaid track H1 (docs/reviews/records-holdings-medicaid.md): the couple excludes one automobile (20 CFR 416.1218(b), S4660; 42 U.S.C. 1396r-5(c)(5) counts the resources the SSI rules do not exclude): the smaller of the spouses' excluded automobiles (ma_ssi_excluded_automobile_equity_in_month, CO-5321, at the determination month) is added back to the two individual figures. A joint holding of the spouses is counted once (each spouse's list states its share). Coverage pass 4, non-MAGI N4-6: the couple excludes one automobile, a car the two own together counted once at its whole equity: the two spouses' own excluded automobiles (ma_ssi_excluded_automobile_equity_in_month, CO-5321) are added back less the couple's one, the larger of the two spouses' ma_ssi_couple_automobile_equity_in_month (CO-6733, a joint car at its whole equity), at least 0. For two different cars this is the smaller car, as before; for one joint car, nothing (it had added back the other spouse's half of the same car). Coverage pass 6, non-MAGI F6-2 (docs/reviews/coverage6-medicaid-nonmagi.md): per month. A person with no community spouse is judged each month on the holdings at that month's first moment (ma_ssi_countable_resources_in_month, CO-5322; 20 CFR 416.1207(a), S4501), so a retroactive month in which the person held more than the limit is not resource eligible (10 CCR 2505-10 8.100.3.E.1, S1503: a retroactive month needs "all applicable eligibility requirements" met in it; 8.100.7.A.2.f, the resource limits of 8.100.5). Before, every month read the determination month's figure (ma_ssi_countable_resources_individual, CO-4623), so a nursing facility resident who spent down before applying was resource eligible in the retroactive months. The couple's attribution and the CSRA stay at their dates (the spousal snapshot and attribution of 8.100.7.L-O are made at the application and the determination).

### CO-649 Medicaid: transfer penalty period, whole months `@engine`

The number of whole months this person is ineligible for Long-Term Care services because of uncompensated transfers of assets on or after the look-back date - the uncompensated value of the person's and the spouse's transfers (ma_uncompensated_transfers_in_lookback, CO-5325, each transfer a holdings record with its own date and the eligibility site's exemption finding) divided by the average regional monthly private-pay rate, with any partial month reported separately - per 42 U.S.C. 1396p(c)(1)(E) and 10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.7.F.2.c.i-d. An exempt transfer adds nothing.

Precision. A whole number, the floor of the division in § 8.100.7.F.2.c.i; the remaining partial month is § 8.100.7.F.2.d's separate day calculation (thirty days times the decimal fractional share, rounded up), reported by ma_transfer_penalty_days (CO-659) rather than folded into this item as a fraction of a month. The start date (8.100.7.F.2.c.ii) is transfer_penalty_period_start_date (CO-886), which ma_transfer_penalty_applies (CO-660) reads. Between institutionalized spouses (8.100.7.F.8) the division is multiplied by this person's share (ma_transfer_penalty_share_rate, CO-2235: half when apportioned) before the floor, and the months reassigned from a spouse who died or left the institution (ma_transfer_penalty_months_assigned_from_spouse, CO-2233) are added (OQ-94, resolved). Expressed as the negation of ceil(-x) because the pattern catalog has no floor operator. Blocked (OQ-1060): the divisor it reads (transfer_penalty_divisor, CO-832) rests on S1228, which is not a quotation. HCPF Operational Memo OM 25-073 (D-125), the only document that states them, could not be fetched on 2026-11-23 (hcpf.colorado.gov refused, HTTP 403; medicaid.gov, sos.state.co.us, ecfr.gov, law.cornell.edu, govinfo.gov and federalregister.gov answered but state no Colorado figure), so the item stays Draft until the memo is stored and the excerpt replaced by its quotation. Resource records, Medicaid track H1 (docs/reviews/records-holdings-medicaid.md): the transfers are the holdings records (CO-5300) with a disposed_date on or after the look-back date (CO-5325), in place of the undated total uncompensated_transfer_value_in_lookback (CO-824) and the one finding transfer_was_exempt (CO-825) for all of a person's transfers. An exemption is a finding about one transfer (decision D9: the record's ma_transfer_exempt), so an exempt transfer adds nothing and the person's other transfers still count; the months reassigned from a spouse are added whether or not any transfer is exempt (they were 0 for a person whose one finding was exempt, which could not tell the transfers apart). Pattern sweep, non-MAGI Medicaid (docs/reviews/pattern-sweep-nonmagi.md, P2): the person's spouse is read from the person's relationships as stated, required where read (decision 4 of 2026-11-23): before, a person with no relationships stated was read as having no spouse, so a spouse's transfers, trust or annuity were not asked for.

Type whole number, scope person, program Medicaid.

```

### CO-650 Medicaid: home equity disqualifies `@engine`

Whether this person's equity interest in the home exceeds the current home equity limit, disqualifying them from nursing facility or other Long-Term Care assistance, unless a spouse is lawfully residing in the home, per 42 U.S.C. 1396p(f) and 10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.5.M.3: the person's ownership interest in the home in the month (ma_home_equity_interest_in_month, CO-5327; § 8.100.5.M.2.a.ii, "The individual’s ownership interest in the home must have an equity value that").

Precision. Reads ma_spouse_or_qualifying_child_lives_in_home (CO-889), not ma_ltc_couple - 1396p(f)(2) excuses the disqualification when the spouse, or a child under 21, or a blind or permanently disabled child of any age, "is lawfully residing in the individual's home," which is a question about who lives in the home, not whether a community spouse exists apart from the institution. This also resolves OQ-92's dependent-child gap, since the new fact's meaning already covers the child branch. Equity equal to the limit disqualifies (">="), because § 8.100.5.M.2.a.ii exempts equity that "Is less than" the indexed amount; 42 U.S.C. 1396p(f)(1)(A)'s "exceeds" sets the federal floor of the disqualification, and the state text is the more restrictive reading at the single boundary value. The limit is read for long-term care only (OQ-820): § 8.100.5.M.2.a.ii, vi and M.3.f state it in the general ABD resource rules, but 42 U.S.C. 1396p(f) is a long-term care rule; the other § 8.100.5.M.2.a rules on the home are ma_home_is_countable_resource (CO-4622). Resource records, Medicaid track H1 (docs/reviews/records-holdings-medicaid.md): the equity is the person's share of the home holdings record's equity (CO-5300), not the whole home's: a couple's home is one joint holding stated on each spouse with each one's share (the twelve stored couples that stated the home's equity on each spouse are restated so), as 1396p(f)(1)(A) tests "the individual's equity interest" and M.2.a.ii "The individual’s ownership interest". A stated holdings list with no home record: no equity, not disqualified. Pattern sweep, non-MAGI Medicaid (docs/reviews/pattern-sweep-nonmagi.md, P1): ma_spouse_or_qualifying_child_lives_in_home (CO-889) is per month; the equity test reads it, as the equity, in the determination month. Coverage pass 7, non-MAGI F7-2 (docs/reviews/coverage7-medicaid-nonmagi.md): per month. The limit is indexed 'from year to year' (§ 8.100.5.M.2.a.ii, S4665), so a month reads the limit in force in it (730,000 in 2025, 752,000 in 2026; docs/operators.md, Resolution step 2), and a retroactive month is judged on what held in it (§ 8.100.3.E.1, S1503), so the equity interest of the month's holdings (CO-5327) and who lived in the home that month (CO-889) are read in the month too, as the long-term care resources are (CO-647, CO-648; coverage pass 6 F6-2). Before, the person-scope value read the determination year's limit and the determination month's equity in every month: equity between 730,000 and 752,000 did not disqualify a retroactive 2025 month of a 2026 determination.

Type yes/no, scope person-month, program Medicaid.
Uses: `ma_home_equity_interest_in_month`, `ma_home_equity_limit`, `ma_spouse_or_qualifying_child_lives_in_home`.

```
all of the following are true:
  - Medicaid: the person's equity interest in the home in the month is at least Home equity limit (752000)
  - it is not the case that Medicaid: spouse or qualifying child lives in the home
```

["all",[">=","ma_home_equity_interest_in_month","ma_home_equity_limit"],["not","ma_spouse_or_qualifying_child_lives_in_home"]]

### CO-652 Medicaid: LTC eligibility status `@engine`

The single Long-Term Care eligibility outcome for this person for the month - eligible for the long-term care setting the person requests (institutional, HCBS or PACE), or the reason for ineligibility - per 10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.7. It answers whether the criteria are met for the month; whether the month falls inside the coverage period (not before the retroactive months of § 8.100.3.E.1, and for QMB not before the effective month) is not tested here, as ma_month_is_before_coverage_period (CO-4101) tests it for the MAGI and OAP outcomes (final verification pass 3, P3-1).

Precision. Tests, in order, whether the person is institutionalized, designated for an HCBS waiver or requesting PACE at all; Colorado residency (§ 8.100.3.G.1.a); aged, blind or disabled (§ 8.100.3.F.1.f-g); citizenship and immigration status (§ 8.100.3.G.1.g; § 8.7100.C.1), where a child, pregnant or postpartum person designated for an HCBS waiver passes under Cover All Coloradans (§ 8.100.3.G.1.g.ix.1.b reaches the Long-Term Care waivers except PACE); the income test; the resource test; home equity; the level of care - nursing facility level of care, or for a waiver designee the level of care that waiver requires (ma_meets_designated_waiver_level_of_care, CO-1178); the transfer penalty, which § 8.100.7.F.2.c.ii starts only once the person is otherwise eligible, so a person who fails income, resources, home equity or level of care is reported for that reason first; then eligibility for the setting the person requests (ma_ltc_setting_requested, CO-2411): PACE (ma_pace_eligible), HCBS (ma_hcbs_waiver_eligible) or institutional care (institutionalized, nursing facility level of care, status). A person who passes every financial and functional test but not the requested setting's own conditions (outside a PACE service area, for example) is not_eligible_for_requested_setting. Coverage pass 7, non-MAGI F7-5 (docs/reviews/coverage7-medicaid-nonmagi.md): reads the general requirement of 10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.3.G.1.c (S659) through ma_meets_imd_requirement (CO-1179), as the SSI-related groups (CO-611) and the MAGI groups (CO-562) do: G.1 states what a person "shall" meet "To be eligible to receive Medical Assistance", and names no category it leaves out. Before, a patient aged 21 to 64 of an institution for mental diseases could be found eligible here although no other Medical Assistance category admitted him (IMD-LTC, stored household CO-1104).

### CO-653 Medicaid: is HCBS waiver eligible `@engine`

Whether this person is eligible for a Home and Community-Based Services waiver for the month - a Colorado resident who is aged, blind or disabled, meets the citizenship and immigration status requirement (or, as a child, pregnant or postpartum person, Cover All Coloradans), is designated for a waiver's target group within its age criteria, meets the level of care that waiver requires, and is eligible through the special income group, SSI eligibility, or the Working Adults with Disabilities Buy-In (for the EBD, CMHS, BI, CIH, SLS and DD waivers) - per 10 CCR 2505-10 §§ 8.100.3.F.1.g, 8.100.3.G.1, 8.100.7.B.1, 8.7100.C and 8.7100.D.

Precision. The designated waiver's age criteria (ma_hcbs_waiver_age_criteria_met, CO-1164, § 8.7101) are tested, and the Buy-In waiver list names the Complementary and Integrative Health waiver (CIH), the current name of the former Spinal Cord Injury waiver, as § 8.7101.H and its eligibility-group list state. § 8.100.7.B.1.c's Buy-In route is not gated on ma_ltc_financially_eligible (which requires the special income group and the LTC resource standard) because § 8.100.6.P.1.c states Buy-In resources are not counted and its income test is 450% FPL, not 300% of the SSI benefit rate; it is limited instead to the waivers § 8.100.7.B.1.c.i names. Residency, aged/blind/disabled (§ 8.100.3.F.1.g) and status are tested (B-3), status through ma_meets_status_for_cover_all_coloradans_categories (CO-1174) because § 8.100.3.G.1.g.ix.1.b reaches the Long-Term Care waivers except PACE; and the level of care is the designated waiver's (ma_meets_designated_waiver_level_of_care, CO-1178: ICF/IID for CES, SLS, DD and CHRP's developmental disability route, nursing facility or hospital for CwCHN and CIH), not nursing facility level of care for every waiver (S-4, D-75 § 8.7101). The SSI-related route is open to every waiver although § 8.7101.C.3 lists CHRP's served groups as foster care children and 42 CFR 435.217 only (N-4); CHRP's population is children, for whom the special income group route gives the same result. Needs-fact sweep: the designated waiver's diagnoses, settings and BI's injury before 65 are tested (ma_meets_hcbs_waiver_condition_criteria, CO-2270; OQ-210, resolved). A person in a Medicaid Buy-In program has no spousal impoverishment computation (ma_ltc_couple, CO-643; OQ-127, resolved). HCPF review note C-14: eligible means eligible, not enrolled; HCBS waivers have enrollment limits and waiting lists (§ 8.7100, D-75), and whether a slot is open is not a test here. § 8.100.3.F.1.i's group of children 18 and under who would otherwise require institutionalization (1902(e)(3), S3005) is served through the Children with Complex Health Needs waiver (cwchn), with the child's own income under the 300% special income group (final verification pass 3, P3-2). Coverage review NM-22: B.1.a's 'SSI (including 1619b) or OAP Medicaid eligible' includes continued SSI status without payment (retains_ssi_status_without_payment) and OAP SISC B (ma_oap_sisc_b_eligible), which were not routes. Coverage pass 4, non-MAGI N4-13 (decision 4 of 2026-11-23: missing information is cannot determine unless the rule says otherwise; readers do not invent defaults): whether the person keeps SSI status without payment (1619(b)) is read as stated, no longer as no when unstated. Pattern sweep, non-MAGI Medicaid (docs/reviews/pattern-sweep-nonmagi.md, P1): aged, blind or disabled is read in the month with the disability onset gate (ma_is_aged_blind_or_disabled_in_month, CO-5201; 10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.5.C.4.b, S3623: disability approved, or 'a disability onset date determined on or prior to the date of a medical service'; § 8.100.3.E.1, S1503), as the SSI-related groups (CO-611) and OAP SISC B (CO-1177) already read it. Before, it read ma_is_aged_blind_or_disabled (CO-603), which has no onset gate, so a retroactive month before the onset of a disability was a disabled month. Pattern sweep, non-MAGI Medicaid (docs/reviews/pattern-sweep-nonmagi.md, P1): SSI status without payment (1619(b)) is read in the month (ma_retains_ssi_status_in_month, CO-7504: for a month before the determination month, not before the month of the SSI award's eligibility date). Before, the status of the determination date was read in every month.

### CO-654 Medicaid: is PACE eligible `@engine`

Whether this person is eligible to enroll in the Program of All-Inclusive Care for the Elderly for the month - a Colorado resident meeting the citizenship and immigration status requirement, aged, blind or disabled, ma_pace_min_age or older, meets the nursing facility level of care, resides in a PACE organization's service area, can live in a community setting without jeopardizing health or safety, and is financially eligible for Long-Term Care, or reaches PACE through SSI (including 1619(b)) or OAP Medicaid (10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.7.B.1.a) with no disqualifying home equity and no transfer penalty - per 10 CCR 2505-10 §§ 8.100.3.F.1.f-g, 8.100.3.G.1, 8.7100.B/8.7100.C.9 and 8.497, and 42 CFR 460.150(b)-(c), which § 8.497.1.B.1 incorporates.

Precision. The age floor is 42 CFR 460.150(b)(1)'s, incorporated by § 8.497.1.B.1 (OQ-93). Residence in a PACE organization's service area (460.150(b)(3)) and the ability to live in a community setting without jeopardizing health or safety (460.150(c)) are tested. Residency, status and aged/blind/disabled are tested; status is ma_meets_citizenship_requirement (CO-509) alone, because § 8.100.3.G.1.g.ix.1.b excepts PACE from the Long-Term Care waivers Cover All Coloradans reaches. Time audit T-1 (2026-11-23): the minimum age reads ma_age_on_last_day_of_month (CO-5402), so a person who reaches 55 during the month meets it for the month (§ 8.100.5.C.1, S3900; OQ-950); it read age (CO-300), the age on the determination date, in every month. Coverage pass 6, non-MAGI F6-9 (docs/reviews/coverage6-medicaid-nonmagi.md): § 8.100.7.B.1 (S3408) gives HCBS and PACE the same routes: "a. are SSI (including 1619b) or OAP Medicaid eligible; or b. are eligible under the Institutionalized 300% Special Income category". PACE now takes the B.1.a route ma_ltc_unmet_requirement (CO-3310) and ma_hcbs_waiver_eligible (CO-653) already take, through ma_reaches_hcbs_without_special_income_group (CO-4630, which reads the requested setting PACE with HCBS; the Buy-In route of B.1.c is HCBS only), keeping the home equity limit and the transfer penalty, which apply to every long-term care route (ma_home_equity_disqualifies, CO-650; ma_transfer_penalty_applies, CO-660). Before, PACE read only ma_ltc_financially_eligible (CO-651: the 300% test and the long-term care resource test), so a 1619(b) worker above 300% of the FBR was not_eligible_for_requested_setting. Pattern sweep, non-MAGI Medicaid (docs/reviews/pattern-sweep-nonmagi.md, P1): aged, blind or disabled is read in the month with the disability onset gate (ma_is_aged_blind_or_disabled_in_month, CO-5201; 10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.5.C.4.b, S3623: disability approved, or 'a disability onset date determined on or prior to the date of a medical service'; § 8.100.3.E.1, S1503), as the SSI-related groups (CO-611) and OAP SISC B (CO-1177) already read it. Before, it read ma_is_aged_blind_or_disabled (CO-603), which has no onset gate, so a retroactive month before the onset of a disability was a disabled month.

### CO-655 Medicaid: Minimum Monthly Maintenance Needs Allowance (MMMNA) `@engine`

The community spouse's minimum monthly income needs - the MMMNA standard plus an excess shelter allowance for shelter costs above ma_mmmna_shelter_threshold_pct of the standard, the two together capped at the current MMMNA maximum, plus the additional amount for the community spouse's and dependents' medical expenses and premiums (ma_community_spouse_medical_needs, CO-3619) - per 42 U.S.C. 1396r-5(d)(3)-(4) and 10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.7.Q.1, Q.2 and Q.4.

Precision. Q.4 caps only "the total that results from adding the current MMMNA and the excess shelter allowance", so the Q.2 amount is added after the cap (OQ-620 records the reading of Q.2's "may be approved"). § 8.100.7.R.2 calls the community spouse's minimum monthly needs "the MMMNA", so the monthly income allowance (CO-656) and the increased resource allowance (CO-1977) read this total. 8.100.7.Q.3's exceptional-circumstances amount is substituted only "if established through a fair hearing", a hearing decision outside the eligibility determination, and is not modeled.

### CO-657 Medicaid: family allowance `@engine`

The sum of the allowance for each dependent family member living with the community spouse: one third of the amount by which the MMMNA standard exceeds that member's own monthly income, the federal floor of 42 U.S.C. 1396r-5(d)(1)(C), which supersedes the smaller figure of 10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.7.T.1.c.i (one third of the MMMNA standard, reduced by the member's income).

Precision. A family member's income includes self-employment (ma_self_employment_net_earnings, CO-1704) and the unearned receipts the spousal impoverishment rules count (ma_spousal_unearned_receipts, CO-5531) with gambling winnings (CO-5512): unemployment compensation included, which the scalar sum left out before receipt records; child support and cash assistance left out as before (OQ-974). The family members are derived from the child, parent and tax-dependent edges and residence with the community spouse (ma_family_allowance_members, CO-2469). The state figure (MMMNA/3 - I) is never more than the federal one ((MMMNA - I)/3) and is smaller whenever the member has income, so the federal floor is the whole formula; a member whose income is at or above the standard gets 0.

Type money, scope person-month, program Medicaid.

### CO-658 Medicaid: patient payment `@engine`

The amount of an institutionalized person's income applied monthly to the cost of Long-Term Care institution care, once they have been determined eligible for Medical Assistance (10 CCR 2505-10 §§ 8.100.7.T.1 and 8.100.7.V.3.b-i; 42 CFR 435.725(c)): the income left after the personal needs allowance and the earned income reserve (ma_patient_payment_available_income, CO-3616), less the community spouse monthly income allowance, the family allowance, the Home Maintenance Allowance (CO-3618), mandatory income tax withheld, garnishments repaying a federal assistance overpayment, the Medicare Part B premium the person pays in the first ma_nf_part_b_premium_deduction_months months in the Nursing Facility and the Medicare Part D premium, floored at zero, plus any Long-Term Care insurance benefits for the month and, for a veteran or surviving spouse of a veteran with no dependents in a State Veterans Home, the VA pension's Aid and Attendance and Unusual Medical Expenses portion (§ 8.100.5.K.2); or 0 for a person who is not institutionalized or who has not been determined financially eligible for LTC.

Precision. Deducts ma_personal_needs_allowance (CO-1987), which is the veterans-related $90 allowance for a resident who qualifies for it, otherwise the base allowance (ma_personal_needs_allowance_institutional, CO-887, OQ-98 and OQ-212 resolved), and the $65 plus one-half earned income reserve, inside CO-3616. The community spouse income allowance term is included only when ma_ltc_couple is true and the institutionalized spouse does not refuse to make it available (ma_institutionalized_spouse_refuses_income_allowance, CO-1949): § 8.100.7.T.1.b deducts the allowance 'only to the extent that income of the institutionalized spouse is actually made available', and T.1.e applies income not made available to the cost of care (coverage review NM-14). An allowance made available in part is read as made available. The deductions follow § 8.100.7.V.3.b.ii in full: 1) the personal needs allowance; 2) the monthly income allowance; 3) the family allowance; 4) the Home Maintenance Allowance; 5) trustee fees, which are the up-to-$20 a month retained by an income trust (ma_income_trust_distribution, CO-2238, OQ-96), so they are inside the distribution; 6) mandatory income tax withheld (V.3.d.iv); 7) garnishments repaying a federal assistance overpayment; 8.a) the Medicare Part B premium only for the first and second month in the Nursing Facility, counted from the month of institution_entry_date (V.3.b.ii.8.a and V.1.e.i, 'the first two months of admission'; V.1.e.ii says 'the first two months of Long-Term Care institution eligibility', OQ-721), and not when the State already pays it through the Medicare Buy-In, which medicare_part_b_premium_paid states as 0 (V.1.e.ii; OQ-520, resolved); 8.b) the Part D premium in every month; 8.c) other medical and remedial expenses go through NF PETI and are not deducted, so other health insurance premiums (health_insurance_premiums_paid less Parts B and D) are not deducted here. SSI paid to the institutionalized person is outside ma_ltc_gross_income (V.3.i.ii). The VA Aid and Attendance and Unusual Medical Expenses portion, which ma_ltc_gross_income (CO-641) leaves out, is added back after the floor at zero when ma_va_aid_and_attendance_is_patient_payment (CO-4103) is true: § 8.100.5.K.2 says the portion 'shall be used as patient payment to the medical facility', so it is not reduced by the deductions, which are taken from the person's other income; under K.1.a-b it is not used. Long-Term Care insurance benefits are added after the floor at zero (V.3.c.i.1 and b: with no income left, only the insurance payment is used); V.3.c.i.1.a's order of application when the total exceeds the cost of care is the facility's, and no cost-of-care fact is read. For a person with an income trust the income applied is the trust's monthly distribution; the trust rule lists only the personal needs allowance, spousal income payments and approved PETI payments as deductions from the distribution; the family allowance is still deducted, because 42 U.S.C. 1396r-5(d)(1) requires it for every institutionalized spouse (OQ-471). § 8.100.7.T.1 makes the deductions only "during each month after the institutionalized spouse becomes Medical Assistance eligible," and § 8.100.7.V.3.b only "once an applicant... has been determined eligible for Medical Assistance"; the outcome's type is money, so a person who is not institutionalized, or who is institutionalized but not yet (or no longer) financially eligible for LTC, reports 0 rather than "not applicable." A resident's private health insurance premium is a Nursing Facility PETI-IME expense, prior authorized (§ 8.482.33.A, C.1-2, S3008), which V.3.b.ii.8.c leaves out of the patient payment deductions (final verification pass 3, P3-3). Income the eligibility site leaves out because it was committed elsewhere in the admission month, or is needed for living expenses in the discharge month (§ 8.100.7.V.4.a.iii-vi; ma_patient_payment_income_committed_elsewhere, CO-4638), is deducted before the floor (coverage review NM-29). Blocked (OQ-1060): the personal needs allowance it deducts (CO-1987, CO-887) rests on S1228, which is not a quotation. HCPF Operational Memo OM 25-073 (D-125), the only document that states them, could not be fetched on 2026-11-23 (hcpf.colorado.gov refused, HTTP 403; medicaid.gov, sos.state.co.us, ecfr.gov, law.cornell.edu, govinfo.gov and federalregister.gov answered but state no Colorado figure), so the item stays Draft until the memo is stored and the excerpt replaced by its quotation. Coverage pass 4, non-MAGI N4-13 (decision 4 of 2026-11-23: missing information is cannot determine unless the rule says otherwise; readers do not invent defaults): the deductions of 8.100.7.V.3 (mandatory income tax, a garnishment repaying a federal assistance overpayment, the Medicare Part B and Part D premiums) and the long-term care insurance benefits added under 8.100.7.C.3 are read as stated; none is read as 0 when unstated any more. A case states 0 where the person has none. OQ-471 is resolved (coverage pass 6, non-MAGI F6-11): 42 U.S.C. 1396r-5(d)(1) (S5033) requires the family allowance for every institutionalized spouse, a person with an income trust included; the institutionalized spouse's refusal to make the income allowance available keeps the default its fact declares (F6-10).

### CO-662 Medicaid: MMMNA standard `@engine`

The current minimum monthly maintenance needs allowance before any excess shelter allowance - ma_mmmna_applicable_pct (CO-1801) of the monthly federal poverty guideline for a family of ma_mmmna_family_size (CO-3032), as adjusted in the most recent July on or before the month evaluated - per 42 U.S.C. 1396r-5(d)(3)(A)(i)/(B)(iii) and 10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.7.Q.1.a.

Precision. § 8.100.7.Q.1.a (S651) states the MMMNA "is equal to 150% of the federal poverty level for a family of two and is adjusted in July of each year", so the standard is derived from the one federal table, federal_poverty_guideline_annual_table (CO-181), as of the first day of the most recent month numbered ma_mmmna_adjustment_month (CO-3031) on or before the month evaluated (P25, P50): January through June uses the guideline adjusted the previous July. OQ-145 resolved; hard-coded numbers audit D-1: the size-2 figure was restated as its own July-dated parameter (CO-1954), now retired. Coverage pass 7, non-MAGI F7-1 (docs/reviews/coverage7-medicaid-nonmagi.md): the July is the most recent one on or before the month evaluated (the month in context), not the one before the determination month. Q.1.a's 'current' MMMNA of a month is the standard in force in that month: a retroactive month is judged on the requirements it met (§ 8.100.3.E.1, S1503), and § 8.100.7.R.4 (S5240) has the MMMNA adjusted 'on a monthly basis' for a continuing change. Before, every month read the July before the determination month, so a retroactive May or June of a determination made from July to September read the new July's standard (2,705 in 2026 in place of 2,643.75), and a month after a later July kept the earlier one (MMMNA-RETRO, stored household CO-1100). Its readers (ma_mmmna CO-655, ma_family_allowance CO-657 and through them the income allowance CO-656 and the patient payment CO-658) take it in each month; the CSRA increase (CO-1977) reads it in the determination month.

The person's unearned receipts of the month that are received infrequently or irregularly (each record's irregular field: received only once in the calendar quarter from a single source and not in the month before or after, or not reasonably expected; 20 CFR 416.1124(c)(6)) and that the SSI method's counting table counts (ma_ssi_receipt_treatment_table, CO-5510: counted, counted because no rule excludes it, or rents), each at the amount ma_ssi_unearned_receipts (CO-5511) counts it: less the parts the method does not count (a plan for self-support's set-aside, what a death benefit paid for the last illness and burial, an award's claim expenses, a veterans benefit's amount for a dependent); a retroactive Title II or SSI payment left out; plus the amount of such a receipt of a person of the case the person lives with that is attributable to the person as a dependent (20 CFR 416.1123(e)(2)(i)), as ma_ssi_unearned_receipts reads it.

Gambling winnings and child support, which the readers add apart (ma_ssi_gambling_receipts, ma_ssi_child_support_receipts), are not part of this sum, so the $60 is taken from the other unearned income only. Receipts not stated: cannot determine (decision 4). Field-effect sweep (docs/reviews/field-sweep-snap-cash-nonmagi.md), FS-MA-1: a receipt stated as a stream (no month and no date) is received only in the months from the month of its start_date through the month of its end_date (each absent: before, or through, the months the case covers; CO-5000), since unearned income "is countable as income in the month received" (10 CCR 2505-10 8.100.5.F.5, S3001) and is counted "when you receive it" (20 CFR 416.1123(a), S4940); in its first and last months it is read at its amount, and a payment stated with its month or date is placed by it, a final payment after the stream ended included. Before, a stream was counted in every month whatever its dates. The clause is SNAP's (snap_counted_recurring_receipts, CO-5011). Field-effect sweep (docs/reviews/field-sweep-snap-cash-nonmagi.md), FS-MA-8: of a retroactive payment from a benefit program other than SSI, the legal fees connected with the claim (designated_for_legal_fees, the part of designated_for_lump_sum_costs that is legal fees) are subtracted, and the payment's other designated costs are not: 20 CFR 416.1123(b)(3) (S4756), "If you receive a retroactive check from a benefit program other than SSI, legal fees connected with the claim are subtracted. ### CO-6731 SSI method: excluded infrequent or irregular unearned income `@engine`

The part of the person's infrequent or irregular unearned income for the month that the SSI method does not count: what remains, after the earlier months of the calendar quarter, of the first ssi_infrequent_unearned_income_quarterly_exclusion ($60) of such income received in the quarter (20 CFR 416.1124(c)(6), S2609), brought to the aged, blind and disabled groups by 42 CFR 435.601(b)(2) (S4754), Colorado's text naming nothing.

Precision. The quarter's running total of the irregular receipts (ma_ssi_irregular_unearned_receipts, CO-6730), capped at the exclusion, less the same total through the month before, so the quarter's first $60 is excluded in the months it is received and no more (the pattern of ma_ssi_excluded_infrequent_earned_income, CO-4883). The quarter is the calendar quarter containing the month. 416.1124(a) applies the exclusions of (c) in the order listed, so (c)(6) comes before the $20 general exclusion ((c)(12)), which the readers apply after ma_ssi_unearned_receipts (CO-5511) subtracts this. Receipts not stated: cannot determine (decision 4).

### CO-6733 Medicaid SSI method: the couple's largest automobile equity on a spouse's list `@engine`

The largest equity, for the couple, of a vehicle on the person's holdings list that is used for transportation and held at the first moment of the month: a vehicle the person owns with the spouse (co_owners spouse) at its whole equity, value less amount owed, since the couple owns all of it; any other at the person's share of its equity; none below 0. The automobile 20 CFR 416.1218(b) (S4660) excludes "In determining the resources of an individual (and spouse, if any)" is one automobile for the couple, so the couple's figures exclude the larger of the two spouses' values of this item, a car the two own together counted once at its whole equity.

Precision. Coverage pass 4, non-MAGI N4-6 (docs/reviews/coverage4-medicaid-nonmagi.md): a car the spouses own together is stated on each list with the same holding_id and each spouse's share (the joint-holding convention, holdings CO-5300), so each spouse's own excluded automobile (ma_ssi_excluded_automobile_equity_in_month, CO-5321) is half of it; the couple figures had added back the smaller of the two, which for one joint car is the other half of the same car, so half the car was counted. The couple figures now add back the two spouses' own exclusions less the couple's one (the larger of this item for the two), which is the smaller of two different cars, as before, and nothing for one joint car. A co_owners field not stated means no one else owns the holding (its absence meaning). Field-effect sweep (docs/reviews/field-sweep-snap-cash-nonmagi.md), FS-MA-4: a holding the person cannot get at (accessible false) because it is in probate, frozen by a creditor's lien or levy or a court order, or held under a trust's terms the person can neither revoke nor direct (inaccessible_reason) is not read: Medical Assistance deems available a resource the person "is not legally restricted from using" (10 CCR 2505-10 8.100.5.E.3.c, S4670), and "If a property right cannot be liquidated, the property will not be considered a resource" (20 CFR 416.1201(a)(1), S4500). One a co-owner refuses to release is still read, since a resource is not "unavailable merely because the individual ... may need to initiate legal proceedings to access" it (E.4, S4670). accessible defaults to true (CO-5300); the reason is required where it is false (decision 4). Before, accessible was not read.

Type money, scope person-month, program Medicaid.
Uses: `holdings`, `ma_ssi_holding_treatment_table`.

```
the largest for each holding in Holdings where
    all of the following are true:
      - Medicaid, SSI method: how each kind of holding is treated (table), for that holding's kind is equal to counted_less_one_transportation_vehicle
      - that holding is valued in the month
      - any of the following is true:
        - that holding's accessible
        - it is not the case that that holding's inaccessible reason is one of: probate, lien_or_court_order, trust_terms
      - any of the following is true:
        - that holding's disposed date is unknown
        - the month containing that holding's disposed date is at least the month
      - that holding's used for transportation
  of
    the greater of 0 and (if (that holding's co owners, otherwise none) is equal to spouse;   then that holding's value minus that holding's amount owed; otherwise (that holding's share, otherwise 1) times (that holding's value minus that holding's amount owed))
```

### CO-7050 Medicaid: children a pregnant member is expected to deliver, counted in the month `@engine`

For a person pregnant at some time in the month (ma_is_pregnant_in_month, CO-3601), the number of children 10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.4.E.2 and 42 CFR 435.603(b) add to her in a MAGI family size for that month: the children she is expected to deliver in that pregnancy (expected_number_of_children), less the children she gave birth to in the month who are persons of the case, since each of them is counted in the household as a person from the month of birth; never below 0. 0 in a month she is not pregnant.

Precision. Coverage pass 5, C5-02 (2026-11-23). E.2 counts a pregnant woman as "herself plus the number of children she is expected to deliver"; the size is taken for each month (C4-08), so the pregnancy is the month's: a retroactive month in which she was pregnant counts her expected children although the pregnancy has ended by the determination, and a retroactive month before the pregnancy began counts none. In the month of a birth she was pregnant on some day of it (§ 8.100.4.G.1, S3351: eligibility on any day of a month is eligibility for the whole month), and the child born that month is also a person of the case: on a day before the birth the family is herself plus the expected child, on a day after it herself plus the child, so the child is counted once, as itself. A child she gave birth to is read by the gave_birth_to relationship (the fact of birth a newborn's case states); a delivered child who is not a person of the case is not subtracted. The relationships not stated: unknown (decision 4).

### CO-7351 Medicaid: receives SSI in the month `@engine`

Whether the person is an SSI recipient in the month (10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.6.C.1.a, 'persons receiving financial assistance under SSI'): SSA has awarded the person SSI (receives_ssi, CO-012) and, for a month before the determination month, the month is not before the month of the original SSI eligibility date (ssi_eligibility_date, CO-7350; § 8.100.6.C.7).

Precision. The determination month and the months after read the award as stated on the determination date. A retroactive month (§ 8.100.3.E.1, S1503: the person 'met all applicable eligibility requirements' in it) is an SSI month from the month the award makes the person eligible (8.100.5.C.1: eligibility is effective 'the first day of the month the person becomes eligible'); a month before it is judged by the SSI-related tests of the month. The eligibility date is required for such a month (decision 4 of 2026-11-23). Coverage pass 7, non-MAGI F7-7 (docs/reviews/coverage7-medicaid-nonmagi.md): an infant within the special provision of § 8.100.6.C.10.a.i (S5245; ma_ssi_infant_eligible_from_birth, CO-7723: born in a hospital, SSA's onset in the stay at birth, the birth within three months of the SSI eligibility date) is an SSI recipient from the month of birth: 'the effective date of Medicaid eligibility shall be the infant's date of birth'. Before, the birth month was judged by the SSI-related tests with the parents' income deemed (INFANT-SSI, stored household CO-1107). The provision is read only after the eligibility-date test fails and from the birth month, so no other person is asked its facts.

### CO-7353 Medicaid SSI method: an ineligible spouse's income is not deemed `@engine`

Whether, for the SSI-related income test of the month, no income is deemed to the person from a spouse who lives with the person (20 CFR 416.1163(d)(1), S5031, as 42 CFR 435.601(b)(2), S4754, applies the SSI methodology where Colorado's text is silent): the spouse is an ineligible spouse (10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.5.H.2.c, 'a parent or spouse who is not applying or eligible for SSI', S1506), is not aged, blind or disabled in the month, and the spouse's earned and unearned income, less the Ineligible Child Allocation (H.3.a.i), is not more than the couple Federal Benefit Rate less the individual one. The person's own countable income is then tested against the individual rate.

Precision. The spouse is a member of ma_ssi_couple_members (CO-3626), so lives with the person in the month. The spouse's income is the unearned receipts the SSI method counts (ma_ssi_unearned_receipts) and gambling winnings, without in-kind support and maintenance (20 CFR 416.1161(a)(11), S5032), plus gross earned income less what the SSI method does not count (as ma_ssi_couple_earned_income_after_exclusions, CO-6051, counts each member's), less the whole Ineligible Child Allocation (ma_ssi_ineligible_child_allocation, CO-2277; allocated from unearned income, then earned, H.3.b.i), not below zero. A spouse who is aged, blind or disabled is not read as an ineligible spouse here: such a spouse, applying with the person, is a possible eligible spouse, and the couple's combined test applies as before (OQ-1385). Not stated whether the spouse applied for SSI (has_applied_for_ssi) where the spouse is not aged, blind or disabled: cannot determine (decision 4). Colorado's Medicare Savings Program text compares a couple's income with the couple maximum 'whether one or both members apply' (§ 8.100.6.L.3), so the Medicare Savings Programs do not read this item. Pattern sweep, non-MAGI Medicaid (docs/reviews/pattern-sweep-nonmagi.md, P1): aged, blind or disabled is read in the month with the disability onset gate (ma_is_aged_blind_or_disabled_in_month, CO-5201; 10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.5.C.4.b, S3623: disability approved, or 'a disability onset date determined on or prior to the date of a medical service'; § 8.100.3.E.1, S1503), as the SSI-related groups (CO-611) and OAP SISC B (CO-1177) already read it. Before, it read ma_is_aged_blind_or_disabled (CO-603), which has no onset gate, so a retroactive month before the onset of a disability was a disabled month. Pattern sweep, non-MAGI Medicaid (docs/reviews/pattern-sweep-nonmagi.md, P2): the SSI method's excluded earned income (ma_ssi_excluded_earned_income, CO-2471; the infrequent part, CO-4883) and in-kind support and maintenance (ssi_in_kind_support_and_maintenance, CO-802) are read as computed, required where read (decision 4 of 2026-11-23): they are unknown only where a fact they rest on is not stated (a student's school attendance, the shelter costs others pay), and no rule reads that as none; before, an unknown figure was read as 0.

### CO-7401 Medicaid: the pregnancy coverage period opens in the month `@engine`

Whether the month is a month of the application being determined in which the person, while pregnant, was eligible for and received Medical Assistance, so that the coverage period of 10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.4.G.5 and 42 U.S.C. 1396a(e)(5) and (e)(16) can run from it: a month from the first month of the requested retroactive period (ma_retroactive_coverage_requested, CO-4100; § 8.100.3.E), or else the month of application, through the determination month, in which the eligibility history (ma_prior_enrollment_category, CO-2424) records the Pregnant Women category; or records other Medical Assistance (Parent/Caretaker Relative or any other category) in a month she was pregnant (ma_is_pregnant_in_month, CO-3601); or in which she met the Pregnant Women category (ma_is_pregnant_category, CO-546) and the residency requirement of the month (ma_meets_residency_in_month, CO-7650), with neither earned nor unearned income verification pending in the month. A month the history records as Pregnant Women opens a period for a pregnancy she had in that month: not a month in the postpartum year of a pregnancy that ended before it (pregnancy_ended_before_month CO-7771, latest_pregnancy_end_date_before_month CO-7772) unless she was pregnant in it (ma_is_pregnant_in_month, CO-3601).

Precision. Coverage pass 6, C6-01 and C6-02 (2026-11-24). 42 U.S.C. 1396a(e)(5) (S5060): 'A woman who, while pregnant, is eligible for, has applied for, and has received medical assistance under the State plan, shall continue to be eligible under the plan, as though she were pregnant, for all pregnancy-related and postpartum medical assistance', and (e)(16)(A) (S224) extends it to the 12-month period for 'an individual who, while pregnant, is eligible for and has received medical assistance under the State plan ... (including during a period of retroactive eligibility)': the provision reaches any Medical Assistance received while pregnant, not only the Pregnant Women category, and any month of the pregnancy, not only the month of application. The history is the record of approvals made before this determination (CO-2424), so it is read only for a month before the determination month; a month the history records as Pregnant Women opens the period as recorded (heavier-definitions audit H-6), and one it records as other Medical Assistance opens it where she was pregnant in that month. A month of this application in which the history records none, or which it does not record, is tested on the category: G.5 ('Once eligibility has been approved') and 8.100.3.E.2 ('An applicant does not have to be eligible in the month of application'), so a pregnant applicant ineligible in the application month (a last paycheck) and eligible in a later month of the same application opens the period in that later month (C6-02). The category needs income verification not pending in the month (G.5, 'once the income verification requirements are met'; audit L-3), tested after it, so a month over the standard is decided without the verification state. A month after the determination month opens nothing in this determination. A retroactive month is a month of this application only where retroactive coverage was requested. Coverage pass 7 (2026-11-24): C7-08, a retroactive month stands on its own facts (42 CFR 435.915(a)(2), S218: 'Would have been eligible for Medicaid at the time he received the services'): the category arm reads the month's residency (ma_meets_residency_in_month, CO-7650, whose retroactive months read state_of_residence_start_date) instead of a supplied date the person became eligible (ma_eligibility_start_date, retired), which a month's own facts decide; C7-02, the history arm opens a month only for a pregnancy she had in it: a month the history records as Pregnant Women in the postpartum year of an earlier pregnancy (on or before the 12th month after a recorded end before the month) is that pregnancy's month, and opens nothing unless she was pregnant again in it, so a later pregnancy opens its own period only in a month of that pregnancy (PG-SECOND: the history records Pregnant Women from March 2025 through September 2026 for a pregnancy that ended 2025-09-10; October 2025 to September 2026 are postpartum months of it and open nothing for the pregnancy that began 2026-10-05). The retroactive period's length is read as ma_pregnancy_coverage_period_start_month (CO-565) reads it, not from CO-2472 (circular).

Type yes/no, scope person-month, program Medicaid.
Uses: `latest_pregnancy_end_date_before_month`, `ma_application_date`, `ma_earned_income_verification_is_pending`, `ma_is_pregnant_category`, `ma_is_pregnant_in_month`, `ma_meets_residency_in_month`, `ma_postpartum_coverage_months`, `ma_prior_enrollment_category`, `ma_retroactive_coverage_change_date`, `ma_retroactive_coverage_months`, `ma_retroactive_coverage_months_other_after_change`, `ma_retroactive_coverage_requested`, `ma_unearned_income_verification_is_pending`, `pregnancy_ended_before_month`.

```
all of the following are true:
  - the month is at most the month containing the Determination Date
  - the month is at least (if Retroactive Medical Assistance coverage requested, otherwise no;   then (if Medicaid: application date is less than Medicaid: first application date under the shorter retroactive periods (2027-01-01);   then Retroactive Medical Assistance coverage period, months (3); otherwise Medicaid: retroactive months for other applicants from 2027 (2)) months before the month containing Medicaid: application date; otherwise the month containing Medicaid: application date)

        - the month is more than Postpartum Medical Assistance coverage period, months (12) months after the month containing Latest pregnancy end before the month, as the case records it
    - all of the following are true:
      - the month is less than the month containing the Determination Date
      - Medicaid: category enrolled in for a past month is one of: parent_caretaker, other_medical_assistance, otherwise no
      - Medicaid: is pregnant in the month
    - all of the following are true:
      - Medicaid: meets the Pregnant Women MAGI category
      - Medicaid: meets the residency requirement in the month

      - it is not the case that Medical Assistance: unearned income verification is pending

### CO-7405 Medicaid: first month of a child's continuous eligibility period `@engine`

The first month of a child's 12-month continuous eligibility period under 10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.3.Q.2: the month CBMS records the period as beginning (continuous_eligibility_period_start_month, CO-094) where stated; otherwise the first month of the application being determined, from the month of application through the determination month, in which continuous eligibility applies to the child (ma_continuous_eligibility_applies, CO-555: the Children's category met, or a period opened in one of the programs Q.2-Q.3 name), which is the month of a transition from CHP+ to the MAGI Children's category where the child was CHP+ eligible before it; where no such month applies, the month of application, in which no period opens.

Precision. Coverage pass 6, C6-08 (2026-11-24). Q.2 (S1724): the period 'will begin on the first day of the month the application is received, or from the date all criteria are met. For a child transitioning from CHP+ to the MAGI Medical Assistance program specified in section 8.100.4.G.2, a new 12-month continuous eligibility period will begin on the first day of the month of the transition'. Before, the period opened only if the child met the category in the application month, so a child who was CHP+ eligible in the application month and in the Children's category from the next (the family's income fell) had no Medicaid period from the month of the transition. The months are tested in order; a month whose test is unknown before any month qualifies leaves the start unknown. A month after the determination month opens nothing in this determination. A period in a non-MAGI program (ma_continuous_eligibility_program: the Children with Disabilities Buy-In, Pickle, Disabled Adult Child or Limited Family Planning; ma_child_is_in_non_magi_continuous_eligibility_period, CO-2448, which reads the end month CO-556) keeps the application month when no start is recorded, as before: the scan is the MAGI Children's category's. Stated per person per month because the rule reads the months' facts (as ma_pregnancy_coverage_period_start_month, CO-565); the value is the same in every month evaluated.

Type month, scope person-month, program Medicaid.
Uses: `continuous_eligibility_period_start_month`, `ma_application_date`, `ma_continuous_eligibility_applies`, `ma_continuous_eligibility_program`.

```
if it is not the case that Continuous eligibility period start month is unknown
  then Continuous eligibility period start month
else if Medicaid: program a child's continuous eligibility period began in, otherwise magi is one of: cbwd_buy_in, pickle, dac, limited_family_planning
  then the month containing Medicaid: application date
else if in at least one of the months from the month containing Medicaid: application date through the month containing the Determination Date:
    Medicaid: continuous eligibility applies
  then the number of months in the months from the month containing Medicaid: application date through the month containing the Determination Date for which it is not the case that (in at least one of the months from the month containing Medicaid: application date through the month:;   Medicaid: continuous eligibility applies) months after the month containing Medicaid: application date
otherwise the month containing Medicaid: application date
```

### CO-7408 Medicaid: household income under the premium tax credit methodology for the previous calendar year, as a share of the poverty level `@engine`

This person's household income for the calendar year before the determination's, as the premium tax credit methodology computes it (26 CFR 1.36B-1(e)): the previous year's income (previous_year_annual_income) of each taxpayer in the person's premium tax credit family (ma_premium_tax_credit_family) and of each other member of the family who is required to file a return, with the sponsor income 8 U.S.C. 1631(a) deems to the person for the last month of that year counted for twelve months, as a fraction of the annual federal poverty guideline for the family's size in effect on the first day of the open enrollment period before that year (45 CFR 155.410(e): November 1 of the year before it). The figure § 8.100.4.C.5 tests for a month of the previous calendar year, as ma_premium_tax_credit_household_income_pct_fpl (CO-4561) is the figure for a month of the determination's year.

Precision. Coverage pass 6, C6-09 (2026-11-24). The family, the taxpayers and the filing requirement are the ones the case states for the determination (the case states one tax household); a retroactive month reaches back at most three months (§ 8.100.3.E.1), so only the previous calendar year is ever read. The guideline for 2025 is the 2024 figure (in force on November 1, 2024), added to federal_poverty_guideline_annual_table (CO-181) and its each-additional figure (CO-182) from 89 FR 2961 (S5061). Unknown where a counted member's previous-year income is not stated.

Type rate, scope person, program Medicaid.

### CO-7505 Medicaid: persons living with the person in the month, for the SSI method `@engine`

The persons of the case who live in the same household as this person in the month, for the SSI method's couple, deeming and allocations (10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.5.H.1.a "spouses living together", H.2.a "living in the same household with a parent", H.3.a.i "each ineligible child in the home"; 20 CFR 416.1163, 416.1165): those who live in this person's home (lives_with, CO-1925), and a spouse, parent, stepparent, child or stepchild who lives elsewhere on the determination date through the month the two ceased to live together (§ 8.100.7.C.2.b; § 8.100.7.A.1; 20 CFR 416.1165(g)(4), 416.1167(a)(1)); a person who died is a member through the month of death and not after (20 CFR 416.1163(f)(4), 416.1165(g)(3)). Two persons who have lived apart throughout the months evaluated (has_lived_apart_throughout_months_evaluated, CO-7860, true on either, or persons_lived_apart_from_throughout_months_evaluated, CO-7891, on either naming the other) are apart in every month.

Precision. Pattern sweep, non-MAGI Medicaid (docs/reviews/pattern-sweep-nonmagi.md, P1 and P3). The date the two ceased to live together is, where one of them lives in a facility (residence_setting_type other than private_dwelling), that one's institution_entry_date; otherwise, for spouses (or persons held out as spouses), ceased_living_with_spouse_date (CO-7352), and for a parent or child, ceased_living_with_parent_or_child_date (CO-7506), stated on either of the two. For spouses the order is the one ma_ssi_couple_members (CO-3626) used since coverage pass 6 F6-1. With the two apart and no date it cannot be determined (decision 4). Living together is read from lives_with as stated, required where read (decision 4; convention rule 17): no text on file says the persons of one application live together unless it says otherwise; 20 CFR 416.1163(a) and 416.1165 deem only from a spouse or parent who lives in the same household. A person who died states date_of_death (CO-2868, which is not stated for a living person). For a parent or a child, a stay in a medical institution the person returns from keeps the home's dwelling_id and the person a member (a temporary absence, 20 CFR 416.1167(a), S5120; duplicate-paths D-M4), and one who lives in the facility is a member through the month of entry and not after (§ 8.100.7.A.1, S3406). For a couple, ma_ssi_couple_members (CO-3626) applies the spouses' institution rules (ma_excluded_from_ssi_household, CO-661; ma_is_institutionalized_spouse_in_institution, CO-5200) beside this group. Coverage verification 7, V7-1 (docs/reviews/verify-coverage7-fixes.md): a pair who never lived together, or who parted before the first month evaluated, has no date they ceased to live together; has_lived_apart_throughout_months_evaluated (CO-7860), stated true on either, places them apart without one, as SNAP's household of the month reads it (snap_lives_with_in_month, CO-7672). Before, a child's parent listed in the case who had never lived with the child could not be placed in any month. Close-out verification F3 (KL-SNAP-5, docs/reviews/known-limits.md; 2026-11-24): a pair who never lived together, one of whom lived in an evaluated month with another person of the case who has since moved, could state neither CO-7860 nor a date; persons_lived_apart_from_throughout_months_evaluated (CO-7891) names the pair: the other person in this person's list, or this person in the other's (the group of this person alone is written as the persons joined to this person by spouse, crossing no edge), places them apart without a date, as SNAP's CO-7672 reads it.

### CO-7550 Medicaid: has held qualified non-citizen status for five years by the end of the month `@engine`

Whether, on some day of the month evaluated, the person has held qualified non-citizen status for the waiting period of 8 U.S.C. 1613(a) (qualified_non_citizen_waiting_period_years, five), counted from the date the person first obtained a qualified status or entered the United States in one (qualified_non_citizen_waiting_period_start_date, CO-7820: first_qualified_status_date, CO-7770; the date of the status held now, qualified_status_date, where the person entered the United States in it, us_entry_date on or after that date, or is a lawful permanent resident admitted directly or adjusted from a status that was not a qualified status, status_before_lpr_adjustment none or non_qualified_status, or another qualified non-citizen who held no earlier qualified status, has_held_earlier_qualified_status false): the period has ended by the last day of the month. Met also where the status held now (qualified_status_date, CO-003) has itself been held for the period, which no earlier status can shorten.

Precision. Coverage pass 7, C7-04 (2026-11-24): the five years were counted from qualified_status_date, the date of the status held now, so a parolee, battered non-citizen or conditional entrant who later became a lawful permanent resident restarted them at the adjustment, though 1613(a) (S176) runs them 'beginning on the date of the alien's entry into the United States with a status within the meaning of the term "qualified alien"' and 10 CCR 2506-1 4.305.B.3.a (S12) 'on the date the non-citizen obtains status as a qualified non-citizen or enters the U.S. in a qualifying status' (LPR-EX-PAROLEE: paroled 2019-05-01, LPR 2023-03-01: the five years ended 2024-04-30; November 2026 was emergency_only, is eligible). The first date is required where read (decision 4), except where the case already shows that the status held now is the first: the person entered the United States in it (us_entry_date not before qualified_status_date: no qualified status is held in the United States before entering it; an unstated entry date only leaves this shortcut unread), or a lawful permanent resident's earlier status (C7-09) is none or non_qualified_status (coverage verification 7, V7-8: a status in which the person was not a qualified alien, such as a student or work visa, so the permanent residence is the first qualified status; before, such a person stated first_qualified_status_date equal to qualified_status_date, or was cannot determine). Pattern sweep, MAGI (2026-11-24, docs/reviews/pattern-sweep-magi.md, PS-01). 8 U.S.C. 1613(a) (S176) bars a qualified alien from a federal means-tested benefit 'for a period of 5 years beginning on the date of the alien's entry into the United States with a status', so whether the bar applies is a fact of each month: a retroactive month before the fifth anniversary is inside it, a later month is not. 10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.4.G.1 (S3351) makes a person eligible for a whole month who is eligible 'at any time during' it, so the month in which the five years end is outside the bar (the last day of the month). has_held_qualified_status_five_years (CO-508), a neutral fact of the person on the determination date, is unchanged; Medicaid's month-scoped status test reads this item (ma_meets_citizenship_requirement_in_month, CO-7551). Close-out verification F1, the arm left (KL-SNAP-3, docs/reviews/known-limits.md; 2026-11-24): the start is read from qualified_non_citizen_waiting_period_start_date (CO-7820), the neutral date SNAP and the cash programs read, in place of the same choice of date written inside this item; it adds has_held_earlier_qualified_status (CO-7890): a qualified non-citizen who is not a lawful permanent resident and held no qualified status before the one held now (a battered non-citizen who entered in no status) counts from qualified_status_date without a first date (was cannot determine), and a first_qualified_status_date the case states is the start wherever the entry does not settle it.

  - Qualified non-citizen waiting period, years (5) is at most (the number of whole years between Start of the qualified non-citizen waiting period and -1 days after the first day of the month after the month)
