### CO-7551 Medicaid: meets the citizenship requirement in the month `@engine`

Whether, in the month evaluated, the person falls into one of the citizenship and immigration status categories of 10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.3.G.1.g that admit a person to full Medical Assistance, as ma_meets_citizenship_requirement (CO-509) states them, with each condition that changes with time read for the month: the five years of 8 U.S.C. 1613(a) (ma_has_held_qualified_status_five_years_in_month, CO-7550), the pregnancy of the lawfully residing pregnant woman (ma_is_pregnant_in_month, CO-3601) and the age of the lawfully residing child, under ma_magi_child_age_limit on the first day of the month (ma_age_on_first_day_of_month, CO-4978). In a month before the determination month that ends before a qualified non-citizen obtained the qualified status held now (qualified_status_date, CO-003), the status held then is tested instead (ma_meets_citizenship_requirement_before_qualified_status, CO-7652).

Precision. Pattern sweep, MAGI (2026-11-24, docs/reviews/pattern-sweep-magi.md, PS-01). 10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.4.G.1 (S3351) makes each month its own ('eligible ... at any time during a calendar month'), and § 8.100.3.E.1 (S217) gives a retroactive month only to a person who 'met all applicable eligibility requirements' in it; CO-509 is one value per person, measured on the determination date, so a lawful permanent resident whose five years ended between a retroactive month and the determination, a lawfully residing child who turned 19 after a retroactive month, and a lawfully residing woman pregnant in a retroactive month but not on the determination date were judged in that month by the determination date's facts. The five years end, the pregnancy and the age under 19 are each met on a day of the month (G.1; docs/operators.md, Ages in a month). The October 2026 federal payment limit (ma_alien_payment_restriction_applies, CO-3034) is read on the determination date, as CO-509 reads it (OQ-510, a recorded state policy choice: the determination date, not the month of service, decides it). Every other condition is CO-509's (the precision and statute_override of CO-509 apply). Read by every Medicaid item that tests status for a month: the MAGI items ma_magi_is_fully_eligible (CO-562), ma_is_emergency_medicaid_only (CO-510), ma_family_planning_status (CO-1154), ma_needy_young_person_category (CO-2419), ma_is_covered_under_cover_all_coloradans (CO-1175) and ma_meets_status_for_cover_all_coloradans_categories_in_month (CO-7553); and, since Medicaid status by month (2026-11-24, docs/reviews/medicaid-status-by-month.md, MS-2), the non-MAGI and shared items ma_is_ssi_related_eligible (CO-611), ma_msp_category (CO-617), ma_ltc_eligibility_status (CO-652), ma_pace_eligible (CO-654), ma_emergency_medicaid_status (CO-1151), ma_pickle_eligible (CO-1159), ma_dac_eligible (CO-1161), ma_disabled_widow_eligible (CO-1162), ma_protected_group_category (CO-1163), ma_oap_sisc_b_eligible (CO-1177), ma_funding_source (CO-2456) and ma_ltc_unmet_requirement (CO-3310): the categories of 8.100.3.G.1.g are one test for every Medical Assistance category, and § 8.100.5.C.1 (S3900) makes the Aged, Blind and Disabled categories effective from the first day of the month the person becomes eligible, so the same day-of-the-month reading applies. MS-2: qualified_status_date is the date of a change the case states, so in a month before the determination month that ends before it the stated qualified status was not held, and CO-7652 tests the status held then; qualified_status_date is required for a qualified non-citizen in a month before the determination month (decision 4 of 2026-11-23). CO-509 itself is unchanged and read only by person-scope items (ma_meets_status_for_cover_all_coloradans_categories, CO-1174; the spouse's status in ma_transfer_penalty_is_apportioned_with_spouse, CO-2232, a test at the determination).

Whether, in the month evaluated, the person is in the population 10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.3.G.1.g.ix.1 (Cover All Coloradans) protects from exclusion on the basis of immigration status: under 19 or with the 19th birthday in the month (ma_is_under_child_age_or_turns_nineteen_this_month, CO-564), pregnant in the month (ma_is_pregnant_in_month, CO-3601), or in the month the most recent pregnancy ended or one of the 12 months after it (most_recent_pregnancy_end_date, CO-7400; ma_postpartum_coverage_end_month, CO-560).

Precision. Pattern sweep, MAGI (2026-11-24, docs/reviews/pattern-sweep-magi.md, PS-02). ix.1 (S607) and CHP+'s § 110.1.B.5.o (S606) name 'Persons who are under the age of 19, whose 19th birthday occurred in the current month, who are pregnant, or who are within 12 months of the beginning of their postpartum period': 'the current month' is the month evaluated (§ 8.100.4.G.1, S3351; § 8.100.3.E.1, S217, a retroactive month's own requirements). ma_is_cover_all_coloradans_person (CO-1173) measures each condition on the determination date, so a youth who turned 19 after a retroactive month was outside the population in that month, and a woman pregnant in a retroactive month whose pregnancy had ended more than 12 months later was too. CO-1173 is unchanged for its person-scope readers (the presumptive determinations, read on the determination date). Since Medicaid status by month (2026-11-24, docs/reviews/medicaid-status-by-month.md, MS-3) the month-scoped non-MAGI and emergency readers read this item too: ma_emergency_medicaid_status (CO-1151) and ma_ltc_unmet_requirement (CO-3310).

### CO-7554 Medicaid: the persons living with the person in the month `@engine`

The persons who live in the home with the person in the month evaluated, for the MAGI household and caretaker rules: the persons of lives_with (CO-1925, from dwelling_id) other than a person who died before the first day of the month (date_of_death, CO-2868, read through is_deceased, CO-2200, for the month before).

Precision. Pattern sweep, MAGI (2026-11-24, docs/reviews/pattern-sweep-magi.md, PS-04). 10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.4.E.1.a.ii ('The Tax-Filer's spouse if living in the home'), E.1.b.ii and iv, E.1.d ('who live in the household'), E.3 ('Married couples living together', S170) and 42 CFR 435.603(f)(3)-(4) (S163) make membership turn on living in the home in the month (8.100.4.G.1, S3351; a retroactive month on its own facts, 8.100.3.E.1, S217); lives_with is one value per case, from the home the case states, so a spouse or parent who died in a month before the month evaluated was still counted as living in the home. A person who died during the month lived in the home on a day of it and is kept for that month (G.1's any day); a person who died before the month lives with no one in it (the group is empty), so the spouse of a claimer who has died is not 'their spouse if living in the home' (E.1.b.ii). date_of_death is not stated for a living person (its declaration, CO-2868), so a person with none stated is living. This item changes only the living-in-the-home condition: a person the tax filer expects to claim as a dependent (E.1.a.iii, 435.603(f)(1), 'for the taxable year') is a member by that claim, which the item does not read. Unknown where lives_with is (dwelling_id not stated: required where read, C6-10).

### CO-7650 Medicaid: meets the residency requirement in the month `@engine`

Whether the person is a resident of Colorado for Medical Assistance in the month evaluated: a resident on the determination date (ma_meets_residency, CO-2250) who was living in Colorado on some day of the month. In the application month and after, the residence the person states for the application holds (10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.3.B.1-2: the person applies in the county where the person lives and is a resident who is living in Colorado 'at the time of application'); in a month before the application month, the person lived in Colorado from the month of state_of_residence_start_date (CO-7651), or, for a person incapable of indicating intent whose residence the institutional rules give, was in the medical institution in the month (ma_resides_in_medical_institution_in_month, CO-7500).

Precision. Medicaid status by month (2026-11-24, docs/reviews/medicaid-status-by-month.md, MS-1). § 8.100.3.E.1 (S1503) gives a retroactive month only to a person who 'met all applicable eligibility requirements' in it, and 42 CFR 435.915(a)(2) (S218) only where the person 'would have been eligible for Medicaid at the time he received the services if he had applied': a person living in another state in a retroactive month was not a resident of Colorado in it (§ 8.100.3.B.2, S1518, 'living within the state of Colorado'). ma_meets_residency (CO-2250) is one value per person, the determination date's, and every month-scoped Medicaid item read it, so a retroactive month before a move to Colorado was a month of residence. A month counts if the person lived in Colorado on any day of it (§ 8.100.4.G.1, S3351, for MAGI; § 8.100.5.C.1, S3900, from 'the first day of the month the person becomes eligible' for the Aged, Blind and Disabled categories), so the month of the move is a month of residence. The application month needs no date: the person applied where the person lived (B.1-2). state_of_residence_start_date is required for a month before the application month (decision 4 of 2026-11-23); ma_application_date is read only for a month before the determination month. B.2 measures the intent to remain 'at the time of application', and 435.915(a)(2) each retroactive month 'at the time': OQ-1445 records the reading (each retroactive month needs living in Colorado in it). The incapable-of-intent arm reads ma_is_incapable_of_indicating_intent with its declared default (not stated: no finding of incapacity), as CO-2250 does. A person who moved away from Colorado and back between a retroactive month and the determination is not stated by any fact (OQ-1425). is_colorado_resident (CO-505), shared with SNAP, CHP+, Colorado Works, Adult Financial, CCCAP and LEAP, is unchanged.

For a qualified non-citizen, in a month that ends before the person obtained the qualified status held now (qualified_status_date, CO-003), whether the person meets a status category of 10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.3.G.1.g in that month: not in a month before the month the person entered the United States (us_entry_date, CO-1726); for a lawful permanent resident who held a qualified status before adjusting (status_before_lpr_adjustment, CO-2700: refugee, asylee, deportation withheld, Cuban or Haitian entrant, or Iraqi or Afghan special immigrant), that earlier status, exempt from the five-year rule (iv.9-10, v; ma_is_five_year_bar_exempt CO-1172), within 42 U.S.C. 1396b(v)(5)(B) only as a Cuban or Haitian entrant; or a lawfully residing non-citizen (ma_is_lawfully_present, CO-507) who entered before August 22, 1996 (ii) or who is pregnant in the month or a child under ma_magi_child_age_limit on its first day (vii).

Precision. Medicaid status by month (2026-11-24, docs/reviews/medicaid-status-by-month.md, MS-2). qualified_status_date is the date of a change the case states (OQ-1425's assumption reads the determination date's status in a retroactive month only where no such date is stated): in a month that ends before it, the person did not hold the qualified status the case states, so its arms (the five years, the exemptions that status opens, its 1396b(v)(5)(B) category) are not read for the month, and the month needs the status held then. The earlier status is stated for a lawful permanent resident (CO-2700), required where read (coverage pass 7, C7-09, 2026-11-24; decision 4 of 2026-11-23: before, read as none, admitted directly in no special class); for another qualified status the case states none, so only the arms that do not depend on it are read: a month before entry into the United States meets no category of G.1.g (each is a status held in the United States); lawful presence (ma_is_lawfully_present), which every qualified status includes and which the case does not date, is read as stated (OQ-1425), so the lawfully residing pregnant woman or child (vii, S1705) and the ii arm keep it. The October 2026 federal payment limit is read on the determination date, as CO-509 and CO-7551 read it (OQ-510). The month counts if the condition holds on any day of it (§ 8.100.4.G.1, S3351; § 8.100.5.C.1, S3900). Read only by ma_meets_citizenship_requirement_in_month (CO-7551) for such a month.

### CO-7720 Medicaid long-term care: receipts a federal statute excludes from income for every federally assisted program `@engine`

The part of the person's gross unearned receipts of the month (ma_ssi_gross_unearned_receipts, CO-5514, counted the same way) that a federal statute bars from being counted as income in any federal or federally assisted program, so that it is not income for the long-term care gross income of 10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.7.A.1 either: home energy assistance under the Low-Income Home Energy Assistance Act (energy_assistance_federal; 42 U.S.C. 8624(f)(1), 'shall not be considered income or resources ... for any purpose under any Federal or State law'), payments to Domestic Volunteer Service Act volunteers below the minimum wage (dvsa_title_i_volunteer_payment; 42 U.S.C. 5044(f)(1), 'shall not in any way reduce or eliminate the level of or eligibility for assistance or services ... under any governmental program'), and the payments the receipt kind federally_excluded_payment names (a payment a federal statute excludes from income for federally funded means-tested programs: the Indian judgment and tribal trust funds, Alaska Native Claims Settlement Act distributions, Civil Liberties Act restitution, Agent Orange settlement, Radiation Exposure Compensation and Nazi persecution payments of § 8.100.5.F.6.h, i, r, s, v and x, among others; 20 CFR 416.1124(b)), and student financial assistance under Title IV of the Higher Education Act or a Bureau of Indian Education program and payments from the employment and training activities for adults and dislocated workers of 29 U.S.C. 3174 (title_iv_or_bie_student_aid, wioa_adult_or_dislocated_worker_payment; 20 U.S.C. 1087uu, 'shall not be taken into account in determining the need or eligibility of any person for benefits or assistance, or the amount of such benefits or assistance, under any Federal, State, or local program financed in whole or in part with Federal funds').

Precision. Each row's receipts are summed by the placement CO-5514 uses (a payment by its month or date, a stream from the month of its start_date through the month of its end_date) at the amount CO-5514 counts (less covered costs, claim expenses, a dependent's part and a retroactive payment's legal fees), so ma_ltc_gross_income (CO-641) subtracts exactly what CO-5514 added for these kinds. A Domestic Volunteer Service Act payment at or above the minimum wage is its own kind (dvsa_title_i_payment_at_or_above_minimum_wage) and is not here: 5044(f)(1) 'shall not apply' to it. Coverage pass 7, non-MAGI F7-6 (docs/reviews/coverage7-medicaid-nonmagi.md): OQ-822 records the conflict between § 8.100.5.F.6's exemptions 'for ... Long Term Care' and § 8.100.7.A.1's 'income before application of deductions, exemptions or disregards', a choice Colorado's own texts leave open; these statutes leave no choice, since each governs 'notwithstanding any other provision of law'. Not here, with the reason: AmeriCorps (42 U.S.C. 12637(d), S5244, excepts programs 'as provided under the Social Security Act', which Medicaid is); educational_assistance and workforce_program_payment, which hold the grants, scholarships, loans and workforce payments 20 U.S.C. 1087uu does not reach (other grants and scholarships, WIOA youth activities, the youth projects), F.6.aa's and F.6.o-p's exemptions of them being Colorado's (OQ-822); the other F.6 exemptions are Colorado's too (OQ-822). NM-KL-3 (2026-11-24, docs/reviews/known-limits.md): 20 U.S.C. 1087uu (S5243) is read from the two receipt kinds that state what it names (CO-5000): Title IV of the Higher Education Act is 'this subchapter', Student Assistance (S5364), and since the 1992 amendment the section reaches the assistance itself, not only its attendance costs (S5364; the attendance-cost wording of 20 CFR 416.1236(a)(14), D-54, cites the 1987 enactment, section 14(27) of Public Law 100-50); the 29 U.S.C. 3174 programs (S5363) were added by Pub. L. 116-260, 'effective July 1, 2024' (S5364), before every month this volume evaluates. Before, a Pell grant or a WIOA training payment, stated as educational_assistance or workforce_program_payment, was counted in the 300% test (STUDENTAID-LTC, stored household CO-1200: 3,100 > 2,982, ineligible_income, where the text gives 2,900, eligible_institutional). Federal Work-Study pay and WIOA on-the-job training wages are earnings (CO-5100), counted in the gross earned income: NM-KL-7.

### CO-7723 Medicaid: an SSI infant is eligible from the date of birth `@engine`

Whether the special provision for infants of 10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.6.C.10.a.i makes the person's SSI Medicaid effective from the date of birth: the person receives SSI (receives_ssi, CO-012), the date of birth is within three months of the date the person became eligible for SSI (ssi_eligibility_date, CO-7350: on or before the same day of the third month after the birth), the person was born in a hospital (born_in_hospital, CO-7721), and the disability onset date SSA reports (disability_onset_date, CO-4887) fell in the hospital stay that began at birth: on or after the date of birth, and on or before the discharge (birth_hospital_discharge_date, CO-7722), or the infant is still in that stay (residence_setting_type hospital, entered on the date of birth).

Precision. C.10.a.i's three conditions, in the order they are read: (3) first, so a person whose birth is not within three months of the SSI eligibility date (every older person) is not asked the place of birth or the stay. 'Within three (3) months of the date on which the infant became eligible for SSI' is read as the eligibility date falling no later than the same day of the third calendar month after the birth month (a birth on the 31st reaches the last day of a shorter third month): the eligibility month before the third month after the birth month, or that month on a day not later than the birth's day of the month. 'Occurred during the infant's hospital stay' is the stay that began at birth, from the date of birth through the discharge date, both days included. ### CO-7774 Medicaid: first month a pregnancy coverage period reaching the month can begin `@engine`

The first month in which a pregnancy coverage period that can still reach the month evaluated (10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.4.G.5; 42 U.S.C. 1396a(e)(5), (e)(16)) can begin: the first month of the application being determined - the first month of the requested retroactive period (ma_retroactive_coverage_requested, CO-4100; § 8.100.3.E.1-2), or else the month containing ma_application_date - or, where later, the month after the latest pregnancy end the case records whose postpartum period (ma_postpartum_coverage_months after the month it ended) ended before the month evaluated: a period that begins in or before that end's month is the period of that pregnancy or an earlier one, and ends before the month evaluated.

Precision. Coverage pass 7, C7-02 (2026-11-24). A period runs from its first month through the 12th month after the end of the pregnancy current in that month (G.5, S640: 'through the last day of the 12th month following the date the pregnancy ends'; (e)(16)(A), S224). An end e reaches the month m when m is no later than ma_postpartum_coverage_months after the month of e, that is when the month of e is not before m less ma_postpartum_coverage_months; the latest end that does not reach m is latest_pregnancy_end_date_before_month (CO-7772) read for that month (at), and whether there is one is pregnancy_ended_before_month (CO-7771). A month from the one after it opens a period of a later pregnancy only. The retroactive period's length is read as ma_pregnancy_coverage_period_start_month (CO-565) reads it: three months before 2027, then two (a person whose period opens in a retroactive month is in the Pregnant Women category in the application month, never an expansion adult; CO-2472 would make the rule circular).

### CO-7775 Medicaid: a pregnancy coverage period begins in the month `@engine`

Whether a pregnancy coverage period (10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.4.G.5; 42 U.S.C. 1396a(e)(5), (e)(16)) can run from the month: the period opens in it (ma_pregnancy_coverage_period_opens_in_month, CO-7401), and the pregnancy whose period it is has a recorded end on or after the month (pregnancy_ended_on_or_after_month, CO-7773), so the period ends with the 12th month after the earliest such end, or continues (the person is pregnant now, is_pregnant). Unknown where it opens, no end is recorded on or after the month and the person is not pregnant now (the end of that pregnancy is the missing fact).

Precision. Coverage pass 7, C7-02 (2026-11-24). G.5 (S640) provides coverage 'for a period beginning with the date of application for Medical Assistance through the last day of the 12th month following the date the pregnancy ends': each period belongs to the pregnancy current in its first month and ends with that pregnancy's postpartum year, and a later pregnancy opens its own period only in a month of that pregnancy (CO-7401). The months a period beginning here reaches are those up to the 12th month after the first recorded end on or after it; ma_is_in_pregnancy_coverage_period (CO-566) reads this item only from ma_pregnancy_coverage_period_search_start_month (CO-7774), the month after the last end whose postpartum year ended before the month evaluated, so every end on or after a month it reads reaches that month.

Type yes/no, scope person-month, program Medicaid.
Uses: `is_pregnant`, `ma_pregnancy_coverage_period_opens_in_month`, `pregnancy_ended_on_or_after_month`.

```
  - Medicaid: the pregnancy coverage period opens in the month
  - if A pregnancy ended on or after the month began, as the case records it
    then yes
  else if Is pregnant
    then yes
```

### CO-7940 Medicaid: the Social Security the disabled widow(er) test disregards `@engine`

The person's current Social Security of the month that the disabled widow(er) group's SSI test disregards (10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.6.I, S625; 42 U.S.C. 1383c(d)(2) (S3416) deems the group SSI recipients 'for so long as such person (i) would be eligible for such supplemental security income benefits ... in the absence of benefits described in paragraph (1)(A)', and (1)(A) describes benefits 'under subsection (e) or (f) of section 402 of this title (or under any other subsection of section 402 of this title if such person is also eligible for benefits under such subsection (e) or (f))'): each receipt of kind social_security other than a retroactive payment, counted as the SSI method counts the current benefit (ma_ssi_counted_social_security_receipts, CO-6250: its amount less a plan-for-self-support set-aside, placed by its month, date or stream dates), whose title_ii_benefit_type (a field of the receipt, CO-5000) is a benefit under 42 U.S.C. 402: retirement_or_survivor, disabled_adult_child or disabled_widow (S5361). A disability insurance benefit on the person's own record (own_disability) is a benefit under 42 U.S.C. 423 (S5362), not one (1)(A) describes, and stays counted.

Precision. NM-KL-2 (2026-11-24; docs/reviews/known-limits.md; coverage pass 7, non-MAGI F7-10): the group read ma_dac_countable_income (CO-1160), which disregards every current Social Security receipt, the Disabled Adult Child test's reading of § 8.100.6.J.1.c.i ('the current OASDI income', S626). A widow(er) in the group is eligible for widow(er)'s benefits under 402(e) or (f), so (1)(A)'s parenthetical reaches every benefit she receives under another subsection of 402 too; it does not reach section 423. The field is read only for a Social Security receipt and only here, after the group's other conditions (ma_disabled_widow_eligible, CO-1162, then ma_disabled_widow_meets_ssi_income_test, CO-7943, only when the SSI income test is not met without it), so it is required where read (decision 4 of 2026-11-23) and asked of no other person.

```
the sum for each receipt in Receipts where

      - it is not the case that that receipt's retroactive
```

### CO-7943 Medicaid: the disabled widow(er) meets the SSI income test in the absence of the widow(er)'s benefits `@engine`

Whether the person meets the SSI income test as the disabled widow(er) group applies it (10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.6.I.1.f, S625; § 8.100.6.A.1, S3411; 42 U.S.C. 1383c(d)(2) (S3416) deems the group SSI recipients 'for so long as such person (i) would be eligible for such supplemental security income benefits ... in the absence of benefits described in paragraph (1)(A)', and (1)(A) describes benefits 'under subsection (e) or (f) of section 402 of this title (or under any other subsection of section 402 of this title if such person is also eligible for benefits under such subsection (e) or (f))'): the SSI income test is met (ma_ssi_income_test_status, CO-5516), or the person's countable income with the Social Security benefits under 42 U.S.C. 402 left out (ma_disabled_widow_countable_income, CO-7941; or, where an ineligible spouse's income is not deemed, the own-income form, CO-7942) is at a rate of not more than the SSI Federal Benefit Rate for the person (ma_ssi_income_standard; 42 U.S.C. 1382(a), S3950).

Precision. NM-KL-2 (2026-11-24; docs/reviews/known-limits.md; coverage pass 7, non-MAGI F7-10). Before, the second arm was ma_ssi_income_test_status's met_with_oasdi_disregarded, which compared the Disabled Adult Child figure (CO-1160), the whole current Social Security taken out; CO-5516 now states the SSI income test alone, so ma_meets_ssi_income_standard (CO-609) never waits on a field only this group reads. 'At a rate of not more than' (S3950), as CO-5516 reads it, so income equal to the rate meets the test. The figures with the benefits taken out are read only when the test is not met without them, so the receipt's benefit type (CO-5000) is asked only of a person in the group whose income is over the rate with them.

The couple's total countable resources as assessed at the time of the initial Medical Assistance application (10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.7.L, S3419: "All non-exempt resources owned by a married couple are counted, whether owned jointly or individually"; M.1: "based on the total resources owned by the couple as of the time of Medical Assistance application"), the figure the CSRA is computed from and "established at intake only": in the month of the person's application (ma_application_date), the person's and the spouse's countable resources (ma_ssi_countable_resources_in_month, CO-5322), each with the real property left out only while efforts to sell it are made added back (ma_real_property_for_sale_excluded_in_month, CO-5323; 8.100.5.M.2.b.vi, S4666), and the couple's one automobile (the smaller spouse's excluded automobile added back, 20 CFR 416.1218(b), S4660).

Precision. Resource records, Medicaid track H1 (decision D8): derived from the holdings the couple states valued in the application month (a holding with no month has the same value in every month the case covers, CO-5300); unknown when the application date is not stated or a holding read in that month cannot be valued (decision 4: never a silent zero). Coverage review NM-18: the meaning had dated the assessment at the start of the first continuous period of institutionalization, the date of 42 U.S.C. 1396r-5(c)(1)(A); Colorado's CSRA is the couple's resources up to the maximum (OQ-126), which 1396r-5(c)(2) attributes at the time of application, so the application date governs here. The spouse is the legal spouse wherever each lives, as in ma_institutionalized_spouse_countable_resources (CO-647). Whether each spouse's home is countable is judged on the determination date's facts (CO-4622), its equity in the application month. A joint holding is stated on each spouse's list with each one's share, so the couple's figure counts it once (L: "whether owned jointly or individually"). Coverage pass 4, non-MAGI N4-6: the couple excludes one automobile, a car the two own together counted once at its whole equity: the two spouses' own excluded automobiles (ma_ssi_excluded_automobile_equity_in_month, CO-5321) are added back less the couple's one, the larger of the two spouses' ma_ssi_couple_automobile_equity_in_month (CO-6733, a joint car at its whole equity), at least 0. For two different cars this is the smaller car, as before; for one joint car, nothing (it had added back the other spouse's half of the same car).

Type money, scope person, program Medicaid.
Uses: `ma_application_date`, `ma_real_property_for_sale_excluded_in_month`, `ma_ssi_countable_resources_in_month`, `ma_ssi_couple_automobile_equity_in_month`, `ma_ssi_excluded_automobile_equity_in_month`, `relationships`.

### CO-889 Medicaid: spouse or qualifying child lives in the home `@engine`

Whether this person's spouse, or a child of this person who is under 21 or blind or disabled of any age, is lawfully residing in this person's home (42 U.S.C. 1396p(f)(2)): read as a spouse or such a child who does not reside in a medical institution and, where this person's lives_with is stated, is in it.

Precision. A person who lives in a facility (residence_setting_type other than private_dwelling) does not share a dwelling with the community home, so lives_with cannot show the relative is in it; the relative's own residence then decides: a relative who lives in a private dwelling is read as living in the person's home. Coverage review NM-5: since lives_with is derived from dwelling_id, a spouse at home had stopped counting for a person in a nursing facility; ma_home_is_countable_resource (CO-4622) reads this item for § 8.100.5.M.2.a.ix. Disability is the SSA finding (meets_ssa_disability_criteria). (Until the pattern sweep: if the person had no stated relationships, Medicaid read no such relative.) Pattern sweep, non-MAGI Medicaid (docs/reviews/pattern-sweep-nonmagi.md, P1, P2, P3): per month. The relative is in the person's home in the month: not in a medical institution in the month (ma_resides_in_medical_institution_in_month, CO-7500: a relative admitted in September was at home in a retroactive August), a child under 21 by the age on the first day of the month ('under' is met on any day of it; docs/operators.md, Ages in a month) and born by the month. ma_home_equity_disqualifies (CO-650) reads it in the determination month. Required where read (decision 4 of 2026-11-23; convention rule 17): the person's relationships, the homes (lives_with) and the settings are read as stated; before, unstated relationships were read as no relative, an unstated home as living together, an unstated setting as not in an institution, and the age was the determination date's. Living in the home in the month is read from ma_ssi_lives_with_in_month (CO-7505): a spouse, parent or child who lives elsewhere on the determination date is in the home through the month the two ceased to live together (for one who entered a facility, the month of entry).

Type yes/no, scope person-month, program Medicaid.
Uses: `date_of_birth`, `is_blind`, `ma_age_on_first_day_of_month`, `ma_home_equity_child_age_limit`, `ma_resides_in_medical_institution_in_month`, `ma_ssi_lives_with_in_month`, `meets_ssa_disability_criteria`, `relationships`, `residence_setting_type`.

### CO-1418 CHP+: verification status `@engine`

Where this person's CHP+ verification stands, in the same states as Medical Assistance: not applicable (coverage is not requested, or the person is neither a child under nineteen nor pregnant, the only people CHP+ covers); none required; complete; pending; past due; pending within a reasonable opportunity period for status; or reasonable opportunity expired.

Precision. Coverage pass 5, C5-03 (2026-11-23): a pregnant applicant is one pregnant in the month evaluated (chp_is_pregnant_in_month, CO-7051), as CHP+ eligibility reads her (CO-706, CO-707), not on the determination date.

Type one of, scope person-month, program CHP+.
Uses: `chp_is_pregnant_in_month`, `chp_is_requesting_coverage`, `chp_pending_verification_count`, `chp_required_verification_count`, `chp_verification_due_date`, `ma_is_under_child_age_or_turns_nineteen_this_month`, `ma_pending_status_verification_count`, `ma_reasonable_opportunity_period_end_date`.

```
if it is not the case that (all of the following are true:;   - CHP+ is requested for the person;   - any of the following is true:;     - Medicaid: under the child age limit, or turns 19 this month;     - CHP+: is pregnant in the month)
  then not_applicable
else if CHP+: required verification count is equal to 0
  then not_required
else if CHP+: pending verification count is equal to 0
  then complete
else if all of the following are true:
    - (CHP+: pending verification count minus Medicaid: pending status verification count) is more than 0
    - the Determination Date is more than CHP+: verification due date
  then past_due
else if all of the following are true:
    - Medicaid: pending status verification count is more than 0
    - the Determination Date is more than Medicaid: reasonable opportunity period end date
  then reasonable_opportunity_expired
else if (CHP+: pending verification count minus Medicaid: pending status verification count) is more than 0
  then pending
otherwise pending_reasonable_opportunity
```

### CO-1641 CHP+: income is reasonably compatible `@engine`

Whether the attested household income is reasonably compatible with the electronic data source's for CHP+, judged against the CHP+ upper income limit plus the ma_magi_income_disregard_pct disregard (10 CCR 2505-3 § 150.2; the income up to which CHP+ grants eligibility, CO-704): both at or below it; the attested figure above it, whatever the data figure (both above, § 8.100.4.C.2.a.iii; or the data below, which Colorado's Medicaid and CHIP verification plan takes as attested, the person ineligible, with no further information requested); or the attested figure at or below it and the data no more than ma_reasonable_compatibility_threshold_pct above the attested figure.

Precision. Coverage review 2, N-04 and N-08: the limit is compared with the disregard added, as CO-1402 compares the Medicaid standard, so an attestation within the disregard band (260% to 265%), on which CO-704 grants eligibility, is checked against the data rather than counted as above the limit. The attested-above, data-below combination is compatible, as F-12 made it for Medicaid: the verification plan (D-317, S3364) covers Medicaid and CHIP alike, and 10 CCR 2505-3 § 130.1 applies § 8.100.4.B's verification to CHP+.

### CO-2228 CHP+: copayment income band `@engine`

Which § 320.1 copayment schedule applies to a CHP+ enrollee's family, by family income as a share of the federal poverty level at the time of the eligibility determination (10 CCR 2505-3 § 320.1): band_a, less than chp_copayment_waiver_limit_pct (all copayments waived except emergency and urgent care, A); band_b, from chp_copayment_waiver_limit_pct to chp_copayment_band_b_max_pct (B); band_c, above chp_copayment_band_b_max_pct to chp_copayment_band_c_max_pct (C); band_d, above chp_copayment_band_c_max_pct (D, which the rule states to 260%, the CHP+ upper limit).

Precision. Income is the MAGI household income ratio on which the enrollee's CHP+ eligibility is determined, in the month of the determination (§ 320.1: "income, at the time of eligibility determination"): the month's figure (ma_magi_monthly_household_income_pct_fpl, CO-6452) where it is within the CHP+ upper limit, and otherwise the budget figure (ma_magi_household_income_pct_fpl, CO-504), the annualized income of 10 CCR 2505-10 8.100.4.C.4.a, which applies only to "Applicants who are found financially ineligible based on current or previous monthly household income" (S3356), or C.5's. Coverage pass 4 (2026-11-23; CO-387, coverage pass 3 C3-08): before, the band read the lower of the two figures, so a seasonal self-employed parent's child eligible for CHP+ on the month's 240.0% had the band of the annualized 160.0% (band_c); the band of the figure eligibility was determined on is band_d. OQ-810 no longer covers the band. § 320.1 states whole percentages ('between 101% and 150%', 'between 151% and 200%'), leaving ratios between chp_copayment_band_b_max_pct and 151%, and between chp_copayment_band_c_max_pct and 201%, in no band; they are read into the next band up (OQ-470).

### CO-2404 CHP+: child is in a continuous eligibility period `@engine`

Whether this month falls inside a CHP+ child's 12-month continuous eligibility period under 10 CCR 2505-3 § 430.2: the child was found eligible for CHP+ in the period's first month, is still under 19, is still a Colorado resident (B.iv), the month is no more than 11 months after the first month, and no other exception of § 430.2.B ends the period - deceased, moved out of the household permanently, cannot be located, asked to be withdrawn, failed to provide documentation in a reasonable opportunity period, or eligibility erroneously granted (ma_continuous_eligibility_exception_applies, CO-2205, the same list § 8.100.3.Q.1.b states, whose reasonable opportunity exception § 430.2.B.vii cites). Income changes do not end it (§ 430.2.A).

Precision. A span CBMS has recorded (chp_eligibility_period_start_month stated, CO-2402) stands as recorded: § 430.2 opens the period "Upon being enrolled", and the enrollment presupposes the finding, so the first month's eligibility is not re-derived from income facts that may not be stated for that month (heavier-definitions audit H-5). With no span recorded, the period is the one the application being determined would open: the child must be CHP+ eligible (chp_child_is_eligible) in the month of ma_application_date, which is then the first month. A child who becomes an inmate of a public institution stays in the period on a limited incarceration benefit (§ 430.2.B.ii), which chp_eligibility_status (CO-707) reports; the period continues on release. Coverage pass 7, C7-05 (2026-11-24): with neither the start month nor the application date stated, whether a period is open cannot be determined (the period opens in a month of the application, which is not known; decision 4 of 2026-11-23); before, the child was read as in no period, so a child in a period whose original application date a renewal left out (CO-088) was read by income alone. Coverage pass 6, C6-05(a) (2026-11-24): residency is read through chp_meets_residency (CO-7402), so an unstated residence is cannot determine, not a non-resident. Coverage pass 6, C6-08 (2026-11-24): with no span recorded, the period opens in the first month of the application, through the determination month, in which the child is CHP+ eligible (chp_child_continuous_eligibility_start_month, CO-7406; § 430.2, 'from the authorization date'; § 430.1.B), not only in the application month.

Type yes/no, scope person-month, program CHP+.
Uses: `chp_child_continuous_eligibility_start_month`, `chp_child_is_eligible`, `chp_continuous_eligibility_months`, `chp_eligibility_period_start_month`, `chp_meets_residency`, `ma_continuous_eligibility_exception_applies`, `ma_is_under_child_age_or_turns_nineteen_this_month`.

```
  - any of the following is true:
    - it is not the case that CHP+: first month of the current eligibility period is unknown
    - CHP+: child is eligible for CHP+: first month of a child's continuous eligibility period
  - Medicaid: under the child age limit, or turns 19 this month
  - CHP+: meets the residency requirement
  - the month is at least CHP+: first month of a child's continuous eligibility period
  - the month is at most CHP+: continuous eligibility period, months (12) minus 1 months after CHP+: first month of a child's continuous eligibility period
  - it is not the case that Medicaid: a continuous eligibility exception applies
```

### CO-2407 CHP+: is in the prenatal coverage period `@engine`

Whether this month falls in a pregnant woman's CHP+ enrollment span under 10 CCR 2505-3 § 430.3, which ends 'on the last day of the month 12 months after the birth of the child or termination of the pregnancy' for which she enrolled: a span recorded by an earlier determination (chp_eligibility_period_start_month) that began on or before this month, in a month she was prenatal-eligible or on or before the month her pregnancy ended, for a pregnancy whose recorded end reaches this month (no pregnancy ended after the span began and more than chp_postpartum_coverage_months before this month) or that continues; or, where none is recorded, a span that begins (chp_prenatal_span_begins_in_month, CO-7777: prenatal-eligible, for a pregnancy with a recorded end on or after the month or that continues) in a month from chp_prenatal_span_search_start_month (CO-7776: the application month, or after the last pregnancy whose span ended before this month) through the determination month and no later than this month. Coverage continues "regardless of changes in the woman's financial circumstances". With no application date and no recorded span: false for a person the case records as never pregnant or whose last pregnancy's span ended before the month (not pregnant now), otherwise unknown.

Precision. Coverage pass 7 (2026-11-24): C7-02, the span ran while she was pregnant on the determination date, so a span opened for a first pregnancy continued through a second (PG-SECOND-CHP: span recorded from 2025-03, birth 2025-09-10, pregnant again from 2026-10-05, $7,000: October 2026 eligible_prenatal; by hand the span ended with September 2026 (2025-09 + 12), and October is size 3, 7,000 / 2,276.67 = 307.5%, ineligible_income). Each span now ends with its own pregnancy's month 12 months after the end, and a later pregnancy begins its own span (CO-7776, CO-7777). C7-05: with no application date and no span recorded the span was read as closed (false); now it cannot be determined, unless the case records no pregnancy at all or her last pregnancy's span ended before the month and she is not pregnant now (decision 4 of 2026-11-23). The reasonable-compatibility exception of § 430.3.A.i is not tested: it is a verification failure the volume's verification items report (chp_verification_status). Prenatal eligibility in the span's first month reads that month's pregnancy (chp_is_pregnant_in_month, CO-7051, through chp_prenatal_is_eligible): a woman who applied while pregnant and delivered before the determination opens the span on the application month's eligibility (coverage pass 5, C5-03; before, chp_prenatal_is_eligible read is_pregnant, the pregnancy on the determination date, and the span never opened for her). A CHP+ span recorded (chp_eligibility_period_start_month) as beginning on or before the month the pregnancy ended is also read as the prenatal span § 430.3 continues, for a span an earlier determination opened. Coverage pass 6 (2026-11-24): C6-02, § 430.3 makes the enrollment 'effective as of the first of the month of the date of application or the first day of the month the pregnant woman becomes eligible': where no span is recorded, the span opens in the first month from the application month through the determination month in which she is prenatal-eligible (CHP-LATER-ELIG: applied 2026-09-28, September 5,000 / 1,803.33 = 277.3% > 260%, October 4,200 / 1,803.33 = 232.9%: the span from October through October 2027; before, only September was tested and nothing opened); a month after the determination month opens nothing in this determination. C6-03: the end of the pregnancy is read from most_recent_pregnancy_end_date (CO-7400); a person not pregnant now who states a pregnancy_start_date with no end and no birth recorded cannot be determined after the span's first month.

Coverage pass 4, C4-07 (2026-11-23; time contract month-v1): the age is measured in the month evaluated (its first day), not on the determination date, so a newborn reported or determined late is guaranteed in the earlier months of its first year ("A newborn can be reported at any time by any person", § 430.5.A), and a newborn determined in its first year is not guaranteed in the months after its first birthday. 'Guaranteed coverage for one year' runs from the birth to the day before the first birthday; CHP+ coverage is by calendar month (eligibility is effective on the first day of a month, § 430.1), so the month of the first birthday, which the guarantee reaches on its first days, is covered and the month after it is not (OQ-1231 records this reading of the birthday month). Then the child is tested as any CHP+ child (chp_child_is_eligible, CO-705), whose 12-month continuous eligibility (§ 430.2) runs from its own start. Coverage review 2, N-11 had read the age on the determination date in every month. Pattern sweep, MAGI (2026-11-24, PS-06): whether the mother was enrolled in CHP+ at the birth is read as stated (chp_mother_was_enrolled_at_birth, from birth_mother_coverage_at_birth), required where read for a child in the first year (§ 430.5 gives no reading for an unstated enrollment; decision 4; was read as not enrolled).

### CO-4565 CHP+: month is before the coverage period `@engine`

Whether the month is one CHP+ cannot cover: a month before the month of the person's birth, or a month before the month of application (ma_application_date) - CHP+ eligibility is effective on the later of the first day of the month of application and the first day of the month the person becomes eligible (10 CCR 2505-3 § 430.1), and the program has no retroactive coverage - unless the person is a newborn of a CHP+ mother, whose guaranteed year runs from birth without an application (§ 430.5).

Precision. Where CBMS records a CHP+ eligibility period (chp_eligibility_period_start_month, CO-2402) that began before the month of the application being determined (a renewal or a later application), the period's first month is the earliest month covered, so a recorded continuous eligibility or prenatal span is not cut back. ### CO-704 CHP+: household income is within the CHP+ limit `@engine`

Whether this person's chp_household_income, as a percentage of the poverty guideline, falls within the band 10 CCR 2505-3-110.1.E states for a child (greater than ma_income_limit_child_pct, not exceeding chp_income_limit_pct_upper of FPL) or 110.1.F states for a pregnant woman (greater than ma_income_limit_pregnant_pct, not exceeding chp_income_limit_pct_upper of FPL), applying the 42 CFR 435.603(d)(4)/10 CCR 2505-10 8.100.4.D ma_magi_income_disregard_pct disregard only when it makes the difference for CHP+, the highest MAGI income standard a child or pregnant person in this band could qualify under.

Precision. The ma_magi_income_disregard_pct disregard (ma_magi_income_disregard_pct) is tested as an alternative to the plain ratio, not always subtracted, because subtracting it unconditionally could push a household that already qualifies without it below the lower bound (a household at 142.5% of FPL, for example, would fail the ma_income_limit_child_pct floor once 5 points are subtracted, which is not what the disregard is for). This item is therefore true when either the plain ma_magi_household_income_pct_fpl falls in the band, or the ratio less the disregard does; both compare against the same lower/upper parameters for the person's category (child or pregnant). Coverage pass 4, C4-05: the month's figure (ma_magi_monthly_household_income_pct_fpl, CO-6452) is tested first, and the budget figure of C.4.a and C.5 only where it fails, so an applicant eligible on the month is determined where the annualized figure cannot be. Coverage pass 5, C5-03 (2026-11-23): pregnancy is read for the month evaluated (chp_is_pregnant_in_month, CO-7051), not on the determination date (is_pregnant), so a woman who applied while pregnant and delivered before the determination is a pregnant woman in the months she was pregnant.

Precision. Citizenship/immigration status (110.1.B) reads chp_meets_status_requirement (CO-2707): CHP+'s own list (110.1.B.1-5, chp_has_qualifying_immigration_status, CO-2706) or the 110.1.B.5.o exception, which reaches every person under 19 regardless of status. 10 CCR 2505-3-120.1.C's exclusion of an inmate of a public institution or a patient in an institution for mental diseases reads is_inmate_of_public_institution (CO-1105) and is_patient_in_institution_for_mental_diseases (CO-1104), added in phase 7 (OQ-58, resolved), not snap_resides_in_institution_providing_meals, which means a nursing-facility or similar long-term care admission; the 90-days-before-release reentry services § 120.1.C carves out are a benefit, not eligibility, and are not modeled. The inmate exclusion reads plain incarceration (CO-1105) and CHP+'s own reentry carve-out (chp_is_in_reentry_period, CO-1749). Final verification pass 3, F3-2: 10 CCR 2505-3 § 120.1.B excludes a person "eligible to receive assistance under Title XIX"; the test reads ma_has_full_coverage_category (CO-1176: full MAGI, SSI-related, OAP SISC B, a protected group, a Buy-In program, long-term care, or a needy person under 21), not only full MAGI eligibility (ma_magi_is_fully_eligible), so an SSI child or a Children with Disabilities Buy-In child is not CHP+ eligible. Emergency-only Medicaid is still not read as Title XIX eligibility (CO-562's reasoning), and CO-1176 reads no CHP+ eligibility item, so no cycle. Coverage review F-26: 10 CCR 2505-3 § 110.1.A.1 says "less than 19 years of age", and § 110.1.B.5.o names the 19th-birthday month ("whose 19th birthday occurred in the current month"); the item reads the age through the end of the 19th-birthday month (ma_is_under_child_age_or_turns_nineteen_this_month, CO-564), as Medicaid's § 8.100.4.G.1 and G.2.a do, so a child turning 19 is not dropped mid-month. Coverage pass 6, C6-05(a) (2026-11-24): residency is read through chp_meets_residency (CO-7402), so an unstated residence is cannot determine, not a non-resident.

### CO-7051 CHP+: is pregnant in the month `@engine`

Whether the person was a pregnant woman (10 CCR 2505-3 § 110.1.A.2) at some time in the month, for a month from the month of application on, the only months CHP+ can cover (§ 430.1). Never a month before the month the pregnancy began, where pregnancy_start_date is stated. Otherwise: a person pregnant now (is_pregnant) in the determination month and later months and in the months from the application month on, never in or before the month a recorded earlier pregnancy ended (most_recent_pregnancy_end_date, CO-7400), and for a month before the determination month that is after such an end only where the end is before the application month or the pregnancy's start is stated; for a pregnancy that has ended (most_recent_pregnancy_end_date, CO-7400: the stated end, or the date of birth of the child of the case she gave birth to), the month it ended and the months from the month it began through it; and, for a person not pregnant now who states the start of a pregnancy but no end, the months from its start cannot be determined. From the month of application on, a month in which a recorded pregnancy ended (pregnancy_ended_in_month, CO-7841) is a pregnant month; a month before it on or before a recorded end is not read (false). A month on or before a recorded end (pregnancy_ended_on_or_after_month, CO-7773) is read from the ended pregnancy, not from the current one: a month after every recorded end before the most recent end's month is of the pregnancy that ended most recently, pregnant from the month it began (pregnancy_start_date where stated on or before that end, else, for a person pregnant now, previous_pregnancy_start_date, CO-7840); a month on or before an earlier end, other than the month of an end, cannot be determined (no fact states an earlier pregnancy's start).

Precision. MAGI close-out, KL-MAGI-2 (2026-11-24; docs/reviews/known-limits.md), as ma_is_pregnant_in_month (CO-3601) reads it, from the month of application on (§ 430.1): a stated pregnancy_start_date governs only the months after the last recorded end before it. Pregnancies do not overlap, so a month on or before a recorded end (CO-7773) belongs to an ended pregnancy, never to the current one: the month of a recorded end is a pregnant month (CO-7841; its last day is in it); a month after the month of every recorded end before the most recent end's month (latest_pregnancy_end_date_before_month, CO-7772, at that month) is of the pregnancy that ended most recently, pregnant from the month it began: its start is pregnancy_start_date where that is on or before the end (CO-3600: for a pregnancy that has ended, the date it began), otherwise, for a person pregnant now, whose pregnancy_start_date is the current pregnancy's, previous_pregnancy_start_date (CO-7840), required where read (decision 4 of 2026-11-23); a month on or before an earlier end that is not itself the month of an end cannot be determined. The months after every recorded end are read as before. Before, a stated start of the current pregnancy made every month before it not pregnant, the months of an earlier pregnancy and its birth month included (CO-1123 with March to August 2025 recorded as other Medical Assistance and the current start 2026-10-05 stated: March to September 2025 not pregnant, so no period opened from them, though she gave birth on 2025-09-10). Ends in the same month are one end for the span: twins born on two days are one pregnancy. Coverage pass 7, C7-02 (2026-11-24): the current pregnancy began after the last recorded end of an earlier one, so it is not read in or before that end's month, and where an earlier pregnancy ended after the application month the months between that end and the determination month are of the current pregnancy only from its stated start (decision 4), as ma_is_pregnant_in_month (CO-3601) reads them. Coverage pass 5, C5-03 (2026-11-23). CHP+ coverage is by the month (§ 430.1, "the first day of the month of application"; § 430.3, a pregnant woman's enrollment "effective as of the first of the month of the date of application"), so a month in which she was pregnant on any day is a pregnant month: the month of the birth is one. A woman who applied while pregnant and delivered before the determination was pregnant in the application month, which opens the § 430.3 enrollment span (chp_is_in_prenatal_coverage_period, CO-2407). For a pregnancy that has ended, the start date is read for the months before its end; not stated, such a month is unknown (decision 4). A month before the application month is never covered by CHP+ (chp_month_is_before_coverage_period, CO-4565; § 430.1), so a pregnancy that has ended is not read in it: such a month is false here, and the CHP+ verification items that read this item (CO-1417, CO-1418) ask nothing for it. CHP+'s own reading of the neutral pregnancy facts, as Medicaid's ma_is_pregnant_in_month (CO-3601) is Medicaid's: CHP+ has no retroactive months, so it reads no month before the application by the dates of a current pregnancy. Coverage pass 6 (2026-11-24): C6-06, a stated pregnancy_start_date governs the months before it whatever is_pregnant says (a pregnancy that began after the application month is not read in it); C6-03, an ended pregnancy is read from most_recent_pregnancy_end_date (CO-7400), so a birth recorded by the child's date of birth and the gave_birth_to relationship ends the pregnancy (CO-814 without pregnancy_end_date: October was not pregnant, ineligible; it is a pregnant month, 4,200 / 1,803.33 = 232.9%, eligible_prenatal, the span through October 2027), the month a pregnancy ended is a pregnant month whether or not its start is stated, and a person not pregnant now who states a start and no end, with no birth recorded, cannot be determined for the months from its start; with no start, no end and no birth she has no ended pregnancy, the reading pregnancy_end_date (CO-089) states.

Precision. Coverage pass 4, C4-15 (2026-11-23): there is no age test. 10 CCR 2505-3 § 50.19 defines "Woman" as "a female who is 19 years in age or older", and § 110.1.A reaches a person under 19 as a child (A.1) and a pregnant woman as such (A.2); a pregnant applicant under 19 is tested as a child first (chp_eligibility_status, CO-707, reads chp_child_is_eligible first, and chp_income_within_limit, CO-704, takes the child's band), but this item also reads her as a Prenatal Care Program client, which exempts her from cost sharing (§ 330.4, CO-1990) and gives her the § 430.3 postpartum span (CO-2407). That reading is OQ-1232's. Parallel to chp_child_is_eligible (CO-705) with is_pregnant in place of ma_is_under_child_age_or_turns_nineteen_this_month and the pregnant-woman income band (chp_income_within_limit already selects the correct band for a pregnant person). Status reads chp_meets_status_requirement (CO-2707), CHP+'s own list or the 110.1.B.5.o exception. The 120.1.C exclusion of an inmate of a public institution or a patient in an institution for mental diseases is modeled (is_inmate_of_public_institution, CO-1105; is_patient_in_institution_for_mental_diseases, CO-1104), as on CO-705 (OQ-58). The inmate exclusion reads plain incarceration (CO-1105) and CHP+'s own reentry carve-out (chp_is_in_reentry_period, CO-1749). Final verification pass 3, F3-2: 10 CCR 2505-3 § 120.1.B excludes a person "eligible to receive assistance under Title XIX"; the test reads ma_has_full_coverage_category (CO-1176: full MAGI, SSI-related, OAP SISC B, a protected group, a Buy-In program, long-term care, or a needy person under 21), not only full MAGI eligibility (ma_magi_is_fully_eligible), so an SSI child or a Children with Disabilities Buy-In child is not CHP+ eligible. Coverage pass 6, C6-05(a) (2026-11-24): residency is read through chp_meets_residency (CO-7402), so an unstated residence is cannot determine, not a non-resident.

### CO-707 CHP+: eligibility status `@engine`

The single CHP+ eligibility outcome for the month - ineligible_before_coverage_period for a month before birth or before the month of application (10 CCR 2505-3 § 430.1); ineligible_deceased for a month after the month of the person's death (date_of_death; § 430.2.B.i); otherwise eligible as a child, as a pregnant (prenatal) applicant, as a newborn of a CHP+ mother (10 CCR 2505-3 § 430.5), or on the limited incarceration benefit during a child's continuous eligibility period (§ 430.2.B.ii); or one of six specific ineligibility reasons (Medicaid-eligible instead per 10 CCR 2505-3-120.1.B, income outside the CHP+ band per 110.1.E-F, other creditable coverage per 120.1.A, failing residency per 110.1.D, failing citizenship/immigration status per 110.1.B, or an inmate of a public institution or a patient in an institution for mental diseases per 120.1.C), or ineligible for a reason this batch does not distinguish further (for example not a child and not pregnant).

Precision. Coverage pass 7, C7-06 (2026-11-24): a month after the month of the person's death is ineligible_deceased, tested after the months before the coverage period (§ 430.1) and before every other row. An application may be made for a person who has died (42 CFR 435.915(a)(2), S218: 'regardless of whether the individual is alive when application for Medicaid is made'; 42 U.S.C. 1396a(a)(34) as amended, S1706: 'application was made on the individual's behalf in the case of a deceased individual'), and it covers the months in which the person would have been eligible 'at the time he received the services' (S218); the month of death is such a month, since a person eligible at any time during a calendar month is eligible for the entire month (10 CCR 2505-10 § 8.100.4.G.1, S3351). No month after it is: the rule ends even the periods that continue regardless of other changes when 'The member is deceased' or the 'Child is deceased', effective in the earliest possible month (§ 8.100.4.G.6.a.i, S3755; § 8.100.3.Q.1.b.i, S1502; 10 CCR 2505-3 § 430.2.B.i, S1714), and no category covers a person after death. The death is read from date_of_death (CO-2868, 'Not stated for a living person'), through is_deceased (CO-2200) for the month before. Before, such a month was answered by the person's facts as if alive (DIED-RETRO: died 2026-08-20, application 2026-09-15 with a request, $1,000: September to December eligible). Coverage review F-09: a month CHP+ cannot cover (before birth, or before the month of application outside a recorded CHP+ period, unless a guaranteed newborn; chp_month_is_before_coverage_period, CO-4565; § 430.1) is ineligible_before_coverage_period, checked first, as ma_magi_eligibility_status (CO-554) checks its own. Otherwise evaluated in the order the branches are listed - eligible outcomes first, then the specific ineligibility reasons. Residency and citizenship/status are checked immediately after the eligible and Medicaid-eligible branches and before the income and coverage tests, so a child or pregnant applicant who fails residency or citizenship is reported ineligible_residency or ineligible_status rather than falling through to the income catch-all - Phase 7 (OQ-58): a child or pregnant applicant who passes every other test, including income, but is an inmate of a public institution or a patient in an institution for mental diseases (10 CCR 2505-3 § 120.1.C) is reported ineligible_institution; income is tested explicitly before it so an income failure keeps its own reason - matching this volume's ma_magi_eligibility_status (CO-554) convention of checking residency before income, and correcting the prior ordering, which found reported every residency or citizenship failure as ineligible_income regardless of the actual reason. A child in a CHP+ continuous eligibility period (chp_child_is_in_continuous_eligibility_period, CO-2404) stays eligible_child whatever the month's income (§ 430.2.A), and a pregnant woman in her enrollment span (chp_is_in_prenatal_coverage_period, CO-2407) stays eligible_prenatal through the twelfth month after the birth (§ 430.3); both are tested after the Medicaid-eligible branch, since a child whose income falls moves to Medicaid with a new period (§ 430.2.A.i). A newborn of a CHP+ mother is eligible_newborn for its first year (§ 430.5) unless Medicaid covers it. Final verification pass 3, F3-2: 10 CCR 2505-3 § 120.1.B excludes a person "eligible to receive assistance under Title XIX"; the test reads ma_has_full_coverage_category (CO-1176: full MAGI, SSI-related, OAP SISC B, a protected group, a Buy-In program, long-term care, or a needy person under 21), not only full MAGI eligibility (ma_magi_is_fully_eligible), so an SSI child or a Children with Disabilities Buy-In child is not CHP+ eligible. Emergency-only Medicaid is still not read as Title XIX eligibility (CO-562's reasoning), and CO-1176 reads no CHP+ eligibility item, so no cycle. Coverage review F-19: § 440.4.C lets the Department disenroll an enrollee admitted to an institution for mental diseases or a correctional facility, while § 430.2.B's closed list of exceptions to a child's 12-month continuous eligibility names incarceration (the limited benefit) and not an IMD admission. The volume reads § 430.2.B as governing during the period: a child in a continuous eligibility period who is admitted to an IMD stays eligible_child, because the continuous eligibility row precedes the institution row; outside a period the child is ineligible_institution (§ 120.1.C). Coverage pass 5, C5-03 (2026-11-23): pregnancy is read for the month evaluated (chp_is_pregnant_in_month, CO-7051), not on the determination date (is_pregnant), so a woman who applied while pregnant and delivered before the determination is a pregnant woman in the months she was pregnant. Coverage pass 5, C5-12 (2026-11-23): a child or pregnant woman excluded as a member of the family of a public agency employee eligible for the state employees' health benefits plan (chp_is_excluded_as_public_agency_employee_family, CO-1978, the last test of CO-705 and CO-706 other than the institution test) has her own reason, ineligible_public_agency_employee_family, tested after income and before ineligible_institution; before, the institution row was the catch-all and reported her as an institution case. The institution row is now reached only by a person who passes every other test of CO-705 or CO-706 and is an inmate (outside the reentry period) or a patient in an institution for mental diseases. Coverage pass 6, C6-02 (2026-11-24): a woman in the CHP+ prenatal span (CO-2407) after the pregnancy has ended who is eligible for Title XIX (ma_has_full_coverage_category: in the Medicaid pregnancy coverage period, which opened in a later month of the same application) is ineligible_medicaid_eligible (§ 120.1.B), not eligible_prenatal: the Medicaid-eligible row reads the span as it reads the month's pregnancy (PG-LATER-ELIG: CHP+ span from September at 221.8%, Medicaid period from October at 166.4%; November on, Medicaid eligible, CHP+ ineligible_medicaid_eligible; before, eligible_prenatal beside Medicaid). Coverage pass 6, C6-05(a) (2026-11-24): residency is read through chp_meets_residency (CO-7402), so an unstated residence is cannot determine, not a non-resident.

### CO-1203 Adult Financial: meets AND-SO eligibility `@engine`

Whether the person meets every eligibility criterion of Aid to the Needy Disabled - State Only for the month - age af_and_so_min_age through af_and_max_age (any age through af_and_max_age if blind), total disability, not approved for SSI or SSDI, has applied for SSI (and SSDI with a work history) and appealed any SSI denial (3.520.71.B), citizenship or qualified non-citizen status with the five-year bar, Colorado residency, the resource limit, and countable income below the AND-SO grant standard, the substance-abuse conditions of 3.541.3 where the certification identifies substance abuse, not in a period of ineligibility for a transfer without fair consideration (3.520.76), not found to have failed to apply for other benefits (3.520.61.G), and not barred by Colorado Works (3.520.61.F) - per 9 CCR 2503-5 3.520.61, 3.520.71.A, 3.540 and 3.544.

Precision. The conjuncts are exactly af_category's former and_so branch (CO-953), lifted into an item so the Home Care Allowance's financial test (3.570.13.B.2, 'Meet all eligibility criteria required for Aid to the Needy Disabled - State Only (AND-SO) program') reads the same test af_category does. See OQ-138 (SSDI recipients excluded) and OQ-151 (the SSI application duty of 3.520.71.B is not a conjunct). Vocabulary fix round (R-5): 'not approved for SSDI' reads receives_ssdi (CO-1727), not SNAP's disability-payment fact. Final cash review FC-6, FC-7 and FC-9: adds af_and_so_meets_substance_abuse_conditions (CO-3849; 3.541.3, C.R.S. 26-2-111(4)(e)-(f)), af_is_in_twfc_penalty_period (CO-3841) and af_has_failed_to_apply_for_other_benefits (CO-3860), each read as met when its facts are not stated; the Home Care Allowance's AND-SO route reads them too. Coverage review F-13: a patient in an institution for tuberculosis or mental diseases, or in a medical institution for tuberculosis or psychosis, is barred by C.R.S. 26-2-111(1)(d) (af_and_is_barred_as_institution_patient, CO-4446). F-14: an IPV disqualification (af_is_serving_ipv_disqualification, CO-4447; 3.583.N), an EBT-misuse ineligibility period (af_is_in_ebt_misuse_ineligibility_period, CO-4448; 3.581.I.3) and an unsigned IM-14 (af_im14_signed, CO-4449; 3.545.A.2, 3.520.4.C.5.a) each bar AND-SO; the first two are read as false and the IM-14 as signed when not stated. Coverage review 2, G-4: not for a month that begins after date_of_death (3.581.C.1-2, S3502). Coverage pass 4 CA4-15: the ages are taken in the month evaluated, 59 or younger on its first day  and 18 or older on its last , with eligibility beginning on the day the client meets all requirements (3.542.B, af_partial_month_payment_factor); before, the determination date's age was read in every month (OQ-951). The grandfathered route (3.570.13.B.3, receiving both OAP and HCA as of December 31, 2013) also requires the person to have been of OAP age (60, af_oap_age) on that date, so a supplied grandfather flag cannot contradict the person's date of birth (phase-8 fix round, C-1). Before, a grandfathered client whose income had risen above the OAP standard kept the route on the flag (probe H1: af_category none, af_hca_grant $977, where the text gives $0).

### CO-1217 Home Care Allowance: eligibility status `@engine`

The person's Home Care Allowance eligibility for the month, checked in order - age five or older, Colorado residency, living in a home rather than a facility, not receiving and not functionally eligible for HCBS, an HCA tier, then the financial routes - eligible only if every check passes, per 9 CCR 2503-5 3.520.61.B, 3.570.11.A, 3.570.12 ("Home"), 3.570.13 and 3.570.14.D.

Precision. '"Home" (3.570.12) is a non-facility residence and "cannot include a homeless shelter or other temporary setting"; this item reads snap_resides_in_institution_providing_meals for a facility stay and af_hca_lives_in_shelter_or_temporary_setting (CO-037) for a shelter (phase-8 fix round, S-5); another temporary setting is af_hca_lives_in_shelter_or_temporary_setting (CO-2010). Functional eligibility for HCBS bars HCA at application and at reassessment, except during the stay of up to three months while a transition delayed outside the client's control is completed (3.570.11.A.2.b, af_hca_is_in_hcbs_transition_period, CO-2009); both facts are read as false when a case does not state them.' Vocabulary fix round (docs/reviews/vocabulary-reuse.md, R-8): reads resides_in_medical_institution (CO-1742), not SNAP's majority-of-meals institution fact. Coverage review F-1: a client out of State on a temporary basis is discontinued on day thirty-one (3.570.17.C.8.b): more than af_hca_absence_max_days days from temporarily_out_of_state_start_date (CO-3806) to the determination date; the general presumptions of 3.520.64.E are in af_meets_residency. P2-4: a stay in a hospital or other long-term care facility ends HCA when it continues thirty days or more (C.4.b): from institution_entry_date, or sooner when the stay is expected to last that long (expects_institutional_stay_of_thirty_days, read as false when not stated); with no entry date stated the stay is read as ending HCA, as before. Coverage review 2, G-3: "Home" is a non-facility residence (3.570.12), and 3.510 makes a facility any residence whose intent is care or treatment ("hospitals, nursing homes, regional centers, group and host homes, and mental health institutions"); C.7 discontinues a client "residing anywhere other than his OR her home". So every residence_setting_type other than private_dwelling, room_and_board and commercial_property (the person's own non-facility residence) is ineligible_setting at once (C.4.a, C.7), assisted living, group and host homes and treatment centres included; the thirty-day reading of C.4.b, with C.7.a's medical leave, is kept only for a stay in a medical institution or a stay away from a home the client keeps for medical treatment (temporary_absence_reason medical_treatment). An unstated setting is read as the home. The forty-two days of combined medical and non-medical leave in the twelve months from approval (C.7.b) are af_hca_combined_leave_days_in_approval_year (CO-4728) against af_hca_combined_leave_max_days (CO-4729), read as 0 when not stated; the start of payment after the approval month (3.570.13.F) is in af_hca_grant (CO-1219). G-4: a client who died before the month is ineligible_deceased (3.570.17.C.10, "effective the day after the client's date of death"; 3.581.C.1-2); the month of death keeps its payment. F-14: an Adult Financial IPV disqualification or EBT-misuse ineligibility period (CO-4447, CO-4448) is ineligible_sanction. Time audit T-6: "N consecutive days" is counted as the days elapsed since the day the absence or stay began (days_between), the day of departure or entry itself not counted (OQ-953): the Home Care Allowance's absence and expected institutional stay of af_hca_absence_max_days: the days elapsed since the day of departure or entry. Pattern sweep (cash) PS-D1 (docs/reviews/pattern-sweep-cash.md), decision 4: the residence setting, the medical institution, the absence reason and the expected stay are required where read (no rule gives the old readings: an unstated setting as the home, an unstated absence as none, an unstated expectation as false and, with neither entry date nor expectation, the stay as ending HCA); the combined leave days are read for a client approved before the determination date (af_hca_approval_date stated: the twelve-month period of 3.570.17.C.7.b has begun) and required there; for a client not yet approved no leave period has begun. The age, the absence out of State and the stay are read on the determination date, which is right for HCA: eligibility is decided at the approval and payment begins only the month after it, with no retroactive payment (3.570.13.F), so no month before the determination is paid.

Type one of, scope person-month, program AdultFinancial.
Uses: `af_hca_absence_max_days`, `af_hca_approval_date`, `af_hca_combined_leave_days_in_approval_year`, `af_hca_combined_leave_max_days`, `af_hca_financially_eligible`, `af_hca_functionally_eligible_for_hcbs`, `af_hca_is_in_hcbs_transition_period`, `af_hca_lives_in_shelter_or_temporary_setting`, `af_hca_min_age`, `af_hca_tier`, `af_is_in_ebt_misuse_ineligibility_period`, `af_is_serving_ipv_disqualification`, `af_meets_residency`, `age`, `date_of_death`, `expects_institutional_stay_of_thirty_days`, `institution_entry_date`, `receives_hcbs_services`, `residence_setting_type`, `resides_in_medical_institution`, `temporarily_out_of_state_start_date`, `temporary_absence_reason`.

### CO-1219 Home Care Allowance: grant amount `@engine`

The monthly Home Care Allowance payment for an eligible client - the CMA-authorized amount, raised by a State Supplementary Payment to the HCA payment floor when below it - or zero for a client who is not eligible, per 9 CCR 2503-5 3.570.11.B, 3.570.11.E.2 and 3.570.13.D.

Precision. The tier maximums are not stated in the rule (OQ-250); the authorized amount is supplied. Coverage review 2 (first-pass P2-4): payment begins on the first of the month after the approval month or with the month of the CMA's payment effective date, whichever is later, and nothing is paid for an earlier month (3.570.13.F, S3503: "There shall be no retroactive HCA payments"); an unstated approval date or payment effective date sets no later start. Pattern sweep (cash) PS-D1 (docs/reviews/pattern-sweep-cash.md): the payment begins the month after approval (3.570.13.F); for a client not approved before this determination (af_hca_approval_date not stated, its declared meaning) the approval is this determination, so nothing is paid for the determination month or a month before it. Before, an unstated approval date was read as no limit, and every month was paid.

Type money, scope person-month, program AdultFinancial.
Uses: `af_hca_approval_date`, `af_hca_eligibility_status`, `af_hca_payment_effective_date`, `af_hca_payment_floor`, `hca_authorized_amount`.

```
if Home Care Allowance: eligibility status is equal to eligible
  then (if any of the following is true:;     - all of the following are true:;       - Home Care Allowance approval date is unknown;       - the month is at most the month containing the Determination Date;     - all of the following are true:;       - it is not the case that Home Care Allowance approval date is unknown;       - the month is at most the month containing Home Care Allowance approval date;     - all of the following are true:;       - it is not the case that Home Care Allowance payment effective date is unknown;       - the month is less than the month containing Home Care Allowance payment effective date;   then 0; otherwise the greater of Home Care Allowance payment floor standard (977) and Home Care Allowance authorized amount)
otherwise 0
```

### CO-1220 Died while receiving Adult Financial or Medicaid assistance `@engine`

The person has died and, at the time of death, was receiving Old Age Pension, Aid to the Needy Disabled (AND-SO or AND-CS), Home Care Allowance, or Colorado Medicaid assistance, per 9 CCR 2503-5 3.570.43.A.1. False for a living person.

Precision. Receipt at death is read from the month of death: a Medicaid enrollment (is_enrolled_in_medical_assistance, the enrollment record, which for a decedent is the record at death) or an Adult Financial payment (adult_financial_cash_income, which includes the Home Care Allowance). Decision 4 of 2026-11-23 (docs/plan-colorado.md: missing information is cannot determine unless the rule says otherwise), applied as for the receipts readers (b49a7f2; earned-income records E1 for the cash programs, docs/reviews/records-earnings-cash.md): 3.570.43.A.1 asks whether the person was receiving at death and gives no reading for payments not reported, so with the receipts not stated an Adult Financial payment in the month of death cannot be determined (a stated empty list is none); a Medicaid enrollment at death still answers on its own. Receipt records, migration phase 1: the grant received in the month of death is af_grant_receipts is read from the receipts (CO-5000). The Home Care Allowance is its own receipt kind (af_home_care_allowance_receipts; coverage review 3 H-5). Coverage pass 4 CA4-16: whether the deceased was enrolled in Medical Assistance is required where read (no Adult Financial grant in the month of death), never read as no when not stated (decision 4 of 2026-11-23: missing information is cannot determine unless the rule says otherwise).

```
    - Is enrolled in Medical Assistance
```
