### CO-1270 Colorado Works: eligible for a diversion payment `@engine`

Whether the person's assistance unit may receive a Colorado Works diversion payment for the month - it is eligible for basic cash assistance, or fails only the basic cash assistance income test and is within the county's higher diversion income limit, or, for a one-time cash payment, fails only because a member refused to sign the application form to avoid assigning support rights (3.606.8.A.6, "All diversion clients who receive a one-time cash payment are not required to assign child support rights"; cw_diversion_is_one_time_cash_payment, CO-7306; cw_unit_eligible_but_for_support_assignment, CO-7307); the assessment finds it does not need long-term or basic cash assistance; it demonstrates a specific crisis need under a diversion agreement; and it is not within an earlier diversion's period of ineligibility - per 9 CCR 2503-6 3.601 ("Diversion") and 3.606.8.A.

Precision. The rule has a single diversion program with a county income option (3.606.8.A.6), which relaxes only the income test (phase-8 fix round, S-1): a unit ineligible for any other reason (no dependent child, residency, status, living arrangement, time limit, sanction closure) is not diversion-eligible whatever the county limit; it states no separate state and county diversion programs. A client cannot receive diversion in a month it receives basic cash assistance (A.7); the unit that needs no basic cash assistance does not take it, so the conjunct needs_long_term_cash_assistance = false covers it. The payment amount is needs-based and not modeled; the period of ineligibility cannot exceed the maximum grant for the household size over the same period (A.4), which is the county's computation. Diversion payments do not count toward the time limit (A.6). Final cash review FC-18: 3.606.8.A.7 (no diversion grant in a month of basic cash assistance) is a conjunct, read from the month's basic cash assistance (cw_basic_cash_assistance_receipts, CO-5653; receipt records, migration phase 2: before them, tanf_cash_income), not only through needs_long_term_cash_assistance. Decision 4 of 2026-11-23 (docs/plan-colorado.md: missing information is cannot determine unless the rule says otherwise), applied as for the receipts readers (b49a7f2; earned-income records E1 for the cash programs, docs/reviews/records-earnings-cash.md): 3.606.8.A.7 gives no reading for a payment not reported, so with the receipts not stated whether the unit receives basic cash assistance in the month cannot be determined (a stated empty list is none); before, a payment not stated was read as none. Coverage pass 6 CA6-6 (docs/reviews/coverage6-cash.md, probe W5r): 3.604.4.A makes the assignment of support rights a condition of the unit's eligibility for basic cash assistance, and 3.606.8.A.6 releases a client who receives a one-time cash diversion payment from it; before, the refusal made the unit ineligible_child_support and the diversion was refused with it (W5r: $0 where the rule gives the county's $500). The release is the assignment's only: a failure to cooperate with Child Support Services, and every later check of CO-921, still bar the diversion (CO-7307). Whether the agreed payment is a one-time cash payment is read only on this path and is required there (decision 4 of 2026-11-23).

Type yes/no, scope person-month, program ColoradoWorks.
Uses: `cw_assistance_unit_members`, `cw_basic_cash_assistance_receipts`, `cw_diversion_is_one_time_cash_payment`, `cw_eligibility_status`, `cw_has_refused_child_support_assignment`, `cw_meets_county_diversion_income_limit`, `cw_unit_eligible_but_for_support_assignment`, `has_specific_crisis_need`, `in_diversion_period_of_ineligibility`, `needs_long_term_cash_assistance`.

```
all of the following are true:
  - any of the following is true:
    - Colorado Works: eligibility status is equal to eligible
    - all of the following are true:
      - Colorado Works: eligibility status is equal to ineligible_income
      - Meets the county's diversion income limit
    - all of the following are true:
      - Colorado Works: eligibility status is equal to ineligible_child_support
      - there is a person in Colorado Works: assistance unit members such that
        that person's Colorado Works: refused to assign child support rights, otherwise no
      - Colorado Works: the diversion payment is a one-time cash payment
      - Colorado Works: eligible but for the assignment of support rights
  - it is not the case that Needs long-term or basic cash assistance
  - Has a specific crisis need
  - it is not the case that In a diversion period of ineligibility
  - it is not the case that Colorado Works: basic cash assistance received in the month is more than 0
```

### CO-1438 Adult Financial: verification status `@engine`

Where this client's Adult Financial verification stands: not applicable (under the Old Age Pension age and without an SSI, blindness or disability basis for Aid to the Needy Disabled or Aid to the Blind); complete; pending before the eleven-day due date, or while the only elements outstanding are the AND-SO medical certification within its thirty days and the proof of an SSA or other benefit application within its own period (eleven days from the SSA application, or the AND-SO sixty days of conditional approval); or past due, after which the county may deny for failure to return verifications.

Precision. The AND-SO certification's thirty days run "following the interview" (3.541.1.A.1.b): they are counted from af_interview_date (CO-2005), read as the verification request date when the case does not state it (OQ-375 resolved). Final cash review FC-9: the proof of application of 3.520.71.C has its own period (af_benefit_application_verification_due_date, CO-3870), read as the medical certification's is. Coverage pass 6 CA6-11 (docs/reviews/coverage6-cash.md): a client eligible for an SSN who refuses or fails to apply for or provide one (9 CCR 2503-5 3.520.65.A.3: "shall result in denial") is reached through this status, not through af_category (CO-953): the SSN element stays pending until its due date and is then past_due, the outcome on which the county denies. af_category does not itself deny for the SSN, as the volume keeps verification a separate outcome; Colorado Works models its SSN duty as a disqualification (cw_has_failed_to_apply_for_ssn).

Type one of, scope person-month, program AdultFinancial.

  then not_applicable
else if Adult Financial: pending verification count is equal to 0
  then complete
else if the Determination Date is at most Adult Financial: verification due date
  then pending
else if ((Adult Financial: pending verification count minus (if all of the following are true:;     - Adult Financial: AND-SO disability verification is pending;     - the Determination Date is at most Adult Financial: AND-SO disability certification due date;   then 1; otherwise 0)) minus (if all of the following are true:;     - Adult Financial: proof of benefit application pending;     - the Determination Date is at most Adult Financial: proof of benefit application due date;   then 1; otherwise 0)) is equal to 0

### CO-1504 Deceased Colorado Works client `@engine`

The person has died and is a deceased Colorado Works client - one who received Colorado Works while alive and whose case was active in the county at death - so that a death reimbursement benefit may be paid toward the funeral, burial or cremation, per 9 CCR 2503-6 3.606.7.A.1, B.1 and F ("The county department in which the deceased client's case is active"). False for a living person.

Precision. A Colorado Works payment in the month of death (cw_basic_cash_assistance_receipts, CO-5653, in that month; receipt records, migration phase 2: before them, tanf_cash_income), or a case receiving or authorized to receive basic cash assistance at death (receives_tanf_cash, CO-013, the case record, which for a decedent is the record at death), is read as an active case at death after receipt while alive (3.606.7.B.1, F). Final cash review FC-19: the month-of-death payment alone was narrower than the rule (a client who died before that month's payment was issued). A payment not stated for that month is none when the receipts are stated. Decision 4 of 2026-11-23 (docs/plan-colorado.md: missing information is cannot determine unless the rule says otherwise), applied as for the receipts readers (b49a7f2; earned-income records E1 for the cash programs, docs/reviews/records-earnings-cash.md): 3.606.7.B.1 gives no reading for payments not reported, so with the receipts not stated a payment in the month of death cannot be determined; an active case at death (receives_tanf_cash) still answers on its own. Coverage pass 4 CA4-16: whether the deceased received Colorado Works cash is required where read (no basic cash assistance receipt in the month of death), never read as no when not stated (decision 4 of 2026-11-23: missing information is cannot determine unless the rule says otherwise).

Type yes/no, scope person, program ColoradoWorks.
Uses: `cw_basic_cash_assistance_receipts`, `date_of_death`, `receives_tanf_cash`.

all of the following are true:
  - it is not the case that Date of death is unknown
  - any of the following is true:
    - Colorado Works: basic cash assistance received in the month is more than 0 for the month containing Date of death
    - Receives TANF cash assistance
```

### CO-1508 Colorado Works: death reimbursement amount `@engine`

The Colorado Works death reimbursement benefit for a deceased client - for a client who received Colorado Works while alive, when the total combined charges for the disposition (a prepaid plot of $2,000 or less, or a donated one, not counted) are at most cw_death_reimbursement_cost_limit - the lesser of the cw_death_reimbursement_max maximum and the charges the decedent's estate leaves unpaid, reduced by the insurance proceeds and by the legally responsible persons' resources over the SSI limit, never below zero; zero otherwise. Per 9 CCR 2503-6 3.606.7.A.2, B, E and F.1-2.

Precision. Insurance proceeds (F.2.f, 'used to reduce the maximum Death Reimbursement') and the responsible persons' resources over the SSI limit (F.2.c, 'used to reduce the State Department funded Death Reimbursement payment') reduce the payment; the estate (B.2, F.2.b) reduces the charges the payment can cover. The Adult Financial burial benefit applies all three against the full costs (3.570.43.D); the two orders give different amounts when the charges are well under cw_death_reimbursement_max or the offsets are large (OQ-354). The responsible persons' excess resources are read from af_burial_responsible_person_excess_resources (CO-1229), the same SSI-limit computation 3.606.7.F.2.c states, cross-program rather than duplicated. Voluntary contributions from the responsible party (F.2.c) reduce the payment too (burial_contributions_from_responsible_persons, CO-4373, read as 0 when not stated; coverage review CW-19); contributions from non-responsible parties do not reduce the benefit (F.2.g). A Social Security lump-sum death benefit is not counted (F.2.e), as af_burial_responsible_person_resources (CO-1225) already states. Coverage pass 6 CA6-7: what responsible persons contribute is required where read (a deceased client whose costs are within the limit; decision 4 of 2026-11-23); before, read as 0 when not stated.

Type money, scope person, program ColoradoWorks.
Uses: `af_burial_responsible_person_excess_resources`, `burial_contributions_from_responsible_persons`, `burial_insurance_proceeds`, `burial_plot_cost_excluded_from_limit`, `burial_services_total_cost`, `cw_death_reimbursement_cost_limit`, `cw_death_reimbursement_max`, `cw_is_deceased_client`, `decedent_estate_value`.

```
if all of the following are true:
    - Deceased Colorado Works client
    - (Total cost of burial services minus Burial plot cost excluded from the burial cost limit) is at most Colorado Works death reimbursement total charge limit (2500)
  then the greater of 0 and (((the lesser of Colorado Works death reimbursement maximum (1500) and (Total cost of burial services minus Decedent's available estate)) minus Burial insurance proceeds) minus (Burial assistance: legally responsible person's resources over the SSI limit plus Burial contributions from legally responsible persons))
otherwise 0

Time audit T-6: "N consecutive days" is counted as the days elapsed since the day the absence or stay began (days_between), the day of departure or entry itself not counted (OQ-953): "a resident for at least thirty (30) consecutive days" (S1008, S1009, S1010): the days elapsed from the day of entry to the first day of the next month, so an entry on the 1st is thirty days in a 30-day month and thirty-one in a 31-day month.

### CO-1511 Adult Financial: barred by Colorado Works `@engine`

Whether the person is barred from Adult Financial programs for the month because of Colorado Works - currently receiving Colorado Works financial assistance, eligible for it, or in a Colorado Works case closed for a sanction - per 9 CCR 2503-5 3.520.61.F and 3.520.71.F.2.

Precision. Receipt is read from receives_tanf_cash (CO-013); eligibility and the sanction closure from the person's own cw_eligibility_status (CO-921) - eligible, or sanction_closure (a fourth-level sanction, 3.608.4.C.2). Coverage pass 2 (CW2-5): F.2.a (S1011) also bars a client whose case was denied or discontinued "Due to a sanction, demonstrable evidence, or disqualification"; the person's own ineligible_disqualified (3.604.2.L-M) and closed_demonstrable_evidence (3.607.5) are read too, as sanction_closure is. Coverage pass 3 (CW3-2): F.2.c (S1011) continues the bar "until the sanction, demonstrable evidence, or disqualification is removed; or until the client is found otherwise ineligible for TANF/Colorado Works benefits", so these three statuses bar only while the client's unit passes every later check of CO-921 (cw_unit_otherwise_eligible, CO-4835); a disqualified client whose unit is over income anyway is not barred. A specified caretaker who is not a parent is not required to join the Colorado Works case (3.520.71.F.1.a); such a person is not in a Colorado Works assistance unit in this volume (CO-900 joins parents and caretakers to their own dependent children only), so cw_eligibility_status does not report them eligible. A closure for demonstrable evidence or a disqualification, or a withdrawal before benefits are exhausted, that still stands (F.2.a-c) is the supplied af_has_open_colorado_works_closure_bar (CO-2008), read as false when a case does not state it. The duty of F.1 to apply for Colorado Works is not a separate test: the bar reads Colorado Works eligibility directly (OQ-357).

Type yes/no, scope person-month, program AdultFinancial.
Uses: `af_has_open_colorado_works_closure_bar`, `cw_eligibility_status`, `cw_unit_otherwise_eligible`, `receives_tanf_cash`.

  - Receives TANF cash assistance
  - Colorado Works: eligibility status is equal to eligible
  - all of the following are true:
    - Colorado Works: eligibility status is one of: sanction_closure, ineligible_disqualified, closed_demonstrable_evidence
    - Colorado Works: otherwise eligible apart from a disqualification, demonstrable evidence or sanction closure
  - Adult Financial: Colorado Works case closed for demonstrable evidence, disqualification or withdrawal, otherwise no
```

### CO-1512 Adult Financial: in-kind support and maintenance `@engine`

The In-Kind Support and Maintenance (ISM) amount for this person for the month under 9 CCR 2503-5 3.520.79: the ISM the Social Security Administration charges an SSI client (B.6); none for a client who pays a full share of the home's shelter costs (B.4-5), owns and lives in the residence (B.1), receives subsidized housing (B.2), is homeless (B.3), or pays shelter costs at least the maximum ISM (B.5); otherwise the full maximum when all shelter is provided (C.3), the maximum less what the client pays when the costs are below market value (C.1), or the lesser of the fair share and the maximum less what the client pays (C.2).

Precision. The client's payment is shelter_cost_monthly; the fair share is home_total_shelter_costs divided by the number of people living in the home (persons_living_in_home_count, CO-7911; KL-CASH-1, below). Homeless is 3.510's definition (af_is_homeless, CO-4410; coverage review F-5): a stay in a relative's home after losing housing is not homelessness unless the person moves among a succession of friends or relatives with no permanent arrangement, so that client's ISM is computed. af_countable_income (CO-946) caps it at af_ism_maximum (CO-1513) and counts it only for an OAP-age or AND-CS client. Not the same figure as ssi_in_kind_support_and_maintenance (CO-802). Coverage review P3: a client with an established life estate whose shelter costs are provided in full has ISM calculated (3.520.79.D); the life estate is not ownership, so the case states owns_and_lives_in_home false for that client. Resource records, step H1 Adult Financial (docs/reviews/records-holdings-snap-af.md): the client owns and lives in the residence (B.1) when a home record of the client's holdings states that the client lives in it (lives_in), in place of owns_and_lives_in_home (CO-3401), which was read as no when not stated; holdings not stated, or a home that does not say, is cannot determine (decision 4) where the earlier tests of B do not settle it. Coverage pass 4 CA4-16: the ISM the Social Security Administration charges (B.6) is read for an SSI recipient (receives_ssi) and required then, and the client's shelter payment (shelter_cost_monthly) is required where the computation reaches it; neither is read as 0 when not stated (decision 4 of 2026-11-23: missing information is cannot determine unless the rule says otherwise). Coverage pass 7, F7-4 (docs/reviews/coverage7-cash.md): the fair share divides the home's shelter costs "by the number of people living in the household" (3.520.79.B.4, C.2), counted as the persons of the case who live in the home (lives_with, CO-1925), so a case evaluated for Adult Financial's in-kind support and maintenance lists every person who lives in the client's home as a person of the case, whether or not that person applies (docs/conventions.md rule 17, the case contract); a case that leaves a housemate out overstates the fair share. KL-CASH-1 (docs/reviews/known-limits.md, 2026-11-24): the divisor is now the neutral case fact persons_living_in_home_count (CO-7911), the number of people living in the home whether or not each is a person of the case, required where the computation reaches the fair share (decision 4 of 2026-11-23) and read nowhere else in this item; the case contract above is withdrawn for this item, and lives_with is no longer read here. A client who pays $200 of a $1,000 market-value home shared with three people who do not apply, $50 of her share paid by others, has a fair share of 1,000 / 4 = 250 and ISM min(250, 351) - 200 = $50; counted over the persons of the case alone (one), the fair share was $1,000 and the ISM min(1,000, 351) - 200 = $151.

Type money, scope person-month, program AdultFinancial.
Uses: `af_is_homeless`, `af_ism_maximum`, `holdings`, `home_shelter_costs_are_market_value`, `home_total_shelter_costs`, `lives_in_subsidized_housing`, `persons_living_in_home_count`, `receives_ssi`, `shelter_cost_monthly`, `shelter_costs_paid_by_others`, `ssa_in_kind_support_and_maintenance_charged`.

```
if all of the following are true:
    - Receives Supplemental Security Income
    - ISM charged by the Social Security Administration is more than 0
  then ISM charged by the Social Security Administration
else if Shelter costs others pay for the person is equal to 0
  then 0
else if any of the following is true:
    - (the sum of 1 for each holding in Holdings where ((all of the following are true:;   - all of the following are true:;     - that holding is valued in the month;     - that holding's disposed date is unknown;   - that holding's kind is equal to home;   - that holding's lives in))) is more than 0
    - Lives in subsidized housing
    - Adult Financial: homeless
  then 0
else if Shelter cost, monthly is at least Adult Financial maximum in-kind support and maintenance amount
  then 0
else if Shelter cost, monthly is at most 0

else if it is not the case that Shelter costs of the home are market value

### CO-1513 Adult Financial maximum in-kind support and maintenance amount `@engine`

The maximum monthly In-Kind Support and Maintenance (ISM) amount for shelter costs that OAP and AND-CS count as unearned income for a client not paying a fair share of shelter costs, per 9 CCR 2503-5 3.520.79, 3.530.B and 3.546.D: the current SSI benefit standard (ssi_federal_benefit_rate_individual, CO-235) times af_ism_benefit_standard_rate, plus af_ism_disregard, rounded to the nearest whole dollar (3.520.79.E.2).

Precision. The SSI benefit standard is 3.510's "maximum monthly Federal amount for a SSI recipient" (S448), the individual federal benefit rate, read in the month evaluated ("current"; docs/operators.md, Resolution), so each January's SSI rate gives that year's maximum with no further figure to load. A half rounds up (round). The rule also states each year's figure (3.530.B): 2025, $342 (967 x 0.3333 + 20 = 342.30, S1020); 2026, $351 (994 x 0.3333 + 20 = 351.30, S700); both come out of the formula and are its tests. 2027: 1,029 x 0.3333 + 20 = 362.97, $363 (S1712). Time audit T-2: this was a parameter carrying the stated figures, whose open 2026 version answered 2027 with $351.

Type money, scope person-month, program AdultFinancial.
Uses: `af_ism_benefit_standard_rate`, `af_ism_disregard`, `ssi_federal_benefit_rate_individual`.

```
(SSI federal benefit rate, individual (1029) times Adult Financial maximum ISM, share of the SSI benefit standard (0.3333)) plus Adult Financial maximum ISM, disregard added (20) rounded to the nearest whole dollar
```

["round",["+",["*","ssi_federal_benefit_rate_individual","af_ism_benefit_standard_rate"],"af_ism_disregard"]]
```

### CO-1647 Colorado Works: ssn verification is pending `@engine`

Whether Colorado Works requires verification of the person's Social Security number (or proof of application) and it has not been provided.

Precision. Only the client without an SSN or proof of application is ineligible, not the unit (3.604.3.B.2.c, K). At application a furnished number or proof of an application satisfies it (ssn_is_verified); at a redetermination the number itself must have been verified (ssn_verified_by_electronic_data_source), since a client who applied for an SSN at the initial determination must have it verified before the next recertification (3.604.3.B.2.c.1, S1630; phase-10 sweep, OQ-373). Coverage review CW-25: a proof of application "is only valid for up to eight (8) months without good cause" (B.2.c, S872); where the application is dated (ssn_application_date, CO-4838) and SSA has not verified a number, the proof no longer satisfies the requirement from the month after the eighth month from the month of the application (cw_ssn_application_proof_validity_months, CO-4840), unless the county finds good cause (cw_has_good_cause_for_pending_ssn_application, CO-4839, read as false when not stated); an application on January 10 is valid through September and pending from October. B.2.c.2's later deadline for a client added within sixty days of the period's end is not separately modeled. False where Colorado Works verification does not apply to the person (cw_verification_is_applicable, CO-2583; case worker review B2). Coverage pass 6 CA6-2: the kind of determination (cw_determination_is_redetermination, CO-2375) is required where verification applies (decision 4 of 2026-11-23); before, an unstated value was read as an application. Due by: cw_status_verification_due_date (CO-1656: thirty days; the member, not the unit, is excluded after it). A number SSA has verified (ssn_verified_by_electronic_data_source) satisfies both readings, so the kind of determination is read only for a number SSA has not verified.

Type yes/no, scope person-month, program ColoradoWorks.
Uses: `cw_determination_is_redetermination`, `cw_has_good_cause_for_pending_ssn_application`, `cw_ssn_application_proof_validity_months`, `cw_verification_is_applicable`, `ssn_application_date`, `ssn_is_verified`, `ssn_verified_by_electronic_data_source`.

### CO-1705 Colorado Works: self-employment business costs `@engine`

The person's cost of doing business for the month that 9 CCR 2503-6 3.605.2.E.1 allows (rent of business premises or the room used at home, wholesale cost of merchandise, utilities, interest, taxes, labor, upkeep of necessary equipment): the cost records the earnings table deducts (operating costs, interest and the home business space); for a licensed, certified or approved day care provider, $55 for the first child and $22 for each additional child unless documented costs are higher (E.1.b); not depreciation, payments on the principal of loans for capital assets, or personal expenses.

Precision. Earned-income records, step E1 Colorado Works (docs/reviews/records-earnings-cash.md): the earnings records (earnings, CO-5100) of a cost kind that cw_earnings_treatment_table (CO-5104) deducts, paid in the month, a farm's included (Colorado Works treats a farm as any other self-employment, 3.605.2.E.4.a); before earnings records each cost fact was read as 0 when not stated, and now an unstated earnings list is cannot determine (decision 4 of 2026-11-23). The costs of providing room or board are not these: they are deducted from the boarder payments (cw_boarder_income, CO-4361). Coverage pass 4 CA4-9 (docs/reviews/coverage4-cash.md): a stream (an earnings record with no month and no date) is read only in the months from the month of its job_start_date through the month of its job_end_date, so the pay of a job that ended before the month, or begins after it, is not counted (9 CCR 2503-5 3.520.781.G, 9 CCR 2503-6 3.605.2.B: income counted when received); a record stated with its month or date is read in that month. Coverage pass 4 CA4-16: the count of children a licensed child care provider cares for is required of a person with business receipts in the month (a self-employed person who is not a child care provider states 0); a person with none has only the cost records' own sum, never read as 0 when not stated (decision 4 of 2026-11-23: missing information is cannot determine unless the rule says otherwise).

Type money, scope person-month, program ColoradoWorks.
Uses: `cw_child_care_provider_cost_each_additional_child`, `cw_child_care_provider_cost_first_child`, `cw_earnings_treatment_table`, `earnings`, `licensed_child_care_children_in_care_count`.

```
if (the sum of that receipt's amount for each receipt in Earnings where ((all of the following are true:;   - all of the following are true:;     - Colorado Works: how each kind of earnings is treated (table), for that receipt's kind is equal to counted_net_of_costs;     - that receipt is received in the month;   - any of the following is true:;     - it is not the case that that receipt's month is unknown;     - all of the following are true:;       - any of the following is true:;         - that receipt's job start date is unknown;         - the month containing that receipt's job start date is at most the month;       - any of the following is true:;         - that receipt's job end date is unknown;         - the month containing that receipt's job end date is at least the month))) is at most 0
  then the sum of that receipt's amount for each receipt in Earnings where ((all of the following are true:;   - all of the following are true:;     - Colorado Works: how each kind of earnings is treated (table), for that receipt's kind is equal to deducted;     - that receipt is received in the month;   - any of the following is true:;     - it is not the case that that receipt's month is unknown;     - all of the following are true:;       - any of the following is true:;         - that receipt's job start date is unknown;         - the month containing that receipt's job start date is at most the month;       - any of the following is true:;         - that receipt's job end date is unknown;         - the month containing that receipt's job end date is at least the month))
else if Children in care of a licensed child care provider is more than 0
  then the greater of (the sum of that receipt's amount for each receipt in Earnings where ((all of the following are true:;   - all of the following are true:;     - Colorado Works: how each kind of earnings is treated (table), for that receipt's kind is equal to deducted;     - that receipt is received in the month;   - any of the following is true:;     - it is not the case that that receipt's month is unknown;     - all of the following are true:;       - any of the following is true:;         - that receipt's job start date is unknown;         - the month containing that receipt's job start date is at most the month;       - any of the following is true:;         - that receipt's job end date is unknown;         - the month containing that receipt's job end date is at least the month))) and (Colorado Works: licensed child care provider cost, first child (55) plus (Colorado Works: licensed child care provider cost, each additional child (22) times (Children in care of a licensed child care provider minus 1)))
otherwise the sum of that receipt's amount for each receipt in Earnings where ((all of the following are true:;   - all of the following are true:;     - Colorado Works: how each kind of earnings is treated (table), for that receipt's kind is equal to deducted;     - that receipt is received in the month;   - any of the following is true:;     - it is not the case that that receipt's month is unknown;     - all of the following are true:;       - any of the following is true:;         - that receipt's job start date is unknown;         - the month containing that receipt's job start date is at most the month;       - any of the following is true:;         - that receipt's job end date is unknown;         - the month containing that receipt's job end date is at least the month))

### CO-1706 Colorado Works: net profit from self-employment `@engine`

The person's net profit from self-employment for the month under 9 CCR 2503-6 3.605.2.E.1: gross receipts (of a business, or of a farm, counted in the month received, E.4.a) less the cost of doing business, not below zero; 3.605.2.E.1.c treats it as earned income. Self-employment income whose receipt is irregular (a business receipts record marked irregular in the twelve months ending with the month) is averaged over those twelve months (3.605.2.E.3): the receipts less the costs of the twelve months, divided by cw_irregular_self_employment_averaging_months, not below zero.

Precision. Earned-income records, step E1 Colorado Works (docs/reviews/records-earnings-cash.md): the receipts are the earnings records the table counts net of costs (self_employment_receipts and farm_self_employment_receipts; cw_earnings_treatment_table CO-5104: counted_net_of_costs) received in the month; a person with no such receipts has none, whatever the cost records say. Boarder payments are cw_boarder_income (CO-4361). An unstated earnings list is cannot determine (decision 4 of 2026-11-23). Coverage pass 4 CA4-9 (docs/reviews/coverage4-cash.md): a stream (an earnings record with no month and no date) is read only in the months from the month of its job_start_date through the month of its job_end_date, so the pay of a job that ended before the month, or begins after it, is not counted (9 CCR 2503-5 3.520.781.G, 9 CCR 2503-6 3.605.2.B: income counted when received); a record stated with its month or date is read in that month. Field sweep fix round (FS-CW-5): 3.605.2.E.2-3 (S4913): "All self-employment income that is received regularly shall be considered income in the month it is received"; "If receipt of self-employment income is irregular or varies significantly from month to month, it shall be averaged over a twelve-month period." Before, a business receipts record marked irregular was counted whole in its month (the precision said irregular income was stated already averaged, which a neutral record does not do). The period: the text names none; the twelve months ending with the month evaluated is OQ-1335's assumption (a state policy choice; Adult Financial's 3.520.783.F names two retrospective periods). The income averaged is the net profit (E.1.c): every counted business receipt of the period less the costs cw_self_employment_business_costs (CO-1705) gives each month, a person with a regular business beside an irregular one having both averaged. "Varies significantly from month to month" has no field and no measure in the text: recorded in OQ-1335, a business whose receipts so vary is stated irregular meanwhile.

### CO-1707 Adult Financial: self-employment business costs `@engine`

The person's cost of doing business for the month, other than a farm's, that 9 CCR 2503-5 3.520.783.B allows (rent of business premises, wholesale cost of merchandise, utilities, interest, taxes, labor, upkeep of necessary equipment): the cost records the earnings table deducts (operating costs and interest); not depreciation, payments on the principal of loans for capital assets, or personal expenses.

Precision. Earned-income records, step E1 Adult Financial (docs/reviews/records-earnings-cash.md): the earnings records (earnings, CO-5100) of a cost kind that af_earnings_treatment_table (CO-5103) deducts, paid in the month, that are not a farm's (farm: a farm's costs are read by af_self_employment_net_profit, CO-1708, with the farm's receipts over the prior year); before earnings records each cost fact was read as 0 when not stated, and now an unstated earnings list is cannot determine (decision 4 of 2026-11-23). Coverage review 2 (first-pass P2-2): for a licensed child care provider (licensed_child_care_children_in_care_count above 0) the cost is af_child_care_provider_cost_first_child for the first child and af_child_care_provider_cost_each_additional_child for each other child, or the documented costs when they are greater (3.520.783.C.3.a-d, S3505). Coverage pass 4 CA4-9 (docs/reviews/coverage4-cash.md): a stream (an earnings record with no month and no date) is read only in the months from the month of its job_start_date through the month of its job_end_date, so the pay of a job that ended before the month, or begins after it, is not counted (9 CCR 2503-5 3.520.781.G, 9 CCR 2503-6 3.605.2.B: income counted when received); a record stated with its month or date is read in that month. Coverage pass 4 CA4-16: the count of children a licensed child care provider cares for is required of a person with business receipts in the month (a self-employed person who is not a child care provider states 0); a person with none has only the cost records' own sum, never read as 0 when not stated (decision 4 of 2026-11-23: missing information is cannot determine unless the rule says otherwise).

### CO-1708 Adult Financial: net profit from self-employment `@engine`

The person's net profit from self-employment for the month under 9 CCR 2503-5 3.520.783: for a business other than a farm, its gross receipts in the month less the cost of doing business (af_self_employment_business_costs), not below zero (B, D); plus, for a farm, the net income of the prior calendar year averaged over af_farm_income_averaging_months (C.1), not below zero, and nothing once the person has ceased to farm. Self-employment income other than a farm's whose receipt is irregular is averaged over a twelve-month period (3.520.783.F): the previous tax year or the twelve months before the month of application, as af_self_employment_averaging_period states, the receipts less the costs of those months divided by af_irregular_self_employment_averaging_months, not below zero, in place of the month's own.

Precision. Earned-income records, step E1 Adult Financial (docs/reviews/records-earnings-cash.md): the business's receipts are the earnings records the table counts net of costs (self_employment_receipts, af_earnings_treatment_table CO-5103: counted_net_of_costs) received in the month; a person with no such receipts has none, whatever the cost records say. A farm's receipts are the records the table averages over the year (farm_self_employment_receipts: counted_averaged_over_year) and its costs the deducted cost records marked farm, each month of the prior calendar year (January to December before the month's year) netted and the twelve summed, the same for every month of the year (C.1, S3505); the person has ceased to farm when a farm receipts record states a job_end_date before the month. Before earnings records a person was either farming (self_employment_is_farming, CO-3720) or not, and a farmer's other business was read as the farm; each business is now its own record, so a farmer with a shop has both. Rental and board income (C.2): rent from property the person manages is stated as the business's receipts as the case figures it; board, room, and room and board payments are af_boarder_income (CO-5131). The three-month proration of 3.520.781.G.2.c is stated in the supplied amounts. An unstated earnings list is cannot determine (decision 4 of 2026-11-23). Coverage pass 4 CA4-9 (docs/reviews/coverage4-cash.md): a stream (an earnings record with no month and no date) is read only in the months from the month of its job_start_date through the month of its job_end_date, so the pay of a job that ended before the month, or begins after it, is not counted (9 CCR 2503-5 3.520.781.G, 9 CCR 2503-6 3.605.2.B: income counted when received); a record stated with its month or date is read in that month. Field sweep fix round (FS-AF-3): 3.520.783.F (S4914): "All self-employment income shall be considered income in the month received. If receipt of self-employment income is irregular, it shall be averaged over a twelve-month period. The twelve-month period can either be the previous tax year (January to December) or the most recent twelve-months prior to the application date." Before, irregular was read only for the $60 quarter (3.520.786.O) and a business receipts record marked irregular was counted whole in its month. A person's self-employment income is irregular in a month when a business receipts record (self_employment_receipts) marked irregular is received in the month or in the period; the period is read (af_self_employment_averaging_period, CO-7102, required there) only for a person with such a record. Both periods are retrospective, so in the month evaluated the average of the period replaces the month's own receipts, which are averaged in a later period; the income averaged is the net profit, every counted business receipt of the period less af_self_employment_business_costs (CO-1707) in each month. Who chooses between the two periods is OQ-1336. A farm is averaged over the prior calendar year by C.1, as before.

### CO-1716 Colorado Works: gross earned income `@engine`

This person's gross earned income for the month for Colorado Works: the pay the earnings table counts (cw_earned_pay: wages and the other pay no paragraph exempts, pay diverted to a third party for the household, in-kind pay at its value, 9 CCR 2503-6 3.605.2.A, B.1, D.1, G), plus the net profit from self-employment, which 3.605.2.E.1.c treats as earned income (3.605.2.D), plus room and board, board-only and room-only payments beyond the one-person Food Assistance allotment per boarder (none for a room only) and the documented costs (3.605.2.E.4.c-e; cw_boarder_income, CO-4361), less the earned income 3.605 does not consider by a property of the pay or of the person (cw_excluded_earned_income: a temporary job's pay, 3.605.2.C; a dependent student's earnings, 3.605.4.B.24.b), never below zero. Coverage review CW-9(c), CW-10, coverage pass 3 CW3-1 (S3159).

Precision. Earned-income records, step E1 Colorado Works (docs/reviews/records-earnings-cash.md): read from the earnings records (earnings, CO-5100) through cw_earnings_treatment_table (CO-5104), replacing wages_gross, in_kind_compensation_value and the parts of wages_gross cw_excluded_earned_income subtracted: a kind the table excludes (work-study, 3.605.4.A.24.a; WIOA on-the-job training and other subsidized employment, B.35, B.16) is never counted, so it is not subtracted either. The same for a member of the unit and every person whose income is deemed to it (the stepparent and minor parent's parent deeming, the sponsor, a disqualified member: cw_budgetary_member_deemed_income and its siblings read this figure). An unstated earnings list is cannot determine (product-owner decision 4 of 2026-11-23); a stated empty list is no earned income.

Type money, scope person-month, program ColoradoWorks.
Uses: `cw_boarder_income`, `cw_earned_pay`, `cw_excluded_earned_income`, `cw_self_employment_net_profit`.

the greater of 0 and ((Colorado Works: pay received in the month plus Colorado Works: net profit from self-employment plus Colorado Works: room, board, and room and board income) minus Colorado Works: excluded earned income)

### CO-2000 Colorado Works: needs deducted in minor-parent deeming `@engine`

For an unmarried minor parent, the needs deducted from her non-participant parents' countable income before it is deemed to her assistance unit under 9 CCR 2503-6 3.605.1.A.4.a: the needs of the parent or parents living in the home and of the individuals in the home for whom they are responsible, measured as the Colorado Works need standard in force in the month evaluated for a unit of those parents and the parents' other children in the home - the One Caretaker row for one parent, the Two Caretakers row for two, keyed by the number of other children.

Precision. Coverage pass 2 (CW2-2): the parents are the ones whose income is deemed, cw_minor_parent_deemed_parents (CO-4660): her parents who are not members of her assistance unit and live in the same home (S3155); a parent living elsewhere, or one who joined her unit (3.604.2.C.2.g), is neither deemed nor counted here, so one such parent takes the One Caretaker row. The individuals they are responsible for are this person's siblings and half siblings (P43, shared parent) who are the child of one of those parents (has_relative_in), live in the same home (lives_with, read as living together where no dwelling is stated; cw_is_considered_living_in_home, CO-3354) and are not members of her assistance unit, whose needs it meets; this person herself is excluded, and her own child is not her parent's child. A stepparent of the minor parent, or another person a parent supports, is not counted. Above ten children the chart's each-additional amount is added. Same-word audit SW-2: the siblings are siblings (CO-2609), the persons who share a legal parent. Pattern sweep (cash) PS-D2 (docs/reviews/pattern-sweep-cash.md): whether persons live together is read from lives_with as stated (dwelling_id), required where read (decision 4 of 2026-11-23; docs/conventions.md rule 17 as amended for Colorado Works and Adult Financial): no text on file says the persons of one application live together (9 CCR 2503-6 3.604.2.A, E, I build the unit from the persons living in the home; 9 CCR 2503-5 3.534.B.3 and 3.549.E name the household of the spouse and the parents in the home). Before, a person whose home was not stated was read as living with every related person of the case. CASH-SW-1 closed (2026-11-24; docs/reviews/known-limits.md, the candidate of the cash pattern sweep's extended run): per month. The need standard of 3.606.1.F (S414) is versioned by State fiscal year from July 1 (cw_need_standard_table CO-274, cw_need_standard_table_two_caretakers CO-353, cw_need_standard_each_additional CO-275; C.R.S. 26-2-709(1)(b), S1800), and 3.605.1.B (S4911) uses the income 'received, or ... expect[ed] to receive in the application month and any month following' to determine eligibility, month by month; the deeming of 3.605.1.A.4 is part of each month's countable income (cw_deemed_parent_income_of_minor_parent, CO-909, per month), so the needs it deducts are measured by the standard of that month, as the unit's own need standard is (cw_need_standard, CO-911, per month: docs/operators.md, Resolution step 2, the version in force on the first day of a month other than the determination month). Before, the item was per person and read the standard in force on the determination date in every month, so an application month in June determined in July read the new fiscal year's figures; the figures of July 2025 and July 2026 are the same (SB 26-181, S1800: no cost-of-living adjustment for the fiscal years 2026-27 and 2027-28), so the reading moves an answer only across a July whose figures differ or are not yet loaded (OQ-530): a June 2028 application month determined in July 2028 now reads the June figure (CO-2000-T6), where it read the July 2028 chart, not yet published. The same pattern as the non-MAGI fix to the MMMNA standard and the personal needs allowance (coverage pass 7, non-MAGI F7-1, F7-2; CO-662, CO-1987).

Type money, scope person-month, program ColoradoWorks.
Uses: `cw_assistance_unit_members`, `cw_is_considered_living_in_home`, `cw_minor_parent_deemed_parents`, `cw_need_standard_each_additional`, `cw_need_standard_table`, `cw_need_standard_table_two_caretakers`, `lives_with`, `relationships`, `siblings`.

if (the number of persons in Colorado Works: a minor parent's non-participant parents in the home) is at least 2
  then Colorado Works need standard by number of children (two caretakers) (table), for (the number of persons in all persons in Siblings such that (all of the following are true:;   - that person is a child of a person in Colorado Works: a minor parent's non-participant parents in the home;   - it is not the case that that person is in Colorado Works: assistance unit members;   - that person is in Lives with;   - that person's Colorado Works: considered living in the home)), adding Colorado Works need standard, each additional child (one caretaker) (67) for each beyond its last row

### CO-2340 Colorado Works: excluded earned income `@engine`

The part of this person's counted earned income for the month that 9 CCR 2503-6 does not consider by a property of the person or of the pay rather than by its kind: all of a dependent child student's earned income (3.605.4.B.24.b, cw_student_earnings_are_disregarded: the counted pay, the net profit from self-employment and boarder income); otherwise the pay from short-term employment of ninety days or less (temporary_job) unless the client was terminated or terminated the employment through the client's own fault (3.605.2.C). College work-study (B.24.a) and wages from subsidized employment, WIOA on-the-job training included (B.35, B.16, 3.605.2.C), are exempt by kind: cw_earnings_treatment_table (CO-5104) never counts them.

Precision. Earned-income records, step E1 Colorado Works (docs/reviews/records-earnings-cash.md): before earnings records this item summed the parts of wages_gross the rule leaves out (work_study_earnings, subsidized_employment_wages, short_term_employment_wages, each read as 0 when not stated) so cw_gross_earned_income (CO-1716) could subtract them; the kinds are now never counted, and what is left here is the temporary job and the student. A temporary job's pay is the earnings records received in the month that the table counts as pay and that state temporary_job: it is not considered when the record states that the job did not end through the client's fault (ended_through_own_fault false), or states neither that fault nor a job_end_date (the job has not ended, so the client has not been terminated); a record that states the job ended (job_end_date) and not whether through the client's fault cannot determine, since 3.605.2.C turns on it. A student's earnings include in-kind pay and boarder income (B.24.b: "All earned income"; coverage review CW-9(c) read in-kind pay; boarder income, which E.4 makes earned income, is added in step E1). A person with no counted earned income has nothing excluded, and whether the person is a disregarded student is not read; for a person with earned income it is read with no default (before earnings records cw_gross_earned_income read this item as 0 when it was unknown, so a child whose student status was not stated had all earnings counted; 3.605.4.B.24.b turns on it, decision 4 of 2026-11-23). An unstated earnings list is cannot determine. Coverage pass 4 CA4-9 (docs/reviews/coverage4-cash.md): a stream (an earnings record with no month and no date) is read only in the months from the month of its job_start_date through the month of its job_end_date, so the pay of a job that ended before the month, or begins after it, is not counted (9 CCR 2503-5 3.520.781.G, 9 CCR 2503-6 3.605.2.B: income counted when received); a record stated with its month or date is read in that month. Coverage pass 4 CA4-7: a difficulty of care payment stated as foster care (foster_care) is not counted pay. Field sweep fix round (FS-CW-4): 3.605.2.B (S4912): wages are "considered available when paid rather than when earned, except that wages held at the request of the employee are considered income in the month they would otherwise have been paid". A pay that states its regular_date and that the employer held at the person's request (regular_date_reason held_at_request, a neutral field of the earnings record) is read in the month of its regular_date; a pay that came early or late for any other reason (a holiday or a weekend, changed pay dates) is read in the month it was paid, so regular_date_reason is required where regular_date is stated (decision 4). Before, every pay was read in the month it came in, so held wages fell into the next month. The contract employment the paragraph excepts is OQ-1295.

Type money, scope person-month, program ColoradoWorks.
Uses: `cw_boarder_income`, `cw_earned_pay`, `cw_earnings_treatment_table`, `cw_self_employment_net_profit`, `cw_student_earnings_are_disregarded`, `earnings`.

```
if (Colorado Works: pay received in the month plus Colorado Works: net profit from self-employment plus Colorado Works: room, board, and room and board income) is at most 0
  then 0
else if Colorado Works: student's earnings disregarded

### CO-2342 Adult Financial: excluded earned income `@engine`

The part of this person's counted earned income for the month that 9 CCR 2503-5 3.520.786 exempts by a field of the pay rather than by its kind: the part of a counted pay, business or boarder payment set aside under a Plan to Achieve Self Support the SSA approved (I), and infrequent or irregular pay O exempts (af_excluded_infrequent_earned_income, final cash review 2, P2-3). Work-study (H) and 37 U.S.C. 310 special pay (K) are exempt by kind: af_earnings_treatment_table (CO-5103) never counts them.

Precision. Earned-income records, step E1 Adult Financial (docs/reviews/records-earnings-cash.md): the PASS set-aside is the earnings records' pass_set_aside (default 0) on the records received in the month that the table counts (pay, a business's receipts, a farm's, boarder payments); before earnings records Adult Financial did not read pass_set_aside_earned_income, so a PASS of wages was counted although I exempts "Income and resources set aside as part of a PASS", earned or unearned (3.520.786: "Certain earned and unearned income ... is exempt"). Work-study is no longer summed here: the table excludes it, so af_gross_earned_income (CO-3830) never adds it. An irregular pay with a PASS set-aside is exempt once (af_excluded_infrequent_earned_income takes the pay less its set-aside). An unstated earnings list is cannot determine. Coverage pass 4 CA4-9 (docs/reviews/coverage4-cash.md): a stream (an earnings record with no month and no date) is read only in the months from the month of its job_start_date through the month of its job_end_date, so the pay of a job that ended before the month, or begins after it, is not counted (9 CCR 2503-5 3.520.781.G, 9 CCR 2503-6 3.605.2.B: income counted when received); a record stated with its month or date is read in that month. Coverage pass 4 CA4-7: a difficulty of care payment stated as foster care (foster_care) is not counted pay.

### CO-2349 Colorado Works: is an optional assistance-unit member `@engine`

This person, living in the home, is an optional member of the assistance unit under 9 CCR 2503-6 3.604.2.C.2: a non-parent caretaker of a dependent child who is not also a parent of a dependent child in the home (C.2.b); the spouse of a parent or of a non-parent caretaker of a dependent child, who is not a parent or caretaker of a dependent child in the home and whose spouse is not pregnant (C.2.a, c; the spouse of a pregnant parent is mandatory, C.1.e); or a member made optional by custody or child support (C.2.d-f, cw_is_optional_member_by_custody_or_support).

Precision. Coverage pass 6 CA6-3, CA6-7 (docs/reviews/coverage6-cash.md): the spouse's pregnancy is one in some month the determination covers (cw_is_pregnant_in_determination, CO-7302), required where read (decision 4 of 2026-11-23); before, a pregnancy left unstated was read as no pregnancy, so the spouse of a pregnant parent (mandatory, 3.604.2.C.1.e) became optional. The parent of a minor parent requesting assistance for her own child (C.2.g) is optional too; cw_assistance_unit_members (CO-900) reaches that parent only when the parent requests inclusion, so this item need not name it. Same-word audit SW-3/SW-4 (OQ-396): the caretaker relation is cw_caretaker_of (CO-2608): a parent, or a non-parent caretaker who is the child's legal guardian or has primary responsibility for the child (3.601); the spouse of a parent who is not a parent stays the optional member of 3.604.2.C.2.a, read from the spouse and parent roles as the rule words it. Duplicate-paths audit D-W1 (P1, fixed 2026-11-23, docs/reviews/records-earnings-cash.md): the non-parent caretaker of C.2.b is read from Colorado Works' caretaker definition (cw_caretaker_of, CO-2608, as cw_has_dependent_child, CO-902, reads it): a person who is the caretaker of a dependent child in the home who is not the person's own child, and not the parent of any dependent child in the home (a parent who cares only for the parent's own children is never asked whether they are dependent children here); before, it was read from the raw legal_guardian and has_primary_responsibility_for roles, so an unrelated adult with primary responsibility for a child whose parent is in the home (not a caretaker under 3.601 and 3.604.2.H) was made an optional member, and a guardian whose ward lives elsewhere too. Coverage pass 6 CA6-7: an optional member by custody (C.2.e, a sibling of a dependent child, so a dependent child) or a parent without custody (C.2.f, a parent of a dependent child) is read only for a person who is a dependent child or has one, and is required there (decision 4 of 2026-11-23); before, read as false when not stated.

### CO-2351 Colorado Works: assistance unit members counted for size `@engine`

The members of this person's assistance unit in the month (cw_assistance_unit_members_in_month, CO-7304) counted for its size: every member except one who is disqualified from or ineligible for basic cash assistance (cw_is_disqualified_member), whom 9 CCR 2503-6 3.604.2.M removes "from the assistance unit for the purposes of determining the assistance unit size", one who is an institution patient for tuberculosis or mental disease or an inmate (cw_is_institution_patient_or_inmate, CO-3802), whom 3.604.1.D-E bar as a client, one who has been temporarily out of State for more than ninety consecutive days (3.604.2.O.1), and one who has not provided a verification of citizenship, qualified non-citizen status, lawful presence, identity or SSN within the thirty days of 3.604.3.K (cw_is_excluded_for_unprovided_status_verification, CO-4372), who "will not receive payment for themselves".

Precision. Final cash review FC-1: a member barred by 3.604.1.D-E while still in the home under the absence rules is not paid for; the member's income still counts as a member's (OQ-660). Final cash review 2, P2-7: a member temporarily out of State for more than cw_temporary_out_of_state_max_days consecutive days (3.604.2.O.1; the same test as cw_meets_residency, CO-904) is an ineligible member and is removed from the size as M requires; a member with no out-of-State date stated stays in it. Coverage review CW-12: cw_verification_status (CO-1427) reported members_excluded once status or SSN verification was past the thirty days, but the size still counted those members; they are now left out, and their income still counts as a member's, as 3.604.3.K's last paragraph (S1064) says. Time audit T-6: "N consecutive days" is counted as the days elapsed since the day the absence or stay began (days_between), the day of departure or entry itself not counted (OQ-953): "shall not exceed ninety (90) consecutive days" (3.604.2.O, S2602), as cw_meets_residency (CO-904) reads it: out of the unit's size once the days elapsed since the day of departure are more than cw_temporary_out_of_state_max_days. Coverage pass 6 CA6-4, CA6-5 (docs/reviews/coverage6-cash.md, probes W3, W7): per month, from the month's members, so a child who is no dependent child of the month, one not yet born and one who died before the month are not counted (the size was one per case, from a dependent child in some month). Pattern sweep (cash) PS-T8 (docs/reviews/pattern-sweep-cash.md): the days out of State are counted to cw_month_reading_date (CO-7600), so a member away more than ninety days only after the application month is in the application month's size.

### CO-2353 Colorado Works: deemed income of a budgetary-unit member outside the assistance unit `@engine`

The income of this person, a budgetary-unit member outside the assistance unit, counted toward the unit: for a stepparent (the spouse of a parent of a dependent child in the home), the 3.605.1.A.4.a countable income - gross earned income less the cw_earned_income_disregard_dollar employment disregard, plus unearned income, less court-ordered support paid outside the unit and payments to tax dependents outside the home, less the needs of the stepparent and of the stepparent's children in the home who are outside the assistance unit (the One Caretaker need standard for that number of children), never below zero; for the spouse of a non-parent caretaker, whom A.4.a does not name, the earned income after the disregard plus unearned income of 3.606.1.J.

Precision. Coverage review CW-20: the maintenance paid to others outside the unit (spousal_maintenance_paid, CO-4354, read as 0 when not stated) is deducted beside child support paid, as 3.605.1.A.4.a (S3155) says. The needs deduction mirrors cw_minor_parent_deeming_needs_deduction (CO-2000): "needs" read as the need standard (OQ-102). The stepparent's children who are in the assistance unit are not counted, since the unit's own standard meets their needs. Coverage pass 2 (P3-2): 3.605.1.A.4.a deducts the needs of "individuals living in the home", so only his excluded children who live in the same home (lives_with, read as living together where no dwelling is stated; cw_is_considered_living_in_home, CO-3354) are counted, as in CO-2000. Coverage pass 4 CA4-16: the spousal maintenance and the support paid to tax dependents outside the home that 3.605.1.A.4 deducts are required where read (a deemed person who pays none states 0), never read as 0 when not stated (decision 4 of 2026-11-23: missing information is cannot determine unless the rule says otherwise). Pattern sweep (cash) PS-M4 (docs/reviews/pattern-sweep-cash.md): the stepparent's own children counted for the need standard are those born by the month's last day and alive on its first, each in the home in the month (cw_is_considered_living_in_home_in_month, CO-7602); before, a child born after the month, or one who had died, was counted. Pattern sweep (cash) PS-D2 (docs/reviews/pattern-sweep-cash.md): whether persons live together is read from lives_with as stated (dwelling_id), required where read (decision 4 of 2026-11-23; docs/conventions.md rule 17 as amended for Colorado Works and Adult Financial): no text on file says the persons of one application live together (9 CCR 2503-6 3.604.2.A, E, I build the unit from the persons living in the home; 9 CCR 2503-5 3.534.B.3 and 3.549.E name the household of the spouse and the parents in the home). Before, a person whose home was not stated was read as living with every related person of the case.

### CO-2364 Colorado Works: sponsor deeming applies `@engine`

The net income of this non-citizen's sponsor and the sponsor's spouse is deemed to the assistance unit for the month (9 CCR 2503-6 3.605.1.A.5): the person is a lawful permanent resident sponsored on an affidavit of support (Form I-864, is_sponsored_non_citizen), and none of the exemptions of A.5.c applies - the person did not adjust to permanent residence from refugee or asylee status, is not a victim of battery or extreme cruelty, has fewer than federal_qualifying_quarters_threshold qualifying quarters, has not rebutted the availability of the sponsor's income (A.5.b), and the combined monthly income of the person, the person's spouse, the sponsor and a co-sponsor spouse is at least cw_sponsor_deeming_fpl_pct of the monthly federal poverty guideline for the combined household size.

Precision. The monthly guideline is the annual cw_poverty_guideline_annual_table (CO-4350) figure, the 2021 guideline that 3.601 adopts with no later editions (S3150; coverage review CW-4, which replaced the current federal_poverty_guideline_annual_table), for the combined size (cw_sponsor_deeming_household_size, CO-2360) divided by twelve. Each person's income is gross earned income and unearned income after Colorado Works' exclusions (cw_gross_earned_income, cw_countable_unearned_income), read from the person's own facts: the non-citizen, the non-citizen's spouse, and each sponsor (sponsors, CO-2713, the co-sponsor spouse included, "the sponsor's spouse (who is also a sponsor)"). A citizen or a non-LPR is out at the first test, so no sponsor fact is needed. Coverage pass 6 CA6-7 (docs/reviews/coverage6-cash.md): a sponsored lawful permanent resident's status before the adjustment and whether she is a victim of battery or extreme cruelty, each an exemption from sponsor deeming, are required where read (decision 4 of 2026-11-23); before, read as none and false when not stated. The county's finding that the sponsor's income is not available is a finding and keeps its reading. Pattern sweep (cash) PS-M3 (docs/reviews/pattern-sweep-cash.md): the 125% test of c.5 needs the sponsor's income, stated on the sponsor as a person of the case (sponsors, CO-2713; the volume's sponsor role is declared whether or not the sponsor lives in the home); with no sponsor a person of the case it cannot be determined (decision 4); before, an absent sponsor's income was read as 0, so the total fell under 125% and nothing was deemed.

Type yes/no, scope person-month, program ColoradoWorks.
Uses: `cw_countable_unearned_income`, `cw_gross_earned_income`, `cw_poverty_guideline_annual_each_additional`, `cw_poverty_guideline_annual_table`, `cw_sponsor_deeming_fpl_pct`, `cw_sponsor_deeming_household_size`, `cw_sponsor_income_availability_rebutted`, `federal_qualifying_quarters_threshold`, `immigration_status`, `is_sponsored_non_citizen`, `is_victim_of_battery_or_extreme_cruelty`, `qualifying_quarters`, `relationships`, `sponsors`, `status_before_lpr_adjustment`.

### CO-2365 Colorado Works: sponsor income deemed `@engine`

The sponsor's net income deemed to this sponsored non-citizen as unearned income for the month (9 CCR 2503-6 3.605.1.A.5.b): the gross earned income of the sponsor and of the sponsor's spouse, each less twenty percent or $175, whichever is less, minus support paid to dependents not living in the sponsor's home, plus their unearned income, never below zero; zero when sponsor deeming does not apply.

Precision. The twenty percent or cw_sponsor_earned_income_deduction_cap is taken from each earner's earnings, since A.5.a deems "the net income of a non-citizen's sponsor and the sponsor's spouse". The earners are the sponsors (sponsors, CO-2713, a co-sponsor spouse included) and a sponsor's spouse who did not sign (sponsor_spouses_not_cosigning, CO-2714), each read from the person's own facts: Colorado Works' gross earned income (wages and self-employment net profit) and countable unearned income, and the support the person paid to dependents outside the home (support_paid_to_dependents_outside_home, CO-2359). Unlike SNAP (4.305.2.D.2.c), Colorado Works states no division among several sponsored non-citizens: each receives the whole amount. Coverage pass 6 CA6-7: the support a sponsor (or a sponsor's spouse) pays to dependents outside the home, which 3.605.1.A.5 deducts, is required where read (decision 4 of 2026-11-23); before, read as 0 when not stated.

Type money, scope person-month, program ColoradoWorks.
Uses: `cw_countable_unearned_income`, `cw_gross_earned_income`, `cw_sponsor_deeming_applies`, `cw_sponsor_earned_income_deduction_cap`, `cw_sponsor_earned_income_deduction_rate`, `sponsor_spouses_not_cosigning`, `sponsors`, `support_paid_to_dependents_outside_home`.

otherwise 0

### CO-2383 Colorado Works: is a parent of a dependent child in the home `@engine`

This person is the parent of a dependent child living in the home (9 CCR 2503-6 3.604.2.C.1.b), as distinct from a non-parent caretaker.

Precision. Coverage pass 4 CA4-24 (docs/reviews/coverage4-cash.md): the meaning's "living in the home" is tested, as the unit's own membership tests it (cw_assistance_unit_members, CO-900): the child lives with the person (lives_with, the household's stated co-residents; a household that names none is read as living together) and is considered living in the home (cw_is_considered_living_in_home, 3.604.1); before, a parent whose own minor child lives elsewhere was a parent of a dependent child, which made the caretaker's husband a stepparent (cw_budgetary_member_deemed_income, CO-2353) rather than the caretaker's spouse of 3.606.1.J. Pattern sweep (cash) PS-D2 (docs/reviews/pattern-sweep-cash.md): whether persons live together is read from lives_with as stated (dwelling_id), required where read (decision 4 of 2026-11-23; docs/conventions.md rule 17 as amended for Colorado Works and Adult Financial): no text on file says the persons of one application live together (9 CCR 2503-6 3.604.2.A, E, I build the unit from the persons living in the home; 9 CCR 2503-5 3.534.B.3 and 3.549.E name the household of the spouse and the parents in the home). Before, a person whose home was not stated was read as living with every related person of the case.

### CO-2384 Adult Financial: income deemed from a spouse or parent `@engine`

The income deemed to this Adult Financial client for the month from the client's spouse, wherever the spouse lives, and, for an AND-CS client who is an unemancipated child, from the parents in the home (9 CCR 2503-5 3.534.A-C, 3.544.D-F, 3.549.C-F): for each such relative, nothing if the relative receives Adult Financial grant payments, SSI or Medicaid and has income no greater than the OAP grant standard (for an OAP client) or the SSI benefit standard (otherwise); else af_earned_income_remainder_rate of the relative's gross earned income over af_earned_income_disregard, plus the relative's unearned income less, for an OAP client, the OAP grant standard, the needs of the relative's dependent children, medical payments for dependents and court-ordered support (3.534.B); for an AND-CS or AND-SO client, the part of the couple's $20 (af_general_income_disregard) the client has not used: the $20 less the client's own disregard applied to unearned income and, for AND-CS, rolled to earned income (3.549.D.2: "A couple shall be allowed a combined $20.00 disregard, which is split between the client and the spouse"; 3.544.E.2: "$20.00 unless the client also has unearned income", split so that no more than $20 is applied).

Precision. The program is read as af_countable_income reads it, without a cycle through af_category: OAP when af_is_oap_age, AND-CS when af_and_cs_eligible, AND-SO otherwise. A relative's income for the exemption is gross earned and unearned income, SSI included; earned income includes in-kind pay and donated work hours (3.520.782.B, 3.520.784, "client, client's spouse, or sponsor(s)"; coverage review F-10). Court-ordered support is child_support_paid_legally_obligated. The MMMNA deduction for an institutionalized spouse (3.534.C, 3.544.F, 3.549.F) is not modeled: an institutionalized spouse in this volume is assessed through the Medicaid post-eligibility items. The allowance the client retains is the client's own unearned income (3.520.785.B.24), stated in the client's other_unearned_income_nontaxable and counted by af_unearned_income_other_than_ssi (CO-3831; coverage review P2-6). Emancipation (3.549.E) is read from is_emancipated_minor (CO-843; same-word audit SW-16); a child under af_and_cs_unemancipated_child_age_limit (CO-3053) is read as unemancipated. The disregards are Adult Financial's own (af_earned_income_disregard, af_earned_income_remainder_rate, af_general_income_disregard; hard-coded numbers audit D-4). Same-word audit SW-7 (convention rule 17): an edge joins persons who live together (lives_with, CO-1925, from dwelling_id); where a case states no dwelling_id the edge is read as living together, as before. Coverage review F-3 (confirmed with the engine on probe PR-APART): the spouse is deemed wherever the spouse lives, as af_client_and_spouse_countable_resources (CO-2389) counts the spouse's resources: 3.534.A-B, 3.544.D-E and 3.549.C-D deem from "the client's spouse" with no living-together condition, 3.520.63.D (S3204) makes a client who is not legally separated or divorced married, and 3.534.B.3 speaks of "each dependent child living in the household of the spouse"; a legally separated spouse states no spouse edge. Parents are deemed to an AND-CS child only from the child's home (lives_with), as the SSI parent-deeming rule 3.549.E adopts. Final cash review FC-4: the client's own disregard is now the client's share of the $20 (af_client_general_income_disregard, CO-3829), so the relative's deduction is what the client leaves of the couple's $20 (af_general_income_disregard_applied_to_unearned and af_general_income_disregard_rolled_to_earned, CO-3832, CO-3833); before, an AND-CS client with earnings could roll the whole $20 to earnings while the spouse also deducted it, and an AND-SO client with any unearned income left the spouse nothing (OQ-661). Receipt records, migration phase 1: a relative's grant is af_grant_receipts is read from the receipts (CO-5000). Coverage pass 6 CA6-4, CA6-7 (docs/reviews/coverage6-cash.md): the AND-CS client's age for the parents' deeming (3.549.E, under 18) is taken on the first day of the month evaluated, as AND-CS's own upper limit is (docs/operators.md, "Ages in a month"; OQ-951), and the client's emancipation (is_emancipated_minor) is required where read (decision 4 of 2026-11-23); before, the determination date's age, and an unstated emancipation read as none. Coverage pass 6 CA6-7 (probe A2u): whether the relative is enrolled in Medicaid (read when the relative has no SSI or Adult Financial grant and income no greater than the standard, 3.534.C) and the medical payments for dependents an OAP spouse's deeming deducts (3.534.B) are required where read (decision 4 of 2026-11-23); before, read as false and 0, so the husband of a couple whose $800 of wages are under the OAP standard was deemed 367.5 to his wife ($189) when his enrollment was not stated, where enrolled he deems nothing ($442). Coverage pass 6 CA6-8: whether a spouse approved in the same determination is "receiving Adult Financial grant payments" (3.534.C) is OQ-1375; the assumption in force reads the grant receipts as stated (af_grant_receipts), so two spouses applying together each have the other's income deemed. Pattern sweep (cash) PS-M1 (docs/reviews/pattern-sweep-cash.md): the spouse is the spouse of the month (af_spouses_in_month, CO-7603) and an AND-CS child's parent counts only while alive on the month's first day, so a spouse or parent who died before the month has nothing deemed in it (3.520.63.A: widowed); before, the deceased's stated income went on being deemed. Pattern sweep (cash) PS-D2 (docs/reviews/pattern-sweep-cash.md): whether persons live together is read from lives_with as stated (dwelling_id), required where read (decision 4 of 2026-11-23; docs/conventions.md rule 17 as amended for Colorado Works and Adult Financial): no text on file says the persons of one application live together (9 CCR 2503-6 3.604.2.A, E, I build the unit from the persons living in the home; 9 CCR 2503-5 3.534.B.3 and 3.549.E name the household of the spouse and the parents in the home). Before, a person whose home was not stated was read as living with every related person of the case. Coverage pass 7, F7-2 (docs/reviews/coverage7-cash.md): a married client whose spouse is not a person of the case in the month (af_spouse_is_outside_case_in_month, CO-7690) cannot be determined here: the spouse's income are not stated (decision 4 of 2026-11-23), as for a sponsor outside the case (PS-M3) and the non-MAGI couple (F6-7, CO-643). Before, they were read as none.

### CO-2386 Adult Financial: income deemed from a sponsor `@engine`

The sponsor's income deemed to this non-citizen Adult Financial client as unearned income for the month (9 CCR 2503-5 3.534.D, 3.544.G, 3.549.G): the total gross earned and unearned income of the sponsor(s) less the SSI benefit standard for an individual for the sponsor, the standard (for a co-sponsor spouse) or af_sponsor_dependent_allowance_rate (CO-3051) of it (for another spouse in the sponsor's household), and that share for each of the sponsor's dependents, the children the sponsor(s) claim on income tax other than the client and the client's spouse (3.520.68.B.2.b.1, which D.2.C cross-refers to), never below zero; all of it is deemed to each non-citizen client the sponsor sponsors, without division; nothing is deemed once the sponsor's obligation has ended (af_sponsor_deeming_applies, 3.520.69.B-C).

Precision. A citizen or national has no sponsor deemed. is_sponsored_non_citizen (CO-1573) is a binding affidavit of support, which exists only for entries after the August 22, 1996 date 3.520.69 names. The SSI benefit standard of 3.510 is ssi_federal_benefit_rate_individual. The sponsor's earned income includes in-kind pay and donated work hours, as for the client (3.520.782.B, 3.520.784; coverage review F-10). The sponsors (sponsors, CO-2713, a co-sponsor spouse included, as "sponsor(s)" in D says) are persons of the case and their income is read from their own facts. The sponsor's dependents are the count stated on the sponsor (sponsor_dependent_count, CO-2387: the children the sponsor claims on income tax other than the persons the sponsor sponsors) plus the other non-citizens of the case the same sponsors sponsor who are a sponsor's tax dependent (tax_dependent edge), other than the client and the client's spouse. OQ-553 resolved (coverage review F-16): the current rule (D-80) cross-refers to 3.520.68.B.2.b.1, which it no longer has; the archived version 10320 (D-300, S3200), the text the cross-reference was written for, defines the sponsor's dependent children as "the children the sponsor(s) claim on his or her income tax", so another non-citizen the sponsor sponsors is a dependent only when the sponsor claims that person. Coverage pass 6 CA6-7 (docs/reviews/coverage6-cash.md): the sponsor's dependents, spouse in the household and co-sponsoring spouse (3.534.D.2) are required where read (decision 4 of 2026-11-23); before, read as 0, false and false when not stated. Pattern sweep (cash) PS-M2 and PS-M3 (docs/reviews/pattern-sweep-cash.md): the sponsors deemed are those living on the month's first day (af_sponsors_in_month, CO-7604; 3.520.69.B.5: the death of one sponsor does not end a joint sponsor's obligation), and a client to whom deeming applies whose sponsor is not a person of the case cannot be determined, the sponsor's income not being stated (decision 4; the volume's sponsor role is declared as a person of the case whether or not the sponsor lives in the home); before, a sponsor outside the case deemed nothing and a deceased sponsor's income went on being deemed. Pattern sweep (cash) PS-D11 (docs/reviews/pattern-sweep-cash.md): the sponsor's tax dependents and the client's spouse among them are read from the relationships stated, with no default (decision 4); before, unstated relationships were read as none. KL-CASH-3 (docs/reviews/known-limits.md, 2026-11-24): the client's spouse D.2.C leaves out of the sponsor's dependents includes the client's partner in a civil union (the civil_union_partner edge), "Marriage" in these rules including a civil union (3.510, S5321), as the client's spouse is read in the deeming and resources (af_spouses_in_month, CO-7603). The sponsor's own spouse (sponsor_spouse_is_cosponsor CO-2362, sponsor_has_spouse_in_household CO-2388, sponsor_spouses_not_cosigning CO-2714) is read through shared items other programs read too, and is unchanged (OQ-1501).
