### CO-2389 Adult Financial: countable resources of the client and spouse `@engine`

The countable resources of this Adult Financial client and the client's spouse, counted and exempted under 9 CCR 2503-5 3.520.72 to 3.520.77 (Adult Financial's own list and exemptions): the client's af_person_countable_resources, and the spouse's resources other than life insurance (af_person_countable_resources_other_than_life_insurance) with the spouse's life insurance counted under the client's program: the OAP rule of 3.520.75.E-F (af_life_insurance_countable_value_for_oap) for a client of OAP age, the whole cash surrender value over the face-value exemption (af_life_insurance_countable_value_other_than_oap) otherwise.

Precision. The spouse of the case wherever the spouse lives: 3.520.72.A counts the countable resources of 'the client, spouse, and sponsor(s)' and sets the married client's limit, with no living-together condition. Final cash review 2, N-1 (confirmed with the engine): the spouse's life insurance had been read under the spouse's own age, so an OAP client of 72 whose 55-year-old spouse owned a $10,000 policy bought in 2010 (cash value $5,000, no premiums in 48 months) had $5,000 counted and was over the $3,000 couple limit; 3.520.75.E exempts "all life insurance policies owned by a client and his or her spouse" for OAP, so the policy is now exempt whichever spouse owns it, and an AND client's spouse's policy is counted whatever the spouse's age. Resource records, step H1 Adult Financial (docs/reviews/records-holdings-snap-af.md): each person's resources are read from that person's own holdings records through the items above (CO-4000, CO-4001, CO-4002), so the client's, the spouse's and each sponsor's holdings are counted by the same rows (3.520.72.E: "in the same manner as the non-citizen client"). Coverage pass 4 CA4-10 (docs/reviews/coverage4-cash.md): each spouse's own resources leave out that spouse's largest transportation vehicle, so a married couple kept two exempt vehicles; the couple's figure adds back af_vehicle_exemption_shared_with_spouse (CO-6804), the smaller of the two, so one vehicle is exempt for the couple (3.520.77: "for an individual or married couple"; 77.A). Coverage pass 4 CA4-13 (docs/reviews/coverage4-cash.md): a figure of the month evaluated, from the holdings valued in that month (3.510 "Resources", S4791: "held as of the first day of a calendar month or as of the date of application"), so an application month before the determination month is judged by its own holdings; before, every month read the determination month's. Pattern sweep (cash) PS-M1 and PS-D4 (docs/reviews/pattern-sweep-cash.md): the spouse is the spouse of the month (af_spouses_in_month, CO-7603), so a spouse who died before the month is not counted in it (3.520.63.A: widowed), and a client whose relationships are not stated, in a case of more than one person, cannot be determined (decision 4); before, every spouse edge counted in every month and unstated relationships were read as no spouse. Coverage pass 7, F7-2 (docs/reviews/coverage7-cash.md): a married client whose spouse is not a person of the case in the month (af_spouse_is_outside_case_in_month, CO-7690) cannot be determined here: the spouse's resources are not stated (decision 4 of 2026-11-23), as for a sponsor outside the case (PS-M3) and the non-MAGI couple (F6-7, CO-643). Before, they were read as none.

The countable resources of this non-citizen client's sponsor(s) (9 CCR 2503-5 3.520.72.A, E): each sponsor's own countable resources (and a co-sponsor spouse's, who is a sponsor), plus those of a sponsor's spouse who did not sign, whose resources share the married sponsor's $3,000 limit; each counted "in the same manner as the non-citizen client" (3.520.72.E): the person's resources other than life insurance by Adult Financial's own list and exemptions (af_person_countable_resources_other_than_life_insurance), and the person's life insurance under the client's program, with "the same exemptions" as the client's (3.520.75.D, E.4, F.4): the OAP rule (af_life_insurance_countable_value_for_oap) for a client of OAP age, the whole cash surrender value over the face-value exemption (af_life_insurance_countable_value_other_than_oap) otherwise.

Precision. Coverage review F-15: each sponsor was counted by the SSI method (ssi_countable_resources_individual, CO-800), whose exclusions differ from Adult Financial's (an old life insurance policy exempt for an OAP client's sponsor under 3.520.75.E.4 was counted in full; revocable burial funds over $1,500 and burial spaces beyond the family's needs were not counted); now each sponsor and non-signing spouse is counted as af_client_and_spouse_countable_resources (CO-2389) counts the client and spouse. The face-value test of a sponsor's policies reads the sponsor and the sponsor's spouse, as the life insurance items read a person and spouse. A sponsor's spouse who is in neither group (the client) adds nothing. ### CO-2392 Adult Financial: needs of a spouse's dependent children `@engine`

For this person, the spouse of an OAP client, the amount 9 CCR 2503-5 3.534.B.3 deducts for the needs of each dependent child living in the household: for each of the person's children under af_dependent_child_age_limit (CO-3054) in the household, af_dependent_child_needs_rate (CO-3050) of the SSI benefit standard for an individual less the child's own income, never below zero.

Precision. A dependent child is read as the person's child under af_dependent_child_age_limit in the case (the assumption that parameter states); the SSI benefit standard of 3.510 is ssi_federal_benefit_rate_individual. The child's own income is gross earned and unearned income. Earned-income records, step E1 Adult Financial (docs/reviews/records-earnings-cash.md): the child's gross earned income is every earnings record of the child's pay received in the month at its gross amount, whatever Adult Financial's table does with it (the child's own income, not a countable figure), plus the net profit of a business (af_self_employment_net_profit) and boarder income (af_boarder_income); before earnings records it was wages_gross (which held every part of the wages) and the net profit, so in-kind pay was left out, which 3.520.782.B makes income too. Same-word audit SW-7 (convention rule 17): an edge joins persons who live together (lives_with, CO-1925, from dwelling_id); where a case states no dwelling_id the edge is read as living together, as before. A dependent child living in the household is read from lives_with. Receipt records, migration phase 1: the child's gross unearned income is the month's receipts of every kind but gambling winnings and a sponsor's money, as the unearned income facts it summed held them; a receipt of a kind Adult Financial reads from the earnings list (af_receipt_treatment_table, CO-5016: read_as_earnings) is left out, so a transition copy is counted once. An unstated earnings or receipts list is cannot determine. Coverage pass 4 CA4-9 (docs/reviews/coverage4-cash.md): a stream (an earnings record with no month and no date) is read only in the months from the month of its job_start_date through the month of its job_end_date, so the pay of a job that ended before the month, or begins after it, is not counted (9 CCR 2503-5 3.520.781.G, 9 CCR 2503-6 3.605.2.B: income counted when received); a record stated with its month or date is read in that month. Coverage pass 4 CA4-17 (docs/reviews/coverage4-cash.md): "less the dependent child's own income" (3.534.B.3) is every receipt of the child, a prize and money from a sponsor included; before, gambling winnings and a sponsor's money were left out, a remnant of the scalar facts. Probe A21: the husband's Social Security $1,600 and his son of 10 wins $500 in October: the child's need 994 x .5 - 500 = 0 (not 497), so 1,600 - 1,032 - 0 = 568 is deemed. Field sweep fix round (docs/reviews/field-sweep-snap-cash-nonmagi.md, FS-AF-1): a stream (a receipt with no month and no date) is read only in the months from the month of its start_date through the month of its end_date, as SNAP's readers read it (snap_counted_recurring_receipts, CO-5011), since "All income shall be countable in the month it is actually received or legally becomes available" (9 CCR 2503-5 3.520.781.G, S4910): a pension that ended, or one not yet begun, is received in no month outside those dates; a receipt stated with its month or date is read in that month. Before, a stream was read in every month whatever its dates. Coverage pass 6 CA6-4, CA6-12 (docs/reviews/coverage6-cash.md): a child counts in the month evaluated when born by the month's last day and under the limit on its first day (docs/operators.md, "Ages in a month"; OQ-951); before, every child under the limit on the determination date was counted in every month, one born after the month included. Pattern sweep (cash) PS-D2 (docs/reviews/pattern-sweep-cash.md): whether persons live together is read from lives_with as stated (dwelling_id), required where read (decision 4 of 2026-11-23; docs/conventions.md rule 17 as amended for Colorado Works and Adult Financial): no text on file says the persons of one application live together (9 CCR 2503-6 3.604.2.A, E, I build the unit from the persons living in the home; 9 CCR 2503-5 3.534.B.3 and 3.549.E name the household of the spouse and the parents in the home). Before, a person whose home was not stated was read as living with every related person of the case.

### CO-2553 Colorado Works: child support counted for eligibility `@engine`

The current child support received for this person that Colorado Works counts against the need standard for the month: at application, the month's current support (9 CCR 2503-6 3.605.5.A); at a redetermination, the person's six-month average when the support was received in all six previous months and the unit's averaged consistent support is over $500, and nothing otherwise (3.605.5.C). Current support is the month's child support receipts (cw_child_support_receipts, CO-5652); arrears are their own receipt kind, which 3.605.5.D exempts (receipt records, migration phase 2: before them, arrears were stated within child_support_received and subtracted here, final cash review FC-2). Coverage pass 6 CA6-2 (docs/reviews/coverage6-cash.md, probe W8): the kind of determination (cw_determination_is_redetermination, CO-2375) is required (decision 4 of 2026-11-23); before, a determination not stated to be a redetermination was read as an application, so a recipient at redetermination whose daughter's support was received in all six months and averaged $400 (not over $500, 3.605.5.C.2) had $400 counted against the $331 need standard and was ineligible, where the rule disregards it and the unit is eligible for $488. Months after approval and before the next redetermination are not distinguished; the codex determines at application or redetermination. A person with no current support in the month and none in the six previous months has none counted under either reading (3.605.5.A and C), so the kind of determination is read only for a person with support. Pattern sweep (cash) PS-D12 (docs/reviews/pattern-sweep-cash.md): the months received and the six-month average are read with no default (decision 4); both come from the same receipts as the month's support, so the old reading of an unknown as 0 changed no answer the receipts state.

### CO-2603 Adult Financial: partial month payment factor `@engine`

The figure this month's Adult Financial grant payment is multiplied by: in the month the client is determined eligible on a day other than the first, the decimal figure of 9 CCR 2503-5 3.581.D.4 for the number of days for which the client is eligible in the month (3.581.D.2-3; 3.532.B.2, 3.543.B.2, 3.548.B.2); in a month before the month of the eligibility date, 0, since eligibility begins on that date (3.542.B: "Eligibility shall begin with the date of application or the date the client meets all eligibility requirements, whichever is later"; 3.510 "Effective date of eligibility"); in a month before the month of the application date (af_application_date), 0, since eligibility begins no earlier than the date of application (3.542.B); otherwise 1, the full monthly payment (3.532.B.1, 3.543.B.1, 3.548.B.1). Where the application date is stated and the eligibility date is not, a month from the month of the application through the determination month cannot be determined: the eligibility date decides it and is required there (decision 4 of 2026-11-23); a month after the determination month is a full month, since eligibility has begun by the determination.

Precision. The days of eligibility run from af_eligibility_date (CO-2391) through the last day of the month, the date itself included: a client eligible from October 10 is eligible for 22 days of October (OQ-491, resolved). A client eligible from the first receives the full payment. Coverage pass 4 CA4-14 (docs/reviews/coverage4-cash.md; the CW3-3 class, fixed for Colorado Works by CO-4358): a client who applied on September 25 and met every requirement on October 3 (af_eligibility_date) is paid nothing for September and 29 days of October (.95342); before, September was paid in full. A redetermination needs no exception: the eligibility date is then before every month it evaluates. Coverage pass 6 CA6-1 (docs/reviews/coverage6-cash.md, probe A1): a case that states neither date is a continuing client, paid the full month; a case that states the application date (af_application_date, CO-3837) and not the eligibility date is paid nothing for a month before the month of the application, and cannot be determined for the months from the month of the application through the determination month, where the eligibility date decides the payment (3.542.B, 3.532.B.2). Before, an unstated eligibility date was read as a full month in every month, so a client who applied on October 12 was paid in full for October and for every month before it ($452 a month for the probe's OAP client, where 3.542.B gives nothing before October 12 and, from the twelfth, 20 days, .65754 x 452 = 297.2, $297).

Type rate, scope person-month, program AdultFinancial.
Uses: `af_application_date`, `af_eligibility_date`, `af_partial_month_payment_factor_table`.

```
if all of the following are true:
    - Adult Financial: eligibility date is unknown
    - Adult Financial: application date is unknown
  then 1
else if all of the following are true:
    - Adult Financial: eligibility date is unknown
    - the month is less than the month containing Adult Financial: application date
  then 0
else if all of the following are true:
    - Adult Financial: eligibility date is unknown
    - the month is more than the month containing the Determination Date
  then 1
else if the month is less than the month containing Adult Financial: eligibility date
  then 0
else if all of the following are true:
    - the month is equal to the month containing Adult Financial: eligibility date
    - it is not the case that Adult Financial: eligibility date is equal to the first day of the month
  then Adult Financial: partial month payment factors (table), for the number of days from Adult Financial: eligibility date to the first day of the month after the month
otherwise 1
```

### CO-2604 Adult Financial: receives SSI in the month `@engine`

Whether the person receives Supplemental Security Income in the month evaluated: an SSI recipient (receives_ssi, CO-012) with SSI received in the month (af_ssi_receipts, CO-5018, the month's SSI other than a retroactive lump sum). AND-SO and the Colorado Supplement are not paid for a month in which SSI is received: "A claim to recover the AND-SO or Colorado Supplement grant payments that are issued in the same month that the SSI or SSDI benefits are received shall be created" (9 CCR 2503-5 3.554.C.6), so AND-SO is barred, and AND-CS (a supplement to SSI received, 3.546, 3.549.A) is open, in a month with SSI received and not in one without. 9 CCR 2503-5 3.581.E drops the cents from every Adult Financial payment except where SSI income reduces the grant, the same test (af_oap_grant CO-951, af_and_grant CO-952).

Precision. Read as receives_ssi (CO-012) and ssi_income (CO-849) above 0, the SSI amount af_countable_income (CO-946) counts for an SSI recipient; a client who does not receive SSI is false without ssi_income being read. Receipt records, migration phase 1: the SSI of the month is af_ssi_receipts is read from the receipts (CO-5000). Pattern sweep (cash) PS-T12 (docs/reviews/pattern-sweep-cash.md): af_and_so_eligible (CO-1203) and af_and_cs_eligible (CO-950) read receives_ssi, a fact about SSA's award as of the determination date, in every month, so an AND-SO applicant whose SSI began after the application month was barred in the application month too, and an AND-CS client whose SSI had not yet begun was paid the whole Colorado Supplement standard in a month with no SSI. A stream of SSI (a receipt with no month) is received in every month the case covers, as before; a dated award is read by its months. Before the sweep this item was af_receives_ssi_in_month, read only for the rounding of 3.581.E; its test is unchanged, its name says what it tests, and the AND-SO bar and the AND-CS condition read it too.

Same-word audit SW-1/SW-3 (OQ-396 resolved): the spouse of a parent who is not a parent is not a caretaker here; 3.604.2.C.2.a makes that person an optional member (cw_is_optional_assistance_unit_member, CO-2349, reads the spouse and parent roles as the rule words it), so a stepparent is not read from the stepparent role. Whether the person is a dependent child is tested by the reader. Same-word audit SW-7 (convention rule 17): an edge joins persons who live together (lives_with, CO-1925, from dwelling_id); where a case states no dwelling_id the edge is read as living together, as before. A temporary absence keeps the person in the home as Colorado Works's 3.604.2.E, G and I allow (cw_is_considered_living_in_home, CO-3354). Coverage review CW-18 (fix round 2026-11-23): when more than one person exercises responsibility for the child, the one highest in the 3.604.2.H hierarchy is the caretaker: a parent always; a legal guardian or a relative (is_related_to) with primary responsibility only when no parent is in the home (cw_parents_in_home, CO-5207); any other person with primary responsibility only when neither a parent nor such a relative or guardian is in the home (cw_relative_or_guardian_caretakers_in_home, CO-5208). Two persons of the same rank are both caretakers; H names no order within a rank. Pattern sweep (cash) PS-D2 (docs/reviews/pattern-sweep-cash.md): whether persons live together is read from lives_with as stated (dwelling_id), required where read (decision 4 of 2026-11-23; docs/conventions.md rule 17 as amended for Colorado Works and Adult Financial): no text on file says the persons of one application live together (9 CCR 2503-6 3.604.2.A, E, I build the unit from the persons living in the home; 9 CCR 2503-5 3.534.B.3 and 3.549.E name the household of the spouse and the parents in the home). Before, a person whose home was not stated was read as living with every related person of the case.

Type group of persons, scope person, program ColoradoWorks.
Uses: `cw_is_considered_living_in_home`, `cw_parents_in_home`, `cw_relative_or_guardian_caretakers_in_home`, `is_related_to`, `lives_with`, `relationships`.

```
all persons in every person in the case such that
  all of the following are true:
    - this person is a parent or legal_guardian or has_primary_responsibility_for of that person
    - that person is in Lives with

        - (the number of persons in that person's Colorado Works: the child's parents in the home) is equal to 0
      - all of the following are true:

        - (the number of persons in that person's Colorado Works: the child's relative or guardian caretakers in the home) is equal to 0
```

### CO-2842 Colorado Works: half sibling of a dependent child who receives child support `@engine`

Whether the person is a half sibling of a dependent child and receives child support, an optional member of the assistance unit whom the caretaker decides whether to include (9 CCR 2503-6 3.604.2.C.2.d, S1625). A half sibling who receives no child support is a mandatory member (C.1.d).

Precision. Child support received for the person in the determination month above zero: the receipts of kind child_support or child_support_arrears (receipts, CO-5000; receipt records, migration phase 2: before them, child_support_received, CO-028, which stated arrears within the support). 3.604.2.C.2.d asks whether the half sibling receives child support, not how Colorado Works counts it, so arrears are support here too. Field sweep fix round (docs/reviews/field-sweep-snap-cash-nonmagi.md, FS-CW-1): a stream (a receipt with no month and no date) is read only in the months from the month of its start_date through the month of its end_date, as SNAP's readers read it (snap_counted_recurring_receipts, CO-5011), since income is "the receipt by a client of a gain or benefit in cash or in-kind during a calendar month" and the unit's income is what it has "received, or ... expects to receive in the application month and any month following" (9 CCR 2503-6 3.605.1.A.2, B, S4911): a pension that ended, or one not yet begun, is received in no month outside those dates; a receipt stated with its month or date is read in that month. Before, a stream was read in every month whatever its dates.

### CO-3312 Burial assistance: legally responsible persons `@engine`

The persons of the case who are the decedent's legally responsible persons (9 CCR 2503-5 3.570.42; for a Colorado Works death reimbursement, 9 CCR 2503-6 3.606.7.F.2.b-c): the decedent's spouse (a spouse edge, or the surviving spouse of a decedent), or, where the decedent is an unemancipated minor under af_burial_responsible_parent_age_limit, the decedent's legal parents.

Precision. Evaluated for the decedent. Responsible persons who are not persons of the case are stated on the decedent (CO-1226's fallback facts, CO-3314 and CO-3315). The definition's further condition, that the person bears legal responsibility for the charges, is read as met by a spouse or a minor's parent. Coverage pass 6 CA6-7: a deceased child's emancipation (read for a decedent under the parents' age limit) is required where read (decision 4 of 2026-11-23); before, read as false when not stated. Pattern sweep (cash) PS-T2 (docs/reviews/pattern-sweep-cash.md): the decedent's age under the parents' limit is the age at death (years from date_of_birth to date_of_death): 3.570.42 asks whether the decedent was an unemancipated minor, which the determination date's age does not answer when a birthday falls between the death and the determination. Pattern sweep (cash) PS-D11 (docs/reviews/pattern-sweep-cash.md): the decedent's relationships are read as stated, with no default (decision 4); before, unstated relationships were read as no spouse and no parent. For a person the case does not state to have died (date_of_death, "Not stated for a living person") the age is the determination date's, as before; the item has a decedent's meaning only for one who died. A case of one person has no other person to be responsible, whatever its relationships.

### CO-3354 Colorado Works: considered living in the home `@engine`

Whether, in some month the Colorado Works determination covers (cw_determination_months, CO-7300), Colorado Works considers the person to be living in the home they usually live in despite a temporary absence: the reading of who may join the assistance unit (cw_assistance_unit_members, CO-900). The test of each month (9 CCR 2503-6 3.604.2.E, G, I: present; away for medical treatment or on active duty; a dependent child under a court's jurisdiction, in an agency's custody without its physical custody, at school away from home, visiting a noncustodial parent under a parenting plan for no more than six months, or in a voluntary foster care placement for no more than three months; away for less than forty-five days with an established intent to return; not a parent or caretaker who has become a resident of an institution, with its exceptions) is cw_is_considered_living_in_home_in_month (CO-7602).

Precision. Months of a visit or placement are counted from the month the absence began. I.3's forty-five days, stated for a parent or caretaker, is also read for a child absent for a reason E and G do not list (OQ-611). If temporary_absence_reason is not stated, Colorado Works reads the person as present. Final cash review FC-1: the medical-treatment absence had kept a parent in the home however long the stay; 3.604.2.O.2 (S2602) now bounds it (cw_is_institution_resident, CO-3804, with the exception of cw_institution_resident_keeps_child_in_care, CO-3805). A dependent child receiving medical care away from home stays in the home under G.1 however long the stay. OQ-660 records the reading of O.2's last words. Final cash review 2, P2-6: a person stated with no temporary absence whose residence_setting_type is an institution entered at least thirty days before (cw_is_institution_resident) is not in the home either, unless a dependent child (G.1) or keeping a child in care (CO-3805), as in the medical-treatment branch; a setting not stated is read as a private dwelling. Coverage pass 6 CA6-7 (docs/reviews/coverage6-cash.md): whether the person is temporarily absent (temporary_absence_reason, none for a person in the home) is required where read (decision 4 of 2026-11-23); before, an unstated absence was read as none. Pattern sweep (cash) PS-T8 (docs/reviews/pattern-sweep-cash.md): whether the person lives in the home in some month the determination covers (cw_determination_months, CO-7300), each month read by cw_is_considered_living_in_home_in_month (CO-7602), which holds the rule above and counts each absence to that month (cw_month_reading_date, CO-7600). This item answers who may join the unit and the caretaker and parent relations, as cw_is_dependent_child (CO-901) answers for the dependent child; the month's unit (CO-7303) and the per-month minor-parent and stepparent items read CO-7602. Before, every absence was counted to the determination date and month, so a member whose absence passed its limit after the application month was no member in the application month either. The earlier sentence that an unstated absence reason reads as present is superseded by coverage pass 6 CA6-7 (required). Coverage pass 7, F7-7 (docs/reviews/coverage7-cash.md): the meaning is restated as the derivation reads since the pattern sweep's PS-T8 (some month of the determination); it described the month's test, which is CO-7602's.

Type yes/no, scope person, program ColoradoWorks.
Uses: `cw_determination_months`, `cw_is_considered_living_in_home_in_month`.

```
(the sum of (if Colorado Works: considered living in the home in the month for that month;   then 1; otherwise 0) for each month in Colorado Works: months the determination covers) is more than 0
```

```json
[">",["sum_months","cw_determination_months",["case",[["at","cw_is_considered_living_in_home_in_month",["that_month"]],1],["else",0]]],0]
```

### CO-3400 Adult Financial: countable resources of the person `@engine`

This person's own countable resources by Adult Financial's own rules (9 CCR 2503-5 3.520.72-3.520.77): cash and convertible assets, retirement and pension accounts (3.520.72.B.5), real and personal property other than the home (B.1, B.3-4), vehicles other than the highest-valued one used for transportation (3.520.77.A), the cash surrender value of life insurance unless the total face value of the client's and spouse's policies is $1,500 or less (3.520.75.D), and for an OAP client only the part 3.520.75.E-F count (af_life_insurance_countable_cash_value); revocable burial trusts and prepaid burial contracts over $1,500 each (3.520.72.B.8, 3.520.77.G-H); and burial spaces beyond the needs of the immediate family (3.520.72.B.9, 3.520.77.I).

Precision. Final cash review FC-8: 3.520.75.E-F's OAP rule for policies above $1,500 is af_life_insurance_countable_cash_value (CO-3854); revocable burial funds (revocable_burial_trust_value, CO-3855; revocable_prepaid_burial_contract_value, CO-3856) are counted over af_revocable_burial_funds_exemption (CO-3858) each, and burial spaces beyond the family's needs (burial_spaces_value_beyond_family_needs, CO-3857) in full; each is read as 0 when not stated. The other 3.520.77 exemptions not stated by the holdings facts are not counted. Final cash review 2, N-1: the holdings other than life insurance are af_person_countable_resources_other_than_life_insurance (CO-4000), and the person's own life insurance is counted under the OAP rule (CO-4001) when the person is of OAP age and under the AND rule (CO-4002) otherwise; a spouse's life insurance follows the client's program in af_client_and_spouse_countable_resources (CO-2389), which reads this item for the client only. Coverage pass 4 CA4-13 (docs/reviews/coverage4-cash.md): a figure of the month evaluated, from the holdings valued in that month (3.510 "Resources", S4791: "held as of the first day of a calendar month or as of the date of application"), so an application month before the determination month is judged by its own holdings; before, every month read the determination month's.

### CO-3804 Colorado Works: is a resident of an institution `@engine`

Whether this person is a resident of an institution under 9 CCR 2503-6 3.604.2.O.2: the person lives in an institution (a general medical or surgical hospital, a nursing home, an assisted living residence, a mental institution, or another care facility of that kind) and the stay has lasted at least cw_institution_resident_min_days consecutive days in the month evaluated (counted to cw_month_reading_date, CO-7600).

Precision. The stay is counted from institution_entry_date (CO-008) to the determination date (OQ-660: the elapsed stay, not an expected one). If residence_setting_type is not stated, Colorado Works reads the person as living in a private dwelling. A correctional facility is 3.604.1.E's (cw_is_institution_patient_or_inmate, CO-3802), not an institution here. Time audit T-6: "N consecutive days" is counted as the days elapsed since the day the absence or stay began (days_between), the day of departure or entry itself not counted (OQ-953): "at least thirty (30) consecutive days" (3.604.2.O, S2602): a resident once the days elapsed since the day of entry are at least cw_institution_resident_min_days, so an entry on August 1 is a stay of thirty days on August 31. Coverage pass 6 CA6-7: the residence setting is required where read (decision 4 of 2026-11-23); before, read as a private dwelling when not stated. Pattern sweep (cash) PS-T8 (docs/reviews/pattern-sweep-cash.md): per month: the stay is counted to cw_month_reading_date (CO-7600), the month's last day for a month before the determination month, the determination date otherwise.

Type yes/no, scope person-month, program ColoradoWorks.
Uses: `cw_institution_resident_min_days`, `cw_month_reading_date`, `institution_entry_date`, `residence_setting_type`.

```
all of the following are true:
  - Residence setting type is one of: hospital, nursing_facility, icf_iid, psychiatric_hospital, tuberculosis_hospital, assisted_living_residence, other_long_term_care_facility
  - (the number of days from Institution entry date to Colorado Works: the day a month's dated circumstances are read on) is at least Colorado Works: days of a stay that make a client a resident of an institution (30)
```

```json
["all",["in","residence_setting_type",["hospital","nursing_facility","icf_iid","psychiatric_hospital","tuberculosis_hospital","assisted_living_residence","other_long_term_care_facility"]],[">=",["days_between","institution_entry_date","cw_month_reading_date"],"cw_institution_resident_min_days"]]
```

### CO-3805 Colorado Works: institution resident keeps responsibility for a child in care `@engine`

Whether this person, a resident of an institution, continues to have the responsibility of a dependent child who also resides in the institution or continues to be cared for in the home, so that the person may still receive Colorado Works (9 CCR 2503-6 3.604.2.O.2): there is a dependent child of whom the person is the parent, legal guardian or the person with primary responsibility, and the child is not away from the home, or lives in the same kind of setting as the person.

Precision. A child with no temporary_absence_reason stated is read as in the home. The same kind of setting (residence_setting_type) stands for the same institution; no fact names the institution itself. If residence_setting_type is not stated, Colorado Works reads the person as living in a private dwelling. The trailing words of O.2, "unless individual needs are provided for through other state", are not modeled (OQ-660). Coverage pass 6 CA6-7: the child's absence and both persons' residence settings are required where read (decision 4 of 2026-11-23); before, read as none and a private dwelling when not stated.

Type yes/no, scope person, program ColoradoWorks.
Uses: `cw_is_dependent_child`, `relationships`, `residence_setting_type`, `temporary_absence_reason`.

```
there is a person in every person in the case such that
  all of the following are true:
    - this person is a parent or legal_guardian or has_primary_responsibility_for of that person
    - that person's Colorado Works: is a dependent child
    - any of the following is true:
      - that person's Temporary absence reason is equal to none
      - all of the following are true:
        - it is not the case that Residence setting type is equal to private_dwelling
        - that person's Residence setting type is equal to Residence setting type
```

```json
["exists",["persons"],["all",["rel",["parent","legal_guardian","has_primary_responsibility_for"],["P"]],["of",["P"],"cw_is_dependent_child"],["any",["=",["of",["P"],"temporary_absence_reason"],"none"],["all",["not",["=","residence_setting_type","private_dwelling"]],["=",["of",["P"],"residence_setting_type"],"residence_setting_type"]]]]]
```

### CO-3827 Adult Financial: excluded infrequent or irregular income `@engine`

The person's infrequent or irregular income for the month (infrequent_or_irregular_income_received) when the infrequent or irregular income of the calendar quarter containing the month is less than af_infrequent_income_quarterly_limit, which 9 CCR 2503-5 3.520.786.O exempts; otherwise 0.

Precision. The quarter is the calendar quarter (January-March, April-June, July-September, October-December) containing the month, found from the month's calendar number (its place in the quarter is that number less one, less three times the whole quarters before it); its total adds the fact for each of its three months, a month not stated being 0. The fact is unearned income. Final cash review 2, P2-3: the quarter's total is af_infrequent_income_quarter_total (CO-4011), which adds infrequent earned income, so the two share O's one limit; the earned part is excluded by af_excluded_infrequent_earned_income (CO-4012). Receipt records, migration phase 1: the month's infrequent or irregular income is its counted receipts marked irregular. When the quarter's total is under the limit and the receipts are not stated, the amount excluded cannot be determined: 3.520.786.O exempts income received and gives no reading for income not reported (decision 4 of 2026-11-23 (docs/plan-colorado.md): missing information is cannot determine unless the rule says otherwise; the phase-1 default of 0 is removed); a stated empty list excludes 0. Records E1 integration: a month with no infrequent or irregular receipt excludes nothing whatever the quarter holds, so the quarter is not read for it; before, a person whose earnings are not stated (the quarter pools infrequent earnings, CO-4011) had unearned income that could not be determined though nothing was there to exempt (CO-94, CO-211: docs/reviews/records-earnings-e1-integration.md). Field sweep fix round (docs/reviews/field-sweep-snap-cash-nonmagi.md, FS-AF-1): a stream (a receipt with no month and no date) is read only in the months from the month of its start_date through the month of its end_date, as SNAP's readers read it (snap_counted_recurring_receipts, CO-5011), since "All income shall be countable in the month it is actually received or legally becomes available" (9 CCR 2503-5 3.520.781.G, S4910): a pension that ended, or one not yet begun, is received in no month outside those dates; a receipt stated with its month or date is read in that month. Before, a stream was read in every month whatever its dates.

Type money, scope person-month, program AdultFinancial.
Uses: `af_infrequent_income_quarter_total`, `af_infrequent_income_quarterly_limit`, `af_receipt_treatment_table`, `receipts`.

```
if (the sum of that receipt's amount for each receipt in Receipts where ((all of the following are true:;   - that receipt's irregular;   - all of the following are true:;     - that receipt is received in the month;     - any of the following is true:;       - it is not the case that that receipt's month is unknown;       - all of the following are true:;         - any of the following is true:;           - that receipt's start date is unknown;           - the month containing that receipt's start date is at most the month;         - any of the following is true:;           - that receipt's end date is unknown;           - the month containing that receipt's end date is at least the month;   - Adult Financial: how each kind of receipt is treated (table), for that receipt's kind is one of: counted, counted_no_rule_excludes, counted_less_one_third_for_ssi_child, counted_less_child_gift_exclusion))) is equal to 0
  then 0
else if Adult Financial: infrequent or irregular income in the calendar quarter is less than Adult Financial: quarterly limit on exempt infrequent or irregular income (60)
  then the sum of that receipt's amount for each receipt in Receipts where ((all of the following are true:;   - that receipt's irregular;   - all of the following are true:;     - that receipt is received in the month;     - any of the following is true:;       - it is not the case that that receipt's month is unknown;       - all of the following are true:;         - any of the following is true:;           - that receipt's start date is unknown;           - the month containing that receipt's start date is at most the month;         - any of the following is true:;           - that receipt's end date is unknown;           - the month containing that receipt's end date is at least the month;   - Adult Financial: how each kind of receipt is treated (table), for that receipt's kind is one of: counted, counted_no_rule_excludes, counted_less_one_third_for_ssi_child, counted_less_child_gift_exclusion))
otherwise 0
```

### CO-3829 Adult Financial: the client's unearned income disregard `@engine`

The part of the $20 unearned income disregard this Adult Financial client receives: all of af_general_income_disregard for an unmarried client; for a married client, the client's equal share of it (af_married_couple_disregard_share), since the disregard "shall be split equally between the client and the client's spouse so that no more than a $20.00 disregard is applied for the married couple" (9 CCR 2503-5 3.533.A.2.c.1, 3.544.B.2, 3.549.A.2.c.1).

Precision. Married is is_married (CO-930): a spouse edge, or marital_status married. The split applies whether or not the spouse is also an Adult Financial client; the spouse's half is what the AND-SO and AND-CS deeming of the spouse's unearned income may use (af_deemed_relative_income, CO-2384). OQ-661 records the reading. Coverage pass 6 CA6-7: reads af_is_married (CO-7308), which asks for the client's marital status (3.520.63.A), not the shared is_married's reading of an unstated status as not married (decision 4 of 2026-11-23). Pattern sweep (cash) PS-M1 (docs/reviews/pattern-sweep-cash.md): per month, from the month's marriage (af_is_married, CO-7308).

Type money, scope person-month, program AdultFinancial.
Uses: `af_general_income_disregard`, `af_is_married`, `af_married_couple_disregard_share`.

```
if Adult Financial: married
  then Adult Financial unearned income disregard (20) times Adult Financial: a married client's share of the unearned income disregard (0.5)
otherwise Adult Financial unearned income disregard (20)
```

### CO-3830 Adult Financial: gross earned income `@engine`

This person's gross earned income for the month for Adult Financial: the pay the earnings table counts (af_earned_pay: gross monetary wages and in-kind earned income at the value of the item supplied, 9 CCR 2503-5 3.520.782.A-B), plus the self-employment net profit of 3.520.783.B (af_self_employment_net_profit), the board, room, and room and board payments less the expenses of providing them (3.520.783.C.2.b-d, af_boarder_income) and donated work hours that count (3.520.784, af_donated_work_income), less the earned income 3.520.786 exempts by a field of the pay (af_excluded_earned_income: a PASS set-aside, I; infrequent or irregular pay, O), never below zero.

Precision. Earned-income records, step E1 Adult Financial (docs/reviews/records-earnings-cash.md): read from the earnings records (earnings, CO-5100) through af_earnings_treatment_table (CO-5103), replacing wages_gross, in_kind_compensation_value and the parts of wages_gross af_excluded_earned_income subtracted (work_study_earnings): a kind the table excludes (work-study, 3.520.786.H; 37 U.S.C. 310 special pay, K) is never counted, so it is not subtracted either. The same for the client, the client's spouse and the sponsor(s): the deeming items (af_deemed_relative_income CO-2384, af_deemed_sponsor_income CO-2386) read it for each relative. An unstated earnings list is cannot determine (product-owner decision 4 of 2026-11-23); a stated empty list is no earned income.

Type money, scope person-month, program AdultFinancial.
Uses: `af_boarder_income`, `af_donated_work_income`, `af_earned_pay`, `af_excluded_earned_income`, `af_self_employment_net_profit`.

```
the greater of 0 and ((Adult Financial: pay received in the month plus Adult Financial: net profit from self-employment plus Adult Financial: income from boarders plus Adult Financial: income from donated work hours) minus Adult Financial: excluded earned income)
```

```json
["max",0,["-",["+","af_earned_pay","af_self_employment_net_profit","af_boarder_income","af_donated_work_income"],"af_excluded_earned_income"]]
```

### CO-3831 Adult Financial: unearned income other than SSI `@engine`

This person's gross unearned income for the month other than SSI, from which 9 CCR 2503-5 3.533.A.2.c, 3.544.B.2 and 3.549.A.2.c deduct the $20 disregard: the counted unearned receipts (af_counted_unearned_receipts, through the counting table af_receipt_treatment_table, 3.520.785-786) less the exclusions that turn on the person (one-third of child support for an SSI-age child, K (c)(11); infrequent or irregular income within the quarterly limit, O; life-threatening-condition gifts to a child, K (c)(21)); for an OAP or AND-CS client, the in-kind support and maintenance the county determines, up to the ISM maximum (3.520.79); and income the client refused or failed without good cause to secure, counted as if available (3.520.71.G.1, af_refused_potential_income), never below zero. The expenses of producing workers' compensation, insurance, school-attendance and rental receipts (B.9, B.14-16, B.20) are left out of the counted receipts themselves (af_counted_unearned_receipts).

Precision. Receipt records, migration phase 1 (docs/reviews/receipts-migration-1.md): read from the receipts (CO-5000), replacing the sum of the unearned income facts less af_excluded_unearned_income (CO-2343). The Adult Financial grant itself is not income (its row is not_income_to_client). Coverage review F-12: prizes (3.520.785.B.13) and an inheritance or other one-time receipt are counted in the month received; before receipt records an inheritance stated only as lump_sum_received, without raising the other unearned income fact it was part of, was not counted (probe PR-LUMP). F-11: the expenses were unearned_income_offsetting_expenses (CO-4444), read as 0 when not stated, until coverage pass 4 CA4-1 read them from the receipts' own fields and the person's rental and school expenses in af_counted_unearned_receipts (CO-5017), so the same money is never stated twice and nothing is subtracted from income the expense is not tied to. P2-6: the minimum monthly maintenance needs allowance a community-spouse client retains from an institutionalized spouse's income (3.520.785.B.24) is a receipt of the client's (other_nontaxable), counted here. The program for the ISM term is read as af_countable_income reads it: OAP when af_is_oap_age, AND-CS when af_and_cs_eligible. af_refused_potential_income is read as 0 when not stated.

Type money, scope person-month, program AdultFinancial.
Uses: `af_and_cs_eligible`, `af_child_support_exclusion`, `af_counted_unearned_receipts`, `af_excluded_infrequent_income`, `af_excluded_life_threatening_condition_gifts`, `af_in_kind_support_and_maintenance`, `af_is_oap_age`, `af_ism_maximum`, `af_refused_potential_income`.

```
the greater of 0 and ((Adult Financial: a person's counted unearned receipts other than SSI minus (Adult Financial: one-third of current child support for an SSI-age child plus Adult Financial: excluded infrequent or irregular income plus Adult Financial: excluded gifts to a child with a life-threatening condition)) plus (if any of the following is true:;     - Adult Financial: is Old Age Pension age;     - Adult Financial: AND-CS eligible;   then the lesser of Adult Financial: in-kind support and maintenance and Adult Financial maximum in-kind support and maintenance amount; otherwise 0) plus (Adult Financial: potential income the client refused to secure, otherwise 0))
```

```json
["max",0,["+",["-","af_counted_unearned_receipts",["+","af_child_support_exclusion","af_excluded_infrequent_income","af_excluded_life_threatening_condition_gifts"]],["case",[["any","af_is_oap_age","af_and_cs_eligible"],["min","af_in_kind_support_and_maintenance","af_ism_maximum"]],["else",0]],["otherwise","af_refused_potential_income",0]]]
```

### CO-3840 Adult Financial: months of ineligibility for a month's transfer `@engine`

The number of months of ineligibility for Adult Financial grant payments for the transfers without fair consideration the person made in the month (9 CCR 2503-5 3.520.76.D-E), for each resource transferred in the month and not returned in whole in the same month (D.6) that counts (af_twfc_transfer_is_counted) and was made within the thirty-six months before the application or after it (A.3): its uncompensated value divided by the TWFC monthly penalty value (af_twfc_monthly_penalty_value, the current grant standard of the client's program) and rounded down, at most af_twfc_max_penalty_months (E: "up to a maximum of 36 months depending on the amount of the uncompensated value for each resource transferred"), and, when the whole resource was returned in a later month, no more than the months from the month after the transfer through the month of the return (D.6.a); the months of the month's resources added together, since each transfer's period follows the one before (D.5; af_is_in_twfc_penalty_period, CO-3841). 0 when the month's transfer does not count.

Precision. The divisor is read at the determination month, D.2's current standard. Final cash review 2, N-5: each month's transfers are divided and rounded down on their own, and af_is_in_twfc_penalty_period (CO-3841) runs the periods one after another (D.5); two transfers of $1,000 by an OAP client in different months give 0 + 0 months, not floor(2,000 / 1,032) = 1. Resource records, step H1 Adult Financial (docs/reviews/records-holdings-snap-af.md): the month's transfers are the holdings records disposed of in it, counted (af_twfc_transfer_is_counted, CO-4008), at their uncompensated value. A transfer returned in whole in the same month adds nothing (D.6); when every transfer of the month was returned in whole in a later month, the months are no more than those from the month after the transfer through the latest month of return (D.6.a). Cross-list records round (docs/reviews/cross-list-records.md; OQ-1254 resolved, CA4-19): each resource transferred is counted on its own record, as D.3 and E say ("Divide the uncompensated value by the TWFC monthly penalty value and round down"; "for each resource transferred", S2614, S2806): the divisor and the application date are facts of the client, read inside the sum over the records as facts of the record's owner (P60, docs/operators.md: [of, [owner], ...]; the holdings read here are the person's own, so the owner is the person). So two resources transferred in one month are each divided and rounded down (OAP, $1,032: $3,000 and $2,200 give 2 + 2 = 4 months, where the month's total would give 5), each is capped at 36 months, each returned in a later month is cut at its own month of return, and in the month thirty-six months before the application month only the resources transferred on or after the application's day of the month are counted (A.3: "within thirty-six (36) months prior to the application date"), however many fall on either side. Before, both cases were cannot determine (P55 lets a sum over the records read no fact of a person). Field sweep defaults list (2026-11-23): af_found_not_twfc is read as the holdings record states it, its default false declared once on the schema (CO-5300) with the rule that gives it (9 CCR 2503-5 3.520.76.A.4.a (S2614): the county presumes a transfer in the look-back was made to become eligible); before, this reader gave the default itself (otherwise false), which conventions rule 12 and decision 4 do not allow a reader. No value changes: the tests that leave the finding out read it as false, as before.

Type whole number, scope person-month, program AdultFinancial.
Uses: `af_application_date`, `af_twfc_lookback_months`, `af_twfc_max_penalty_months`, `af_twfc_monthly_penalty_value`, `af_twfc_transfer_is_counted`, `holdings`.


### CO-3841 Adult Financial: in a period of ineligibility for a transfer `@engine`

Whether the month falls in the person's period of ineligibility for transfers without fair consideration (9 CCR 2503-5 3.520.76.D.5): each transfer's months (af_twfc_penalty_months) begin with the month after the month of the transfer or, where an earlier transfer's period is still running, with the month after that period ends, so the month is in the period when, for some month with a counted transfer before it, the months of ineligibility of the transfers from that month through the month before this one are at least the number of months from that month to this one.

Precision. Final cash review 2, N-5: D.5 says the period for further transfers 'would begin the month following the end date of the first transfer's period of ineligibility'; a transfer made after an earlier period has ended starts its own period the month after it, since a period cannot begin before the transfer it is for. The months examined begin af_twfc_lookback_months months before the application month (af_application_date, required where a transfer is stated before the month: af_twfc_transfer_is_counted, CO-4008, reads it too). False when there is no penalty. A month in the period may also be a month of ineligibility for another reason (E). Example: transfers of $2,064 in January 2026 (2 months) and $3,096 in February 2026 (3 months) by an OAP client: February to June 2026. Coverage pass 6 CA6-7 (docs/reviews/coverage6-cash.md): with no holding disposed of before the month there is no transfer and no period, whatever the look-back; otherwise the application date is required (decision 4 of 2026-11-23); before, the determination month stood for an unstated application date, which moved the look-back.

Type yes/no, scope person-month, program AdultFinancial.
Uses: `af_application_date`, `af_twfc_lookback_months`, `af_twfc_penalty_months`, `af_twfc_transfer_is_counted`, `holdings`.

### CO-3854 Adult Financial: countable cash value of life insurance `@engine`

The part of this person's life insurance cash surrender value that Adult Financial counts for an Old Age Pension client, whether the person is the client or the client's spouse, when the total face value of the client's and spouse's policies is more than $1,500 (9 CCR 2503-5 3.520.75.E-F, "For OAP only"): the whole cash surrender value if any policy of the client or spouse was bought within the last af_oap_life_insurance_lookback_months months; otherwise only the money contributed within those months, plus this person's share of the combined cash surrender value over af_oap_life_insurance_cash_value_cap, never more than the cash surrender value.

Precision. Final cash review 2, N-1: the item no longer reads the owner's age; it states the OAP count, and af_life_insurance_countable_value_for_oap (CO-4001) reads it when the client is of OAP age, for the client's own policies and the spouse's alike. The look-back is counted in calendar months from the determination month (a policy bought in the month forty-eight months before it is within the look-back). The combined cash value and the look-back add the spouse wherever the spouse lives (3.520.63.D, as af_client_and_spouse_countable_resources, CO-2389, counts the spouse; coverage review 2, G-2); a cash value not stated is estimated from the 3.520.75.H chart (af_life_insurance_cash_value, CO-4722; G-7); the excess over the cap is divided between the spouses in proportion to their cash values, so the couple's countable excess is the excess. A spouse who owns no policy with a cash value states no purchase date. Resource records, step H1 Adult Financial (docs/reviews/records-holdings-snap-af.md): the face value, the purchase dates and the premiums are read from the person's (and the spouse's) life insurance records (af_life_insurance_face_value, af_life_insurance_bought_within_lookback, af_life_insurance_premiums_in_lookback, CO-5347 to CO-5349) in place of the person facts (CO-3397, CO-3850, CO-3851), each of which was read as 0 or unstated when not given; a face value not stated is now cannot determine (decision 4). Coverage pass 4 CA4-13 (docs/reviews/coverage4-cash.md): a figure of the month evaluated, from the holdings valued in that month (3.510 "Resources", S4791: "held as of the first day of a calendar month or as of the date of application"), so an application month before the determination month is judged by its own holdings; before, every month read the determination month's. Pattern sweep (cash) PS-M1 and PS-D4 (docs/reviews/pattern-sweep-cash.md): the spouse is the spouse of the month (af_spouses_in_month, CO-7603), so a spouse who died before the month is not counted in it (3.520.63.A: widowed), and a client whose relationships are not stated, in a case of more than one person, cannot be determined (decision 4); before, every spouse edge counted in every month and unstated relationships were read as no spouse.

Type money, scope person-month, program AdultFinancial.
Uses: `af_life_insurance_bought_within_lookback`, `af_life_insurance_cash_value`, `af_life_insurance_premiums_in_lookback`, `af_oap_life_insurance_cash_value_cap`, `af_spouses_in_month`.

### CO-3877 Adult Financial: eligible for disaster assistance `@engine`

Whether the client may receive an Adult Financial disaster assistance payment for the month (9 CCR 2503-5 3.570.52): the client requested it, has an emergent need related to the disaster, a declared disaster is in effect, and the client is approved for or receiving an Adult Financial grant payment (an OAP, AND-SO or AND-CS category, a Home Care Allowance, or a grant received this month).

Precision. A client who has not requested it is not eligible, and nothing else is asked. The county may also pay through general assistance (3.570.52.D); that is not this payment. Final cash review 2, P2-8, a documented limit: 3.570.53.B (S2625) lets the county "Only request verification related to the client's request for disaster assistance if the county considers the request questionable"; the volume states no verification element for the request, since the rule names no document and no due date, and D forbids asking how the payment was used. A county that finds a request questionable asks for verification outside the Adult Financial pending count (af_pending_verification_count, CO-1436). Receipt records, migration phase 1: the grant received this month is af_grant_receipts is read from the receipts (CO-5000). A Home Care Allowance received this month is its own receipt kind (af_home_care_allowance_receipts; coverage review 3 H-5). Decision 4 of 2026-11-23 (docs/plan-colorado.md: missing information is cannot determine unless the rule says otherwise), applied as for the receipts readers (b49a7f2; earned-income records E1 for the cash programs, docs/reviews/records-earnings-cash.md): 3.570.52 asks whether the client is approved for or receiving a payment and gives no reading for payments not reported, so with the receipts not stated a grant received this month cannot be determined (a stated empty list is none); an approved category or Home Care Allowance still answers on its own. Pattern sweep (cash) PS-D10 (docs/reviews/pattern-sweep-cash.md): the declared disaster is required where read, once the client has requested disaster assistance and has an emergent need (decision 4); the request keeps its reading as none when not stated, since disaster assistance is determined on the client's request (3.570.52.C). Before, an unstated declaration was read as none.

### CO-4000 Adult Financial: countable resources of the person other than life insurance `@engine`

This person's own countable resources by Adult Financial's own rules (9 CCR 2503-5 3.520.72-3.520.77) other than the cash surrender value of life insurance, read from the person's holdings records (holdings, CO-5300) through af_holding_treatment_table (CO-5302): cash and convertible assets less the part exempt now (af_cash_and_convertible_holdings less af_exempt_liquid_resources, CO-5340, CO-4412), retirement accounts less the taxes on withdrawing them (CO-5341), real property other than the home (CO-5342), self-support property over its exemption (CO-4422), vehicles other than the one with the highest equity used for transportation (CO-5343), burial funds, contracts and spaces over their exemptions (CO-5344), personal property held as an investment (CO-5345), a home no longer exempt (CO-5346), the trust corpus that can be paid to or for the person (3.520.72.B.13; corpus_available_value) and potential resources the person refused to secure (3.520.71.H.1), never below zero.

Precision. Resource records, step H1 Adult Financial (docs/reviews/records-holdings-snap-af.md): each holding is stated once, as its own record, and counted by its kind's row and the fields beside it, never as a part of one figure subtracted from another; the old reader defaults (each holding read as 0 when not stated; intends_to_return_home read as true) are gone: a person whose holdings are not stated, or whose home, vehicle or held money does not state a field the rule reads, is cannot determine (decision 4 of 2026-11-23), and af_meets_resource_limit (CO-948) still answers where the parts that are known already exceed the limit (af_resources_known_lower_bound, CO-5350). Life insurance is counted apart because 3.520.75.E-F apply "For OAP only" to the policies of "a client and his or her spouse": the client's program governs a spouse's policy, so af_client_and_spouse_countable_resources (CO-2389) adds the spouse's other resources from this item and the spouse's life insurance under the client's program (final cash review 2, N-1). Findings fixed in step H1: personal property held as an investment is counted (3.520.77.B; H0-F2, OQ-1203); the vehicle exempt is the one with the highest equity used for transportation, chosen from the records (3.520.77.A; P58, OQ-1205 assumption A) rather than stated by the household; a retroactive SSI or Social Security payment stated for the SSI method is the same record Adult Financial exempts for nine months (3.520.77.J); each burial trust and contract has its own $1,500 exemption (3.520.77.G.3, H.2). This item also counts a spouse's and each sponsor's resources (CO-2389, CO-2390), as 3.520.72.E and 3.520.73.B.1.a direct. The estate of a client adjudicated incapacitated (3.520.72.B.12) is the client's own holding. Coverage review P3: the holdings are stated as of the determination date, which for Adult Financial is the first day of the month or the date of application (3.510 "Resources"). Coverage pass 4 CA4-13 (docs/reviews/coverage4-cash.md): a figure of the month evaluated, from the holdings valued in that month (3.510 "Resources", S4791: "held as of the first day of a calendar month or as of the date of application"), so an application month before the determination month is judged by its own holdings; before, every month read the determination month's.

Type money, scope person-month, program AdultFinancial.
Uses: `af_cash_and_convertible_holdings`, `af_countable_burial_holdings`, `af_countable_home_equity`, `af_countable_personal_property`, `af_countable_real_property`, `af_countable_retirement_accounts`, `af_countable_vehicles`, `af_exempt_liquid_resources`, `af_holding_treatment_table`, `af_refused_potential_resources_value`, `af_self_support_property_countable_value`, `holdings`.

### CO-4001 Adult Financial: countable life insurance under the OAP rule `@engine`

The part of this person's life insurance cash surrender value that counts toward the resources of an Old Age Pension client, whether the person is the client or the client's spouse: nothing when the total face value of the person's and the spouse's policies is af_life_insurance_face_value_exemption_limit or less (9 CCR 2503-5 3.520.75.D); otherwise the part 3.520.75.E-F count (af_life_insurance_countable_cash_value).

Precision. The total face value adds the spouse wherever the spouse lives, as 3.520.75.D-F read "a client and his or her spouse" and as af_client_and_spouse_countable_resources (CO-2389) counts the spouse (3.520.63.D; coverage review 2, G-2). A face value not stated is read as 0. Coverage review P3: the face value is the original face value at purchase, not a face value increased by dividends or their reinvestment (3.520.75.A, G); a case states life_insurance_face_value so for an Adult Financial client. Resource records, step H1 Adult Financial (docs/reviews/records-holdings-snap-af.md): the face value, the purchase dates and the premiums are read from the person's (and the spouse's) life insurance records (af_life_insurance_face_value, af_life_insurance_bought_within_lookback, af_life_insurance_premiums_in_lookback, CO-5347 to CO-5349) in place of the person facts (CO-3397, CO-3850, CO-3851), each of which was read as 0 or unstated when not given; a face value not stated is now cannot determine (decision 4). Coverage pass 4 CA4-13 (docs/reviews/coverage4-cash.md): a figure of the month evaluated, from the holdings valued in that month (3.510 "Resources", S4791: "held as of the first day of a calendar month or as of the date of application"), so an application month before the determination month is judged by its own holdings; before, every month read the determination month's. Pattern sweep (cash) PS-M1 and PS-D4 (docs/reviews/pattern-sweep-cash.md): the spouse is the spouse of the month (af_spouses_in_month, CO-7603), so a spouse who died before the month is not counted in it (3.520.63.A: widowed), and a client whose relationships are not stated, in a case of more than one person, cannot be determined (decision 4); before, every spouse edge counted in every month and unstated relationships were read as no spouse.

### CO-4011 Adult Financial: infrequent or irregular income in the calendar quarter `@engine`

The infrequent or irregular income, earned and unearned together, the person received in the calendar quarter containing the month (the receipts stated as irregular, receipts CO-5000, and the earnings records stated as irregular, earnings CO-5100), which 9 CCR 2503-5 3.520.786.O compares with af_infrequent_income_quarterly_limit.

Precision. The quarter is the calendar quarter (January-March, April-June, July-September, October-December) containing the month, found from the month's calendar number (its place in the quarter is that number less one, less three times the whole quarters before it); its total adds the irregular receipts and earnings of each of its three months. O says "Infrequent or irregular income of less than $60 in a calendar quarter" with no split by kind, so earned and unearned infrequent income share the one limit (where 20 CFR 416.1112(c)(1) and 416.1124(c)(6) give SSI separate limits). Receipt records, migration phase 1: the unearned part is the receipts marked irregular; Decision 4 of 2026-11-23 (docs/plan-colorado.md: missing information is cannot determine unless the rule says otherwise), applied as for the receipts readers (b49a7f2; earned-income records E1 for the cash programs, docs/reviews/records-earnings-cash.md): O exempts income received and gives no reading for income not reported, so with the receipts not stated the quarter's total cannot be determined (before, each month's receipts were read as 0 when not stated); a stated empty list is none; a receipt of a kind Adult Financial reads from the earnings list (af_receipt_treatment_table, CO-5016: read_as_earnings) is left out, so a transition copy is counted once. Earned-income records, step E1 Adult Financial (docs/reviews/records-earnings-cash.md): the earned part is the earnings records marked irregular (irregular) of every kind of pay or receipts, at their gross amount, not the cost kinds; before earnings records it was infrequent_or_irregular_earned_income_received, each month read as 0 when not stated; an unstated earnings list is now cannot determine (decision 4 of 2026-11-23). Each earlier month's records are summed in that month ("in that month"), so a record is counted with the treatment table in force in the month it is received (docs/operators.md, Resolution step 2 and P57). Coverage pass 4 CA4-9 (docs/reviews/coverage4-cash.md): a stream (an earnings record with no month and no date) is read only in the months from the month of its job_start_date through the month of its job_end_date, so the pay of a job that ended before the month, or begins after it, is not counted (9 CCR 2503-5 3.520.781.G, 9 CCR 2503-6 3.605.2.B: income counted when received); a record stated with its month or date is read in that month. Field sweep fix round (docs/reviews/field-sweep-snap-cash-nonmagi.md, FS-AF-1): a stream (a receipt with no month and no date) is read only in the months from the month of its start_date through the month of its end_date, as SNAP's readers read it (snap_counted_recurring_receipts, CO-5011), since "All income shall be countable in the month it is actually received or legally becomes available" (9 CCR 2503-5 3.520.781.G, S4910): a pension that ended, or one not yet begun, is received in no month outside those dates; a receipt stated with its month or date is read in that month. Before, a stream was read in every month whatever its dates.

### CO-4012 Adult Financial: excluded infrequent or irregular earned income `@engine`

The person's infrequent or irregular pay for the month that Adult Financial counts (the earnings records received in the month marked irregular whose kind af_earnings_treatment_table counts as pay, at their amount less any PASS set-aside) when the infrequent or irregular income of the calendar quarter containing the month, earned and unearned together (af_infrequent_income_quarter_total), is less than af_infrequent_income_quarterly_limit, which 9 CCR 2503-5 3.520.786.O exempts; otherwise 0.

Precision. Read by af_excluded_earned_income (CO-2342), so the exempt earnings come off gross earned income before the $65 and one-half disregards. Earned-income records, step E1 Adult Financial (docs/reviews/records-earnings-cash.md): before earnings records the pay was infrequent_or_irregular_earned_income_received (part of wages_gross); it is now the irregular records of the kinds af_earned_pay (CO-5130) counts, so pay the table never counts (work-study) is not taken off again. A business's irregular receipts count toward the quarter's total (CO-4011) but are not taken off here: they enter gross earned income only through the business's net profit (af_self_employment_net_profit, CO-1708; 3.520.783.F averages irregular self-employment income over twelve months, as the case states it). The PASS set-aside of an irregular pay is taken off by CO-2342, so it is not taken off twice. An unstated earnings list is cannot determine. Coverage pass 4 CA4-9 (docs/reviews/coverage4-cash.md): a stream (an earnings record with no month and no date) is read only in the months from the month of its job_start_date through the month of its job_end_date, so the pay of a job that ended before the month, or begins after it, is not counted (9 CCR 2503-5 3.520.781.G, 9 CCR 2503-6 3.605.2.B: income counted when received); a record stated with its month or date is read in that month. Coverage pass 4 CA4-7: a difficulty of care payment stated as foster care (foster_care) is not counted pay.

### CO-4352 Colorado Works: minor parent assisted as an adult `@engine`

This person is a minor parent who does not live in the home of a caretaker and so receives Colorado Works assistance as an adult, not as a dependent child (9 CCR 2503-6 3.604.2.N.2.c): in the month evaluated, under cw_minor_parent_age_limit on its first day, with a dependent child of her or his own in the month (cw_has_dependent_child_in_month, CO-7305), and either emancipated, of a marital status other than single (who are "not considered to be living in the home of a caretaker even if they are living in the home of their parent", N.2.b), or living with no person who is her or his caretaker (a parent, legal guardian or person with primary responsibility, in the home under Colorado Works' absence rule, as cw_caretaker_of reads it). The unit's standards then count the minor parent as a caretaker (cw_unit_caretaker_count, CO-926) and not as a child (cw_unit_child_count, CO-927).

Precision. "If approved" (N.2.c) is the living-arrangement condition of N.1-N.2.a (cw_minor_parent_living_arrangement_met, CO-906, read by cw_eligibility_status, CO-921): a minor parent who is not approved is ineligible, so this item only prices the unit of one who is. The caretaker test is the inverse of cw_caretaker_of (CO-2608): a person the minor parent is the child, ward or in the primary care of, living in the same home (lives_with; an edge with no dwelling stated is read as living together, convention rule 17) and considered living in the home (cw_is_considered_living_in_home, CO-3354). Coverage pass 6 CA6-7 (docs/reviews/coverage6-cash.md): whether the minor parent is emancipated (is_emancipated_minor) is required where read (decision 4 of 2026-11-23); before, an unstated emancipation was read as not emancipated. Coverage pass 6 CA6-4: per month, the age taken on the month's first day (docs/operators.md, "Ages in a month"; OQ-951), as the dependent child of the month is (CO-6807); the per-person readers (cw_child_only_unit CO-916, cw_unit_has_striking_adult CO-3808) read the determination month. The 3.601 definition of a dependent child ("a person who resides with a parent or non-parent caretaker") is otherwise carried by the unit closure (CO-900), which joins a child to a unit only through a caretaker in the home. Pattern sweep (cash) PS-D2 (docs/reviews/pattern-sweep-cash.md): whether persons live together is read from lives_with as stated (dwelling_id), required where read (decision 4 of 2026-11-23; docs/conventions.md rule 17 as amended for Colorado Works and Adult Financial): no text on file says the persons of one application live together (9 CCR 2503-6 3.604.2.A, E, I build the unit from the persons living in the home; 9 CCR 2503-5 3.534.B.3 and 3.549.E name the household of the spouse and the parents in the home). Before, a person whose home was not stated was read as living with every related person of the case.

Type yes/no, scope person-month, program ColoradoWorks.
Uses: `cw_has_dependent_child_in_month`, `cw_is_considered_living_in_home_in_month`, `cw_minor_parent_age_limit`, `date_of_birth`, `is_emancipated_minor`, `lives_with`, `marital_status`, `relationships`.

```
all of the following are true:
  - (the number of whole years between Date of birth and the first day of the month) is less than Colorado Works minor age limit (18)
  - Colorado Works: has a dependent child in the month
  - any of the following is true:
    - Is an emancipated minor
    - it is not the case that Marital status is equal to single
    - it is not the case that (there is a person in every person in the case such that;   all of the following are true:;     - this person is a child or ward or in_primary_care_of of that person;     - that person is in Lives with;     - Colorado Works: considered living in the home in the month;     - that person's Colorado Works: considered living in the home in the month)
```

### CO-4358 Colorado Works: partial month payment factor `@engine`

The figure the authorized Colorado Works grant for the entire month is multiplied by for the month: in the month of the initial payment, when assistance begins on a day other than the first, the decimal figure of 9 CCR 2503-6 3.609.2.A.1 for the number of days for which payment is made, from the date assistance begins (the date of application, or the later date on which a unit ineligible on the date of application became eligible) through the last day of the month; in a month before the month in which assistance begins, 0, since the initial payment includes assistance only from that date; otherwise 1, the entire month.

Precision. The days run from the date assistance begins through the last day of the month, that date included: an application on October 12 is paid for 20 days of October (.65754). Assistance beginning on the first of the month is the entire month. The date of application is cw_application_date (CO-2372); the later eligibility date is cw_unit_eligible_from_date (CO-4359), read as the application date when not stated. A redetermination (cw_determination_is_redetermination, CO-2375) is not an initial payment, and a case that states no application date is read as a full month. Coverage pass 6 CA6-2: a case that states an application date states whether the determination is a redetermination (required, decision 4 of 2026-11-23); before, an unstated value was read as an application. Coverage pass 3 (CW3-3): a unit that applied on September 25 and became eligible on October 3 is paid nothing for September (factor 0) and 29 days of October (.95342); before, September was paid as an entire month.

Type rate, scope person-month, program ColoradoWorks.
Uses: `cw_application_date`, `cw_determination_is_redetermination`, `cw_partial_month_payment_factor_table`, `cw_unit_eligible_from_date`.

```
    - it is not the case that Colorado Works: application date is unknown
    - it is not the case that Colorado Works: determination is a redetermination
    - the month is less than the month containing Colorado Works: date a unit ineligible on the date of application became eligible, otherwise Colorado Works: application date
  then 0
else if all of the following are true:
    - it is not the case that Colorado Works: application date is unknown
    - it is not the case that Colorado Works: determination is a redetermination
    - the month is equal to the month containing Colorado Works: date a unit ineligible on the date of application became eligible, otherwise Colorado Works: application date
    - it is not the case that (Colorado Works: date a unit ineligible on the date of application became eligible, otherwise Colorado Works: application date) is equal to the first day of the month
  then Colorado Works: partial month payment factors (table), for the number of days from Colorado Works: date a unit ineligible on the date of application became eligible, otherwise Colorado Works: application date to the first day of the month after the month
otherwise 1
```

### CO-4361 Colorado Works: room, board, and room and board income `@engine`

The payments this person received in the month from boarders and lodgers that Colorado Works counts as earned income (9 CCR 2503-6 3.605.2.E.4.c-e): room and board payments less, for each boarder, the maximum Food Assistance allotment for a one-person household and the other documented expenses directly related to providing the room and board (E.4.e); board-only payments less the same allotment for each person paying and the documented expenses of providing the board (E.4.c); and room-only (lodging) payments less the documented expenses directly related to providing the room (E.4.d). Each part is never below zero.

Precision. Earned-income records, step E1 Colorado Works (docs/reviews/records-earnings-cash.md): each part is the earnings records (earnings, CO-5100) received in the month of kind boarder_payments that provide it (provides: room_and_board, board_only or room_only), other than foster care payments, which cw_earnings_treatment_table (CO-5104) counts above the boarder allowance; the number of boarders is each record's boarders, read only where its part's payments are more than 0; the costs are the business_cost_boarder_provision records that provide it (deducted_from_boarder_payments). Room only: no allotment is deducted, since E.4.d names none. The allotment is the SNAP maximum allotment for one person (snap_maximum_allotment_table, CO-130, read for 1) in force in the month the payments are received (read in the month evaluated, docs/operators.md, Resolution; time audit T-3). Boarder payments that are foster care payments (foster_care) are not counted: 3.605.4.B.11 exempts the income of a Title IV foster child and the volume reads foster care provider payments as exempt (cw_receipt_treatment_table, CO-5650: foster_care_payment excluded). Before earnings records the room and board part read room_and_board_payments_received, its payer count, its costs and the foster care flag (the costs and flag read as 0 and false when not stated), and the board-only and room-only parts read the receipts of kind board_only_payment and room_only_payment with their cost facts; those receipt rows are now read_as_earnings (cw_receipt_treatment_table), so a transition copy stated in both lists is counted once. An unstated earnings list is cannot determine (decision 4 of 2026-11-23: E.4.c-e count the payments received and give no reading for payments not reported); a stated empty list is no boarder income. Coverage pass 3 (CW3-1) withdrew the earlier reading that a lodger's payment is rent counted as unearned income. Coverage pass 4 CA4-9 (docs/reviews/coverage4-cash.md): a stream (an earnings record with no month and no date) is read only in the months from the month of its job_start_date through the month of its job_end_date, so the pay of a job that ended before the month, or begins after it, is not counted (9 CCR 2503-5 3.520.781.G, 9 CCR 2503-6 3.605.2.B: income counted when received); a record stated with its month or date is read in that month.
