### CO-4363 Colorado Works: money from a sponsor counted as a gift `@engine`

The money this non-citizen received in the month from a sponsor or a sponsor's spouse living elsewhere (the receipts Colorado Works' counting table treats as a sponsor's contribution, cw_receipt_treatment_table: sponsor_contribution) that Colorado Works counts as unearned income, a gift (9 CCR 2503-6 3.605.3.A.14): all of it when sponsor deeming does not apply; none when it does, since the sponsor's net income is then deemed to the unit (cw_sponsor_deemed_income, CO-2365) and the money is part of that income.

Precision. Receipt records, migration phase 2 (docs/reviews/receipts-migration-2-cw.md): the money is the month's receipts of the kind sponsor_payment. When deeming does not apply and the receipts are not stated, the amount cannot be determined: 3.605.3.A.14 counts gifts received and gives no reading for gifts not reported (decision 4 of 2026-11-23 (docs/plan-colorado.md): missing information is cannot determine unless the rule says otherwise; the default of 0 kept from money_received_from_sponsor, CO-3707, is removed, as it is from SNAP's sponsor money, CO-3701); a stated empty list is no money from a sponsor, 0. Kept apart from cw_countable_unearned_income (CO-908) because cw_sponsor_deeming_applies (CO-2364) reads CO-908 for the combined-income test. Field sweep fix round (docs/reviews/field-sweep-snap-cash-nonmagi.md, FS-CW-1): a stream (a receipt with no month and no date) is read only in the months from the month of its start_date through the month of its end_date, as SNAP's readers read it (snap_counted_recurring_receipts, CO-5011), since income is "the receipt by a client of a gain or benefit in cash or in-kind during a calendar month" and the unit's income is what it has "received, or ... expects to receive in the application month and any month following" (9 CCR 2503-6 3.605.1.A.2, B, S4911): a pension that ended, or one not yet begun, is received in no month outside those dates; a receipt stated with its month or date is read in that month. Before, a stream was read in every month whatever its dates.

Type money, scope person-month, program ColoradoWorks.
Uses: `cw_receipt_treatment_table`, `cw_sponsor_deeming_applies`, `receipts`.

```
if Colorado Works: sponsor deeming applies
  then 0
otherwise the sum of that receipt's amount for each receipt in Receipts where ((all of the following are true:;   - Colorado Works: how each kind of receipt is treated (table), for that receipt's kind is equal to sponsor_contribution;   - all of the following are true:;     - that receipt is received in the month;     - any of the following is true:;       - it is not the case that that receipt's month is unknown;       - all of the following are true:;         - any of the following is true:;           - that receipt's start date is unknown;           - the month containing that receipt's start date is at most the month;         - any of the following is true:;           - that receipt's end date is unknown;           - the month containing that receipt's end date is at least the month))
```

### CO-4369 Colorado Works: unearned income deductions `@engine`

The amounts Colorado Works takes off this person's counted unearned receipts for the month (cw_counted_unearned_receipts, CO-5651) besides the receipts its counting table exempts or treats as earned and the parts of a receipt it leaves out as fields of the receipt (cw_receipt_treatment_table, CO-5650): the allowable expenses paid on rental property (9 CCR 2503-6 3.605.3.A.2), up to the month's rent; and, for a spouse, parent or stepparent who is not in the assistance unit, a military allotment received for persons not living in the home up to the need standard for those persons (3.605.3.B.10).

Precision. Receipt records, migration phase 3 (docs/reviews/receipts-migration-3.md): what is left here is an expense, which is not a receipt, and the one deduction that turns on the person and a count of other persons. The money the scalar facts stated as a part of a counted receipt is now its own receipt kind or field, so it is no longer taken off here: savings account distributions (3.605.4.B.20-22, B.25), an SMIB refund (3.605.3.B.9) and insurance cash value (B.30) are kinds the counting table excludes; board-only and room-only payments are kinds it treats as earned income (3.605.2.E.4.c-d; cw_boarder_income, CO-4361); the amounts of a one-time receipt spent on the costs it covers or designated for the costs of obtaining it are its spent_on_covered_costs and designated_for_lump_sum_costs, which cw_counted_unearned_receipts leaves out (3.605.3.A.5-6, 3.605.4.B.33). Before phase 3 these were neutral facts read as 0 when not stated (savings_account_distributions_received, CO-3816; medicare_premium_refund_received, CO-4370; insurance_cash_value_withdrawn, CO-4368; board_only_payments_received, CO-4832; room_only_payments_received, CO-4830; lump_sum_amounts_spent_or_designated, CO-4365), all retired. Rental expenses (rental_property_expenses_paid, CO-4458) reduce only the rent, the month's receipts of kind rental_income, and are taken up to that amount (A.2: "countable to the extent it exceeds allowable expenses"); they are read only when the person has rental income in the month, and required then (coverage pass 4 CA4-16, decision 4 of 2026-11-23; before, they were read as 0 when not stated, and a rent stated before receipt records in the other unearned kinds was capped with them; a rent is now stated as rental_income). Coverage pass 3 (CW3-4): the allotment for persons outside the home is the for_person_living_elsewhere of the person's military_allotment receipts (it was military_allotment_received_for_persons_outside_home, CO-4836, part of the other nontaxable receipts; when the receipts are not stated the deduction cannot be determined, since B.10 gives no reading for an allotment not reported (decision 4 of 2026-11-23 (docs/plan-colorado.md): missing information is cannot determine unless the rule says otherwise; the default of 0 kept from CO-4836 is removed); a stated empty list is no allotment, 0) and its persons military_allotment_persons_outside_home_count (CO-4837); the person is a non-recipient when outside every unit (cw_is_excluded_from_assistance_unit, CO-2350) or a disqualified member (cw_is_disqualified_member, CO-928); the need standard for those persons is the No Caretaker row for that number of children (cw_need_standard_table_no_caretaker, CO-351, up to ten; OQ-860), and up to that amount of the allotment is taken off. An allotment for persons in the home is counted with the other unearned income; a stepparent's or parent's deeming already deducts the needs of those in the home (3.605.1.A.4.a; OQ-860). The readers subtract this item from the counted receipts and floor the result at zero. Field sweep fix round (docs/reviews/field-sweep-snap-cash-nonmagi.md, FS-CW-1): a stream (a receipt with no month and no date) is read only in the months from the month of its start_date through the month of its end_date, as SNAP's readers read it (snap_counted_recurring_receipts, CO-5011), since income is "the receipt by a client of a gain or benefit in cash or in-kind during a calendar month" and the unit's income is what it has "received, or ... expects to receive in the application month and any month following" (9 CCR 2503-6 3.605.1.A.2, B, S4911): a pension that ended, or one not yet begun, is received in no month outside those dates; a receipt stated with its month or date is read in that month. Before, a stream was read in every month whatever its dates. Pattern sweep (cash) PS-D5 (docs/reviews/pattern-sweep-cash.md): whether the person is excluded from the unit or disqualified is read with no default (decision 4); the county's findings inside them keep their readings.

Type money, scope person-month, program ColoradoWorks.
Uses: `cw_is_disqualified_member`, `cw_is_excluded_from_assistance_unit`, `cw_need_standard_table_no_caretaker`, `military_allotment_persons_outside_home_count`, `receipts`, `rental_property_expenses_paid`.

### CO-4372 Colorado Works: excluded for status or SSN verification not provided `@engine`

This person has not provided, within the thirty calendar days of 9 CCR 2503-6 3.604.3.K, a verification of citizenship, qualified non-citizen status, lawful presence, identity or social security number that is pending for the person: "Individuals unable to provide this verification will not receive payment for themselves and their income will be used to determine eligibility for the household" (K, last paragraph; 3.604.3.I.3).

Precision. The determination date is after the person's thirty-day due date (cw_status_verification_due_date, CO-1656) and, in the month of the determination date, the person has at least one such element pending (cw_person_pending_status_verification_count, CO-1655). Where no verification request date is stated the thirty days have not begun, so the person is not excluded; the same reading as cw_verification_status (CO-1427), whose members_excluded result rests on the same two tests. The person is left out of the unit's size (cw_assistance_unit_members_for_size, CO-2351) and reported ineligible_member_verification (cw_person_participation_status, CO-2561); the person's income still counts as a member's (CO-910, CO-923).

Type yes/no, scope person, program ColoradoWorks.
Uses: `cw_person_pending_status_verification_count`, `cw_status_verification_due_date`.

```
(all of the following are true:;   - the Determination Date is more than Colorado Works: status verification due date;   - Colorado Works: person's pending status verification count for the month containing the Determination Date is more than 0), otherwise no
```

### CO-4400 Adult Financial: sponsor deeming applies `@engine`

Whether a sponsor's income and resources are deemed to this Adult Financial client (9 CCR 2503-5 3.520.69.B-C): the client is not a citizen or national, is sponsored on an affidavit of support (is_sponsored_non_citizen), and the sponsor's obligation has not ended - the client has fewer than federal_qualifying_quarters_threshold qualifying quarters of coverage under Title II (B.2), not every sponsor has died (B.5: "The death of one sponsor does not terminate the support obligation of a joint sponsor"), and the client was not admitted as a refugee or political asylee (C.1), here a lawful permanent resident who adjusted from refugee or asylee status.

Precision. Citizenship (B.1) is read from is_us_citizen_or_national. The forty quarters are qualifying_quarters (CO-004), which already includes quarters credited from a spouse or parent; read as 0 when not stated, so deeming applies, as before this item. The sponsor's death is sponsor_has_died (CO-2336: every individual who signed has died), read as false when not stated. A non-citizen admitted as a refugee or asylee who has not adjusted states that immigration_status and has no affidavit of support; one who adjusted states status_before_lpr_adjustment (CO-2700), read as none when not stated. B.3 (the client leaves the United States and gives up permanent residence) ends Colorado residence and lawful permanent resident status, which the residency and citizenship items read; B.4 (the client dies) leaves nothing to determine; B.6 (a new grant of admission on a new affidavit) is stated as the new affidavit and its sponsors (sponsors, CO-2713). Coverage review 2, G-8 (2): the removal of the non-citizen (3.520.69.B.6) is not a separate condition: a new grant of admission status rests on a new affidavit of support, whose signer the case states as the sponsor (sponsored_by), so deeming follows the new obligation. Coverage pass 4 CA4-16: a sponsored non-citizen's qualifying quarters are required, never read as 0 when not stated (decision 4 of 2026-11-23: missing information is cannot determine unless the rule says otherwise). Coverage pass 6 CA6-7 (docs/reviews/coverage6-cash.md): the status before adjustment (3.520.69.C.1) is required where read (decision 4 of 2026-11-23); before, read as none when not stated. Pattern sweep (cash) PS-M2 (docs/reviews/pattern-sweep-cash.md): per month: deeming ends when every sponsor of the case has died before the month's first day (af_sponsors_in_month, CO-7604; 3.520.69.B.5), not when every sponsor has died by the determination month (sponsor_has_died), which ended deeming for an application month in which the sponsor lived.

Type yes/no, scope person-month, program AdultFinancial.
Uses: `af_sponsors_in_month`, `federal_qualifying_quarters_threshold`, `is_sponsored_non_citizen`, `is_us_citizen_or_national`, `qualifying_quarters`, `sponsors`, `status_before_lpr_adjustment`.

```
all of the following are true:
  - it is not the case that Is a U.S. citizen or national
  - Is a sponsored non-citizen
  - Qualifying quarters is less than Federal qualifying quarters threshold (40)
  - it is not the case that (all of the following are true:;   - (the number of persons in Sponsors) is more than 0;   - (the number of persons in Adult Financial: the client's sponsors in the month) is equal to 0)
  - it is not the case that Status before lawful permanent residence is one of: refugee, asylee
```

### CO-4401 Adult Financial: presumed not a resident because of an absence from Colorado `@engine`

Whether this client's absence from Colorado creates the rebuttable presumption of 9 CCR 2503-5 3.520.64.E that the client is no longer a resident and is ineligible for Adult Financial programs, and the client has not rebutted it: the client has been out of the country af_out_of_country_presumption_days (30) or more consecutive days (E.1); has been out of the State af_out_of_state_presumption_days (90) or more consecutive days, other than to receive medical treatment (E.2) or to care for an immediate family member injured in the line of military duty (E.4); has been out of the State af_out_of_state_extended_presumption_days (180) or more consecutive days to care for such a family member (E.4); or has been out of the State more than af_out_of_state_extended_presumption_days days in the calendar year, consecutive or not (E.3).

Precision. The consecutive days are counted from the date the client left Colorado (temporarily_out_of_state_start_date, CO-3806) to the determination date (days_between); a client in Colorado states no date and is read as not absent. Out of the country is temporary_absence_is_outside_united_states (CO-4402); the medical exception of E.2 is temporary_absence_reason (CO-3351) medical_treatment, documented as E.2 requires; the E.4 absence is is_out_of_state_caring_for_family_member_injured_in_military_duty (CO-4404), read in place of E.2's ninety days (OQ-780); the calendar-year count is days_out_of_state_in_calendar_year (CO-4403). Each is read as false or 0 when not stated. The client's rebuttal ("unless the client comes forward with enough information to prove otherwise") is the county's finding af_nonresidence_presumption_rebutted (CO-4405), read as false when not stated. Read by af_meets_residency (CO-942), so every Adult Financial program, Home Care Allowance included, applies it; Home Care Allowance's own thirty days (3.570.17.C.8.b) are in af_hca_eligibility_status (CO-1217). Time audit T-6: "N consecutive days" is counted as the days elapsed since the day the absence or stay began (days_between), the day of departure or entry itself not counted (OQ-953): "a period of thirty (30) or more consecutive days", "ninety (90) or more" and "one hundred eighty (180)" (3.520.64.E, S3201): the days elapsed since the day of departure, so a client who left on August 1 reaches thirty days on August 31. Coverage pass 4 CA4-16: the days spent outside Colorado in the calendar year (E.3) are required where read (a client who has not left Colorado states 0), never read as 0 when not stated (decision 4 of 2026-11-23: missing information is cannot determine unless the rule says otherwise). Coverage pass 6 CA6-7 (docs/reviews/coverage6-cash.md, probe A5): for a client stated to be out of Colorado, where the absence is (another country, 3.520.64.E.1, 30 days), its reason (medical treatment, E.2) and whether the client is caring for a family member injured on military duty (F, 180 days) are required (decision 4 of 2026-11-23); before, read as another State, none and false, so a client away 45 days whose absence abroad was not stated was paid ($452) where abroad she is presumed a nonresident (none). Pattern sweep (cash) PS-T9 (docs/reviews/pattern-sweep-cash.md): per month: the consecutive days are counted to the month's reading day, the month's last day for a month before the determination month, the determination date otherwise. The calendar-year count (days_out_of_state_in_calendar_year) is a count through the determination date and stays so (no record of each absence's dates is stated), which the review lists.

### CO-4410 Adult Financial: homeless `@engine`

Whether the person is homeless as 9 CCR 2503-5 3.510 defines it: no permanent living arrangement, neither a member of a household nor a resident of an institution - sleeping in a supervised shelter, a halfway house or similar facility giving temporary residence, a place not designed for or ordinarily used as regular sleeping accommodations, or a motel, hotel, trailer park or campground for lack of an alternative, or abandoned in a hospital; or staying with a succession of friends or relatives with no permanent living arrangement.

Precision. Read from nighttime_residence_type (CO-2810, the primary nighttime residence on the determination date). A stay in another person's home (shared_housing_due_to_loss_or_hardship or shared_housing_other_temporary) is homeless only when the person moves among a succession of friends or relatives with no permanent arrangement (stays_with_succession_of_others_without_permanent_arrangement, CO-4411, read as false when not stated): a client living rent-free in one relative's home after losing her own is a member of that household, the usual case for in-kind support and maintenance. The 3.510 list is illustrative ("This can mean"); the motel, campground and hospital options are read as homeless because each is the absence of a permanent living arrangement. Coverage pass 6 CA6-7: for a person in shared housing, whether she stays with a succession of others without a permanent arrangement (3.520.79.B.3) is required where read (decision 4 of 2026-11-23); before, read as false when not stated.

### CO-4412 Adult Financial: exempt part of liquid resources `@engine`

The part of this person's cash and convertible assets (af_cash_and_convertible_holdings, CO-5340) that 9 CCR 2503-5 3.520.77 exempts now, from the person's holdings records: an ABLE account (M) and the cash and convertible assets necessary for the person's trade or business (D.1.b) (row excluded); an income tax refund, the PTC rebate included, until twelve months after the date it was received (K); retroactive SSI or Social Security retirement or disability benefits through the ninth month after the month received (J); money from a bona fide loan in the month received (L); and proceeds held to restore or replace property, for three months (personal property) or six (real property, a replacement home included) after the month received, or longer with the county's good-cause extension (E, F); each at its value times the person's share.

Precision. Resource records, step H1 Adult Financial (docs/reviews/records-holdings-snap-af.md): each exempt holding is its own record dated by source_date (held_income_tax_refund, held_retroactive_ssa_benefit, held_loan_proceeds, held_replacement_proceeds), so the windows are applied to the date the money came in, where before the facts (CO-4172, CO-4413, CO-4414) said only that it came within the window and each part was read as 0 when not stated: a refund, retroactive payment or loan held with no date is cannot determine (decision 4 of 2026-11-23). K's twelve months run from the date received to the same day twelve months later (a day the later month lacks runs into the next month); J's nine months follow the month received (received in June 2026: exempt through March 2027); L's month is the month of the determination date. The loan exempt is the money from the loan still held (held_loan_proceeds), no longer the loan receipt of the determination month (receipts, kind loan), which says nothing of what is left of it. Replacement proceeds are exempt while the determination month is no later than af_replacement_proceeds_exemption_months_table months after the month received (E.3, F.3: counted "in the month following the month in which the time period expired") or the county has granted an extension (af_replacement_proceeds_extension_granted, read as no when not stated: an extension the county has not determined is not granted). A retroactive payment stated for the SSI method (CO-4639, with its date) and for Adult Financial (CO-4414) is one record, so Adult Financial now exempts the payment the SSI-method fact stated. Coverage pass 4 CA4-13 (docs/reviews/coverage4-cash.md): a figure of the month evaluated, from the holdings valued in that month (3.510 "Resources", S4791: "held as of the first day of a calendar month or as of the date of application"), so an application month before the determination month is judged by its own holdings; before, every month read the determination month's. A date the rule measures from is the determination date in the determination month and the first day of any other month.

### CO-4422 Adult Financial: countable value of self-support property `@engine`

The countable value of this person's non-business self-support property (9 CCR 2503-5 3.520.77.D.3-4), from the person's real property holdings records: for non-business income-producing property (income_producing, not used_in_trade_or_business), the equity of all such property less a combined exemption of at most af_self_support_property_equity_exemption ($6,000), to which each property adds its equity up to $6,000 only when its net annual return (net_annual_return) is at least af_income_producing_property_min_return_rate (6%) of its excluded equity, or the county excuses a shortfall beyond the client's control (D.4.c); plus the equity of property producing goods only for the household's own use (produces_for_household_use) over af_self_support_property_equity_exemption.

Precision. Resource records, step H1 Adult Financial (docs/reviews/records-holdings-snap-af.md): each property is its own record, so D.4.a's "the rate-of-return requirement applies individually to each. However, the total combined exemption for all such properties shall not exceed $6,000" is applied as written: before step H1 the properties were one figure and the test was applied to their total. A property's income_producing and used_in_trade_or_business are the county's to establish from the tax returns (D); not stated, the property is not self-support property and is counted in full as real property (af_countable_real_property, CO-5342). The net annual return is required where read (decision 4). Property used in a trade or business, tools for a job and licenses are exempt (D.1-2, D.5) and not read. The twelve- or twenty-four-month continuation of the exemption for property not now in use (D.1.c, D.3.c) is the county's statement of the property as still used. Coverage pass 4 CA4-13 (docs/reviews/coverage4-cash.md): a figure of the month evaluated, from the holdings valued in that month (3.510 "Resources", S4791: "held as of the first day of a calendar month or as of the date of application"), so an application month before the determination month is judged by its own holdings; before, every month read the determination month's. Field sweep defaults list (2026-11-23): af_found_unsaleable is read as the holdings record states it, its default false declared once on the schema (CO-5300) with the rule that gives it (9 CCR 2503-5 3.520.72.A (S1636): "Unless otherwise specified, a resource is countable"; the 3.520.741.D and 742.C exemptions are the county's to find (S3209)); before, this reader gave the default itself (otherwise false), which conventions rule 12 and decision 4 do not allow a reader. No value changes: the tests that leave the finding out read it as false, as before.

### CO-4443 Adult Financial: income from donated work hours `@engine`

The earned income Adult Financial counts for the person's donated work hours in the month (9 CCR 2503-5 3.520.784.A-B): when the work is regular and scheduled, a necessary service and work someone would have to be hired for, and averages more than af_donated_work_min_weekly_hours a week, the month's donated hours times the greater of the going community rate for similar work and the minimum wage; otherwise nothing.

Precision. The minimum wage is the full Colorado minimum wage (colorado_minimum_wage, CO-4730; OQ-781 resolved, coverage review 2, G-8 (3)): 3.520.784.B.2's "current minimum wage standard" for work in Colorado is the statewide wage every Colorado employer must pay (COMPS Order 7 CCR 1103-1 Rule 3.1, S3508), which the PAY CALC Order (7 CCR 1103-14) publishes; before, the federal figure ($7.25) stood in. Volunteer work for the betterment of the community (3.520.784.C) is not stated as donated work. Coverage pass 4 CA4-16 (docs/reviews/coverage4-cash.md): no fact is read as 0 or false when not stated (decision 4 of 2026-11-23: missing information is cannot determine unless the rule says otherwise): the weekly donated hours are required (a person with no donated work states 0), and the tests of A.1-3, the month's hours and the community rate are read only for work over five hours a week; before, every fact was read as 0 or false when not stated.

```

  then 0
else if it is not the case that Donated work is regular, necessary work someone would be hired for
  then 0
otherwise Unpaid work hours donated in the month times (the greater of Going hourly rate for the donated work and Colorado minimum wage (15.16))
```

### CO-4446 Adult Financial: AND barred as a patient of a mental-disease or tuberculosis institution `@engine`

Whether, this month, C.R.S. 26-2-111(1)(d) bars Aid to the Needy Disabled (AND-SO and AND-CS) payments to the person because the person is a patient in an institution for tuberculosis or mental diseases (a psychiatric or tuberculosis hospital, or another institution whose overall character is the care of persons with mental diseases), or a patient in a medical institution as a result of having been diagnosed as having tuberculosis or psychosis. Not read for the Old Age Pension: the volume reads the proviso that (1)(d) "shall not be applicable to or in any way affect the class of old age pension recipients provided for in subsection (2)(a)(III)" together with 9 CCR 2503-5 3.520.61.B and 3.532.D.3 (a personal needs allowance for an OAP client in a psychiatric facility) as leaving every OAP client outside the bar. Read literally the proviso spares only the (2)(a)(III) class, an inmate of a non-penal institution maintained by the state, a municipality or a county, so an OAP client who is a patient in a private psychiatric hospital would be barred (OQ-901, needs Legal).

Precision. Read from the neutral setting facts: residence_setting_type (CO-3330), residence_setting_is_primarily_for_mental_diseases (CO-3333, read as false when not stated), resides_in_medical_institution (CO-1742) and medical_institution_stay_is_for_tuberculosis_or_psychosis (CO-4445, read as false when not stated), as of the determination date. An institution for mental diseases here has no bed-count test: the statute names any institution for mental diseases, as the Old Age Pension Health Care Program's exclusion does (ma_oap_is_patient_in_tb_or_mental_health_institution, CO-1748, a Medicaid item this one does not read). The statute's first clause, an inmate of a public institution other than a patient of a public medical institution, is carried by af_is_inmate_of_correctional_institution (CO-3343) in af_meets_residency (3.520.61.B: a correctional institution); a public non-medical, non-correctional institution housing inmates is not otherwise stated in this volume. Coverage pass 6 CA6-7: for a resident of an institution, whether it is primarily for mental diseases, and for one in a medical institution, whether the stay is for tuberculosis or psychosis (C.R.S. 26-2-111(1)(d)), are required where read (decision 4 of 2026-11-23); before, read as false when not stated.

Type yes/no, scope person-month, program AdultFinancial.
Uses: `medical_institution_stay_is_for_tuberculosis_or_psychosis`, `residence_setting_is_primarily_for_mental_diseases`, `residence_setting_type`, `resides_in_medical_institution`.

```
  - all of the following are true:
```

### CO-4660 Colorado Works: a minor parent's non-participant parents in the home `@engine`

The parents of this person whose income 9 CCR 2503-6 3.605.1.A.4.a deems to her assistance unit: each person she is the child of (a stated parent edge) who is not a member of her assistance unit (a non-participant; a parent who requested inclusion under 3.604.2.C.2.g is a participant) and who lives in the same home as she does. Empty for a person with no such parent.

Precision. Living in the same home is read from lives_with (CO-1925; where no dwelling is stated the parent edge is read as living together, convention rule 17) and cw_is_considered_living_in_home (CO-3354) for both, as cw_caretaker_of reads the home. Whether the person is an unmarried minor parent is not tested here: cw_deemed_parent_income_of_minor_parent (CO-909) gates the deeming on it. Coverage pass 3 (P3-1): "non-participant" (3.605.1.A.4.a) is read as not a member of the minor parent's own assistance unit; a parent who receives Colorado Works in a separate unit (with the minor parent's siblings, the minor parent having applied apart under 3.604.2.C.1.b) is still deemed. Excluding that parent would make this item read the parent's own unit's eligibility, which reads this item through the minor parent's income; the parent's countable income in that unit is below the same need standard that cw_minor_parent_deeming_needs_deduction (CO-2000) deducts, so the deemed amount is $0 except where the two counts differ (redetermination child support averaging, for example). Pattern sweep (cash) PS-D2 (docs/reviews/pattern-sweep-cash.md): whether persons live together is read from lives_with as stated (dwelling_id), required where read (decision 4 of 2026-11-23; docs/conventions.md rule 17 as amended for Colorado Works and Adult Financial): no text on file says the persons of one application live together (9 CCR 2503-6 3.604.2.A, E, I build the unit from the persons living in the home; 9 CCR 2503-5 3.534.B.3 and 3.549.E name the household of the spouse and the parents in the home). Before, a person whose home was not stated was read as living with every related person of the case.

Type group of persons, scope person, program ColoradoWorks.
Uses: `cw_assistance_unit_members`, `cw_is_considered_living_in_home`, `lives_with`, `relationships`.

```
all persons in every person in the case such that
  all of the following are true:
    - this person is a child of that person
    - it is not the case that that person is in Colorado Works: assistance unit members
    - that person is in Lives with
    - Colorado Works: considered living in the home
    - that person's Colorado Works: considered living in the home
```

### CO-4720 Adult Financial: a deemed relative's or sponsor's unearned income after exemptions `@engine`

This person's unearned income for the month as Adult Financial deems it from a client's spouse, an AND-CS child's parent or a sponsor: the counted unearned receipts and the exclusions the client's own income takes (af_counted_unearned_receipts and the person's exclusions, as in af_unearned_income_other_than_ssi; 9 CCR 2503-5 3.520.786: "Certain earned and unearned income that is not countable to the client, client's spouse, or sponsor(s) in whole or in part is exempt"), plus the person's SSI and Adult Financial grant receipts (3.534.C, 3.544.F, 3.549.F test the relative's income against the standard), never below zero; the expenses of producing workers' compensation, insurance, school-attendance and rental receipts are left out of the counted receipts themselves (af_counted_unearned_receipts).

Precision. Receipt records, migration phase 1: the same counted receipts as the client's own income (one counting table, coverage review 3 H-1, H-2), so a spouse's or sponsor's income tax refund, energy assistance, educational grant or interest is not deemed (coverage review 2, G-1). The sponsor paragraphs' "total gross earned and unearned income" (3.534.D.1, 3.544.G.1, 3.549.G.1) is read after these exemptions, since 3.520.786 names the sponsor(s) and 3.510 defines countable income for the sponsor(s) "after the application of valid exemptions". The earned side is af_gross_earned_income (CO-3830). Coverage review 3 H-5: a spouse's or sponsor's Home Care Allowance is a receipt of kind home_care_allowance, which the counting table excludes (3.520.786.E), so it is neither deemed nor counted in the 3.534.C, 3.544.F and 3.549.F exemption tests; af_grant_receipts reads the other grants only.

Resource records, step H1 Adult Financial (docs/reviews/records-holdings-snap-af.md): each policy is estimated from its own purchase date, where before the person stated only the newest policy's date and its row was used for all of them. ### CO-5017 Adult Financial: a person's counted unearned receipts other than SSI `@engine`

The person's receipts of the month that Adult Financial's counting table counts, other than SSI and the Adult Financial grant, a receipt paid once in the month received (9 CCR 2503-5 3.520.785.B.1.a), each less the parts of it the rule leaves out: the part set aside under a PASS (3.520.786.I), the part of VA Aid and Attendance used for uncovered medical care (F), the medical, legal or related expenses of a workers' compensation claim that the award includes (claim_expense; 3.520.785.B.9: "deducted prior to determining the amount of countable unearned income"), and the part of life insurance proceeds spent on the insured's last illness and burial or of health insurance or injury proceeds spent or to be spent on medical care (spent_on_covered_costs; B.14-15); a savings account distribution at the part the person's federal return counts (taxable_amount); rental income less its allowable expenses (af_rental_expenses_deducted, B.20); and the benefits conditional on school attendance above the expenses of attendance (af_school_attendance_benefits_counted, B.16). A retroactive lump sum of SSI or of the grant is counted here, in the month received (OQ-887). The one figure the client's own income (af_unearned_income_other_than_ssi, CO-3831) and a deemed spouse's, parent's or sponsor's (af_relative_deemable_unearned_income, CO-4720) both read, before the exclusions that turn on the person (child support for an SSI-age child, life-threatening-condition gifts to a child, infrequent income). The part of a veterans benefit paid for a dependent (for_dependent) is the dependent's income, not the veteran's (3.520.785.B.4): it is left out of the veteran's figure and counted in the figure of the person of the case it is for (for_person), whoever's list the record is on.

Precision. Coverage pass 4 (docs/reviews/coverage4-cash.md): CA4-1, the parts of a receipt B.9, B.14 and B.15 deduct are its fields claim_expense and spent_on_covered_costs (receipts, CO-5000), as Colorado Works reads them (cw_counted_unearned_receipts, CO-5651); before, Adult Financial left the fields unread and subtracted a second statement of the same money (unearned_income_offsetting_expenses, CO-4444, read as 0 when not stated), so a household stated per the record schema was counted gross. The rental expenses and the expenses of school attendance are facts of the person, not parts of a receipt, so they are read outside the sum by their own items, each only when the person has such a receipt (decision 4: required where read). CA4-3: a loan, a reimbursement, the proceeds of a resource and cash value taken from a policy are not income (their rows are not_income); a savings account distribution counts at its taxable_amount, which a record must state where this item reads it. Field sweep fix round (docs/reviews/field-sweep-snap-cash-nonmagi.md, FS-AF-1): a stream (a receipt with no month and no date) is read only in the months from the month of its start_date through the month of its end_date, as SNAP's readers read it (snap_counted_recurring_receipts, CO-5011), since "All income shall be countable in the month it is actually received or legally becomes available" (9 CCR 2503-5 3.520.781.G, S4910): a pension that ended, or one not yet begun, is received in no month outside those dates; a receipt stated with its month or date is read in that month. Before, a stream was read in every month whatever its dates. Field sweep fix round (FS-AF-2): 3.520.785.B.4 (S4044): "Any portion of a VA pension paid to a veteran for support of a dependent shall be considered countable unearned income to the dependent rather than to the veteran." Before, the part was counted for the veteran and for no one else. The dependent's part is read from the receipts of a counted kind received in the month, on the stated receipts list of any person of the case, whose for_person names this person (the record field of type person, compared with this person as the persons joined to this person by no edge, [reachable, [spouse], false]: the person alone, read only for a record that names someone); a case of one person has no one else's award (0). A person of the case whose receipts list is not stated gives no dependent part here: that person's own income is then unknown to every figure that reads it (a spouse, parent or sponsor deemed, a member of the unit), so the outcome cannot be determined there already, and a person no program reads (a relative in another home) is not asked for a list only to look for an award naming this person. A part for someone not in the case (for_person not stated) is the dependent's outside the case and no one's here. Whether the dependent lives with the veteran does not matter to B.4.

Type money, scope person-month, program AdultFinancial.
Uses: `af_receipt_treatment_table`, `af_rental_expenses_deducted`, `af_school_attendance_benefits_counted`, `receipts`, `relationships`.

### CO-5019 Adult Financial: a person's grant receipts `@engine`

The Adult Financial grant payments (Old Age Pension, Aid to the Needy Disabled, Aid to the Blind; not the Home Care Allowance, af_home_care_allowance_receipts) the person received in the month, other than a retroactive lump sum: the receipt of a grant that 3.532.B.3, 3.534.C, 3.570.43.A.1 and 3.570.52 ask about, and a relative's or sponsor's income (3.534.C).

Precision. Field sweep fix round (docs/reviews/field-sweep-snap-cash-nonmagi.md, FS-AF-1): a stream (a receipt with no month and no date) is read only in the months from the month of its start_date through the month of its end_date, as SNAP's readers read it (snap_counted_recurring_receipts, CO-5011), since "All income shall be countable in the month it is actually received or legally becomes available" (9 CCR 2503-5 3.520.781.G, S4910): a pension that ended, or one not yet begun, is received in no month outside those dates; a receipt stated with its month or date is read in that month. Before, a stream was read in every month whatever its dates.

Type money, scope person-month, program AdultFinancial.
Uses: `af_receipt_treatment_table`, `receipts`.

```
the sum for each receipt in Receipts where
    all of the following are true:
      - Adult Financial: how each kind of receipt is treated (table), for that receipt's kind is equal to not_income_to_client
      - it is not the case that that receipt's retroactive
      - all of the following are true:
        - that receipt is received in the month
        - any of the following is true:
          - it is not the case that that receipt's month is unknown
          - all of the following are true:
            - any of the following is true:
              - that receipt's start date is unknown
              - the month containing that receipt's start date is at most the month
            - any of the following is true:
              - that receipt's end date is unknown
              - the month containing that receipt's end date is at least the month
  of
    that receipt's amount
```

### CO-5130 Adult Financial: pay received in the month `@engine`

The pay this person received in the month for services performed as an employee, as 9 CCR 2503-5 3.520.782 counts it: the earnings records (earnings, CO-5100) received in the month whose kind Adult Financial's earnings table (af_earnings_treatment_table, CO-5103) counts as pay, gross monetary wages (3.520.782.A) at their amount, in-kind pay and an employer's payment of a household expense as part of the person's pay at the value of the item supplied (3.510 "Earned Income", 3.520.782.B), a difficulty of care payment that is not a foster care payment (3.520.786.M), and special pay stated as combat-zone pay (combat_zone, OQ-1140); pay under contract employment at one twelfth of the contract's yearly pay (annual_contract_pay; 3.520.781.G.2.b, af_annual_contract_months); and a pay stated as a stream (no month, no date) only in the months from the month its job began through the month it ended (job_start_date, job_end_date; 3.520.781.G: income "countable in the month it is actually received"). A business's receipts, boarder payments and costs are counted elsewhere (af_self_employment_net_profit, CO-1708; af_boarder_income, CO-5131); exempt pay (work-study, 37 U.S.C. 310 special pay) is not counted (3.520.786).

Precision. Earned-income records, step E1 Adult Financial (docs/reviews/records-earnings-cash.md). The same for the client, the client's spouse and the sponsor(s) (3.520.782.B.2 names all three). A record that recurs (no month and no date) is received in every month; a pay received once is placed by its month or date. The exemptions that turn on a field of the pay (a PASS set-aside, 3.520.786.I; infrequent or irregular pay, O) are taken off by af_excluded_earned_income (CO-2342). An unstated earnings list is cannot determine (product-owner decision 4 of 2026-11-23); a stated empty list is no pay. Coverage pass 4 (docs/reviews/coverage4-cash.md): CA4-6, the employer's vendor payment is counted by the table (it was not counted for want of a rule); CA4-7, a difficulty of care payment stated as foster care (foster_care) is exempt, as LEAP and CCCAP read it; CA4-8, a record that states annual_contract_pay is read at one twelfth of it in place of its amount, as SNAP (CO-5113) and CCCAP (CO-5152) read it, so the months of the year without contract pay count the twelfth too; CA4-9, a stream is counted only in the months its job's dates cover (a stream with no job dates began before and continues through the months the case covers, CO-5100), so the pay of a job that ended before the month, or begins after it, is not counted; a pay stated with its month or date is counted in that month, a final pay after the job ended included.

Uses: `af_annual_contract_months`, `af_earnings_treatment_table`, `earnings`.

### CO-5131 Adult Financial: income from boarders `@engine`

The payments this person received in the month from persons who pay for regular meals only (board), lodging only (room), or regular meals and lodging (room and board), which 9 CCR 2503-5 3.520.783.C.2.b-d counts as earned income in the month received, each less the documentable expenses directly related to providing it: for each of the three, the boarder payments (earnings records of kind boarder_payments that provide it, other than foster care payments, which 3.520.786.M exempts) less the costs of providing it (business_cost_boarder_provision records that provide it), never below zero.

Precision. Earned-income records, step E1 Adult Financial (docs/reviews/records-earnings-cash.md). The kinds are read through af_earnings_treatment_table (CO-5103: boarder_payments counted_less_provision_costs, business_cost_boarder_provision deducted_from_boarder_payments). C.2 subtracts, per boarder, the expenses of providing the board or room; the costs are stated as records of what they provide, so the sum of a kind's costs is the sum of its boarders' expenses. Unlike Colorado Works (3.605.2.E.4.c, e) and Medicaid (8.100.3.K.10), Adult Financial deducts no Food Assistance allotment per boarder: C.2 names none. Before earnings records Adult Financial read no room and board payment (room_and_board_payments_received was not among its facts) and counted a payment for a room only or meals only as unearned income (af_receipt_treatment_table, CO-5016, counted because no rule excludes it); 3.520.783.C.2 counts each as earned income, so the earned income disregards apply. The same for the client, the client's spouse and the sponsor(s) (C.2.b-c name all three). An unstated earnings list is cannot determine; a stated empty list is no boarder income. Coverage pass 4 CA4-9 (docs/reviews/coverage4-cash.md): a stream (an earnings record with no month and no date) is read only in the months from the month of its job_start_date through the month of its job_end_date, so the pay of a job that ended before the month, or begins after it, is not counted (9 CCR 2503-5 3.520.781.G, 9 CCR 2503-6 3.605.2.B: income counted when received); a record stated with its month or date is read in that month.

### CO-5140 Colorado Works: pay received in the month `@engine`

The pay this person received in the month that Colorado Works counts as earned income (9 CCR 2503-6 3.605.2): the earnings records (earnings, CO-5100) received in the month whose kind Colorado Works' earnings table (cw_earnings_treatment_table, CO-5104) counts as pay: wages, salaries and commissions and the other pay no paragraph of 3.605.4 exempts (3.605.2.D.1: "Unless otherwise specified, any earned income is countable"), pay an employer diverts to a third party for the household's expenses (3.605.2.B.1), and in-kind pay at the value of the item supplied (3.605.2.A, G). A business's receipts, boarder payments and costs are counted elsewhere (cw_self_employment_net_profit, CO-1706; cw_boarder_income, CO-4361); exempt pay (work-study, WIOA on-the-job training and other subsidized employment, 3.605.4.B.24.a, B.35, B.16) is not counted.

Precision. Earned-income records, step E1 Colorado Works (docs/reviews/records-earnings-cash.md). The same for a member of the assistance unit and every person whose income is deemed to it. A record that recurs (no month and no date) is received in every month; a pay received once is placed by its month or date (3.605.1.A.2: income is countable when actually available; 3.605.2.B: wages are available when paid). A temporary job's pay and a dependent student's earnings are counted here and taken off by cw_excluded_earned_income (CO-2340). An unstated earnings list is cannot determine (product-owner decision 4 of 2026-11-23); a stated empty list is no pay. Coverage pass 4 CA4-9 (docs/reviews/coverage4-cash.md): a stream (an earnings record with no month and no date) is read only in the months from the month of its job_start_date through the month of its job_end_date, so the pay of a job that ended before the month, or begins after it, is not counted (9 CCR 2503-5 3.520.781.G, 9 CCR 2503-6 3.605.2.B: income counted when received); a record stated with its month or date is read in that month. Coverage pass 4 CA4-7: a difficulty of care payment stated as foster care (foster_care) is not counted pay. Field sweep fix round (FS-CW-4): 3.605.2.B (S4912): wages are "considered available when paid rather than when earned, except that wages held at the request of the employee are considered income in the month they would otherwise have been paid". A pay that states its regular_date and that the employer held at the person's request (regular_date_reason held_at_request, a neutral field of the earnings record) is read in the month of its regular_date; a pay that came early or late for any other reason (a holiday or a weekend, changed pay dates) is read in the month it was paid, so regular_date_reason is required where regular_date is stated (decision 4). Before, every pay was read in the month it came in, so held wages fell into the next month. The contract employment the paragraph excepts is OQ-1295.

Uses: `cw_earnings_treatment_table`, `earnings`.

```
the sum for each receipt in Earnings where
    all of the following are true:

          then the month containing that receipt's regular date is equal to the month

  of
    that receipt's amount
```

### CO-5141 Colorado Works: pay from a job begun since the application `@engine`

The pay this person received in the month, of the kinds Colorado Works counts (cw_earned_pay), from a job that began on or after the unit's Colorado Works application date (cw_application_date): the earnings records whose job_start_date is on or after that date. It is the new source of earned income of 9 CCR 2503-6 3.606.2.A.2.a ("A new source of earned income shall receive a one hundred percent (100%) earned income disregard for the first certification period that the income impacts") when the month falls in that certification period (cw_is_new_earned_income_source, CO-1502); cw_payment_countable_earned_income (CO-922) reads it there.

Precision. Earned-income records, step E1 Colorado Works (docs/reviews/records-earnings-cash.md): replaces cw_new_source_earned_income (CO-2374), the part of wages_gross a case stated for a month with both a new and a current source (phase-10 sweep, OQ-350): each job is now its own record, so its start date (job_start_date; a record that states none began before the months the case covers, earnings CO-5100) says which pay is new. A source is new when it began while the unit was receiving basic cash assistance (3.606.2.A.2); the unit cannot have begun receiving before it applied, so a job begun before the application date is a current source, and one begun on or after it is new; a job begun after the application but before the unit was approved is within the first certification period, which A.1 disregards in full whatever the source. Whether the month falls in the first certification period that the new income impacts depends on the certification periods (six months, 3.606.1.E) and on when the change takes effect (3.606.3.A), which no supplied fact states; it stays the county's statement, cw_is_new_earned_income_source (OQ-1142). A business begun since the application is a new source too, but its receipts are counted net of costs (cw_self_employment_net_profit) and are not in this sum; a person whose only new source is a business states cw_is_new_earned_income_source alone, as before. The application date is read only for a record that states its job_start_date. An unstated earnings list is cannot determine. Coverage pass 4 CA4-9 (docs/reviews/coverage4-cash.md): a stream (an earnings record with no month and no date) is read only in the months from the month of its job_start_date through the month of its job_end_date, so the pay of a job that ended before the month, or begins after it, is not counted (9 CCR 2503-5 3.520.781.G, 9 CCR 2503-6 3.605.2.B: income counted when received); a record stated with its month or date is read in that month. Field sweep fix round (FS-CW-4): 3.605.2.B (S4912): wages are "considered available when paid rather than when earned, except that wages held at the request of the employee are considered income in the month they would otherwise have been paid". A pay that states its regular_date and that the employer held at the person's request (regular_date_reason held_at_request, a neutral field of the earnings record) is read in the month of its regular_date; a pay that came early or late for any other reason (a holiday or a weekend, changed pay dates) is read in the month it was paid, so regular_date_reason is required where regular_date is stated (decision 4). Before, every pay was read in the month it came in, so held wages fell into the next month. The contract employment the paragraph excepts is OQ-1295.

### CO-5207 Colorado Works: the child's parents in the home `@engine`

The persons who are this child's parent (natural or adoptive) and live in the home with the child, counting a temporary absence Colorado Works allows (cw_is_considered_living_in_home): the first rank of the caretaker hierarchy of 9 CCR 2503-6 3.604.2.H.1.

Precision. Read for a dependent child; for anyone else it is the same set and nothing reads it. Where the case states no dwelling_id, a stated parent edge is read as living in the home (convention rule 17). Pattern sweep (cash) PS-D2 (docs/reviews/pattern-sweep-cash.md): whether persons live together is read from lives_with as stated (dwelling_id), required where read (decision 4 of 2026-11-23; docs/conventions.md rule 17 as amended for Colorado Works and Adult Financial): no text on file says the persons of one application live together (9 CCR 2503-6 3.604.2.A, E, I build the unit from the persons living in the home; 9 CCR 2503-5 3.534.B.3 and 3.549.E name the household of the spouse and the parents in the home). Before, a person whose home was not stated was read as living with every related person of the case.

### CO-5208 Colorado Works: the child's relative or guardian caretakers in the home `@engine`

The persons in the home with this child who rank second in the caretaker hierarchy of 9 CCR 2503-6 3.604.2.H.2: the child's court-appointed legal guardian, or a relative by blood, marriage or adoption (is_related_to) who has primary responsibility for the child.

Precision. A relative must also exercise responsibility for the child (the has_primary_responsibility_for role) to be a caretaker at all (3.601). "Within the fifth degree of kinship" is read from is_related_to (CO-2845), whose roles (grandparent, sibling, stepparent, aunt, uncle, first cousin, niece, nephew, great-grandparent, in-law) are all within the fifth degree; the relationship roles state no degree, so a more distant relative stated as other_relative would be read as within it. A legal custodian appointed by a court is stated as legal_guardian. Pattern sweep (cash) PS-D2 (docs/reviews/pattern-sweep-cash.md): whether persons live together is read from lives_with as stated (dwelling_id), required where read (decision 4 of 2026-11-23; docs/conventions.md rule 17 as amended for Colorado Works and Adult Financial): no text on file says the persons of one application live together (9 CCR 2503-6 3.604.2.A, E, I build the unit from the persons living in the home; 9 CCR 2503-5 3.534.B.3 and 3.549.E name the household of the spouse and the parents in the home). Before, a person whose home was not stated was read as living with every related person of the case.

### CO-5340 Adult Financial: cash and convertible holdings `@engine`

The person's cash and convertible assets (9 CCR 2503-5 3.520.72.B.5-6, 3.520.73): the person's holdings records (holdings, CO-5300) valued in the determination month and still held whose row in af_holding_treatment_table (CO-5302) is a cash row - counted (cash, accounts, securities, installment contracts, mortgages and notes the person holds; personal property held as an investment, also counted, is af_countable_personal_property, CO-5345), counted because no rule excludes it, an annuity the person can assign or surrender (counted_if_revocable: an investment vehicle convertible to cash, 3.520.72.B.5, 3.510 "Convertible asset"), excluded (an ABLE account, business cash) or excluded for a time (refunds, retroactive benefits, loan proceeds and replacement proceeds still held) - each at its value times the person's share (3.520.73.A.2: a joint account "in proportion to the number of persons on the account"). The part exempt now is af_exempt_liquid_resources (CO-4412).

Precision. Resource records, step H1 Adult Financial (docs/reviews/records-holdings-snap-af.md): the money a rule exempts by its source is its own record (held_income_tax_refund, held_retroactive_ssa_benefit, held_loan_proceeds, held_replacement_proceeds), never a part of one liquid figure, so it is counted here once and exempted by CO-4412 while its window runs. An account the person cannot reach (accessible) is counted, as before: 3.520.72.A counts every resource "unless otherwise specified" and 3.520.741.D.1 does not treat a co-owner's refusal as a restriction; Adult Financial reads no accessible field. The value of an account is read as stated (no encumbrance, as before step H1); an installment contract and a mortgage or note the person holds are counted at their value less what is owed against them, never below zero (3.520.741.B.1, the equity, as the real property they were part of before step H1). Coverage pass 4 CA4-12: a surrenderable annuity is counted at its value (revocable, required where read); before, the annuity row counted none. CA4-22: a holding valued as of the date of application (3.510 "Resources", S4791: "less the value counted as income in the same month") is stated at its value less the month's income already counted in it; the stored households value holdings as of the first of the month, so nothing is subtracted. Coverage pass 4 CA4-13 (docs/reviews/coverage4-cash.md): a figure of the month evaluated, from the holdings valued in that month (3.510 "Resources", S4791: "held as of the first day of a calendar month or as of the date of application"), so an application month before the determination month is judged by its own holdings; before, every month read the determination month's.

Type money, scope person-month, program AdultFinancial.
Uses: `af_holding_treatment_table`, `holdings`.

```
the sum for each holding in Holdings where
    all of the following are true:
      - all of the following are true:
        - that holding is valued in the month
        - that holding's disposed date is unknown
      - any of the following is true:
        - Adult Financial: how each kind of holding is treated (table), for that holding's kind is one of: counted, counted_no_rule_excludes, excluded, excluded_within_twelve_months, excluded_within_nine_months, excluded_in_month_received, excluded_three_or_six_months
        - all of the following are true:
          - Adult Financial: how each kind of holding is treated (table), for that holding's kind is equal to counted_if_revocable
          - that holding's revocable
      - it is not the case that that holding's kind is equal to investment_personal_property
  of
    (if that holding's kind is one of: installment_contract, loan_receivable;   then the greater of 0 and (that holding's value minus that holding's amount owed); otherwise that holding's value) times (that holding's share, otherwise 1)
```

### CO-5342 Adult Financial: countable real property `@engine`

The equity of the person's real property other than the home that Adult Financial counts in full (9 CCR 2503-5 3.520.72.B.1, 3.520.741.B-C): each real_property record (row counted_less_self_support_and_unsaleable) at its value less what is owed on it ("the actual value less encumbrances"), times the person's share (741.C.2: "charged in proportion to the client, client's spouse, or sponsor(s)'s share of ownership"), leaving out property the county exempts because it cannot be sold for two-thirds of its value despite continuing efforts, its sale would cause a co-owner undue hardship, or legal reasons prevent its sale (af_found_unsaleable; 3.520.741.D), property used to produce income or goods for the household, which the self-support rules count (3.520.77.D; af_self_support_property_countable_value, CO-4422).

Precision. Resource records, step H1 Adult Financial (docs/reviews/records-holdings-snap-af.md): the self-support exemptions are the county's to establish: 3.520.77.D (S3206) exempts property "essential to the self-support of the client" and directs that "To determine whether property is producing income or being used in a trade or business, the county department shall obtain a copy of the most recent tax returns", and 3.520.72.A (S1636) counts a resource "Unless otherwise specified"; so a parcel whose record does not say it produces income (income_producing), is used in a trade or business (used_in_trade_or_business) or produces goods for the household (produces_for_household_use) is counted, the rule's own reading (design decision D3), as before step H1, when such property was stated apart from real_property_other_than_home_equity. Property used in the person's trade or business is self-support property and not counted (3.520.77.D.1). The county's finding that the property is unsaleable not stated is read as no: 3.520.741.D.3 exempts the property only once the county finds it cannot be sold for two-thirds of its value (the person fact it replaces, af_property_exempt_as_unsaleable_value, was read as 0 when not stated). Each parcel's equity is floored at 0, so a parcel owing more than it is worth does not lower another's. Installment contracts and the notes and mortgages the person holds are cash and convertible assets (3.520.72.B.6; CO-5340). (A request to the integration owner: these defaults belong on the fields, per program, docs/reviews/records-holdings-snap-af.md.) Coverage pass 4 CA4-13 (docs/reviews/coverage4-cash.md): a figure of the month evaluated, from the holdings valued in that month (3.510 "Resources", S4791: "held as of the first day of a calendar month or as of the date of application"), so an application month before the determination month is judged by its own holdings; before, every month read the determination month's. Field sweep defaults list (2026-11-23): af_found_unsaleable is read as the holdings record states it, its default false declared once on the schema (CO-5300) with the rule that gives it (9 CCR 2503-5 3.520.72.A (S1636): "Unless otherwise specified, a resource is countable"; the 3.520.741.D and 742.C exemptions are the county's to find (S3209)); before, this reader gave the default itself (otherwise false), which conventions rule 12 and decision 4 do not allow a reader. No value changes: the tests that leave the finding out read it as false, as before.

Type money, scope person-month, program AdultFinancial.
Uses: `af_holding_treatment_table`, `holdings`.

```
the sum for each holding in Holdings where
    all of the following are true:
      - all of the following are true:
        - that holding is valued in the month
        - that holding's disposed date is unknown
      - Adult Financial: how each kind of holding is treated (table), for that holding's kind is equal to counted_less_self_support_and_unsaleable
      - it is not the case that that holding's af found unsaleable
      - it is not the case that that holding's income producing, otherwise no
      - it is not the case that that holding's produces for household use, otherwise no
  of
    (the greater of 0 and (that holding's value minus that holding's amount owed)) times (that holding's share, otherwise 1)
```

### CO-5343 Adult Financial: countable vehicles `@engine`

The equity of the person's vehicles that Adult Financial counts (9 CCR 2503-5 3.520.72.B.4, 3.520.77.A): the equity of every vehicle record (row counted_less_highest_transportation_vehicle), each its value less what is owed on it times the person's share, never below zero, less the largest such equity of a vehicle used for the transportation of the client or a member of the household (used_for_transportation; P58 largest): "The vehicle with the highest value is exempt if it is used for the transportation of the client or a member of the household".

Precision. Resource records, step H1 Adult Financial (docs/reviews/records-holdings-snap-af.md): "highest value" is read as the highest equity (OQ-1205, assumption A), which is what P58 returns over the equities; each vehicle's equity is floored at 0 before the sum and before the largest (P58 returns the true largest, negative when every vehicle owes more than it is worth, docs/operators.md), so a vehicle owing more than it is worth neither adds nor exempts anything and never lowers what another vehicle counts. Before step H1 the household stated which vehicle was exempt (transportation_vehicle_equity_value, CO-3395) as a part of the vehicles' total. A vehicle that does not say whether it is used for transportation is cannot determine (decision 4; used_for_transportation is required where read). Coverage pass 4 CA4-10: the vehicle exempt is af_exempt_transportation_vehicle_equity (CO-6803); a married couple's single exemption is taken in the couple's figure (af_client_and_spouse_countable_resources, CO-2389, through CO-6804). Coverage pass 4 CA4-13 (docs/reviews/coverage4-cash.md): a figure of the month evaluated, from the holdings valued in that month (3.510 "Resources", S4791: "held as of the first day of a calendar month or as of the date of application"), so an application month before the determination month is judged by its own holdings; before, every month read the determination month's.

### CO-5344 Adult Financial: countable burial holdings `@engine`

The person's burial funds, contracts and spaces that Adult Financial counts (9 CCR 2503-5 3.520.72.B.8-9, 3.520.77.G-I): each revocable burial trust or prepaid burial contract (rows counted_above_burial_exemption, not irrevocable) over af_revocable_burial_funds_exemption ($1,500), each on its own (G.3: "A revocable burial trust is exempt if the value of the trust does not exceed $1,500 ... Any amount over $1,500 is a countable resource"; H.2), and the value of burial spaces beyond the burial needs of the immediate family (row counted_beyond_family_needs, not for_immediate_family; 3.520.72.B.9, 3.520.77.I), less what is owed on them (3.520.742.A.3: "first determine the actual value; then subtract encumbrances"), never below zero, times the person's share.

Precision. Resource records, step H1 Adult Financial (docs/reviews/records-holdings-snap-af.md): each trust and each contract has its own $1,500 exemption, as G.3 and H.2 state it of "the trust" and "the prepaid burial contract"; before step H1 the trusts were one total and the contracts another, each with one exemption, so two revocable trusts of $1,000 counted 2,000 - 1,500 = 500 and now count 0. An irrevocable contract is exempt (H.1); an irrevocable trust of which the client is both trustor and beneficiary is not irrevocable in the holdings record (its schema), so it is counted over $1,500 (G.2.d). The interest on the exempt $1,500 is exempt (G.3, H.2.b): the interest accrued is not read, as before (OQ-1253). What is owed on a burial space is required where read (decision 4; the fact before step H1, burial_spaces_value_beyond_family_needs, stated a value with no debt). Coverage pass 4 CA4-13 (docs/reviews/coverage4-cash.md): a figure of the month evaluated, from the holdings valued in that month (3.510 "Resources", S4791: "held as of the first day of a calendar month or as of the date of application"), so an application month before the determination month is judged by its own holdings; before, every month read the determination month's. Field sweep fix round (FS-AF-5): G.3 and H.2.b (S2619): "Any interest on the exempt $1,500 is also exempt." A revocable trust or contract whose principal (its value less the interest accrued in it, accrued_interest) is $1,500 or less is exempt whole, its interest being interest on the exempt $1,500: a $1,550 fund of which $50 is interest counts 0, where before 1,550 - 1,500 = 50 counted. accrued_interest is read only for a record whose value is over $1,500 (required there, decision 4). With a principal over $1,500, how the interest splits between the exempt $1,500 and the rest is still OQ-1253 (narrowed), and the value over $1,500 counts, interest included, as before.

### CO-5345 Adult Financial: countable personal property `@engine`

The equity of the personal property the person holds because of its value or as an investment, which Adult Financial counts (9 CCR 2503-5 3.520.77.B: "This does not include effects that the client holds because of the value or as an investment, which are countable as personal property as outlined in Section 3.520.742"): each investment_personal_property record (row counted) at its value less what is owed on it (3.520.742.A.3, B: "the appraised value less liabilities" of "art, jewelry or valuable collections"), times the person's share; and the other personal property the person owns, not household goods or personal effects the person uses in the home (personal_property records that do not state household_goods_or_personal_effects): equipment, livestock, tools, a mobile home or recreational vehicle not lived in (3.520.72.B.3-4, 3.520.742.B: "the appraised value less liabilities, i.e., vehicles, farm equipment and livestock"), at its value less what is owed on it times the person's share, unless the county finds it cannot be sold (af_found_unsaleable, 3.520.742.C) or it is used to produce income or goods for the household, which the self-support rules govern (3.520.77.D).

Precision. Resource records, step H1 Adult Financial (docs/reviews/records-holdings-snap-af.md): finding H0-F2 fixed (OQ-1203): before step H1 no Adult Financial item read investment_personal_property_value (CO-4642), so an OAP or AND client's collectibles were not counted. What is owed on the property is required where read (decision 4). Household goods and personal effects the client uses are exempt (3.520.77.B; row excluded_household_goods) and not read. Coverage pass 4 CA4-11 (docs/reviews/coverage4-cash.md): the holdings kind personal_property holds household goods and other personal property alike, and the table excluded the whole kind, so livestock or equipment was never counted; the record now says which it is (household_goods_or_personal_effects, CO-5300, required where read), and OQ-1203's part on this property is settled by the text. The county's findings (af_found_unsaleable) and the self-support properties (income_producing, produces_for_household_use) are read as not so when not stated, as for real property (CO-5342). Coverage pass 4 CA4-13 (docs/reviews/coverage4-cash.md): a figure of the month evaluated, from the holdings valued in that month (3.510 "Resources", S4791: "held as of the first day of a calendar month or as of the date of application"), so an application month before the determination month is judged by its own holdings; before, every month read the determination month's. Field sweep defaults list (2026-11-23): af_found_unsaleable is read as the holdings record states it, its default false declared once on the schema (CO-5300) with the rule that gives it (9 CCR 2503-5 3.520.72.A (S1636): "Unless otherwise specified, a resource is countable"; the 3.520.741.D and 742.C exemptions are the county's to find (S3209)); before, this reader gave the default itself (otherwise false), which conventions rule 12 and decision 4 do not allow a reader. No value changes: the tests that leave the finding out read it as false, as before.

Type money, scope person-month, program AdultFinancial.
Uses: `af_holding_treatment_table`, `holdings`.

```
the sum for each holding in Holdings where
    all of the following are true:

        - that holding's disposed date is unknown
      - any of the following is true:
        - all of the following are true:

          - that holding's kind is equal to investment_personal_property
        - all of the following are true:

          - it is not the case that that holding's household goods or personal effects
          - it is not the case that that holding's af found unsaleable
          - it is not the case that that holding's income producing, otherwise no
          - it is not the case that that holding's produces for household use, otherwise no
  of
```

### CO-5346 Adult Financial: countable home equity `@engine`

The equity of a home Adult Financial no longer exempts (9 CCR 2503-5 3.520.77.C): nothing for an OAP-C client during the commitment (C.4, receives_oap_c); otherwise each home record (row excluded_home_rules) that is not the person's principal place of residence (lives_in) and that the person does not intend to return to (intends_to_return; C.2, C.3), at its value less what is owed on it, times the person's share (C.5: "If a client's home can no longer be excluded due to a change in his or her principal place of residence, the equity value of the property shall count as a resource"). A home the person left to live in a long-term care facility (residence_setting_type a nursing facility, assisted living residence, intermediate care facility, group home, host home or other long-term care facility) stays exempt only when the intent to return is documented in writing (C.3.a; intent_in_writing); a home left for long-term medical care elsewhere needs the intent alone (C.2).

Precision. Resource records, step H1 Adult Financial (docs/reviews/records-holdings-snap-af.md): the home's own record says whether the person lives in it, in place of the person's residence setting (residence_setting_type), so a client living in a rented apartment who still owns a home she left without intent to return has its equity counted (C.5), where before only a client in a facility did. Whether the person lives in the home, and if not whether she intends to return, are required where read (decision 4); before step H1 an intent not stated was read as an intent to return (coverage review P2-5). Coverage pass 4 CA4-13 (docs/reviews/coverage4-cash.md): a figure of the month evaluated, from the holdings valued in that month (3.510 "Resources", S4791: "held as of the first day of a calendar month or as of the date of application"), so an application month before the determination month is judged by its own holdings; before, every month read the determination month's. Field sweep fix round (FS-AF-4): C.3 (S3218): "When a client requires care in a long-term care facility, the home continues to be exempt so long as there is intent for the client to return to the home. a. ... Such intent is documented by the following: 1) A written statement from the client ...; or, 2) A written statement from the client's spouse, legal fiduciary, doctor, or authorized representative". C.2 (long-term medical care outside the county) asks the intent only. Before, the intent was read alone in every setting, so a home left for a nursing facility with an unwritten intent stayed exempt. The setting is the person's residence_setting_type (the facilities 3.532.D.1-2 list as long-term care, the hospital left out), read only when a home the person intends to return to has no written statement. intent_in_writing defaults to false, the rule's: C.3.a requires the statement, so an intent not shown in writing is not documented. Pattern sweep (cash) PS-D6 (docs/reviews/pattern-sweep-cash.md): whether the client receives OAP-C (receives_oap_c, from adult_financial_program_received) is read with no default (decision 4), and only where it decides the figure: where some equity of a home not lived in would count; before, an unstated program was read as not OAP-C.

### CO-5350 Adult Financial: resources known, a lower bound `@engine`

The part of this person's countable resources other than life insurance that is known when some is not: each part af_person_countable_resources_other_than_life_insurance (CO-4000) adds (cash and convertible assets less what is exempt, retirement accounts, real property, self-support property, vehicles, burial holdings, personal property, the home, trusts, potential resources refused), each read as 0 when it cannot be determined. Every part is never below zero, so the person's countable resources are at least this much.

Precision. Resource records, step H1 Adult Financial (docs/reviews/records-holdings-snap-af.md): read by af_meets_resource_limit (CO-948): when the client's and the spouse's known parts already exceed the resource limit, the limit is not met whatever the parts that cannot be determined (each of which only adds), so the answer is given, not cannot determine. This is an inference from the rule, not a default for a fact: no part is taken as 0 in the countable resources themselves (decision 4). Coverage pass 4 CA4-13 (docs/reviews/coverage4-cash.md): a figure of the month evaluated, from the holdings valued in that month (3.510 "Resources", S4791: "held as of the first day of a calendar month or as of the date of application"), so an application month before the determination month is judged by its own holdings; before, every month read the determination month's.
