### CO-5651 Colorado Works: a person's counted unearned receipts `@engine`

The person's receipts of the month that Colorado Works' counting table counts (cw_receipt_treatment_table: counted, or counted because no rule excludes it), a receipt paid once in the month received, each less the parts of it the rule leaves out: income set aside under a plan for self-support (9 CCR 2503-6 3.605.4.B.15), the medical, legal and related expenses included in a workers' compensation award (3.605.3.B.4), VA Aid and Attendance used for medical supplies or medical or attendant care no insurance covers, for a person who lives in the person's own home (3.605.4.A.6; lives_in_own_home, CO-5940), the part of insurance or injury proceeds spent or to be spent on the last illness and burial or medical care (3.605.3.A.5-6, spent_on_covered_costs) and the part of a lump sum designated or legally obligated for legal fees of obtaining it, medical bills, funeral and burial or income taxes (3.605.4.B.33, designated_for_lump_sum_costs); and the benefits conditional on school attendance to the extent they exceed the expenses of attendance (3.605.3.A.4, cw_school_attendance_benefits_counted). Child support (3.605.5) and money from a sponsor (A.11, A.14) are counted by their own items. The one figure the eligibility test (cw_countable_unearned_income, CO-908), the grant (cw_payment_countable_unearned_income, CO-2554) and the income to verify (cw_has_countable_unearned_income, CO-2871) read, for a member of the unit and for every person whose income is deemed to it. The part of a veterans benefit paid for a dependent (for_dependent) is the dependent's income, not the veteran's (3.605.3.B.5): it is left out of the veteran's figure and counted in the figure of the person of the case it is for (for_person). The PASS set-aside is left out of Social Security benefit payments only (3.605.4.B.15).

Precision. Receipt records, migration phase 2 (docs/reviews/receipts-migration-2-cw.md): replaces the sum of the scalar unearned income facts less cw_excluded_unearned_income (CO-2341). A receipt is counted in each month it is stated for, or in every month when it states no month (P57); one paid once states its month or date, and a counted one-time receipt that states neither cannot determine. An amount withheld by garnishment or recoupment stays counted (3.605.3.A.12), so the recouped field is not read. Receipt records, migration phase 3: the parts the scalar facts stated of a counted receipt are now kinds of their own (board-only and room-only payments, treated as earned income; savings account distributions, an SMIB refund and insurance cash value, excluded; an adoption subsidy, excluded under 3.605.4.B.32; a military allotment, counted) or fields of it (spent_on_covered_costs and designated_for_lump_sum_costs, left out here, which cw_unearned_income_deductions took off as lump_sum_amounts_spent_or_designated before); only an allotment for persons outside the home is still taken off by cw_unearned_income_deductions (CO-4369), since it turns on the person and a count of other persons. VA Aid and Attendance (2026-11-23 follow-up): 3.605.4.A.6 (S2605) exempts the part "used for medical supplies and medical or attendant care not covered by Medicare or Medicaid, or other health insurance programs" as income "to determine eligibility for public assistance in the applicant's or recipient's own home", so the receipts' used_for_uncovered_medical_care is left out only when lives_in_own_home (CO-5940) is true; for a person who does not live in the person's own home (a care facility, another household's home as a guest, a shelter) the whole receipt is counted, A.6 giving no exemption there. Since a person fact cannot be read inside a receipt sum (docs/operators.md, P55), the part is summed over the same counted receipts and subtracted outside it; lives_in_own_home is asked only when that sum is more than 0, and when it is not stated the figure cannot be determined. Before, the part was left out in every setting. Whether a person living as a member of a relative's household, or as a guest in another's home, is in "own home" is OQ-1051. Field sweep fix round (docs/reviews/field-sweep-snap-cash-nonmagi.md, FS-CW-1): a stream (a receipt with no month and no date) is read only in the months from the month of its start_date through the month of its end_date, as SNAP's readers read it (snap_counted_recurring_receipts, CO-5011), since income is "the receipt by a client of a gain or benefit in cash or in-kind during a calendar month" and the unit's income is what it has "received, or ... expects to receive in the application month and any month following" (9 CCR 2503-6 3.605.1.A.2, B, S4911): a pension that ended, or one not yet begun, is received in no month outside those dates; a receipt stated with its month or date is read in that month. Before, a stream was read in every month whatever its dates. Field sweep fix round (FS-CW-2, FS-CW-3). FS-CW-2: 3.605.3.B.5 (S4001): "Any portion of a VA pension that is paid to a veteran for support of a dependent shall be considered countable unearned income to the dependent rather than the veteran." Before, the part was counted for the veteran and for no one else; for a stepparent or a parent outside the unit whose income is deemed (3.605.1.A.4), the part was deemed as the parent's. The dependent's part is read from the receipts of a counted kind received in the month, on the stated receipts list of any person of the case, whose for_person names this person (the record field of type person, compared with this person as the persons joined to this person by no edge, [reachable, [spouse], false]: the person alone, read only for a record that names someone); a case of one person has no one else's award (0). A person of the case whose receipts list is not stated gives no dependent part here: that person's own income is then unknown to every figure that reads it (a spouse, parent or sponsor deemed, a member of the unit), so the outcome cannot be determined there already, and a person no program reads (a relative in another home) is not asked for a list only to look for an award naming this person. A part for someone not in the case (for_person not stated) is the dependent's outside the case and no one's here. FS-CW-3: 3.605.4.B.15 (S2606) exempts "Social Security benefit payments and the accrued amount thereof paid to a client when an individual plan for self-care and/or self-support has been developed"; before, the set-aside was left out of every counted kind (a pension's set-aside included), which B.15 does not exempt. Colorado Works counts SSI not at all (3.605.4.B.27), so a set-aside of SSI is not read.

Type money, scope person-month, program ColoradoWorks.
Uses: `cw_receipt_treatment_table`, `cw_school_attendance_benefits_counted`, `lives_in_own_home`, `receipts`, `relationships`.

### CO-5652 Colorado Works: current child support received in the month `@engine`

The current child support received for this person in the month: the receipts Colorado Works' counting table treats as child support (cw_receipt_treatment_table: child_support), which 9 CCR 2503-6 3.605.5 counts against the need standard at application and, when consistent and averaging over $500 for the unit, at redetermination, and never in the grant. Arrears are their own kind, exempt (3.605.5.D), and are not part of it.

Precision. Receipt records, migration phase 2 (docs/reviews/receipts-migration-2-cw.md): replaces child_support_received less the arrears stated within it (child_support_arrears_received). The months before the determination month are read in each month (cw_child_support_months_received_of_last_six, CO-2550; cw_child_support_six_month_average, CO-2551), so a receipt summed for an earlier month reads that month. Child support turned over to the IV-D agency stays received (the transferred field is not read), as before receipt records. Field sweep fix round (docs/reviews/field-sweep-snap-cash-nonmagi.md, FS-CW-1): a stream (a receipt with no month and no date) is read only in the months from the month of its start_date through the month of its end_date, as SNAP's readers read it (snap_counted_recurring_receipts, CO-5011), since income is "the receipt by a client of a gain or benefit in cash or in-kind during a calendar month" and the unit's income is what it has "received, or ... expects to receive in the application month and any month following" (9 CCR 2503-6 3.605.1.A.2, B, S4911): a pension that ended, or one not yet begun, is received in no month outside those dates; a receipt stated with its month or date is read in that month. Before, a stream was read in every month whatever its dates.

Uses: `cw_receipt_treatment_table`, `receipts`.

The part of this person's benefits conditional upon school attendance that Adult Financial counts for the month: the U.S. Department of Veterans Affairs educational assistance (G.I. Bill) payments and other military or veterans benefits paid only while the person attends school, "to the extent that they exceed expenses necessary for school attendance" (9 CCR 2503-5 3.520.785.B.16). The expenses are school_attendance_expenses_paid (CO-4662), taken from these benefits only, never below zero.

The expenses are a fact of the person, which a receipt sum cannot read (docs/operators.md, P55), so they are subtracted here, from the benefits' sum; they are read only when the person has such benefits in the month, and required then (decision 4 of 2026-11-23: B.16 gives no reading for expenses not stated). The months a Colorado Works determination decides: at an application, the months from the month of the application (cw_application_date) through the determination month, since "all countable gross income received in the month prior to, if available, and in the month of application shall be used to determine eligibility" and the unit's income is what it has received or expects to receive "in the application month and any month following" (9 CCR 2503-6 3.605.1.A.1, B); at a redetermination (cw_determination_is_redetermination), and when the case states no application date or one after the determination month, the determination month alone.

### CO-7301 Colorado Works: pregnant in the month `@engine`

Whether the person was pregnant at some time in the month evaluated, for Colorado Works' expectant parent (9 CCR 2503-6 3.601: "'Parent' means an adoptive or natural/biological parent, including an expectant parent") and its pregnancy allowance, for which "the client is eligible ... through the month in which the pregnancy ends" (3.606.1.G). Never a month before the month the pregnancy began, where pregnancy_start_date is stated. Otherwise: for a person currently pregnant (is_pregnant), the determination month and later months and the months from the month of the application (cw_application_date) on; for a pregnancy that has ended (most_recent_pregnancy_end_date, CO-7400: the stated end, or the date of birth of the child of the case she gave birth to), the month it ended and the months from the month it began through it; and, for a person not pregnant now who states the start of a pregnancy but no end, the months from its start cannot be determined.

Coverage pass 6 CA6-3 (docs/reviews/coverage6-cash.md, probe W4), following Medicaid's month-by-month pregnancy (ma_is_pregnant_in_month, CO-3601; ma_expected_children_in_month, CO-7050): is_pregnant (CO-009) is the pregnancy on the determination date, so a pregnancy that ended between the application and the determination was read as none in every month, and one that is current was read in a month the case does not say she was pregnant in. The month the pregnancy ends is a pregnant month (3.606.1.G), and a child born in it is a dependent child of the month from the month of birth (cw_is_dependent_child_in_month, CO-6807). A pregnancy that has ended is read from its end, the stated pregnancy_end_date or the birth of a child of the case (most_recent_pregnancy_end_date, CO-7400, the shared end Medicaid and CHP+ read since coverage pass 6 C6-03): the month it ended is a pregnant month, and an earlier month needs the start date (an unstated start leaves such a month unknown, not pregnant or not); a person who is not pregnant and states neither an end nor a birth has no ended pregnancy in the months the case covers, unless she states a start, when those months cannot be determined. is_pregnant is required where read (decision 4 of 2026-11-23): Colorado Works reads it for every member of a unit whose allowance or basis it decides, so a case states it for every member, an infant or a man included (false).

### CO-7303 Colorado Works: a member of the unit in the month `@engine`

For a person of a Colorado Works assistance unit (cw_assistance_unit_members, CO-900, the persons who may join it in some month the determination covers), whether the person is a member of the unit in the month evaluated: born on or before the month's last day; not dead before the month's first day (9 CCR 2503-6 3.609.2.C.1-2: "A client's eligibility shall end on the date of his or her death. If a client dies before 12:00 a.m. on the first day of a month, no eligibility for a grant payment for the following month exists"); and either a member who is not in the unit as a dependent child (cw_is_dependent_child false: a parent, a caretaker, a spouse or another optional member) or, for one who is a dependent child in some month, in this month a dependent child (cw_is_dependent_child_in_month, 3.601), a parent or caretaker of one (cw_has_dependent_child_in_month), or an expectant parent (cw_is_pregnant_in_month; 3.601 "Parent ... including an expectant parent").

Precision. Coverage pass 6 CA6-4 and CA6-5 (docs/reviews/coverage6-cash.md, probes W3, W7, W9): the unit is one per case (CO-900), built from a dependent child in some month, so a month on the other side of a birthday, a birth or a death was built with the other month's members: a daughter who turned 18 before October 1 was still counted as a child in October (W3: $620 for two children where the rule gives one caretaker and one child, $488); a minor parent who turned 18 was a dependent child in the month she was an adult (W9); a child who died in September kept the unit eligible in October (W7). A person who joins only as a dependent child and is none in the month is not a member that month, unless she is then a parent or caretaker of a dependent child of the month or pregnant (an 18-year-old mother with her own baby is a caretaker). A member who dies during a month keeps that month (3.609.2.C.3 holds the payment for the personal representative). Every month-scoped figure of the unit reads the month's members (cw_assistance_unit_members_in_month, CO-7304). Pattern sweep (cash) PS-T8 (docs/reviews/pattern-sweep-cash.md): and living in the home in the month (cw_is_considered_living_in_home_in_month, CO-7602), each absence counted to the month (cw_month_reading_date, CO-7600), so a member whose absence passed its limit after the application month is a member of the application month and not of the later month. Coverage pass 7, F7-3 (docs/reviews/coverage7-cash.md): a person who receives an Adult Financial grant in the month (cw_receives_adult_financial_grant_in_month, CO-7691) is not a member of the unit in that month: C.R.S. 26-2-706(1.5)(c) (S5210) lets no one participate who is "receiving financial assistance from other financial assistance programs administered by the state of Colorado", and 3.609.1.D.6 (S5211) names Adult Financial programs among the benefits that "may not be received concurrently with a Colorado Works grant"; the person is left out of the unit as 3.604.2.C.3 leaves out an SSI recipient (CO-2350), so the grant is not the unit's income. Whether a parent who is a mandatory member is left out (a child-only unit) or makes the unit ineligible, and the reach of the statute beyond Adult Financial, are OQ-1451. Before, an Old Age Pension recipient who asked to join her grandchild's unit was a member and her pension the unit's income (probe G2).

Type yes/no, scope person-month, program ColoradoWorks.
Uses: `cw_has_dependent_child_in_month`, `cw_is_considered_living_in_home_in_month`, `cw_is_dependent_child`, `cw_is_dependent_child_in_month`, `cw_is_pregnant_in_month`, `cw_receives_adult_financial_grant_in_month`, `date_of_birth`, `date_of_death`.

```
all of the following are true:
  - Date of birth is less than the first day of the month after the month
  - any of the following is true:
    - Date of death is unknown
    - Date of death is at least the first day of the month
  - Colorado Works: considered living in the home in the month
  - any of the following is true:

    - Colorado Works: dependent child in the month
    - Colorado Works: has a dependent child in the month
    - Colorado Works: pregnant in the month
  - it is not the case that Colorado Works: receives an Adult Financial grant in the month
```

### CO-7308 Adult Financial: married `@engine`

Whether the Adult Financial client is married, as the county determines the client's marital status (9 CCR 2503-5 3.520.63.A: "Single, never married; Married; Widowed; or, Divorced or legally separated"; D: a client not legally separated is married): a spouse of the case in the month (af_spouses_in_month, CO-7603: a spouse edge or a civil union partner edge to a person of the case), or marital_status married, or other (a civil union), for a spouse or partner who is not a person of the case, "Marriage" in these rules including a civil union (3.510), with neither the relationships nor the marital status read as none when not stated: a client with no spouse edge whose marital status is not stated is not known to be unmarried.

Precision. Coverage pass 6 CA6-7 (docs/reviews/coverage6-cash.md): is_married (CO-930), a shared item, reads a person who states neither a spouse edge nor a marital status as not married, a default no Adult Financial rule gives (decision 4 of 2026-11-23); Adult Financial's readers (the couple's $20, af_client_general_income_disregard CO-3829; the couple's resource limit, af_meets_resource_limit CO-948; the SSI child, af_is_ssi_child CO-4022) read this item, which asks for the marital status 3.520.63.A makes the county determine. is_married itself is unchanged; its other readers (CO-005, CO-1164, CO-1986, CO-4103, CO-4260) are other programs' and are listed in the review, not changed here. Pattern sweep (cash) PS-M1 (docs/reviews/pattern-sweep-cash.md): per month: a spouse of the month (af_spouses_in_month, CO-7603), so a client whose spouse died before the month is widowed in it (3.520.63.A.3) unless marital_status states a marriage to a spouse outside the case; before, a spouse edge made the client married in every month. KL-CASH-3 (docs/reviews/known-limits.md, 2026-11-24): 3.510 (S5321): "“Marriage” (for the purpose of these rules) means a marriage as defined in Section 14-2-104(1), C.R.S., a common law marriage as defined in Section 14-2-104(2), C.R.S., and a civil union, as defined in Section 14-15-103(1), C.R.S." A client in a civil union is married: with a partner who is a person of the case through the civil_union_partner edge (CO-7603), with one who is not through marital_status other, which coverage verification 7 (V7-10) defined as a civil union with a person who is not a person of the case. ### CO-7600 Colorado Works: the day a month's dated circumstances are read on `@engine`

The day on which a Colorado Works circumstance that changes on a stated date (the days an absence from the home or the State has lasted, the days a stay in an institution has lasted, the months a visit or placement has lasted) is read for the month evaluated: for a month before the determination month, the month's last day, so the month is judged on the absence or stay as it stood in that month; for the determination month and any later month, the determination date, the day the case's facts are stated as of. Each month is judged on its own circumstances (9 CCR 2503-6 3.605.1.A.1: the month of application's circumstances determine eligibility; 3.609.2.A.1: the initial payment runs from the date of application or the later date the unit became eligible); which day of an earlier month is read is OQ-1435.

The determination month keeps the determination date, so no answer for the determination month or a later month changes.

### CO-7602 Colorado Works: considered living in the home in the month `@engine`

Whether, in the month evaluated, Colorado Works considers the person to be living in the home they usually live in despite a temporary absence (9 CCR 2503-6 3.604.2.E, G, I): present (no absence); away for medical treatment (E.1, I.2) or on active duty in the uniformed services (I.1); a dependent child of the month under a court's jurisdiction, in an agency's legal custody without its physical custody, or attending school away from home (E.2-4); a dependent child of the month visiting a noncustodial parent under a parenting plan for no more than six months (G.2) or in a voluntary foster care placement for no more than three months (G.3); or away for less than forty-five days with an established intent to return (I.3). A parent or caretaker who has become a resident of an institution in the month (a stay of at least thirty consecutive days, 3.604.2.O.2; cw_is_institution_resident, CO-3804) is not in the home, unless the person keeps the responsibility of a dependent child who lives in the institution too or is still cared for in the home. The months and days of an absence are counted to cw_month_reading_date (CO-7600): the month's last day for a month before the determination month, the determination date otherwise.

Precision. Pattern sweep (cash) PS-T8 (docs/reviews/pattern-sweep-cash.md): cw_is_considered_living_in_home (CO-3354) was one value per case, measuring every absence to the determination date and the determination month, so a member whose absence passed its limit after the application month was out of the unit in the application month too (a child who left on a visit under a parenting plan on 2026-04-20, determined 2026-10-15: no more than six months through September, G.2, so in the home in September; the seventh month is October). This item is the month's reading; CO-3354 is now whether the person lives in the home in some month of the determination (who may join the unit), as cw_is_dependent_child (CO-901) is for the dependent child, and the month's unit (cw_is_assistance_unit_member_in_month, CO-7303), the minor-parent items (CO-906, CO-4352) and the stepparent's children in the home (CO-2353) read this item. A visit or placement is measured as the length of time elapsed from temporary_absence_start_date to cw_month_reading_date, not in calendar months (coverage pass 7, F7-1, docs/reviews/coverage7-cash.md): the child is in the home while the reading date is on or before the date cw_parenting_plan_visit_max_months (six) or cw_voluntary_foster_care_max_months (three) months after the start, the same day of the month that many months later (the last day of that month where it has no such day), since G.2's visit "not exceeding six (6) months" and G.3's placement "for a period not expected to exceed three (3) months" (S2203; C.R.S. 26-2-706(1)(a.5)(V)) are lengths of time; on that date the absence has lasted the full length, which does not exceed it. Before, the months were counted as calendar months from the month the absence began, so a visit begun on 2026-04-30 had "exceeded" six months on 2026-10-15 after five months and fifteen days (probe V1; stored household CO-1032, October restated). Whether G.3's placement is measured by its elapsed length or by the length the county expects at the placement is OQ-1452. OQ-611 is I.3 read for a child; OQ-660 the institution stay. Whether the person is temporarily absent (temporary_absence_reason) is required where read (coverage pass 6 CA6-7), and so is the residence setting of a person stated present (decision 4 of 2026-11-23; pattern sweep PS-D3: the old reading of an unstated setting as a private dwelling is gone).

Type yes/no, scope person-month, program ColoradoWorks.
Uses: `cw_institution_resident_keeps_child_in_care`, `cw_is_dependent_child_in_month`, `cw_is_institution_resident`, `cw_month_reading_date`, `cw_parenting_plan_visit_max_months`, `cw_temporary_absence_max_days`, `cw_voluntary_foster_care_max_months`, `temporary_absence_reason`, `temporary_absence_start_date`.

```
if Temporary absence reason is equal to none
  then (any of the following is true:;   - it is not the case that Colorado Works: is a resident of an institution;   - Colorado Works: dependent child in the month;   - Colorado Works: institution resident keeps responsibility for a child in care)
else if Temporary absence reason is equal to active_military_duty
  then yes
else if Temporary absence reason is equal to medical_treatment
  then (any of the following is true:;   - it is not the case that Colorado Works: is a resident of an institution;   - Colorado Works: dependent child in the month;   - Colorado Works: institution resident keeps responsibility for a child in care)
```

### CO-7603 Adult Financial: the client's spouse in the month `@engine`

The persons of the case who are this client's spouse in the month evaluated: a spouse (the spouse relationship) or a partner in a civil union (the civil_union_partner relationship), since "Marriage" in these rules includes a civil union (9 CCR 2503-5 3.510), who had not died before the month's first day. A client whose spouse died before the month is widowed in it (9 CCR 2503-5 3.520.63.A.3), so the spouse's income is not deemed (3.534, 3.544.D-F, 3.549.C-F) and the spouse's resources are not counted with the client's (3.520.72.A) for that month.

Precision. Pattern sweep (cash) PS-M1 (docs/reviews/pattern-sweep-cash.md): the Adult Financial couple readers took every person with a spouse edge as the client's spouse in every month, so a spouse who died during the months a determination covers still had income deemed and resources counted, and the client kept the couple's resource limit and the split $20, in the months after the death. A spouse who is not a person of the case is read through marital_status (af_is_married, CO-7308). Whether a person is a spouse is read from the client's relationships, stated (an empty list where there is none): a client whose relationships are not stated cannot be determined (decision 4 of 2026-11-23; pattern sweep PS-D4), except in a case of one person, who has no other person to be married to. KL-CASH-3 (docs/reviews/known-limits.md, 2026-11-24): 3.510 (S5321): "“Marriage” (for the purpose of these rules) means a marriage as defined in Section 14-2-104(1), C.R.S., a common law marriage as defined in Section 14-2-104(2), C.R.S., and a civil union, as defined in Section 14-15-103(1), C.R.S." A partner in a civil union who is a person of the case is the client's spouse here, read exactly as a spouse of the case is (deemed, counted with the client, widowed after a death before the month); before, the civil_union_partner edge was read by LEAP alone, and a client in a civil union was read as unmarried. The other programs' readings of a civil union are unchanged (SNAP's 4.000.1, S5320: a civil union is "without the legal recognition of these individuals as spouses").

Type group of persons, scope person-month, program AdultFinancial.
Uses: `date_of_death`, `relationships`.

```
if (the number of persons in every person in the case) is equal to 1
  then all persons in every person in the case such that no
otherwise all persons in every person in the case such that (all of the following are true:;   - this person is a spouse or civil_union_partner of that person;   - any of the following is true:;     - that person's Date of death is unknown;     - that person's Date of death is at least the first day of the month)
```

### CO-900 Colorado Works: assistance unit members `@engine`

The persons who make up this person's Colorado Works assistance unit under 9 CCR 2503-6 3.604.2.A-C and 26-2-703(2.5), C.R.S. - a dependent child living with a caretaker, and that caretaker (the child's parent, or a non-parent caretaker who requests assistance), crossed reciprocally, with the spouse of a pregnant parent and, when they request assistance, a stepparent, a non-parent caretaker's spouse and the other optional members of 3.604.2.C.2, except that the edge between a dependent child who is themselves a minor parent and that minor parent's own parent is not crossed, because 3.604.2.C.1.b excludes a minor parent's own parent from mandatory inclusion when the minor parent is requesting assistance for their own child. Excludes anyone receiving SSI or a Title IV foster care, adoption subsidy, or kinship payment (3.604.2.C.3) and an optional member who has not requested assistance (C.2). Each member's value of this item is the same set (their own unit); an excluded person's own value is empty or a singleton of themselves.

Precision. Living in the home is read from lives_with (CO-1925) and Colorado Works's temporary-absence rule, 3.604.2.E, G and I (cw_is_considered_living_in_home, CO-3354). The 3.604.2.H multiple-caretaker hierarchy is applied to both caretaker edges, as cw_caretaker_of (CO-2608) applies it (coverage review CW-18, fix round 2026-11-23): a non-parent's edge to a child is crossed only when no higher-ranked caretaker of the child is in the home (cw_parents_in_home, CO-5207; cw_relative_or_guardian_caretakers_in_home, CO-5208). Phase-10 sweep (OQ-152, OQ-101): a spouse edge is crossed when either spouse is a parent or caretaker of a dependent child in the home or is pregnant, so the spouse of a pregnant parent (C.1.e, mandatory), a stepparent (C.2.a) and a non-parent caretaker's spouse (C.2.c) are reached; the edge between a minor parent requesting assistance for her own child and her parent is crossed when that parent requests inclusion (C.2.g); and the final filter leaves out cw_is_excluded_from_assistance_unit (CO-2350): SSI and Title IV recipients (C.3) and an optional member (cw_is_optional_assistance_unit_member, CO-2349) who has not requested assistance. Siblings and half siblings are reached through their parent or caretaker as dependent children (C.1.c-d); those made optional by custody or child support (C.2.d-f) are stated by cw_is_optional_member_by_custody_or_support (CO-2347). Same-word audit SW-3/SW-4 (OQ-396): the caretaker relation is cw_caretaker_of (CO-2608): a parent, or a non-parent caretaker who is the child's legal guardian or has primary responsibility for the child (3.601); the spouse of a parent who is not a parent stays the optional member of 3.604.2.C.2.a, read from the spouse and parent roles as the rule words it. Coverage pass 4 CA4-16: whether a spouse with no dependent child is pregnant is required where read, never read as no when not stated (decision 4 of 2026-11-23: missing information is cannot determine unless the rule says otherwise). Coverage pass 6 CA6-3, CA6-4 (docs/reviews/coverage6-cash.md): the spouse edge reads a pregnancy in some month the determination covers (cw_is_pregnant_in_determination, CO-7302), as the dependent child is one in some month (CO-901); the persons here are those who may join in some month, and the month's members are cw_assistance_unit_members_in_month (CO-7304), which every month-scoped figure reads. Pattern sweep (cash) PS-D2 (docs/reviews/pattern-sweep-cash.md): whether persons live together is read from lives_with as stated (dwelling_id), required where read (decision 4 of 2026-11-23; docs/conventions.md rule 17 as amended for Colorado Works and Adult Financial): no text on file says the persons of one application live together (9 CCR 2503-6 3.604.2.A, E, I build the unit from the persons living in the home; 9 CCR 2503-5 3.534.B.3 and 3.549.E name the household of the spouse and the parents in the home). Before, a person whose home was not stated was read as living with every related person of the case. Coverage pass 7, F7-6 (docs/reviews/coverage7-cash.md): two sentences that described readings since replaced (an unstated dwelling_id read as living in the home; an unstated pregnancy read as none) were deleted; both are required where read, as the sentences above say (PS-D2; CA4-16, CA6-7).

### CO-901 Colorado Works: is a dependent child `@engine`

The person is a "dependent child" under 26-2-703(9), C.R.S. and 9 CCR 2503-6 3.601 in some month the determination covers (cw_determination_months, CO-7300) - under 18, or cw_dependent_child_age_limit and a full-time secondary (or vocational/technical equivalent) student reasonably expected to complete before turning 19 (cw_is_dependent_child_in_month): the months from the month of the application (cw_application_date) through the determination month, or the determination month alone at a redetermination or when no application date is stated. The month-scoped tests read cw_is_dependent_child_in_month for their own month.

Precision. Reads is_full_time_secondary_student_finishing_before_nineteen (CO-1720) for the 18-year-old prong (vocabulary fix round R-2; it had read half-time secondary enrollment), which includes vocational or technical training and high school equivalency as 3.601 states. Coverage pass 4 CA4-15 (docs/reviews/coverage4-cash.md): the age is taken in each month the determination covers (cw_is_dependent_child_in_month), so a child who turns 18 between the application and the determination is a dependent child for the application month (probe W5: born 2008-10-05, application 2026-09-25, determined 2026-10-15: eligible from September 25, .19726 x 488 = $96); before, the determination date's age was read in every month (OQ-951). The unit's composition is one per case, so a child dependent in any of those months is a member, and the eligibility test asks whether the unit has a dependent child in the month (cw_eligibility_status, CO-921). Coverage pass 6 CA6-2: the months are cw_determination_months (CO-7300), which reads the kind of determination with no default when an application date is stated.

### CO-904 Colorado Works: meets residency requirement `@engine`

The person is a Colorado resident for Colorado Works purposes under 26-2-706(1.5)(a), C.R.S. and 9 CCR 2503-6 3.604.1.A - living in Colorado with no durational requirement - and is not, for the month at issue, a person another state already paid TANF benefits to (3.604.1.A.3), nor temporarily out of State for more than ninety consecutive days (3.604.2.O.1).

Precision. Does not model the 3.604.1.A.1-2 intent-to-remain and retained-until-abandoned tests beyond reading the stated state_of_residence fact, consistent with is_colorado_resident's (CO-505) treatment of the parallel Medicaid rule. Vocabulary fix round (docs/reviews/vocabulary-reuse.md, U-4): state residence reads is_colorado_resident (CO-505) instead of restating the comparison. Final cash review FC-1: 3.604.2.O.1 (S2602) limits a temporary stay out of State to ninety consecutive days (cw_temporary_out_of_state_max_days, CO-3807), counted from temporarily_out_of_state_start_date (CO-3806) to the determination date; a person with no such date stated is read as in Colorado. Time audit T-6: "N consecutive days" is counted as the days elapsed since the day the absence or stay began (days_between), the day of departure or entry itself not counted (OQ-953): "shall not exceed ninety (90) consecutive days" (3.604.2.O, S2602): within while the days elapsed since the day of departure are at most cw_temporary_out_of_state_max_days, so a client who left on August 1 is within through October 30 and out from October 31. Pattern sweep (cash) PS-T8 (docs/reviews/pattern-sweep-cash.md): per month: the days out of State are counted to cw_month_reading_date (CO-7600), the month's last day for a month before the determination month, the determination date otherwise; before, every month counted them to the determination date, so an application month was judged on days not yet away.

### CO-906 Colorado Works: minor parent living arrangement met `@engine`

Whether a minor parent's living arrangement satisfies 9 CCR 2503-6 3.604.2.N - not applicable (vacuously satisfied) unless the person is both under cw_minor_parent_age_limit and has a dependent child; if so, satisfied when the minor is emancipated, has a marital status other than single, lives with her own parent, lives with an adult relative (N.2.a) or with another adult caretaker (3.604.2.N.1) who is related to her or is a member of her assistance unit (N.3.a-b), or is in a county-approved setting.

Precision. 'Lives with her own parent' is read from lives_with (CO-1925) to a person she is the child of (same-word SW-7; where no dwelling_id is stated, the parent edge is read as living together, convention rule 17); 3.604.2.N.3.c does not require county approval in that case regardless of whether the parent joins the assistance unit. Coverage review CW-7: N.1 (S3153) also accepts residence "with another adult caretaker" and N.2.a "with an adult relative": a person of the case, 18 or older (not a minor, cw_minor_parent_age_limit), who is related to the minor parent (is_related_to, CO-2845: a grandparent, aunt, uncle, adult sibling and the like) or is her caretaker (she is the child, ward or in the primary care of that person, as cw_caretaker_of, CO-2608, reads it) and a member of her assistance unit (cw_assistance_unit_members, CO-900), living in the same home (lives_with, read as living together where no dwelling is stated) and considered living in the home (cw_is_considered_living_in_home, CO-3354). Coverage pass 2 (CW2-1, S3450): N.3.a requires a county approved setting when the minor parent "lives with an unrelated non-parent caretaker who chooses not to be a member of the assistance unit", so an unrelated caretaker who has not joined her unit is not enough without county approval (county_approved_living_arrangement), and neither is an unrelated adult who is not her caretaker. An unrelated caretaker who has joined her unit (N.3.b) is accepted without approval: the county "may choose" to require it (OQ-830). cw_eligibility_status (CO-921) reads a failure for every member of the unit. Coverage pass 6 CA6-4 (docs/reviews/coverage6-cash.md, probe W9): per month: the minor parent's age and the other adult's are taken on the month's first day and her dependent child is the month's (cw_has_dependent_child_in_month, CO-7305), so a mother who turns 18 is held to N in the months she is under 18 only (docs/operators.md, "Ages in a month"; OQ-951). ### CO-908 Colorado Works: countable unearned income `@engine`

This person's countable unearned income for the month for the Colorado Works eligibility test under 9 CCR 2503-6 3.605.3: the receipts Colorado Works' counting table counts (cw_counted_unearned_receipts, CO-5651, through cw_receipt_treatment_table, CO-5650), plus the child support counted against the need standard (cw_counted_child_support, CO-2553: the month's current support at application, consistent support averaging over $500 at redetermination, 3.605.5.A and C) and potential income the client refuses to make a reasonable effort to secure (3.605.1.A.3.c), less the amounts cw_unearned_income_deductions (CO-4369) takes off, never below zero. The unit's own Colorado Works grant is not income to it. The grant calculation reads cw_payment_countable_unearned_income (CO-2554), which leaves child support out (3.605.5.B). The same figure is the income of a person whose income is deemed to the unit (a budgetary member, a minor parent's parent, a sponsor).

Precision. Receipt records, migration phase 2 (docs/reviews/receipts-migration-2-cw.md): read from the receipts (CO-5000) through the counting table, replacing the sum of the scalar unearned income facts (Social Security, pension, unemployment, Adult Financial grants, other unearned income taxable or not, tax-exempt interest, lottery winnings) less cw_excluded_unearned_income (CO-2341, removed). Vocabulary fix round (R-1): the unit's own grant is not counted; Adult Financial grants are (counted because no rule excludes them). SSI is not counted: 3.605.4.B.27 exempts an SSI recipient's income. Child support arrears are exempt (3.605.5.D) and are their own receipt kind. Coverage review (CW-9, CW-11, CW-14, CW-22, CW-23): a lottery or gambling prize is counted (3.605.3.A.14) as a receipt of its own; potential income the client refuses to make a reasonable effort to secure (cw_refused_potential_income, CO-4362, 3.605.1.A.3.c, S3160), a county finding rather than a receipt, is read as 0 when not stated. cw_unearned_income_deductions (CO-4369) is subtracted: allowable rental expenses and a military allotment for persons outside the home (S3157, S3580). Receipt records, migration phase 3: insurance and lump-sum amounts spent or designated for the costs the rule names are fields of the receipt that cw_counted_unearned_receipts leaves out, and insurance cash value taken, an SMIB refund, savings account distributions and an adoption subsidy are kinds the counting table excludes (S3163, S3166, S2606, S4040); board-only and room-only payments are kinds it treats as earned income.

### CO-909 Colorado Works: deemed income of a minor parent's non-participant parent `@engine`

For an unmarried minor (under 18) who has a dependent child of her own, the countable income of her own non-participant parent(s) living in the same home, deemed to her assistance unit under 9 CCR 2503-6 3.605.1.A.4 - zero for anyone who is not an unmarried minor parent. A parent who is a member of her assistance unit (an optional member who requested assistance, 3.604.2.C.2.g) is a participant, whose income the unit already counts, and a parent living elsewhere is not in the same home; neither is deemed.

Precision. Per 3.605.1.A.4.a's formula: each such parent's gross earned income minus the cw_earned_income_disregard_dollar employment disregard (floored at zero), plus their unearned income, summed over the parents in the home, minus the needs of those parents and of the individuals in the home for whom they are responsible (cw_minor_parent_deeming_needs_deduction, CO-2000: the need standard for the parents and their other children; OQ-102). Open-question sweep: the deduction had been the One Caretaker need standard for zero children, deducted once per parent; it now counts the parents' other children (3.605.1.A.4.a, S1307) and is deducted once from the parents' combined income. The deductions of 3.605.1.A.4.a for support paid outside the unit are made (phase-10 sweep, OQ-140): child support paid (child_support_paid_legally_obligated, CO-033), spousal maintenance paid (spousal_maintenance_paid, CO-4354, coverage review CW-20; read as 0 when not stated) and amounts paid to tax dependents outside the home (cw_support_paid_to_tax_dependents_outside_home). Coverage review CW-5, CW-6 (S3155): only a non-participant parent is deemed (one not in cw_assistance_unit_members: a parent who requested inclusion was counted twice, as a member and as deemed income), and only one living in the same home (lives_with, read as living together where no dwelling is stated, convention rule 17; and cw_is_considered_living_in_home, CO-3354, for both, as cw_caretaker_of reads the home). Coverage pass 2 (CW2-2): that set is now named once, cw_minor_parent_deemed_parents (CO-4660), which the needs deduction (CO-2000) reads too. Fix round (C-11(a)): the deeming guard now reads marital_status = single, per 3.605.1.A.4's own title and first sentence ('Income of a non-participant stepparent and a non-participant parent of an unmarried minor parent') - a married minor parent's own parent's income was previously deemed too, which the rule's own text excludes. Fix round (C-11(b)): reads [of, [P], cw_countable_unearned_income] (CO-908) for the parent's unearned income instead of re-enumerating four of its six components (social_security_income, pension_income, unemployment_income, other_unearned_income_nontaxable), which had silently dropped tanf_cash_income and child_support_received; 3.605.1.A.4.a's 'plus any unearned income' does not admit a shorter list than the program's own unearned-income definition. Vocabulary fix round (R-1): earned income is cw_gross_earned_income (CO-1716): gross wages plus the self-employment net profit 3.605.2.E.1.c treats as earned income; it had read wages only. Coverage pass 3 (P3-2): each parent's income less the support that parent pays is floored at zero before the parents are summed, since A.4.a subtracts "the maintenance or child support paid to others" from the income of the parent who pays it; one parent's payments do not offset the other parent's income. Coverage pass 4 CA4-16: the spousal maintenance and the support paid to tax dependents outside the home that 3.605.1.A.4 deducts are required where read (a deemed person who pays none states 0), never read as 0 when not stated (decision 4 of 2026-11-23: missing information is cannot determine unless the rule says otherwise). Coverage pass 6 CA6-4 (docs/reviews/coverage6-cash.md, probe W9): the minor parent's age is taken on the first day of the month evaluated and her dependent child is the month's (cw_has_dependent_child_in_month, CO-7305): a mother born 2008-09-20 living with her own mother is a minor parent in September 2026 (17 on September 1), whose mother's income is deemed, and an adult parent in October (18 on October 1), whose mother's income is not (A.4 is for an unmarried minor parent); before, the determination date's age decided both months. Pattern sweep (cash) PS-M4 (docs/reviews/pattern-sweep-cash.md): a parent who died before the month is no parent living in the home in it, so nothing of that parent's is deemed for the month. CASH-SW-1 (2026-11-24; docs/reviews/known-limits.md): the needs deducted (CO-2000) are now per month, measured by the need standard in force in the month, as this item is.

### CO-910 Colorado Works: countable income `@engine`

The total net countable income of this person's assistance unit for the month - the sum of each member's countable earned and unearned income (CO-907, CO-908), plus any income deemed under 3.605.1.A.4 from a minor-parent member's non-participant parent (CO-909) - the figure 3.606.1.H compares against the need standard and 3.606.1.I-K use to compute the grant. A required member disqualified for an intentional program violation or as a fleeing felon has gross earnings counted without disregards (3.604.2.M), and one disqualified for citizenship, status, lawful presence or SSN reasons has earnings net of the cw_earned_income_disregard_dollar employment disregard (3.605.1.A.6); the sponsor's deemed net income (cw_sponsor_deemed_income, 3.605.1.A.5) is added for each sponsored member; and the income of a budgetary-unit member outside the assistance unit (cw_budgetary_member_deemed_income: a stepparent under 3.605.1.A.4.a, a non-parent caretaker's spouse under 3.606.1.J) is added.

Precision. Coverage review CW-9(b): money a member received from a sponsor (cw_sponsor_contributions_counted, CO-4363) is added when sponsor deeming does not apply, a gift under 3.605.3.A.14 (S3157). OQ-490 resolved (CDHS review S-5): a member disqualified for citizenship, non-citizen status, lawful presence or SSN reasons (cw_is_disqualified_for_status_or_ssn, CO-2557) has net income deemed under 3.605.1.A.6, gross earnings less the cw_earned_income_disregard_dollar employment disregard of 3.605.1.A.4.a (S1808); a member disqualified for an IPV or as a fleeing felon counts gross earnings without disregards (3.604.2.M). This eligibility figure applies the same deeming in both computations, since A.6 deems net income to the unit rather than giving the member the unit's payment disregard (3.606.2 excludes disqualified individuals). Coverage pass 6 CA6-4, CA6-5 (docs/reviews/coverage6-cash.md): the members whose income is summed are the month's (cw_assistance_unit_members_in_month, CO-7304), so a child who is no member in the month (no dependent child of it, not yet born, or dead before it) brings no income to it. Pattern sweep (cash) PS-M4 (docs/reviews/pattern-sweep-cash.md): a member of the budgetary unit outside the assistance unit (a stepparent) has income deemed only in a month he was alive on the first day of (3.609.2.C.1-2); before, a stepparent who died went on having his stated income deemed in the months after.

### CO-914 Colorado Works: basic cash assistance grant amount `@engine`

The authorized Colorado Works basic cash assistance grant for this person's assistance unit for the month: zero unless the unit's eligibility status (cw_eligibility_status, CO-921) is eligible; for an eligible unit, the grant before any sanction (cw_grant_before_sanction, CO-1260: the grant standard for the unit's size plus any pregnancy allowance, minus net countable income computed with the payment disregard, floored at zero, with cents dropped, 9 CCR 2503-6 3.606.1.I and K) less the sanction reduction of 3.608.4.C (cw_sanction_reduction, CO-1265), with the cents dropped. In the month of the initial payment, when assistance begins after the first of the month, the grant for the entire month is multiplied by the partial month figure of 3.609.2.A.1 (cw_partial_month_payment_factor, CO-4358); a partial month grant under $10 is not paid, and one that the deductions bring under $10 is paid unless it is under $1 (A.1.e), with the cents dropped (3.609.2.D).

Precision. Drops cents by flooring rather than rounding (3.606.1.K.2's 'drop the cents'); the engine has a round-up (ceil) operator but no floor, so this item computes floor(x) as -ceil(-x), which is exact for any real x. The pre-sanction grant (cw_grant_before_sanction, CO-1260) subtracts cw_payment_countable_income (CO-923), computed with the payment disregards of the current 3.606.2.A (S1000) - 100% in the first certification period and for a new source, 67% for a current source after it (phase-8 fix round, B-1) - not cw_countable_income (CO-910), which carries the eligibility-test figure. The $10 pregnancy allowance (3.606.1.G) is added in CO-1260. Phase 8 (OQ-141 resolved): the sanction reduction of 3.608.4.C (cw_sanction_reduction, CO-1265) is subtracted here. CDHS review B-1: the payment is gated on cw_eligibility_status being eligible, as af_oap_grant, snap_allotment, leap_benefit_amount and cccap_parent_fee are; an applicant whose earnings fail the $90 eligibility test (3.606.1.H, J.4) but pass the 100% payment disregard, a unit past the time limit, or a non-resident unit is paid nothing (3.606.1.I: grant payments are computed for an eligible assistance unit). Coverage review CW-8 (S3156): the authorized grant for the entire month (A.1.a-b) is cw_grant_before_sanction (the grant standard and pregnancy allowance less net countable income); the partial month grant is that times the factor (A.1.c-d), compared with cw_partial_month_minimum_grant (CO-4356) before any deduction; the deductions of A.1.e are the sanction reduction (overpayment recovery is outside the volume, notes); the result is compared with cw_partial_month_minimum_payment_after_deductions (CO-4357) and its cents dropped. ### CO-915 Colorado Works: months of assistance used `@engine`

The number of months already counted toward this person's sixty-month federal TANF lifetime limit, per 26-2-706.5, C.R.S. and 9 CCR 2503-6 3.606.6.A and F - the statewide automated system's running count (months_of_assistance_received, CO-840) less the months received while living in exempt Indian Country, for every member: 3.606.6.C bars a unit containing any individual who has received federal TANF assistance as an adult for sixty or more cumulative months, whatever that individual's place in the unit is now.

Precision. Coverage review CW-3: 45 CFR 264.1(b)(1)(i) (S421) says which months are not added to a person's count ('Any month of receipt of assistance by an individual who is not the head-of-household or married to the head-of-household'), and 3.606.6.A (S3154) which months are; the supplied count (CO-840, the count 'already counted toward this person's sixty-month lifetime limit ... as tracked by the statewide automated system') has already applied both, so this item reads it as stated for every member. The item formerly read 0 for anyone who is not now the head or the head's spouse, which erased months a person accrued earlier as a head: unmarried parents whose non-head father had sixty counted months were eligible, where 3.606.6.C makes the unit ineligible. cw_time_limit_reached (CO-918) still reads only the unit's adult members (cw_is_adult_member, CO-924). Vocabulary fix round (R-3, R-7): the head is the Colorado Works head of the assistance unit (cw_is_head_of_assistance_unit, CO-1733), not the SNAP head of household; and 3.606.6.F's Indian Country months are subtracted (cw_months_received_in_exempt_indian_country, CO-1723) instead of zeroing every month for a tribal member. Phase-10 sweep (OQ-143): 9 CCR 2503-6 3.604.2.M (S1004) counts the month of a disqualified or ineligible member (cw_is_disqualified_member, CO-928) toward that member's own sixty-month maximum when a grant is paid for others in the unit, so such a member's count is read as stated even when the member is neither the head nor the head's spouse; Colorado's rule counts more than 45 CFR 264.1(b)(1)(i) requires, and the volume follows the rule.

Type whole number, scope person, program ColoradoWorks.

```
the greater of 0 and (Months of federal TANF assistance received minus Colorado Works: months of assistance received while living in exempt Indian Country)
```

### CO-918 Colorado Works: time limit reached `@engine`

This person's assistance unit contains an adult (or minor head-of-household) member who has used sixty or more cumulative months of federal TANF assistance, and the unit is not exempt from (or extended beyond) the time limit - per 9 CCR 2503-6 3.606.6.C ("an assistance unit containing an individual who has received ... assistance ... as an adult for sixty (60) or more cumulative months shall not be eligible") and 45 CFR 264.1(a)(1). Every member of the same unit shares the same value.

Precision. Read at the unit level per the phase-5 review's C-2 finding: 3.606.6.C bars the whole unit, not only the member whose own count reached sixty months, so a unit containing one adult past the limit is time-limit-reached for every member, including a dependent child or a caretaker whose own months are under sixty. Tests cw_is_adult_member (CO-924) so a dependent child's own (zero) months never trigger the unit-level test directly, though cw_months_of_assistance_used (CO-915) already zeroes a non-head, non-spouse member's count. Coverage pass 6 CA6-4: an adult member is read in the determination month (cw_is_adult_member, CO-924, per month). Pattern sweep (cash) PS-T10 (docs/reviews/pattern-sweep-cash.md): per month: the members of the month (cw_assistance_unit_members_in_month, CO-7304) and their adult status in it (cw_is_adult_member, CO-924), so a minor parent who becomes an adult member after the application month does not bar the unit for the application month, when she was a dependent child; before, the determination month's adult status and the determination's members were read for every month.

### CO-919 Colorado Works: is a work-eligible individual `@engine`

The person is a "work-eligible individual" under 45 CFR 261.2(n) - an adult, minor child head-of-household, or spouse of a minor child head-of-household (9 CCR 2503-6 3.607.1.A.1; coverage review P3-4) receiving Colorado Works assistance, or a non-recipient parent living with a child receiving it - unless the person is a minor parent who is not the head of household or a head's spouse (3.607.1.B.1), a non-citizen ineligible for assistance due to immigration status, or an SSI recipient (Colorado's state-option exclusion, read as elected because it tracks the same SSI exclusion 3.604.2.C.3.a states for assistance unit membership).

Precision. Fix round (C-6): three defects the phase-5 review found. (a) No assistance test at all: added the last conjunct below, reading cw_eligibility_status (CO-921) directly rather than a bare literal-18 age test - this person's own unit is eligible, or this person is a non-recipient parent living with a child whose own unit is eligible (261.2(n)(1)'s 'non-recipient parent living with a child receiving such assistance'). No circularity with CO-921, which does not read this item. (b) The prior second conjunct, [not, [all, [<, age, 18], [not, snap_is_head_of_household]]], was by De Morgan's law identical to the first conjunct and never read cw_has_dependent_child, so it excluded every non-head minor rather than 261.2(n)(1)(i)'s minor-parent-who-is-not-head-of-household; rewritten below to read cw_has_dependent_child. (c) The bare literal 18 in the first conjunct is replaced with cw_dependent_child_age_limit (CO-270), per governance's name.digits rule, since 261.2(n)'s 'adult' is the complement of the minor child the same title defines. Scope changed from person to person-month because the new assistance-test conjunct reads cw_eligibility_status (CO-921), which is person-month. Vocabulary fix round (R-7): reads cw_is_head_of_assistance_unit (CO-1733), not the SNAP head of household. The minor parent's own dependent child is the child of the month (cw_has_dependent_child_in_month, CO-7305), with the ages (PS-T3).

### CO-920 Colorado Works: meets work participation requirement `@engine`

A work-eligible individual's participation hours for the month meet the 45 CFR 261.31 weekly-hours requirement (cw_work_participation_hours_per_week, with the core-activity minimum not separately modeled here) - or the reduced requirement of 45 CFR 261.35 (cw_work_participation_hours_per_week_young_child) for a single custodial parent or caretaker relative with a child under six. Informational: no rule reads it and it is not a declared outcome; it reports whether a work-eligible individual meets the federal participation hours, which the State's participation rate, not the person's eligibility, turns on (household cases check it).

Precision. Compares the month's countable work activity hours (cw_work_activity_hours, CO-1745) against the weekly requirement multiplied by cw_weeks_per_month (CO-3044) to approximate a monthly figure; see OQ-104. Vocabulary fix round (docs/reviews/vocabulary-reuse.md, R-12): it had added hours worked for pay and SNAP employment and training hours. Same-word audit SW-3/SW-4 (OQ-396): the caretaker relation is cw_caretaker_of (CO-2608): a parent, or a non-parent caretaker who is the child's legal guardian or has primary responsibility for the child (3.601); the spouse of a parent who is not a parent stays the optional member of 3.604.2.C.2.a, read from the spouse and parent roles as the rule words it. Coverage pass 4 CA4-15: the dependent child is the child of the month evaluated (cw_is_dependent_child_in_month, CO-6807), the age taken in that month. Pattern sweep (cash) PS-T4 (docs/reviews/pattern-sweep-cash.md): the child's age under six is taken on the first day of the month evaluated too (OQ-951); before, the determination date's age was read in every month.

```
if there is a person in Colorado Works: persons of whom this person is the caretaker such that
    all of the following are true:
      - that person's Colorado Works: dependent child in the month
      - (the number of whole years between that person's Date of birth and the first day of the month) is less than Colorado Works young child age limit (reduced work hours) (6)

otherwise Colorado Works: countable work activity hours is at least (Colorado Works work participation hours per week (30) times Colorado Works weeks per month for the participation hours test (4))
```

### CO-921 Colorado Works: eligibility status `@engine`

This person's Colorado Works eligibility determination for the month, checked in order: an optional member who has not requested assistance is not in the unit; a unit with no dependent child and no pregnant member (a parent includes an expectant parent, 9 CCR 2503-6 3.601) cannot be aided; a client who died before the first day of the month has no eligibility for it (3.609.2.C.1-2); then residency (including a temporary stay out of State of no more than ninety days, 3.604.2.O.1), the person's being an institution patient for tuberculosis or mental disease or an inmate (3.604.1.D-E), citizenship/immigrant status, the person's own disqualification (a fugitive or fleeing felon, an intentional program violation disqualification or a failure to apply for a Social Security number, 3.604.2.L.1, M; cw_is_disqualified_member, CO-928: the person is removed from the unit, whose other members are determined without them), a minor parent's living arrangement (the person's own, or any member's, so the unit is barred), an adult of the unit participating in a strike (3.604.2.L.2), the child support assignment and cooperation (3.604.4.A), a member's diversion period of ineligibility (3.606.8.A.4-5), a county closure in effect for a member (not participating before the first Individualized Plan, 3.607.5; continued EBT misuse, 3.609.2.J.3-4; a minor parent's education non-participation without good cause, 3.604.2.N.1.b), the sixty-month time limit, a fourth-level sanction (3.608.4.C.2, the unit is closed for the month), then the income test. Eligible only if every check passes.

Precision. ineligible_resources is never reached by this item's derivation: 26-2-706(2)(a) expressly forbids an asset test as a condition of Colorado Works eligibility, so this volume does not author cw_countable_resources or cw_meets_resource_limit items. The option is kept in the fixed vocabulary for schema compatibility with the batch-10 interface; see the batch report. Fix round (C-13): adds a branch gated on cw_minor_parent_living_arrangement_met (CO-906), which no item previously read, per 26-2-706(2)(b) ('an unmarried parent under eighteen years of age shall not receive assistance unless' the stated living-arrangement conditions are met) and 3.604.2.N.1 ('grant payments may not be approved unless the minor parent resides with another adult caretaker or ... an appropriate setting'). CO-906's own vacuous-true design (satisfied whenever the person is not both under 18 and a parent) means this branch is a no-op for anyone who is not an unmarried minor parent. CDHS review B-3: a pregnant person with no other children is an expectant parent (3.601, S1806); 3.604.3.C.7 verifies pregnancy "when no children are in the assistance unit" (S1807) and the 3.606.1.F chart prices a zero-child unit, so the first check now fails only a unit with neither a dependent child nor a pregnant member; a pregnancy left unstated was read as none (is_pregnant). County case worker review S5: an optional member who has not asked to join (cw_is_optional_member_not_requesting, CO-2558) is reported as not_in_unit_did_not_request rather than as having no dependent child. Final cash review FC-1: three checks the current rule states had no item - the institution patient and inmate bar of 3.604.1.D-E (cw_is_institution_patient_or_inmate, CO-3802, a bar on the person, reported as ineligible_institution), the strike bar of 3.604.2.L.2 (cw_unit_has_striking_adult, CO-3808, on the unit, ineligible_strike) and the child support conditions of 3.604.4.A (cw_meets_child_support_requirements, CO-3811, on the unit, ineligible_child_support); the institution-resident rule of 3.604.2.O.2 is read through the unit's membership (cw_is_considered_living_in_home, CO-3354) and the ninety days out of State through cw_meets_residency (CO-904). Coverage review (CW-1, CW-7, CW-13, CW-24): a member within a diversion period of ineligibility bars the unit (ineligible_diversion_period; in_diversion_period_of_ineligibility, CO-1269, read as false when not stated; S3152), since the client agreed not to receive further Colorado Works assistance and only the county can end the POI or grant basic cash assistance before it ends; a minor parent whose living arrangement is not met bars every member of the unit, so her child is not paid while she is barred (S3153); the three county closures are cw_county_closure_type (CO-4353, read as none when not stated; S3161, S3162, S3153); a client whose date_of_death is before the first day of the month is ineligible_deceased (S3165), while one who dies during the month keeps that month (3.609.2.C.3 holds the payment for the personal representative). Coverage pass 4 CA4-15: the dependent child is the child of the month evaluated (cw_is_dependent_child_in_month, CO-6807), the age taken in that month. Coverage pass 6 CA6-3, CA6-5, CA6-7 (docs/reviews/coverage6-cash.md, probes W1, W4, W7): the unit has a dependent child or a pregnant member in the month when one of the month's members (cw_assistance_unit_members_in_month, CO-7304: born by the month's end, not dead before its first day) is a dependent child of the month or was pregnant in it (cw_is_pregnant_in_month, CO-7301); before, a child who died in September kept the unit eligible in October, a child born in October gave the unit a dependent child in September, and a pregnancy not stated was read as none (decision 4 of 2026-11-23: is_pregnant is now required where read). Pattern sweep (cash) PS-D5 (docs/reviews/pattern-sweep-cash.md): the disqualified member (CO-928) is read with no default; the IPV finding inside it keeps the county's reading (3.609.5) and the fleeing-felon fact is required.

### CO-922 Colorado Works: payment countable earned income `@engine`

This person's gross earned income for the month less the earned income disregard that determines the payment amount, floored at zero, per 9 CCR 2503-6 3.606.2.A - cw_new_earnings_disregard_rate at application and through the unit's first certification period (A.1) or for a new source of earned income in the first certification period that the income impacts (A.2.a); cw_earned_income_disregard_rate for a current source after the first certification period (A.1, last sentence; A.2.b). The figure the grant payment is computed from; distinct from the cw_earned_income_disregard_dollar eligibility test at application, which cw_countable_earned_income (CO-907) carries.

Precision. Applies the disregard to every person's own earned income, the same assumption cw_countable_earned_income (CO-907) states for cw_earned_income_disregard_dollar, since 3.606.2.A reads 'gross wages for clients' without an adult-only limitation. A unit not yet receiving (receives_tanf_cash false) is at application, whose payment A.1 computes with cw_new_earnings_disregard_rate for the first certification period. For a unit currently receiving, neither cw_in_first_certification_period (CO-1501) nor cw_is_new_earned_income_source (CO-1502) has a default: a case must state which situation a person's earnings fall in; a person with no earned income needs neither, since nothing is disregarded from zero. A person whose month mixes a new and a current source (phase-10 sweep, OQ-350): the new part takes cw_new_earnings_disregard_rate and the rest cw_earned_income_disregard_rate. Earned-income records, step E1 Colorado Works (docs/reviews/records-earnings-cash.md): the new part is the pay from jobs begun on or after the application date (cw_new_source_earnings, CO-5141, read from each record's job_start_date), never more than the gross earned income, in a month the case states falls in the first certification period that the new source impacts (cw_is_new_earned_income_source); a person whose records state no start date then has all earned income from the new source, as before (OQ-1142); before earnings records the new part was a second statement of part of the wages (cw_new_source_earned_income, CO-2374, now read by no item). Vocabulary fix round (R-1): earned income is cw_gross_earned_income (CO-1716): gross wages plus the self-employment net profit 3.605.2.E.1.c treats as earned income; it had read wages only.

The total net countable income of this person's assistance unit for the month, computed with the payment-computation earned income disregard of 3.606.2.A (CO-922 - 100% in the first certification period or for a new source, 67% for a current source after it) rather than the eligibility-test figure (CO-907) - the sum of each member's payment countable earned income and countable unearned income (CO-908), plus any income deemed under 3.605.1.A.4 from a minor-parent member's non-participant parent (CO-909) - the figure 3.606.1.I.3 and 3.606.1.K.1 subtract from the grant standard to compute the authorized grant. A required member disqualified for an intentional program violation or as a fleeing felon has gross earnings counted without disregards (3.604.2.M), and one disqualified for citizenship, status, lawful presence or SSN reasons has earnings net of the cw_earned_income_disregard_dollar employment disregard (3.605.1.A.6); the sponsor's deemed net income (cw_sponsor_deemed_income, 3.605.1.A.5) is added for each sponsored member; and the income of a budgetary-unit member outside the assistance unit (cw_budgetary_member_deemed_income: a stepparent under 3.605.1.A.4.a, a non-parent caretaker's spouse under 3.606.1.J) is added.

OQ-490 resolved (CDHS review S-5): a member disqualified for citizenship, non-citizen status, lawful presence or SSN reasons (cw_is_disqualified_for_status_or_ssn, CO-2557) has net income deemed under 3.605.1.A.6, gross earnings less the cw_earned_income_disregard_dollar employment disregard of 3.605.1.A.4.a (S1808); a member disqualified for an IPV or as a fleeing felon counts gross earnings without disregards (3.604.2.M). Does not model 3.604.2.M.4 (failure to apply for an SSN unless a federally allowable reason under 20 CFR 422.107 exists) - no supplied fact states it - or M.6 (a non-qualified non-citizen), which meets_public_assistance_citizenship_requirement (CO-905) already denies at the person's own status (OQ-143). Whether the person is a resident of Colorado and not barred from Adult Financial programs as a fleeing felon or as an inmate of a city, municipal, county, State or Federal correctional institution, and does not receive, for the month, a payment of financial assistance from another State (3.520.64.B.2), per C.R.S. 26-2-111(1)(a) and 9 CCR 2503-5 3.520.61.B, 3.520.64.A-B, 3.532.E.1, 3.543.E.1 and 3.548.E.1.

Precision. Reads state_of_residence directly, the same as is_colorado_resident (CO-505); adds the 3.520.61.B fleeing-felon and inmate exclusions, which the Medicaid residency test does not carry, so this item's derivation is not identical to CO-505's. Incarceration is read from af_is_inmate_of_correctional_institution (CO-3343), Adult Financial's own bar on a city, municipal, county, State or Federal correctional institution (same-word audit SW-21; final cash review FC-16 corrected this sentence, which had named is_inmate_of_public_institution, CO-1105); CHP+'s 90-day reentry carve-out is CHP+'s own fact, so the Adult Financial bar has no carve-out, as 3.520.61.B states. Scope changed from person to person-month (phase-8 fix round, K-2) because incarceration is a monthly fact; every reader is person-month. Vocabulary fix round (R-6): the fleeing-felon bar reads is_fleeing_felon (CO-038) alone; 3.520.61.B does not name probation or parole violators. Vocabulary fix round (docs/reviews/vocabulary-reuse.md, U-4): state residence reads is_colorado_resident (CO-505) instead of restating the comparison. Final cash review FC-9: 3.520.64.B.2 (S2620) bars a month in which another State pays the person financial assistance; received_financial_assistance_from_another_state_this_month (CO-3859) states it, read as false when not stated. Coverage review F-1: a client temporarily out of State stays a resident unless the absence creates 3.520.64.E's rebuttable presumption and the client has not rebutted it (af_is_presumed_nonresident_by_absence, CO-4401; S3201). ### CO-946 Adult Financial: countable income `@engine`

The person's total countable income for the month for Adult Financial purposes, per 9 CCR 2503-5 3.533 (OAP), 3.544 (AND-SO) and 3.549 (AND-CS) - countable unearned income is gross unearned income less any SSI, less the client's unearned income disregard (af_general_income_disregard_applied_to_unearned, CO-3832: the $20 of af_general_income_disregard, or a married client's equal share of it, A.2.c.1; never more than that income, so an SSI-only client gets none), with the full SSI added back (A.2.a-e); for OAP and AND-CS clients, unearned income includes the in-kind support and maintenance the county determines, up to the ISM maximum (3.520.79); for OAP and AND-CS clients only, when unearned income is under that disregard its unused part goes to the earned income calculation (3.533.A.2.f, 3.549.A.2.f; af_general_income_disregard_rolled_to_earned, CO-3833); countable earned income is gross earned income less that unused amount and af_earned_income_disregard (CO-3047), times af_earned_income_remainder_rate (CO-3048) (A.1).

Precision. SSI is read as ssi_income (CO-849) when receives_ssi is true and as zero otherwise, so a non-SSI client needs no ssi_income statement. OQ-351 resolved (CDHS review S-5): the unused part of the ssi_general_income_exclusion that A.2.f rolls to earned income is measured on the unearned income other than SSI, because A.2.b sets SSI aside before A.2.c deducts the ssi_general_income_exclusion 'from the remainder' and SSI, income based on need, cannot absorb the exclusion (20 CFR 416.1124(c)(12), S310, the SSI program's own order); an SSI recipient whose other unearned income is under ssi_general_income_exclusion rolls the rest to earnings. The unused amount is subtracted before the $65, the SSI order of 20 CFR 416.1112(c). The ISM term is limited to an OAP-age person or an AND-CS-eligible person (af_is_oap_age, af_and_cs_eligible, neither of which reads this item) because 3.520.79 applies to OAP and AND-CS only. Final cash review FC-4 and FC-5, both confirmed with the engine: the $20 is split equally for a married client (af_client_general_income_disregard, CO-3829; OQ-661), so two OAP spouses with $500 of Social Security each have 490 countable each, not 480; and the unused $20 rolls to earnings for OAP and AND-CS only, since 3.544 (AND-SO, S2611) states no rollover, so an AND-SO client with $465 of wages has (465 - 65) / 2 = 200 countable, not 190. The gross earned income, the unearned income other than SSI, the disregard applied and the amount rolled are their own items (CO-3830 to CO-3833), which the spouse deeming of CO-2384 also reads. Income the client refused to secure is counted as available (3.520.71.G.1, af_refused_potential_income, through CO-3831). Reads Adult Financial's own disregards (af_earned_income_disregard CO-3047, af_earned_income_remainder_rate CO-3048, af_general_income_disregard CO-3049): hard-coded numbers audit D-4 found that it read the SSI-method parameters (CO-230 to CO-232) because 3.533/3.544/3.549 state the same dollar figures, but the rule states its own figures and an SSI change would not change them without an amendment. Vocabulary fix round (R-1): gross earned income includes the self-employment net profit of 3.520.783.B (af_self_employment_net_profit, CO-1708); unearned income no longer includes the Adult Financial grant itself (the shared cash assistance fact was split, and tanf_cash_income is Colorado Works only). Receipt records, migration phase 1: the SSI added back is af_ssi_receipts is read from the receipts (CO-5000).

Type money, scope person-month, program AdultFinancial.
Uses: `af_deemed_relative_income`, `af_deemed_sponsor_income`, `af_earned_income_disregard`, `af_earned_income_remainder_rate`, `af_general_income_disregard_applied_to_unearned`, `af_general_income_disregard_rolled_to_earned`, `af_gross_earned_income`, `af_ssi_receipts`, `af_unearned_income_other_than_ssi`, `receives_ssi`.

```
Adult Financial: income deemed from a spouse or parent plus Adult Financial: income deemed from a sponsor plus ((the greater of 0 and ((Adult Financial: gross earned income minus Adult Financial: unearned income disregard rolled to earned income) minus Adult Financial earned income disregard (65))) times Adult Financial share of earned income counted after the disregard (0.5)) plus (Adult Financial: unearned income other than SSI minus Adult Financial: unearned income disregard applied) plus (if Receives Supplemental Security Income;   then Adult Financial: a person's SSI receipts; otherwise 0)
```

### CO-947 Adult Financial: countable resources `@engine`

The countable resources considered against this Adult Financial client's resource limit (9 CCR 2503-5 3.520.72.A, E): the client's and spouse's countable resources under Adult Financial's own rules, plus, for a sponsored non-citizen, the sponsor's countable resources over the sponsor's limit - af_resource_limit_individual (CO-3045) for an unmarried sponsor, af_resource_limit_couple (CO-3046) for a married sponsor whose spouse is not a co-sponsor, and the individual limit for each of a sponsor and co-sponsor spouse.

Precision. The client's and spouse's figure is af_client_and_spouse_countable_resources (CO-2389), Adult Financial's own count of their holdings; the SSI-method figure no longer stands in (same-word SW-31, OQ-392). The limits are Adult Financial's own (af_resource_limit_individual, _couple; hard-coded numbers audit D-4), which af_meets_resource_limit (CO-948) also reads; a sponsor with a spouse who is not a co-sponsor is married wherever the spouse lives (3.520.72.A.2.b, "a married sponsor whose spouse is not a co-sponsor"; coverage review 2, G-5: read from sponsor_spouses_not_cosigning, CO-2714, not from the same-household test sponsor_has_spouse_in_household, CO-2388, which the income deduction of 3.534.D.2.B reads). Coverage review F-15: the stale assumption that Adult Financial's figures equal the SSI-method figures and that a sponsor's resources are not modeled (R-11, OQ-392) is removed; the client's, spouse's and sponsor's resources are all Adult Financial's own count (CO-2389, CO-2390). F-2: the sponsor's resources are deemed only while the sponsor's obligation lasts (af_sponsor_deeming_applies, CO-4400; 3.520.69.B-C). Coverage pass 4 CA4-13 (docs/reviews/coverage4-cash.md): a figure of the month evaluated, from the holdings valued in that month (3.510 "Resources", S4791: "held as of the first day of a calendar month or as of the date of application"), so an application month before the determination month is judged by its own holdings; before, every month read the determination month's. Coverage pass 6 CA6-7: whether the sponsor's spouse co-sponsored is required where the sponsor's resources are deemed (decision 4 of 2026-11-23); before, read as false when not stated.
