Whether the person's af_countable_resources is at or below the Adult Financial resource limit - af_resource_limit_couple (CO-3046) for a married client, af_resource_limit_individual (CO-3045) otherwise - per 9 CCR 2503-5 3.520.72.A and C.R.S. 26-2-111(1)(b), (2)(a)(I).

Precision. Hard-coded numbers audit D-4: the item read the SSI-method limits (ssi_resource_limit_individual, _couple) on the ground that 3.520.72.A's figures are the same dollar amounts; the rule states its own figures and an SSI change would not change them without an amendment, so it reads Adult Financial's own parameters. Final cash review FC-14: resources equal to the limit meet it (at most), following C.R.S. 26-2-111(2)(a) and the SSI rule, against 3.520.71.A.1's "below the resource limit" (OQ-662). Resource records, step H1 Adult Financial (docs/reviews/records-holdings-snap-af.md): where the client's and the spouse's countable resources cannot be determined (a holding that does not state a field the rule reads), the limit is still not met when the parts that are known already exceed it (af_resources_known_lower_bound, CO-5350: every part only adds), as a household with $172,500 in the bank and a home it does not say it lives in. Coverage pass 4 CA4-13 (docs/reviews/coverage4-cash.md): a figure of the month evaluated, from the holdings valued in that month (3.510 "Resources", S4791: "held as of the first day of a calendar month or as of the date of application"), so an application month before the determination month is judged by its own holdings; before, every month read the determination month's. Coverage pass 6 CA6-7: reads af_is_married (CO-7308), which asks for the client's marital status (3.520.63.A), not the shared is_married's reading of an unstated status as not married (decision 4 of 2026-11-23). Pattern sweep (cash) PS-M1 and PS-D4 (docs/reviews/pattern-sweep-cash.md): the spouse is the spouse of the month (af_spouses_in_month, CO-7603), so a spouse who died before the month is not counted in it (3.520.63.A: widowed), and a client whose relationships are not stated, in a case of more than one person, cannot be determined (decision 4); before, every spouse edge counted in every month and unstated relationships were read as no spouse.

### CO-951 Adult Financial: OAP grant amount `@engine`

The monthly Old Age Pension grant payment - for a client resident in a facility listed in 3.532.D for the full calendar month after thirty consecutive days, only a personal needs allowance of at most af_personal_needs_allowance_maximum less countable income (3.532.D, F); otherwise the OAP grant standard minus the client's total countable income, raised to the OAP payment floor by a State Supplementary Payment when it falls below the floor, for a client in the oap category - per 9 CCR 2503-5 3.531.D.2, 3.532.B, D-F and 3.533.

Precision. K-2 (phase-8 fix round): the personal needs allowance is read as a grant standard of af_personal_needs_allowance_maximum from which countable income is deducted, with no payment floor (OQ-352); a psychiatric facility stay counts for a client at or above af_oap_psychiatric_facility_min_age (CO-3052; 3.532.D.3, af_resides_in_psychiatric_facility_thirty_consecutive_days, CO-2006), and a resident of an unlicensed private or uncertified public facility gets neither a PNA nor a grant (3.532.E.2, af_resides_in_unlicensed_or_uncertified_facility, CO-2007; S1318); inmates are barred through af_meets_residency (CO-942). Engineering follow-up 4: 9 CCR 2503-5 3.581.E (S1825) drops the cents from every payment, partial payments included, except where SSI income reduces the grant (af_receives_ssi_in_month, CO-2604); this replaces the phase-5 M-7 reading that Adult Financial grants carry cents, which had not found 3.581.E. Phase-10 sweep (OQ-120), engineering follow-up 4: in the month containing af_eligibility_date (CO-2391) the monthly payment is multiplied by af_partial_month_payment_factor (CO-2603), the 3.581.D table figure for the days of eligibility (the day of eligibility counted, OQ-491 resolved); a client eligible on the first, or with no date stated, gets the full grant. The payment floor is applied to the monthly amount before the factor (3.581.D.1). Coverage pass 4 CA4-25: the first sentence, which said the item did not model 3.532.B.2's proration, is struck; the proration is af_partial_month_payment_factor's (CO-2603), which also pays nothing for a month before the eligibility date (CA4-14), and the program transition of 3.532.B.3 is af_is_oap_age's (CO-940). Pattern sweep (cash) PS-T1 (docs/reviews/pattern-sweep-cash.md): the psychiatric facility's age of 65 (3.532.D.3) is taken on the last day of the month evaluated, as af_is_oap_age takes the OAP age (OQ-951), not on the determination date; before, a client who turned 65 after the determination month began was paid the full grant for that month.

The monthly Aid to the Needy Disabled grant payment - for an AND-SO or AND-CS client resident in a facility listed in 3.543.D or 3.548.D for the full calendar month after thirty consecutive days, only a personal needs allowance of at most af_personal_needs_allowance_maximum less countable income (3.543.D-F, 3.548.D-F); otherwise the applicable AND-SO or AND-CS grant standard minus the client's total countable income, floored at zero for AND-SO and raised to the AND-CS payment floor for AND-CS (3.546.C.2, E) - per 9 CCR 2503-5 3.543.B, 3.544, 3.546, 3.548.B, and 3.549.

Precision. Engineering follow-up 4: in the month containing af_eligibility_date (CO-2391) the monthly payment is multiplied by af_partial_month_payment_factor (CO-2603), the 3.581.D table figure for the days of eligibility (3.543.B.2, 3.548.B.2; OQ-120, OQ-491 resolved); the AND-CS payment floor applies to the monthly amount before the factor. K-2 (phase-8 fix round): the personal needs allowance is read as a grant standard of af_personal_needs_allowance_maximum from which countable income is deducted, with no payment floor; a resident of an unlicensed private or uncertified public facility gets neither a PNA nor a grant (3.543.E.2, 3.548.E.2, af_resides_in_unlicensed_or_uncertified_facility, CO-2007; S1318); Coverage review F-4 (confirmed with the engine on probe PR-PNA): 3.548.F's rule that "The AND-CS grant shall not be reduced until the month following the first full calendar month that the client is a resident in an approved facility" (S1010) was said to be carried by af_resides_in_care_facility_thirty_consecutive_days (CO-1510), but that item is now derived from institution_entry_date and is true in the first full calendar month; an AND-CS client therefore gets the PNA only when the client entered on or before the first day of the month before (the whole of the previous month in the facility), and the full AND-CS grant before then. AND-SO (3.543) has no such rule. There is no Aid to the Blind branch: the current rule has no Aid to the Blind program (3.500, S1017; OQ-112 resolved) and af_category has no ab category (coverage review P3). Engineering follow-up 4: 9 CCR 2503-5 3.581.E (S1825) drops the cents from every payment, partial payments included, except where SSI income reduces the grant (af_receives_ssi_in_month, CO-2604); this replaces the phase-5 M-7 reading that Adult Financial grants carry cents, which had not found 3.581.E. Phase-10 sweep (OQ-120): in the month containing af_eligibility_date (CO-2391) the grant is prorated by the days from that date through the end of the month over the days in the month (3.532.B.2, 3.543.B.2, 3.548.B.2; the day of eligibility is counted, OQ-491); a client eligible on the first, or with no date stated, gets the full grant. No rounding is stated.

### CO-953 Adult Financial: category `@engine`

The single Adult Financial category this person qualifies under for the month - none for a person receiving or eligible for Colorado Works or closed out of it by a sanction (3.520.61.F, 3.520.71.F); otherwise OAP, AND-CS, AND-SO, or none - tested in that order, per C.R.S. 26-2-111 and 9 CCR 2503-5 3.520, 3.530-3.534, 3.540-3.544, and 3.546-3.549.

Precision. Phase-8 fix round: K-3 - the Colorado Works bar (af_barred_by_colorado_works, CO-1511) is the last conjunct of every branch (the and_so branch through af_and_so_eligible, CO-1203), since 3.520.61.F makes it a non-financial requirement of every Adult Financial program (OQ-117 resolved); placed last so that a person who fails an earlier test (age, SSI, disability) is not asked the Colorado Works facts. OQ-112 resolved - the current rule has no Aid to the Blind program (3.500, S1017) and a blind client 0-59 is AND-SO (3.520.61.A); CDHS review N-1: the Aid to the Blind branch, kept until this round as the statute-only route of C.R.S. 26-2-111(5), is removed, since no current rule pays Aid to the Blind and a county could not act on an "ab" result; af_ab_eligible (CO-945) is retired with it. OAP (age 60+) and the AND programs (age 0-59) are mutually exclusive by age (3.520.61.A), so the test order among them does not change the result for any one person; AND-CS is tested before AND-SO because an SSI recipient (AND-CS) would otherwise also satisfy AND-SO's own disability prong. Each branch applies its own income (af_countable_income vs. the relevant grant standard), citizenship, and resource (af_meets_resource_limit) test directly, per 3.520.71.A's 'shall' list (S453: "income below the income limit") and 3.520.781.A's 'equals or exceeds the Adult Financial program grant standard, not eligible for that specific program' (S4382; T-9 hand-check A-1: 3.549, AND-CS, has no sentence of its own, and 3.520.781.A covers every Adult Financial program; 3.533 for OAP, S457, and 3.544 for AND-SO, S2611, say the same), rather than through af_grant_standard (CO-949), which is instead derived from this item's result. The and_so branch also excludes anyone already receiving SSI or SSDI, per 3.540's 'have not been approved for Supplemental Security Income (SSI) or Social Security Disability Insurance (SSDI)' - see OQ-138 for the tension with 26-2-111(4)(a)'s SSDI-determined alternative route. Fix round (C-10): the oap branch now reads af_meets_citizenship_requirement_oap (CO-929, no five-year bar) instead of meets_public_assistance_citizenship_requirement (CO-905, renamed from af_meets_citizenship_requirement), because 3.520.61.C and 3.520.68.A both scope the citizenship prong and the bar to AND only; the and_cs/and_so branches keep reading the AND version. See OQ-113, OQ-114, OQ-119, OQ-138, OQ-151, OQ-357 for this item's dependencies' assumptions and unmodeled nuances. Final cash review FC-6 and FC-9: every branch (the and_so branch through af_and_so_eligible, CO-1203) now also requires that the month is not in a period of ineligibility for a transfer without fair consideration (af_is_in_twfc_penalty_period, CO-3841; 3.520.76, C.R.S. 26-2-111(1)(c)) and that the county has not found the client failed without good cause to apply for and accept retirement or public assistance benefits (af_has_failed_to_apply_for_other_benefits, CO-3860; 3.520.61.G, and for OAP 3.520.71.B and D). Receipt of financial assistance from another State is read in af_meets_residency (CO-942). Coverage review F-13: the AND-CS branch, like AND-SO, bars a patient of an institution for tuberculosis or mental diseases (af_and_is_barred_as_institution_patient, CO-4446; C.R.S. 26-2-111(1)(d)), which (2)(a)(III) does not apply to OAP. F-14: every branch bars a client serving an Adult Financial IPV disqualification (CO-4447; 3.583.N) or in an EBT-misuse ineligibility period (CO-4448; 3.581.I.3), each read as false when not stated (the and_so branch through CO-1203). Coverage review 2, G-4: a client who died before the first day of the month has no category for it (3.581.C.1-2, S3502: eligibility ends on the date of death, and a death before the first of a month leaves no eligibility for that month); the month of death keeps its category and payment (C.3). date_of_death (CO-2868) not stated is read as living.

### CO-1288 CCCAP: all children in part-time care `@engine`

Every child in the CCCAP household is authorized for part-time care - an average of fewer than thirteen full-time-equivalent units of care a month, including a child in grades one through twelve authorized for part-time care during the school year - so the parent fee is 55% of the calculated fee, per 8 CCR 1403-1 3.124.U-W. Stated on the household's adult caretaker or teen parent.

Precision. The children in care are the eligible children for whom care is requested (cccap_care_is_requested_for_child, read as requested when not stated, as the parent-fee formula reads it).

### CO-1289 CCCAP: parent fee by formula `@engine`

The monthly CCCAP parent fee the formula assesses before reductions and exceptions, per 8 CCR 1403-1 3.124.A, P and Q: cccap_parent_fee_base_rate of income up to the monthly 100% federal poverty guideline for the household (cccap_poverty_guideline_monthly, CO-3007), cccap_parent_fee_second_band_rate, _third_band_rate and _top_band_rate of the dollars in the bands above it (cccap_parent_fee_second_band_limit_pct_fpl and _third_band_limit_pct_fpl), and, when income is above the guideline, cccap_parent_fee_additional_child_amount for each child in care after the first. 3.124.P (through July 31, 2028) and 3.124.Q (from August 1, 2028) differ only in the versions of those parameters.

Precision. One marginal formula with dated parameters (engineering follow-up 3, Corticon S-9). Through July 2028 (3.124.P, S785) the three band rates (CO-2115 to CO-2117) are P's base rate plus its marginal increase on each dollar above the guideline and the per-child amount (CO-1286) is P's, which is P's formula: the base rate of income at or below the guideline, and above it the base rate of income plus the increase on each dollar above it plus the per-child amount for each child in care after the first. From August 2028 (3.124.Q, S786) the band rates are Q's and there is no per-child amount; Q's bands are written "101%-130", "131%-160%" and "161% and above", read here as continuous at the band limits so no dollar falls between bands (the band-edge reading stays open, OQ-254). The band rates and the per-child amount are read as of the determination date, not the month evaluated: the county "must assess" the fee at the referral, application or redetermination, and during the twelve-month eligibility period it "cannot be assessed higher than the parent fee determined at the most recent" one (3.124.C, S2850), so a determination made from August 1, 2028 applies Q to every month it evaluates, and one made before applies P (time audit T-3: every other parameter is read in the month evaluated, docs/operators.md, Resolution). The children in care are the household's eligible children: cccap_is_eligible_child requires that care be requested because the child needs care for part of the day (cccap_child_needs_care_for_part_of_day, 3.111.F), so a child not in care is not counted (OQ-254 part 1, resolved). CDHS review C-7/C-8: the formula is applied to cccap_parent_fee_income (CO-2578: the household income, or a protective services household's children's income), and the per-child amount counts the eligible children for whom care is requested (cccap_care_is_requested_for_child, CO-2579; read as requested when not stated), not every eligible child; when the per-child amount is 0 the children are not counted. The amount is not rounded here: 3.124.A (S782) has the parent fee calculated in whole dollars by dropping the cents, which cccap_parent_fee (CO-1290) applies after the reductions (engineering follow-up 4).

### CO-1290 CCCAP: parent fee `@engine`

The monthly parent fee (co-payment) an eligible CCCAP household pays its child care provider - the formula amount, reduced by cccap_quality_rating_fee_reduction_rate (CO-3002) when a top-three quality-rated provider is used and assessed at cccap_part_time_care_fee_rate (CO-3003) of it when all children are in part-time care, in whole dollars with the cents dropped, and no more than $5 while a county hardship reduction is in force (3.124.S) - or nothing for a household that is not eligible, a Child Welfare Child Care household, a family experiencing homelessness during its stabilization period, a teen-parent household whose fee the county waived for hardship, a household whose fee the county waived for dual Head Start enrollment, a declared disaster or teen-parent hardship (3.124.G, I.8, X), a household with no income (a protective services household whose children have no countable income included), or a Colorado Works household whose caretakers have no paid employment, per 8 CCR 1403-1 3.124.A, G, H, I, P, S, U and X.

Precision. CDHS review C-7: 3.124.I.1 (teen-parent hardship waiver, cccap_teen_parent_fee_waiver_granted, CO-2575), I.4 (Child Welfare Child Care, CO-2576) and I.5 (homelessness stabilization period, CO-2577) are applied, each read as false when not stated; a protective services household pays the formula fee on its children's countable income when they have any (I.6, cccap_parent_fee_income, CO-2578), and nothing otherwise. The county-discretion waivers of dual Head Start enrollment, a declared disaster and teen-parent hardship (3.124.G, I.8, X; cccap_parent_fee_waived_by_county, CO-3505) and the $5 hardship reduction (3.124.S; cccap_parent_fee_hardship_reduction_approved, CO-3506, and cccap_parent_fee_hardship_reduced_amount, CO-3507) are applied, each read as false when not stated (OQ-254). The formula fee after the quality and part-time reductions is cccap_parent_fee_assessed (CO-3508). A Colorado Works household is read as having no paid employment when no household member has earned or self-employment income (earned-income records, step E1: gross wages are cccap_person_gross_wages, CO-5152, from the earnings records, replacing wages_gross). Final pass F-02 and F-03: a Child Welfare Child Care household and a family experiencing homelessness in its stabilization period now have their own eligibility statuses (eligible_child_welfare, eligible_homelessness_stabilization), so the I.4 and I.5 rows are reached; the stabilization test is cccap_is_in_homelessness_stabilization (CO-3907). Second-pass review N-1: at a change during the eligibility period or a transition from Colorado Works the assessed fee is capped at the fee last determined (cccap_parent_fee_within_period_cap, CO-4052; 3.124.B-C, 3.117.F).

Whether the person's residence must be verified for CCCAP: every adult caretaker and teen parent must be a verified resident of the county (3.111.A), except in a family experiencing homelessness during its stabilization period, which self-declares residency (3.121.B.4), a Protective Services or Child Welfare Child Care household, for which the county with the open child welfare case is the county of residence (3.119.E, 3.120.E), and a caretaker referred for Colorado Works Child Care, whose residency the Colorado Works program verifies (3.116.E).

Coverage pass 3 C3-3: the referral is read over the household (as cccap_household_unearned_income, CO-2873, reads it), so a second caretaker in the Colorado Works unit who is not stated as referred is not asked for CCCAP documents either; before the fix he was (probe Y-2). ### CO-1451 CCCAP: verification status `@engine`

Where this person's CCCAP household stands on verification: not applicable (no eligible child in the household); none required; complete; pending within the noticing period; past it with only child support paid unverified (the deduction is not allowed); or past due with an eligibility element unverified: the application is denied, or at a redetermination the case is closed (3.111.H.5.e.2). Coverage round F-28: at a change reported during the eligibility period, past_due means only that the verification the change needs is overdue; H.5.e's denial and closure are for applications and redeterminations, and the household's status for the period is cccap_eligibility_status (3.125.Q).

Precision. Assets are self-declared (3.111.H.5.c, S891) and need no verification. Final pass F-02 and F-16: a household transitioning from Colorado Works needs no additional verification until its twelve-month redetermination (3.117.B), so it is not_required; a family experiencing homelessness in its stabilization period has sixty days from the request (cccap_homelessness_verification_due_date, CO-3909), not fifteen (3.121.B.1, B.3.b). Second-pass review N-6: a protective services household has sixty days for its children's income and the immunization record and six months for a child's citizenship, age and identity (3.119.B, F, G; cccap_protective_services_verification_due_date, CO-4061).

    - CCCAP: determination type is equal to transition_from_colorado_works

### CO-1709 CCCAP: self-employment business expenses `@engine`

The person's verified business expenses for the month that 8 CCR 1403-1 3.111.I.2.a allows (rent of business premises, wholesale cost of merchandise, utilities, taxes, business mileage, labor, upkeep of necessary equipment): the operating costs and business vehicle costs; not depreciation, payments on the principal of loans for capital goods, or personal expenses (3.111.I.2.b).

Precision. Earned-income records, step E1 (CCCAP): the costs are earnings records (earnings, CO-5100) of a cost kind, each deducted or not by its row in cccap_earnings_treatment_table (CO-5105; D4: no deduction by silence), paid in the month, replacing the cost facts CO-3370 to CO-3375, each read as 0 when not stated; a cost of the farm kind deducted_for_farm (interest) is deducted when the record is a farm's cost (farm). Second-pass review N-5 (was F-17): the costs are deducted only when verified (3.111.G.2.a: "The county shall obtain verification of all expenses ... or they will not be considered"; I.2: "minus verified business expenses"): receipts (self_employment_cost_receipts_received, CO-3927) or other documents (self_employment_costs_verified_by_other_documents, CO-4062), each read as false when not stated; otherwise nothing is deducted. Coverage round F-20: for a farm (self_employment_is_farm_operation, CO-4465, read as false when not stated) the interest on its debts (self_employment_interest_costs, CO-3371) is deducted too, since 3.111.I.3.b lists "Interest on farm mortgages" among a farm's operating expenses (S3263); I.2.a lists no interest for other self-employment. Coverage pass 5, C5-1 (docs/reviews/coverage5-care-energy.md): a record stated with neither a month nor a date (a stream) is the pay or payment of the days its source ran (docs/conventions.md, "A record's time"; job_start_date and job_end_date for pay, start_date and end_date for a receipt). It stands for the thirty days only when its source ran through all of them (none of its dates after their first day or before their last); it is not read when its source ended before their first day or began on or after cccap_application_or_redetermination_date; and a source that began or ended inside the thirty days is placed by its dated records, so a stream without them cannot determine and the record's date is named as missing (8 CCR 1403-1 3.111.H.4, H.5.a.1, H.5.b, S2704, S891: the income "received during the prior thirty (30) day period"; OQ-680 (2)). A record stated with its month or its date is placed as before. KL-CE-1 (coverage pass 7, R7-3; docs/reviews/known-limits.md, 2026-11-24): a cost of rental property whose rents are unearned income, because the person manages it under an average of cccap_rental_property_self_employment_min_hours_per_week (CO-7252, twenty) hours a week (8 CCR 1403-1 3.111.H.4.e, S2704; the line as cccap_rental_property_receipts_as_unearned, CO-7251, tests it), is not a cost of self-employment: it is taken against the property's rents (cccap_rental_property_costs, CO-7910; I.12, I.17 "Net rental income"). A cost record says which business it is of by its job, the job its business's receipts record states (earnings, CO-5100); the records are read in this order: whether any of the person's business receipts records is rental property (rental_property), then the line, then the cost's business, so the job is read only for a person with rental property. Before, every cost record of the person was a cost of self-employment, so the costs of a rental under the line were taken against no self-employment receipts and lost (probe CR2).

Type money, scope person-month, program CCCAP.
Uses: `cccap_application_or_redetermination_date`, `cccap_earnings_treatment_table`, `cccap_prior_income_period_days`, `cccap_rental_property_management_hours`, `cccap_rental_property_self_employment_min_hours_per_week`, `earnings`, `self_employment_cost_receipts_received`, `self_employment_costs_verified_by_other_documents`.

```
if any of the following is true:
    - Receipts received for the self-employment costs, otherwise no
    - Self-employment costs verified by documents other than receipts, otherwise no
  then the sum of that receipt's amount for each receipt in Earnings where ((all of the following are true:;   - if CCCAP: how each kind of earnings is treated (table), for that receipt's kind is equal to deducted;     then yes;   else if CCCAP: how each kind of earnings is treated (table), for that receipt's kind is equal to deducted_for_farm;     then that receipt's farm;   otherwise no;   - if it is not the case that that receipt's month is unknown;     then that receipt is received in the month;   else if any of the following is true:;       - all of the following are true:;         - it is not the case that that receipt's job end date is unknown;         - that receipt's job end date is less than 0 minus CCCAP: the days before the application or redetermination whose income is read (30) days after CCCAP application or redetermination date;       - all of the following are true:;         - it is not the case that that receipt's job start date is unknown;         - that receipt's job start date is at least CCCAP application or redetermination date;     then no;   else if all of the following are true:;       - any of the following is true:;         - that receipt's job start date is unknown;         - that receipt's job start date is at most 0 minus CCCAP: the days before the application or redetermination whose income is read (30) days after CCCAP application or redetermination date;       - any of the following is true:;         - that receipt's job end date is unknown;         - that receipt's job end date is at least -1 days after CCCAP application or redetermination date;     then that receipt is received in the month;   otherwise (all of the following are true:;   - that receipt's date is at least 0 minus CCCAP: the days before the application or redetermination whose income is read (30) days after CCCAP application or redetermination date;   - that receipt's date is less than CCCAP application or redetermination date);   - it is not the case that (all of the following are true:;   - (the sum of 1 for each receipt in that receipt's owner's Earnings where ((all of the following are true:;   - that receipt's kind is equal to self_employment_receipts;   - that receipt's rental property))) is more than 0;   - (that receipt's owner's CCCAP: hours in the month managing rental property stated as a business divided by ((the number of days from the first day of the month to the first day of the month after the month) divided by 7)) is less than CCCAP: hours a week of active management that make rental property self-employment (20);   - if that receipt's job is equal to job_1;     then (the sum of 1 for each receipt in that receipt's owner's Earnings where ((all of the following are true:;   - that receipt's kind is equal to self_employment_receipts; ### CO-1710 CCCAP: countable self-employment income `@engine`

The person's countable self-employment income for the month under 8 CCR 1403-1 3.111.I.2: 'declared gross income minus verified business expenses' from self-employment, not below zero; or, while the self-employment is in its launch period, the projected income of 3.111.G.2.e, the federal minimum wage times the declared hours of self-employment.

Precision. Earned-income records, step E1 (CCCAP; docs/reviews/records-earnings-care-energy.md): the gross receipts are cccap_self_employment_gross_receipts (CO-5156), and the declared hours of the launch period are the hours each self-employment record of the month states (hours, required where read), replacing self_employment_gross_receipts (CO-1700) and self_employment_hours_worked (CO-4461), which read all of hours_worked (CO-022) when not stated: G.2.e projects "the number of declared hours worked" in the business, and hours_worked holds a wage job's hours too, so the default could project a wage job's hours as self-employment (decision 4 of 2026-11-23: an unstated required field is cannot determine). A person with no gross receipts has none, whatever the cost records say, unless in the launch period. Coverage round F-11: G.2.e: "Projected income for the launch period shall be determined based upon the federal minimum wage times the number of declared hours worked"; in the launch period (cccap_self_employment_in_launch_period, CO-2113, read as false when not stated) the income is federal_minimum_wage (CO-160) times self_employment_hours_worked (CO-4461; all of hours_worked when not stated), not the receipts (probe RV-H: $300 of receipts and 120 hours counted $300, fee $3; projected $870, fee $8). Coverage round F-20: farm self-employment (3.111.I.3, S3263) is read from the same neutral facts, the receipts stated without the farm products the family used (I.3.c); its operating expenses include the interest on farm debts (cccap_self_employment_business_expenses, CO-1709, with self_employment_is_farm_operation, CO-4465). Coverage pass 4 C4-3: the declared hours are cccap_self_employment_hours (CO-6404), the item cccap_caretaker_in_eligible_activity (CO-984) also reads, instead of the same sum written here. Coverage pass 5, C5-5 (docs/reviews/coverage5-care-energy.md): a business in its launch period that has no receipts yet states a self-employment record of amount 0 with the month's declared hours (hours), since the hours are read from the month's self-employment records (cccap_self_employment_hours, CO-6404) and a caretaker with no such record has no business for G.2.e to project (S1410).

Type money, scope person-month, program CCCAP.
Uses: `cccap_self_employment_business_expenses`, `cccap_self_employment_gross_receipts`, `cccap_self_employment_hours`, `cccap_self_employment_in_launch_period`, `federal_minimum_wage`.

  then Federal minimum wage (7.25) times CCCAP: hours of self-employment in the month
else if CCCAP: a person's self-employment gross receipts in a month is at most 0
  then 0
otherwise the greater of 0 and (CCCAP: a person's self-employment gross receipts in a month minus CCCAP: self-employment business expenses)
```

### CO-2107 CCCAP: resident of the county applied to `@engine`

Whether this adult caretaker or teen parent meets the residency test of 8 CCR 1403-1 3.111.A: at an application or a redetermination, a Colorado resident whose county of residence is the county from which Low-Income Child Care assistance is sought or received; at a change reported during the eligibility period or a transition from Colorado Works, a Colorado resident, since a caretaker who moves to another county "shall remain eligible for the duration of the eligibility period" (3.111.A, 3.125.GG).

Precision. Coverage round F-05: 3.111.A's second sentence and 3.125.GG let a household that moves out of the county during the eligibility period stay eligible until its redetermination, the originating county keeping the case; only a move out of the state ends eligibility during the period (3.114.A.2, 3.125.Q.3), and a county move is acted on at the redetermination (3.114.B.8). At a change during the eligibility period (cccap_determination_type, CO-3307) the test is therefore Colorado residency alone; cccap_application_county is the originating county. GG's other two conditions, income below 85% of state median income and an eligible activity, are tested by cccap_eligibility_status (CO-989) at every determination. Coverage pass 2 C2-8: a transition from Colorado Works is read the same way: 3.116.L (S3531) keeps Colorado Works Child Care for a caretaker who moves county during the twelve months, 3.117.B (S3531) requires "No additional verification ... until the household's twelve (12) month re-determination", and 3.117.A lists the only conditions that stop a transition (S2851); before the fix a Colorado Works family that had moved county was ineligible at its transition. Before the fix a stated county move failed the test at a change (probe RV-C).

Type yes/no, scope person, program CCCAP.
Uses: `cccap_application_county`, `cccap_determination_type`, `county_of_residence`, `is_colorado_resident`.

all of the following are true:

    - County of residence is equal to CCCAP: county applied to
    - CCCAP: determination type is one of: change_during_eligibility_period, transition_from_colorado_works
```

### CO-2578 CCCAP: income the parent fee is computed on `@engine`

The monthly income the CCCAP parent-fee formula is applied to: for a protective services household, the countable income of the household's eligible children (8 CCR 1403-1 3.119.A, cccap_protective_services_income), since such a household has no fee unless the children have countable income (3.124.I.6); for a Colorado Works Child Care household, only the earned income of the household (3.116.C: "only earned income that is reported and verified by the county Colorado Works worker will be considered countable income"; 3.124.E), less the court-ordered child support deduction (3.111.K.1); for any other household, the household's countable gross income (cccap_household_income, CO-985).

Precision. Second-pass review N-2: cccap_protective_services_income (CO-994) is now itself the sum over the household's eligible children, so it is read as it is. The rule does not state the base of a protective services household's formula fee; the children's countable income is read as the base because it is the only income 3.119.A counts for such a household (OQ-536). Final pass F-08: a Colorado Works household's earned income is the sum of cccap_person_earned_income (CO-3915: wages and CCCAP self-employment income, nothing for a household child who is not a teen parent) over the household, as the Colorado Works worker verifies it; its unearned income (a child's survivor benefit, child support received) is not counted. The 3.111.K deduction (cccap_child_support_paid_deduction, CO-3902) applies "when calculating parent fees", not below zero.

Type money, scope person-month, program CCCAP.
Uses: `cccap_child_support_paid_deduction`, `cccap_eligibility_status`, `cccap_household_income`, `cccap_household_income_members`, `cccap_person_earned_income`, `cccap_protective_services_income`.

if CCCAP: eligibility status is equal to eligible_protective_services
  then CCCAP: protective services household income
else if CCCAP: eligibility status is equal to eligible_colorado_works
  then the greater of 0 and ((the sum of that person's CCCAP: a person's countable earned income for each person in CCCAP: household members whose income counts) minus (the sum of that person's CCCAP: child support paid deduction for each person in CCCAP: household members whose income counts))
otherwise CCCAP: household income
```

### CO-2607 CCCAP: persons of whom this person is an adult caretaker `@engine`

The persons of whom this person is the "parent, adoptive parent, step-parent, legal guardian, or person who is acting in 'loco parentis'" of 8 CCR 1403-1 3.103.C (S481): read from the neutral roles parent (natural or adoptive), stepparent, legal_guardian and has_primary_responsibility_for; and, under 3.111.D.2, an adult or teen parent in the home who contributes financially to the welfare of the child (contributes_financially_to).

Precision. Same-word audit SW-1/SW-3/SW-4 (OQ-396 resolved): a person acting in loco parentis is read as one with primary responsibility for the child (has_primary_responsibility_for), the role a case states for a non-parent who has taken on the child's care; 3.103.C's presence in the home and financial contribution are tested by cccap_is_adult_caretaker (CO-992). A relative who shares the care while the parent is in the home and has not taken it on is not stated with that role and is not an adult caretaker (OQ-540). Same-word audit SW-7 (convention rule 17): an edge joins persons who live together (lives_with, CO-1925, from dwelling_id); where a case states no dwelling_id the edge is read as living together, as before. Physical custody of the child in the home (3.103, S481) is read as living with the child; an involuntarily absent caretaker is CO-898. Coverage round F-15: 3.111.D.2 (S3254): "Households are considered households with two adult caretakers or teen parents when two adults or teen parents contribute financially to the welfare of the child and/or assume parent rights, duties, and obligations similar to those of a biological parent, even without legal adoption"; the "and/or" is read as making financial contribution alone enough, so a partner in the home who contributes financially to the child's welfare (the neutral role contributes_financially_to) is an adult caretaker of the child, his income counts and he must be in an activity (D.4). OQ-540 records the reading against 3.103.C. Three-pattern sweep D-1 (docs/reviews/pattern-sweep-snap-ce.md): lives_with (CO-1925) is read as stated, required where read: no text on file says that persons related on the application live together unless it says otherwise (8 CCR 1403-1 3.103.LLL: the household is the children in the home and the adult caretakers, S3636), so a stated relationship is no longer read as living together where no dwelling_id is stated (decision 4; docs/conventions.md rule 17, as MAGI's readers since coverage pass 6, C6-10); a case with persons related across the edge states dwelling_id for each of them.

Type group of persons, scope person, program CCCAP.
Uses: `lives_with`, `relationships`.

```
all persons in every person in the case such that
  all of the following are true:
    - this person is a parent or stepparent or legal_guardian or has_primary_responsibility_for or contributes_financially_to of that person
    - that person is in Lives with
```

["filter",["persons"],["all",["rel",["parent","stepparent","legal_guardian","has_primary_responsibility_for","contributes_financially_to"],["P"]],["in_group",["P"],"lives_with"]]]
```

The monthly 100% federal poverty guideline for the size of this person's CCCAP household (cccap_household_size, CO-983), the base of the entry income limit (3.111.H.1.a) and of the parent fee formula (3.124.P-Q): the annual HHS guideline in force on the most recent October 1 on or before the determination date (cccap_poverty_guideline_start_month, CO-3006), for the household's size up to the table's last row (eight persons), divided by twelve and rounded to the cent, plus, for each member beyond that row, the HHS step for each additional person divided by twelve and rounded to the cent, as 8 CCR 1403-1 3.111.H.2-3 state the figures in their table (sizes 1 to 8 and an 'Each Additional person' amount).

The court-ordered child support this adult caretaker or teen parent pays in the month for children not living in the household that 8 CCR 1403-1 3.111.K deducts from the household's monthly gross income, both before the income is compared with the income guidelines and when the parent fee is calculated: the current support paid under a court order, not the part paid toward arrears, and only when the order and the payments are verified (K.2); otherwise nothing.

Verification is child_support_paid_is_verified (CO-1363): electronic data or documents showing both the order and the payments (K.2.a). ### CO-3915 CCCAP: a person's countable earned income `@engine`

This person's earned income that CCCAP counts (8 CCR 1403-1 3.111.I.1-3, J): the gross wages received in the prior thirty days (3.111.H.4-5: "income received during the prior thirty (30) day period shall be used in determining eligibility"), each earnings record (earnings, CO-5100) whose kind CCCAP's counting table counts as wages (cccap_earnings_treatment_table, CO-5105: wages, armed forces pay, WIOA wages, I.1 and I.31, and the other pay no paragraph of J excludes; not work-study, J.16), without the irregular pay J.28 excludes when the quarter's irregular income is under ninety dollars; plus CCCAP's self-employment income (taxable gross income less verified business expenses, prorated to a month, H.4.c, I.2-3; cccap_self_employment_net_earnings, CO-1710); or nothing for a child in the household who is not a teen parent, whose earnings 3.111.J.1 excludes.

Precision. Earned-income records, step E1 (CCCAP; docs/reviews/records-earnings-care-energy.md): read from the earnings records, replacing wages_gross_received_prior_thirty_days (CO-3910) and the month's wages_gross less work_study_earnings (each read as 0 when not stated). A pay stated with its date is read when its date is in the cccap_prior_income_period_days (CO-5151) days before cccap_application_or_redetermination_date (CO-5150): the thirty days end the day before that date (OQ-680), so a weekly earner paid on five Fridays in them has five pays counted. A pay stated by its month, or a stream with no date, is read for the month determined, standing for the thirty days as CCCAP's receipts do (cccap_counted_recurring_receipts, CO-5721; OQ-680). J.28 (finding E1-C3): a pay marked irregular is left out when the irregular income of the calendar quarter, receipts (cccap_irregular_receipts_in_quarter, CO-5724) and earnings (cccap_irregular_earnings_in_quarter, CO-6151) together, is under cccap_irregular_income_quarterly_limit (CO-4075); the quarter is read only when the person has an irregular pay in the thirty days. In-kind pay, an employer's vendor payments and boarders are "other income" (I.4, I.5, I.18; cccap_other_countable_receipts, CO-4464), not earned income. The J.1 exclusion is keyed to the 3.103.LLL household-child term (cccap_is_household_child, CO-990), not the narrower 3.111.F eligible-child term. Read by cccap_person_countable_income (CO-3917) and, for a Colorado Works Child Care household, by cccap_parent_fee_income (CO-2578), which counts earned income only (3.116.C). Coverage round F-27: owners of a limited liability corporation or S corporation "are considered employees of the corporation" (3.111.G.1.c, D-87), so the pay they draw is wages; VISTA payments are receipts (CO-5000), counted as CCCAP's receipt table reads them (3.111.I.32). Coverage pass 4 (docs/reviews/coverage4-care-energy.md): C4-1, an irregular pay is tested under J.28 against the calendar quarter of its own date (a pay dated in the thirty days, against the quarter the thirty days begin in, cccap_irregular_income_in_first_quarter_of_period CO-6402, when its month is on or before cccap_prior_income_period_first_quarter_end CO-6401, else the quarter they end in, CO-6403), or of the month determined for a pay stated without a date; it is counted when that quarter's irregular income, earned and unearned, is not less than ninety dollars (OQ-713). C4-4, a pay that states annual_contract_pay is counted at one twelfth of the contract (cccap_annual_contract_months, CO-6406) in each month, in place of its amount, as H.4.b (S2704) prorates contract employment "over the term of the contract" (OQ-1221); the earnings record states the contract on one record of the job for each month (CO-5100). C4-5, a VISTA payment at or above the minimum wage (receipts of kind dvsa_title_i_payment_at_or_above_minimum_wage, cccap_receipt_treatment_table row counted_as_earned_unless_receiving_cccap_when_joined) is earned income unless the client was receiving CCCAP when joining VISTA (I.32, S4601; received_cccap_when_joined_vista, CO-6407, with no default, read only when there is such a payment); placed as the other receipts are, in the thirty days when dated. A person whose receipts are not stated has earned income that cannot be determined, since a VISTA payment may be among them (decision 4 of 2026-11-23). Coverage pass 5, C5-1 (docs/reviews/coverage5-care-energy.md): a record stated with neither a month nor a date (a stream) is the pay or payment of the days its source ran (docs/conventions.md, "A record's time"; job_start_date and job_end_date for pay, start_date and end_date for a receipt). It stands for the thirty days only when its source ran through all of them (none of its dates after their first day or before their last); it is not read when its source ended before their first day or began on or after cccap_application_or_redetermination_date; and a source that began or ended inside the thirty days is placed by its dated records, so a stream without them cannot determine and the record's date is named as missing (8 CCR 1403-1 3.111.H.4, H.5.a.1, H.5.b, S2704, S891: the income "received during the prior thirty (30) day period"; OQ-680 (2)). A record stated with its month or its date is placed as before. Coverage pass 5, C5-3 (docs/reviews/coverage5-care-energy.md): AmeriCorps payments (receipts of kind americorps, cccap_receipt_treatment_table row counted_as_earned) are earned income: 3.111.I.32 (S4020) reads "Earned AmeriCorps income includes ... wages of AmeriCorps volunteers"; a recurring payment is placed as the VISTA payments are, and one paid once counts one twelfth in the month received (H.4.i, the more beneficial count, as cccap_one_time_receipts_averaged reads a lump sum); a household child who is not a teen parent has none (J.1, S486). Before, they were counted as unearned income (cccap_counted_recurring_receipts, CO-5721).

### CO-3916 CCCAP: a person's countable unearned income `@engine`

This person's unearned income that CCCAP counts (8 CCR 1403-1 3.111.I.6-33, J): the recurring receipts of the month that CCCAP's counting table counts, standing for the unearned income received in the prior thirty days (3.111.H.5.b; cccap_counted_recurring_receipts: pensions, unemployment, child support, interest, Social Security (I.25) and the other unearned income, less Social Security set aside under a plan for self-support, J.13), plus one twelfth of each counted receipt paid once in the month (H.4.i: a non-recurring lump sum is counted in the month received or averaged over twelve months, "whichever is most beneficial"; cccap_one_time_receipts_averaged: an inheritance, a gift or a prize, I.20, a lump-sum child support payment, and any other one-time payment), plus the receipts 3.111.I counts that are not money received as unearned income (in-kind compensation, employer vendor payments, boarders), less the irregular receipts J.28 excludes and the receipts and deductions 3.111.I-J take out that the counting table does not (cccap_excluded_unearned_receipts). What CCCAP counts or excludes, kind by kind, is its counting table (cccap_receipt_treatment_table).

Precision. Receipt records, migration phase 2 (docs/reviews/receipts-migration-2-cccap-sunbucks.md): read from the receipts (CO-5000), replacing unearned_income_prior_thirty_days (CO-3913, removed), social_security_income, lump_sum_received, lottery_gambling_winnings_received, retroactive_ssi_or_public_assistance_lump_sum_received and insurance_proceeds_spent_on_medical_or_burial. SSI (J.2) and Colorado Works, OAP and AND grants (J.26) are excluded by their kinds, a retroactive lump sum of them included. The month's receipts stand for the prior thirty days, and one-time receipts are read by the month received (OQ-680). A receipt paid once is averaged whatever its kind (OQ-873). Work-study earnings are excluded (J.16; cccap_person_earned_income, CO-3915, leaves them out of the wages) and a household child's earnings are earned income (CO-3915). Second-pass review P2: irregular income under $90 in the calendar quarter is taken out (J.28, cccap_excluded_irregular_income, CO-4076), not below zero. Coverage round F-07 to F-10, F-25: cccap_other_countable_receipts (CO-4464: I.4, I.5, I.18) is added and cccap_excluded_unearned_receipts (CO-4463: the adoption subsidy and research study payments that have no kind of their own, the net rental and early-payout penalty deductions of I.8, I.12, I.17, and a diversion that is cash assistance) is taken out; the part of life insurance, health insurance or personal injury proceeds spent on last illness and burial or medical care is the receipt's spent_on_covered_costs, taken off before it is averaged (I.21-22). Coverage pass 6 for CCCAP, R6-4: the receipts of rental property the person manages under an average of twenty hours a week, stated as a business, are unearned rent (cccap_rental_property_receipts_as_unearned, CO-7251; 3.111.H.4.e), counted here and net of the landlord's expenses (CO-4463).

Type money, scope person-month, program CCCAP.
Uses: `cccap_counted_recurring_receipts`, `cccap_excluded_irregular_income`, `cccap_excluded_unearned_receipts`, `cccap_one_time_receipts_averaged`, `cccap_other_countable_receipts`, `cccap_rental_property_receipts_as_unearned`.

```
the greater of 0 and ((CCCAP: a person's counted recurring receipts plus CCCAP: a person's one-time receipts, averaged plus CCCAP: other countable receipts plus CCCAP: rental property receipts that are unearned income) minus (CCCAP: excluded irregular income plus CCCAP: unearned receipts excluded from countable income))
```

```

### CO-3917 CCCAP: a person's countable income `@engine`

This person's monthly countable income for CCCAP (8 CCR 1403-1 3.111.H.4-5, I, J): generally the income received in the prior thirty days, earned (CO-3915) and unearned (CO-3916); or, where the county found case by case that those thirty days do not give an accurate indication of anticipated income and used another period, the monthly income the county so determined (cccap_county_determined_monthly_income, CO-3914).

Precision. The county's figure, when stated, replaces the thirty-day figure for the person; it is not added to it. cccap_household_income (CO-985) sums this item over the household and subtracts the 3.111.K child support deduction.

Type money, scope person-month, program CCCAP.
Uses: `cccap_county_determined_monthly_income`, `cccap_person_earned_income`, `cccap_person_unearned_income`.

```
CCCAP: monthly income the county determined from another period, otherwise CCCAP: a person's countable earned income plus CCCAP: a person's countable unearned income
```

["otherwise","cccap_county_determined_monthly_income",["+","cccap_person_earned_income","cccap_person_unearned_income"]]

### CO-4052 CCCAP: assessed parent fee, capped during the eligibility period `@engine`

The parent fee as the formula assesses it (cccap_parent_fee_assessed, CO-3508), but, at a change during the twelve-month eligibility period or a transition from Colorado Works to Low-Income Child Care, no higher than the fee determined at the household's most recent Colorado Works Child Care referral, Low-Income application or redetermination (cccap_parent_fee_at_last_determination, CO-4050), unless the change is one of the circumstances in which 8 CCR 1403-1 3.124.B.1, B.3 or B.4 lets the fee rise (cccap_parent_fee_increase_basis, CO-4051) (3.124.B-C, 3.117.F).

Precision. At an application or a redetermination (cccap_determination_type, CO-3307) the formula fee is used as it is: a new eligibility period begins and 3.124.R updates the fee to the formula in effect. A lower formula fee is always used (B.2). cccap_parent_fee (CO-1290) applies its waivers and the 3.124.S hardship reduction to this figure; capping first and then reducing gives the same fee as reducing first, since both take the lesser amount. Whether B.1, B.3 and B.4 lift the cap altogether or only allow the increase they cause is not stated; the volume lifts it (OQ-712). Coverage round F-26: 3.124.R (S3261) says counties "update parent fees at the next scheduled re-determination" for the new federal poverty guideline and formula; the formula fee at a change during the period reads the guideline in force in the month determined (CO-3007), so after October 1 a change can lower the fee under the new guideline before the redetermination. The cap keeps an increase from taking effect; a decrease the new guideline alone causes is allowed, as B.2 allows any decrease.

Type money, scope person-month, program CCCAP.
Uses: `cccap_determination_type`, `cccap_parent_fee_assessed`, `cccap_parent_fee_at_last_determination`, `cccap_parent_fee_increase_basis`.

```
if all of the following are true:
    - CCCAP: determination type is one of: change_during_eligibility_period, transition_from_colorado_works
    - (CCCAP: reason the parent fee may rise during the eligibility period, otherwise none) is equal to none
  then the lesser of CCCAP: parent fee as assessed by the formula and CCCAP: parent fee determined at the most recent referral, application or redetermination
otherwise CCCAP: parent fee as assessed by the formula
```

["case",[["all",["in","cccap_determination_type",["change_during_eligibility_period","transition_from_colorado_works"]],["=",["otherwise","cccap_parent_fee_increase_basis","none"],"none"]],["min","cccap_parent_fee_assessed","cccap_parent_fee_at_last_determination"]],["else","cccap_parent_fee_assessed"]]
```

### CO-4056 CCCAP: a child of eligible age who needs care for part of the day `@engine`

The person is a child from birth to age thirteen, or a child with verified additional care needs under age nineteen who is physically or mentally incapable of self-care or under court supervision, who needs child care during a portion of the day but less than twenty-four hours: the age and need parts of the "eligible child" definition (8 CCR 1403-1 3.103.UU, 3.111.F), without its citizenship part, which 3.103.UU applies to "Any child served through the Colorado Works program or the Low-Income Child Care program".

Precision. cccap_is_eligible_child (CO-980) adds the citizenship part. Read by itself for Child Welfare Child Care (cccap_eligibility_status, CO-989), which is not funded through the Child Care Development Fund (3.120.F) and which 3.103.UU's citizenship sentence does not name (OQ-710). Residing with the caretaker is read from the household (cccap_household_members, CO-982), as for CO-980. Coverage round F-06: a child who exceeds the age limits during the eligibility period stays an eligible child until the redetermination: 3.114.B.1 ends care for an "Eligible child [who] exceeds age limits" "at re-determination only" (S3251), and 3.125.Q's closed list of reasons to discontinue care before the redetermination does not name age (S3252). At a change reported during the period (cccap_determination_type, CO-3307), a child authorized at the last determination (cccap_child_was_authorized_at_last_determination, CO-4462, read as false when not stated) is not tested on age; a child added during the period is (3.125.FF). Before the fix a child who turned thirteen during the period made the household ineligible_child at a change (probe RV-D). T-9 hand check A-8: "from birth to the age of thirteen (13) years" (3.103.UU, 3.111.F) is read with the Child Care and Development Fund rule CCCAP's Low-Income and Colorado Works child care are paid from, 45 CFR 98.20(a)(1) (S4420): a child "under 13 years of age", or, at the Lead Agency's option, "under age 19 and physically or mentally incapable of caring for himself or herself, or under court supervision": a child of thirteen is not an eligible child by age, nor one of nineteen with additional care needs (CO-4056-T7 to T10). Child Welfare Child Care, which is not funded through the Child Care Development Fund (3.120.F), reads the same state words the same way; whether its 'eligible child' reaches a child of thirteen is OQ-1163. CO-950's "age zero (0) to fifty-nine (59)" (Adult Financial) is another program's text and is not read here.

Type yes/no, scope person, program CCCAP.
Uses: `age`, `cccap_child_has_additional_care_needs`, `cccap_child_needs_care_for_part_of_day`, `cccap_child_was_authorized_at_last_determination`, `cccap_determination_type`, `cccap_disabled_child_age_limit`, `cccap_eligible_child_age_limit`.

```
all of the following are true:
  - any of the following is true:
    - Age is less than CCCAP eligible child age limit (13)
    - all of the following are true:
      - Age is less than CCCAP additional-care-needs child age limit (19)
      - Has verified additional care needs
    - all of the following are true:
      - CCCAP: child authorized at the last determination, otherwise no
      - CCCAP: determination type is equal to change_during_eligibility_period
  - CCCAP: child needs care for part of the day
```

### CO-4060 CCCAP: immunization verification is pending `@engine`

Whether CCCAP still needs this child's immunization record (or a religious or medical exemption): an eligible child who is not attending school and is in care outside the home from an unrelated qualified exempt provider (8 CCR 1403-1 3.111.F.2), outside a homeless family's stabilization period (3.121.B.6), whose record has not been received, where CCCAP verification applies to the person.

Precision. The element cccap_person_pending_verification_count (CO-1448) counted inline, made its own item so the protective services due date (cccap_protective_services_verification_due_date, CO-4061) can tell it from the others. Due by: cccap_verification_due_date (CO-1450); sixty days for a protective services household (3.119.G). Coverage round F-06: the record is asked for at an application, a redetermination (3.113.A.3; a missing record ends care "at re-determination only", 3.114.B.7, S3251) and for a child added during the period, not again at a change for a child already authorized (cccap_child_was_authorized_at_last_determination, CO-4462, read as false when not stated): 3.125.Q (S3252) does not let a missing record discontinue care before the redetermination.

Type yes/no, scope person-month, program CCCAP.
Uses: `cccap_care_is_from_unrelated_exempt_provider_outside_home`, `cccap_child_was_authorized_at_last_determination`, `cccap_determination_type`, `cccap_immunization_record_received`, `cccap_is_attending_school`, `cccap_is_eligible_child`, `cccap_is_in_homelessness_stabilization`, `cccap_verification_is_applicable`.

all of the following are true:
  - CCCAP: verification applies to this person
  - CCCAP: is an eligible child
  - it is not the case that (all of the following are true:;   - CCCAP: determination type is equal to change_during_eligibility_period;   - CCCAP: child authorized at the last determination, otherwise no)
  - CCCAP: care from an unrelated exempt provider outside the home, otherwise no
  - it is not the case that CCCAP: attending school
  - it is not the case that CCCAP: family experiencing homelessness in its stabilization period
  - it is not the case that CCCAP: immunization record received

### CO-4061 CCCAP: verification due date for a protective services household `@engine`

The date by which a protective services household must provide the verification still pending (8 CCR 1403-1 3.119.B, F, G): fifteen days after the county's request (cccap_verification_due_date, CO-1450) when any element other than the children's income, the immunization record and a child's citizenship, age or identity is pending; otherwise sixty days for the children's income (cccap_protective_services_income_verification_days, CO-4057) and for the immunization record (cccap_protective_services_immunization_verification_days, CO-4058), the earlier where both are pending; and, when only a child's citizenship, age or identity is pending, six months (cccap_protective_services_child_identity_verification_months, CO-4059).

Precision. Counted over the household (cccap_household_members, CO-982): the pending elements in all (cccap_pending_verification_count, CO-1449) less the income (CO-2590, CO-1681), immunization (CO-4060) and citizenship, age and identity (CO-1678 to CO-1680) elements. The six months are counted from the county's request, the same day as the referral when the Child Welfare worker cannot attest at the referral (3.119.F, F.3: "within six (6) months of the referral"), as the same day of the month six months later (a request on the 31st of a month whose sixth month is shorter runs into the following month); the sixty days from the request (OQ-716). The request date is the program's own, else the shared checklist date (OQ-300). Read by cccap_verification_status (CO-1451) for a protective services case.

Type calendar date, scope person-month, program CCCAP.
Uses: `cccap_age_verification_is_pending`, `cccap_citizenship_verification_is_pending`, `cccap_earned_income_verification_is_pending`, `cccap_household_members`, `cccap_identity_verification_is_pending`, `cccap_immunization_verification_is_pending`, `cccap_pending_verification_count`, `cccap_protective_services_child_identity_verification_months`, `cccap_protective_services_immunization_verification_days`, `cccap_protective_services_income_verification_days`, `cccap_unearned_income_verification_is_pending`, `cccap_verification_due_date`, `cccap_verification_request_date`, `verification_request_date`.

```
if (CCCAP: pending verification count minus (the sum of (if that person's CCCAP: unearned income verification is pending;   then 1; otherwise 0) plus (if that person's CCCAP: earned income verification is pending;   then 1; otherwise 0) plus (if that person's CCCAP: immunization verification is pending;   then 1; otherwise 0) plus (if that person's CCCAP: citizenship verification is pending;   then 1; otherwise 0) plus (if that person's CCCAP: age verification is pending;   then 1; otherwise 0) plus (if that person's CCCAP: identity verification is pending;   then 1; otherwise 0) for each person in CCCAP: household members)) is more than 0

else if there is a person in CCCAP: household members such that

### CO-4064 CCCAP: household members whose income counts `@engine`

The members of this person's CCCAP household (cccap_household_members, CO-982) whose income and child support deduction count toward the household's income: all of them, except the spouse or the child's other parent of a member who is separated from them and holds a validly issued temporary order for parental responsibilities or child custody (has_temporary_order_for_parental_responsibilities, CO-4063), whose financial resources 8 CCR 1403-1 3.111.D.10 does not let the county count against that caretaker.

Precision. The other parent is a member who is a parent or stepparent of a household child one of whose parents holds the order (cccap_has_parent_with_temporary_order, CO-4070); the order holder's own income still counts. Membership is unchanged: D.10 speaks of the other spouse's or parent's "financial resources", not of who is in the household. The order is read as false when not stated.

Type group of persons, scope person, program CCCAP.
Uses: `cccap_has_parent_with_temporary_order`, `cccap_household_members`, `has_temporary_order_for_parental_responsibilities`, `relationships`.

```
all persons in CCCAP: household members such that
  any of the following is true:
    - that person's Separated, with a temporary order for parental responsibilities or custody, otherwise no
    - it is not the case that (any of the following is true:;   - that person is a spouse of a person in all persons in CCCAP: household members such that that person's Separated, with a temporary order for parental responsibilities or custody, otherwise no;   - that person is a parent or stepparent of a person in all persons in CCCAP: household members such that that person's CCCAP: a parent of the child holds a temporary order)
```

### CO-4076 CCCAP: excluded irregular income `@engine`

The person's irregular recurring receipts that CCCAP counts (those cccap_counted_recurring_receipts, CO-5721, holds, marked irregular: "received too infrequently or irregularly to be reasonably anticipated") that 8 CCR 1403-1 3.111.J.28 (S2858) excludes, each because the calendar quarter of its own date (or of the month determined, for a receipt stated without a date) holds less than cccap_irregular_income_quarterly_limit (CO-4075) of irregular income, earned and unearned ("Irregular income in the certification period that totals less than ninety dollars ($90) in any calendar quarter"); otherwise 0.

Precision. The quarter's total is cccap_irregular_receipts_in_quarter (CO-5724) with the irregular earnings of the quarter (cccap_irregular_earnings_in_quarter, CO-6151; earned-income records, step E1, finding E1-C3: J.28 totals "Irregular income", earned and unearned, and before the records CCCAP's wages could not say which pay was irregular); the earnings are read only when the month has irregular receipts to take out. The month read is the month determined, whose receipts stand for the prior thirty days, so a receipt in the thirty days but in the month before is not taken out (OQ-713). J.28's "slight fluctuations in regular monthly income" are left to the stated amounts: a figure that already averages the fluctuation (CO-3914) carries none. Receipt records, migration phase 2 (2026-11-23): read from the receipts marked irregular, through CCCAP's counting table, replacing infrequent_or_irregular_income_received (CO-3822) and the shared quarter total (infrequent_or_irregular_income_in_quarter, CO-4077, which no rule reads now). Coverage pass 4 C4-1 and C4-2 (docs/reviews/coverage4-care-energy.md): rewritten to take out exactly the irregular recurring receipts cccap_counted_recurring_receipts (CO-5721) counts, each by the calendar quarter of its own date: a receipt dated in the thirty days is tested against the quarter the thirty days begin in (cccap_irregular_income_in_first_quarter_of_period, CO-6402) when its month is on or before cccap_prior_income_period_first_quarter_end (CO-6401), else against the quarter they end in (CO-6403); a receipt stated without a date against the quarter of the month determined. It no longer reads cccap_irregular_receipts (CO-5723), which places receipts by month for the quarter totals. Coverage pass 5, C5-1 (docs/reviews/coverage5-care-energy.md): a record stated with neither a month nor a date (a stream) is the pay or payment of the days its source ran (docs/conventions.md, "A record's time"; job_start_date and job_end_date for pay, start_date and end_date for a receipt). It stands for the thirty days only when its source ran through all of them (none of its dates after their first day or before their last); it is not read when its source ended before their first day or began on or after cccap_application_or_redetermination_date; and a source that began or ended inside the thirty days is placed by its dated records, so a stream without them cannot determine and the record's date is named as missing (8 CCR 1403-1 3.111.H.4, H.5.a.1, H.5.b, S2704, S891: the income "received during the prior thirty (30) day period"; OQ-680 (2)). A record stated with its month or its date is placed as before. Coverage pass 5: each irregular receipt is taken out at the value cccap_counted_recurring_receipts (CO-5721) counts it at, the early-payout penalty (C5-2), the share of jointly owned property's income (X5-1) and the proceeds spent on the costs they cover taken into account. Coverage pass 6 for CCCAP, R6-2 (docs/reviews/coverage6-care-energy.md): the share test of 3.111.H.4.e is applied once per property in the household: a record of jointly owned property whose co-owner is another member of the household (the receipt's co_owner, in cccap_household_members, CO-982) counts what the person received, since what the property paid the co-owner is counted on the co-owner's own list and the household's income from the property is what its members received; the share is the floor only against owners outside the household (OQ-1316). Before, each co-owner took the larger of the share and the amount on the own list, so a co-owner who received nothing still added a share the other had received.

### CO-4463 CCCAP: unearned receipts excluded from countable income `@engine`

The part of the person's unearned income for the month that 8 CCR 1403-1 3.111.I-J does not count and that CCCAP's counting table (cccap_receipt_treatment_table) still counts: a landlord's expenses up to the rents (I.12 and I.17 count net rental income); and a state Colorado Works diversion paid over four or more consecutive months, which 3.103.S makes cash assistance and J.26 excludes.

Precision. Receipt records, migration phase 2 (docs/reviews/receipts-migration-2-cccap-sunbucks.md): foster care and kinship care payments (J.10), Social Security set aside under a PASS (J.13), WIA and WIOA training allowances and youth project payments (J.17, J.18), Colorado Works supportive services (J.23) and the Home Care Allowance (J.24) are now rows of the counting table, and are no longer taken out here. Receipt records, migration phase 3: adoption subsidy payments (J.10) and early childhood research study payments (J.29) are receipt kinds of their own, which the counting table excludes, so they are no longer taken out here (they were adoption_subsidy_received, CO-4451, and early_childhood_research_study_payments_received, CO-4453, parts of the other unearned income, both retired). rental_property_expenses_paid (CO-4458) is taken against the month's recurring receipts of rent (rental_income) and the other taxable unearned income (other_taxable) together, no more than they are, since the expenses' meaning covers rents "stated in the person's other unearned income facts" (coverage pass 2 C2-4, probe Z-5). retirement_early_withdrawal_penalty (CO-4459) is no more than the month's recurring pension receipts. A diversion is a cash assistance when tanf_state_diversion_payment_months (CO-4911, read as 0 when not stated) is at least cccap_state_diversion_cash_assistance_months (CO-4912, four), and is then taken out at what it was counted at (a one-time diversion at one twelfth, H.4.i). A shorter state diversion and a county diversion are not cash assistance; 3.111.I neither names nor excludes them, and they are counted (OQ-873). Before the fix every diversion was counted (probe Y-7). cccap_person_unearned_income (CO-3916) subtracts this item. Coverage pass 4 C4-2: the recurring receipts these deductions are taken against are placed as cccap_counted_recurring_receipts (CO-5721) places them, by date in the thirty days when dated, so a deduction is never taken against a receipt that is not counted; a diversion paid once stays in the month received (H.4.i). Coverage pass 4 X4-1: tanf_state_diversion_payment_months is read only for a person whose receipts hold a diversion, and with no default: 3.103.S gives no reading for a diversion whose kind (state or county) or length is not stated (decision 4 of 2026-11-23; before it, read as 0, not cash assistance). rental_property_expenses_paid and retirement_early_withdrawal_penalty keep their reading as 0 when not stated: each is a deduction the client claims, and I.8, I.12 and I.17 count the income less an expense shown, as G.2.a does not consider business expenses that are not verified. Coverage pass 5, C5-1 (docs/reviews/coverage5-care-energy.md): a record stated with neither a month nor a date (a stream) is the pay or payment of the days its source ran (docs/conventions.md, "A record's time"; job_start_date and job_end_date for pay, start_date and end_date for a receipt). It stands for the thirty days only when its source ran through all of them (none of its dates after their first day or before their last); it is not read when its source ended before their first day or began on or after cccap_application_or_redetermination_date; and a source that began or ended inside the thirty days is placed by its dated records, so a stream without them cannot determine and the record's date is named as missing (8 CCR 1403-1 3.111.H.4, H.5.a.1, H.5.b, S2704, S891: the income "received during the prior thirty (30) day period"; OQ-680 (2)). A record stated with its month or its date is placed as before. Coverage pass 5, C5-2 (docs/reviews/coverage5-care-energy.md): the penalty deducted from an early payout (I.8) is no longer taken here: it is the payment's own field (early_withdrawal_penalty, CO-5000), taken off by cccap_counted_recurring_receipts (CO-5721) and cccap_one_time_receipts_averaged (CO-5722) for a pension or a retirement account's distribution, recurring or paid once; retirement_early_withdrawal_penalty (CO-4459) has no reader now and waits for the final cleanup, and the sentences above about it describe the reading before. X5-1: the rents the expenses are taken against are each rent's counted value, the owner's share of jointly owned property's rent when it is more than what the owner received. Coverage pass 6 for CCCAP, R6-2 (docs/reviews/coverage6-care-energy.md): the share test of 3.111.H.4.e is applied once per property in the household: a record of jointly owned property whose co-owner is another member of the household (the receipt's co_owner, in cccap_household_members, CO-982) counts what the person received, since what the property paid the co-owner is counted on the co-owner's own list and the household's income from the property is what its members received; the share is the floor only against owners outside the household (OQ-1316). Before, each co-owner took the larger of the share and the amount on the own list, so a co-owner who received nothing still added a share the other had received. Coverage pass 6 for CCCAP, R6-4: the rents the expenses are taken against include the receipts of rental property managed under an average of twenty hours a week and stated as a business (cccap_rental_property_receipts_as_unearned, CO-7251), which 3.111.H.4.e makes unearned income. KL-CE-1 (coverage pass 7, R7-3; docs/reviews/known-limits.md, 2026-11-24): rental_property_expenses_paid (CO-4458) is taken against the rent receipts only (rental_income, other_taxable), the expenses of rental property that is not a business, and no longer against a rental business's rents; those rents (CO-7251) are net of the business's own cost records (cccap_rental_property_costs, CO-7910), no more than the rents are. One rental property is so stated once for CCCAP and LEAP: its rents as a business's receipts record, its costs as that business's cost records naming it (job). Probe CR2 (the costs as a cost record of the rental: $3,400, ineligible_income, where the rule gives $3,100, eligible_low_income) and stored households CO-1082, CO-1190 give the rule's answer; a household that stated a rental business's costs as rental_property_expenses_paid (CO-1082 before) states them as the business's cost records.

### CO-4464 CCCAP: other countable receipts `@engine`

Receipts 8 CCR 1403-1 3.111.I counts that are not in the wages, self-employment or recurring unearned income CCCAP otherwise reads: in-kind compensation for employment at its cost or fair market value (I.4, "counted as other income"); vendor payments that are part of the compensation for employment (I.5); and receipts from boarders or lodgers (I.18): the earnings records (earnings, CO-5100) of those kinds (cccap_earnings_treatment_table, CO-5105: counted_at_value, counted_other_income) received in the prior thirty days, without the irregular ones J.28 excludes when the quarter's irregular income is under ninety dollars. GI Bill subsistence allowances (I.7.c) are already in the unearned income CCCAP reads and are not added here.

Precision. Earned-income records, step E1 (CCCAP): read from the earnings records, replacing in_kind_compensation_value (CO-4506), employer_vendor_payments_received (CO-4455) and room_and_board_payments_received (CO-4161), each read as 0 when not stated: an unstated earnings list is cannot determine and a stated empty list is none (decision 4 of 2026-11-23). Boarders' payments for a room only or meals only, which the receipts held (board_only_payment, room_only_payment; cccap_receipt_treatment_table, CO-5720, counted them under I.18), are boarder_payments records here, and their receipt rows read counted_in_earnings, so a payment the transition states in both lists is counted once. The places and the thirty days are those of cccap_person_earned_income (CO-3915): a record with a date in the cccap_prior_income_period_days (CO-5151) days before cccap_application_or_redetermination_date (CO-5150), else the record's month (OQ-680); J.28 as there (finding E1-C3). I.4 says an in-kind benefit is "counted as other income", so these are not earned income for the Colorado Works Child Care fee (3.116.C, CO-2578) or the minimum-wage test. cccap_person_unearned_income (CO-3916) adds this item. The gross receipts from boarders are counted: I.18 names "Receipts from boarders or lodgers" and no paragraph deducts the cost of the room or meals (business_cost_boarder_provision is not deducted, a row for the owner's signature). Coverage pass 3 C3-4 and C3-5: in-kind pay is one statement (CO-4506 retired CO-4454 into it), and the GI Bill living allowance is a receipt of kind gi_bill_housing_food_allowance, counted under I.7.c by cccap_receipt_treatment_table, so this item does not add it. Coverage pass 4 C4-1: an irregular record is tested under J.28 against the calendar quarter of its own date, or of the month determined when it states none, as cccap_person_earned_income (CO-3915) tests irregular pay (CO-6401 to CO-6403; OQ-713). Coverage pass 5, C5-1 (docs/reviews/coverage5-care-energy.md): a record stated with neither a month nor a date (a stream) is the pay or payment of the days its source ran (docs/conventions.md, "A record's time"; job_start_date and job_end_date for pay, start_date and end_date for a receipt). It stands for the thirty days only when its source ran through all of them (none of its dates after their first day or before their last); it is not read when its source ended before their first day or began on or after cccap_application_or_redetermination_date; and a source that began or ended inside the thirty days is placed by its dated records, so a stream without them cannot determine and the record's date is named as missing (8 CCR 1403-1 3.111.H.4, H.5.a.1, H.5.b, S2704, S891: the income "received during the prior thirty (30) day period"; OQ-680 (2)). A record stated with its month or its date is placed as before. Coverage pass 5, C5-3 (docs/reviews/coverage5-care-energy.md): a household child who is not a teen parent has no in-kind pay and no employer's vendor payment counted: J.1 (S486) excludes "Earnings of a child in the household when not a teen parent", and I.4-5 (S3255) count in-kind benefits and vendor payments as compensation for employment of "the adult caretaker(s) or teen parent(s)", so they are the child's earnings, read as cccap_person_earned_income (CO-3915) reads the child's pay. Receipts from boarders or lodgers (I.18) are listed beside rents and royalties, not as anyone's earnings, and are counted for a child as for anyone; the child's status is read only when the person has in-kind or vendor pay counted.

Type money, scope person-month, program CCCAP.
