### CO-4467 CCCAP: incapacity verification is pending `@engine`

Whether CCCAP still needs the physician's statement or other medical verification of this adult caretaker's or teen parent's incapacity (8 CCR 1403-1 3.111.C.2.g, D.1.c.3, D.9): the caretaker is stated to be incapacitated, CCCAP verification applies to the person, and the verification has not been received.

Precision. Incapacity is cccap_caretaker_is_incapacitated (CO-1744) and the document incapacity_verification_document_received (CO-4466), each read as false when not stated. Counted as an eligibility element by cccap_person_pending_verification_count (CO-1448), due by cccap_verification_due_date (CO-1450); while it is pending the household's status reads the stated incapacity and cccap_verification_status (CO-1451) reports pending, then past_due or case_closed.

Type yes/no, scope person-month, program CCCAP.
Uses: `cccap_caretaker_is_incapacitated`, `cccap_is_adult_caretaker`, `cccap_is_teen_parent`, `cccap_verification_is_applicable`, `incapacity_verification_document_received`.

```
all of the following are true:
  - CCCAP: verification applies to this person
  - any of the following is true:
    - CCCAP: is an adult caretaker
    - CCCAP: is a teen parent
  - CCCAP: caretaker is incapacitated, otherwise no
  - it is not the case that Incapacity verification document received, otherwise no
```

["all","cccap_verification_is_applicable",["any","cccap_is_adult_caretaker","cccap_is_teen_parent"],["otherwise","cccap_caretaker_is_incapacitated",false],["not",["otherwise","incapacity_verification_document_received",false]]]
```

### CO-5152 CCCAP: a person's gross wages `@engine`

The gross wages the person received for employment as an employee (8 CCR 1403-1 3.111.I.1, S486: "Gross earnings, salary, armed forces pay ... commissions, tips, and cash bonuses are counted before deductions") in the prior thirty days (3.111.H.4-5): the earnings records (earnings, CO-5100) of pay for work as an employee, every kind CCCAP's counting table (cccap_earnings_treatment_table, CO-5105) counts as wages or excludes as wages (work-study, J.16), not self-employment, in-kind pay, an employer's vendor payments or boarders. It is the wage I.1 and G.1.b divide by the hours worked (cccap_caretaker_in_eligible_activity, CO-984), and whether a caretaker has paid employment (cccap_parent_fee, CO-1290).

Precision. Earned-income records, step E1 (CCCAP; docs/reviews/records-earnings-care-energy.md): replaces wages_gross (CO-023) for the minimum-wage test and the Colorado Works fee test, which read every part of the wages, work-study included; the countable wages are cccap_person_earned_income (CO-3915), which leaves work-study out (J.16). A pay stated with its date is read when its date is in the cccap_prior_income_period_days (CO-5151) days before cccap_application_or_redetermination_date (CO-5150), the day before that date included and the date itself not (OQ-680); a pay stated by its month, or as a stream with no date, is read for the month determined, standing for the thirty days as CCCAP's receipts do (cccap_counted_recurring_receipts, CO-5721; OQ-680). Coverage pass 4 C4-4: a pay that states annual_contract_pay is read at one twelfth of the contract (cccap_annual_contract_months, CO-6406) in each month, in place of its amount (H.4.b, S2704: "the income shall be prorated over the term of the contract"; OQ-1221), so the minimum-wage test divides the prorated pay too. Coverage pass 5, C5-1 (docs/reviews/coverage5-care-energy.md): a record stated with neither a month nor a date (a stream) is the pay or payment of the days its source ran (docs/conventions.md, "A record's time"; job_start_date and job_end_date for pay, start_date and end_date for a receipt). It stands for the thirty days only when its source ran through all of them (none of its dates after their first day or before their last); it is not read when its source ended before their first day or began on or after cccap_application_or_redetermination_date; and a source that began or ended inside the thirty days is placed by its dated records, so a stream without them cannot determine and the record's date is named as missing (8 CCR 1403-1 3.111.H.4, H.5.a.1, H.5.b, S2704, S891: the income "received during the prior thirty (30) day period"; OQ-680 (2)). A record stated with its month or its date is placed as before.

Type money, scope person-month, program CCCAP.
Uses: `cccap_annual_contract_months`, `cccap_application_or_redetermination_date`, `cccap_earnings_treatment_table`, `cccap_prior_income_period_days`, `earnings`.

```
(the sum of that receipt's amount for each receipt in Earnings where ((all of the following are true:;   - CCCAP: how each kind of earnings is treated (table), for that receipt's kind is one of: counted, counted_no_rule_excludes, excluded, counted_unless_foster_care;   - CCCAP: how each kind of earnings is treated (table), for that receipt's kind is one of: counted, counted_no_rule_excludes, excluded, counted_unless_foster_care;   - it is not the case that that receipt's annual contract pay is unknown; ### CO-5156 CCCAP: a person's self-employment gross receipts in a month `@engine`

The gross receipts of the person's self-employment in the month: the earnings records (earnings, CO-5100) of a business's or a farm's gross receipts, which CCCAP counts as self-employment (cccap_earnings_treatment_table, CO-5105: counted_self_employment; 8 CCR 1403-1 3.111.I.2 "declared gross income", I.3 "gross receipts" of a farm), received in the month.

Precision. Earned-income records, step E1 (CCCAP): replaces self_employment_gross_receipts (CO-1700) for CCCAP. The month is the month determined, the prorated monthly figure H.4.c reads as received in the prior thirty days; the receipts are not placed by date. The value of farm products the family used is not a receipt (I.3.c). Read by cccap_self_employment_net_earnings (CO-1710), cccap_has_earned_income (CO-5153) and the self-employed caretaker's activity schedule (cccap_requires_verification_of_activity_schedule, CO-5154). Coverage pass 5, C5-1 (docs/reviews/coverage5-care-energy.md): a record stated with neither a month nor a date (a stream) is the pay or payment of the days its source ran (docs/conventions.md, "A record's time"; job_start_date and job_end_date for pay, start_date and end_date for a receipt). It stands for the thirty days only when its source ran through all of them (none of its dates after their first day or before their last); it is not read when its source ended before their first day or began on or after cccap_application_or_redetermination_date; and a source that began or ended inside the thirty days is placed by its dated records, so a stream without them cannot determine and the record's date is named as missing (8 CCR 1403-1 3.111.H.4, H.5.a.1, H.5.b, S2704, S891: the income "received during the prior thirty (30) day period"; OQ-680 (2)). A record stated with its month or its date is placed as before. Coverage pass 6 for CCCAP, R6-4 (docs/reviews/coverage6-care-energy.md): a business's receipts record (self_employment_receipts) that is rental property (the record's rental_property) when the caretaker's business hours in the month (cccap_rental_property_management_hours, CO-7254) average under cccap_rental_property_self_employment_min_hours_per_week (CO-7252, twenty) a week (the hours divided by the month's days over seven; OQ-1366) is not self-employment: 3.111.H.4.e (S2704), "Income from rental property will be considered as unearned income if the adult caretaker(s) or teen parent(s) are not actively managing the property an average of at least twenty (20) hours per week"; its receipts are unearned rent (cccap_rental_property_receipts_as_unearned, CO-7251) and its hours are not hours of an eligible activity. The record's rental_property is read only when those hours are under the line (required there: decision 4). Coverage pass 7, R7-1 (docs/reviews/coverage7-care-energy.md): the twenty hours are the hours the caretaker manages the rental property (cccap_rental_property_management_hours, CO-7254, the hours of the records whose rental_property is true), not the hours of every business: 3.111.H.4.e (S2704) asks whether the caretaker actively manages "the property" twenty hours a week, and no reading makes another business's hours management of it. The record's rental_property is read first, so it is required on every business receipts record CCCAP reads (decision 4). Before, a landlord who managed her rental five hours a week and ran a cleaning business thirty was read as actively managing the property (probe CR3: ineligible_income where the rule gives eligible_low_income). Coverage verification 7, V7-7 (docs/reviews/verify-coverage7-fixes.md): the review proposed testing a record's own hours before its rental_property, so a lone business of twenty hours a week or more would be self-employment with the flag unstated (C1-F). Done so, the same business stated as two records of half the hours each (the records harness's split relation, ME-1) was cannot determine while the single record answered, since two records with the flag unstated cannot be told from two businesses of which one may be a rental under twenty hours: the answer would turn on how the case divides one business into records. The flag therefore stays required on every business receipts record CCCAP reads (decision 4), the field's meaning now says so (CO-5100), and C1-F stays cannot determine (stored household CO-1167).

Type money, scope person-month, program CCCAP.
Uses: `cccap_application_or_redetermination_date`, `cccap_earnings_treatment_table`, `cccap_prior_income_period_days`, `cccap_rental_property_management_hours`, `cccap_rental_property_self_employment_min_hours_per_week`, `earnings`.

### CO-5721 CCCAP: a person's counted recurring receipts `@engine`

The person's recurring receipts of the month that CCCAP's counting table counts (cccap_receipt_treatment_table), at the amount received in the month: the unearned income received in the prior thirty days (8 CCR 1403-1 3.111.H.4, H.5.b), Social Security included (I.25) less the part set aside under a plan for self-support (J.13).

Precision. A receipt is recurring when it is not paid once; it is received in the month when it states the month, or states none (it recurs in every month). The month's receipts stand for the prior thirty days, as the volume reads a case that states calendar-month receipts (OQ-680). A Colorado Works diversion is counted here and taken out again by cccap_excluded_unearned_receipts when it is cash assistance (3.103.S, J.26). An irregular receipt is counted here and taken out by cccap_excluded_irregular_income when J.28's quarterly limit is not reached. The set-aside part is no more than the receipt it is part of. Replaces unearned_income_prior_thirty_days (CO-3913, with the thirty-day figure unearned_income_received_prior_thirty_days, CO-3911, which the receipts do not restate) and the month's social_security_income for CCCAP. Coverage pass 4 C4-2: a recurring receipt stated with its date is read when its date is in the cccap_prior_income_period_days (CO-5151) days before cccap_application_or_redetermination_date (CO-5150), as a dated pay is (cccap_person_earned_income, CO-3915), not by its month: H.5.b counts "Unearned income received during the prior thirty (30) day period" (S2704; OQ-680), so a receipt first paid after the date is not counted and one paid in the thirty days but the month before is. A receipt stated without a date (a stream, or a month) stands for the thirty days as before. Coverage pass 5, C5-1 (docs/reviews/coverage5-care-energy.md): a record stated with neither a month nor a date (a stream) is the pay or payment of the days its source ran (docs/conventions.md, "A record's time"; job_start_date and job_end_date for pay, start_date and end_date for a receipt). It stands for the thirty days only when its source ran through all of them (none of its dates after their first day or before their last); it is not read when its source ended before their first day or began on or after cccap_application_or_redetermination_date; and a source that began or ended inside the thirty days is placed by its dated records, so a stream without them cannot determine and the record's date is named as missing (8 CCR 1403-1 3.111.H.4, H.5.a.1, H.5.b, S2704, S891: the income "received during the prior thirty (30) day period"; OQ-680 (2)). A record stated with its month or its date is placed as before. Coverage pass 5 (docs/reviews/coverage5-care-energy.md; docs/reviews/field-sweep-care-energy.md): C5-2, a payment from a pension, an annuity or a retirement account is counted less the amount deducted for penalties for an early payout, the record's early_withdrawal_penalty (receipts, CO-5000), whatever its kind (pension or savings_account_distribution) and whether recurring or paid once (8 CCR 1403-1 3.111.I.8, S3256: "minus the amount deducted for penalties, if early payouts are received from these accounts"); it replaces retirement_early_withdrawal_penalty (CO-4459), a person-month figure that could not say which payment it belonged to and was taken only from recurring pension receipts. X5-1, income from property the person owns jointly with others (a record stating ownership_share and property_income) is counted at the larger of the owner's share of the property's income and the amount received (H.4.e, S2704: "as a percentage at least equal to the percentage of ownership or, if receiving more than percentage of ownership, the actual amount received"; OQ-1316). Field sweep: insurance or injury proceeds paid as a recurring receipt are counted less the part spent or to be spent on the costs they cover (spent_on_covered_costs; I.21-22, S3256), as a one-time payment already was. None below zero. cccap_excluded_irregular_income (CO-4076) and cccap_irregular_receipts (CO-5723) read the same value. C5-3: AmeriCorps income is earned (I.32) and is read by cccap_person_earned_income (CO-3915), not here. Coverage pass 6 for CCCAP, R6-2 (docs/reviews/coverage6-care-energy.md): the share test of 3.111.H.4.e is applied once per property in the household: a record of jointly owned property whose co-owner is another member of the household (the receipt's co_owner, in cccap_household_members, CO-982) counts what the person received, since what the property paid the co-owner is counted on the co-owner's own list and the household's income from the property is what its members received; the share is the floor only against owners outside the household (OQ-1316). Before, each co-owner took the larger of the share and the amount on the own list, so a co-owner who received nothing still added a share the other had received.

Type money, scope person-month, program CCCAP.
Uses: `cccap_application_or_redetermination_date`, `cccap_household_members`, `cccap_prior_income_period_days`, `cccap_receipt_treatment_table`, `receipts`.

```
the sum for each receipt in Receipts where
    all of the following are true:
      - CCCAP: how each kind of receipt is treated (table), for that receipt's kind is one of: counted, counted_no_rule_excludes, counted_less_pass_set_aside, counted_child_support, counted_unless_cash_assistance
      - it is not the case that that receipt's frequency is equal to once
      - if it is not the case that that receipt's month is unknown
        then (if that receipt's date is unknown;   then that receipt is received in the month; otherwise (all of the following are true:;   - that receipt's date is at least 0 minus CCCAP: the days before the application or redetermination whose income is read (30) days after CCCAP application or redetermination date;   - that receipt's date is less than CCCAP application or redetermination date))
      else if any of the following is true:
          - all of the following are true:
            - it is not the case that that receipt's end date is unknown
            - that receipt's end date is less than 0 minus CCCAP: the days before the application or redetermination whose income is read (30) days after CCCAP application or redetermination date
          - all of the following are true:
            - it is not the case that that receipt's start date is unknown
            - that receipt's start date is at least CCCAP application or redetermination date
        then no
      else if all of the following are true:
          - any of the following is true:
            - that receipt's start date is unknown
            - that receipt's start date is at most 0 minus CCCAP: the days before the application or redetermination whose income is read (30) days after CCCAP application or redetermination date
          - any of the following is true:
            - that receipt's end date is unknown
            - that receipt's end date is at least -1 days after CCCAP application or redetermination date
        then (if that receipt's date is unknown;   then that receipt is received in the month; otherwise (all of the following are true:;   - that receipt's date is at least 0 minus CCCAP: the days before the application or redetermination whose income is read (30) days after CCCAP application or redetermination date;   - that receipt's date is less than CCCAP application or redetermination date))
      otherwise (all of the following are true:;   - that receipt's date is at least 0 minus CCCAP: the days before the application or redetermination whose income is read (30) days after CCCAP application or redetermination date;   - that receipt's date is less than CCCAP application or redetermination date)
  of
    if CCCAP: how each kind of receipt is treated (table), for that receipt's kind is equal to counted_less_pass_set_aside
      then that receipt's amount minus (the lesser of that receipt's pass set aside and that receipt's amount)
    otherwise the greater of 0 and ((if that receipt's ownership share is unknown;   then that receipt's amount; else if all of the following are true:;     - it is not the case that that receipt's co owner is unknown;     - that receipt's co owner is in that receipt's owner's CCCAP: household members;   then that receipt's amount; otherwise the greater of that receipt's amount and (that receipt's ownership share times that receipt's property income)) minus (that receipt's spent on covered costs plus that receipt's early withdrawal penalty))

### CO-5722 CCCAP: a person's one-time receipts, averaged `@engine`

One twelfth (cccap_lump_sum_averaging_months) of the person's receipts paid once in the month that CCCAP's counting table counts, whatever their kind: a non-recurring lump sum is "included as income in the month received or averaged over a twelve (12) month period, whichever is most beneficial for the recipient" (8 CCR 1403-1 3.111.H.4.i, "including lump sum child support payments"); an inheritance, a gift or a prize (I.20) among them. Each is less the part of life insurance, health insurance or personal injury proceeds spent or to be spent on the last illness and burial or on medical care (I.21-22) and, for Social Security, the part set aside under a plan for self-support (J.13).

Precision. Receipt records, migration phase 2: a receipt paid once is one whose frequency is once, so 3.111.H.4.i reaches every non-recurring payment, however the case would have named it (OQ-873's second question: before receipt records only a payment stated as lump_sum_received, CO-3367, or as lottery winnings was averaged, and a one-time payment stated in another unearned income fact was counted in full in its month). One twelfth is always the more beneficial count in the month received, and a receipt paid once in an earlier month is not counted (counting it in its own month is then the more beneficial), OQ-680. A retroactive Social Security lump sum is counted here (I.25); a retroactive SSI or Colorado Works or Adult Financial lump sum is excluded by its kind (J.2, J.26). A receipt of a kind the table excludes is never asked for its month. Coverage pass 5 (docs/reviews/coverage5-care-energy.md; docs/reviews/field-sweep-care-energy.md): C5-2, a payment from a pension, an annuity or a retirement account is counted less the amount deducted for penalties for an early payout, the record's early_withdrawal_penalty (receipts, CO-5000), whatever its kind (pension or savings_account_distribution) and whether recurring or paid once (8 CCR 1403-1 3.111.I.8, S3256: "minus the amount deducted for penalties, if early payouts are received from these accounts"); it replaces retirement_early_withdrawal_penalty (CO-4459), a person-month figure that could not say which payment it belonged to and was taken only from recurring pension receipts. X5-1, income from property the person owns jointly with others (a record stating ownership_share and property_income) is counted at the larger of the owner's share of the property's income and the amount received (H.4.e, S2704: "as a percentage at least equal to the percentage of ownership or, if receiving more than percentage of ownership, the actual amount received"; OQ-1316). None below zero. Review household CP1 (CO-5722-T10): a $12,000 early 401(k) withdrawal paid once with a $1,200 penalty counts (12,000 - 1,200) / 12 = 900. Coverage pass 6 for CCCAP, R6-2 (docs/reviews/coverage6-care-energy.md): the share test of 3.111.H.4.e is applied once per property in the household: a record of jointly owned property whose co-owner is another member of the household (the receipt's co_owner, in cccap_household_members, CO-982) counts what the person received, since what the property paid the co-owner is counted on the co-owner's own list and the household's income from the property is what its members received; the share is the floor only against owners outside the household (OQ-1316). Before, each co-owner took the larger of the share and the amount on the own list, so a co-owner who received nothing still added a share the other had received.

Type money, scope person-month, program CCCAP.
Uses: `cccap_household_members`, `cccap_lump_sum_averaging_months`, `cccap_receipt_treatment_table`, `receipts`.

(the sum of (the greater of 0 and ((if that receipt's ownership share is unknown;   then that receipt's amount; else if all of the following are true:;     - it is not the case that that receipt's co owner is unknown;     - that receipt's co owner is in that receipt's owner's CCCAP: household members;   then that receipt's amount; otherwise the greater of that receipt's amount and (that receipt's ownership share times that receipt's property income)) minus (that receipt's spent on covered costs plus (if CCCAP: how each kind of receipt is treated (table), for that receipt's kind is equal to counted_less_pass_set_aside;   then that receipt's pass set aside; otherwise 0) plus that receipt's early withdrawal penalty))) for each receipt in Receipts where ((all of the following are true:;   - CCCAP: how each kind of receipt is treated (table), for that receipt's kind is one of: counted, counted_no_rule_excludes, counted_less_pass_set_aside, counted_child_support, counted_unless_cash_assistance;   - that receipt's frequency is equal to once;   - that receipt is received in the month))) divided by CCCAP lump sum averaging period, months (12)

### CO-5723 CCCAP: a person's irregular receipts `@engine`

The person's receipts of the month that CCCAP's counting table counts and that were received infrequently or irregularly ("received too infrequently or irregularly to be reasonably anticipated", 8 CCR 1403-1 3.111.J.28), at the amount counted in the month: the receipts J.28's exclusion reads.

Precision. A receipt is irregular when its record says so (irregular). A receipt paid once is a non-recurring lump sum, counted at one twelfth under 3.111.H.4.i (cccap_one_time_receipts_averaged), and is not read here; the recurring receipts are counted at their amount (cccap_counted_recurring_receipts), and this is the irregular part of them. Replaces infrequent_or_irregular_income_received (CO-3822) for CCCAP. Coverage pass 4 C4-1 and C4-2: this item now holds the month's irregular receipts by the month of each record only, the figure cccap_irregular_receipts_in_quarter (CO-5724) adds over a calendar quarter; which irregular receipts of the thirty days J.28 excludes is cccap_excluded_irregular_income (CO-4076). Coverage pass 5, C5-1 (docs/reviews/coverage5-care-energy.md): a stream (a record with neither a month nor a date) is placed only in the months its source ran, from the month of its job_start_date (start_date for a receipt) through the month of its job_end_date (end_date), as SNAP (CO-5011) and the cash programs place one (docs/conventions.md, "A record's time"). Coverage pass 5: each receipt at the value cccap_counted_recurring_receipts (CO-5721) counts it at (C5-2, X5-1). Coverage pass 6 for CCCAP, R6-2 (docs/reviews/coverage6-care-energy.md): the share test of 3.111.H.4.e is applied once per property in the household: a record of jointly owned property whose co-owner is another member of the household (the receipt's co_owner, in cccap_household_members, CO-982) counts what the person received, since what the property paid the co-owner is counted on the co-owner's own list and the household's income from the property is what its members received; the share is the floor only against owners outside the household (OQ-1316). Before, each co-owner took the larger of the share and the amount on the own list, so a co-owner who received nothing still added a share the other had received.

Type money, scope person-month, program CCCAP.
Uses: `cccap_household_members`, `cccap_receipt_treatment_table`, `receipts`.

```
the sum for each receipt in Receipts where

      - CCCAP: how each kind of receipt is treated (table), for that receipt's kind is one of: counted, counted_no_rule_excludes, counted_less_pass_set_aside, counted_child_support, counted_unless_cash_assistance

### CO-5725 CCCAP: a person's counted child support `@engine`

The child support the person's countable unearned income holds for the month (8 CCR 1403-1 3.111.I.29), as it is counted there: current support and arrears received in the month at their amount, a lump-sum child support payment received in the month at one twelfth (H.4.i). The amount a protective services household does not count (3.119.A: "Child support income shall not be included as income").

Precision. Reads the receipts of the kinds the counting table treats as child support (counted_child_support: child_support and child_support_arrears). Replaces child_support_received (CO-028, which held arrears as a part) for cccap_protective_services_income (CO-994) and cccap_has_countable_unearned_income (CO-2873). Coverage pass 4 C4-2: a recurring child support receipt stated with its date is placed in the thirty days, as cccap_counted_recurring_receipts (CO-5721) places it, so this figure is the child support the unearned income holds; a lump sum paid once stays in the month received (H.4.i). Coverage pass 5, C5-1 (docs/reviews/coverage5-care-energy.md): a record stated with neither a month nor a date (a stream) is the pay or payment of the days its source ran (docs/conventions.md, "A record's time"; job_start_date and job_end_date for pay, start_date and end_date for a receipt). It stands for the thirty days only when its source ran through all of them (none of its dates after their first day or before their last); it is not read when its source ended before their first day or began on or after cccap_application_or_redetermination_date; and a source that began or ended inside the thirty days is placed by its dated records, so a stream without them cannot determine and the record's date is named as missing (8 CCR 1403-1 3.111.H.4, H.5.a.1, H.5.b, S2704, S891: the income "received during the prior thirty (30) day period"; OQ-680 (2)). A record stated with its month or its date is placed as before.

The person's irregular income that CCCAP counts, earned and unearned (cccap_irregular_receipts_in_quarter, CO-5724, and cccap_irregular_earnings_in_quarter, CO-6151), over the calendar quarter that contains the first of the thirty days before the application or redetermination date: the total 8 CCR 1403-1 3.111.J.28 (S2858) compares with ninety dollars for an irregular pay or receipt dated in that quarter ("Irregular income in the certification period that totals less than ninety dollars ($90) in any calendar quarter").

Precision. Each quarter total is read in the month containing the first of the thirty days, so it is the total of that month's quarter, every irregular record placed by its own month or date. Read by cccap_person_earned_income (CO-3915), cccap_other_countable_receipts (CO-4464) and cccap_excluded_irregular_income (CO-4076) only for an irregular record dated in that quarter (coverage pass 4 C4-1; OQ-713).

Type money, scope person-month, program CCCAP.
Uses: `cccap_application_or_redetermination_date`, `cccap_irregular_earnings_in_quarter`, `cccap_irregular_receipts_in_quarter`, `cccap_prior_income_period_days`.

CCCAP: a person's irregular receipts in the calendar quarter plus CCCAP: a person's irregular earnings in the calendar quarter for the month containing 0 minus CCCAP: the days before the application or redetermination whose income is read (30) days after CCCAP application or redetermination date
```

### CO-6403 CCCAP: irregular income of the calendar quarter in which the prior thirty days end `@engine`

The person's irregular income that CCCAP counts, earned and unearned (cccap_irregular_receipts_in_quarter, CO-5724, and cccap_irregular_earnings_in_quarter, CO-6151), over the calendar quarter that contains the last of the thirty days before the application or redetermination date (the day before that date): the total 8 CCR 1403-1 3.111.J.28 (S2858) compares with ninety dollars for an irregular pay or receipt dated in the thirty days after the end of the quarter they begin in.

Precision. Read in the month containing the day before the application or redetermination date. ### CO-6404 CCCAP: hours of self-employment in the month `@engine`

The hours the person worked in self-employment in the month, as each self-employment record of the month states them (earnings, CO-5100, the field hours, of the kinds cccap_earnings_treatment_table counts as self-employment): the "number of hours worked" of 8 CCR 1403-1 3.111.G.2.d and the "number of declared hours worked" of G.2.e (S4602).

Precision. A business record of the month that states no hours is cannot determine, naming the record's hours (decision 4 of 2026-11-23). A person with no self-employment record has none. Read by cccap_self_employment_net_earnings (CO-1710), which projects the launch period's income from them, and by cccap_caretaker_in_eligible_activity (CO-984), which tests employment and self-employment each over its own hours (coverage pass 4 C4-3). Coverage pass 5, C5-1 (docs/reviews/coverage5-care-energy.md): a record stated with neither a month nor a date (a stream) is the pay or payment of the days its source ran (docs/conventions.md, "A record's time"; job_start_date and job_end_date for pay, start_date and end_date for a receipt). It stands for the thirty days only when its source ran through all of them (none of its dates after their first day or before their last); it is not read when its source ended before their first day or began on or after cccap_application_or_redetermination_date; and a source that began or ended inside the thirty days is placed by its dated records, so a stream without them cannot determine and the record's date is named as missing (8 CCR 1403-1 3.111.H.4, H.5.a.1, H.5.b, S2704, S891: the income "received during the prior thirty (30) day period"; OQ-680 (2)). A record stated with its month or its date is placed as before. Coverage pass 6 for CCCAP, R6-4 (docs/reviews/coverage6-care-energy.md): a business's receipts record (self_employment_receipts) that is rental property (the record's rental_property) when the caretaker's business hours in the month (cccap_rental_property_management_hours, CO-7254) average under cccap_rental_property_self_employment_min_hours_per_week (CO-7252, twenty) a week (the hours divided by the month's days over seven; OQ-1366) is not self-employment: 3.111.H.4.e (S2704), "Income from rental property will be considered as unearned income if the adult caretaker(s) or teen parent(s) are not actively managing the property an average of at least twenty (20) hours per week"; its receipts are unearned rent (cccap_rental_property_receipts_as_unearned, CO-7251) and its hours are not hours of an eligible activity. The record's rental_property is read only when those hours are under the line (required there: decision 4). Coverage pass 7, R7-1 (docs/reviews/coverage7-care-energy.md): the twenty hours are the hours the caretaker manages the rental property (cccap_rental_property_management_hours, CO-7254, the hours of the records whose rental_property is true), not the hours of every business: 3.111.H.4.e (S2704) asks whether the caretaker actively manages "the property" twenty hours a week, and no reading makes another business's hours management of it. The record's rental_property is read first, so it is required on every business receipts record CCCAP reads (decision 4). Before, a landlord who managed her rental five hours a week and ran a cleaning business thirty was read as actively managing the property (probe CR3: ineligible_income where the rule gives eligible_low_income). Coverage verification 7, V7-7 (docs/reviews/verify-coverage7-fixes.md): the review proposed testing a record's own hours before its rental_property, so a lone business of twenty hours a week or more would be self-employment with the flag unstated (C1-F). Done so, the same business stated as two records of half the hours each (the records harness's split relation, ME-1) was cannot determine while the single record answered, since two records with the flag unstated cannot be told from two businesses of which one may be a rental under twenty hours: the answer would turn on how the case divides one business into records. The flag therefore stays required on every business receipts record CCCAP reads (decision 4), the field's meaning now says so (CO-5100), and C1-F stays cannot determine (stored household CO-1167).

Type hours, scope person-month, program CCCAP.
Uses: `cccap_application_or_redetermination_date`, `cccap_earnings_treatment_table`, `cccap_prior_income_period_days`, `cccap_rental_property_management_hours`, `cccap_rental_property_self_employment_min_hours_per_week`, `earnings`.

the sum for each receipt in Earnings where
    all of the following are true:
      - CCCAP: how each kind of earnings is treated (table), for that receipt's kind is equal to counted_self_employment
      - it is not the case that (all of the following are true:;   - that receipt's kind is equal to self_employment_receipts;   - that receipt's rental property;   - (that receipt's owner's CCCAP: hours in the month managing rental property stated as a business divided by ((the number of days from the first day of the month to the first day of the month after the month) divided by 7)) is less than CCCAP: hours a week of active management that make rental property self-employment (20))

### CO-7251 CCCAP: rental property receipts that are unearned income `@engine`

The receipts, in the month, of the person's rental property stated as a business (earnings, CO-5100: a self_employment_receipts record whose rental_property is true) that the person does not actively manage an average of at least cccap_rental_property_self_employment_min_hours_per_week (CO-7252, twenty) hours a week: 8 CCR 1403-1 3.111.H.4.e (S2704), "Income from rental property will be considered as unearned income if the adult caretaker(s) or teen parent(s) are not actively managing the property an average of at least twenty (20) hours per week". CCCAP counts it as unearned rent (cccap_person_unearned_income, CO-3916), net of the landlord's expenses (I.12 and I.17, "Net rental income"; cccap_excluded_unearned_receipts, CO-4463), not as self-employment (cccap_self_employment_gross_receipts CO-5156, cccap_self_employment_hours CO-6404).

Precision. Coverage pass 6 for CCCAP, R6-4 (docs/reviews/coverage6-care-energy.md). The average is the caretaker's hours in the month in the businesses stated as receipts records (cccap_rental_property_management_hours, CO-7254) divided by the month's days over seven, the weeks in the month (OQ-1366): the hours are read together, so the same business stated in one record or in two gives one answer. The record is placed in the month as cccap_self_employment_gross_receipts (CO-5156) places a business's receipts (the thirty days before the application or redetermination date, or the month). The property's costs were stated as rental_property_expenses_paid (CO-4458), which CO-4463 took against the rents, this figure included, and a business cost record was a cost of a business CCCAP counts as self-employment; since KL-CE-1 (2026-11-24; docs/reviews/known-limits.md) they are the business's own cost records, each naming the business (job), which cccap_rental_property_costs (CO-7910) gathers and CO-4463 takes against these rents, no more than they are, and rental_property_expenses_paid states only the expenses of rental property that is not a business (rental_income receipts). The record's rental_property is read only when the hours are under the line (decision 4: required there); at twenty hours a week or more the business is self-employment whether or not it is rental property. Coverage pass 7, R7-1 (docs/reviews/coverage7-care-energy.md): the twenty hours are the hours the caretaker manages the rental property (cccap_rental_property_management_hours, CO-7254, the hours of the records whose rental_property is true), not the hours of every business: 3.111.H.4.e (S2704) asks whether the caretaker actively manages "the property" twenty hours a week, and no reading makes another business's hours management of it. The record's rental_property is read first, so it is required on every business receipts record CCCAP reads (decision 4). Before, a landlord who managed her rental five hours a week and ran a cleaning business thirty was read as actively managing the property (probe CR3: ineligible_income where the rule gives eligible_low_income). Coverage verification 7, V7-7 (docs/reviews/verify-coverage7-fixes.md): the review proposed testing a record's own hours before its rental_property, so a lone business of twenty hours a week or more would be self-employment with the flag unstated (C1-F). Done so, the same business stated as two records of half the hours each (the records harness's split relation, ME-1) was cannot determine while the single record answered, since two records with the flag unstated cannot be told from two businesses of which one may be a rental under twenty hours: the answer would turn on how the case divides one business into records. The flag therefore stays required on every business receipts record CCCAP reads (decision 4), the field's meaning now says so (CO-5100), and C1-F stays cannot determine (stored household CO-1167).

### CO-7254 CCCAP: hours in the month managing rental property stated as a business `@engine`

The hours the person spent in the month managing the rental property the person rents out as a business (earnings, CO-5100: self_employment_receipts records whose rental_property is true, their hours), placed in the month as cccap_self_employment_gross_receipts (CO-5156) places the receipts: the hours 8 CCR 1403-1 3.111.H.4.e's twenty-hour average of active management of rental property is taken over (cccap_rental_property_receipts_as_unearned, CO-7251).

Precision. Coverage pass 6 for CCCAP, R6-4, and coverage pass 7, R7-1 (docs/reviews/coverage6-care-energy.md, coverage7-care-energy.md). Only the records of rental property are read (rental_property true, required on every business receipts record: decision 4): 3.111.H.4.e (S2704) asks whether the caretaker actively manages "the property" twenty hours a week, so another business's hours are not management of it. The hours of every rental record are read together, so the same property stated in one record or split over two gives one answer (the records harness's split relation); two rental properties are read together (OQ-1366 records the other reading, property by property). Unknown when a rental record's hours are unstated (decision 4). Before pass 7 the hours of every business stated as receipts were summed (the identifier was cccap_business_receipts_hours), so a cleaning business's hours made a small rental self-employment (probe CR3).

### CO-7680 CCCAP: hours managing rental property that is not self-employment `@engine`

The hours the person spent in the month managing rental property whose income CCCAP counts as unearned, because the person does not actively manage the property an average of at least cccap_rental_property_self_employment_min_hours_per_week (CO-7252, twenty) hours a week (8 CCR 1403-1 3.111.H.4.e, S2704: "Income from rental property will be considered as unearned income if the adult caretaker(s) or teen parent(s) are not actively managing the property an average of at least twenty (20) hours per week"): cccap_rental_property_management_hours (CO-7254) when they average under the line, else none. They are not hours of an eligible activity: the employment minimum-wage test of 3.111.G.1.b ("gross income divided by the number of hours worked") takes them out of hours_worked (cccap_caretaker_in_eligible_activity, CO-984).

Precision. Coverage pass 7, R7-2 (docs/reviews/coverage7-care-energy.md). hours_worked (CO-022) states the hours the person worked for pay in the month, including hours of self-employment, and a rental property stated as a business states its management hours as the business's hours (earnings: hours, rental_property); since 3.111.H.4.e makes such rent unearned income under the line, its hours are not hours worked for the wage test, as cccap_self_employment_hours (CO-6404) already leaves them out of the self-employment hours. The average is the hours divided by the month's days over seven (OQ-1366), as CO-7251 reads it.

  then CCCAP: hours in the month managing rental property stated as a business
otherwise 0

### CO-7910 CCCAP: costs of rental property managed under twenty hours a week, taken against its rents `@engine`

The costs, in the month, of the person's rental property stated as a business whose receipts are unearned rent because the person does not actively manage the property an average of at least cccap_rental_property_self_employment_min_hours_per_week (CO-7252, twenty) hours a week (8 CCR 1403-1 3.111.H.4.e, S2704; cccap_rental_property_receipts_as_unearned, CO-7251): the business's own cost records (earnings, CO-5100: a business_cost_operating or business_cost_interest record whose job names a business whose self_employment_receipts record states rental_property true), the expenses that make its rents "Net rental income" (I.12) and "Net income from rental of a house, store, or other property to others" (I.17, S3256). cccap_excluded_unearned_receipts (CO-4463) takes them against those rents, no more than the rents are; they are not costs of self-employment (cccap_self_employment_business_expenses, CO-1709).

Precision. KL-CE-1 (coverage pass 7, R7-3; docs/reviews/known-limits.md, 2026-11-24). One rental property is stated once for every program: its rents as a business's receipts record (rental_property true, its hours the hours spent managing it) and its costs as that business's cost records, each naming the business (job) and saying whether it is the property's maintenance (property_maintenance, which LEAP reads and CCCAP does not). Before, CCCAP took a small rental's costs only from rental_property_expenses_paid (CO-4458) and read its cost records as costs of self-employment, which a rental under the line is not, so the costs were lost against no self-employment receipts (probe CR2: $3,400, ineligible_income, where the rule gives $3,100, eligible_low_income); LEAP's statement rule asked for the opposite statement. rental_property_expenses_paid now states only the expenses of rental property that is not a business (rental_income receipts). The costs taken are those whose kind's meaning covers the expenses rental_property_expenses_paid lists for a landlord's net rent (property taxes, insurance, repairs and maintenance, utilities and fees: business_cost_operating; interest on the property's mortgage: business_cost_interest), not payments on the principal and not depreciation (business_cost_capital_principal, business_cost_depreciation; CO-4458: "Not payments on the mortgage principal and not depreciation"); the text names no cost of net rental income, and the other cost kinds (vehicle, home space, a boarder's provision) are not taken (OQ-1515). The line is the person's rental management hours in the month (cccap_rental_property_management_hours, CO-7254) over the month's days divided by seven, as CO-7251 and cccap_self_employment_gross_receipts (CO-5156) test it (OQ-1366); every rental property under it is read together, so the costs of two small rentals are taken against their rents together. A cost record is placed in the month as CO-1709 places it (the thirty days before the application or redetermination date for a dated record, the month for a stream; OQ-680). The records are read in this order: whether any of the person's business receipts records is rental property (rental_property, required on every business receipts record CCCAP reads since coverage pass 7, R7-1), then the line, then the cost's business (the cost record's job, and the job of the business receipts records it is compared with), so a person with no rental property states no job (decision 4: required only where read). As with rental_property_expenses_paid, the costs are those the person shows; G.2.a's verification of business expenses is a self-employment criterion, and these are not costs of self-employment.

Type money, scope person-month, program CCCAP.
Uses: `cccap_application_or_redetermination_date`, `cccap_prior_income_period_days`, `cccap_rental_property_management_hours`, `cccap_rental_property_self_employment_min_hours_per_week`, `earnings`.

### CO-981 CCCAP: is a teen parent `@engine`

The person is a "teen parent" under 8 CCR 1403-1 3.103.EEEEE (version effective 2026-08-14) - a person under twenty-one years of age who is financially contributing to the welfare of the child, is the parent, adoptive parent, stepparent, legal guardian or person acting in loco parentis with custody of the child for the period care is requested, and is in an eligible activity such as attending basic education, employment, self-employment, or job search. A person under twenty-one who participates in workforce training or post-secondary education is an adult caretaker, not a teen parent.

Precision. Phase-8 fix round (K-7): the current definition (S1016) adds the financially-contributing conjunct, read from cccap_is_financially_contributing_to_child (CO-897) with no default (OQ-135, resolved), and moves a person in workforce training or post-secondary education (cccap_is_in_workforce_training_or_post_secondary_education, CO-1518, no default) to adult caretaker. Custody is read from a stated parent/child or caretaker/dependent relationship to a CCCAP-eligible child, the same convention cw_has_dependent_child (CO-902) uses for Colorado Works. Requires the custodial child to be a cccap_is_eligible_child, which 3.103.ZZZZ's own text ('his/her child(ren)') does not state; this narrows the term slightly, but costs nothing in practice, since a teen parent with no eligible child also has no eligible child in the household under 3.103.GGG. The eligible-activity conjunct is read with [otherwise, ..., false] (defaults to not-in-an-activity when the case does not state hours_worked/cccap_is_in_job_search_activity/snap_is_enrolled_half_time_in_school_or_training for this person), for the same case-coverage reason as OQ-134/OQ-135/OQ-136 - most existing cases in this chapter's own item tests do not state activity facts for a custodial minor whose teen-parent status was previously age-and-custody-only - see OQ-157. Phase-10 sweep: the referral, financially-contributing and activity facts are read without a default; a case states them (OQ-134, OQ-135, OQ-157, OQ-395). Same-word audit SW-1/SW-3/SW-4 (OQ-396): the adult caretaker relation is cccap_adult_caretaker_of (CO-2607): parent, stepparent, legal guardian, or a person with primary responsibility for the child (in loco parentis, OQ-540).

### CO-982 CCCAP: household members `@engine`

The persons who make up this person's CCCAP household under 8 CCR 1403-1 3.103.GGG and 3.111.B.3, D - the adult caretaker(s) or teen parent(s) and the children in the home who are under eighteen, or under nineteen and still in high school - reciprocally closed over the spouse relationship and over the parent/child and caretaker/dependent relationships where the child side is such a child. An adult child living with their parents is not joined to them, so a grandparent household and their adult child's own household stay separate.

Precision. As with snap_household_members (CO-305) and cw_assistance_unit_members (CO-900), a stated parent/child, caretaker/dependent, or spouse relationship edge is read as physical custody/co-residence; the voluntarily-absent and incapacitated second-caretaker shapes of 3.111.D.1.a and c stay members (the activity test, CO-991, reads them), and the unrelated-caretaker verification of 3.111.D.5 is OQ-125. Coverage pass 3 C3-2: a caretaker who is involuntarily out of the home (cccap_caretaker_is_involuntarily_absent, CO-898, read as false when not stated) is not joined, and joins no one: 3.111.D.1.b (S1409) makes such a household "a household with one adult caretaker or teen parent", D.1.a keeps only a caretaker voluntarily out of the home "part of the household", and 3.103.LLL (S3636) counts the children "in the home". So the absent caretaker's county residency, asset declaration, documents and income are not read and he is not counted in the household size (OQ-872); before the fix a father in jail in another county made the household ineligible (probe Y-8b) and, stated in the county, raised the size to 3 and asked for his residency document (probe Y-8c). Each member's value of this item is the same set (their own household). Same-word audit SW-1/SW-3/SW-4 (OQ-396): the adult caretaker relation is cccap_adult_caretaker_of (CO-2607): parent, stepparent, legal guardian, or a person with primary responsibility for the child (in loco parentis, OQ-540). Same-word audit SW-7 (convention rule 17): an edge joins persons who live together (lives_with, CO-1925, from dwelling_id); where a case states no dwelling_id the edge is read as living together, as before. CCCAP's household is the persons in the home (3.103, S481). Second-pass review N-7 (was F-14): a spouse is joined only when both spouses are adult caretakers, and a stepparent only when an adult caretaker (a teen parent is joined through her own child, by the parent edge), since 3.103.LLL's household is the children and "the adult caretaker(s) or teen parent(s)" and 3.103.C makes a stepparent an adult caretaker only when "financially contributing to the welfare of the child"; a legal parent, guardian or person with primary responsibility is still joined through the child, and the teen parent's own parent through her. A separated caretaker's temporary order (3.111.D.10) leaves membership alone and takes the other spouse's or parent's income out of the sums (cccap_household_income_members, CO-4064). cccap_is_adult_caretaker (CO-992) reads no household item, so the condition makes no cycle. Coverage round F-15: an adult or teen parent in the home who contributes financially to the welfare of a household child (contributes_financially_to, 3.111.D.2) is joined through the child, as a parent is. Three-pattern sweep T-8 (docs/reviews/pattern-sweep-snap-ce.md): a person of the case who died before the determination date (date_of_death, CO-2868) is not joined: the household is the persons living in the home when the county determines eligibility at application or redetermination, which then holds for the twelve-month period (8 CCR 1403-1 3.103.LLL; 3.125.Q, S3252). A person whose date of death is not stated is living. Before, a stated death changed nothing (probe CO-948). Three-pattern sweep D-1 (docs/reviews/pattern-sweep-snap-ce.md): lives_with (CO-1925) is read as stated, required where read: no text on file says that persons related on the application live together unless it says otherwise (8 CCR 1403-1 3.103.LLL: the household is the children in the home and the adult caretakers, S3636), so a stated relationship is no longer read as living together where no dwelling_id is stated (decision 4; docs/conventions.md rule 17, as MAGI's readers since coverage pass 6, C6-10); a case with persons related across the edge states dwelling_id for each of them.

Type group of persons, scope person, program CCCAP.
Uses: `cccap_caretaker_is_involuntarily_absent`, `cccap_is_adult_caretaker`, `cccap_is_household_child`, `date_of_death`, `lives_with`, `relationships`.

### CO-984 CCCAP: caretaker or teen parent is in an eligible activity `@engine`

This adult caretaker or teen parent is actively participating in a low-income eligible activity under 8 CCR 1403-1 3.111.B.1, G - employment or self-employment (hours worked), job search while enrolled in Low-Income Child Care or on transition from Colorado Works, or training/education (for a teen parent, attending school itself qualifies per 3.103.EEEEE); from July 1, 2026, for an adult caretaker, enrollment in a licensed substance use disorder treatment program at an intensive outpatient level of care or higher, for a year from the start of each instance (3.111.G.4.a.3); or is on a temporary break in such an activity that the rule keeps as participation: verified maternity or paternity leave (3.111.D.8), and, while the household already receives Low-Income Child Care, verified medical leave that leaves the caretaker unable to care for the children (D.9) or a seasonal interruption, temporary layoff or scheduled education break (3.112.C).

Precision. Employment and self-employment count when the caretaker works and the gross wages plus CCCAP self-employment income divided by the hours worked is at least the federal minimum wage (3.111.G.1.b, G.2.d; federal_minimum_wage, CO-160), or the self-employment is in its launch period (G.2.e); the two sources are combined into one ratio. Earned-income records, step E1 (CCCAP): the gross wages are cccap_person_gross_wages (CO-5152), from the earnings records of the prior thirty days (every pay for work as an employee, work-study included, as wages_gross held it), replacing the month's wages_gross (CO-023); hours_worked (CO-022) stays outside the records (an activity fact). Job search counts only for a caretaker who "met the eligibility criteria on the most recent eligibility determination" (G.3.a) and ended an activity "while enrolled in the Low-Income program" (G.3.f), or who transitions from Colorado Works (3.117.D) - read from cccap_is_receiving_assistance (CO-2103), true at a redetermination, a change during the eligibility period or a transition (cccap_determination_type, CO-3307); at an initial application job search is not an activity (final pass F-05) - and while the weeks used in the instance are fewer than cccap_job_search_weeks (a county plan may allow more, OQ-162). Education or training counts until its time limit is reached (cccap_education_activity_time_limit_reached); coverage round F-06: at a change reported during the eligibility period (cccap_determination_type, CO-3307) the limit is not applied, since 3.114.B.3 ends care for exceeding a time limit "at re-determination only" and 3.125.Q does not list it (S3251, S3252); whether 3.132.B.3's shorter authorization for a time-limited activity ends the care earlier is OQ-790. The substance use disorder treatment route is read only for an adult caretaker, from the month containing cccap_sud_treatment_instance_start_date (CO-3905: the later of the instance's start, sud_treatment_start_date, and July 1, 2026) for cccap_sud_treatment_activity_max_months months (final pass F-06); the arm is cccap_is_in_sud_treatment_activity (CO-4074). A temporary break is temporary_activity_break_reason (CO-3903, read as none when not stated; final pass F-04): maternity or paternity leave counts at an application too (D.8 names it among eligible households); medical leave needs an open case and the caretaker's inability to care for the children (D.9, cccap_caretaker_is_incapacitated, CO-1744, read as false when not stated); the other breaks of 3.112.C are breaks in an activity the household is already authorized for. The leave is verified as the eligible activity is (cccap_requires_verification_of_eligible_activity, CO-1441). Coverage pass 2 C2-2: at a change reported during the eligibility period medical leave counts without D.9's inability to care for the children, since 3.112.C.2 (S2701) makes "extended verified medical leave" a temporary break and 3.125.Q.2 (S3252) discontinues care before the redetermination only for reasons "that do not constitute a temporary break"; medical leave includes leave to care for a family member (3.103.WWW, S3530). At a redetermination D.9's conjunct is kept (OQ-850). Before the fix a mother on medical leave who could still care for her child was ineligible_activity at a change (probe Z-2). Coverage pass 4 C4-3 and C4-6 (docs/reviews/coverage4-care-energy.md): G requires "at least one of" the activities (S4602), so employment and self-employment are tested each on its own and either is enough. Employment (G.1.b): the gross wages over the hours worked, or over the hours worked less the business's hours (cccap_self_employment_hours, CO-6404) when the wages fall short over all of them. Self-employment (G.2.c-e), only for a caretaker with a self-employment record in the month: CCCAP's net self-employment income over the hours worked, or over the business's own hours, at least the federal minimum wage, or the launch period (CO-2113, read as false when not stated: G.2.e "may be granted", and no grant is none). A caretaker with no business is never asked about a launch period (before the fix, a caretaker whose wages fell short was cannot determine, naming it). The hours worked (CO-022) include the hours of self-employment, so the ratio over all of them is never above the ratio over an activity's own; the business's hours are read only when it decides. Coverage pass 5, C5-1 (docs/reviews/coverage5-care-energy.md): a record stated with neither a month nor a date (a stream) is the pay or payment of the days its source ran (docs/conventions.md, "A record's time"; job_start_date and job_end_date for pay, start_date and end_date for a receipt). It stands for the thirty days only when its source ran through all of them (none of its dates after their first day or before their last); it is not read when its source ended before their first day or began on or after cccap_application_or_redetermination_date; and a source that began or ended inside the thirty days is placed by its dated records, so a stream without them cannot determine and the record's date is named as missing (8 CCR 1403-1 3.111.H.4, H.5.a.1, H.5.b, S2704, S891: the income "received during the prior thirty (30) day period"; OQ-680 (2)). A record stated with its month or its date is placed as before. Coverage pass 7, R7-2 (docs/reviews/coverage7-care-energy.md): the hours of rental property managed under twenty hours a week (cccap_rental_property_unearned_hours, CO-7680) are taken out of hours_worked before the wages and the self-employment income are divided by it: under 3.111.H.4.e (S2704) such rent "will be considered as unearned income", so managing it is not an hour worked for G.1.b's "gross income divided by the number of hours worked", and hours_worked by its meaning holds a business's hours (CO-6404 already takes them out of the self-employment hours). The stated hours are tested first (over 0), so a caretaker with no hours worked is not asked for her earnings here. Before, a caretaker earning $9.20 an hour for 87 hours who managed a rental 43 hours in the month was read at $6.15 an hour and failed the test (probe CR4).

### CO-985 CCCAP: household income `@engine`

The CCCAP household's monthly countable gross income under 8 CCR 1403-1 3.111.H-K: the sum over every household member of the person's countable income (cccap_person_countable_income, CO-3917: generally the income received in the prior thirty days, H.4-5, or the figure the county determined from another period), less the verified court-ordered current child support the household's adult caretakers and teen parents pay for children not living in the household (3.111.K.1, cccap_child_support_paid_deduction, CO-3902), not below zero. The same figure is compared with the entry and exit income limits and used for the parent fee (K.1: "prior to applying the monthly gross income to the maximum gross monthly income guidelines and when calculating parent fees").

Precision. Each member's countable income is earned (CO-3915: wages and CCCAP self-employment income, nothing for a household child who is not a teen parent, 3.111.J.1) plus unearned (CO-3916: the recurring receipts of the month standing for the prior thirty days, Social Security included, and one twelfth of each receipt paid once in the month). What 3.111.J excludes is left out by CCCAP's counting table (cccap_receipt_treatment_table, CO-5720; receipt records, migration phase 2), J.2 (SSI) and J.26 (public cash assistance) among its rows; the J.28 irregular-income exclusion (under $90 a quarter) is applied there too (cccap_excluded_irregular_income, CO-4076; second-pass review, OQ-713). Final pass F-01 and F-09: the 3.111.K deduction is applied, and the income period is the prior thirty days rather than the calendar month. Second-pass review N-7: the sums run over cccap_household_income_members (CO-4064), which leaves out the spouse or other parent of a separated caretaker holding a temporary order (3.111.D.10).

Type money, scope person-month, program CCCAP.
Uses: `cccap_child_support_paid_deduction`, `cccap_household_income_members`, `cccap_person_countable_income`.

```
the greater of 0 and ((the sum of that person's CCCAP: a person's countable income for each person in CCCAP: household members whose income counts) minus (the sum of that person's CCCAP: child support paid deduction for each person in CCCAP: household members whose income counts))
```

### CO-986 CCCAP: income within the county entry limit `@engine`

Whether the CCCAP household's countable income (cccap_household_income, CO-985) is at or below the lesser of the county's entry income eligibility limit for the household's size and eighty-five percent of the state median income, under 8 CCR 1403-1 3.111.H.1 and H.1.a.

Precision. The county entry limit is the county percentage (cccap_entry_income_limit_pct_fpl, CO-870) of the monthly 100% FPG for the household (cccap_poverty_guideline_monthly, CO-3007); that figure is capped at the 85% SMI table for cccap_household_size (cccap_smi_income_limit_table, CO-1804, read beyond its last row with cccap_smi_income_limit_each_additional, CO-1805), per 3.111.H.1's opening sentence ("gross income must not exceed eighty-five percent (85%) of the state median income"). Does not distinguish this entry-limit test from the separate 3.111.H.1.b exit limit a continuing household is held to instead (see cccap_income_within_exit_limit, CO-993, and OQ-133). The 85% SMI table is read as of the determination date in every month evaluated: the entry limit is the test at the initial application or redetermination (3.111.H.1.a), whose figures hold for the twelve-month eligibility period (time audit T-3, docs/operators.md, Resolution). T-9 hand check A-11 (docs/reviews/t9-threshold-handcheck.md): the comparison at the entry level is settled by 3.103.YY (S4421), the "Entry income eligibility level" is the level "above which an adult caretaker(s) or teen parent(s) is not eligible at original application": income equal to the level is eligible (CO-986-T7); the 85% SMI side reads "must not exceed" (H.1). Coverage pass 5, C5-6: the exit limit (CO-993) reads the table the same way.

Type yes/no, scope person-month, program CCCAP.
Uses: `cccap_entry_income_limit_pct_fpl`, `cccap_household_income`, `cccap_household_size`, `cccap_poverty_guideline_monthly`, `cccap_smi_income_limit_each_additional`, `cccap_smi_income_limit_table`.

```

This person's CCCAP household meets the Low-Income Child Care eligibility criteria of 8 CCR 1403-1 3.111 - every adult caretaker and teen parent a verified resident of the county applied to, and within the self-declared asset limit, the caretakers actively in an eligible activity, within the income guidelines (entry or, for a household already receiving assistance, exit), and having physical custody of at least one eligible child in the household.

### CO-988 CCCAP: Colorado Works child care eligible `@engine`

This person's CCCAP household is eligible for Colorado Works Child Care under 8 CCR 1403-1 3.115.A, 3.116.A: an adult caretaker or teen parent of the household is determined work eligible per Colorado Works, receiving Colorado Works basic cash assistance, and referred for child care by the county Colorado Works worker; or, in a county that provides Colorado Works Child Care for households approved for a Colorado Works diversion, approved for a diversion and referred for child care (3.116.H).

Precision. "Approved for Colorado Works and ... determined work eligible per Colorado Works rule" (3.115.A) and "referred for child care by the county Colorado Works worker" (3.116.A) are decisions in the Colorado Works case, read from its records: receives_tanf_cash (CO-013, the unit receives or is authorized to receive basic cash assistance), is_work_eligible_individual_in_tanf_case (CO-2709) and is_referred_for_colorado_works_child_care (CO-896). This volume's own Colorado Works determination is not re-run for CCCAP (convention rule 11). Per 3.111.D.6, a caretaker or teen parent caring for a child receiving Colorado Works cash assistance who is not determined work eligible falls through to the Low-Income Child Care determination instead of this branch, rather than being denied outright. Phase-10 sweep: the referral, financially-contributing and activity facts are read without a default; a case states them (OQ-134, OQ-135, OQ-157, OQ-395). Final pass F-16: the county-elected diversion route reads receives_tanf_diversion_payment (CO-3931, false when not stated) and the county's choice, cccap_county_provides_cw_child_care_for_diversion_table (CO-3932), which has no version until the counties' choices are published (OQ-682). Coverage round F-01: the conditions are tested on the household's adult caretakers and teen parents (cccap_household_members, CO-982), not on the person evaluated, so a child reads its caretaker's Colorado Works case and referral and every member gets the same value (3.116.A: caretakers "that have been determined eligible for Colorado Works ... and have been referred for child care by the county Colorado Works worker ... must receive Colorado Works Child Care").

### CO-989 CCCAP: eligibility status `@engine`

This CCCAP household's eligibility determination for the month, reported on every household member (including a child, who reads the household's caretakers' and other members' facts rather than their own) - checked in order - a disqualification of an adult caretaker or teen parent for an intentional program violation (3.114.A.6, 3.139.D); Child Welfare Child Care (3.120) for a household with a child of eligible age who needs care; having an eligible child in the household (3.103.UU, 3.111.F); a Protective Services referral within its own household-of-one income test (3.119.A, C); unpaid parent fees not resolved, at a redetermination or a new application (3.114.B.2, 3.124.N); Colorado Works Child Care eligibility; at an application or a redetermination, an adult caretaker or teen parent who is part of the Colorado Works assistance unit but not Colorado Works Child Care eligible (3.115.C, 3.114.B.6); at a transition from Colorado Works, a caretaker's Colorado Works intentional program violation (3.117.A.1); unexplained absences of every eligible child, except at an application (3.114.A.5, B.11, 3.117.A.3); a family experiencing homelessness in its stabilization period (3.121.B, no activity required); being in an eligible activity; the county entry income limit; and, last, the remaining Low-Income criteria (residency, the asset self-declaration) bundled in cccap_low_income_child_care_eligible - eligible for Low-Income Child Care only if every one of those checks passes.

Precision. Colorado Works Child Care households are not subject to the low-income eligible-activity or entry-income tests (3.111.D.6), so that route is checked first and short-circuits the rest. Protective Services households are not subject to the low-income eligible-activity or residency-verification requirements (3.119.D, E), but 3.119.A does not waive the income test - it only redefines it (household of one, placed child's income only, no child support) - so the Protective Services branch now carries its own income conjunct (cccap_protective_services_income_within_limit, CO-995) and falls through to the ordinary rows, rather than granting eligible_protective_services on the referral flag alone. A residency or asset-limit failure that survives to the final row (the only two 3.111 criteria this item does not give their own reason code) reports the generic ineligible rather than a more specific option, since the outcome's option list has no ineligible_residency or ineligible_assets entry. Final pass F-02, F-03 and F-07: a household with an adult caretaker or teen parent serving a CCCAP IPV disqualification (cccap_is_serving_ipv_disqualification, CO-3906, read as false when not stated) is ineligible_disqualified, whatever its category, since 3.139.D makes the penalty affect any household the person is a member of; a Child Welfare Child Care household (cccap_is_child_welfare_child_care_household, CO-2576, read as false when not stated) is eligible_child_welfare, its eligibility being the Child Welfare division's case-by-case finding under 12 CCR 2509-4 7.302 (3.120.D), not the Low-Income tests; a family experiencing homelessness during its stabilization period (cccap_is_in_homelessness_stabilization, CO-3907) with an eligible child is eligible_homelessness_stabilization, since 3.121.B requires an authorization for the period and B.3.a waives the activity requirement; its income and residency are verified for ongoing eligibility by the end of the period (B.1). Second-pass review N-3, N-4: the eligible-child test now precedes the Protective Services and Colorado Works rows (3.103.UU: "Any child served through the Colorado Works program or the Low-Income Child Care program must be a citizen/legal resident"; 3.119.F makes the Protective Services child's citizenship, age and identity a condition of care), so a Colorado Works household whose only child is fifteen is ineligible_child, not eligible_colorado_works (RV-S8). Child Welfare Child Care keeps its place ahead of it but needs a child of eligible age who needs part-day care (cccap_is_child_of_eligible_age_needing_care, CO-4056), not the citizenship part, since it is not funded through the Child Care Development Fund (3.120.F) and 3.103.UU names only Colorado Works and Low-Income (OQ-710). Unpaid parent fees not resolved (cccap_parent_fee_nonpayment_unresolved, CO-4054) make a household ineligible at a redetermination (3.114.B.2; for Colorado Works Child Care, the end of its period, 3.124.N) and at a new application (3.124.N: "will remain ineligible until"); a child's twenty-two unexplained absences with two failed contacts (cccap_child_has_unexplained_absences_finding, CO-4055) end that child's authorization, and the household is ineligible when every eligible child has such a finding, at a change, a redetermination or a transition (3.114.A.5, B.11, 3.117.A.3; OQ-711); at a transition from Colorado Works a caretaker serving a Colorado Works IPV disqualification (cw_is_serving_ipv_disqualification, CO-1730) bars the transition (3.117.A.1). These rows report the generic ineligible, or ineligible_disqualified for the IPV. N-2: the Protective Services income is the placed children's, one figure for the household (CO-994); N-10: an income requirement the Child Welfare worker waived is met (CO-995). Coverage round F-12: 3.115.C (S3253) lets a caretaker who is not work eligible and cares for children receiving basic cash assistance be Low-Income eligible only "if the adult caretaker or teen parent is not a part of the Colorado Works assistance unit", and 3.114.B.6 (S3251) ends Low-Income care at the redetermination when a caretaker "has become a participant in Colorado Works"; 3.111.D.6 (S511) states the same route without the unit condition, and the more specific 3.115.C is read as governing. So, after the Colorado Works Child Care row, a household with an adult caretaker or teen parent in the assistance unit (receives_tanf_cash, CO-013, read from the caretaker) is ineligible at an application or a redetermination; at a change during the period it is not, since 3.125.Q does not list it (S3252), and at a transition the household is leaving Colorado Works. A caretaker who is not in the unit (a relative caring for a child-only grant) is not barred (probe RV-I: before the fix a non-work-eligible mother in the unit was eligible_low_income).

### CO-991 CCCAP: household caretakers in eligible activity `@engine`

At least one adult caretaker or teen parent in this person's CCCAP household who is in the home (not involuntarily out of it) is engaged in a low-income eligible activity this month, and every other adult caretaker or teen parent is either in an activity too or excused from one, under 8 CCR 1403-1 3.111.D.1 and E: a one-caretaker household whose caretaker is in an activity (D.1.a); a two-caretaker household where both are (D.1.c.1), one being voluntarily absent included (D.1.c.2); one in an activity and the other incapacitated under a physician's or other medical verification (D.1.c.3); or one in an activity in the home and the other involuntarily out of the home, a one-caretaker household (D.1.b).

Precision. The caretakers are cccap_is_adult_caretaker (CO-992) household members plus any cccap_is_teen_parent (CO-981). Coverage round F-03: a caretaker who is not in an eligible activity is excused when cccap_caretaker_is_incapacitated (CO-1744; 3.111.D.1.c.3) or cccap_caretaker_is_involuntarily_absent (CO-898, 3.111.D.1.b; a voluntary absence under c.2 excuses no one) holds for them, but only if another caretaker in the home is in an activity: two incapacitated caretakers, or one incapacitated and one involuntarily absent (a one-caretaker household under D.1.b whose caretaker is incapacitated), fail, per 3.111.E's rule that "Incapacitated single adult caretakers ... who are not in a low-income eligible activity are not eligible"; before the fix any second caretaker, active or not, excused the first (probes RV-A1, RV-A2). A household whose only caretaker is involuntarily out of the home has no caretaker in the home in an activity and fails (see OQ-136 on the involuntary/voluntary distinction this does not carry, and OQ-125 on unrelated-caretaker verification). Evaluated for any household member, child included, so a child's CCCAP status reads the caretakers' activity rather than the child's own. Coverage pass 3 C3-1: at a change reported during the eligibility period (cccap_determination_type, CO-3307), a caretaker who joined the household during the period (cccap_caretaker_joined_during_eligibility_period, CO-4910, read as false when not stated) is neither tested nor counted as the household's active caretaker, since 3.125.EE.2 (S3635) holds a change in household composition other than an additional child until the redetermination and 3.125.Q.2 (S3252) discontinues care only for a caretaker who is "no longer" in an activity; before the fix a new spouse with no activity ended the household's care at a change (probe Y-1). A caretaker who leaves during the period is simply no longer stated, and the caretakers who remain are tested as the household now stands (OQ-871). Vocabulary fix round (docs/reviews/vocabulary-reuse.md, R-12, C-4): incapacity reads cccap_caretaker_is_incapacitated (CO-1744), not SNAP's unfitness statement; an unstated incapacity or absence reads as false, as the facts' meanings now say.

### CO-992 CCCAP: is an adult caretaker `@engine`

The person is an "adult caretaker" under 8 CCR 1403-1 3.103.C - a person in the home who is financially contributing to the welfare of an eligible child in the household and is the parent, adoptive parent, step-parent, legal guardian, or a person acting in loco parentis with physical custody of the child, and who is not themselves a household child - or, under twenty-one, participates in workforce training or post-secondary education, which 3.103.EEEEE makes an adult caretaker rather than a teen parent.

Precision. Phase-8 fix round (K-7) - a household child under twenty-one in workforce training or post-secondary education (cccap_is_in_workforce_training_or_post_secondary_education, CO-1518) is an adult caretaker (3.103.EEEEE, S1016); the fact is read only for a household child. Physical custody is read from a stated parent/child or caretaker/dependent relationship to a CCCAP eligible child, the same convention cccap_is_teen_parent (CO-981) uses; "financially contributing to the welfare of the child" is read from the supplied cccap_is_financially_contributing_to_child (CO-897, defaulted to true absent a stated value, see OQ-135). Phase-10 sweep: the referral, financially-contributing and activity facts are read without a default; a case states them (OQ-134, OQ-135, OQ-157, OQ-395). Same-word audit SW-1/SW-3/SW-4 (OQ-396): the adult caretaker relation is cccap_adult_caretaker_of (CO-2607): parent, stepparent, legal guardian, or a person with primary responsibility for the child (in loco parentis, OQ-540). Coverage round F-15: a person who contributes financially to an eligible child's welfare (the role contributes_financially_to, 3.111.D.2) is an adult caretaker by that edge; the edge states the contribution, so cccap_is_financially_contributing_to_child is not needed for him (OQ-540).
