### CO-994 CCCAP: protective services household income `@engine`

For a Protective Services household, the only countable income under 8 CCR 1403-1 3.119.A - the income received by the child(ren) placed in kinship or foster care, excluding child support (which is intercepted by the county child welfare department and not counted) - one figure for the household, the same for every member.

Precision. A Protective Services household is a household of one for income purposes (3.119.A), and its income is the placed children's: the sum over the household's eligible children (cccap_household_members, CO-982, filtered by cccap_is_eligible_child, CO-980; the children the referral is for, the reading cccap_parent_fee_income, CO-2578, already uses, OQ-536) of each child's income as CCCAP counts any person's - the earned part (cccap_person_earned_income, CO-3915), which 3.111.J.1 makes nothing for a child in the household who is not a teen parent, and the unearned part (cccap_person_unearned_income, CO-3916), which leaves out what 3.111.J excludes - less the child's child support as that unearned part counts it (cccap_counted_child_support, CO-5725, from the receipts), which 3.119.A does not count. Receipt records, migration phase 2 (2026-11-23): the child support is read from the receipts, not from child_support_received with its 0 when not stated. The caretakers' income is not read (second-pass review N-2: the item read the evaluated person's own income, so a kin caretaker and the placed child in one household had different statuses and fees). Coverage pass 3 C3-9: 3.119.A counts the income of the children "that have been placed in kinship or foster care"; the volume has no fact for which household children are placed, so the sum runs over every eligible child of the household. A caretaker's own child who is not placed adds income only through unearned income such as a child's Social Security benefit (a household child's earnings are excluded, J.1); a case with such a child and such income overstates the household's income.

### CO-995 CCCAP: protective services income within the size-1 limit `@engine`

Whether the Protective Services household's countable income (cccap_protective_services_income, CO-994) is at or below the county entry income limit for a household of cccap_protective_services_household_size (CO-3008), since 3.119.A makes every Protective Services household a household of one for income eligibility.

Reads the same entry-limit computation as cccap_income_within_entry_limit (CO-986) - the county percentage of the 100% FPG figure, capped at the 85% SMI figure - fixed at the protective services household size rather than cccap_household_size (CO-983), per 3.119.A. The 100% guideline is computed as cccap_poverty_guideline_monthly (CO-3007) computes it, for the protective services household size instead of the household's own size: the HHS guideline in force on the most recent October 1, divided by twelve and rounded to the cent. N-2: the income tested is the placed children's, one figure for the household (CO-994). The 85% SMI table is read as of the determination date in every month evaluated: the entry limit is the test at the initial application or redetermination (3.111.H.1.a), whose figures hold for the twelve-month eligibility period (time audit T-3, docs/operators.md, Resolution). ### CO-998 CCCAP: child meets citizenship requirement `@engine`

Whether this child is a citizen/legal resident under 8 CCR 1403-1 3.111.F.1 and 3.103.Z - required of "all children who have had an application made on their behalf or are receiving child care assistance": a citizen or national of the United States, or a qualified alien (a lawful permanent resident or another status of 8 U.S.C. 1641), the only non-citizens lawfully present for the Child Care and Development Fund under Title IV of PRWORA.

Precision. 3.103.Z defines "citizen/legal resident" as a citizen, a current legal resident, or "a person lawfully present in the United States pursuant to Title IV of the Personal Responsibility and Work Opportunity Reconciliation Act" and the Federal Register notices it incorporates (S1910). Title IV makes a non-citizen who is not a qualified alien ineligible for any Federal public benefit (8 U.S.C. 1611(a), S1911), and the incorporated HHS notice lists the Child Care and Development Fund as one (63 Fed. Reg. 41658, S1912), so the non-qualified lawfully present categories (Temporary Protected Status and the others) do not meet it (OQ-394 resolved). 3.103.Z and 3.111.F.1 impose no test on the adult caretaker, only the child.

### CO-1000 LEAP: household members `@engine`

The individuals living together as one economic unit for whom primary heating fuel is customarily purchased in common, or who make undesignated payments for heat in the form of rent, under 9 CCR 2503-7 3.751.1's "Household" definition - a spouse, or a child under eighteen living in the same dwelling as the parent or guardian (unless emancipated), per 3.751.2.D, or anyone the case states shares heating fuel in common under 3.751.1's general economic-unit test, reciprocally closed - leaving out a person who does not live at the dwelling (institutional group care), a member already counted in another household approved for the same eligibility period (3.751.2.A), a member who does not meet the citizenship requirement (3.753.18), and a member who meets it as declared but has provided no SSN or proof of application for one (3.751.1 "Completed Application" B) or whose declared immigration status SAVE has not verified (3.753.15, 3.753.17.A). The income of a member left out for status or verification is still counted (leap_household_members_for_income, CO-1009).

Precision. As with snap_household_members (CO-305), a stated spouse or parent/child relationship edge is read as living together for LEAP purposes, extended beyond 3.751.2.D's unconditional age-based joins by a stated shares_heat_with relationship (the role that replaced the retired shares_heating_fuel_with fact when OQ-132 was resolved), which joins any two persons who buy heating fuel in common, related or not (OQ-132, resolved), except that an edge is not crossed to or from a person whose own leap_living_arrangement is institutional_group_care: 3.751.1 joins individuals "living together" and 3.751.2.B counts "each person living at a dwelling", so a spouse who has entered a nursing facility is not in the household at home (OQ-358, resolved). If leap_living_arrangement is not stated, LEAP reads it as an ordinary dwelling. The SSN test reads ssn_is_verified (a number furnished, an application shown, or SSA's confirmation); 3.751.1 B states no exception for a person who cannot obtain a number. Coverage review C-8 (final pass F-18): a civil union partner (the civil_union_partner role) is joined as a spouse is (3.751.2.D.3, S3312). 3.751.2.E is modeled: when a parent living with an ex-spouse after divorce or legal separation elects a separate household (leap_is_listed_separately_from_ex_spouse, CO-4519, read as false when not stated), the spouse or civil union edge to that parent is not crossed, and a child under eighteen of the electing parent (leap_is_child_of_parent_listed_separately, CO-4520) is not joined to the other parent; a shares_heat_with edge stated between the two still joins them. 3.751.21 and 3.751.22 need nothing further: a divorced couple has no spouse edge, and a legally separated couple who do not elect E stay joined, as the presumption of marriage reads. Coverage review C-7 (OQ-801): 3.752.23.U says "foster care/kinship individuals are not considered LEAP Household members", so a person whose child_welfare_payment_type is foster care (IV-E, State-funded, or IV-B services in foster care) or kinship guardianship (IV-E or State) is left out, the reading that the specific exclusion governs D.2's general join of a child with a guardian; adopted children are members. Same-word audit SW-4: a child under 18 joins a parent's or legal guardian's household (3.751.2.D, "parent or guardian"); the legal_guardian role is crossed as the parent role is. Same-word audit SW-7 (convention rule 17): an edge joins persons who live together (lives_with, CO-1925, from dwelling_id); where a case states no dwelling_id the edge is read as living together, as before. LEAP's household is individuals living together at a dwelling (3.751.1, 3.751.2.B, S1400). Coverage pass 4 L4-4: a child's age is read on the application date (leap_age_on_application_date, CO-6400; 3.752.2, "household composition" considered "as of the date of application"), so a child who turns eighteen between the application and the determination is still a child of the household. Three-pattern sweep T-8 (docs/reviews/pattern-sweep-snap-ce.md): a person of the case who died before leap_application_date (date_of_death, CO-2868) is not a member: the household is the persons living at the dwelling, as they stand on the date of the application (9 CCR 2503-7 3.751.1 "Household" and "Point in Time"). A person whose date of death is not stated is living. Before, a stated death changed nothing (probe CO-947). Three-pattern sweep D-1 (docs/reviews/pattern-sweep-snap-ce.md): lives_with (CO-1925) is read as stated, required where read: no text on file says that persons related on the application live together unless it says otherwise (9 CCR 2503-7 3.751.1 "Household": the persons living at the dwelling, S489), so a stated relationship is no longer read as living together where no dwelling_id is stated (decision 4; docs/conventions.md rule 17, as MAGI's readers since coverage pass 6, C6-10); a case with persons related across the edge states dwelling_id for each of them.

### CO-1002 LEAP: household income `@engine`

The LEAP household's countable gross monthly income under 9 CCR 2503-7 3.752.21-23 - the sum over each member of the economic unit (a 3.753.17-excluded member included) of the member's wages converted to a month by the pay schedule (3.752.22.B-C, leap_person_wages, CO-3925), except a child under eighteen residing with a parent or guardian, whose earnings 3.752.23.Q excludes; the member's self-employment income for the full month prior to the application date (3.755.21.I.1 as amended effective November 1, 2026), except that child's; and the member's countable unearned income (3.752.21-22.A, leap_person_unearned_income, CO-3926). The figure is monthly; leap_household_income_pct_fpl (CO-1278) annualizes it.

Precision. Sums over leap_household_members_for_income (CO-1009, the unfiltered economic unit, not leap_household_members, CO-1000, which 3.753.17 excludes a non-citizen from although his income still counts). LEAP determines income at the application (3.751.1 "Point in Time"), so this item is read for the month of leap_application_date (leap_is_eligible, CO-1007; leap_benefit_amount, CO-1281); self-employment (leap_self_employment_income, CO-1712) is read for the month before it, the "full month prior to the application date" (OQ-681). Second-pass review P2 (3.752.23.Q, S2860): a child under eighteen has the earned income excluded, wages and self-employment alike, only when residing with a parent or guardian, read as a legal parent or legal guardian among the members (child or ward of a member); a child living with neither (with a grandparent, say) has it counted. The condition is leap_earnings_are_excluded_as_child (CO-5123), which leap_requires_verification_of_earned_income (CO-1455) reads too (duplicate-paths audit D-L2). Payments from boarders, which 3.752.21 counts as payments from any other source and Q does not exclude, are in each member's unearned income (leap_person_unearned_income, CO-3926, through leap_boarder_payments, CO-5124; finding E1-L2). What 3.752.23 excludes is left out of the figures read (CO-3913, CO-3926); leap_excluded_income (CO-2345) is retired. Coverage review 2 N-2 (3.752.23.DD, S3300, "Income that is deemed necessary for the fulfillment of a Plan for Achieving Self-Support", earned and unearned alike): the earned income a member sets aside under an approved plan is taken off the pay it is part of: earned-income records, step E1 (LEAP), state it as the pass_set_aside of each earnings record (earnings, CO-5100), taken off that record by leap_person_wages (CO-3925, through CO-3912, CO-5120 to CO-5122) and leap_self_employment_income (CO-1712), so it is subtracted once, from the pay it came out of and in the period that pay is read for; this item no longer subtracts pass_set_aside_earned_income (CO-4618), which was read as 0 when not stated. The unearned set-aside is in leap_excluded_unearned_income (CO-4511).

### CO-1003 LEAP: income within limit `@engine`

Whether the LEAP household's countable income (leap_household_income, CO-1002) is at or below sixty percent of the state median income level for the household's size, under 9 CCR 2503-7 3.752.22.D.

Precision. Reads leap_income_limit_monthly (CO-875), the Department's season table keyed by household size 1 through 15 (S1406), by this person's leap_household_size (CO-1001); 3.751.2.C caps a household at fifteen members (S1407), so a larger size has no figure and is unknown. The table is read as of the determination date, not in the month whose income is tested: the limit is the heating season's (3.752.22.D, the Department's table for each season), and CO-875 keeps a season's table in force until the next season begins, so the determination of an application for the season reads it even when the income month falls before November 1 (a public assistance household's October application, 3.752.1; time audit T-3, docs/operators.md, Resolution). Coverage pass 5, L5-5 (docs/reviews/coverage5-care-energy.md): the season's table is read as of the first day of the program year the application is for (leap_application_program_year_start_month, CO-4517), not the determination date: a LEAP case is now determined as of its application date (leap_determination_is_as_of_application_date, CO-7000), and a public assistance household's application received before November 1 is for the season that begins then (3.752.1, S3308: "eligibility shall not be effective until November 1st"; 3.752.22.D, S491: income "for the eligibility period"), whose table is in force from that day. For an application received in the season the two readings are the same table.

### CO-1007 LEAP: is eligible `@engine`

Whether this person's LEAP household is eligible for a Heating Fuel Assistance Program payment for the month under 9 CCR 2503-7 3.752.2 - the month is within the November-April eligibility period, Colorado resident, at least one lawfully present household member, at or below the income limit, vulnerable to heating cost, and having a primary heating source.

Precision. Final pass F-12: the 3.754.1 factors for denial are read as follows - excess income (A, leap_income_within_limit), not vulnerable (B), no citizen or qualified alien member (C, leap_has_countable_household_member), a duplicate household or a member approved in another household (D, through leap_household_members, CO-1000, and leap_is_in_another_approved_household, CO-2100), benefits received from another county (F, leap_received_benefit_in_another_county, CO-3930), not a Colorado resident (H), an application outside the application period (J, leap_month_in_eligibility_period), a refused weatherization or CIP inspection (L, T, leap_has_denial_hold, CO-3928), a non-traditional dwelling or no primary heating source (P, R, has_primary_heating_source and the vulnerability test), the applicant's fraud conviction (U, leap_applicant_is_serving_fraud_penalty, CO-3929) and homelessness (W, the vulnerability test); each finding is read as false when not stated. The procedural factors (E withdrawn, G and V incomplete application or verification, I unsigned, K applicant not located, M to O identification and affidavit, Q not living at the address applied for, S a refused bulk delivery) are the county's case actions, reported by leap_verification_status (CO-1462) where they concern verification. Reads is_colorado_resident (CO-505, Medicaid's chapter) rather than a separate leap_meets_residency item: 3.753.21's Colorado-residency-with-intent-to-remain test and 10 CCR 2505-10 8.100.3.B's test derive identically (state_of_residence = colorado_state_code), and governance's dup.compact check flags an identical derivation as an error, not merely a warning, so this batch reuses the existing item and accepts the cross-program read rather than duplicating it (see the batch report). 3.751.1's Point in Time (S776) is applied: the residency, household, income, vulnerability and heating-source tests are evaluated in the month of leap_application_date (CO-2122), and the month evaluated must be in the eligibility period, in the same program year as the application and not before it, so a change after the application date does not change the result (OQ-137, resolved). Coverage review C-3 and C-4: the program year is the one the application is for (leap_application_program_year_start_month, CO-4517), and the month evaluated is not before the month the application was filed (leap_application_filing_date, CO-4514: the postmark of a mailed form, otherwise the date received). An application must be received or postmarked within the application period, April 30 extended to the next business day after a weekend or holiday (leap_application_is_within_application_period, CO-4516; 3.752.1, 3.754.1.J), except that a public assistance household's application filed before November 1 (leap_is_public_assistance_household, CO-4518, read in the month of the application) is accepted for the program year that begins that November 1 (3.752.1: "eligibility shall not be effective until November 1st"). The circumstances are still those of the month the application was received (3.752.1). Coverage pass 5, L5-5 (docs/reviews/coverage5-care-energy.md): the point-in-time factors (residency, citizenship and alien status, household composition, vulnerability and dwelling type, the heating source, the public assistance household) are read only when the case is determined as of its application date (leap_determination_is_as_of_application_date, CO-7000; 3.752.2, S4600; 3.751.1 "Point in Time", S776): a person's facts are stated as of the determination date, so a case stated for a later day could read a shelter the household moved to after applying, or a status granted after the application, and cannot determine instead (the time contract, docs/conventions.md "Scopes"). The tests of the month, the filing month and the program year come first and still answer false for a month LEAP cannot cover.

### CO-1009 LEAP: household members for income `@engine`

The individuals living together as one economic unit for whom primary heating fuel is customarily purchased in common, or who make undesignated payments for heat in the form of rent, under 9 CCR 2503-7 3.751.1's "Household" definition - the same economic unit leap_household_members (CO-1000) computes, without CO-1000's citizenship and verification exclusions, since 3.753.18 and 3.751.1 "Completed Application" B count an excluded individual's income even though the individual is not a household member. A person who does not live at the dwelling (institutional group care) or who was already counted in another household approved for the same eligibility period (3.751.2.A) is not part of the unit.

Precision. As with leap_household_members (CO-1000), a stated spouse or parent/child relationship edge is read as living together for LEAP purposes, extended beyond 3.751.2.D's unconditional age-based joins by a stated shares_heat_with relationship (the role that replaced the retired shares_heating_fuel_with fact when OQ-132 was resolved) between any two persons, related or not (OQ-132, resolved), and an edge is not crossed to or from a person whose leap_living_arrangement is institutional_group_care (OQ-358); if leap_living_arrangement is not stated, LEAP reads it as an ordinary dwelling. Coverage review C-8 (final pass F-18): a civil union partner (the civil_union_partner role) is joined as a spouse is (3.751.2.D.3, S3312). 3.751.2.E is modeled: when a parent living with an ex-spouse after divorce or legal separation elects a separate household (leap_is_listed_separately_from_ex_spouse, CO-4519, read as false when not stated), the spouse or civil union edge to that parent is not crossed, and a child under eighteen of the electing parent (leap_is_child_of_parent_listed_separately, CO-4520) is not joined to the other parent; a shares_heat_with edge stated between the two still joins them. 3.751.21 and 3.751.22 need nothing further: a divorced couple has no spouse edge, and a legally separated couple who do not elect E stay joined, as the presumption of marriage reads. Coverage review C-7 (OQ-801): 3.752.23.U says "foster care/kinship individuals are not considered LEAP Household members", so a person whose child_welfare_payment_type is foster care (IV-E, State-funded, or IV-B services in foster care) or kinship guardianship (IV-E or State) is left out, the reading that the specific exclusion governs D.2's general join of a child with a guardian; adopted children are members. Same-word audit SW-4: a child under 18 joins a parent's or legal guardian's household (3.751.2.D, "parent or guardian"); the legal_guardian role is crossed as the parent role is. Same-word audit SW-7 (convention rule 17): an edge joins persons who live together (lives_with, CO-1925, from dwelling_id); where a case states no dwelling_id the edge is read as living together, as before. LEAP's household is individuals living together at a dwelling (3.751.1, 3.751.2.B, S1400). Coverage pass 4 L4-4: a child's age is read on the application date (leap_age_on_application_date, CO-6400; 3.752.2, "household composition" considered "as of the date of application"), so a child who turns eighteen between the application and the determination is still a child of the household. Three-pattern sweep T-8 (docs/reviews/pattern-sweep-snap-ce.md): a person of the case who died before leap_application_date (date_of_death, CO-2868) is not a member: the household is the persons living at the dwelling, as they stand on the date of the application (9 CCR 2503-7 3.751.1 "Household" and "Point in Time"). A person whose date of death is not stated is living. Before, a stated death changed nothing (probe CO-947). Three-pattern sweep D-1 (docs/reviews/pattern-sweep-snap-ce.md): lives_with (CO-1925) is read as stated, required where read: no text on file says that persons related on the application live together unless it says otherwise (9 CCR 2503-7 3.751.1 "Household": the persons living at the dwelling, S489), so a stated relationship is no longer read as living together where no dwelling_id is stated (decision 4; docs/conventions.md rule 17, as MAGI's readers since coverage pass 6, C6-10); a case with persons related across the edge states dwelling_id for each of them.

Whether this person is a U.S. citizen, national or qualified alien under 9 CCR 2503-7 3.753.16-3.753.17, so that this person counts as a member of a LEAP household rather than being excluded: a lawful permanent resident; a parolee for at least one year; a conditional entrant; a refugee; an asylee; a person whose deportation is withheld; a Cuban or Haitian entrant; a trafficking victim certified by HHS; an Iraqi or Afghan granted Special Immigrant Visa status; a battered non-citizen; an Amerasian immigrant (a lawful permanent resident); or an American Indian born in Canada or tribal member (3.753.16.A-L).

Precision. Reads immigration_status (CO-002). A Compact of Free Association migrant is not in 3.753.16's list A-L (S1909) and is not a qualified alien for LEAP, so is not a household member (the income still counts, 3.753.18) (CDHS review S-3). An Afghan or Ukrainian humanitarian parolee is read as paroled for at least one year (B) (OQ-550). An applicant for a status, a non-citizen with no status verification and a temporary visitor, student or worker are not eligible (3.753.17); none of the lawfully present categories of other programs is on LEAP's list. LIHEAP is a Federal public benefit (63 Fed. Reg. 41658, S1912), for which 8 U.S.C. 1611 allows only qualified aliens.

### CO-1281 LEAP: Heating Fuel Assistance benefit amount `@engine`

The heating-season Heating Fuel Assistance benefit for an eligible household - one amount for the whole November-April season, reported on each month of the season in which the household is eligible, not a monthly payment to be multiplied by the months - the adjusted estimated home heating costs less the statewide adjustment and the household income contribution (each a share of those costs), less the subsidized-housing heating allowance where it applies, kept within the Department's minimum and maximum for the program year - or zero when the household is not eligible, per 9 CCR 2503-7 3.758.47 Steps B, D, F and G.

Precision. Step G subtracts the Step B-F adjustments from the estimated costs; this item reads Steps B and D as shares of the costs after Steps C and E and subtracts them together, then deducts the leap_subsidized_housing_heating_allowance seasonal subsidized-housing allowance (Step F), and floors the result at zero before the minimum and maximum apply. The rule does not say whether Step D applies before or after Step B; the additive reading is recorded in OQ-253. Point in Time (3.751.1, S776): the household income contribution is taken in the month of leap_application_date (OQ-137).

Type money, scope person-month, program LEAP.

```
otherwise 0
```

The living arrangement of the person for the LEAP vulnerability test of 9 CCR 2503-7 3.752.25.B - an ordinary dwelling, or one of the arrangements that is not vulnerable: institutional group care, public or private, where the provider is liable for shelter and heating, such as a nursing home, group home or substance abuse treatment center (B.1); room and board or bed and breakfast (B.2); a correctional facility (B.3); a dormitory, fraternity or sorority house (B.4); subsidized housing without an individual heat meter or evidence of responsibility for heating surcharges (B.5); a commercial property that is also the dwelling (B.7); or a hotel without thirty days' continuous residence at the time of application with heat included in rent (B.8). Homelessness or a non-traditional dwelling (B.6) is leap_is_homeless_or_in_non_traditional_dwelling.

B.8's 'has lived or will live' is read from the days lived by the application date (OQ-610). A person in institutional group care does not live at the household's dwelling, so leap_household_members (CO-1000) does not join that person. ### CO-1462 LEAP: verification status `@engine`

Where this person's LEAP household stands on verification: not applicable (no one in the person's LEAP economic unit meets the citizenship requirement as declared, so LEAP cannot reach it); none required; complete; pending within the two weeks allowed; or past due (the application is denied for failure to provide required verification). A member without an SSN or a verified status is excluded (leap_member_is_excluded_for_verification) rather than making the household past due; a unit whose declared-citizen members are all excluded that way is still reported, not not_applicable.

Precision. Coverage review C-22: 9 CCR 2503-7 3.756.12.D has the county reopen and complete a denied application when the requested verification arrives after the denial (within fifteen calendar days of receipt, by June 15). This item reports the status on the facts stated; it has no dated path from past due back to complete, so a reopened application is read from the verification facts as they then stand, with the due date unchanged. Coverage pass 6 for LEAP, R6-5 (docs/reviews/coverage6-care-energy.md): LEAP's time contract fixes an eligibility determination's date at the application date (leap_determination_is_as_of_application_date, CO-7000; docs/conventions.md, Scopes), but whether verification is pending or past due turns on the day the county looks (3.755.11; the due date, leap_verification_due_date, CO-1461, is two weeks after the request). The verification status is therefore reported on a separate evaluation of the same facts, stated as of the day the county looks, and that evaluation is not an eligibility determination: leap_is_eligible (CO-1007) does not read this item, and CO-7000 makes it cannot determine on any date but the application date. A case stated as of the application date reads a request made after it as pending (review probes LV1 and LV2).

Type one of, scope person-month, program LEAP.
Uses: `leap_household_members_for_income`, `leap_pending_verification_count`, `leap_person_required_verification_count`, `leap_verification_due_date`, `leap_verification_is_applicable`.

```
if it is not the case that LEAP: verification applies to this person
  then not_applicable
else if (the sum of that person's LEAP: person's required verification count for each person in LEAP: household members for income) is equal to 0
  then not_required
else if LEAP: pending verification count is equal to 0
  then complete
else if the Determination Date is at most LEAP: verification due date
  then pending
otherwise past_due
```

```json
["case",[["not","leap_verification_is_applicable"],"not_applicable"],[["=",["sum","leap_household_members_for_income",["of",["P"],"leap_person_required_verification_count"]],0],"not_required"],[["=","leap_pending_verification_count",0],"complete"],[["<=",["det_date"],"leap_verification_due_date"],"pending"],["else","past_due"]]
```

### CO-1711 LEAP: self-employment allowable costs `@engine`

The person's business-related expenses for the month supported by receipts that 9 CCR 2503-7 3.755.21.I allows as deductions from declared gross self-employment income: the cost records (earnings, CO-5100) whose kind LEAP's counting table deducts (leap_earnings_treatment_table, CO-5102: operating costs, interest and business mileage), paid in the month; nothing when receipts for the expenses have not been received (I.2: "Receipts for business-related expenses are required in order to be considered as deductions").

Precision. Earned-income records, step E1 (LEAP): the costs are records of a cost kind, each deducted or not by its row (D4: no deduction by silence), replacing the cost facts CO-3370 to CO-3375 each read as 0 when not stated. Verification pass V-1: the costs are deducted only when receipts for them have been received (self_employment_cost_receipts_received, CO-3927, read as false when not stated, the reading I.2-3 gives: credit card and bank statements are not receipts); otherwise nothing is deducted and the records are not read. Coverage review 2 N-9: 3.755.21.I.2.D (S3596) limits a rental property's allowable expenses to "the costs of maintenance of the property"; for self-employment from rental property a case stated its maintenance costs as business_cost_operating and no interest or vehicle costs (a statement rule, withdrawn by KL-CE-1 below). KL-CE-1 (coverage pass 7, R7-3; docs/reviews/known-limits.md, 2026-11-24): the item reads I.2.D itself. A cost record says which business it is of by its job, the job its business's receipts record states (earnings, CO-5100), and whether it is the property's maintenance by property_maintenance; a cost of a business whose receipts record states rental_property true is deducted only when it is maintenance (and its kind's row deducts it), a cost of any other business as before. The records are read in this order: whether any of the person's business receipts records is rental property (rental_property, required there: decision 4), then the cost's business (its job), then property_maintenance, so a person with no rental property states neither a cost's job nor property_maintenance, and a non-maintenance cost of rental property needs only its business named. Before, LEAP did not read rental_property and deducted every cost record of a deducted kind, so a rental business whose mortgage interest was stated as a cost record had it deducted (probe LRB1: $3,300, eligible, where I.2.D gives $3,900, ineligible), and the statement rule conflicted with CCCAP's, which asked for the costs as rental_property_expenses_paid (probe LRB3). One rental property is now stated once for both programs; what LEAP reads as maintenance is OQ-1516. Capital principal, depreciation, home space and the cost of providing a boarder's room or meals are not deducted (rows for the owner's signature, docs/reviews/earnings-e0.md, section 7). Coverage pass 5, L5-1 (docs/reviews/coverage5-care-energy.md): a business's stream (a record with neither a month nor a date) is read only in a month its job dates cover, from the month of job_start_date through the month of job_end_date, so a business that began after the full month prior to the application, or ended before it, has no income in it (3.755.21.I.1 as amended effective November 1, 2026, S2719: "total gross income received in the full month prior to the application date").

Type money, scope person-month, program LEAP.
Uses: `earnings`, `leap_earnings_treatment_table`, `self_employment_cost_receipts_received`.

```
if Receipts received for the self-employment costs, otherwise no
  then the sum of that receipt's amount for each receipt in Earnings where ((all of the following are true:;   - LEAP: how each kind of earnings is treated (table), for that receipt's kind is equal to deducted;   - all of the following are true:;     - that receipt is received in the month;     - any of the following is true:;       - it is not the case that that receipt's month is unknown;       - all of the following are true:; ### CO-2815 LEAP: homeless or in a non-traditional dwelling `@engine`
```

Whether the person is considered homeless or resides in a non-traditional dwelling, a living arrangement 9 CCR 2503-7 3.752.25.B.6 (S774) excludes from vulnerability to rising heating costs: read as having no fixed and regular nighttime residence of the household's own, or living in a shelter, a halfway house, a motel, hotel, trailer park or campground for lack of an alternative, a hospital the person was abandoned in, or a place not designed for sleeping.

Precision. LEAP's rule defines a non-traditional dwelling (3.751.1, S2303) as a structure providing housing that is not affixed to a permanent physical address, including cars, vans, buses, tents and lean-tos, which the place-not-designed-for-sleeping arrangement carries; it does not define "considered homeless" (OQ-561). This reading keeps the meaning the shared is_homeless had for LEAP: a fixed home that is substandard, and a stay in another household's home, are not counted, since the person then lives in a traditional dwelling. Coverage review C-2: a household that will imminently lose its home (an eviction notice) is not counted either. It still lives in its traditional dwelling, and 9 CCR 2503-7 3.751.1 (S3311) serves a client "responsible for heating costs that are included in rent" who "has received an eviction notice to vacate the premises within thirty (30) calendar days" as an emergency applicant, not as an excluded household; OQ-561's Assumption does not list it. Coverage review 2 N-4: 3.752.25.B.8 (S774) is the paragraph that speaks to hotels, and it keeps vulnerable a household that "has lived or will live in the hotel continuously for thirty (30) calendar days at the time of application and that heat is included in rent"; a household in a hotel for lack of an alternative that meets B.8 (residence_setting_type hotel and leap_living_arrangement, CO-1283, traditional_dwelling from its hotel branch) is therefore not read as homeless here (OQ-561).

Type yes/no, scope person, program LEAP.
Uses: `leap_living_arrangement`, `nighttime_residence_type`, `residence_setting_type`.

```
all of the following are true:
  - Nighttime residence type is one of: motel_or_hotel_for_lack_of_alternative, trailer_park_for_lack_of_alternative, campground_for_lack_of_alternative, emergency_or_transitional_shelter, halfway_house, abandoned_in_hospital, place_not_designed_for_sleeping
  - it is not the case that (all of the following are true:;   - Nighttime residence type is equal to motel_or_hotel_for_lack_of_alternative;   - Residence setting type is equal to hotel, otherwise no;   - LEAP living arrangement is equal to traditional_dwelling, otherwise no)
```

### CO-3912 LEAP: gross wages in the income verification period `@engine`

The gross pay the person actually received in LEAP's income verification period, "from the date of application to the same date of the prior month" (9 CCR 2503-7 3.751.1, S2712), from a job whose income "is terminated as of the application date" or that is "a new source of earned income as of the application date" (3.752.22.C.3.a-b, S2713: "use actual income received in the income verification period"): each earnings record (earnings, CO-5100) of a kind LEAP's counting table counts as pay (leap_earnings_treatment_table, CO-5102: wages, in-kind pay at its value and the other pay no paragraph of 3.752.23 excludes; not work-study, 3.752.23.P, or an employer's health insurance subsidy, HH), whose job began on or after the first day of the period or ended on or before the application date, and whose date falls in the period, less the part set aside under a Plan for Achieving Self-Support (3.752.23.DD).

Precision. Earned-income records, step E1 (LEAP; docs/reviews/records-earnings-care-energy.md): read from the earnings records by their dates, replacing wages_gross_received_prior_thirty_days (CO-3910), employment_began_or_ended_prior_thirty_days (CO-3923, read as false when not stated) and the month's wages_gross less work_study_earnings. The period runs from leap_income_verification_period_start (CO-5002) through leap_application_date, both days included, as LEAP's one-time receipts are placed (leap_one_time_receipts_in_period, CO-5009; OQ-886). A job "began" in the period when its record's job_start_date is on or after the period's first day, and "ended" when its job_end_date is on or before the application date (the job dates' when_absent: a record that states neither is ongoing pay, read by leap_ongoing_wage_streams and leap_ongoing_dated_wages, CO-5120 and CO-5121). A job that ended before the period has no pay in it and counts nothing: its income is terminated as of the application date. A record of such a job that states no date cannot be placed in the period, so the figure cannot be determined and the record's date is named as missing (decision 4 of 2026-11-23). Senior Community Service Employment Program pay is read by leap_scsep_wages (CO-5122), which applies the age test of 3.752.23.CC outside the sum. The set-aside part is no more than the pay it is part of. Coverage pass 6 for LEAP, R6-1 (docs/reviews/coverage6-care-energy.md): a record stated as a stream (no date) whose job ended before the income verification period's first day, or begins after the application date, is not read: the job paid nothing in the period (3.752.22.C.3.a, "use actual income received in the income verification period"; C.3.c, "If a household member has not received his/her first check from this source of income as of the income verification period, do not count any income from this source", S2713), as leap_counted_recurring_receipts (CO-5003) reads a receipt stream since L5-1. A dated pay is read by its date, so a last paycheck received in the period after the job ended is counted. Before, such a stream was selected as a job that ended or began and its missing date made the figure cannot determine.

Type money, scope person-month, program LEAP.
Uses: `earnings`, `leap_application_date`, `leap_earnings_treatment_table`, `leap_income_verification_period_start`.

```
    all of the following are true:

        - LEAP: how each kind of earnings is treated (table), for that receipt's kind is one of: counted, counted_no_rule_excludes, counted_at_value
        - all of the following are true:
          - LEAP: how each kind of earnings is treated (table), for that receipt's kind is equal to counted_unless_foster_care
```

### CO-3925 LEAP: a person's monthly wages `@engine`

This person's gross monthly earned income other than self-employment for LEAP (9 CCR 2503-7 3.752.22.B-C): for each job that began in the income verification period or ended on or before the application date, the pay actually received in the period (C.3.a-b; leap_wages_in_income_verification_period, CO-3912); for every other job, its earned ongoing income from the eight weeks before the application date, one pay converted by the job's pay schedule (four weekly, two bi-weekly, two semi-monthly, one monthly amount; leap_ongoing_wage_streams, CO-5120, for a pay stated as a stream; leap_ongoing_dated_wages, CO-5121, the average of the pays dated in the eight weeks); with the declared value of in-kind pay (C.4); without the pay 3.752.23 excludes (work-study, P; an employer's health insurance subsidy paid to the person, HH; payments an employer makes to others, T), and without the Senior Community Service Employment Program pay of a person fifty-five or older (CC; leap_scsep_wages, CO-5122); each pay less its part set aside under a Plan for Achieving Self-Support (DD).

Precision. Earned-income records, step E1 (LEAP; docs/reviews/records-earnings-care-energy.md): read from the earnings records (earnings, CO-5100) through leap_earnings_treatment_table (CO-5102), replacing wages_pay_frequency and wages_gross_per_pay_period (CO-3921, CO-3922: one schedule per person), employment_began_or_ended_prior_thirty_days (CO-3923, read as false when not stated), scsep_wages (CO-4504), employer_health_insurance_subsidy_received (CO-4505) and in_kind_compensation_value (CO-4506), each read as 0 when not stated, and pass_set_aside_earned_income (CO-4618), which leap_household_income (CO-1002) subtracted. Each record is one pay or one stream of a job's pay, disjoint from the others, so nothing is subtracted from a total it was part of. Whether a job began or ended is read from the record's job dates (job_start_date on or after leap_income_verification_period_start, CO-5002; job_end_date on or before leap_application_date); a record that states neither is ongoing pay. The SCSEP age is the person's age on the application date (leap_age_on_application_date, CO-6400; 3.752.2, coverage pass 4 L4-4), compared with leap_scsep_exclusion_min_age (CO-4510), and read only when the person has SCSEP pay. leap_household_income (CO-1002) excludes the earned income of a child under eighteen residing with a parent or guardian (3.752.23.Q, leap_earnings_are_excluded_as_child, CO-5123). The readings of the period and of "any four weeks of the eight" are OQ-681's; the frequencies 3.752.22.C does not convert, OQ-1160; two jobs on one schedule stated as dated pays are averaged together until a record can name its job (CO-5121; request R-2 in docs/reviews/records-earnings-care-energy.md).

Type money, scope person-month, program LEAP.
Uses: `leap_age_on_application_date`, `leap_ongoing_dated_wages`, `leap_ongoing_wage_streams`, `leap_scsep_exclusion_min_age`, `leap_scsep_wages`, `leap_wages_in_income_verification_period`.

```
LEAP: gross wages in the income verification period plus LEAP: ongoing pay stated as streams, converted to a month plus LEAP: ongoing pay stated as dated pays, averaged and converted to a month plus (if LEAP: a person's Senior Community Service Employment Program pay is equal to 0;   then 0; else if LEAP: age on the application date is less than LEAP: age from which SCSEP funds are excluded (55);   then LEAP: a person's Senior Community Service Employment Program pay; otherwise 0)
```

### CO-3926 LEAP: a person's countable unearned income `@engine`

This person's countable unearned income for LEAP (9 CCR 2503-7 3.752.21-23): the counted recurring receipts of the month, or of the income verification period for a receipt stated with its date, one month's income (3.752.22.A, C.3; leap_counted_recurring_receipts) with the AmeriCorps payments at or above the minimum wage (3.752.23.F; leap_counted_service_payments), and Social Security without its cents (3.752.211.H), less the parts set aside under a PASS or paid for a workers' compensation claim's expenses (3.752.23.DD, 3.752.211.D), not below zero; plus SSI without its cents (3.752.21.I); plus Colorado Works and Adult Financial cash assistance (3.752.21.L); plus the counted one-time receipts of the income verification period (3.752.21.A, C, D, 3.752.22.A); plus payments from boarders, "payments from any other source, which is considered to be a gain or benefit" (3.752.21; leap_boarder_payments). What LEAP counts or excludes, kind by kind, is its counting tables (leap_receipt_treatment_table; for boarders, leap_earnings_treatment_table).

Precision. Receipt records, migration phase 1 (docs/reviews/receipts-migration-1.md): read from the receipts (CO-5000), replacing unearned_income_prior_thirty_days (CO-3913, which CCCAP still reads), leap_excluded_unearned_income (CO-4511), leap_person_one_time_income (CO-4069), leap_excluded_source_receipts (CO-4961) and leap_excluded_receipts_in_lump_sum (CO-4962), and the facts they read. Coverage review 3 F3-1: the set-aside parts are subtracted from the recurring receipts and Social Security together, because income set aside under a PASS is most often Social Security disability income. SSI is counted "in the month received" (3.752.21.I) and the recurring receipts are read for the month of the application, the month leap_household_income (CO-1002) is read for (OQ-681). The recurring income includes family and medical leave insurance (FAMLI) benefits (3.752.211.J, as amended effective November 1, 2026) and a military allotment received for a member (3.752.212), stated as receipts of the kind that names their source. The cents are dropped by rounding down. Earned-income records, step E1 (LEAP; finding E1-L2): payments from boarders are earnings records (earnings, CO-5100; design 2.3), counted here at their gross by leap_boarder_payments (CO-5124), for room and board as for a room or meals only, which the receipts counted before (their receipt rows read counted_in_earnings now); a person whose earnings are not stated has unearned income that cannot be determined, since a boarder's payments may be among them (decision 4 of 2026-11-23). Coverage pass 6 for LEAP, R6-6: the part of another person's veterans benefit paid for this person, when that person is outside this person's LEAP household, is this person's unearned income (leap_dependent_part_of_awards_to_others, CO-7253; 3.752.211.E).

### CO-4515 LEAP: the closing date of the application period `@engine`

The last day of the LEAP application period of the program year that begins on or before the date the application was filed: April 30, or, when April 30 falls on a weekend or holiday, the next business day (9 CCR 2503-7 3.751.1 "Eligibility Period", 3.752.1).

Precision. The program year is the one starting in the most recent November (leap_eligibility_period_start_month, CO-1806) on or before leap_application_filing_date (CO-4514); its April (leap_eligibility_period_end_month, CO-1807) is the first April within eleven months after it, and April 30 is the day before the first of May. The extension is leap_application_period_extension_days_table (CO-4513) for the year of that April. For a filing date from November to April this is the coming April 30 (or its extension); for one from May to October it is the April 30 just past.

### CO-4517 LEAP: the program year the application is for `@engine`

The November that begins the LEAP program year the application is for (9 CCR 2503-7 3.751.1 "Program Year", 3.752.1): the program year in whose application period it was received or postmarked; for an application filed after that period closed and before November 1, the program year that begins the next November 1, the only one for which 3.752.1 lets it take effect ("Such applications received prior to November 1st shall be accepted ... however, eligibility shall not be effective until November 1st").

Precision. The most recent November (leap_eligibility_period_start_month, CO-1806) on or before leap_application_filing_date (CO-4514) when the application is within that program year's application period (leap_application_is_within_application_period, CO-4516); otherwise the November twelve months after it. Whether an application filed before November 1 is accepted at all is leap_is_eligible's test (CO-1007): only a public assistance household's is.

### CO-4518 LEAP: a public assistance household `@engine`

Whether this person's LEAP household is a public assistance household whose application 9 CCR 2503-7 3.752.1 accepts before November 1 ("public assistance households (such as Colorado Works, Old Age Pension (OAP), Aid to the Needy Disabled (AND), Aid to the Blind (AB), and Supplemental Social Security Disability Benefits.)"): a member of the household receives Colorado Works basic cash assistance, an Adult Financial grant (Old Age Pension or Aid to the Needy Disabled), Supplemental Security Income, or Social Security disability insurance benefits on the member's own record.

Precision. Reads the members of leap_household_members_for_income (CO-1009, the economic unit, a member excluded for status included, since the list names the household's receipt) and their receipt records: receives_tanf_cash (CO-013), an Adult Financial grant received in the month (a receipt of kind adult_financial_cash, other than a retroactive lump sum; receipts, CO-5000), receives_ssi (CO-012) and title_ii_benefit_type own_disability (CO-2821). The Adult Financial grant is read from the member's receipts with no default: 3.752.1 names the households and gives no reading for a grant not reported (decision 4 of 2026-11-23 (docs/plan-colorado.md): missing information is cannot determine unless the rule says otherwise; the phase-1 default of 0 is removed), so a member whose receipts are not stated and who meets none of the other tests leaves the household cannot determine; a stated empty list is no grant. leap_is_eligible (CO-1007) reads it in the month of the application date. OQ-800: "Supplemental Social Security Disability Benefits" is read as both SSI and SSDI; Aid to the Blind has no receipt fact of its own in this volume (adult_financial_cash_income names OAP and AND), and Non-Categorical Refugee Assistance, which 3.751.1's "Public Assistance Income" lists but 3.752.1 does not, has none either. Coverage pass 4 X4-1 (docs/reviews/coverage4-care-energy.md): receives_tanf_cash, receives_ssi and title_ii_benefit_type are no longer read as not received when not stated: 3.752.1 names the public assistance households and gives no reading for a receipt not reported, so a member who meets none of the tests stated and leaves one of them unstated makes the household cannot determine (decision 4 of 2026-11-23), as the Adult Financial grant already did; a member shown to receive any of them still decides it. Coverage pass 5, L5-1 (docs/reviews/coverage5-care-energy.md): a stream of grant payments (a receipt with neither a month nor a date) is read only in a month its start_date and end_date cover, so a grant that ended before the application month is not received in it.

```
    - (the sum of that receipt's amount for each receipt in that person's Receipts where ((all of the following are true:;   - that receipt's kind is equal to adult_financial_cash;   - it is not the case that that receipt's retroactive;   - all of the following are true:;     - that receipt is received in the month;     - any of the following is true:;       - it is not the case that that receipt's month is unknown;       - all of the following are true:;         - any of the following is true:;           - that receipt's start date is unknown;           - the month containing that receipt's start date is at most the month;         - any of the following is true:;           - that receipt's end date is unknown;           - the month containing that receipt's end date is at least the month))) is more than 0
```

### CO-4526 LEAP: requires verification of unearned income `@engine`

Whether the person's unearned income must be verified for LEAP by documents or an electronic source (9 CCR 2503-7 3.755.11, 3.755.21.A-C): the person has countable unearned income beyond what the applicant's declaration verifies, which is gift income (3.755.21.K) and, when the applicant has provided court evidence of domestic violence or takes part in the Address Confidentiality Program, child support (3.755.21.B.4).

Precision. leap_person_unearned_income (CO-3926) less the gift receipts and, where has_domestic_violence_court_evidence_or_acp_participation (CO-4525) is true for the person (read as false when not stated), the child support receipts it counts, is more than zero (receipts, CO-5000; migration phase 1). Coverage pass 5, L5-6 (docs/reviews/coverage5-care-energy.md): the declared parts are taken exactly as CO-3926 counts them: recurring receipts by leap_counted_recurring_receipts' placement and value (CO-5003: by date in the income verification period, a stream by its source's dates) and receipts paid once by leap_one_time_receipts_in_period's (CO-5009), so a one-time gift or weekly gifts dated in the period are verified by the applicant's declaration (3.755.21.K, S3313: "Gift income shall be considered verified with applicant declaration"; B.4) as the month's recurring gifts were (review households LG1 and LG2: before, verification required; now not). Before, only the month's recurring receipts were taken off (OQ-681). Coverage pass 6 for LEAP, R6-2 (docs/reviews/coverage6-care-energy.md): the share test of 3.752.21.F is applied once per property in the household: a record of jointly owned property whose co-owner is another member of the household (the receipt's co_owner, in leap_household_members_for_income, CO-1009) counts what the person received, since what the property paid the co-owner is counted on the co-owner's own list and the household's income from the property is what its members received; the share is the floor only against owners outside the household (OQ-1316). Before, each co-owner took the larger of the share and the amount on the own list, so a co-owner who received nothing still added a share the other had received.

### CO-5002 LEAP: the first day of the income verification period `@engine`

The first day of the income verification period (9 CCR 2503-7 3.751.1: "from the date of application to the same date of the prior month"): the application date less the number of days in the month before the application month.

Precision. For an application on the 29th to the 31st of a month whose preceding month is shorter, the same date of the prior month does not exist; the result is then a day or two into the application month (the application date less the days of the shorter month), OQ-886.

Type calendar date, scope case, program LEAP.
Uses: `leap_application_date`.

```
0 minus (the number of days from the first day of the month before the month containing LEAP application date to the first day of the month containing LEAP application date) days after LEAP application date
```


### CO-5003 LEAP: a person's counted recurring receipts `@engine`

The person's recurring receipts of the month that LEAP's counting table counts (leap_receipt_treatment_table: counted, or counted because no rule excludes it), at the amount received in the month, or, for a receipt stated with its date, received in the income verification period after its first day through the application date: one month's income (9 CCR 2503-7 3.752.22.A), other than Social Security and SSI (each counted without its cents) and Colorado Works and Adult Financial cash assistance (leap_cash_assistance_receipts). Each is less the part received for a person who does not live with the person (3.752.212, S3306: a military allotment is income "for those individuals included in the budget unit"; 3.752.211.E, S4043: the part of a VA pension paid for a dependent is "countable unearned income to the dependent rather than the veteran") and the part of insurance or injury proceeds spent or to be spent on the costs they cover (3.752.21.C-D); income from jointly owned property at the larger of the owner's share of the property's income and the amount received (3.752.21.F, S4850).

Precision. A receipt is recurring when it is not paid once; it is received in the month when it states the month, or states none (it recurs in every month). Read for the month of the application (leap_household_income, CO-1002). Replaces unearned_income_prior_thirty_days (CO-3913) for LEAP: the thirty-day figure the case could state is not restated, since 3.752.22.A caps the period's unearned income at one month's income. Coverage pass 4 L4-3 (docs/reviews/coverage4-care-energy.md): a recurring receipt stated with its date is read by its date in the income verification period (9 CCR 2503-7 3.752.22.A: "received in the income verification period, not to exceed one month's income"; C.3.a, C.3.c), after the period's first day (leap_income_verification_period_start, CO-5002) through the application date (leap_application_date), not by the calendar month: the period is then one month long, so a monthly source paid on the application date's day of the month is counted once (the cap of A; OQ-681); a receipt stated without a date is read in the month, as before. Coverage pass 5, L5-1 (docs/reviews/coverage5-care-energy.md): a recurring receipt stated with neither a month nor a date (a stream) is read in the month of the application only when its source ran through the whole income verification period (its start_date before the period's first day or not stated, its end_date after the application date or not stated); it is not counted when its end_date is before the period's first day (3.752.22.C.3.a: "use actual income received in the income verification period", none) or its start_date is after the application date (C.3.c: "If a household member has not received his/her first check from this source of income as of the income verification period, do not count any income from this source", S2713); and a source that began or ended in the period is read from its dated receipts (C.3.a, C.3.c), so a stream without them cannot determine and the record's date is named as missing, as leap_wages_in_income_verification_period (CO-3912) reads a job that began or ended (OQ-681 (4)). Coverage pass 5 (docs/reviews/coverage5-care-energy.md): L5-2, the record's for_person_living_elsewhere is taken off: the part of an allotment or a VA award paid for a child living with a former spouse is not the household's (review households LM1 and LM2, CO-801 and CO-802). A VA dependent living with the veteran is a member of the veteran's household (3.751.1 "Household", S1400: "living together as one economic unit"; 3.751.2.D, a spouse and a child under eighteen cannot be a separate household), so the dependent's part (for_dependent) is the household's income either way and is not read; a dependent who lives elsewhere and is not a person of the case is the part for_person_living_elsewhere states, and a dependent who is a person of the case is named in for_person and taken off from for_dependent when not in this person's LEAP household (R6-6, below), wherever the dependent lives (coverage verification 7, V7-2: the statement of the receipts' meanings, CO-5000; R7-4 had stated every dependent's part in for_dependent alone, so the part of a dependent outside the case was counted as the veteran's, L4-D: $4,000, ineligible, where 3,000 + 700 = $3,700 is eligible). X5-1: a record stating ownership_share and property_income counts the larger of the share of the property's income and the amount received (OQ-1316). Field sweep (docs/reviews/field-sweep-care-energy.md): proceeds paid as a recurring receipt are counted less spent_on_covered_costs (3.752.21.C-D, S3303), as a one-time payment is. None below zero. Coverage pass 6 for LEAP, R6-2 (docs/reviews/coverage6-care-energy.md): the share test of 3.752.21.F is applied once per property in the household: a record of jointly owned property whose co-owner is another member of the household (the receipt's co_owner, in leap_household_members_for_income, CO-1009) counts what the person received, since what the property paid the co-owner is counted on the co-owner's own list and the household's income from the property is what its members received; the share is the floor only against owners outside the household (OQ-1316). Before, each co-owner took the larger of the share and the amount on the own list, so a co-owner who received nothing still added a share the other had received. Coverage pass 6 for LEAP, R6-6 (docs/reviews/coverage6-care-energy.md): the part of a veterans benefit paid for a dependent who is a person of the case (for_dependent, for_person) and not in this person's LEAP household (an adult dependent in the same dwelling who buys heat apart, 3.751.2.B-D) is taken off: 3.752.211.E, "Any portion of a VA pension that is paid to a veteran for support of a dependent shall be considered countable unearned income to the dependent rather than the veteran"; the dependent's household counts it (leap_dependent_part_of_awards_to_others, CO-7253). A dependent in this person's household is counted here, in the household's income, as before (L5-2).

Type money, scope person-month, program LEAP.
Uses: `leap_application_date`, `leap_household_members_for_income`, `leap_income_verification_period_start`, `leap_receipt_treatment_table`, `receipts`.

```
the sum for each receipt in Receipts where
    all of the following are true:
      - it is not the case that that receipt's frequency is equal to once
      - if it is not the case that that receipt's month is unknown
        then (if that receipt's date is unknown;   then that receipt is received in the month; otherwise (all of the following are true:;   - that receipt's date is more than LEAP: the first day of the income verification period;   - that receipt's date is at most LEAP application date))
      else if any of the following is true:
          - all of the following are true:
            - it is not the case that that receipt's end date is unknown
            - that receipt's end date is less than LEAP: the first day of the income verification period
          - all of the following are true:
            - it is not the case that that receipt's start date is unknown
            - that receipt's start date is more than LEAP application date
        then no
      else if all of the following are true:
          - any of the following is true:
            - that receipt's start date is unknown
            - that receipt's start date is less than LEAP: the first day of the income verification period
          - any of the following is true:
            - that receipt's end date is unknown
            - that receipt's end date is more than LEAP application date
        then (if that receipt's date is unknown;   then that receipt is received in the month; otherwise (all of the following are true:;   - that receipt's date is more than LEAP: the first day of the income verification period;   - that receipt's date is at most LEAP application date))
      otherwise (all of the following are true:;   - that receipt's date is more than LEAP: the first day of the income verification period;   - that receipt's date is at most LEAP application date)
      - LEAP: how each kind of receipt is treated (table), for that receipt's kind is one of: counted, counted_no_rule_excludes
      - it is not the case that that receipt's kind is one of: social_security, ssi, colorado_works_cash, adult_financial_cash
  of
    the greater of 0 and ((if that receipt's ownership share is unknown;   then that receipt's amount; else if all of the following are true:;     - it is not the case that that receipt's co owner is unknown;     - that receipt's co owner is in that receipt's owner's LEAP: household members for income;   then that receipt's amount; otherwise the greater of that receipt's amount and (that receipt's ownership share times that receipt's property income)) minus (that receipt's for person living elsewhere plus that receipt's spent on covered costs plus (if all of the following are true:;     - it is not the case that that receipt's for person is unknown;     - it is not the case that that receipt's for person is in that receipt's owner's LEAP: household members for income;   then that receipt's for dependent; otherwise 0)))
```

### CO-5004 LEAP: a person's counted service payments `@engine`

The person's recurring AmeriCorps payments of the month that LEAP counts: those whose amount for the hours served is at or above the minimum wage (colorado_minimum_wage); payments below it are excluded (9 CCR 2503-7 3.752.23.F).

Precision. The hours served are a field of the receipt (hours_served), with no default: payments whose hours are not stated cannot be placed above or below the wage, so the result is unknown (decision 4 of 2026-11-23; before receipt records the payments were counted when the hours were not stated). OQ-781 (resolved) reads the minimum wage as the statewide wage. Coverage pass 4 L4-3 (docs/reviews/coverage4-care-energy.md): a recurring receipt stated with its date is read by its date in the income verification period (9 CCR 2503-7 3.752.22.A: "received in the income verification period, not to exceed one month's income"; C.3.a, C.3.c), after the period's first day (leap_income_verification_period_start, CO-5002) through the application date (leap_application_date), not by the calendar month: the period is then one month long, so a monthly source paid on the application date's day of the month is counted once (the cap of A; OQ-681); a receipt stated without a date is read in the month, as before. Coverage pass 5, L5-1 (docs/reviews/coverage5-care-energy.md): a recurring receipt stated with neither a month nor a date (a stream) is read in the month of the application only when its source ran through the whole income verification period (its start_date before the period's first day or not stated, its end_date after the application date or not stated); it is not counted when its end_date is before the period's first day (3.752.22.C.3.a: "use actual income received in the income verification period", none) or its start_date is after the application date (C.3.c: "If a household member has not received his/her first check from this source of income as of the income verification period, do not count any income from this source", S2713); and a source that began or ended in the period is read from its dated receipts (C.3.a, C.3.c), so a stream without them cannot determine and the record's date is named as missing, as leap_wages_in_income_verification_period (CO-3912) reads a job that began or ended (OQ-681 (4)).

### CO-5005 LEAP: a person's Social Security without its cents `@engine`

The person's recurring Social Security receipts of the month, without their cents (9 CCR 2503-7 3.752.211.H: "When determining income, do not consider cents in the gross income amount").

Precision. Each receipt's amount rounded down to the whole dollar, then the month's receipts added. A retroactive lump-sum payment is not recurring and 3.752.23.EE excludes it. Coverage pass 4 L4-3 (docs/reviews/coverage4-care-energy.md): a recurring receipt stated with its date is read by its date in the income verification period (9 CCR 2503-7 3.752.22.A: "received in the income verification period, not to exceed one month's income"; C.3.a, C.3.c), after the period's first day (leap_income_verification_period_start, CO-5002) through the application date (leap_application_date), not by the calendar month: the period is then one month long, so a monthly source paid on the application date's day of the month is counted once (the cap of A; OQ-681); a receipt stated without a date is read in the month, as before. Coverage pass 5, L5-1 (docs/reviews/coverage5-care-energy.md): a recurring receipt stated with neither a month nor a date (a stream) is read in the month of the application only when its source ran through the whole income verification period (its start_date before the period's first day or not stated, its end_date after the application date or not stated); it is not counted when its end_date is before the period's first day (3.752.22.C.3.a: "use actual income received in the income verification period", none) or its start_date is after the application date (C.3.c: "If a household member has not received his/her first check from this source of income as of the income verification period, do not count any income from this source", S2713); and a source that began or ended in the period is read from its dated receipts (C.3.a, C.3.c), so a stream without them cannot determine and the record's date is named as missing, as leap_wages_in_income_verification_period (CO-3912) reads a job that began or ended (OQ-681 (4)). Coverage pass 6 for LEAP, R6-7 (docs/reviews/coverage6-care-energy.md): the cents are dropped from each benefit amount, as 3.752.21.I and 3.752.211.H-I say ("do not consider cents in the gross benefit amount"), each record's amount rounded down to the whole dollar before the month's receipts are added; before, the sum was rounded down, so two amounts of $500.60 and $300.70 counted $801 rather than $800.

### CO-5006 LEAP: a person's SSI without its cents `@engine`

The person's recurring SSI receipts of the month, counted in the month received and without their cents (9 CCR 2503-7 3.752.21.I).

Precision. Each receipt's amount rounded down to the whole dollar, then the month's receipts added. Coverage pass 4 L4-3 (docs/reviews/coverage4-care-energy.md): a recurring receipt stated with its date is read by its date in the income verification period (9 CCR 2503-7 3.752.22.A: "received in the income verification period, not to exceed one month's income"; C.3.a, C.3.c), after the period's first day (leap_income_verification_period_start, CO-5002) through the application date (leap_application_date), not by the calendar month: the period is then one month long, so a monthly source paid on the application date's day of the month is counted once (the cap of A; OQ-681); a receipt stated without a date is read in the month, as before. Coverage pass 5, L5-1 (docs/reviews/coverage5-care-energy.md): a recurring receipt stated with neither a month nor a date (a stream) is read in the month of the application only when its source ran through the whole income verification period (its start_date before the period's first day or not stated, its end_date after the application date or not stated); it is not counted when its end_date is before the period's first day (3.752.22.C.3.a: "use actual income received in the income verification period", none) or its start_date is after the application date (C.3.c: "If a household member has not received his/her first check from this source of income as of the income verification period, do not count any income from this source", S2713); and a source that began or ended in the period is read from its dated receipts (C.3.a, C.3.c), so a stream without them cannot determine and the record's date is named as missing, as leap_wages_in_income_verification_period (CO-3912) reads a job that began or ended (OQ-681 (4)). Coverage pass 6 for LEAP, R6-7 (docs/reviews/coverage6-care-energy.md): the cents are dropped from each benefit amount, as 3.752.21.I and 3.752.211.H-I say ("do not consider cents in the gross benefit amount"), each record's amount rounded down to the whole dollar before the month's receipts are added; before, the sum was rounded down, so two amounts of $500.60 and $300.70 counted $801 rather than $800.

### CO-5009 LEAP: a person's one-time receipts in the income verification period `@engine`

The person's receipts paid once that LEAP's counting table counts (inheritances, gifts, prizes and lottery winnings, insurance and injury proceeds: 9 CCR 2503-7 3.752.21.A, C, D) received in the income verification period, from the same date of the month before the application date through the application date (3.751.1, 3.752.22.A), other than a retroactive lump-sum Social Security, SSI or public assistance payment (3.752.23.EE); less the part of insurance or injury proceeds spent or to be spent on the costs they cover (3.752.21.C-D) and the claim expenses a one-time workers' compensation award includes (3.752.211.D). Each is less the part received for a person who does not live with the person (3.752.212, 3.752.211.E); income from jointly owned property at the larger of the owner's share of the property's income and the amount received (3.752.21.F).

Precision. A receipt is placed by its month first: one received in a month before the month the period starts in, or after the application month, is outside; one received in the month before or the month of the application needs its date, and without it the result is unknown (the record's date is named as missing). A one-time receipt of a kind the table excludes is never asked for its date (before receipt records LEAP could not determine its income when such a payment was stated without the thirty-day facts). Replaces leap_person_one_time_income (CO-4069) with its thirty-day facts and the placement items CO-4961 and CO-4962. Coverage pass 5 (docs/reviews/coverage5-care-energy.md): L5-3, 3.752.23.EE (S2208) excludes "retroactive lump-sum social security, SSI, and public assistance payments", so only a retroactive payment of kind social_security, ssi, colorado_works_cash or adult_financial_cash (the public assistance income 3.751.1 defines, S3309: Colorado Works, OAP, AND, AB) is left out; any other retroactive payment received in the period (back pay of unemployment, workers' compensation, a pension or a VA award) is counted as received under 3.752.22.A (review household LR1, CO-800: $800 of retroactive unemployment counted). Whether a county's general or emergency assistance is "public assistance" for EE is OQ-1320. L5-2: less for_person_living_elsewhere, as leap_counted_recurring_receipts (CO-5003) reads it. X5-1: the share of jointly owned property's income (OQ-1316). The value is not below zero. Field sweep (docs/reviews/field-sweep-care-energy.md): the part of a one-time receipt set aside under a Plan for Achieving Self-Support is left out (3.752.23.DD, S3301: "Income that is deemed necessary for the fulfillment of a Plan for Achieving Self-Support"), as the recurring receipts' part is (leap_receipts_set_aside, CO-5008). Coverage pass 6 for LEAP, R6-2 (docs/reviews/coverage6-care-energy.md): the share test of 3.752.21.F is applied once per property in the household: a record of jointly owned property whose co-owner is another member of the household (the receipt's co_owner, in leap_household_members_for_income, CO-1009) counts what the person received, since what the property paid the co-owner is counted on the co-owner's own list and the household's income from the property is what its members received; the share is the floor only against owners outside the household (OQ-1316). Before, each co-owner took the larger of the share and the amount on the own list, so a co-owner who received nothing still added a share the other had received.

Type money, scope person, program LEAP.
Uses: `leap_application_date`, `leap_household_members_for_income`, `leap_income_verification_period_start`, `leap_receipt_treatment_table`, `receipts`.

```
the sum for each receipt in Receipts where
    all of the following are true:
      - that receipt's frequency is equal to once
      - it is not the case that (all of the following are true:;   - that receipt's retroactive;   - that receipt's kind is one of: social_security, ssi, colorado_works_cash, adult_financial_cash)
      - LEAP: how each kind of receipt is treated (table), for that receipt's kind is one of: counted, counted_no_rule_excludes
      - if any of the following is true:
          - that receipt's month is less than the month containing LEAP: the first day of the income verification period
          - that receipt's month is more than the month containing LEAP application date
        then no
      otherwise (all of the following are true:;   - that receipt's date is at least LEAP: the first day of the income verification period;   - that receipt's date is at most LEAP application date)
  of
    the greater of 0 and ((if that receipt's ownership share is unknown;   then that receipt's amount; else if all of the following are true:;     - it is not the case that that receipt's co owner is unknown;     - that receipt's co owner is in that receipt's owner's LEAP: household members for income;   then that receipt's amount; otherwise the greater of that receipt's amount and (that receipt's ownership share times that receipt's property income)) minus (that receipt's spent on covered costs plus that receipt's claim expense plus that receipt's for person living elsewhere plus that receipt's pass set aside))
```

### CO-5120 LEAP: ongoing pay stated as streams, converted to a month `@engine`

The person's earned ongoing income (9 CCR 2503-7 3.752.22.B, S2713) from the earnings records (earnings, CO-5100) that state a job's pay as a stream (no pay date) and whose kind LEAP's counting table counts as pay (leap_earnings_treatment_table, CO-5102: wages and the other pay no paragraph of 3.752.23 excludes, and in-kind pay at its declared value, 3.752.22.C.4), converted to a month as 3.752.22.C does for a household member "paid less than monthly": four gross weekly amounts (C.1.a), two bi-weekly amounts (C.1.b) or two semi-monthly amounts (C.2), the amount of one pay being the record's per_payment; for pay made monthly, or less often, the amount the record states for the month; less the part set aside under a Plan for Achieving Self-Support (3.752.23.DD). A job that began in the income verification period or ended on or before the application date is read by its pays in the period instead (leap_wages_in_income_verification_period, CO-3912).

Precision. Earned-income records, step E1 (LEAP): replaces the person's one pay schedule (wages_pay_frequency, CO-3921, and wages_gross_per_pay_period, CO-3922), so each job is converted by its own schedule and two jobs are statable. The number of pays is leap_pay_periods_per_month (CO-3924). A stream recurs in every month (its month's when_absent) unless it states a month, and is read in the month determined (leap_household_income, CO-1002, reads the month of the application). A monthly stream's month is its amount; when it states only the amount of one pay (per_payment), that pay is the month's (one monthly pay is the month's income). A weekly, bi-weekly or semi-monthly stream with no per_payment cannot be converted, and the per_payment is named as missing. A stream of a frequency 3.752.22.C does not convert (once, every other month, quarterly, twice a year, annually) is counted at the amount it states for the month (OQ-1160). The set-aside of a converted stream is the month's and is taken off the converted pay, not below zero. Senior Community Service Employment Program pay is leap_scsep_wages (CO-5122).

Type money, scope person-month, program LEAP.
Uses: `earnings`, `leap_application_date`, `leap_earnings_treatment_table`, `leap_income_verification_period_start`, `leap_pay_periods_per_month`.

```
the sum for each receipt in Earnings where
    all of the following are true:
      - any of the following is true:
        - LEAP: how each kind of earnings is treated (table), for that receipt's kind is one of: counted, counted_no_rule_excludes, counted_at_value
```
