### CO-5121 LEAP: ongoing pay stated as dated pays, averaged and converted to a month `@engine`

The person's earned ongoing income (9 CCR 2503-7 3.752.22.B, S2713: "the countable gross income in any four (4) weeks of the eight (8) weeks prior to the application date") from the earnings records (earnings, CO-5100) that state a pay with its date, of a kind LEAP's counting table counts as pay (leap_earnings_treatment_table, CO-5102), from a job that neither began in the income verification period nor ended on or before the application date: for each job (the record's job) paid on a schedule 3.752.22.C converts, the average of that job's pays dated in the eight weeks before the application date, each less the part set aside under a Plan for Achieving Self-Support (3.752.23.DD) and times the number of pays C adds for its schedule (four weekly, two bi-weekly, two semi-monthly, one monthly), the jobs added together; and the pays of a frequency C does not convert received in the income verification period.

Precision. Earned-income records, step E1 (LEAP). The eight weeks are the leap_earned_ongoing_income_weeks (CO-5125) times seven days before leap_application_date (CO-2122), the application date itself not included ("prior to the application date"). "Any four (4) weeks of the eight (8)" is read, as before the records, as the average pay of the pays stated in the eight weeks times the number of pays C adds (OQ-681), which equals any four weeks when the pay is regular and lets a case state four weeks of pay stubs (3.755.21.D) or all eight. The average is taken over the pays of one job (the record's job, job_1 to job_6; coverage pass 4 L4-1: two jobs paid weekly are each four weekly amounts, C.1.a, not one average of both), each pay converted by its own frequency before averaging, so a job whose pays all share a schedule gives its average pay times the pays C adds. A dated pay names its job and states its frequency (CO-5100: job is required, and frequency is required on a dated record, coverage pass 4 L4-2, OQ-1181 resolved): a pay in the eight weeks that states neither is cannot determine, naming the field, never a monthly pay of one pooled job. A pay dated before the eight weeks, or on or after the application date, is not read. A pay of another frequency (once, every other month, quarterly, twice a year, annually) is counted at its amount when received in the income verification period (leap_income_verification_period_start, CO-5002, through the application date), as LEAP counts income received once (3.752.22.A; OQ-1160). Pay of a job that began or ended is leap_wages_in_income_verification_period (CO-3912); Senior Community Service Employment Program pay is leap_scsep_wages (CO-5122).

Type money, scope person-month, program LEAP.
Uses: `earnings`, `leap_application_date`, `leap_earned_ongoing_income_weeks`, `leap_earnings_treatment_table`, `leap_income_verification_period_start`, `leap_pay_periods_per_month`.

    - that receipt's date is less than LEAP application date;   - that receipt's frequency is one of: weekly, biweekly, semimonthly, monthly;   - that receipt's job is equal to job_6))); otherwise 0) plus (the sum of (that receipt's amount minus (the lesser of that receipt's pass set aside and that receipt's amount)) for each receipt in Earnings where ((all of the following are true:;   - any of the following is true:;     - LEAP: how each kind of earnings is treated (table), for that receipt's kind is one of: counted, counted_no_rule_excludes, counted_at_value;     - all of the following are true:;       - LEAP: how each kind of earnings is treated (table), for that receipt's kind is equal to counted_unless_foster_care;       - it is not the case that that receipt's foster care;   - it is not the case that (any of the following is true:;   - if that receipt's job start date is unknown;     then no;   otherwise that receipt's job start date is at least LEAP: the first day of the income verification period;   - if that receipt's job end date is unknown;     then no;   otherwise that receipt's job end date is at most LEAP application date);   - it is not the case that that receipt's date is unknown;   - all of the following are true:;     - that receipt's date is at least LEAP: the first day of the income verification period;     - that receipt's date is at most LEAP application date;   - it is not the case that that receipt's frequency is one of: weekly, biweekly, semimonthly, monthly)))

### CO-5122 LEAP: a person's Senior Community Service Employment Program pay `@engine`

The person's pay for community service employment under the Senior Community Service Employment Program (Title V of the Older Americans Act), the earnings records (earnings, CO-5100) of kind scsep_employment, made monthly as LEAP makes every pay monthly: the pays actually received in the income verification period from a job that began in it or ended on or before the application date (9 CCR 2503-7 3.752.22.C.3); for ongoing pay stated as a stream, the pay converted by its schedule (3.752.22.C.1-2); for ongoing pay stated with its dates, the average pay of the eight weeks before the application date times the number of pays C adds (3.752.22.B-C); less the part set aside under a Plan for Achieving Self-Support (3.752.23.DD). leap_person_wages (CO-3925) counts it for a person under the age 3.752.23.CC names and excludes it from that age on.

Precision. Earned-income records, step E1 (LEAP). The same reading as the other pay (leap_wages_in_income_verification_period, leap_ongoing_wage_streams, leap_ongoing_dated_wages: CO-3912, CO-5120, CO-5121), for the one kind whose row in leap_earnings_treatment_table (CO-5102) is excluded_age_55_or_older: the age is the person's, which a sum over the records may not read (P55), so the kind is summed here and the age is applied outside the sum. Dated pays are averaged job by job (the record's job), as in leap_ongoing_dated_wages (coverage pass 4 L4-1). Replaces scsep_wages (CO-4504), which was part of wages_gross and read as 0 when not stated. Coverage pass 6 for LEAP, R6-1 (docs/reviews/coverage6-care-energy.md): a record stated as a stream (no date) whose job ended before the income verification period's first day, or begins after the application date, is not read: the job paid nothing in the period (3.752.22.C.3.a, "use actual income received in the income verification period"; C.3.c, "If a household member has not received his/her first check from this source of income as of the income verification period, do not count any income from this source", S2713), as leap_counted_recurring_receipts (CO-5003) reads a receipt stream since L5-1. A dated pay is read by its date, so a last paycheck received in the period after the job ended is counted. Before, such a stream was selected as a job that ended or began and its missing date made the figure cannot determine.

Type money, scope person-month, program LEAP.
Uses: `earnings`, `leap_application_date`, `leap_earned_ongoing_income_weeks`, `leap_earnings_treatment_table`, `leap_income_verification_period_start`, `leap_pay_periods_per_month`.

### CO-5123 LEAP: a child whose earnings are excluded `@engine`

Whether 9 CCR 2503-7 3.752.23.Q (S2860) excludes this person's earned income: "Earned income of children under the age of eighteen (18) who are residing with a parent or guardian": the person is under leap_household_child_age_limit on the application date (leap_age_on_application_date, CO-6400: 3.752.2 considers income and household composition "as of the date of application"; coverage pass 4 L4-4) and is the child or ward of a member of the LEAP household (leap_household_members_for_income, CO-1009).

Precision. A parent or guardian is read as a legal parent or legal guardian among the members (second-pass review P2): a child living with neither, with a grandparent say, has the earnings counted. One item for the condition leap_household_income (CO-1002) and leap_requires_verification_of_earned_income (CO-1455) both read (duplicate-paths audit D-L2, docs/reviews/duplicate-paths-audit.md: the condition was written in each, and CO-1455's precision said it must match CO-1002).

Type yes/no, scope person-month, program LEAP.
Uses: `leap_age_on_application_date`, `leap_household_child_age_limit`, `leap_household_members_for_income`, `relationships`.

```
all of the following are true:
  - LEAP: age on the application date is less than LEAP household child age limit (18)
  - there is a person in LEAP: household members for income such that
    this person is a child or ward of that person
```

```json
["all",["<","leap_age_on_application_date","leap_household_child_age_limit"],["exists","leap_household_members_for_income",["rel",["child","ward"],["P"]]]]
```

Examples: 5, all passing.

### CO-5124 LEAP: a person's payments from boarders `@engine`

The payments the person receives from persons who pay to live, or to take regular meals, in the person's home (earnings records, CO-5100, of kind boarder_payments, room and board, room only or board only), which LEAP counts as unearned income: 9 CCR 2503-7 3.752.21 (S4100) counts "payments from any other source, which is considered to be a gain or benefit to the applicant or recipient", and no paragraph of 3.752.23 excludes them. Like LEAP's other unearned income (3.752.22.A), a recurring payment is counted at its amount in the month determined, and a payment received once when it is received in the income verification period.

Precision. Earned-income records, step E1 (LEAP; docs/reviews/records-earnings-care-energy.md, finding E1-L2). Before the records LEAP counted a boarder's payment for a room only or for meals only (the board_only_payment and room_only_payment receipts, leap_receipt_treatment_table, CO-5001, counted because no rule excludes them) and did not read a payment for room and board (room_and_board_payments_received, CO-4161), which 3.752.21 counts the same way; the earnings records state all three as boarder_payments, and the receipt rows read none (counted_in_earnings). The gross payment is counted: no LEAP text deducts the cost of providing the room or meals (business_cost_boarder_provision is not deducted, a row for the owner's signature). A payment received once is placed by its date in the period from leap_income_verification_period_start (CO-5002) through the application date; without its date it cannot be placed. Coverage pass 4 L4-3 (docs/reviews/coverage4-care-energy.md): a recurring receipt stated with its date is read by its date in the income verification period (9 CCR 2503-7 3.752.22.A: "received in the income verification period, not to exceed one month's income"; C.3.a, C.3.c), after the period's first day (leap_income_verification_period_start, CO-5002) through the application date (leap_application_date), not by the calendar month: the period is then one month long, so a monthly source paid on the application date's day of the month is counted once (the cap of A; OQ-681); a receipt stated without a date is read in the month, as before. Coverage pass 5, L5-1 (docs/reviews/coverage5-care-energy.md): a recurring receipt stated with neither a month nor a date (a stream) is read in the month of the application only when its source ran through the whole income verification period (its start_date before the period's first day or not stated, its end_date after the application date or not stated); it is not counted when its end_date is before the period's first day (3.752.22.C.3.a: "use actual income received in the income verification period", none) or its start_date is after the application date (C.3.c: "If a household member has not received his/her first check from this source of income as of the income verification period, do not count any income from this source", S2713); and a source that began or ended in the period is read from its dated receipts (C.3.a, C.3.c), so a stream without them cannot determine and the record's date is named as missing, as leap_wages_in_income_verification_period (CO-3912) reads a job that began or ended (OQ-681 (4)). Field sweep (docs/reviews/field-sweep-care-energy.md): less the part set aside under a Plan for Achieving Self-Support (3.752.23.DD, S3301), no more than the payment, as a pay's is (leap_wages_in_income_verification_period, CO-3912).

Type money, scope person-month, program LEAP.
Uses: `earnings`, `leap_application_date`, `leap_earnings_treatment_table`, `leap_income_verification_period_start`.

```
the sum for each receipt in Earnings where
    all of the following are true:
      - LEAP: how each kind of earnings is treated (table), for that receipt's kind is equal to counted_as_unearned_income
      - if that receipt's frequency is equal to once
        then (all of the following are true:;   - that receipt's date is at least LEAP: the first day of the income verification period;   - that receipt's date is at most LEAP application date)
```

The part of a veterans benefit paid to a person of the case who is not in this person's LEAP household (leap_household_members_for_income, CO-1009) because of this person as a dependent (the receipt's for_dependent, its for_person naming this person), placed in the income verification period as leap_counted_recurring_receipts (CO-5003) places a recurring receipt: 9 CCR 2503-7 3.752.211.E, "Any portion of a VA pension that is paid to a veteran for support of a dependent shall be considered countable unearned income to the dependent rather than the veteran". ### CO-1292 Is school aged `@engine`

Whether the child is of Colorado's compulsory school attendance age for the school year that begins in the period of eligibility of the summer the month belongs to (sebt_summer_year, CO-2581): the child had attained the age of six on or before the first August 1 on or after the period's first day (the July 1 that starts the instructional year, sebt_instructional_year_start_month) and was under seventeen on it (C.R.S. 22-33-104(1)(a)). 7 CFR 292.2 makes these the "school aged" years for Summer EBT, and 292.6 reaches a child school aged "at any time during the period of eligibility".

Precision. Coverage pass 4 S4-2 (docs/reviews/coverage4-care-energy.md): the test reads the month evaluated, as sebt_summer_year (CO-2581) and the F3-5 fix of CO-4527 and CO-4528 do, so one summer reads one school year: the August 1 is the most recent month numbered compulsory_school_attendance_age_date_month (CO-2605, August) on or before the eleventh month after the period's first month, which is the first August on or after the period's first day (P50). A July determination is for the next summer (OQ-535) and reads the August 1 a few weeks on, which is in that summer's period; from August through June the August 1 read is the one before, as before the fix (review households S1 and S1b now agree). Before the fix the test read the most recent August 1 on or before the determination date, a year earlier for a July determination. The exceptions of 22-33-104(2) excuse individual children from attendance (illness, private or home schooling, graduation) and do not change the ages. Whether the July days of the period that fall in the school year before (the August 1 before the period's first day) also count as "any time during the period of eligibility", and an August 1 inside a summer operational period that runs into August, are not read: the summer operational period is in Colorado's Plan for Operations and Management, not on file (OQ-535).

### CO-1298 Summer EBT (SUN Bucks): eligibility status `@engine`

Whether the child is eligible for Summer EBT (Colorado's SUN Bucks) and on which ground - categorically eligible (a member of a household receiving SNAP or TANF, or another categorical ground) and either school aged or enrolled in an NSLP/SBP school; or enrolled in an NSLP/SBP school with household income at or below the reduced-price meal guideline - per 7 CFR 292.2, 292.5 and 292.6.

Precision. SNAP and TANF receipt is read from the receipt records of the members of the child's household, the persons living with the child as one economic unit (sebt_household_child_receives_snap_or_tanf, CO-2708; 7 CFR 292.2; OQ-552, resolved). A child for whom any categorical prong is unknown and the income test is not met is unknown. The period of eligibility spans the preceding school year through the summer (292.7); coverage review C-6: SNAP and TANF receipt is read for every month of the period up to the month evaluated (CO-2708; 292.6, "at any time during the period of eligibility"), and, coverage review 2 N-3, Colorado Works receipt also from the month's tanf_cash_income and the other categorical grounds at any time in the period up to the determination date: foster care and homelessness that ended in the period (foster_care_exit_date, homelessness_ended_date, read by CO-4527), FDPIR receipt that ended in the period (fdpir_participation_ended_date, CO-4528), and migrant, runaway, Head Start and the other documented grounds as identifications stated for the period (CO-2848 to CO-2850, CO-2852). School age is derived from Colorado's compulsory attendance ages (sebt_is_school_aged, CO-1292, C.R.S. 22-33-104(1)(a)). Colorado's choices among the optional streamlined-certification sources (Medicaid and other means-tested programs, 292.12(d)(2)) are not in any published Colorado text: there is no Colorado Summer EBT rule (OQ-255). CDHS review C-10: the month evaluated lies in the period of eligibility of the summer sebt_summer_year (CO-2581) names, so SNAP or TANF participation in that month, or in an earlier month of the same period, establishes eligibility for that summer (292.7(a)); the benefit is keyed to the same summer. Coverage review 2 N-7: a household that refuses to cooperate with verification has its eligibility terminated (292.14(f)(5), S1093; sebt_household_refused_verification, CO-4854, read as false when not stated), so the child is ineligible. Coverage review 3 F3-3: the termination for refusing to cooperate (292.14(f)(5)) applies to a household required to verify (sebt_requires_verification_of_income, CO-1699), so a household 292.14(f)(1) excepts, such as a SNAP household, is not terminated by a refusal stated for it.

### CO-1299 Summer EBT (SUN Bucks): summer benefit amount `@engine`

The total Summer EBT benefit for an eligible child for the summer the determination is for (sebt_summer_year, CO-2581) - that summer's monthly benefit level (sebt_monthly_benefit_table, CO-1244) times the months of benefits for a summer (sebt_summer_benefit_months, CO-3013) - or zero for a child who is not eligible, or while an application selected for verification in the sample is pending verification, per 7 CFR 292.14(f)(9), 292.15(d)-(e) and the annual benefit levels notice.

Precision. The benefit is issued in full for the summer regardless of the date of application (292.15(f)(2)(iii)). CDHS review C-10: the level is that of the summer the determination is for, so a determination from July 2026 on is for summer 2027 and is unknown until FNS publishes the 2027 levels. Final pass F-21 (second-pass round): 292.14(f)(9) (S1094): "Benefits cannot be issued for applications selected for verification until the verification process is completed with the exception of verification for cause", so nothing is issued while sebt_verification_status (CO-1698) is pending, unless the selection was for cause (sebt_selected_for_verification_for_cause, CO-4073, read as false when not stated); the amount is issued in full once verification is complete. Coverage review C-10 and C-20: nothing is issued to a child another State or ITO has already issued benefits for the summer (sebt_received_benefits_from_another_agency_this_summer, CO-4521; 292.15(d)(1), no dual participation) or whose household declined benefits (sebt_household_declined_benefits, CO-4522; 292.12(f)(3)), each read as false when not stated. Coverage review C-18: 292.14(f)(11) (S3318) stops further issuance when a questionable application comes to light after issuance, until verification for cause is complete; the item gives the summer's whole amount, and an issuance already made is not reversed by it, so a for-cause selection after issuance is the agency's issuance action, not a change in this amount. Coverage review 2 N-7: a household that refuses to cooperate with verification has its eligibility terminated (292.14(f)(5), S1093), so nothing is issued when sebt_household_refused_verification (CO-4854, read as false when not stated) is true, a for-cause selection included (OQ-377). Coverage review 3 F3-3 and F3-4: the refusal applies to a household required to verify (sebt_requires_verification_of_income, CO-1699); the for-cause exception of 292.14(f)(9) is to the income verification only, and confirmation of enrollment for a child who applied by application is required "prior to benefit issuance" (292.12(e)(2), S1095), so nothing is issued while sebt_school_enrollment_verification_is_pending (CO-1696), for cause or not.

### CO-2708 SUN Bucks: a child in the household receives SNAP or TANF `@engine`

Whether, in some month of the period of eligibility up to this month, this child or another child of the child's household (a member under eighteen) is receiving SNAP or Colorado Works (TANF) assistance: the receipt that makes a child categorically eligible for Summer EBT (7 CFR 292.2, "one or more children in that household are receiving assistance under SNAP, TANF, or FDPIR") and that streamlined certification reads from SNAP and TANF records (292.12(d)). The household is 292.2's: the persons living with the child as one economic unit (lives_as_one_economic_unit_with), related or not.

Precision. Receipt is the record, not this volume's own SNAP or Colorado Works determination: receives_snap (CO-1936, the person is a member of a SNAP household receiving benefits) and receives_tanf_cash (CO-013). The household is every person joined to the child by a chain of lives_as_one_economic_unit_with edges (S2301), so a cousin, a step-sibling or a foster child living in the economic unit is read and a sibling who lives elsewhere is not (OQ-552, resolved). Final pass F-13: receipt is read for the child and for the unit's other children only, the members younger than sebt_adult_min_age (CO-3933, eighteen, the 292.2 "adult" boundary): 292.2 asks whether "one or more children in that household are receiving assistance", and 7 CFR 245.6(b)(7) (S2720), the school-meals rule it follows, extends eligibility when "any child is identified as a member of a household receiving assistance under SNAP, FDPIR, or TANF". An adult who receives SNAP as a separate SNAP household (an elderly grandparent, 7 CFR 273.1(b)(2)) while sharing the school-meals economic unit makes no child categorically eligible; the child is then tested on income. A case that states no relationships for the child leaves the household unknown. FDPIR receipt is within sebt_other_categorical_basis (CO-1296). Coverage review C-6: 7 CFR 292.6 makes eligible the children who "at any time during the period of eligibility" are categorically eligible (S790), and 292.14(e)(2) (S3317) needs eligibility shown only "at a single point in time during the period of eligibility"; the months read are those from the first month of the instructional year (sebt_instructional_year_start_month, CO-3014: July, the start of the period of eligibility of the summer sebt_summer_year names) through the month evaluated, so receipt that ended earlier in the period still counts, and 292.7(b)'s no-change-reporting rule keeps it. A month of the period not stated is read from the case's month defaults. Coverage review 2 N-3: receives_tanf_cash is a fact about the current Colorado Works case and holds one value, so Colorado Works receipt in a past month of the period is read from a payment in that month, as SNAP is read from the month's receives_snap; either the record or a payment in the month is receipt. Receipt records, migration phase 2 (2026-11-23): the payment is the member's Colorado Works cash receipts in the month (sebt_tanf_assistance_receipts, CO-5731, through SUN Bucks' table of receipts, CO-5730), not tanf_cash_income (CO-029); read as 0 when the member's receipts are not stated, as tanf_cash_income was, a default kept for the decision-4 round (docs/reviews/receipts-migration-2-cccap-sunbucks.md, section 4). Decision 4 of 2026-11-23 (docs/plan-colorado.md; as the round for the receipts readers applied it, b49a7f2): the Colorado Works assistance receipts of the child and of each other child of the unit (sebt_tanf_assistance_receipts, CO-5731) are read with no default. Receipts migration phase 2 kept a reading of 0 for receipts not stated, as tanf_cash_income had been read; 292.2 and 292.12(d) give no reading for assistance not reported, so a child who is not shown to receive SNAP or TANF by the flags and whose receipts (or another child's in the unit) are not stated has a categorical test that cannot be determined; a stated empty list is no assistance. A flag or a receipt that shows assistance still decides the test without the rest (the first true stops it). Coverage pass 5, S5-2 (docs/reviews/coverage5-care-energy.md): another member is a child of the household in a month of the period when younger than sebt_adult_min_age on the month's first day (the youngest day of the month, so a member under eighteen on any day of it), not on the determination date: 292.6 (S790) reads eligibility "at any time during the period of eligibility", so a sibling who received Colorado Works at seventeen in July and turned eighteen in October was a child receiving assistance in July.

Type yes/no, scope person-month, program SunBucks.
Uses: `date_of_birth`, `receives_snap`, `receives_tanf_cash`, `relationships`, `sebt_adult_min_age`, `sebt_instructional_year_start_month`, `sebt_tanf_assistance_receipts`.

```
  any of the following is true:
    - Receives SNAP

    - there is a person in the persons joined to this person by lives_as_one_economic_unit_with such that
```

Whether the child is a homeless child under 7 CFR 245.2 (S1952), which 7 CFR 292.2 makes categorically eligible: lacking a fixed, regular and adequate nighttime residence as 42 U.S.C. 11434a(2) specifies (S1953): sharing the housing of others because of loss of housing, economic hardship or a similar reason; living in a motel, hotel, trailer park or camping ground for lack of alternative adequate accommodations; living in an emergency or transitional shelter; abandoned in a hospital; or living in a place not designed for sleeping, a car, park, public space, abandoned building, substandard housing, or a bus or train station.

Precision. 245.2 asks that the child be identified as homeless by the local educational agency liaison, a shelter director or another person FNS names; nighttime_residence_type (CO-2810) is that identification as the case states it. A migratory child (11434a(2)(B)(iv)) is homeless when living in one of these circumstances, so needs no separate arm. A temporary stay in another's home for a reason other than loss of housing or hardship is not homelessness under McKinney-Vento.

### CO-4072 SUN Bucks: a ground that excepts the child from verification `@engine`

Whether the child has one of the grounds, other than SNAP or TANF receipt, on which 7 CFR 292.14(f)(1) excepts a household from verification: a member of a household receiving FDPIR or another means-tested program the Secretary has approved, or a foster, homeless, migrant or runaway child as defined in 7 CFR 245.2.

Precision. Not Head Start enrollment or individual certification for free or reduced price meals, which are categorical grounds (sebt_other_categorical_basis, CO-1296) that (f)(1) does not list. Foster care is the foster_child role, or a foster care payment or IV-B service in the child welfare record, as in CO-1296; FDPIR, migrant, runaway and another approved program are positive identifications, their absence read as no such ground. SNAP and TANF receipt is read by sebt_requires_verification_of_income (CO-1699) from sebt_household_child_receives_snap_or_tanf (CO-2708). Coverage review C-21: the union of the two groups 292.14(f)(1) tests separately, sebt_child_is_foster_homeless_migrant_or_runaway (CO-4527) and sebt_child_has_fdpir_or_approved_program_basis (CO-4528); CO-1699 reads the two.

```
  - SUN Bucks: eligible through FDPIR or another approved program
```

### CO-4523 Summer EBT: household size `@engine`

The number of people in the child's school meal and Summer EBT household, the related or unrelated individuals living as one economic unit with the child (7 CFR 292.2 "Household"), for the household size and income standards of 292.5(a).

Precision. Coverage review C-11 (final pass F-20): read from the household the case states as a group, the persons joined to the child by lives_as_one_economic_unit_with (S2301), the same group sebt_household_child_receives_snap_or_tanf (CO-2708) reads, so the size and the categorical test count the same people. When the case states no economic unit for the child (the child alone, or its relationships unstated), the size reported on the application (school_meal_household_size, CO-1294) is read instead; a child cannot be a household of one in a school meal application with others in it, so the group of one means the unit is not stated. The household's income stays the application's reported figure (school_meal_household_income, CO-1295; 292.2 "Current income").

Type whole number, scope person, program SunBucks.
Uses: `relationships`, `school_meal_household_size`.


### CO-4527 SUN Bucks: a foster, homeless, migrant or runaway child `@engine`

Whether the child is a foster, homeless, migrant or runaway child as 7 CFR 245.2 defines them: the second group whose members, when all the children of a household belong to it, except the household from verification (7 CFR 292.14(f)(1)).

Precision. Foster care is the foster_child role, or a foster care payment or IV-B service in the child welfare record, as in sebt_other_categorical_basis (CO-1296); homeless is sebt_is_homeless_child; migrant and runaway are positive identifications, their absence read as no such ground. Coverage review 2 N-3: 7 CFR 292.6 (S790) makes eligible the children who "at any time during the period of eligibility" are categorically eligible, and 292.12(d)(1) certifies those who "during the period of eligibility were" foster, homeless, migrant or runaway children. The role, the child welfare payment and nighttime_residence_type state the present, so a child whose foster care ended (foster_care_exit_date, CO-2853) or who stopped being homeless (homelessness_ended_date, CO-4851) on or after the first day of the period of eligibility (the month numbered sebt_instructional_year_start_month, CO-3014, on or before the month evaluated) is in the group too; either date not stated is read as no earlier ground. is_migrant_child and is_runaway_child are identifications at any time in the period (CO-2848, CO-2849). Coverage review 3 F3-5: the period of eligibility is placed from the month evaluated, as sebt_household_child_receives_snap_or_tanf (CO-2708) and sebt_summer_year (CO-2581) place it, so this item is read by month. F3-6: 245.2 is not limited to Colorado placements, so a placement by another State that ended in the period (other_state_foster_care_exit_date, CO-4963) counts as foster_care_exit_date does.

Type yes/no, scope person-month, program SunBucks.
Uses: `child_welfare_payment_type`, `foster_care_exit_date`, `homelessness_ended_date`, `is_migrant_child`, `is_runaway_child`, `other_state_foster_care_exit_date`, `relationships`, `sebt_instructional_year_start_month`, `sebt_is_homeless_child`.

### CO-5731 SUN Bucks: a person's TANF assistance receipts `@engine`

The assistance under TANF paid to the person in the month that SUN Bucks' table of receipts reads (sebt_receipt_treatment_table: Colorado Works basic cash assistance), other than a retroactive payment for months before the month received: a payment that shows a child of the household "receiving assistance under ... TANF" in the month (7 CFR 292.2).

Precision. A receipt is read in the month it states, or in every month when it states none (it recurs). A retroactive lump sum is paid for earlier months and is not read as receipt in the month it comes in. Replaces tanf_cash_income (CO-029, paid in the month for the member's needs) for SUN Bucks. Read by sebt_household_child_receives_snap_or_tanf (CO-2708) for each month of the period of eligibility, for the child and the other children of the economic unit. Coverage pass 5, S5-1 (docs/reviews/coverage5-care-energy.md): a stream (a receipt with neither a month nor a date) is read only in the months from the month of its start_date through the month of its end_date (docs/conventions.md, "A record's time"), so a Colorado Works grant that ended before the period of eligibility is not assistance received in it (7 CFR 292.6, S790: children who, "at any time during the period of eligibility", are categorically eligible; 292.2), as SNAP reads a stream (snap_counted_recurring_receipts, CO-5011). Review household SS1: CO-5731-T5, CO-2708-T16.

Type money, scope person-month, program SunBucks.
Uses: `receipts`, `sebt_receipt_treatment_table`.

```
the sum for each receipt in Receipts where
    all of the following are true:
      - SUN Bucks: how each kind of receipt is treated (table), for that receipt's kind is equal to tanf_assistance
      - all of the following are true:
        - that receipt is received in the month
        - any of the following is true:
          - it is not the case that that receipt's month is unknown
          - all of the following are true:
            - any of the following is true:
              - that receipt's start date is unknown
              - the month containing that receipt's start date is at most the month
            - any of the following is true:
              - that receipt's end date is unknown
              - the month containing that receipt's end date is at least the month
      - it is not the case that that receipt's retroactive
  of
    that receipt's amount
```
